Study the HWs to do well on exams, but make sure you actually understand how to use the formulas, not just memorizing how to do certain problems. Go to lectures, go to TA's for HWs, you'll be fine

Dr. Jones is a helpful and caring professor if you go to his office hours. Beware that office hours might have lines of over 20 people though. His lectures are pretty boring and not that useful. I felt like I couldve learned alot of the functions by myself. Make sure to start the HW early and practice every week.

Dr. Jones is a great professor. You are graded on your performance so if a grade brings down your overall grade he won't even put it in the grade book. He will help you with the homework. Just go to class and the assignments will be a breeze.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Jones was a great professor and the class was easy if you kept up with the work. A little bit of prior excel knowledge goes a long way for this class, but it is not necessary at all. I would recommend going to the lectures because he teaches you the formulas you need to know for the exams, homeworks, and lab exercices.

Dr Jones is not caring at all, never responded to my email. homework and lab exercises are annoying and he doesn't really get through main stuffs during lecture. He only talks about a lot of unnecessary stuffs. The exams are not so bad, they kind of reflected lab exercises. Also, if get perfect grades on exams but did poorly on hw still above A-

Prof. Jones is a really smart dude but lectures are bland and doesn't really provide notes for you to take since he's just typing formulas in on excel. His grading criteria is frustrating as he looks for exact excel formulas on exams although you can come up with many different formulas and get the same answer, but it would be considered incorrect.

Take him for MIS250, he knows what he is doing and how to explain it. You have to go to class tho. Extra credit costs money since its a different textbook. 7 homeworks (pretty easy, there is a hw party where you can finish it) , 3 exams (timed 1 hour, hard) , 2 labs (75 minutes, moderate to hard). Worth taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The class overall was easy. The homework and labs were fine, go to the TA hours if you have problems with the homework, they are very helpful. The exams are an hour long, but they are not hard, it's just he never gives enough time so it's easy to make mistakes. The lectures are somewhat boring, but go to learn the information. He is a fast teacher
Had him in the summer for LEAP, but as long as you follow along with the examples and stay on top of the homework you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Definitely a smart guy, but a very boring lecturer. Sits at a podium and talks at the class the whole time. He moves very quickly but it's worth it to go because he occasionally helps you with the homework. Redo the homeworks for practice. Tests are not timed and go by very quickly. Work together on the homework and go to TA office hours for help.

Good instructor that shows you easy-intermediate excel tools. He teaches it well and shows the significance of the material. Exams are timed and can be tricky if you didn't do well on the homeworks. Don't cheat on the exams or he will likely catch you. Also rounds up grades a good amount at the end of the semester

Jones is a smart guy and definitely knows what hes talking about, and he tries to help students out the best he can. However, he can be quite bland at times and about half the lectures don't contribute much to the actual course, homeworks aren't bad if you start them ahead of time with a group, labs are easy, exams tough just because they're timed.

Jones is a smart guy and definitely knows what hes talking about, and he tries to help students out the best he can. However, he can be quite bland at times and about half the lectures don't contribute much to the actual course, homeworks aren't bad if you start them ahead of time with a group, labs are easy, exams tough just because they're timed

jones is rogue thats all i can say. lectures are only good before the first test if u have no prior knowledge of mis just so your not overwhelmed once hw comes. if u redo homeworks before tests youll most likely be fine. tough class but the tas all really help. grading is based off of what you do right not how much you do on tests. labs r hard too

I do not recommend taking this class. If you are good at excel, you will probably do fine. But I have never used excel and this class was definitely not the place to start learning. Going to class was pretty useless and basically I thought the class was way harder than it needed to be.

I didn't have any problems with Jones, unlike everyone else on here. If you are somewhat familiar with Excel, this class is a breeze. Follow along with his formulas in your own excel sheet, know where the formulas are, and you can mimic them on exams if you forget the exact formatting. If you understand the format, exams are easy.

Super nice guy but he spent most classes manipulating data to show you how he catches people cheating or going over exams rather than teaching.. What you do learn in this class is actually very helpful you just have to make sure you put the time in. Start the homework with ample time and go to the TA's with questions, they helped a lot.

Spends 80% of the class talking or showing you how he manipulates test data of students to catch cheaters and whatnot, and then 20% actually showing you a few formulas you need to know. I could literally teach myself the stuff and do fine and not waste my time in class. Sometimes class helped if he showed a specific way he likes doing something.

Nice guy but requires very specific formulas on homework and exams. If you know how to do a problem a different way and get the right answer, he will mark it wrong unless it is done his way. Other than that, the class isn't that bad. There is also a significant curve of your grade at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Only business professor to curve exams so well in favor. He is a really smart guy - most useful class i have taken this semester. I would not skip many classes since the material you need will be taught in class. Don't be too scared when he says problem solve - you need to understand the components of the formula not a plug and chug application

This guy doesn't really teach. He kind of shows you the basics of excel and then the homeworks and tests are the most complicated applications ever. It's easy to do well if you go to class and really take your time and try on assignments but you don't have enough time on exams to complete them. Go to TA office hours and do the extra credit.
dont recommend taking him, lectures are useless, exams are extremely hard
Lectures are terribly boring but the class as a whole is pretty easy. As long as you can confidently do the homework before the exam you'll be fine.

Hw's worth 30% of the grade tests are other 70%. Tests are open hw & open web. Not all tests resemble hw's but similar. Not enough time on exams, but he'll curve some of them. Lectures are really fast and confusing. If you have a background in excel (i didn't), you'll be fine. He curves class at end based on average. Got D's on all tests ended B-
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Professor Jones has a good personality and teaches the material well. I already had a solid background in Excel so I only showed up to class once every two weeks or so and still got an A. I didn't have the class in a computer lab, so unless you plan on bringing a laptop to class, don't bother showing up. His exams are timed and somewhat short.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was dreadfully boring. It was mostly Jones lecturing, group projects and a few individual assignments. There are no exams which was nice. You really only had to go to class on work days for group projects. Most of the group projects are PPTs and you can find all necessary info online. Jones isn't a bad teacher, he's just boring. Easy A.

I had to take my class with Dr. Gu. To some, she was a horrible professor. I thought she taught the material well. Very fast during lectures, and does not connect with students one on one. Wish I had Jones as my professor. Every question I had, Dr. Gu did not answer and told me to email Prof. Jones (while he is receiving hundreds of emails).

This class requires effort if you haven't learned excel before. Jones' lectures are a bit fast and its easy to get distracted. The exams are exactly like the homeworks but there is not enough time given on the exams, but he curves every exam a lot. Buying the extra credit it helpful so you should be able to get an A if you averge a B on exams.

If you have to take MIS204, take it with Jones. You don't need to go to class, just make sure you understand the homework (they aren't hard)  for the exams and you'll be good. You don't need a book and he gives 5% extra credit. At the end of the semester he will curve the whole entire class. He lets you look up the answers to the quizzes too.

Cool teacher. If you know excel from an internship there is no need to go to class. The grading is pretty odd because it's done electronically and there are many ways to do things in excel/some of the exams it is difficult to identify what exactly he wants or how to do calculations because you have to move fast and instructions are not clear.

Not as bad as everyone makes him out to be. He doesn't give enough time for exams which is what makes the course hard, but besides that he was a decent teacher. If you take him, I would definitely recommend doing all the extra credit he offers.

Art really is not as bad of a guy as some people like to make him out to be. He has a very difficult job overseeing so many students for such a complex subject. Excel stuff was very easy to me, but could be difficult to those who have never used it. Tests are weighted for you to succeed, whether you finish them or not. HW takes an afternoon to do.
Very easy material but to compensate for it he give you no time... horrible teacher

Prof Jones is overall a nice guy. He makes excel kind of interesting. But he goes really fast when moving through the material and it is rather hard to ask questions when confused. Last test is extremely hard, but if you do good throughout the semester you will be fine.

This class is way too hard for what it is supposed to be. The last two homeworks and all of the exams are super hard. Did not attend class but heard from the people that did that it didnt help on exams or homeworks. Had to pay $100 just to do extra credit which is a necessity if you want B or higher.  Do not take with him.

This could have been a helpful class, but it wasn't. Homework starts out easy and then gets extremely difficult. Exams are extremely hard (I always ran out of time) and the final was totally different from everything on homework, practice, and previous exams (15% of it was based on one excel function he never even mentioned). DO NOT TAKE WITH HIM

This class changed tremendously this semester. It has become extremely extremely hard. Basically, the lessons are like 1+1 2, however, once you go onto assignments, tests and exams, it will be a different world totally.

This class is so much harder than it should be. He'll go teach you a basic function in excel and then make you figure out a way to combine that formula with five other functions for the homeworks and exams. Exams are awful as you have three full excel worksheets to do within 1:30. I will usually end up finishing about 60% of the exam for grading.

The reason why the reviews are worse for this class in 2015 is because the structure of the class was changed. The exams change every year, and are only slightly similar to the homework. They are significantly harder. 30mins per a sheet(3 sheets). He is willing to help. If you are VERY familiar with excel you're fine, beginners will have a hardtime

This class is really hard. No other way to put it. The homeworks are absurdly challenging (mostly towards the middle and end of the semester) and the tests are even harder and you are pressed for time. If there was not extra credit in this class I would have done much worse. He isn't clear with his instructions either. Nice guy though.

This class is not as easy as people make it out to seem. Jones is a great guy and class is interesting but once you get to the homework, boom, it's like nothing you've ever seen. It's 20 times harder than class material.  You'll spend hours on the homework! And the tests are very HARD.  Thank goodness there was extra credit, you'll need it!

He is super easy and helpful. If you have to take MIS204, you should take his class. Actually, you do not need to buy the textbook since excel things are every where on google. Only need to buy the access code to do the MyITLab. During tests, you can google, bring your notes and textbook, and even ask the TAs or him how to do it.

Dr. Jones was an awesome professor and MIS 204 was an easy class. Came in with no prior Excel knowledge and now I feel very proficient with my skills. Helpful at office hours for homeworks, exam questions, etc. MyITLab stuff was kind of annoying but he didnt make it a huge part of his grade and understood it had a lot of problems.
Really easy course. Unfortunately he's kinda lazy and even though he says he will help if you ask, he usually says he will 'look into it' and never returns.. Still.. it's an easy A so take it

Class was very enjoyable with Dr Jones. Rather than focusing on memorizing material he let us work through programs and learn actual skills. I wish I had taken 432 earlier in my MIS major so I would have some career related skills to talk about at career fairs, rather than 390 and 446 which did nothing for me.

Nice guy!  Fairly easy class if you go to class and pay attention, can be a little fast-paced if you do not know a lot about excel.  Takes a long time to grade stuff, but overall not a super hard grader.  I expect to get an A or A-.

Skipped majority of the classes and ended up getting an A. Memorize answers to the study guide. The excel assignments are a little annoying but not difficult if you have common sense. However, learned nothing in this class. Art is a good guy though and wants to do what he can to help

Art Jones is a really awesome guy.  His class is the easiest you will ever take, and he is an all around cool guy.  Even though it was useless to go to class I would still attend just because he was so nice.  If you have the choice definitely take him.
Skipped every class...got a 98%.
Gave you the questions to the exams beforehand and lectures were obnoxiously boring.  Skipped probably half of his lectures and still got an A.

Dr. Jones' class is really easy. He gives you the questions to all of the tests, and then even makes a discussion forum...where everyone posts the answers. Started studying for the final less than 5 hours before and got 100. Nice, funny guy. Nothing to lose if you take him.
The class was pretty easy but i didnt learn anything

By far the worst professor I've had at Penn State. The course offers little support for applying material outside of lectures (few assignments or practice resources), and Verma is largely inaccessible. He doesn't respond to emails, dismisses questions, and doesn't advertise office hours. If possible, take this course with a different professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: guy makes machine learning a pain and a slog to learn about. Mock Midterm was hardly anything like the actual one, homework and coding requirements have 0 rhyme or reason to them, and he hands out pop quizzes just to spite you. Not looking forward to the final.
gives random pop quizzes to accompany his bad lectures and expects that to boost attendance. The average of his midterm was a 35... that should tell you everything
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: The lectures are very wordy and mostly follow the slides with limited explanation. Attendance feels important due to mentions of pop up quizzes, though there has been very little use of them. Communication can be slow, especially over email. Grading is strict and feedback is limited.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The rating speaks for itself! Doesn't check his emails nor does any of his 3 TAs. have no ides what's going on and barely any communication. This far into the semester, we've only had 1 homework and it was wildly different than the exam. Run!
This class is a disappointment.

I'm in this class currently, and nobody knows what's going on. This guy just talks, reads off his slides. So boring, assumes we came into class with a bonkers amount of knowledge. From what I have heard, exams are unbelievably difficult; you get 1 cheat sheet, no calc. Stay FAR AWAY! Even if you read this and think "im smart ill be fine"... beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I've never seen someone so apathetic toward the class they're teaching. He did not respond to messages; quite literally, he just read the slides. I learnt absolutely nothing in this class and it was not due to a lack of effort. We weren't given a lot of feedback or practice material to learn the concepts that he merely, dryly read in the class.
A very generous curving, other than that awful.
I we so excited about this course, but professor was not organized at all, did not care. I learned mostly by myself, lectures did not help. Try to take with another professor if you can.

reviews.comment:
In class, I learned little, with lectures so dull,
Skipped them; their boredom just too much to cull.
Homeworks complex, one of three barely scored,
Finals near, panic aboard.
Midterm at fifty, emails ignored,
Excitement for abstracts, quickly outpoured.
Hoped to learn more, but found just a smidge,
In this class, lost concepts over the ridge.
Final in two days, only one HW graded the whole semester. Boring and overly complicated lectures and slides. Does not respond to any students questions on classroom discussion boards.

I literally have never taken a class worse than this. Lectures are awful, homework assignments are even worse when we get them. We got our first assignment grade 40 minutes before the late drop deadline. A midterm with an average of 50%. God bless everyone on this final, because we're all going to need it.
