reviews.comment: Barely taught anything. Lectures were so boring, I couldn't attend them. The homeworks were complicated, and only 1 out of 3 has been graded and it's finals next week. The midterm average was a 50%. Never responded to any emails, and hardly communicated with us. I was excited for this class, but it's just all abstract concepts. Didn't learn much :(
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: We're 5 weeks into the course and our only assignment so far was a math review at the start of the semester. Literally no practice material whatsoever. Mumbles through math theory during lecture and tells us to just read the textbook to actually learn the content. By FAR the most useless class I've taken at PSU. Take this class with someone else!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Made what could have been an a very hard class so much easier. She is so clear on what will be on the exam and will literally tell you the questions in the review videos sometimes. All she ask is for respect and effort. One of my favorite STEM classes I have taken so far and has made me excited to continue to learn about immunology.

She talks very fast and is hard to understand which makes learning the course material very difficult, however, lectures are mandatory but a waste of time. To study for exams she doesn't give any study guides but instead expects you to review hundreds of slides from class.

Dr. Katkere does absolutely nothing to make this course easy to understand. She talks at the speed of lightning, so that I can't even begin to process what she's just said before she's halfway through the next topic. She quite literally snickered while informing us about how low the class average was, and said "It'll only get worse". Avoid Katkere.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. K is my all-time favorite professor; she is kind and flexible about anything that happens. Highly recommend!

She's my favorite prof I've ever had. I love her she's super nice and has really good slides. The class is hard so be ready to study and there is a lot of info, but she gives a ton of extra credit so good grades are very achievable. She also has an extra credit assignment for each test that can give you up to 20 points back on each test.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a great prof - the class material itself is challenging, but she gives a lot of extra credit and rewards her students for attendance. Very passionate about what she teaches and clearly wants to see her students succeed.

Intro Immunology is a really hard course. There's lots of memorization and frustrating details. Dr. Katkere did not make the content harder than necessary, but she didn't make it easier either; her teaching was average. However, she rewards attendance and hard work. She reminded my class often that this stuff is on the MCAT, which... is true.

Dr. Katkere was not the most popular teacher. My group of friends had great respect for her. I personally found her lectures super interesting and the tests super predictable. She stays after to talk with students. She about cried when a student disrespected her in front of the whole class over a test question. I would take a class with  her again.
Not clear in her lectures. Changes the grading scale multiple times throughout the semester. Doesn't provide office hours.
I took both 140 and 141 with her and she is very helpful and good at her job!
Dr. Pallone is great. Very helpful and cares about students' success. Would recommend doing homework and going to lecture even though it is not required.

Dr. Pallone is one of the best professors I have had at PSU. Her lectures made calculus easy, and she makes herself easily available outside class during her office hours. I would recommend Calc 140B for its Specs Grading system, and if you take it with Dr. Pallone, it is not difficult to get an A if you put in the work. Definitely recommend!!!

I had her for Math 140 and would take her again in a heartbeat. She was so down to earth. Along with that, she was amazing at teaching. She took the time to explain the ins and outs of why everything worked the way it did and cared so much about her students. She was helpful when we had a question and truly wants to help. I recommend!!!!
Genuinely one of the best professors I have ever had, hands down. If you can take this class with her, do it. (My grade is the way it is because I had to focus on other finals and tank this one's)
Great Professor, but Calc 2 is a nightmare no matter who the professor is
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Homework took me hours to complete and there was a ton of homework for this class. I ended up being really sick on the day of finals and submitted documentation and she would not let me make it up, so I ended up failing the class. She gives quizzes in-class.

Dr. P is an amazing professor with a really good plan for the semester. Her lectures are great, and she makes sure to answer any questions people have before, after, and during class. There are scheduled quizzes once a week, and online homework as well. She never tries to kill you with work and is very understanding and accommodating to everyone.
Pretty much everything you could ask of a professor. She brought worksheets to work on and proceeded to explain it all very clearly. She's possibly the reason I found Calc 2 very easy.

Professor Pallone was my favorite professor in my first semester. I am an astrophysics student, and I took 141, not 141B. The content was difficult at times, and I admittedly did not do well on the third exam, but Professor Pallone was always kind and helpful. Use her office hours, as she genuinely will want to help you and any way! Best professor.

Professor Pallone was the best teacher I had my first semester. She explained things very well and was always happy to answer any questions. She's super lighthearted and gets her points across easily and quickly. There are individual quizzes, group quizzes, and post-exam quizzes to help boost your grade. 10/10 would take this class again.

i took 141 not 141b btw but they're like the same thing
she's an awesome professor, i really sucked at the class, but she was always willing to help. one of the better math professors i've had in my 3 semesters at penn state. her lectures were easy to follow, there was always access for help, and she kept me engaged as somebody who struggles w adhd
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Pallone is the best! She explains topics very well and answers questions if you find anything unclear. Her office hours are also very great, and the quizzes aren't too hard but they still prepare you for the exams.
Literally the best math professor ever! Genuinely wants her students to do well and is super chill. Math 140 is hard but she breaks down the material well. Try to take math with her if you can!

THE ABSOLUTE BEST CALC PROFESSOR. Dr. Pallone is an amazing teacher and person overall. She is incredibly understanding and totally understands if you have a lot on your plate. She wants you to succeed in her class, and is more than willing to help you wherever you are struggling. If you are scared about taking MATH140 or MATH141, she will help.

Super great teacher, I learned so easily from her! Also, you can get a lot of extra points from attending LA sessions which are super helpful anyway! She is super caring. If she doesn't think she covered a topic well enough she will change quiz and homework due dates. Loved this class and exams are not hard if you study.

The best math teacher you can have for this class!! Office hours were super helpful. The lectures are fast but you can always ask questions. There was plenty review material for exams and in class review time too. Exams were not too hard and all the homework is helpful and not too much. Pallone cares about her students!! THE BEST

Taking this math course with Dr. P was so lucky because of how amazing she is! She is a very participating and collective teacher that works with the class not just lectures. Do all the homework and go to the LA sessions, do well and try and talk to Dr. P and you will breeze by!
She was a really amazing professor and her way of explanation was easy.

Dr. Pallone is a caring of her students and explains everything so thoroughly. She explains things in multiple different ways and explains why things are the way they are, which made it easier to understand personally. For a class like calc 1, it's really important to have a good understanding of the basics if you need high level calculus.

Dr. Pallone is a great professor. She is super nice and always willing to help out if you have questions. Her notes are super helpful and so are her office hours. Her quizzes can be hard but you just have to study for it. The exams aren't bad at all as long as you understand the topics. She is amazing and I would definitely recommend her.

Dr. Pallone is the BEST Math 140 professor. For how hard Calc 1 is, she makes the material easily understandable. Never hesitate to ask questions, she will take the time to answer them! The homework takes some time but helps you understand the material better. Quizzes every week but they are really easy! Take her if you can!
Love prof pallone! She is really nice and understanding and genuinely wants you to learn. Her notes are easy to follow and she goes through examples really well. She knows her stuff.

She is a great professor but I will warn you, YOU NEED A IPAD FOR THIS CLASS. Unless you can write at Godspeed, it is nearly impossible to keep up with the notes. She does post them after lectures but the speed at which she is able to do things on her iPad is much quicker than what I can do by hand, causing me to fall slightly behind in class.

If you have the opportunity, TAKE THIS CLASS WITH DR. P! She is a very good professor and goes through many examples of problems that you will see on exams. She helped me see things from a different perspective than I was taught in my high school calc class, and it paid off TREMENDOUSLY. Be sure to attend class even though attendance doesn't count.
She is literally the best professor at Penn State. Explains everything so well and honestly I dont have anything bad to say

Best math teacher you will ever have. Really easy going, nice, and made sure everyone understood the material. Prepared you for exams, helped each student succeed, and gave homework that really helped as well. Taking her again for math 141B.

I was never really great at Calculus or enjoyed math until I took this class. Honestly the best professor I have had so far. She is super friendly and understand the struggles that students go through. The exams can be tricky but if you ever have questions about any problems you can go to her office hours. Overall amazing experience!

I really loved Dr. Pallone. She actually cares about her students and want's to make it easy for you to pass. I had no trouble in her class and went less than half the time. She's accessible outside of class and happy to answer questions. Overall an enjoyable experience and I highly recommend her classes.
Very strict on talking and phone use, but his lectures are entertaining. The textbook was easy to read too. No exams, just 5 point open note quizzes every Friday. He offers extra credit as well!
You learn a lot

I thought this was a good class to take. No electronics allowed, but I think it helped me learn better. 5 point quizzes every Friday helped my grade a bunch. Very informational class that would help anyone.

He's a hardass about talking and phone use but that's honestly kind of refreshing in this day and age. He is a very boring lecturer though. He also makes you buy the textbook he wrote. The class itself is very easy and you'll get an A if you show up every day.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just show up to class and you will do amazing. Open note quizzes every Friday and the final is only 10 questions. You're not allowed to have your phone out but the lecture is super entertaining so it makes up for it. Super useful class and loved him as a professor! 10/10 semester for sure.

Professor Billy is a very strict and straightforward guy. No electronics, only paper and pencil. Course is based on 100 points total so pretty much any point you miss is a percentage of your grade. There is ample amount of extra credit opportunities, so take advantage of that. The material is super interesting though

This class is interesting and it is honestly easy as long as you go to class and pay attention. There is a quiz every friday but your lowest 2 grades get dropped. This class was very interesting and I really enjoyed it. There is little to no work outside of going to class. The quizzes are easy as long as you take notes in class; they are open note

Class is from the perspective of a doctor (take that as you will), doesn't know how commas work 50% of the time, and textbook is outdated. Easy class if you show up every Friday for quiz, read the chapters, and go to the majority of classes. Content 5/5 Professor 1/5 good luck
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Billy is great! The class is very beneficial for everyone, especially if you plan to go to medical school. As long as you do the readings and take advantage of the extra credit, you should have no problems. Everything you learn is something you can utilize in the future.

Dr. Billy is passionate about teaching. He is the doctor for the football team and sees outside patients as well, so he doesn't have to do this. You'll learn about different types of doctors, conditions, and insurance. Attendance, weekly quizzes, final, and two extra credit opportunities. Great Gen-Ed that will be useful for the rest of your life!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very weird class structure. Quizzes every week. Lectures were super boring. Quizzes were wayyyy too hard and based on lecture material and textbook content. Most people took this course as a GenEd, so it shouldn't have been so difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Great professor. He is super fair and doesn't overload work by any means. Delightful class. I would definitely take again.

Dr. Billy's standards were "no nonsense," which I liked a lot. You truly earn your grade in this course. Plenty of opportunities for EC, clear-cut grading criteria, and simple 5-point quizzes. If you can't handle that, probably shouldn't even be in college. His lectures were very interesting and definitely left me better prepared for med school.

The only two grades in the course are attendance and 5 question weekly quizzes. Only 3 of the questions are actually from lecture, and the other two are from the required text. This required text was written by Doctor Billy however, and is by no means cheap. Basically, buy the book he makes royalty on or fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class is only out of 100 points, so every point off a quiz or from missing a class is 1 percent off your grade. I liked Dr. Billy, but wasn't a fan of the grading system. Quizzes were tricky, so you have to know what to look out for as some of the questions were taken directly from the lectures. I would recommend this class for GHW credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Billy definitely knows his stuff and is passionate about sharing his knowledge with students. Very useful class for real life application. What made me rate Dr. Billy slightly lower was his not-so-great attitude and big ego. Didn't make for the best class environment, but still worth checking out for helpful information.

AVOID THIS CLASS. The lectures are boring and he doesn't allow electronic devices in class. Students are kicked out if they use one, and then, open note opportunities are closed. Grades are based on attendance, Friday quizzes, and the final, with Friday quizzes being the worst. Extra credit opportunities are available but time-consuming.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Most fascinating class at Penn State. Dr. Billy is old-school, but knows his stuff. Will boot people from class and remove open-note privileges for quizzes for phones/laptops. Normal doctor's ego, but worth it. Expect a 4/5 on each quiz unless you absorb the whole textbook word for word. Picky with chosen questions. Get that extra credit, though.

Dr. Billy is an amazing professor!!! Every lecture you attend has meaning and he gives you so many good tips and strategies to use. You are not allowed to go on your phone, but you should be able to last 50 minutes without your phone. He has weekly quizzes every  and if you want to do well go to class and take notes on the textbook readings.

Dr Billy's class was very interesting. While I didn't do as well as I'd hoped (mostly my fault for not doing extra credit) you will learn a lot and if you go to class and do the extra credit you should get a B+ at least.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: easy gen ed. he is strict with no technology/attendance, but its a manageable class. buy the textbook. quizzes every week and a final. 5 extra credit points are offered. he is nice when you speak to him one on one.

Honestly, take this class if you need a GenEd. He's really strict on no technology but your grade is made up of weekly quizzes, a final (10 question quiz), and a lot of extra credit. Definitely get the textbook its really helpful.
Saw him in a commercial and was convinced to take his class. Was totally worth it!!

Pretty easy health gen ed. Weekly open note quiz on Friday (from textbook reading and lectures). Quizzes can be pretty specific. Top Hat attendance. Plenty of extra credit assignments. Final is cumulative but there is a final review that makes it easy. No phone policy (if someone uses phone they get kicked out and next quiz is closed note).
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He made the content itself interesting, but there are not a lot of points to be graded on. He is pretty easy to email and he will get back you in a timely manner. He is very strict especially with technology as he does not allow any during his class period.

Dr. Billy knows his stuff and teaches a useful course. His quizzes were a little harder than expected as the questions he chose were oddly specific sometimes, and he's very strict about no technology in class and will walk around the room to make sure. But, if you can manage without your phone for 50 minutes it's fine! He posts lecture slides!

Dr. Billy is a chill dude. He's picky when it comes to electronics in the class which is weird. Reading the textbook chapters each week is important. There's a small quiz at the end of each week and you should be able to do good if you pay attention and read the chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Show up to class and pay attention. Weekly open note quiz on lectures and his book. Extra credit options are easy to complete. Lectures- very interesting material. 10-question final the week before finals week. One simple rule- no electronics. Dr. Billy cares about students and made it easy to learn the material. Great professor! Highly recommend!

It's hard to do bad in this class. Show up to the required lectures and take it with a friend to do a little studying with and it's an easy A. Can get 5% of your grade back from extra credit. Very informative class just don't have your phone out.

Make sure you put your phone away for at least an hour or he will make your Friday quizzes closed notes unfortunately. While his lectures come off as kind of dry and monotone, it is very informational, and is probably one of the most helpful gen-ed courses I've taken in my 3 years of Penn State. Put your phone away, study hard, and you'll do well.

Professor Billy is a pretty decent teacher. The class is just him lecturing about the slides he has on the screen, but you need to make sure you are good at note taking. I would usually just take the notes outside of class. He has a strict no phone policy so if he catches you on it, your quiz every Friday is closed notes and he kicks you out.

Easy class, great information that will help you later in life. Don't have your phone out, he will make the open note quizzes closed note and kick you out, it isn't that bad to put your phone away for 50 minutes. lecture never lasts the whole time, Dr. Billy is amazing!

One of my favorite professors and classes at PSU. He is very funny, but is very strict about a no phone policy. Class is super easy with weekly quizzes and extra credit. The information you learn in class is super useful in real life. Would definitely recommend taking his class.

Dr. Billy is very clear about his expectations and from day 1- especially his no electronics policy. He's kicked out two people so far. He gives a lot of opportunities of extra credit and the quizzes each friday are open note. He's genuinely a really cool guy and funny- show up to class and do the short readings. you're fine, trust me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's not arrogant. One open notes quiz every friday, will make it closed notes if someone has their phone out during class. Read the textbook & take notes. Attendance via TopHat every class. Drops two lowest quizzes, and no final during finals week. He posts the slides after every class, and they're pretty much just word for word from the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Overall the class is pretty interesting. Quiz every Friday, 5 questions, but tend to be difficult. Extra credit bumps your grade about 3-5%. Very strict with technology, will kick you out of the class if he sees you using your phone. Lastly, would recommend taking his class in Fall as he travels with the football team so some classes are remote.
This class was super easy. Show up and you'll get an A for the semester. Weekly quiz on Friday is open note and final is small percentage of total grade.

Weekly (open note) quizzes covering lecture and reading material. Attendance is mandatory, but as someone said below, if you take him in the Fall there will be some online pre-recorded lectures. He drops the two lowest quizzes and allows you to miss two lectures. Lots of extra credit options that give a 2-5% grade boost.

Easy Gen Ed and I can say I actually learned some pretty unique things from it. Since he is an actual doctor, getting his insight on certain topics was cool. Tells you what you need to know for the real world, respectable. All these bad reviews are bogus. Tells you from day 1 to keep electronics away, is it that hard to listen to his ONE request?

HPA 57 with Dr. Billy wasn't too bad of a class. A quiz every week, attendance, and a small final are the only grades, but he offers extra credit. He is super strict with technology and will kick people out if they use it. I would take this class in the fall because he travels to every away game, so no class on Fridays sometimes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I highly recommend HPA 57 to satisfy the GWH requirement! This class was very interesting and helpful- the class is all about how to navigate the healthcare world as a patient. I feel much more knowledgeable about healthcare issues and how insurance works. Love Dr. Billy and NO tests in the class- weekly 5 point quiz based on the weeks lectures.

HPA 57 is a 3 credit GHW. There is a clicker question every class and there are weekly quizzes that are based on the lectures that week. Professor Billy offers extra credit points as well. You will learn a lot of useful information to help you navigate the medical field. I highly recommend this class.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very straightforward. I learned so much from this class and I think everyone should take it if they can. The textbook is written by him, and it is actually really interesting. It is probably the only text book I have actually read that for my classes.

This is my favorite class I have ever taken. Lectures are very interesting, and I learned so much from him. The people who don't like this class definitely are not paying attention at all. There is no outside of class work, and short 5 question weekly quizzes that you take in class. I love this class and this prof, definitely take this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Literally the easiest class I've ever taken but also the most useful. I learned a ton from Dr. Billy, and as long as you show up to class, you'll pass. I have very little interest in medicine, but the content of his class is necessary for everyone to know regardless of major or interest.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: A lot of the people who are complaining are the ones who dont pay attention. Dr Billy gives easy lectures, and as long as you come to class and read the very short chapters, youll get an a on every quiz. He even hints or directly says what questions are on the quiz if you pay attention in class. Very friendly guy and gives out 5pts extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I'm not sure why everyone is hating on Dr. Billy because this class really wasn't that bad. As long as you come to class every day and get your participation points, you'll be fine. Read the book with short chapters, take some notes, and the quizzes aren't awful either. He even gives out a bonus point for simply answering a question in class.

Dr. Billy is a little dry, but he seems like a nice guy and is very knowledgeable. He is an actual doctor so his insight is very helpful. The class itself is a little dull, just reading lectures and quizzes, but it's very passable. Overall an easy GHW credit and intro into the HPA minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I found that attending the class was very difficult since the lecture is spent on unnecessary information that you can find in one google search, but somehow all the class revolves around it, very boring too. The quizzes are the most important, but have the most ridiculous questions. However, the class is passable but poorly presented.

STAY AWAY FROM THIS CLASS AND PROFESSOR. I got a D in this class and I have never gotten a D and I am a senior. This class was a challenge for no reason. His attendance policy was ridiculous. He only did participation once in a blue moon and if you missed that lecture, your grade went down every time. He was also very rude to students, STAY AWAY!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Taking this class online was ridiculously easy. All the quizzes and the final were open note, so you could just look up everything. If you just showed up to class and knew which textbook chapters and slides to look at, there was nothing to worry about. I could see it being tougher in person, but I'd imagine it would still be manageable.

So this man clearly has no passion for teaching sadly. He is the football trainer so makes sense why he wouldn't care about anyone other than student-athletes. Dude is going bald and so is his attitude and mood towards students. Really sad to see, hope he retires soon :(

I love this class because Dr. Billy is so insanely smart. Any health-related question you ask him he can answer with full confidence and it is crazy impressive. Taking it during covid/online seems much easier than in person. Just 1 quiz a week based on the lectures and an online final. I definitely recommend this class and professor.
This class is very informative but is graded on mostly quizzes. Do the extra credit and you will be fine. Professor Billy is passionate about informing students about the class content.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Basically the only grades are the quizzes which are the most random questions from the whole week and textbook so it's hard to study and know what will be on it. Also if u get one question wrong you're at a B, 2 wrong you're at a D. Extra credit is helpful and there's not really any work other than attending class and the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very easy/low workload GHA. Grades from attendance (can miss 6-8 classes), 5-question clicker quizzes every Friday which has 3 questions from lecture/2 from his textbook, & a 10 question final on the last day of class that he provides a review for. Also, has extra credit worth 5% toward your final grade. Attend class & read the textbook. Easy A.

If you are looking for GHA credit, don't take his class. As some people mentioned below, he is way too strict about electronic devices including clickers and even rude to students when they are just trying to reach out for him. I really don't think he likes the students and idk why he stays as a professor when it's so obvious that he hates teaching
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: You will have some extra credit opportunities. Easy A- but you need to be prepared for the quiz to get an A. I would recommend to take other classes if you are looking for a GHA class
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: So strict and not flexible at all. It's just HPA57 after all, and it isn't 400 level course right? Crazy about electronic devices in class. A few kids were kicked out from class in front of people because they used phones/laptop. Seriously? Really have to do that? Who would take this if there is no GHA requirement? Mr good doctor, hospital need you
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He will not give you your participation credit even if you had a clicker problem just for a day or two throughout the whole semester. He doesn't care if you are injured, had difficulties on clickers whatsoever. He is too stubborn for his policy and not flexible at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great class. I feel like I learned a lot of applicable knowledge I want to pass on to the rest of my family and friends . As long as you have a good attitude and do the readings you will succeed. The extra credit is pretty cool too - I got an extra 5% for running a 5K.

He makes you buy a textbook that costs over $50 which has all the information covered in the power points except a few details. Every Friday, you have a 5 question quiz and 2 come from the 2 sentences he decided not to put in the powerpoint, it's really dumb. No technology except your clicker. One participation point every class, 3x a week.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The class is super easy. Pretty boring cause it is all common sense, and it being at 9 am did not make me want to go often.

Very easy class, content is not hard to understand at all. Exams are super easy and you'll do well on projects if you follow instructions. However, Dr. P contradicts herself often, and she does not seem very knowledgeable about the field of psych. She makes the class very frustrating, but it's all common sense.

She makes all the quizzes very based on the lecture powerpoints, so you should go to class, and besides that she tends to help you more if you show up to class more. Go to her office hours, even if its just to yap.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: People are dramatic, this class is very straightforward and easy if you attend class. Take notes on her lectures and you will do fine on the exams. She is a very caring person you just need to reach out to her

Worst professor in the psych department. I recently experienced a family loss and was planning on leaving the week before break for the funeral. Until I realized that the makeup exams are in essay format, and are heavier concepts and more in-depth. Fortunately for her, I missed the funeral for the exam. Hope she never receives tenure.

Imo, she's not that bad. Not the best, but tolerable. She uses tophat so you have to go to class to get those points, but missing a few won't hurt you too bad. Doesn't post the lecture notes though! Hard to understand, but is kinda funny. Exams are closed note and are a little hard, but if you study/go to the review sessions, you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Pan's class was one of the weirdest I've ever taken. She doesn't post slides, but she moves fast through them and will rarely go back if asked. She gave out grades that didn't make sense, and when I asked her about them, she gave little clarification. It is possible to do well on the tests, but honestly, I just gave up because I was so over it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: People are being dramatic. Go to class take down the notes and you'll get an A. She isn't super approachable but she's accommodating if you're nice. The exams are extremely easy as long as you look at the study guide and your notes. Not the best professor but doesn't deserve a 1 rating at all. This class was easy asf as long as you GO TO CLASS

Class is very exam heavy (86% of your grade). If you are a good test taker you won't have a problem with this class. I definitely could have gotten an A if I took more time to study for the first two exams. Professor herself is not very nice and hard to understand. Going to class would be pointless if she posted the slides but she doesn't.

Honestly not bad. Not approachable at all and doesn't give out her slides. I'd recommend making a friend to help get notes. As long as you study the notes and go to class you should get an A-B. Do the extra credit (2 extra sona hours) Pretty much your only grade will be 4 exams. class average is a B
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She's a weird individual and extremely rude. She won't post PowerPoint slides and when u miss some material, she gets annoyed when u ask to go back to the slide. Lecture slides make absolutely no sense. Only grades are your exams. Supposed to be an easy course and it's my most dreaded class of the week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures from slides that she refuses to post, one point saying we weren't allowed to take pics of the slides even though she goes super-fast and gets annoyed if you ask to go back. Doesn't let you go to her office hours to see the slides if you missed a class. Rude to students and some of the info in class is blatantly incorrect. AVOID HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Easy class. I got nothing below 90 in all the exams. Most of the exam questions are straight from her knowledge check. No additional reading, everything is from her lecture notes. Two simple assignments. My only gripe is she doesn't post the slides.

This class is graded off of 80% exams. Yes, you read that correctly. There is little to no other coursework aside from the exams. Pretty much no opportunities to get your grade up, aside from a few assignments worth a small number of points. 100 level class yet slides are not posted, and canvas is a blank piece of paper with maybe four things on it

By far the most painful class I've taken at Penn State to date. Attendance isn't mandatory but she does not post the slides, so you need to go to get the material. Her lectures are robotic and she reads directly off the slides, and does not elaborate when students ask questions. 50 question exams on topics often not covered. Avoid at all costs.

Lectures are content heavy with information that makes no sense. Awful teacher she just reads directly off the slides but refuses to post the slides to canvas. If her goal is to make people not want to go to grad school she's doing a great job because she often talks about how horrible getting your phd is and how you will be miserable/sad youll be.

This was one of the worst classes I've taken. Lectures are packed with content but make no sense, and she doesn't actually teach. Makes odd comments about students. Exams are way harder than they need to be, and some material she presents is just wrong. I'm a senior with a good GPA and might still need to retake this class. Avoid if possible.

She's difficult not bc of the material, but because she makes it difficult. Her lecture style is a *talk at you* style. She doesn't like students asking questions. 50q exams. 


I'm writing this SP25 so maybe in the future she'll improve, but given her overall attitude, I'm not struck by an immense amount of humility so I doubt she'll change much.

I had to flip the name because it would not let me add professor Paneerselvam. Take a different professor if you have to take PSYCH 105. Horrible at lecturing, extremely boring. She does not elaborate on most of the slides and reads directly off of what is on the screen. Gives awful responses when students ask questions or to go back a slide.

Can't say enough nice things about this prof. He means business but is super flexible and easy to talk to. Class is designed to help you professionalize in your major for jobs after graduation, which is very useful. Attend class, do all the work while following directions, and you'll get an A/A-. Just find a good peer review partner!
He will fail you for
ough grader, but a very nice guy. Just make sure to read the rubrics and assignment directions carefully.

Dr. Seekford gives really good feedback on your writing, and will make you a better writer. The most important thing with this class is participation - discussion in class and going to office hours is expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He is a very reasonable grader and makes time for students, and if you talk with him in class and office hours, you'll know how to improve and get the grade you want. Talk with him early in the semester though. Also does a really good job at helping you get beyond high school writing. I'm super happy I took this class.

He means well, but can get very overboard. The class is very hard to pay attention to, but the essays are tailored to you. He grades everything on a 4.0 scale which is hard to bring up your grade over a assignment. He's not the greatest at explaining things but is always available to help outside of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: This rating is for ENGL30H. Professor Seekford is one of the best teachers I've taken at Penn State. Attendance is important, but that's only because he gives good instructions and information for assignments, which he doesn't always provide outside of class. Prof Seekford is very caring about you as a student. Offers assignment extensions.

This prof is very helpful and easy to talk to. He isn't always easy, but he works hard to help you succeed. I think he really just wants to see work ethic and improvement in the assignments. His lessons are normally decently engaging too. If you wanna become a better writer, he's def the guy for you.

Take this class with someone else. He will fail u for 4 absences even with a valid excuse. He doesn't care if it is medical/emergency etc, when the university even requires it to be accommodating for it. He's a total jerk about it. Everything is graded so harshly and will nitpick little grammar mistakes. Has very unclear instructions of his want

English literacy is not one of my strong suit, but he was a phenomenal instructor who cares about his students. Getting an A is very hard but a B is very achievable putting a normal amount of effort in. He's a very fair grader who will point out where you done well and where you should improve
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Brett is a fair grader who genuinely wants his students to succeed. The amount of homework is reasonable and helps a lot with the writing process. English isn't my favorite subject, but he gives great feedback, encourages you to do your best work, and is very knowledgeable. He offers great advice during office hours on how to improve your papers.

Prof. Seekford is so caring and insanely organized. He goes out of his way to help his students. I can't imagine anyone getting less than a B if they attend class and do all the assignments, though some papers are challenging. I definitely grew a lot as a writer thanks to his help.

Prof Seekford is nice, but I didn't like the format of the class. 5% of your grade is participation, which is hard to get when there aren't a lot of opportunities for everyone to participate. Everything is on a 4 point scale, which makes it hard to bring your grade back up from any low grade, so stay on top of it. Lots of group discussions too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Somewhat nice dude, but please take this class with another professor. He grades extremely hard, and loves to flex that he is a tough grader. You will have a million assignments a week. His lectures are also pointless, he requires that you participate A LOT, and he always held us at least 5 minutes over.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Brett makes it clear that he wants everyone to succeed, but he also emphasizes that an A requires a lot of effort. Overall, he's a very caring teacher who makes you want that grade and provides the support to get you there. He clearly wants everyone to succeed as long as you put the work in!

This professor delivers lessons effectively and ensures you learn the material well. However, he is a tough grader, and your grade directly reflects your understanding of the class. If you're aiming for an A, be prepared to put in significant effort. Earning an A in his class is a true accomplishment you can be proud of.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: A very caring teacher who runs a smooth and organized class. He is always offering help and is lenient with submissions. I am not the greatest writer and think his grading can be very hard, but it is never unfair as he provides a long and detailed feedback paragraph. Overall, I recommend.

Very reasonable and approachable prof. Most Engl15 sections seem to be tough with grading, but Professor Seekford provided good feedback and was always available outside of class to help. You will definitely become a better writer through his classes. Make sure to also participation a lot!

Imo the reviews here have aged poorly. The exams average 80 for the midterms. Homework is difficult but you get a bonus question on each one to earn extra credit on. He does kinda get carried away in class and rambles but it just comes across as him enjoying the subject. He is also very helpful and open to questions. Just pay attention in class.
His teaching ability is very limited. Making the material harder than they are. Avoid taking his class.

This professor gives exams that are inconsistent with his lectures and assignments. His blackboard writing is terrible. He doesn't have a good grasp of the material, so you won't learn much from taking his lectures.

Confusing grading scheme that didn't get figured out until the end of the semester. Exams were super long. Put R questions on the hw that were hard to do if you had no prior experience- the rest of the hw was easy and so were the exams. Handwriting was very hard to read. Ended up grading everything fine at the end though but it was stressful.

Lectures were very hard to follow and he did not explain the material at all. He did not do any example problems in class so it was very hard to understand homework. Exams questions were nothing like homeworks.

Sam is very kind, open to feedback, and willing to help if you just ask. We had many extra credit opportunities for all homeworks and exams. Exams were really dense, so practicing solving problems quickly is very important. All exams were curved at the end of the semester, but even the raw grade distributions were better than reviews for 414 say.

His exams are super difficult. He's nice and is understanding. He accommodates for a lot, but the exams were stressful even when he moved them online. They were harder when he moved them online tbh. However, he wanted feedback and wanted to know what he could do better which is a good mindset to have in a professor.

Made this class way more difficult than it needed to be. Class notes were confusing and not helpful. Homeworks were brutal and there is no resource that exists to adequately aid in completing it. The class avg on the first exam was 32% and even the take home avg was a 50 something. Def would avoid taking this class with Sam if possible.

spared a point bc he genuinely is a very great guy. idk why the exams are crafted to be so hard tho. all hws and exams have a bonus question tho. But exam scores were always awful (1st Midterm mean ~32%), causing an insane curve. got so bad that all exams are take-home now...STILL 40s-50s averages afterwards. idek. hard class made harder?
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very nice person, and his lectures are easy to follow with his style of teaching, but I wish he went over more practice problems and applications of various distributions of random variables so exams would not be extremely hard unlike the homeworks, which are a cake walk in comparison.
Difficult class and exams are extremely hard, but he is a very nice guy.

15 or so in person weekly quizzes from lecture vids posted each week. They are pretty hard compared to the videos and practice, but doable. Never saw him only TAs. Final/Midterm are not based on intellect, but memorization. An annoying class, but far better than CMPSC 201. Gets better as it goes on. Grade has about 30% buffer so room to struggle

1 'exam' per week. a free mc mutiple choice part, and a much harder free response (both worth equal weight). class is just hard bc there is not much to study, you can't really prepare for the free response. Theres one practice worksheet, other than that nothing else than some easy lecture examples. Should not be async.

Easy class but never saw Professor Sottile a single time in the semester. All lectures are pre-recorded videos. Mon is rec, Wed is quiz. Takes about 2-3 hours a week to watch all lectures plus 1 more hour for homework. If you do the HW and take detailed lecture notes you'll be fine on quizzes and exams.
You do not learn anything in recitation because the TAs do not explain anything.
The guy's a joke you never see him and he is very condescending based on his emails. Exams are also brutal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Brad is bad.
You never see Brad. Only lecture videos from 10 years ago.
you will not see brad. have fun

all materials have been reused since 2016. wont let you see your quiz for feedback after you take it, so its hard to improve. basically unreachable outside of class, is condescending, blames adhd for not answering emails. recitations led entirely by ta's and you will never see him. exams are not related to coding, only random facts from slideshows.

Poorly made, 10-year-old lectures that contain outdated and useless information are all you have for the semester. He is nice enough if you have to reach out, but he's condescending and you'll most likely never talk to/see him. The exams are super heavy on random facts from lecture but weekly assignments are graded strictly and on weekly code

Another badly constructed computer science course at Penn State. You learn all the vague information on online videos, then you go to a recitation with TA's that gloss over very simple problems, and then after studying using the material THEY provided to you, the assessment's end up being way harder than they should be. Compsci at psu SUCKS!

Recitation on Mondays are a waste of time. Weekly assessments are difficult, lectures are all online to watch. Weekly quiz/discussions can get tedious. The content itself isn't bad but some weeks there is a lot. MC Midterm/ final which you can use a note sheet so take advantage on that to do better. You barely see Brad, recitations taught by a TA.

Recitation on Mon then assessment every Wed and watch 2016 lecture videos over the weekend. You never actually meet the guy as only TA's in classroom. The assessments and midterm aren't released so hard to get feedback and improve. Exam questions just meant to trip you up so copy everything you can onto cheat sheet and memorize the tiniest details.

Decent professor, gets the job done. Assessments/Quizzes are weekly and usually have a multiple choice + coding section. The midterm and final are multiple-choice exams that test how well you can memorize the slideshows rather than code. Recitations are useless, its easier to self-study for this course and just go when required.

Assessments weekly were brutal and stressful because you have to submit your file within the amount of time given otherwise no credit at all. No feedback given on assessments either because he reuses them. Exams multiple choice meant to trip you up not to teach. Reuses lectures from years ago and they are not helpful at all for assessments.

Horrible professor. Doesn't lecture, uses lecture videos from 8 years ago.  I'm pretty sure he uses the same material, including same quizzes, same assessments and same tests every year. The class is overall boring and tedious. Every test is multiple choice with many questions intended to trip you up, rather than help you learn and improve.

Since the lectures are online, this class is very recitation heavy. Good luck getting a good TA to work through problem sets with. Mine wasn't the best, but they were very lenient with open notes for assessments. Only one exam besides final so focus on it! As for Brad, he's very clear and concise with his online lectures and HAS updated them.
Literally got on zoom with me at 11:30 pm to go over something I had questions about. He is the GOAT

He does nothing. All his lectures are from like 2016. Because of the outdated videos, some of the new features arent there and I had an assesment on a feature that no longer exists. The exams are meant to be rote memory. I asked a few upper classmen and they said you only learn matlab from matlab, not class. Should've been an easy course, wasn't.

Prof, Sottile was the worst part of my semester. The class itself is not very hard, but studying for the midterm and final was not easy. He does not allow you to see what you've gotten wrong on any assessments or quizzes without being with a TA. This is not optimal for studying for anything. Overall this class felt like a waste of time.
The professor is very nice and friendly. Class needs more time to fit the process. But compared with other computer science classes, this is a very great one to take.
Professor is nice but he doesn't teach. Each week the assessment is so awful and stressful. You need to pay attention so much to get a not bad grade.
His lectures are from 2017 but they are interesting for people who are learning to code for the first time. His office hours are helpful, but the TA's are not always clear during recitations.

This entire class is extremely time-consuming and if you fall behind kiss your grade goodbye. Brad seemed like a nice guy but he doesn't actually teach the class. His recorded videos are helpful but they can get very long and tedious. I recommend just making friends with one of the TAs to get help with your code so you can prepare for recitation.

It is a hit or miss. This class is ran by TA's so it depends on who you get. Brad's videos are very helpful though so make sure you watch them. Tedious class though really take your time and put in effort
The weekly assessment is much harder than he taught in the video lecture. Just get ready to be surprise with those questions.

brad's lectures are easy to follow and you literally just use those to write your cheat sheets for the weekly assessments and you're good.
i got an awful TA for my recitation, so i've never really been able to understand the problems during recitation time, but through the video lectures it's easy to do them. his office hours are super useful

I came in with no coding experience and struggled at first but ended up fine.  The midterm (and final) are pure memorization based.  If you ask your TA's for help during the assessments and attend the recitations, you will be completely fine even if you do not watch the lectures.  Just make sure that you write down the code from the recitations.

The structure of the class was unique but easy to get used to. Weekly online lectures which were easy to follow, weekly Canvas quizzes, and then weekly in person assessments. Some weeks, assessments can be a little tough, but you get used to the set up. TAs are incredibly helpful and there are plenty of office hours available if help is needed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: To start I only saw Professor Sottile one time in person. The lectures were all prerecorded which was helpful but I think it also makes it harder to understand the content. The rest of the course is directed by TAs who just code a problem set and you just copy what they do. Brad seems like an interesting guy but you do not get the chance to tell.
Brad just posts the lectures for the class and most of the work is done online. Attendance is not taken at recitation but it is important to go for the weekly assessments.

Great professor himself, but the examples done in class were way easier than what we were tested on. Attendance is required for 1/2 the classes. Discussion posts were kind of pointless, but easy points.

I mean I never actually saw Brad in person, but on 2x speed, his lectures aren't bad. The format of the class is two recitations/week. One is just time to practice and get help, the other is for taking weekly assessments. Not much of a commitment though, I spent 1.5 hours/week doing work for the class outside of recitations.

Brad's recorded lectures were a nice resource and held all of the information needed to do well in the class. Some of the recitations and discussion posts were a little boring and felt unnecessary, but as long as you had a strong running cheat sheet (allowed for weekly quizzes) the assessments weren't anything crazy.

Brad's lectures were pretty solid for sure. With prior coding experience, I watched them on 2x speed which definitely helped save some time. The weekly discussion posts weren't my favorite, but I still learned some cool things from them. I thought assignments were pretty easy and his life advice each week was always something thoughtful.

The assignments were usually much harder than the examples gone over in class. Make sure you know about the CODY assignment weeks before it is due to have time for it, it takes forever. The class was hard but he was an extremely nice person.

His class was fine and easy to comprehend but the weekly homework and discussions were unnecessarily time consuming. The final was ridiculous and while it was untimed you had 24 hours to complete an assignment that would take 1-2 hours on top of a 50 minute opened ended response, also there is a CODY assignment that will likely take 12 total hours

Brad has been fantastic this semester with online classes. The class is structured super well and there is ample support for you if you need it. I had no coding experience prior to this semester and I'm doing very well. Just watch the pre-recorded lectures, go to live recitation, and office hours (if needed) and you will be good. Amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Brad was a good professor and his class structure is very organized. Navigating classes online is much more difficult than in person, but Brad made it easy and lectures really helped me learn.

A snip from a canvas announcement: "I have reviewed the midterm exam schedules *lists 13 classes*. I know this doesn't cover the full scope ... I thought that looking at these courses gave me a reasonably good chance for reducing the majority of potential conflicts. " AND PUSHED THE EXAM BACK 2 WEEKS BECAUSE OF OTHER CLASS EXAM SCHEDULES

The difficulties of the projects are incommensurate with the quality of the online lectures. He does not give useful feedback when you are stuck at the project. Quality of the lecture plunged significantly after the late drop deadline(one less loose end). You would learn more from your TA than from him.

Professor Sottile is extremely caring and will help you if you need it. The class is tough, especially if you haven't had coding experience before. You will definitely need to study for the weekly quizzes and tests.

Brad's method of teaching is sending links to lectures that are on YouTube and recorded 5 years ago. The entire course is basically run by your TA, and the only thing Brad really contributes is sending you canvas announcements, you see him twice a semester at most. The class can be confusing and can be even worse if your TA isn't helpful.
Worst class I have ever taken

I didn't know Brad much, but I enjoyed the course, even if the final was quite difficult. I met with Brad after the final just to meet him, and he's a really great dude! It's clear to me that he's very approachable and accommodating when you need him. No real complaints about the class - just watch lectures on 1.5 speed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: A lot of work goes into this class. Watching online lectures, attending recitation for a weekly quiz, then a weekly assessment, and an additional discussion post that is essentially pointless. The assessments can be super difficult and confusing. Attend every class and do every assignment and you will pass, but effort is required for an A for sure.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class is pretty easy as long as you go through the lectures and show up to class to take the quizzes and such. The discussion boards are pretty useless and can be annoying, but they are required. Brad himself doesn't do much besides the lectures he recorded 5 years ago. Also, his quiz/test questions can sometimes be written confusingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: You have to attend each class and study hard every week if you wish for a good grade. The assessments are sometimes really easy and others really confusing and hard. The class requires a ton of work, there's always something to do every week. The class itself starts off really easy then picks up a lot on abstract theoretical concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is mandatory because every class you have either a test or a quiz, so skipping class is a no-no. Brad is a nice guy in person, but he rarely comes to recitation so it's hard to really know. His lectures are pretty decent and very explanatory. Don't buy the textbook, it's useless. Go to recitation and do the practice to get the A
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: the class itself if pretty boring but of the two classes per week, one has a quiz and the other has an assessment so you can't really skip class. the online lectures are really slow so I put it on 2x speed. Also helps to stay for recitation as the examples covered are very similar to assessment questions.

Brad is awesome! This guy genuinely cares, and is constantly evolving his class. I honestly feel that online is the best way to teach this class, and I can't imagine having to attend a lecture because I liked to go back and watch the lecture videos. If you show up to recitations and assessments a B is manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: It's kind of hard to rate him because you only actually see him on the first and last day. The rest are just lecture videos, which do a pretty good job of explaining things. You will have a quiz and assessment each week, which end up being most of your grade. Every quiz day you will have a problem set led by a TA, so just hope they are good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brad is a great professor & genuinely cares about how he is doing. He is very receptive to reasonable feedback and every test/quiz is 100% fair. it is a bit memorization heavy but this is necessary to be able to successfully code. He knows that most people taking hos class are not going to be cmpsci majors and that this is a 1st time coding class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He only does the online lectures and the other two days you are taught by a TA so just hope your TA is good. The class is very heavy with assessment with a quiz every Wednesday and an assessment every Friday. The class can be tricky at times but over all was not too bad
Brad was a great professor and his quizzes and assessments, while frequent, were generally SUPER easy and he himself is a great guy. I'd take this course again!

Dr. Sottile has clear lectures, but they are long and seem to be packed with an excess amount of information. This class requires an obscene amount of memorization, making tests quite difficult towards the end.

Having zero programming experience coming into this class, I can say that Brad ran a fantastic course. His lectures are very helpful and they tell everything you need to know for his assessments. Going to "class" is convenient, as you can pull up his CANVAS lectures anytime you need to. Don't waste money on buying the textbook - you won't use it.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY--Would take again

reviews.comment: Heavy class with a lot of online lectures. You will never see the professor first person because of it, and the online lectures are on average 10 minutes each, and 5-10 of those lectures a week. PS, they will make you sleep. Very confusing class, because most of the material is theory based, and he doesn't really specify which one we have to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This man seems very knowledgable but does not AT ALL care about teaching this subject. the online lectures are the worst as he sounds so disinterested he will make sure to put you to sleep faster than your nyquill. You just never want to listen to the lectures because of his annoying voice. I learnt way more from the TA's of this course than him.
Class is a lot of work but if you keep up with it you'll be fine. DO NOT BUY THE TEXTBOOK! YOU WILL NOT USE IT AT ALL. But Brad's a nice guy and  is a decent teacher.

This class is so much work its not even funny. There are 2 sets of weekly lectures you must watch or there is not chance of you passing. There is a weekly quiz and a weekly assessment (which consists of 2 parts, open ended and multiple choice). On top of all of this , there are projects throughout the semester.  Get ready to put in a ton of time!!
You have to spend a long time for this course if you didn't learn matlab before.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Web classes are always heavy. Take this class in a semester at which your schedule is not too busy, because you need to spend A LOT OF time practicing. Watch every video that he posed and take notes very carefully, don't skip any details. Details always on the quiz. Open-ended assignment is time-limited. Better perfect yourself before you take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Mr. Sottile decided to incorporate weekly exams into our course this semester in order to bypass the need for a mid-semester final. However, he gave almost no feedback on the weekly exams. If you got behind you had to hunt down a TA. He refused to open the exams even though they proctored online. It made the final terrible and the course confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Brad was trying something new this semester, where he didn't give midterms but had a smaller assessment every week. For the most part this was fine, but it hurt on the final because none of us knew what an actual exam would look like. Overall, a solid professor who really wants all of his students to be successful in his class.
Awesome guy, very laid back. allows for a ton of notes on the exams. really used the matlab code later in my career so very helpful
Easy class, good teacher, great guy.

Lectures can get confusing when he tries to explain math equations and sequences, but in general pretty clear. Near the end a lot of the material taught wasn't needed for the final. Didn't give a final practice exam sadly but he did for the first 2. Very helpful if you are completely lost but not as useful for explaining kinks in your specific code

Brad was a helpful professor and desire for his students to understand the material and do well was clear. He answered any questions present and made matlab fairly simple. Weekly labs and quizzes were completed fairly quickly. Projects took a little more time but helped ensure you are prepared for the exams.

Brad goes through so much to help out the students that take his course. He give up a lot of time to teach the students how to program, and is even available for skyping if you're really struggling and can't meet with him.

Brad was a great guy and a professor I really enjoyed.  I had never had any type of programming class before, but he really eased the transition and made programming something I have come to enjoy.  Would definitely take his class again.

Brad is a very nice and understanding person. He will always give you an extension if you need one and is super helpful when you have labs. Sometimes I feel like he can almost be too helpful because he will literally write sections of code for you, and then you never learn it and it shows up on exams and you're mildly screwed.

Brad is a nice guy, passionate about all things computing. I loved his inspirational advice, but the rest of lectures almost put me to sleep. He allows cheat sheets on exams that you wouldn't survive without unless you are basically a professional programmer. The biggest thing with Brad is his grading. It took almost two weeks to get our exam score

Nice guy. Cares about his students, always giving weekly advice for what employers truly look for in students beyond grades. He is very knowledgeable and tries his best to remember all 250+ students names. He allows one cheat sheet double sided for exams, take advantage of this and you will be set for at least a high B.

Has a bit of a tendency to ramble and get off-topic. However,  you can tell he really loves what he's teaching. If you go to him for help, he'll make sure you understand the material. Very dedicated to his students and, even with a large number of students, makes a strong effort to get to know his students on a personal level.

If you see Professor Sottile teaching CMPSC 200, sign up immediately. He was so much better than the professors who taught the class previously. There are labs and small quizzes every week but that's really the only way to learn the material. Exams were straightforward and he allowed one page of notes for each exam.
What can I say, Brad is the man!!
Brad was the only reason I had a chance of passing Aerospace Dynamics.  His review sessions were a "must-attend" affair for anyone in the know.  Also candy at reviews.

Brad was a great TA.  He had great feedback and help for everyone.  it was easy to tell that he wanted all of us to succeed and gave a lot of opportunity to do so.  He's always open on how to change things to improve your experience and make sure you get the most out of the class.  If there was every any issue, all someone had to do was speak up.
Brad is the best!

Not very clear on anything. Problems on labs are much harder than they need to be. Sometimes seems like he gets lost in trying to just show you how hard engineering can be rather than teaching you about computer science

I'd say he pretty good at explaining the concepts of finance. With that being said hes very bad at over explaining basic formulas making it confusing and doesn't teach very much that's on the exam. Also very small room for error to get an A. Getting LionTutors is a must and makes the class much easier except for exam 3 that one is way harder.

Bundro is amazing. He walks around and really wants to help you out. Negative reviews are from people who cheated on and exam and got caught. 4 exams, 2 homeworks each exam, grading is test heavy. If you go and pay attention in class, there is no way you get anything lower than a B plus. I love this guy so much I'm taking his other FIN class

I'm not sure why this professor has negative reviews. If you attend class, pay attention, and study the course manageable. Professor Bundro explains topics clearly, and the course structure is straightforward. I highly enjoyed his class; don't be scared by other bad reviews. Nice guy. Not too hard if you work at it.

Lecture is pointless all he does is yap about nothing and barely teaches you. Makes you watch videos that he made 2 years ago instead. Miserable professor who doesn't do a good job at teaching. Depends on Ta's to do bulk of work for class. Very boring and do not recommend in any aspect. No curves, No extra credit, no late credit, no hw drops, hw due at 7 am, doesn't respond to emails at all.

The lectures are boring and not helpful. He posts videos of the content online so watch those rather than sitting through lecture where he spends half the class talking about other stuff. “This is just my 9-5.” First thing he said lol, won't answer emails, doesn't care about students. Finance is relatively simple and yet he makes it hard for no reason. Don't like this guy and hope the serpentine belt on his subaru snaps.

The rate my professor for Bundro makes it seem a lot worse than it is. His lectures are pretty straightforward and he ends class early 99% of the time. Fall 2024 was his first year teaching here and he was horrible. Took him spring 2025 and he changed the whole curriculum and you can easily get an A if you pay attention and study for exams. The content was not hard at all

I don't find him boring but most people do. He is still review bombed because last semester half the class got caught switching tabs. He posts videos that have EVERYTHING for exams which is amazing, if you take bad lecture notes you can rewatch the videos and be good.

Richard was an interesting guy. His lectures are very boring and he didn't get a lot done during the lectures. He explains every topic perfectly and exams are so easy.. This is an easy class if you pay attention. Most people pay attention that's why they complain, it's that simple. This is seriously such an easy class just be a half decent student and you'll do good if me with my 3.0 gpa can get an easy A, so can u

This guy is great. He gives you everything you need to succeed on his exams he legit tells u what you need to know. He actually talks way too much and thinks hes in a movie or something. not only that but the classroom is so hot i feel like im gonna die everytime i walk into thomas 100 and then i see him and get more upset. earring.

Terrible. GPA decreased by a lot

not a great professor, unclear grading scale, hw = 20%, 4 exams= 80% of your grade, very slow in class gets through very few examples. hw is different than exams and equations differ from each other as well. :(

Professor Bundro is nice (except for the one time he crashed out on the class), and the class is not terribly difficult. However, his lectures are maybe the most boring thing I have sat through. He spends an hour slowly explaining around 2-3 examples, but basically teaches nothing in the process.

Terrible professor! He does not explain anything clearly, and his lectures are awful. He only completes about two problems during the hour and fifteen-minute class. Overall, it was a terrible experience, and I strongly recommend not taking his class.

Very slow talker and tests not like homework or class questions. Doesn't actually teach just rushes through examples in class and never answers questions. Had to teach myself everything

Ignored my emails. Confusing grading scale that makes 0 sense. Barely goes over examples in class and rushes through them and does not answer questions. Exams are nothing like what he teaches in class.

Honestly, this may be the worst professor I have ever had. He barely reviews any examples in class (3 examples per class AT MOST). The formulas on the homework are different from those he provides us with in class. The exam grading scale makes no sense; the TA does not understand it. If you have the choice, do not take a class with him.

I liked Rich's teaching style more than any other professor at Smeal, I learned a ton from his course. I hope he teaches another 400-level finance class before I graduate so I can take him again. He had a really cool background in CompSci that brought an interesting perspective to the class. I strongly recommend his class.
Awful. Makes assignments due at 7 AM??? Who does that??? Do not take. Truly awful.

Rich is a top 3 professor. Not only is he chill and a cool dude to talk to, but he truly wants to help the students who care. On weeks with quizzes, there was no class on Friday which was nice. Non-quiz weeks were typically case study weeks which were really just group projects that reinforced material from the video lectures.

The GOAT. I learned a ton about using Excel and Modern Portfolio Theory from his 406 course and I really appreciated how I was able to focus on learning without unnecessary exam stress. Only need 90% for an A and assignments are graded very fairly.

Flipped classroom format, so you watch the lectures on your own. In exchange, there's no class the day after quizzes. Watching the lectures definitely helps with quizzes. Attendance is mandatory for quizzes and case study days, but not otherwise. Pay attention while he explains the case studies and they'll be much easier. He's a chill professor.

Professor Bundro had a loose flow of class that at first I was skeptical of, however if you read the syllabus and actually look at the due dates, it is easy to know what you have to do each week. Everything is excel and real world based which can be tough at first, but since I am starting my internship in finance this summer, it helps a lot!
Chill guy. Pretty flexible on timelines. Pretty easy A if you put the time in

Flipped classroom: lectures + practice problems  2ish hours a week. Group case studies (never got below 100), podcast quizzes (online + practically free points), 7ish lecture quizzes in class (mult. choice, 10 pts, delegate # of points to the 4 questions urself), 1 final. Rich is funny & cool. Only need a 90 in the class to get an A!!!

Professor Bundro is super chill. He wants to teach his students relevant finance like how a mortgage works, where is better to invest, and/or how retirement works. The material is not difficult, even if you see it for the first time, because the professor explains it simply and is willing to answer questions all the time.

He often has quuizzes on information that was not lectured on or gives notes on. It is an in person class and can be extremely difficuult to learn considering he talks abouut nothing in class and has youu watch lectures online on your own time.

Great professor, I feel like it would've been better in-person though. Loved his sarcastic humor and he shows real-world examples on material, but it is easy to zone out during online lectures.
