Exams are exactly the information on the outlines she uploads to ANGEL and anything you don't have in your lecture notes can be found in the textbook.

Dr. Hunt is an awesome teacher. I've taken 3 classes with her now. She makes everything really easy with notes and study guides. Going to lecture is helpful but not necessary if you have the book. She's good for recommendations too!

She's nice but she goes through the same annoying spiel every class about putting your cell phones away and keep out of other applications on your laptop. WE GET IT! We don't need to hear it every day. Just because we're in child psych doesn't mean you have to treat us like children. Her examples make no sense, but otherwise she's decent.

Dr. Hunt is cool overall but after the first test, the material and the examples she gives makes you feel like you're in child development rather than learning psych. I understand that the material is relevant but after exam 1 everything got sloppy. I wouldn't recommend the class and her voice is annoying

Dr. Hunt is very knowledgeable in Psychology.  She presents the material in a down-to-earth way.  Her tests are really straightforward and online quizzes are extremely easy (assuming you were in class that day).  Many students complained about the "research participation".  I did not find a problem with it, but it may be something to keep in mind.
My favorite lecturer of all time! She's attentive to any questions, she explains concepts very well and she's hilarious. She could make any class enjoyable!
She was a great teacher. Although, the class was fairly difficult because of the tests. Overall, she kept the class interesting, but it definitely wasn't my favorite class to go to.
You have to go to class in order to get the notes. She has a very nasal voice. mid-terms have 70 questions. She is funny at times. Over all she is Ok, i didn't love her.
Tests are really hard and you're taking down an average of 6-7 pages of notes per day. She doesn't offer any review, only classnotes which are really general. Ruined psychology for me. Don't take it.

Dr Hunt is a decent teacher. She was previously a sex psychologist so she loves talking sex. She's very repetitive, but all in all not a bad teacher. She does respond well to emails. Average psych teacher...nothing special
Excellent teacher! So interesting. In order to do well you have to read the book. She is interesting and so helpful. A very fun class. She is funny!
Loved her, would absolutely recommend her to anyone, she is halarious and knows absolutely everything about what she teaches.

Dr. Hunt is brilliant. Her exams are very hard but if you go to class and listen to her examples, you will do fine. I would reccomend her for Evolutionary Psych but not for Psychology of Learning. She is very evolutionary focused.

Do not take this psychology class unless it's required. The exams are not easy and the material is very boring. Every day is a lecture. Besides exams, the only other assignments include sniffy the virtual rat. I had numerous problems with that thing. The rat was definitely a waste of time- you have to sit and train a rat on your computer.
She is so funny. Cool teacher, really chill and sounds like she  is high sometimes because she has such a soft calming voice, i love it. Shes funny too. Take her if you can

Dr. hunt is really funny, and I had her for developmental psych so I thought this class would be easy as well... its not-the material is realllyyy dry, and the tests are ALL examples.  Besides that, she is a really nice person and a pretty good lecturer.  But pick a different psych class if you dont absolutely have to take this one.

interesting. breaks up notes with stories and studies which are nice. teaches concepts, not just facts. tests are EASY- she practically gives you the answer via study guides. online quizes ensure class attendance, but i skipped frequently and still made an A. lots of extra credit offered.

Dr. Hunt is really cool.  She tries to keep the class involved with jokes and whatnot-gets annoying.  The notes are very straightforward-write down the examples she gives!  The material is not hard to learn so you dont need to study that much- id  recommend getting the book or sharing with a friend. I missed an A- by .03 but wasnt priority class.

In reality, Solo is a 4. He is so nice and teaches the material so well. The other reviews will give you all the positives. BUT, the one negative is he yaps sooooo much. Like to the point where 75 minute lectures could be done in 45 minutes. I understand talking a little bit about yourself and tying it into class, but it gets to a point.

goat. thats it. this class can be so easy if you just pay attention. there were times when it was boring but solo is one of the nicest, funniest, professors ive ever had. actually cares about his students.
Chris is the boy. If you just roll up and pay half attention and do the top hats you getting an A . There are 4 tests and you can just study the night before and be fine they are pretty easy

take solo, one of the BEST profs in Smeal. he cares about his students and sets you for success. just need to put in effort for the homeworks, exams are pretty easy but need to read textbook chapter. group project not bad either. he has guest speakers come in throughout semester which was nice.
The boy! Take the class if u can
absolute brotha man.
Dr Solo is a fantastic professor. Take the honors section if you can for 301. He is very engaging and helpful; you will do just fine in his course

One of the best professors I've had so far. There were 10 total homework which had about a week window to complete and were structured similarly to the exams. The lectures were pretty long but he made up for it with real-world comparisons and funny stories. Also, the honors version of this class includes a group project, unlike the regular class.

High character prof, take the honors section if you can. Homeworks can get long but they're just like the exams so nothing is unexpected. He's good appealing to non-SCM majors and has so much real-world experience to bring into the classroom, making concepts click. Guest speakers are hit or miss - no TopHat those days, so up to you for attendance.

If you can take the honors version of SCM 301 pls take it. Dr. Solo is amazing at what he does, and you actually learn a lot. Brings guest speakers in throughout the sem as a nice change of pace from the material. Tests are on paper, but you get a notecard and similar to the paper HWs, which you have a week to do. You won't regret taking this class

Dr. Solo gives me hope for the future of universities. It was really refreshing to have a no nonsense, disciplined, and down-to-Earth professor; definitely not a pushover (like most other professors). Would highly recommend Solo's honors section to any serious student that wants to learn about what runs his or her life.

My favorite professor--he is amazing. Hilarious, caring, helpful, and kind, even if he is TA-reliant and a bit disorganized. The course is engaging and thorough, and Chris himself is one of the greatest people you will ever meet. You wouldn't catch that man ever speaking a bad word about his wife or his students. Great, great guy.

The dry humor he adds to his lectures make them a lot more engaging. Exam-heavy class but they are very easy. However, make sure to attend every class because if you do not get enough participation questions correct your grade could suffer.

Professor Solo is one of the coolest guys out there. Lectures are funny and engaging, yet when doing problems in class it can go very slowly. 10% of your grade is participation tho so either attend class or make sure you're always on tophat during your class time. Exams were easy, I'd recommend him to anyone.

The Tophat questions are very anxiety inducing during class and you need an 80% for a 100% or else you lose significant points. It is unfair since you can still lose participation points even if you have attended class and legitimately attempted each question. Otherwise, he was decent. Very homework heavy w/ a strict no late work policy.

Solo is an absolute dawg. He cares about what he is teaching and makes you through what you need to do in order to be successful in his class. Only thing is you have to go to class in order to get the tophats.

Professor Solo is by far my favorite professor I've had at Penn State. I would sit in the first few rows every class and by the middle of the semester he already knew me by my first name. I would go to office hours and he was very personable and helpful with homework questions. He even convinced me to change my major to Supply Chain.
SCM was just boring to me, but Professor Solo tried his best to make it as engaging as possible. Exams are only worth 12.5% each, so if you mess up on one you are still good

There's a reason why Solo does not have any bad reviews. This guy is the man and genuinely cares about his students. Lectures can be a bore at times, but gives fair assessments and grading criteria. You can tell that Solo is an actual human and makes an effort to integrate tasteful Dad humor into lectures. Would definitely take his class again.

Very easy and well-organized course. Very straightforward about what's on the exams. Honestly, better than RonJon. Beware of TopHat questions he uses to grade for attendance. They're easy questions though. Exams are on Canvas during your scheduled class time. Easy Pearson HW and easy exams. Also easy and fun extra credit. Definitely recommend.

Had Professor Solo Spring 2022 for SCM 301. Although the lectures were boring, I did really well in the class. It was apparent that he knew what he was talking about. Our tests were not difficult and homework was a little lengthy, but not horrible. Definitely recommend him!

Although the material is pretty boring, solo made up for it with jokes and telling interesting stories. Exams are on canvas and there's maybe an hour of hw per week. The hw is a waste of time, but it's a grade booster. Exams have a lot of word for word questions from lectures so go to every class. Attendance is marked through tophat questions

Awesome professor with a great heart. Would highly recommend him to anyone who has to take SCM 301. Made me want to major in supply chain. He makes class material interesting and relates it to topics we understand.
Solo is an amazing guy. Really cares about his students and often checks to make sure everyone is understanding what he is saying. Go to class, take notes, do the homeworks, you'll be fine for exams.
if you have to take SCM 301, solo is 100% your best bet.

He is so good at teaching, but he teaches very slow. He'll take about 30-40min in the beginning of the class to go over what we already learned. To slow learners, that's good, but I just thought it wasted my time so I barely showed up the class. Class is easy as long as you do your HW and I still ended with an A- when I showed up to 2 classes.
Not always the most exciting class but easy. Show up for attendance. Exams are not hard whatsoever.
Dr solo is great. The class can be boring at times but he tries his best to make it somewhat entertaining. Just go to class and take notes
Very easy class and a great teacher. If u can take him for scm 301 easy A.

Solo is a good teacher and the class is taught well. My one issue with the class was how pointless and time-intensive each homework was. Each hw would consist of 10-12 questions but each question would have at times 10+. The homework never required you to complete hard calculations, but they were always mind-numbing and pointless. HW is busy work.

Dr Solo is one of the kindest, most helpful, and encouraging professors I've ever met. He did a really great job with making the class as interesting and interactive as possible. If you do take him for SCM 301 make sure you go into each class ready to learn and participate, take good notes, read the textbook, and do the homeworks and extra credit!

Simple courses, responsible professors. Pro Solo's class is simple and clear, which reduces the difficulty of this class, and will give specific examples to help understand. The four exams accounted for a total of 50%, homework 40%, 10% participation, and 5% extra credit. If you want to really learn knowledge, choose Solo.

Solo is a good professor. His lectures were good and interactive, even over Zoom. He has a child who is college age so he is very understanding. He cares about his students' success and makes sure that people understand the course content. He also grades participation though an app. We also have MyLab homeworks.

I did not think he was that memorable of a teacher, yet he was very nice and his exams were more on the easy side. Extra credit is great but the homeworks are hard and some info from the homeworks are irrelevant. Some of the material is highly interesting while some is very boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great guy! Go to class to fill in the course packet, do the homework and extra credit, and go to the review sessions before exams and you will be fine. His exams are very straightforward and don't try to trick you. His lectures can be boring, but he's a genuine guy and wants everyone to succeed. Cracks a few dad jokes too. Take him if you can!!

This is one of the easiest introductory Smeal classes. He describes everything in detail & is a great professor. He moves pretty slow & the lectures are very boring. If you go and fill out the notes, do all the HW and extra credit, it is such an easy A. He does a "review" before each exam & tells you what to know. Take him for 301, no one else!!!

Solo is a solid professor. SCM is known to be difficult and he helps by giving several bonus opportunities. I did not read and just studied other peoples quizlets. Reading would help but I found it too boring. Classes are all lectures. Only negative is he never finishes early and goes from bell to bell.

60 percent exams 40 percent homework for final grade. Cant really beat that when the homework is straightforward and he tells you everything you need to know in the lectures. Great guy, funny, and really tries to make connections with students. Dude is heaven compared to some of the other SCM teachers, couldn't ask for anything more.

solo is dope because he rlly cares about his students doing well if you go to his office hours to prep for exams or review exams it helps clear up a lot for a subject that is pretty boring he makes class interesting and fun and tests are always pretty fair at the end of class before a test he also tells you exactly what to study def recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Solo is actually the homie. If you go to his lectures and pay attention you will pass his class with flying colors. His exams aren't hard at all, usually pretty straight forward with a couple tricky ones. He is always available for office hours or even to talk to about majors. One of my favorite professors I have taken at PSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Solo is one of my favorite at Penn State so far and made me confident in my decision to purse a Supply Chain major. Go to class, do the homework and the extra credit and you'll do well.

LOVE solo! he's the best prof out of all the scm 301 classes... he tells you exactly what you need to study for exams and the homeworks are straight-forward and helpful. def take him if you have the chance

Hands down the best professor I've had at Penn State. He makes what would be a really dry and boring class, super easy and interesting. He actually cares about his students and takes the time giving multiple examples. Try to do really good on the first exams and do hw and extra credit and you'll be able to get a 50% on the final and still get an A.

Solo is an amazing professor who truly cares about his students. You don't need the textbook, but will need access to MyOMLab for homework and Extra Credit. DO ALL EXTRA CREDIT, as it is easy and will help your grade. Exams aren't bad if you pay attention through some dry material. I literally needed a 33% on the final to get an A in this class.
The classes are pretty boring and the 4 exams are okay, but with the homework and the extra credit it is easy to get an A

AMAZING professor. The material is so boring and dry but he makes it less dull with his amazing personality. Do the extra credit and do well on the exams in the beginning and you can chill later. Don't buy the textbook, waste of money. Overall amazing professor, highly recommend him

do well on the first few exams, get perfects on homework (few math problems & textbook definitions), attempt extra credit and you will be able to relax on the last exam. The material is not hard - i would study in the same way you would for RonJon's Mgmt301 class.
This guy is an utter beast.

I hated scm 301. it's vague. the class is so boring I paid half attention so I read the textbook and MYOM LAB helps. my friend has sees and she doesn't use it. he shares personal stories and cracks jokes to keep the class alive. gives lots of examples and seems to want us to succeed but the class material kills me, calculations can get complicated

Very nice guy, make sure you read the book for his exams because there's stuff on it that he doesn't cover in class so depth, and will be on the exam. Take all the extra credits, you get the points just for trying. Also, use the "study plan"on myomlab for quizzes and extra homework problems that will definitely help on the exam!!!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Solo is a great guy. Just show up to class and do the work and you'll walk out with an A.
Amazing ability to teach. Come to office hours for help and to review your test. MIS 204 is a better class to take freshman or sophomore year.
Favorite Smeal Professor. Great guy keeps the material engaging in a tricky class. Helped me a lot during my internship process. As long as you put in the work you will succeed.

Dr. Solo is a great professor who truly wants his students to succeed. Getting an A in his class is definitely manageable if you use all resources he gives. There are no surprises on his exams and he is extremely helpful and welcoming in office hours. He also provides several homework and extra credit opportunities to help your grade.

Multiple extra credit opportunities. Gives multiple examples in class to ensure you get the material. Always talks about how he is available for office hours and the exams are completely doable if you read the text, go over his examples and look at the online lab quizzes.

This was his first semester teaching SCM 301 and it was okay. 1st and 3rd exams were difficult. Homeworks weren't bad. Definitely read the book. Dude doesn't match up his slides with the course packet so don't even bother buying it, use your laptop and take notes on there otherwise you'll be writing 25 slides worth of info in the margins.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Solo is by far the best professor I have had at Penn State. He truly wants his students to succeed and if you are willing to put in the extra hours to understand the material an "A" is very reasonable. I highly reccomend taking one of his classes, in SCM 421 he was able to incorporate real life problems that will only help you in the work place
If you go to class and work hard on the homework assignments, it's an easy A for anyone who doesn't hate MIS.

Prof. Solo is one of the best professor I have in Penn State so far. He truly cares about you and gives you the best advice in the process of the course. He would try to help you and gives you the best he can offer if any odd situation occurs (weird situation is often in this computer-based class). Just pay attention in class, A is there for you.

I believe this is his first semester but I definitely lucked out getting Dr. Solo. He is always willing to help and teaches us very relevant Excel skills. He also gives very fair exams- if you know what is going on in class and keep up with the work you can get a 100% on all of them. I feel so much more prepared for my internship this summer. TAKE!
He's a great semester and I loved going to class! He is always available to help you, the exams and homeworks are really easy.  He's the best prof. for MIS 204!! Definitely take his class!!

He is a really great professor. While attendance is mandatory you only have to go 75% of the time to get full credit. His exams are easy if you pay attention in class and have good notes, as his exams are open note. He also isn't hard when grading which I appreciate. I am taking another class with him next semester because I liked him so much.

This was the most unprofessional professor in my four years at Penn State. His guidelines were often unclear, and the criteria for assignments change each class, making it difficult to know what was expected. Participation was strict missing more than three classes resulted in an automatic letter-grade deduction. He's opinionated and narcissistic.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Attendance was graded, but only needed to be there 75% of the time for full credit. There were six writing assignments throughout the semester, but they were spread out nicely and graded nicely. There were 4 exams, they are online in class, and you could use notes and the PowerPoint lectures; there was no final.

He is a cool guy however his class is just really confusing. He is always willing to help but sometimes you're just on your own. Class is only graded by a few things which kinda sucks. Be prepared for absolutely everything in the class to revolve around 3 textbooks. Have to say he's a nice and funny guy, but painfully boring class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a great professor! He cares about his students and he loves his job. He try his best to make the lectures enjoyable. I learned a lot from his lectures. I took his LHR 100 and it is a decently easy class. High recommend! (I checked LHR 304 cuz for some reason this website won't let me post my review until I select that)

Took his LHR100 class and was super easy. If you show up ready to take notes, you are pretty much set. That does mean you have to go to class but the exams are open notes. Only grades are exams and 3 other assignments so almost no homework with the trade-off of showing up to class and taking notes.

He follows the textbook like its gospel, which sucks because it's hard and boring to read. Attendance is mandatory except for 2 freebies, but those can count towards sick days, and he has it written in the syllabus that if you miss a certain percentage of classes he'll outright fail you. Essay instrs. are often vague yet considerably difficult.

Professor Stephens is great. I urge you to ignore the lower ratings because he is one of the best professors I have had. He is funny and cares about his students, and if you get to know him he is a great guy. I was very shocked to see the other ratings, but I can assure you that you will not regret taking his course!
lectures teach you nothing. reading heavy. I recommend taking it over the summer or else you have to take it with him.

He only has a few assignments. 4 activities, 1 exam and the final, a group project, and a major paper. He is an ok grader but the tests dont teach you much, just memorization of the topics at hand. I dont think I have ever taken an memorization essay test before. He is very passionate about the topics and overall chill guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Stephens is a wonderful professor! He's a very chill guy and really cares about his students. Lectures are easy to follow and his vast knowledge of course content is impressive. He gives thoughtful feedback to students' questions and designates class time to discuss content from readings. Easily one of my favorite professors at PSU!

Entirely discussion based with few graded assignments (all easy). Expect to read 5 books in the semester, complete a group presentation, and write a 5 page analysis of a book of your choosing. Easy, fun, good prof.

This class is targeted towards non chem/science majors who have to take a physical science and that is exactly how it was structured. Danny is super caring and always willing to help. While the lectures were sometimes long, Danny is super passionate about what he is teaching and the content focuses on environmental chem which was super interesting.

Super nice prof but the grading system was a bit weird. GO TO CLASS. At the end of each class you have a graded activity that sums to most of your grade. There is no homework other than 4 readings. However, the lectures are very boring and the activities don't relate. If you ask for help on an activity, he is always ready and willing to help.

Supercool chem+lit interdomain w/ fascinating lectures (not much need to take notes, favorite part of the class), entertaining books, easy group discussions. Pick a solid group for the group presentation, stay on top of readings/papers, and mind what he says in discussions/feedback for writing papers. Having a final was unexpected, but it went fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Sykes was really a great professor. I think 227 was the first time that a lot of people needed to put a lot more effort to be successful, but Sykes himself is awesome. Ask him if you need help and spend lots of time with the material making connections about meanings, not just knowing steps. He genuinely wants everyone to succeed.
Hard class, good professor. Don't fall behind and you can do just fine!
The course takes a lot of time but the instructional team is friendly. The content is not conceptually difficult but the exams are intimidating.

Took this class as a fourth year due to scheduling issues. Wasn't the easiest or the hardest chem class I've ever taken. Dr. Sykes is a great teaching professor and is able to convey difficult concepts well. Lab reports were unfortunately hand-written and because of this took awhile to do.

There is nothing more intimidating than walking into CHEM 227 on your first day, but youll come to find out that its very manageable. While theres a lot of homework and very difficult, Dr. Sykes made this class fun. The lab reports are terrible as you hand write about 100 pages throughout the semester. tests are hard so study hw and study guides

This class starts really hard and intimidating but turned into my favorite class. Dr. Sykes cares about his students and the subject he's teaching. He is very knowledgeable but sometimes doesn't understand that not everyone is on the same level as him.

Dr. Sykes and Dr. B did a great job acquainting us chemistry majors with the college and the resources available to us. Dr. Sykes is a great professor and advisor and is definitely willing to help you with scheduling and planning for whatever you need. Even if you don't need to take the first year seminar, I would still recommend it.

Chem 227 does not have hard topics, but the workload makes it the hardest chem course at PSU. Dr. Sykes was very accessible outside of class and he's really helpful and a very caring professor. I thought that the lectures were informative, but the issue was that there was way too much extra information. Hand-wrote 70 pages in the lab notebook...
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--So many papers

reviews.comment: Plenty of help outside of class.

Dr. Sykes was a fantastic professor who cared and wanted us to succeed. I recommend going to lecture because we worked on problems in class which really helped with understanding the material because we discussed them together. When reviewing for exams redo the HW problems. Exam problems can be challenging since he will put new, unseen problems.

Dr. Sykes is a genuinely caring guy. He really cares fro his students, and he wants to see us succeed. Chromatography is a tough course, but if you put in the effort, he'll put the effort in to help! My main issue with him is that he talks so quietly.
Dr. Sykes gave good information on how to succeed as a chemistry major. Hes a good guy. Seems to care about his students.

I really enjoyed Dr. Sykes, however, he is tough. He expects a lot out of his students and doesn't always give them everything. His exams were a challenge but in the end, you learn more from them because they were. Sometimes I felt his lectures could have been more productive with doing problems instead but the homework sessions are a must!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He is probably the worst lecturer I've had. His idea of teaching was giving the CA's worksheets to have us do and then leave the class. When he did lecture it was either him talking about slides and writing equations on the board for about twenty min. or going through random problems on the board. The homework was hard and so were the exams.
Dr. Sykes, is great professor. Hands down the best I had at PSU. He made analytical chemistry interesting and inspired me to pursue it in graduate school.

Dr Sykes is the best of the instructors for Chem 110 despite being new to the course. The course is tough, and grades in the course are based heavily off of the 3 tests and final, while recitation, quizes, and ALEKS are used to pad your grades. Dr Sykes occasionally gets stuck on a tangent, but is usually focused and occasionally funny.
He seems like a very nice guy, but sometimes messed up example problems or demonstrations.
He is a nice professor but Chem 110 is a hard class so I didn't go to most of the classes.

Dr Sykes is new to lecturing lower level chemistry material.  For our class, this meant that for the first twothirds of the semester, attending lectures meant listening to a verbatim read-through of a power point presentation. Once he got in the hang of Chem 110, and began incorporating more practice problems into class, everything improved.

He's just great. This was his first year teaching this class (got demoted from the higher-level stuff, apparently), but he did a great job, since he knows his stuff. He always made good connections to non-chem things in his lectures. He's really sweet and pretty bad at demos, and also the class itself SUCKS. But, I'd take another class with him.
Best chem professor ever! Get to know him, and you'll see how much he cares that you get as much from the course as possible.

I have taken several courses with him and I have learned more in those courses than all other courses combined. He cares about the subject, cares that you learn what's important (in future careers, not just exams), and structures the class in a way that your grade accurately reflects how hard you worked. Yeah, it's hard, but you learn and it's fair

This was his first time teaching chem110. He really wants his students to do well. He's always ahead schedule so we review alot for exams which is good because the review is somewhat similar to the exam. I went to his office hours a few times and he helps you alot. Very sweet, down to earth professor! Highly recommend him for chem110!

Dr. Skyes is a genuinely good guy.  This was his first year teaching CHEM 110 and he is doing an amazing job so far.  His lectures are helpful and clear-cut.  He plays music before class and he keeps class funnyinteresting.  Overall helpful and I highly recommend him as a professor for CHEM 110 in the Chemistry Dept.

Dr. Sykes is a really awesome teacher. He really makes class interesting and gets involved with the students during class. He also really wants his students to pass. He gives us so many great opportunities to do well in the class. He is also really funny so you don't get too bored during lecture. Overall, I highly recommend him!
Even though I hated Chem, Sykes was the reason I went to class every day. He can be kind of unorganized, but this was his first year teaching Chem 110 so I can cut him some slack.

I took a few chemistry courses with Dr Sykes and he is by far the best professor I have ever had. He teaches with such passion for the subject and seems to have never ending knowledge on every topic possible. He is a remarkable professor
favorite class and professor! so cool, so clear, so smart, and easy to earn grades if worked as he instructed. very straightforward and useful materials taught!

My favorite professor at PSU, by far. The way his class is set up, you get the grade you work for. The exams are not weighted too heavy, so there's less stress. This class made me love chemistry. Dr. Sykes is very approachable and helpful outside of class. The lectures were organized and straight-forward, and Dr. Sykes is extremely fair.

Dr. Sykes: Great guy. Joy to be around and his jokes are pretty funny in class. This was my most demanding class because it required about 10-12 hrs per week on homework and about 5 for the lab notebook. If you did the homework there is no need to study for the exams because if you can do his problem sets, you can do the test. A+ quality professor

Lectures were extremely boring and hard to follow.  Most learning done outside the classroom or in lab with the TA's. A lot of extra credit given out at the end of the semester. Don't kill yourself over this class in the beginning he makes it sound a lot harder than the class really is.

Very friendly and approachable.  Most explanation outside of class was handled by TAs, but he was helpful and fielded in-class questions well.  Lecture problems and activities count for a lot of points, be sure to attend!  Labs were sometimes disorganized, but overall useful and informative.

Not hard, but a lot of work.  Lecture problems and quizzes almost every class.  Disorganized class, the assignments he gives are sometimes not relavant to what he is teaching. Very flexible, extends due dates if the entire class complains. A lot of outside work, for special project. ok class, I wouldnt' reccomend taking it unless it is required.

He's very nice, but not very organized and where there were problems with some of the labs it often seemed as if he didn't even know how things worked himself. Overall though, very nice... some of the stuff in the class was new so perhaps the organizational issues will fix themselves.

He ruined this class for me. He knows nothing and yet is extremely arrogant. Grades are completely subjective. He tries to be friends with students to make up for crappy lectures and no organization. Tries to make students feel stupid for his own mistakes. I can't believe this guy is in 2 departments. He is ruining Penn State science.

His grades are biased, so if he doesn't like you, watch out!  He's pompous and thinks he's brilliant but he's far from it.  He's not even trained as a chemist, he's a geologist!  He took an important class to chemistry majors and ruined it.  He retaught physics 212 and 214 instead of teaching how to operate and troubleshoot the instrments.

In this class Sykes will assign you a project that will advance his career, but that he knows nothing about. For our project, we had to go meet with a guy who worked on Science Park Road and was more disorganized than Sykes himself to get him to do our project.
Quite disorganized in class but I dont know why that I love him to death.
He was not very easily understood because he didn't seem to know what he was talking about. Very nice guy though.
The FRIENDLIEST professor at PSU!  He will help you with anything.  He may be disorganized, but he's extremely funny and personable.  Great guy to know.
No Comments

I am done with chem, but I took chem 13 a long time ago over a summer, and had Sykes.  The class keeps you on edge about your grade, but at the end you end up passing somehow.  Its one of those classes you just have to get through and Sykes makes it palitable.
homework counts for most of your grade--do the homework and you will get an A even if u dont study for the tests.  he is very helpful if u ask and gives lots of bonus points.

Dr. sykes is extreemly easy if you go to the S.I. for homework answers. He is a nice guy who gives a lot of bonus. His lectures are hard to understand. Read the book and go to S.I. and you will do well.

Hate chemistry just need this for a pre-req. Nice guy but very disorganized. Can fail tests and pass with hwk. Go to extra help in resource room learn more there then in class, plus good grade on hwk. Chem 13 is a pain in the ass class you need it for no reason, gives extra credit always a plus.
Sykes is seriously a good man.  Good teacher for chem too.  He knows chem sucks and tries to help you out whenever possible.  Good guy.
when hes in charge of the way the class goes its hard to fail, homework counts for most of the grade and hes really nice. *THIS CLASS WONT NECESSARILY BE TEH SAME WITH HIM IN FUTURE SEMISERS*
No Comments

Seems nice and tries to be funny, but fails to connect with students.  There are no practice exams, lectures are disorganized and redundant, and his examples are full of mistakes.  You'd think he'd never seen the lecture materials before in his life.  Sadly, CHEM13 is required for many majors.

This class sux, but the prof. is so nice!  What other prof do u know that buy u a beer after a major test?  Chem 13 students need to learn its not this professor's fault you did poorly.  Open notes and open book tests!  Very helpful in answering questions and is almost always available.

Dr. Sykes spent time covering material that he even told the class would not be covered on  tests.  It is evident he tries to teach, but reading the book thoroughly and doing practice tests is key to obtain a good grade in his classes
Very poor
horrible teacher. Made a lot of mistakes in his lectures, and spent a lot of time on stuff that wasn't on the exam.
No Comments

Dr. C always makes his class meetings fun and enjoyable. He cares for his students and tries to make sure everyone understands the material. His humor and many office hours ensure that his students always have a fun time while learning Physics.

Super helpful to struggling students, but fairly regular otherwise. He offers lots of help outside of class and always comes around the room to help with the TA's. If you took physics in high school, this isn't too much harder than that. Lots of work though.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. C is kinda the goat. The course material itself can be tough at times, but I didn't really care because Costantino is just a chill guy. For some reason, I can't hate him or the course.

The mandatory homework and the other practice materials he provides are the best way to prepare for his course. His lectures are mostly focused on solving problems rather than explaining the topics at a conceptual level, so it is massively helpful to look through the textbook or learn the concepts yourself before class.

His class is ok. You get a homework every week, 3 tests which can be hard, and a final. He doesn't teach you much though. Personally I had to really learn everything myself as I just didn't find he lectures helpful. This class was very bipolar. He was mid.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Costantino is a good professor. He teaches a hard class, but he does a good job of explaining the content. He gives partial credit on the exams. He utilizes a free online textbook. Each week is structured the same, with 1-2 pre class videos, pre class notes, and a pre class quiz, as well as one homework assignment that is about 15 questions.

Great guy and loves to make jokes. The class is difficult, but he prepares you to succeed. Just show up and do the work and you'll pass this weed out class. Equation sheet could be a little more organized.
He was very good at keeping you engaged in the lectures and was helpful if you went to office hours to review test material or just needed some help. Loved cracking stupid jokes as well.

Dr C is a good professor he just teaches a tough class. All the people complaining are just too lazy to put any outside work in so they did bad but won't take accountability. He is very passionate in lecture, but expects you to read and watch preclass videos because he skims over content and spends most of the time doing example problems.

I didn't learn a single thing in this class. The exams were not like the samples, the provided equation sheet was pointless, and the problems were worded horrendously. I tried numerous tutoring sessions for help just to get by and I still couldn't pass a single exam. I do not recommend.

This class sucked every last bit of life out me. The exams are only 15 questions so if you get 1 question wrong that's practically an entire letter grade off. He hardly explains anything. Everything I knew in this class was based off my prior knowledge from physics in high school. This class is so unnecessarily difficult and needs to be rewritten.

Great professor, but tough classes. It can be tempting to skip lectures, but if you watch the preclass videos and go to lecture regularly, you will succeed.  Can be tempting to ChatGPT the ExpertTA homework as well, but it is really one of the best ways to study for the exams. If you follow the way Dr. C has the class set up, you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Costantino is amazing, you can tell how passionate he is and how much he wants students to succeed. Explains things very well and is incredibly helpful if you meet with him 1-on-1. Lectures are mostly spent doing practice problems so watch the videos.

He is very accessible outside of class. Practice exams are indicative of actual exams so I would recommend studying those. I would also watch the pre-class videos rather than read the textbook, they are much more helpful.
I would take a different course if you can. The lectures were nothing like the homeworks and it was hard to learn. I had a different learning style than how he teaches.
This was the worst physics class I have taken. It wasn't my
Very nice down-to-earth and fun guy. Made class fun. Didn't give out too much homework, he made the concepts easy to understand. Would recommend for sure.

Dr. C is an enthusiastic and caring professor who makes a tough course manageable. Attend lectures, use the provided resources like exam reviews, and try unstuck AI for extra study prep - you'll do well!

Good guy, but the lectures can be unrelated to the tests. Still show up because he'll drop some random tech that'll be very useful on the tests (which there are four of). A test may get dropped, so don't freak if your grade is dropping. Don't read the textbook. Spam the practice tests. Make sure to sign up for the extra credit quizzes.

As someone whose high school did not teach Physics, this class is challenging. Lectures are somewhat disorganized and hard to follow. What I found most helpful was going over practice problems in the lecture, as they are very similar to exam questions. Exams are much easier than homework/labs/recitation. Dr. C is very caring, definitely talk to him

He is a great and caring individual but makes lectures and videos a lot more complicated than it really is. At the end of the day this is a freshman level class and he makes it a lot more complicated than it really looks.

Always asks his students how their day is going as they walk in. Extremely helpful during office hours and questions after class. Super nice guy overall and grades pretty kindly. I would take him for all my physics classes if I could.

Went to class in the beginning but I was not learning much. Prelecture videos are the exact lecture. I stopped going to class and only watched the videos. I looked up all the HW and did not put much time into any of the material they gave us. Instead I used liontutors and had over 100% in the class before the final. Definitely invest in liontutors.

Went to first lecture, never watched any video reviews or anything. Did sample tests day before each exam and got 85 avg on exams. Professor is a great guy that is very understanding and easy to work. Overall similar to Ap physics but with with some calc + more complex conceptual problems.

Dr. C is the GOAT, you can tell how passionate he is. Lectures are mostly spent doing practice problems so watch the pre-class videos. He is incredibly helpful during office hours, explains things amazingly well 1-on-1. HW and lab make up a good chunk of grade but exams are still very important. Lots of resources for studying and practice provided.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Costantino is the best you can get for PHYS211 at Penn State.  Enthusiastic lecturer, very willing to help, very present in office hours and Canvas to provide assistance.  Labs felt unnecessary but recitations and homeworks were helpful, and you should absolutely plan to put the time in and attend exam GSGs.

Dr. C does his best to make his lectures engaging even with boring content. He is always willing to help online or in office hours, and provides plenty of resources for success. If you go to the exam reviews (which will be around 3 hours long), and do the practice exams, you should do well in this course.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Extremely accessible and one of the most caring teachers I have ever had; he wants you to do well. It can be a difficult class but if you need help he is always available for his students.
The course itself is hard but Dr.C in general is a good person!

Great guy and readily available but the material is horrendously organized and hard to understand without prior physics knowledge (though this is more of a problem with the department than him). Exams and labs are out of the scope of the notes so I'd figure them out from someone who's taken the class. I'd be more worried about my TAs than him.

This guy is great. Definitely one of my favorite professors. He is always very available. If you have an issue, you can either talk to him in person, or ask him on email, or ask him on Piazza (a website he uses). I would definitely recommend him.

Incredibly chill guy. You can tell he's really knowledgeable and cares a lot about his students. He's especially helpful during office hours. He makes a lot of deadpan jokes during lectures which helps keep them engaging. You need to watch pre-class videos to get the notes, since you just do practice problems in class, but it isn't a big deal.

I won't lie: PHYS212 is an extremely difficult course. However, Dr. C does a phenomenal job of making it as easy as it can be. He is totally dedicated to your success and is a fantastic teacher and resource. He makes excruciatingly difficult and boring material fun and enjoyable, but you will still need to do a lot of work.
The exam is easy, no more difficult than the homework
Had him for 211 and 212, fantastic professor. Always goes out of his way to help. How many profs host like 15 hours of office hours during finals week?

Costantino is the worst prof in penn state. he makes lessons hard to follow, explains horribly, and assumes you understand everything without much explanation. he's the only reason why the phys dept has a terrible reputation. words can't describe how little i enjoy his class. his LA's who've taken phys212 online with other profs say he can't teach.

Lectures were extremely boring. The 2 hour lectures were sleep inducing. He goes too fast in lectures and if you don't attend office hours or already know physics already, makes it nearly impossible to keep up with whats being taught.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Nice man, always gives many office times to students! The class itself is hard for the people who don't learn anything before. It needs more hard working.

I heavily disliked this course but I didn't entirely dislike Dr. C. He was always available to answer any questions and his office hours were very helpful. However, his lectures were very boring and it is very easy to get lost in what is being taught. Get help early on or you will struggle.

Very good professor for such a difficult class. Goes through rows before each lecture asking if anyone has any questions. He brings a lot of props to class as examples. Exams are extremely difficult and you will have to put in at least 10 hours of studying for each one. Lab, Hw, recitation, and EC help boost your grade after exams.

Costantino is a good professor that explains things very thoroughly, and is always happy to clarify a part of a problem. The grading for 211 was pretty lenient so even though I'm not the best at physics I still got an A.
Very good professor; he allows us to answer some questions via top hat to check our understanding. The materials he posts on canvas are super helpful.
Lectures are not helpful. I only learned from my TA's in lab and recitation. Homework is long and difficult.
He's an awful prof. Explanations don't make sense. Literally going to class is a waste of time, I haven't learnt a single thing from him all semester.

Pretty good prof. Lots of interesting demos. Tests are 20 MCQ and pretty easy if you know what you are doing. HW takes about 2 hours per week. There are also 2 pre-lecture videos per week, around 10-20 min each. Labs and recitations are easy. As long as you are working the whole time you get an A. If you took AP physics in HS this is an easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class itself is very challenging but Dr. C really cares for his students and does everything he can to make sure everyone does their best. As long as you're willing to put work into this class, you should do fine.

He is a perfectly nice person, just not one who teaches well. Hes very slow when going through examples, to the point that it sometimes took him half an hour to finish a simple mechanics problem. It was an easy class though. Theres no real calculus involved in PHYS 211.

Before class Dr Constantino makes you watch a pre lecture video and then when you get to class he explains nothing of what was covered and jumps straight into example problems. Then when the exam comes around the questions on the exam are nothing like the problems he did in class. All around his lectures are not helpful.

Costantino is a pretty experienced professor. He is very professional and helps any student who needs help. Since he teaches Physics the course is obviously super tough, but if you put in the work it is not too stressful. The tests are super hard, so you have to know your stuff. Also, there is a Lab, Rec, Pre-Class, and HW due every week.

Professor Costantino is a decent lecturer. His notes can be a bit confusing but he gets the concepts across well enough. This is a very hard course but he still taught well enough so that I understood the concepts. Definitely read the textbook before class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. C is an excellent example of why the physics department at Penn State has a bad reputation. He is a cold and quite frankly arrogant individual who quite clearly became a professor to experience a power trip. I currently have above a 95% in the course and can genuinely say I very infrequently benefited from his presentation of material.

Dr C was probably the worst professor I've ever had in my life. He expected everyone to know calc and all of the intro to physics so he never goes in depth with explaining. During the lectures he just does problems and doesn't show how to do them, and you're basically only graded on 3 tests and a final. DO NOT TAKE DR. C FOR PHYS211!!!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is very nice and doesn't mind (even discourages) questions. I'm a big fan and I ask like 4 questions per lecture between 250 students without feeling discouraged. The labs and recitation are very mercifully graded, and there is only one long online homework and two very short Pre Lecture assignments per week.

I did not take physics 211 with Dr. C, however it was not hard to understand what he expected from you as a student. Physics 212 is definitely hard and you will need to put in a lot of extra work to do well. Dr. C is very helpful as he is willing to help you as long as you are willing to reach out and ask him. Getting a good TA is also key.

I had Dr. C for 211 And 212. The thing is that he is very boring and hard to pay attention to, but also very nice, very understanding, and everything besides the exams are easy to get good grades on. So what Im saying is you probably wont learn anything but you can pass anyway.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I respectfully think he is the worst prof I've ever had. Terrible teacher, I taught myself everything I learned. worked my butt off for a B-. Don't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. C. is very consistent. You know exactly what you are expected of. If you had 211 with Dr. C., 212 is exactly the same. The tests are fair. There are tons of TAs/LAs, and Dr. C. is available very often in Piazza or office hours.

Dr. Costantino is an amazing professor, but PHYS211 is designed in a way where you need to have good study habits. I can see how the lectures would be hard to process for some, but Dr. Costantino holds regular office hours that are extremely helpful. Extra credit is also offered in the form of a pre/post quiz at the beginning and end of semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: In the nicest way possible, this is the worst teacher I've ever had. I tried to hire a tutor but after taking one look at the practice exam he quit because the material was "ridiculous" . Save yourself a lot of stress crying and avoid Dr C.
Dr. C is a great professor and is very respectful, professional, and polite. He explains everything well and is always happy to help.

He is the worst teacher Ive had in all my years as a student. Very cold and unavailable. He offers no help outside of his office hours sessions. Lab/Recitations are useless due to their content & grade weight. To pass, you will need to teach yourself everything. Lectures are just reading off PowerPoints and are unhelpful. Pick a different prof.

Dr. C is a solid physics professor. Physics is a difficult course for most people, but Dr. C provides many review and practice opportunities and is an avid user of piazza, where he posts solutions to the practice exam problems. He does do a lot of practice problems rather than notes. But his pre-class videos provide good intros to the material.

Dr.C was by far the worst professor I've had. While he is easily accessible, he was not very helpful when I would go. When asking for different ways to study, his only response is "do more problems." Plus, the avg on the final was a 55% so that only reflects on the poor quality of his teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought this class was as hard as everyone says until finals week came. I went to Dr C's review sessions, I went to his office hours, and I did all 3 sample exams. The final ended up saving my grade. Dr C formats this class identically to PHYS 211; the only difference is the material. He will help you as long as you reach out to him.

This class is a breeze if you took AP Physics 1. If not, you can still do well by staying on top of the HW, which helps you learn a LOT more than Dr. C's lectures. After all, there's only so many problems Dr. C can do in class. He uses clickers, so get ready for that. He also offers review sessions where he'll do problems that students request.

I had Dr. C for 211 as well, but was able to coast because it was so similar to high school level physics. Not the case for 212. You have to work your butt off to get a good grade in the class. Dr. C is nice and does his best to help especially on exam reviews, but not even he (or his dad jokes) can save you. Try taking 212 at a community college.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is terrible at teaching, but YouTube really helped me get an A in this class. If you do the practice tests and understand the concepts behind each question then you'll do well on the tests which is basically the only part that matters in that class. If you need help, then ask some of your friends because he won't make much sense. Good luck.

Honestly the only saving grace is that the tests are mostly concept based, which makes the grades better. Other than that, good luck learning anything from the lectures, I did most of my learning the day before the test by rereading the slides and doing the practice tests online. The class is doable, but youll really need to work for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Phys 211 is not an easy class but isn't too bad. Costantino is a decent professor but sometimes seems to overcomplicate things. Decent lectures, wouldn't mind taking him again
No offense but Costantino simply sucks. If you didn't have good physics teacher in high school, you're likely to get a B or C in the class. He doesn't do his job right. He SUCKS
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Worst decision ever to take physics 211 with him if you dont have and prior knowledge about physics

Dr. C is great, he knows his stuff and does his best to teach the material. Labs, recitations, and homework make passing possible because the exams are really difficult, obviously. Office hours are throughout the week and are the best way to learn out of lecture, he also takes his own exams to grant students partial credit which goes a long way.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: This class is about as hard as people say it is. If you can, take at a community college over summer. Dan tries but honestly, it's not in his power to make the class much easier. I got lucky and got a good TA, they will be your friends through this. If you put in a lot of work you should survive, but I consider my grade more luck than knowledge

Dr. C would be the greatest physics professor in the world if he was able to teach in a classroom of 30-40 students. Unfortunately, in a lecture of 300 people, the material is very rushed and hard to understand. Definitely need to do the notes on your own from the slides on canvas and come to class for the clicker points and just pay attention.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. C is a great, quirky guy and explains everything step-by-step to make sure everyone understands. PHYS 211 is not easy though. The online homework can be difficult and confusing, but most of the time is bearable. Lectures are good as long as you go over the slides multiple times, which he posts on Canvas. It was tough, but its doable.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Costantino was a really nice guy who cared a lot about his students, but lectures were usually over complicated and at times hard to understand. Not a bad class overall with a lot of easy points through lab, recitations, and hw, but tests will be difficult if you dont fully understand the concepts.

He really cares about his students, but phys211 is no joke at psu. Tests are really different from HW problems, if you don't understand the real concepts, you will drown pretty quick. But passing the course is easy if you do HW, recitations, and labs regularly.

Dr. Costantino is a very nice guy, and he is also very knowledgable about physics. However, having class with 250 other students doesn't allow for a more personal connection to the professor. While recitations and labs are mandatory and ran by TA's, I often times found the TA's talking down to me because they knew more than me. Overall, not great.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. C is incredibly knowledgeable on his field of study as should be but he doesnt always do a great job at explaining the subject material. But he makes a genuine attempt to explain the material for his students and will give those who desire the time to explain in greater detail after class or in office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. C is a good professor under tough circumstances. His lectures can feel fast-paced and confusing, but 211 is a tough class and massive lectures are the only way that the PSU can teach everyone that has to take it each semester. Go to his office hours if you need help; Dr. C is very knowledgeable and provides good answers to one-on-one questions.

Dr. Costantino is overall a very nice guy, but prepare to be bored in his lectures. Paying attention was very hard for me because he wasn't the most interesting guy. I understood the material well but found myself skipping class often. He explains things fairly well, but lacks the ability to keep students' attention in my opinion.

Dr. C is a solid teacher. That said, he can be disruptive when kids are trying to complete in class problems due to his incessant checking if they have any questions. You will learn a lot from his class too. There will certainly be a thumbs up in the middle for his class!

Great guy but tends to over complicate problems. Lectures are fast and confusing and overall he just can't teach large classes effectively. Homework labs and recitations saved my grade in this class, exams are difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Dr. C is very knowledgable and truly cares for the students. That being said, I think he is not very capable of explaining concepts in different ways if you are not understanding it how he has already presented it. He will just repeat the exact explanation from lecture but he tries which counts. TAs in this class are terrible and LAs do nothing.

Dr. C is amazing. Sometimes he moves too fast when explaining and you feel lost and frustrated but he really cares about his students. If you go to office hours he will do everything in his power to help you. He's a great guy, his tests are fair, and he tries his best. Not the easiest class but I couldn't ask for more from a professor.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. C is extremely helpful. Whenever you are struggling, deff go to his hours office. Always willing to help his students. It is a hard class. It may look easy in the beginning, but you have to study if want to get the grade you want. One of the nicest professors I had. Deff take him if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: He seems like a nice guy. But class is a joke and he cannot explain the material on a level for you to understand. Also equation sheet is very confusing and not helpful. Practice exams didn't help and were not like exams. Exams were very difficult. Lots of credit given besides exam.

Dr. C is one of the kindest, warmhearted professors I've ever had, however he does a poor job of explaining material in simple terms. This is supposed to be an easy A but I really struggled in this class, more so than I did in orgo chem. The material seems to just stick for some and not for others.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I don't recommend him at all!!! It is a big class but I don't think he can actually handle it. He makes everything more confusing than it is supposed to be. I am doing good in this class is only because I took phys in high school.  I mean he is a really nice teacher and he is always trying to help, but I just can't stand the way he teaches.

This is the most boring class I've taken at Penn State. But Dr. C does his job well, he's low key funny, and always tries to help. Obviously, some things aren't in his hands as the class is huge. But for the part that I've needed him, he's been there.

Course structure itself takes the fun out of Physics, Dr. C however is extremely helpful. Homework and Exams are WAY different than lectures. you must dedicate a lot of your time on practicing questions on practice exams and masteringphysics, therefore, i won't recommend taking this course as part of 15+ credits schedule.  Recitation and lab? easy.

Costantino is a very good professor. He is enthusiastic about physics and he is very helpful. Phys 211 can be a really hard class but if you have to take it, take it with him. He constantly asks if anybody has questions in class, and has a wide availability of office hours. tests can be hard, especially the final!

Phys211 is not too bad. Costantino is an alright teacher. Go through lectures when posted online. 3 tests-not the easiest. If you put in the work you can do well. Online hwk, textbook may depend on what type of student you are. I did not use mine, but others did. Maybe share or check out from library.  Clicker pts may be only reason to go to class.

Lectures are dreadful, the examples he does on the overhead are nothing like the homeworks or the tests. If there weren't clickers I would have never gone to class and still done fine. He usually puts out 5 sample exams per test yet 3/5 of these "contain material not on the exam" and there are usually repeating questions on all the sample exams.

Although extremely helpful and willing to extend office hours, review sessions, etc. Dr. C is the easiest professor to get a headache from and going to lectures is useless except for clicker points. His explanations are often way too complex. You have to take him for 211 so just learn from doing the weekly hw and read the textbook when confused.

Large group lectures, labs and recitations are vital to passing.  They can be easy grades, but are a pain to go to every week.  Attendance isn't taken but there's a graded clicker question every class, so you have to be there for that. Mandatory homework every week, most answers can be found online but it helps to learn as you go instead.

This is the best physics professor in the entire Penn State Physics Department. The department sucks and the way the class is set up makes it hard to succeed. He really wants you to do well though and he is very helpful. His exams are more problem based instead of concepts making them easier. He also gives several practice exams that are similar.
The homework is a lot harder than any of the tests.  Tends to rely heavily on the book for lectures.  Pretty easy going.

You might not like the fact that you have to do homework every week, but it helps you so much for the exam. Do come to his office hours, he's very helpful and you can understand better. His grading is straight-forward and no extra credit. He'll give out two sample exams before each midterms and it is really helpful.
He is extremely helpful. Be regular with the homework and you'll ace his classes.

PHYS211 - Class was pretty clear cut.  I think he did a very good job covering the material but that might be because I had already taken a physics course before coming here. PHYS212 - Class was a lot rougher but if you went to lectures, took decent notes and actually tried in labrecitation then you'll do fine. He'll help if you go to his office.
Dr. C is the most helpful professor I've ever had. He's always available to answer questions, does the homework in his office hours, and always takes time to answer questions in class.
Dr. C is so good at explaining material. Word on the block is that his tests are also easier than other professors.
One of the most helpful professors I have ever seen in my life.

He's very clear and always willing to help. He sincerely likes physics and teaching and tries to make physics a good experience for everyone. There are clicker points, the labs and recitations are only going to help you if you already know what you are doing (so try to do your hw beforehand). The tests are difficult but fair if you study.

Mid-semester review, that way I'm not emotional about my final grade.  Dr. C's a solid prof. Always open to help,  but you will have to work for this class, unless you're some kind of a wizard. The material is challenging, recitations are more helpful than labs, and you need an iClicker for participation credit
Great lectures, although somewhat lengthy.
He's always willing to answer questions and help with homework during office hours.

Dr C is an awesome teacher, but to the detriment of Physics 211 students, knows too much physics. He will often explain lecture material as if you already understand the subject. Go to his office hours.  From my experience, he has no problem explaining problems and concepts 1-on-1.  Plus, he is the nicest guy.
He's a nice guy and all, but he's completely useless in lecture, which is mandatory but you'll hardly learn anything.

He is an amazing professor, he makes sure that everyone gets the concepts and clicker questions are, inspite of being as I put it "tricky", easy as he explains how to do them, lectures are not the best I've seen, but overall it's a good class and an amazing professor
Boring lectures, but necessary.
Dr. Costantino is a great professor and is always willing to help with questions. The class does require plenty of work if you want to do well.

Prof.Costantino is one of the nicest professor I have had on campus. He is helpful with homework questions and always makes himself available even during my random walk in for help. Do your homework and try your best on recitation and labs, if you can do homework without trouble, you will usually do pretty well on the exams. Work hard and get an A.
Best prof ever! Come to his office hours!!!! He will help you anytime!

Costantino is the man even though the material is boring. Class overall is very easy. If you do well on the HWs, recitations, and labs, you really only need a 88 exam average for an A. Extremely nice and helpful. 251 is all plug-and-chug algebra problems. If you can use a calculator, multiply and divide, and use a formula sheet, you're golden
He's not very good. He leaves out so much in his lectures that when it comes time for the homework you have little to no idea what you're doing. avoid him if you can.

Doc C is the man. If you've taken Phys 250, you'll have a good idea as to the difficulty and style of the exams. Do the sample exams; do your homework; go to recitation; and most importantly, GO to his office hours. He's tremendously helpful if you approach him.  And a nice guy all-around. (As usual, the labs were an utter waste of time & effort.)
not a favorable professor

Hes a nice guy i didnt go to any of the lecture but went to all the labs and recitations. The hws are where you learn everything just go on facebook and everyone helps you. go to his help sessions that he has b4 the test they will help a lot he doesnt put you on the spot nice guy dont blame him for boring material and I usually hate all professors

Was the easiest physics class I ever took. Go to class - Dr. C has a way of taking difficult physics concepts and putting them into simple terms for even a biology major to understand. I took my own notes instead of printing out the lecture slides because writing everything down in my own words made it easier to study later. He's great though.

It's hard going to lecture because he's so boring and you really don't learn anything there anyway.  I sometimes questioned whether he even knew what he was doing because he'd always get himself confused.  The class is easy though so I did fine just by reading the book before the exams.

He tries really hard to help you, but this is a class where you need to work hard. Try lion tutors reviews to help you stay on top of it. That helped me a lot. Also do lots of practice problems and everything he gives you for homework. If you put forth effort you should do well in the class.

He really tries hard in lectures to teach the material, but they are so boring that its tough to learn it.  Very nice guy though, and the class isn't too hard if you do the homework and attend labs and rescitations.
Lectures are awful and will put you to sleep. Go to his office hours because he will actually teach you there
His lectures aren't that good, but he is possibly the most helpful professor on campus. He really goes out of the way to make sure you understand the material, and cares about his students.
Boring lecturer. Usually not clear explanations of concepts. Hard to pay attention because he makes things much harder than they need to be. Easy tests, though.
Boring lecturer and usually did not have clear explanations of concepts. Tests were easy though
Boring lecturer. Easy exams.
hands down one of the most helpful instructors on campus. He doesn't just have his office open to you, he goes out of his way to make sure you understand the material.
Very helpful, good at explaining, and willing to help any time
No Comments
He's the best TA ever. He just knows the best way to explain everything everytime. He makes sure that u understand the stuff and not just know the answer. To sum up he's just the BEST.
Excellent TA. Always willing to help. Does a great job teaching the material.
Best TA I've ever had in any course.  Always more than willing to help, whether it be through email, office hourse, or appointment.  Very clear explanations.  Flat out good
I feel bad that so many students don't take this course seriously because she does an excellent job teaching it.
great professor, easy class, "what did you have for lunch today" ahh questions

This seminar is very easy, and Denise is extremely nice and accommodating. This class is basically listening to guest speakers about Nutrition and then writing a short reflection due that night. There are a few papers that are 1-2 pages so nothing crazy. As long as you go to class and complete the assignment you should have an A.

this was the easiest class ive ever taken at psu. prof lawson is so sweet and makes the class super manageable. There are quizzes almost every week but they are so easy and 3 projects throughout semester that take maybe an hour or 2. take this class if u want a super easy gen ed!

Easy gened, I go to class and do my homework the whole time. Quizzes weekly, but you can do them at home on your own time. 1 big project, but if you do it and follow requirements there's no reason you won't get an A.

An easy A. There's 3 projects you have to do all semester which each take 1-2 hours. Other than that, it's just participation, weekly online quizzes, and a weekly assignment, took me about 15 minutes a week. You learn about macro and micro nutrients through personal nutrition, and she cares about the topics. Highly recommend!

Easiest class I have ever taken. Weekly quiz and super easy assignment, takes 5 minutes each. 3 projects that also take less than an hour total. Do not have to show up everyday for class have like 6 classes you can skip, otherwise I just sat in class and did work for other classes, ended with high A. Very sweet professor and clearly loves her job

Easiest class ever. No exams besides weekly open book online quizzes (that you take whenever - they are like 5 questions). Then you have three projects over the year but they are based on your personal nutrition so its really hard to mess up. And there are also very short weekly assignments based on what was talked about that week. Recommend

Easier than my first-year seminar. If you want to learn absolutely nothing at college, this class allows that. However, the content she teaches is interesting and quite relevant to your life, so I would recommend paying attention in class.
Come to class.
I love her so much she is so sweet and always smiling. Had her for a morning class yet she still made it enjoyable
Attendance is mandatory! You have to complete TopHat questions during class. Weekly homework assignments and a big personal nutrition project, which is a big part of the class.

She is amazing! We have one day off almost every week, and we always get out early. Homework and quizzes are easy, and there is no midterm or final. There are only three annoying things, but all nutrition classes do it. Overall, take her over anyone else.

Dr. Lawson was great. She is very nice and cares about her students a lot. Big chunk of grade comes from a nutrition portfolio project that was very easy. Textbook is free but be prepared to spend money on NutritionCalc Plus. Lots of Top Hat questions during class. No midterms or finals which was great. If you need a GHW gen ed, take her class.

Prof Lawson is a great professor if you're looking for a decent gened in the health and wellness category. She cares about her students and attendance is required, but she has a generous time off bank so you don't need to come to every class. She definitely tries to make class interesting and the projects aren't too complicated.

Nutrition 100 is quite possibly the easiest A you will receive at Penn State. The hardest part about this class is mustering up the motivation to show up to the lectures every week. That being said, Denise is very very sweet and funny, and I highly recommend this class to students who need GHW credits.

I can't believe I had to pay for this course. It was a complete waste of my time. Most of the time in class I would work on other classes' work. The assignments were tedious and I learned nothing from them. Mrs. Lawson went on and on about random things and It just was so lecture-heavy and boring. Do not recommend it.

Lawson is the sweetest professor so far. She loves that you're there which makes you want to be there. the grading is super easy and so are the projects. she is always happy to help and very good at responding to emails. class if just lectures but she will throw in class activities every once in awhile.
Lectured at everyone all the time and was constantly going on rants that didn't apply to what we were learning. Tons of busy work and super time consuming. Overall, horrible class. DON'T TAKE!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Her class is easy and the lectures aren't bad but I usually do homework during them. The workload is light. She is very nice and often cancels class on Fridays if she gets through enough material during the other classes. I would recommend her.
