seems like a hard class during the whole semester but during the end she makes the class easy. she gives you a study guide for the final and if you fill out the study guide you will get an A. the final is given over finals week but on canvas so you can take it anywhere in the world.

Need to attend 5 plays throughout the semester and write a reflection on them. Have to pay for the tickets yourself. Only have class on Monday's & Wednesday's... Friday's there are no classes but there are online quizzes on canvas and the questions are from the textbook. She gives the last exam during finals week.
Very good professor, very easygoing and down to earth.  Definitely take a class with him if you can!

Professor Engels is very laid back, and his class in general was very easy.  Midterm questions are given beforehand, making studying easy, and a majority of the class was discussion, which was enjoyable.  Would definitely recommend.
Super chill dude and very personable. His class is easy and only two exams which he makes sure everyone does well on.

Nice professor, easy midterms with the questions given to you beforehand, would take again
lot of homework first half of semester then no homework second half of semester
Best teacher at psu. I took cas83 with him and it was so fun. We had class outside sometime, yoga, watch movies and more. He really cares about students and is so great to have!!!
Great teacher and lecturer who really cares about his students. Very interesting guy in general, was a college athlete whose also a yoga instructor.

Best professor of the entire CAS department at PSU. Period. You will never regret taking any one of his classes. I took two courses with him during my time here and I've become a better man and better communicator overall. His classes are best for those who like to talk speak their minds passionately and with respect for others.

Absolutely the best teacher I have ever had. He is extremely enthusiastic and engaging in all of his lectures. The exams have no surprises because he takes no joy in surprising students. He genuinely wants you to do well. He is also just a wonderful human being as well. BEST TEACHER EVER

Without a doubt one of the most amazing professors I have ever had. Professor Engles' lectures and discussions truly make the class and are the reasons students show up. Taking any class with Professor Engles should be in the back of every student's mind when scheduling classes
Jeremy is really wonderful. Super supportive and caring. Very easy grader. as long as he sees you putting in effort, you will get an A

Jeremy wants everyone to participate and if you answer a question 10/10 times he will ask you to explain it in further detail.  He does this to engage more class opinions and he never argues against what you say.  He was awesome
He's a great professor- you'll learn a great deal. And he's easy on the eyes.

Jeremy is a great professor who loves his field of study. He's always interested in engaging his students with the subject and loves hearing different points of view. You will learn a lot from this class without even realizing it.

Awesome professor. Gives good feedback and is an overall great class. I wasn't to excited for war rhetoric, but he made it a great class. Few papers with a take home exam. Best CAS professor i've had at state. Take him.

Absolute best..took him twice as a Freshman and a senior.  As a freshman made the transition from h.s. to college extremely interesting, as a senior kept me motivated to succeed with interesting discussion even when I was tying to coast out.  Absolutely worth taking at least once.

Amazing professor. Extremely invested in both the material and his students. If you put in the effort, he'll reward you. Any class with him is worth taking. Most of his classes are based on group discussions of readings and a few papers.

AMAZING professor. everything that you should expect to find at a great university. his class is super useful and interesting, and he really gets you involved and gets you to care about what is going on in our world. i would recommend him to everyone.
No Comments

Jeremy Engels is the best teacher I have ever had. He cares about making the class useful for the students. He is available to help at all times and is really flexible when you have a time conflict. Best professor I've ever had! He's young and relates to the students.
Wonderful class with a great professor who cares about your opinions

Dr. Endres' class was actually very good. He is very good at explaining concepts and actually cares enough in class to help people. The content isn't too much harder than BIO 110, but it definitely goes a lot more in-depth. If you have to take this class or want to, Dr. Endres is a great option!

He is an enjoyable guy, and lectures aren't bad, but he never stops talking; he doesn't give you nearly the amount of support the other professors do, and barely teaches you what's on the learning guides he gives you.

FunnyNice but distracts you from his mid teaching. Extra credit is IMPOSSIBLE makes the LAs guess the exactnumber of students that got a tophat question correct Other section (martin) gets to drop lowest exam and we do not. one of the midterms is right after Thon which SUCKS. I find myself asking friends from prof martins class for notes and stuff
Don't listen to any reviews about him he rambles a lot, we are currently behind in class for the exam, and he continuously makes mistakes. Save urself
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Endres is a good professor and you can tell he's passionate about the subject he's teaching and wants us to do well in the course. It's just hard to go to class when there is zero incentive to do so. The re-recorded lectures are so much more organized and informational, I end up putting airpods in and just going to class for the tophats.

BIO 230W is a relatively tough class and you have to put time outside of class to do well. Dr. Endres provided weekly packets that made following along in class really easy. He also gave us access to his powerpoints and lecture videos which made studying for the exams easier. Dr. Endres gets distracted very easily but he is a very good prof.

This class is work-heavy, but Dr. Endres has made it so enjoyable. You can tell he really enjoys his job. He brings such good energy to lectures, and I'm so glad I had him as a professor. He's very helpful and loves to talk to his students. I'd definitely recommend him!

He wasn't a bad professor by any means, just didn't love the set up of his class. The slides are very important for the exams and I only did well when I watched his lecture videos posted on canvas. There are no like practice problems or anything for exams so just beware. He is a nice guy, kinda cooky…. But overall a decent professor.

Dr. Endres is really funny and his lectures are pretty interesting. However, if you're not well-versed in cellular biology you might want to consider a different professor. The lectures can be kind of ramble-y and almost no study material is provided for exams.

He post lecture videos for every lecture, as long as you do the tophat questions before the end of the week you get the participation points. Its honestly not worth it to go to lecture, he teachers really well in the videos he posts and they are great to review before the exams. The lab for this course is a waste of time.

I don't personally dislike the guy, he's actually cool. Lectures were more like rants with clear goal. No form of study guide or assistance on what you should know for exams. The learning objectives don't help, your understand doesn't matter you will be examed on low quality pictures. I think the course is set up bad more than he's a bad prof.

This class is the most difficult I have taken so far. His lecture slides don't really correspond to the packets we are given, and he provides no resources for exams whatsoever. Exams are mainly all interpretation questions, and they're rough. He is nice and funny, but I feel like I learn nothing in his lectures.

Little to no resources are provided to study for exams. Don't get your hopes up for a review session or a study guide, because there won't be one. The lecture slides do not allow you to easily make sense of concepts. He also scheduled an exam the Tuesday after THON, so students have no choice but to do poorly or sacrifice time at THON. Do not rec.

Some people think he is weird, but personally I love him! He can be cooky, but thats my favorite part. He keeps everyone engaged and is a great lecturer. He is also incredibly helpful in office hours and genuinely wants to see his students succeed. I would reccomend.

Professor Endres is a terrible professor. He makes his classes so difficult and is extremely rude when you come to him for help/accomodations. Thank god I dropped this class or I would have failed it.
Do not take him!

Like most biology classes at PSU, I taught myself most of the material. The TopHat questions in class help with understanding, but aren't for credit. The exams are challenging, but manageable if you study and understand the content. He offers 2 points of extra credit for every exam. 4 non-cumulative exams, only 25 questions in the testing center.

Sweet and caring professor who teaches in a way that all students can understand. Responds to emails, and if you engage, you'll definitely learn. He provides great resources for success. Honestly, I would've earned an A if I had tried harder. Do well on ALL exams as your grade depends on them. Go to office hours ahead of time. Would take again!
Egotistical and off-putting. Video lectures were better than attending in-person lectures. Good luck!
Great professor and set up of the course. I would love to take another class with Dr. Endres again.

Very good professor who is able to explain content very well. If you do not understand certain material he and his TA/LA's are very accesible outside of class. He also has lecture recordings available to look back on for better understanding. Not a hard class, but you still have to work a little for the A. Overall great professor and well taught.

Endres has definitely been one of my more entertaining professors throughout my time here at Penn State. He does get off topic a lot and is pretty funny, but if you really sit and PAY ATTENTION, he makes perfect sense. The exams are just the learning objectives (given at the start of each week) but asked in a different way. LA OFFICE HOURS CARRY!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not entirely sure why this guy gets so much hate. Sure his lectures were a bit boring at times, but honestly a great professor who was knowledgable, caring, and funny. His office hours were helpful as well as the recorded lecture videos (no practice questions like BIOL110, but office hours + filling out learning objectives were really helpful!)

Not entirely sure why this guy gets so much hate. Sure his lectures could've been more engaging at times, but honestly a great professor who was knowledgable, caring, and funny. His office hours were really helpful as well as the recorded lecture videos (exams felt harder than BIOL110, but office hours really help and fill out learning objectives!)

This class was the worst I've done in all of college in a class, but I wouldn't blame it all on Endres. He got sidetracked a bit sometimes, but overall I think he lectured pretty well. Over 50% of the grade is from the exams (5 total plus cumulative final section) and I struggled a lot on those, but that was more due to outside circumstances.

I loved taking BIOL 222 with Endres. He had all of his lectures posted online in case you couldn't attend class. Some of the material was difficult, but it was easier to understand after taking the time to study. I also had BIOL 230W with Endres and didn't like him as much in that class. He is much better at teaching BIOL 222 in my opinion.

He is a super smart guy but for kids like myself who are not bio majors his explanations can feel confusing. I also felt a lack of understanding snowballed quickly and by the end of the semester I was really confused. I blame the layout of the class for my crappy grade- I would spend a long time on homework and do well but get poor exam grades.
u were pretty chill, sometimes u get off topic dawg. go Nittany lions

Endres is a great guy.  His in-person lectures may seem intimidating, but he re-records ALL of his lectures and goes into explicit detail which is so nice.  I used to lecture recordings after the 2nd exam and did not get below a high B on the exams.  He is also very available outside of class.  Weekly packets are a pain but SO helpful for exams

The professor is okay, but the material is not well-taught due to unclear explanations and annoying weekly homework assignments. These are unnecessary and can be found online, they're extra work for no reason. Exams are in Pollock. Take Malcos, PLEASE

Endres is a great professor and really cares about his students learning the material. He asks if we have any questions often and post recordings of the lecture online. He also give you a week to do or redo the tophat questions so you can get them right. The lab isn't difficult and we also get out early.

Dr. Endres is a nice guy but his lectures are boring. Tophat for attendance but it isn't worth much of your grade. Weekly packets. Tests at pollock are hard. Lab is okay. I would take it with a more engaging professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Endres is my favorite professor ever. He kept lectures interesting and was very good at explaining the material. I highly recommend Professor Endres for all bio classes you can take him for.

Be ready to write down EVERYTHING that he says during lecture since he talks about exam topics that aren't included on the slides. Lab is never in conjunction to what you're learning in class and grades heavily for no reason. Exams are hard since many of the questions are select all that apply and can be on even the smallest detail from lecture.

He is so funny and very understanding! He shows an amazing amount of enthusiasm about what he teaches. In all honesty, I would listen to anything he has to talk about. While he does take attendance on tophat, if you miss class, he posts lecture recordings, so it's SUPER easy to catch up. Make sure to participate in class so he doesn't get sad!!!!

requires Tophat grades, but you don't actually have to be in class to answer. He leaves the questions open for the entire week for students to answer (or change their answer) at anytime. If you do this and watch the lecture videos posted on canvas, you essentially never have to be in class. Expect to lose ~15 points in lab even with perfect work.

I think that the content of this class is really interesting and fun but Dr. Endress makes it difficult to understand. We do not have any resources for studying (more than Wikipedia) and the packets are not even completely graded. So even if you do a lot of effort it will be hard to have a good score on the exams if you don't go to office hours.

This class was okay. The lab is infinitely better than the lecture by a wide margin. The worst part about the class is the grading; sometimes it sets you up for failure -- you never really know what you got right or wrong. Please find effective ways to study for tests, it will do you much good.

Dr. Endres was a funny guy but awful at teaching. I think the packets were useless and just a waste of time. The only way I learned from this class was by watching the videos that he posted on Canvas. The actual lectures themselves were super boring and I couldn't learn anything. The lab was very dumb too, literally a repeat of Bio 110.

I really liked Dr. Endres, he is a super nice guy and he records all the lectures which is very helpful with studying. The lab is really easy and a big grade booster. The exams are mainly application questions but if you know the material well you will have no problem getting an A.

Dr Endres wasn't too bad of a professor, but was kind of confusing in the way he teaches things as he seems to contradict himself a lot which makes learning the material much more difficult than it needs to be. Lecture videos were super helpful and barely any homework involved. Easy exams if you study the lecture slides and watch the videos.

Im SHOCKED as to how many people dislike Dr. Endres. We have 1-2 homeworks each week - answers online. Theres weekly packets. I felt he explained concepts really well and "dumbed down" so we can understand. He records lectures and exams are easy if you study. The people complaining about "hard" exams just didn't pay attention. Lab is easy! TAKE HIM

Dr. Endres is a cool dude, but he really doesn't understand how to teach. Most of the class time is spent working out packet problems with classmates and not understanding any of it. Wikipedia is the main source of information, and the exams are pretty difficult to study for. He's funny, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr Endres is a really nice guy but I don't like the way he teaches. He is very confusing in how he explains things. The powerpoint slides don't match up with the packet and you have to watch an additional video outside of class for each lecture if you want to get the packet questions right. The lecture videos are more helpful than lecture
Lab absolutely sucks and this dude expects us to do homework during break. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS
The explanations are unclear and we can hardly get the answers to the packet questions.

Dr. Endres is super nice and great at explaining the material. I didn't really like how the course was formatted- lots of lecture time wasted and instead spent "discussing" packet questions with the people next to you, but overall I found this course to be pretty easy and very interesting! No textbook used and attendance not mandatory.

Endres is truly a nice guy, but this class absolutely sucks. Hard material and the information is from wikipedia. The homework is pretty easy but the only time you will learn is if you put in a MULTITUDE of extra time outside of class learning. The exams are super hard too good luck if you dislike select all that apply questions. Lab is easy though
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: No textbook but there are required readings and weekly homework. The 4 exams and final aren't too bad. Class setup is good with lectures and group work so it doesn't get too boring. Dr. Endres is super funny, caring, and very interested in the material. One of the best professors I've had since I've been here and would 100% recommend.

He seems like he has no idea about what he's talking about most of the time. Confuses himself first, then confuses the rest of the class. The LA's in class try their best to help, but it really isn't much help. Teaches for 5 minutes and then makes us do group activities. I don't pay tuition to just talk to random people. Oh, and lab is a disaster.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Endres is a good professor that means well, but I'm not sure if his lectures truly expanded my knowledge in the course. I had him at 8am, which didn't help, but I noticed a lot of lecture time is spent "discussing" with people next to you and not getting through material. His recorded lectures and LA video reviews were basically the only help.

I also had Endres for BIOL110 FRI Lab and I can definitely say he is better at teaching a lab than a lecture. In the lab, he would sit down with me one on one to work through my lab project with me. For the lecture, he spends a good portion of the time letting students work with peers on packets, rather than teaching the material in depth.

Dr. Endres is a really nice guy! I had him at 8am, so I appreciated his efforts to get his tired students engaged. Tests are a pain, but if you focus on lecture content from slides, and especially packets and learning objectives you'll do alright! Test heavy with hard content, but Dr. Endres is a goofy guy! Enjoy the incoming dad jokes.

Endres is a great professor who actually remembers his students and connects with them personally. Doesn't make you feel stupid when you are confused. The course is hard and so are the exams, but he does not try to trick you or fail you. His voice is soothing making it hard to pay attention sometimes but he is absolutely hilarious!!

Dr. Endres made an online biology class much more bearable than normal. Every few slides during lecture we'd break off to practice what we learned on worksheets, and he also used imbedded questions to test if we understood material. The main goal of the class is application, which he has you practice throughout the class so you're ready for exams.
Dr. Endres honestly does not care about his students. I attended every class, but his explanations could be quite unclear and confusing.
first teacher i've ever heard that ENCOURAGED us to use wiki... no curving whatsoever

Endres is a very good professor. He's funny and caring about his students. The test could be difficult, but if you pay attention in class and take good notes, you should be fine. Plus, there are a lot of opportunities for points elsewhere.

Endres is a nice guy, but I would not recommend this class to anyone. I spent so much time studying just to do horrendous on the exams. His lectures are very dry and he just talks in circles. He's awful at explaining and expects you to already know definitions of everything without him really explaining them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Endres is a great teacher and wants his students to succeed. He is accessible outside of class, has several TA's to help during class and after hours, and teaches the material straight up. Exams aren't difficult if you study and take notes. It's not an easy A, you have to work for your grade in his class but it's not overly difficult either.
This class is honestly just hard. Endres is super funny though and honestly cares about his students. Just redo the worksheets, the lecture problems and study the SCILITS.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not much chances to prepare yourself for exams, no practice exams, little to no help from LA's or Professor.

Dr. Endres really does care about the students. However, I found that his lectures are extremely dry and the course material is confusing at times. The best way to succeed in his class is to really pay attention in class and study the powerpoint slides. The textbook is wiki which is practically useless for exam prep.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Endres is a super nice guy. He is very accessible outside of class and truly wants his students to succeed. There are so many course points that you can bounce back from one bad test. His lectures can be boring, but I would still suggest taking his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Nice guy. Very boring lectures. Material being taught is already boring if you're not into cell bio but he talks very slow and soft. Hard to pay attention but if you miss even one thing nothing else makes sense. Missed 2 classes and it took me so long to catch up. Wiki is the book. Annoying lab, tough exams, hard readings. Need to teach yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: The course itself is not that difficult, but Dr Endres is not great at teaching either. If you learn better from a professor lecturing rather than on your own, do not take the course with him. I relied heavily on outside sources to understand the material. He is a nice guy but does not teach well at all.

The subject matter isn't particularly difficult, and there's no textbook. There's a lot of busy work, but pretty straight forward. There are 5 exams, a final, and 2 homework assignments due every week. Clickers are used every class and only correct answers are counted, but you only need 75% of clicker points to get full credit.
You must learn the material yourself. He does not explain information well. You will not pass if you solely rely on his lectures to learn the information.

I was a TA for this course with Matt. I can say that he definitely cares about the students and wants us to learn the material. It was his first semester teaching the course so he def has great potential to be a solid instructor. Ask questions and get help from the instructional team and the class will be one of the best you've taken at psu!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Endres is a really nice guy but is new and does not really explain things very well. This class has 5 exams and an online final which is super easy. A lot of my friends took this class when Dr. Malcos taught it and said it was really easy, but I just dont think Endres explains things well.

Dr. Rochette is such a funny and nice guy! Anthropology isn't really my thing so honestly I did find the class pretty boring. The exams were kind of difficult, but he was always fair with giving points back! Overall, if you need an interdomain, I would take this class with him.

Each week included a set of slides in Canvas, a textbook chapter (I just skimmed it to find definitions for a given vocab list), and an activity (short quiz, discussion, or HW). Everything was open book including the midterm and final (multiple choice). Very easy to work ahead, the only due date were on the activities and exams. Very nice professor
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Definitely a great professor, but you need to come to class. He doesn't post the lecture slides, so that it's important to show up in order to understand what's going on for quizzes. Exams are not horrible if you take notes. I was honestly a bad student in this class and managed an A-, definitely would have gotten an A if I showed up to class haha

I have taken multiple classes with Erick and I have loved all of them. He is a really nice guy, always knows what he is talking about, and really cares about his students. He is very understanding and accommodating. this class is very hands on and you will spend multiple weeks in the woods, or field but it is super fun, even if it is raining. 10/10

I really enjoyed his class. his lectures are very interesting and he always lets you ask questions. there are minimal assignments in the class, maybe a reading every other week and short online quizzes that are based on the lectures. there are 3 online exams and they are really not bad if you go to class. really nice guy!
Genuinely the best professor I've ever had at this godforsaken nightmare college

Gives engaging, amusing lectures. However, he doesn't post slides on Canvas, so attendance is necessary given that there's no other way to access the material. Aside from a weekly quiz based on the past week's lectures, assignments are few and far between. Exams are moderately challenging, but they are on Canvas and not at a specific time.
His lectures were very interesting and he has a good sense of humor. This class is an easy B/B+ but a relatively hard A due to the super specific test questions. Not a lot of work otherwise.

Dr. Rochette is great, lectures were pretty interesting and the course didn't feel too work heavy. Don't buy the textbook, it's not really used. assignments are pretty easy and so are the quizzes if you show up to class. Exams were a little difficult, but overall an easyish and interesting gen ed, if you go to class.

75% of the grade is the closed note exams. meaning unless you average at least an 86% on them, its impossible to get an A in the class. Bruh. And don't expect to achieve that, the questions are ultra specific and covering things from across the entire semester.

This class is graded very hard and a majority of your grade is based on the three exams. You can also lose points on discussion  posts if you respond to classmates too soon. He is very knowledgeable and nice, however this class does require more work for an online course.

If you're looking for a Gen Ed that requires very minimal effort or attendance for an A, this isn't it. The exams and quizzes are heavily based on lectures and reading from textbooks. You shouldn't expect to get an A by just looking up the questions on Quizlet the entire semester. If you attend every lecture and take notes, it should be an easy A.

Great class to take, only complaint is you have to have a 94 for an A. All material is posted on canvas and he has very clear instructions. Sometimes you can lose points on discussion posts because you respond on the same day you posted. He is easy to contact and very knowledgeable! 
Course is asynchronous.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great guy and tries keeps lectures interesting but I took this class as an easy A and it certainly was not that. You have to do the weekly readings and although he does not take attendance, missing lectures will make the exams impossible. Exams are on canvas but questions are difficult to understand so even if you study expect a B at best.

Dr. Rochette was very nice and extremely knowledgeable. Given the strict lecture style, classes were sometimes interesting but were particually boring at times. The coursework consisted of just weekly mini-quizzes and 3 exams. Exam questions were awfully specific, requiring you to read the textbook & go to every class. Do not take for an easy A!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Learned a lot for a class I took as a gen-ed! Really allowed me to understand cultural contexts and concepts through examples shown in class, with very detailed lectures. Grading seemed simple, though exams are definitely testing knowledge in lectures, documentaries, and sometimes textbook. Easy gen-ed if you're interested in anth, which I am now!
Great guy and brings up a lot of interesting topics to think about.

Love this guy!! Second time taking him and it won't be the last. His teaching convinced me to get a minor in anthro when I otherwise never would have had any interest in pursuing the subject (engineering major). Take notes during lecture and watch the assigned videos/do the readings and you'll be fine! Rare to find such a passionate professor.

I took ANTH8 spring of 2020. Rochette is my favorite prof at penn state so far. He really cares about his students and is SUPER passionate about the material. Exams rely heavily on lectures - as long as you pay attention and take notes you'll be fine! Never thought I would like Anthro but now I'm looking to take more classes about the subject!

Two pieces of advice: Don't give full assignments the same week as a midterm/final, it kills interest and makes students resentful. Also, There are several anti-western themes. I would challenge the prof to step outside the 'Woke-sphere' and valuate cultural impacts outside that lens, it would give the course a broader appeal and a proper basis.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class should be VAG045 for vaguery. Had a similar, more interesting class via Clarion University, the aim there was to actually teach and engage, not just give a tricky exam and act like its the same thing. No thought engagement, which is sad, the topic is very rich. Works Karl Marx into each lesson. Politically indoctrinating much?
He is really nice and this is an easy interdomain with some reading. Take it with some friends and it can fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: His classes should be super easy because they are all just lectures but when exams come they are only multiple choice and true and false and he says if you come to the lectures you'll get an A which is sooooo wrong. his exam questions are so specific and often not in the simple notes from lectures that he gives out.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The exams are on canvas but are impossible to do well on and a lot of times he doesn't show up to class and has the TA play a movie. Do not take for an easy GenEd.

The lectures were interesting and I enjoyed the class. However, don't take the class if you're looking for an easy A. There are four tests that essentially make up your grade. The tests are taken on Canvas, but are hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Easy A as long as you go to class and take decent notes. Exams were online so I just searched my notes for the answers. Some questions were tricky but I got several extra credit points just for showing up to class. No work outside of class either. Overall easy gen ed as long as you show up to class

Do NOT take this class for an easy A. The exams are online but they are very specific and it's not like you can just google it. He has had to curve every exam because everyone was doing poorly. I respect the man but not his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Give yourself a break and dont take this class, yeah its somewhat interesting but the exams are tough, and it requires that you read the textbook and go to every class. TA is nice but way too strict with grading. Every exam is on canvas, but dont get excited only a handful of questions out of all 4 exams were online. Dont take as an easy gen ed
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Best professor this semester. Engaged, hilarious, and quick with responses. His lectures were clear and very helpful with quizzes and exams.

I loved going to Rochette's lectures. They were usually very interesting and he liked to spice things up by including participation activities and videos. The homework was very easy and the quizzes were straight forward (and usually online). He made anthropology fun and was accessible during office hours.
He's awesome! Makes a field not many know of super fun!
Keeps class light and is really funny. Gave me new appreciation for anthropology as a field.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: the exams and quizzes in this class were entirely vague. The instructor has no exam writing skills. He flies through powerpoint presentations totally unenthused. He does not  accommodate the needs of the students.

My sleep rate in his class approaches 33.333%. He has a habit of including in his tests facts he only mentions once in lectures. Oh and get ready to read, your eyes will bleed. I just wish his topics were coherent in structure, linear/hierarchical or told like a story. That worked in my World History highschool class. That class really engaged me.

I took this class for Gen Ed. Not worth it too much work and the teacher to me is too rude. The quizzes are easy but if your short essay sounds too much like the reading you get a zero and basically get a D. The tests have some random questions. Honestly unless required I suggest a different class or teacher. No book required all materials given.

Be prepared to read A LOT!!  Very dense reading and the scope of the course in incredibly broad.  Exams were rough but I did get an A and had to work really hard for it. Only complaint is he takes forever to return papers back.

Take this course! He's a great guy, really sincere about his work and although I took it in a huge classroom setting, he was still approachable and the class was still fun and lively. He has great powerpoints, if you know the material he gives you - you're GOLD for tests. DO NOT BUY THE BOOK, I spent $136 dollars for a book I never had to use.

Plays music before every lecture that either ties into the lecture itself or is "anthropological" and provides info about it.  The other day, he played songs about the Irish potato famine before talking about intensive agriculture.  Great at making anthro relevant to students' lives and really funny.

Online course with assignments every week based on the readings.  As long as you do the reading, its a breeze.  Assignments are with 10 question quizzes on the reading or short (3 page) essay assignments.  He replied to my emails quickly with good explanations of stuff I didn't get.  Good, interesting class.

Online course, so it is all reading, but it wasn't hard, so long as you read the material.  Most of your grade comes from the assignments, with only 20% from the exams, so its a breeze even if you don't do well on the exams.

I am taking the class online and im not doing very well. There is def a ton of reading and i should have taken it in a classroom but Mr. Rochette, is willing to work with you and help you. He is very smart and takes the time to work with you. long story short i dont think its him i thinks its the medium chosen to take the class that makes it hard.
No Comments

OMG! Some people sure are lazy! There is def a lot of reading, but it's interesting and not THAT hard.  Also, assignments every week (essays, quizzes), but not too bad.  He's replied to my emails within a day every time, so ok on that.  Exams are a bit hard, but I have an A & I do maybe 10 hrs wrok/week, same as a regular class, but w./o lecture.
NO, NO, NO dont take if you dont have to,if you have no intrest in it, or just plain if this guy is teaching it.

Erick Rochette was very entertaining and engaging. Although, he could slow his lecture delivery down a bit.  I enjoyed this class and would recommend it to others. He did not "dumb down" the material because it was an introductory class. I feel that I am well prepared to take future anthropology courses.

The material is intertesing and there is alot of reading def more than an hours worth of work a week. But i do agree that for the level of 045 it isnt worth it. I would not take this class online again.

I am also taking this class now and it is not that hard.  There is a lot of reading and assignments, but my grade is an A right now, and I do maybe one hour of work a day, if even that.  He doesn't make regular posts, but he answers questions quickly and helpfully.  The material is a bit dry at times, but it is definitely interesting.

i am taking this class right now online and i have to say its the hardest class i have taken and its only an 045 level class. He expects wayyy too much for what level class this is and is a hard grader. I'd advise anyone to not take this class but if you have to dont take him.

He was just a horrible professor. He was extremely boring and never gave enough time for people take notes. I'll never understand how someone could possibly make such a potentially fascinating class so horrifying. Everyone I asked hated the class.
I had a great experience with Professor Reynolds. He explained exactly what we needed to do and thoroughly answered any questions asked.

His lectures are very boring and slow, but you don't really need to pay attention. He appreciates when students participate and if nobody answers him there will be long pauses while he waits for anybody to say anything, so just participate and class will keep moving. The assignments aren't difficult, if you put decent effort in you will do fine.

He told my class that getting an A was nearly impossible. Attendance is mandatory (do not skip more than 6 classes)! Lectures are very boring and by the middle of the semester you will stop using the textbook. Participate occasionally because he does take notice to it! Very nice guy overall but seems a little shy.

Lectures were very boring and didn't get much out of them but he takes attendance. Hard grader in my opinion, A- is pretty achievable because of the weird scale the class has but A or A+ is extremely hard. Textbook not really needed.
He is very caring and soft spoken. He is very respectful of his students work. A very passive teacher, but basically teaches out of the textbook.

Not a bad professor but not the greatest. Lectures are boring and pretty slow but assignments are easy. It's rare to get an A on papers but an A- is pretty attainable. Assignments are straightforward. You do 3 essays and one infographic.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The class isn't hard to do well in. Lectures are so boring, just do work for other classes. There is a free version of the textbook online, you do not have to buy it. No one participated. Office hours were helpful before turning my final essays in.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I did not mind this professor, but he was incredibly boring. We did nothing every single class and he would just talk in a very monotone voice. He was nice but made no effort to make the lectures interesting. I do think it is pretty easy to receive an a- but I think getting an a is difficult.
He is very nice, but all we do is write paper after paper and the things we talk about in class is very boring. Not very beneficial for our papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Very easy grader and you read a lot.
Very easy grader, but lectures can be a bit boring. Compared to what I have heard about other professors I would 1000% recommend taking English 15 with him.

The class itself is pretty easy, Reynolds is pretty boring, and just yaps and reads everything off the slides. He's also really quiet but pretty helpful when you have a specific question on something with your essays. His grading is a little bit confusing but it's not too tough. Also, don't buy the textbook, he barely uses it.
To be honest with y'all, as long as you show up to class and try to do the work, you will pass.

Eh. The guy just yaps to a very bored class. The class itself isn't too hard, with a paper due ever 3 three weeks or so. Don't buy the text book, he barely uses it, and when he does someone else will probably answer.

He is super mid. Also, he's pretty quiet. There is a decent amount of reading, but no one really reads it and you don't really have to. Also for anyone wondering, English 15 is not a big class size at PSU.

His lectures are extremely boring. He has a monotone voice and shows no interest in the class. He reads off the provided slides word for word while adding nothing. You are forced to attend these lectures or lose points quite quickly. He provides little information than what is provided on the documents. He is a pretty easy grader though.
If you take away one thing from all these comments let it be DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH THIS PROFESSOR! If you think "it can't be that bad" IT IS!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If I could give her a 0, I would. She has a VERY strong accent, which made the class material even harder to understand. She also reads off the slides during class, which was very unhelpful when it came to doing problems. Chemistry is hard enough as it is, and this professor somehow found a way to make it harder.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I am currently taking CHEM110 here at Penn State (Spring 2026). The ratings here are not lying, do not think "Oh it surely can't be that bad". Oh it is much worse. Average was 60s on the first exam and she just said welp study harder guys. Her style is the worst possible style in the world. Simply avoid at all costs, I will pass but it wont be easy

This is by far the worst class that I have taken at Penn State and the worst professor I have ever had. She is very hard to understand and does not teach. It is expected that you know everything going on on your own, she only goes over material, does not teach it. Prepare to spend all your time on this class, especially if you have her.

Get ready to watch a lot of the Organic Chemistry Teacher on YouTube. He essentially taught me the course. As for the teacher, she mumbles through lectures and really only uses TopHat. Goes through material awfully fast and put down our class when the midterm average was failing. Avoid her if you can, I would give her a 0/5 if I could.
horrible professor, doesn't teach for anything. no wonder everyone drops out of chem. learnt the material on my own so its not worth it.

Worst professor ever! The lectures are extremely boring and hard to understand. It seriously  seems like she doesn't even know what she is talking. The test averages were always in the low 60s, but she blames it on us and our studying. DO NOT TAKE!!!!!

Elvira was the worst instructor I have ever had for a course until the end of my PhD. I remember when I asked questions several times, she said why would you as a non-chemistry student take this course and everyone laughed at me. I had to take this course for a mandatory credit at MatSE but regretted every second of it. AVOID her if you can.

Dr. S honestly was one of the worst professors I've ever had. She is terrible at explaining the information. I learned the most from doing the homework. She says the practice exams are like the midterms but they are similar for having the same topics but she twists it in a way so that you are guaranteed to not know everything. Avoid if you can!!!!

Professor was very rude to students and was not receptive to any criticism. All of the midterm averages were just above failing. Moved grade cutoffs up the day grades were entered so less people would get a good grade overall. Professor mumbled through lectures and only read off the slides which made going to class useless except for participation.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Did not learn a single thing in this class. Professor was rude and condescending during lectures. Lectures were not helpful at all. Practice exams were very similar to exams, which was helpful, but homework and lectures were little help in order to prepare for the exams.

She is not the nicest person. Blamed the class for doing poorly on the first exam rather than re-evaluating her teaching style. My friend left crying, it was brutal. If you do the practice exams, the test will be the same thing, different font. Still difficult, and the professor made it no better.

She refused to use the microphone in a large classroom. If you don't answer the questions correctly she accuses you of not paying attention. The average on the first exam was a 40% and she blamed us for not studying hard enough. She also accused us of lying to her when we reported that we did indeed study intensely. Let alone her thick accent. 0/10

Dr. Epple is the type of professor that will give you respect if you prove to her that you care about her class, and are willing to try. She inspired me like no other, but many other students in the class dreaded it. She is very big on respect, and this class requires you to dig deep.

Dr. Epple was unhappy that some people had similar answers on an activity we did. She then outright accused EVERY student in the class via a class announcement in writing of using AI to cheat, and told us that none of us would be allowed to say we didn't. How can she accuse us of cheating, offer no evidence, and not allow us to defend ourselves?

She is a tough grader, and participation matters a lot. She does get to know her students and I feel like she was kind. I honestly wouldn't take this class again because it was annoying. Go to the writing center and office hours and you will be okay.

She has easily been my favorite professor so far at Penn State. As long you show up to class, go to office hours every now and then, and possess the ability to write, you'll be more than fine in her class.  She is a much easier grader than many of the other reviews say. She gave me A's for all my papers when I was a B English student in high school
Chill Teacher.

Dr. Epple was my yoga teacher at a different campus. She is a very sweet teacher, but gave unnecessary assignments for a 1.5 credit yoga class and was a very harsh grader. She graded more hardly at the end of the year when grades were meant to be placed. I had an A the whole semester in the class, then dropped down to a B+ after more assignments.

- Very nice but very strict
- 80% of your entire grade is the papers you write throughout the semester
- The other 20% is your participation in class
- TOUGH grader on papers
- Not many A's given

I switched into her class the second week and I was a bit nervous at first while reading these comments. I went to her office hours and put in a lot of effort into her assignments and she helped me out so much. She is very understanding and personal and cares a lot about her students!!

She is the toughest grader and only gives like 2 students an A. She is passive aggressive and expects WAY too much from students. She uses the term "Cs get degrees". She is not flexible. This is a mandatory class that most students get an A in however she makes it impossible. She is nice but that doesn't account for the way she grades and teaches.
Don't take her class...

If you happen to get sick and are unable to go to class, be prepared to fail. Ms. Epple does not take late assignments no matter what the excuse is and she gives no accommodations for illness, even if it is serious. She is also a very tough grader and takes a VERY long time to grade assignments.

If you take this class, be prepared to feel ashamed. She takes body language into account and will take off points from your participation if the believes you are not showing embodied engagement. Takes a long time to grade. Overall, the vibe of the classroom was very passive aggressive for my section and not fun..
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She grades tough, but also putting in decent effort will get you far. This class is way too easy for anyone to not put in a valiant effort, and I took 10 other classes this semester as a music major and am finishing with an A. Time management is your friend, and DO THE READING. It sucks, but just do it. She cares a TON about her students :)

She grades fairly harshly but is also VERY detailed in what she wants. If you listen, you'll know exactly what to do to get the grade you want. Office hours are very helpful if you feel like you aren't doing as well on an essay. She gets a strict layout to follow for assignments, so she can't control that, but she makes it really fun. I recommend!

If you are looking for an elective to take care of a health credit, I definitely recommend this class/professor. She is very kind and considerate and overall just good at her job. All you have to do is show up and do what is assigned and you'll get an A. All quizzes are open note and online. Group project isn't bad either.

This class is far from a walk (jog) in the park if you're not much of a runner. youll be running 3-5 miles within the first month with timed jogs on fridays that go up to 43 minutes. erin is really cool and really nice but be prepared to actually jog a lot in the class. really good if you want to get in shape. attendance is almost all of the greade
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's really nice and understanding. Show up to class and jog, and you'll get an A.

Great class! Erin really encourages you to succeed and push yourself but allows you to set your own goals. She genuinely loves teaching the class and fitness in general. Erin is one of the nicest professors I've ever had at Penn State.

he uses a chalkboard but his handwriting is hard to read; the class is literally graded based on 90 perc. of exams and 10 perc. 6 HW assignments; Speaking of the HW, the questions are things he doesn't teach, nor do they appear in the textbook; He is funny, but does call you out in class if you've been to his office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although the class is curved, the exams are the entire grade. Even though the content is based heavily on lectures, there is no structure to the lectures. He just writes whatever on the chalk board without any organization so if you zone out for even a minute you're lost. TA's are the only way I got through this class take someone else if you can.

Tests are 90% of grade, but they are very similar to practice exams so if you put in time to prepare it is possible to get A's on every exam. I also took Orgo 1 at a CC and got better grades on these exams. You do have to expect to show up to class and you get all the information for HW and exams. Textbook was free. I thought lectures were engaging

Despite what other reviewers say, having professor Funk is a win. He is easier than other professors and quite forgiving. He is also such a nice dude and makes class fun. You get used to his system of teaching. Don't let other students deter you, go to class, pay attention and you will be fine. He is an overall great guy and loves teaching clearly.
This guy is the worst prof at PSU. Bro has dementia and is still teaching. 90% tests and 10% HW is so unreasonable. Raymond put the fries in the bag!!!

he's really funny but he is very old school. doesn't use canvas, you have to turn in paper homework, and writes on a chalkboard. the board is hard to read. he doesn't really explain concepts. graded on 6 hw, 3 exams, and a final. go to TA office hours they are a huge help! it's the only way i learned things

Although lectures are optional they are so important just to get the notes even if you don't understand the content. I had to learn everything outside of class in office hours but in turn I did well on the exams which heavily mirrored the practice exams
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Taking with funk helped me realize how cool Chem can be. If ur taking this class just to check it off take with a professor who does specs grading. The exams are literally copy and paste form the practice exams and homeworks, with a few things changed. This class is great if you wanna learn, just be ready to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funk is a nice old man that I would love to hang out with if he were my neighbor, but he needs to retire from teaching chemistry. He doesn't have any PowerPoint slides; he only writes on the chalkboard in a large lecture hall and then covers what he's writing with his body, so you're struggling to keep up with what he's writing. Avoid his class.

Some may say that Ray Funk is an acquired taste, and I think I've acquired it. At first he may seem old school and unhinged, and he honestly is *in the best way possible*. In another life I would have loved chewing grass with him. Just memorize the reactions and do the practice exams. It may be a fever dream, but it's not that deep.

Ray Funk is a great guy, but not the best professor. He moves extremely fast through material (especially for Honors) and erases things extremely fast, too; this wouldn't be that bad if he uploaded literally anything to canvas (which he didn't). Go to office hours and MAKE FLASHCARDS and you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Really old school and his note on the board is not readable. You will need to organized your own notes. His exams are similar to his practice ones.

He's old school but he's a funny guy. Only writes on a chalkboard and doesn't use canvas, so even though attendance isn't mandatory its rough to miss even one lecture. The textbook is also optional, but reading it will definitely help.

Dr. Funk is incredibly smart, BUT there is a reason he only teaches on the off schedule for ORGO. His class is 10% HW based, 90% exam based.  Read the textbook and lecture points, and DON'T SKIP the lectures. For HW help go to office hours with the TAs. Practice exams and homework are very similar to the exams. With Funk, this isn't an easy course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funk is an acquired taste that I did not enjoy. If you don't go to class, you won't be passing. He uses lecture points to move through lessons but it is mostly based on what he writes on the board. He is the type of prof to lecture from his own memory/experiences. He is very "old school" in only using a chalkboard, you're only graded on HW & exams.

You have to go to lecture to pass this class. Read the book, go to lecture, and go to review sessions- you'll be fine. He has a very unique teaching style that can take a while to get used to, but if you do the work to understand what's going on, you'll be fine. The TA's and the review sessions are truly where you learn.
he was horrible at lecturing

Anybody who hates Funk didn't put in the effort outside of class necessary for a weed out course. Lectures move fast, but if you read lecture points and textbook before/directly after class it clarifies a lot. He's fair, funny, and amazing at putting hard concepts into perspective by relating them to a topic you care about so you don't give up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I don't understand how he became a professor. He doesn't use canvas or emails. When teaching on the chalkboard, he barely erases the old stuff, making it hard to follow since his old and new scribbles overlap. Exams are90%.The only resources are very confusing lecture notes. Only pro ispractice exams are verysimilar to actual exams. DONT TAKE

He's tough but fair. He grades on a curve, and also gives extra credit. He only writes on a chalkboard with no online functionality, so you'd better not miss class. It's possible to succeed without reading the textbook, but it makes it much easier to read. The class is also graded only on exams, no homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had Funk for both CHEM210 and CHEM212. Nice professor but makes the courses way more difficult than they need to be with his teaching style. Take another professor if you can. If you have to take Funk, go to all of his review sessions and study hard for the exams and you will get through it.

If you have the option, please take the CHEM 210H version, it will definitely help with the detailed concepts on Orgo Chem. Obviously, he writes on the chalkboard, but you are a lot closer. But he is genuinely a nice professor if you meet the guy personally. He is funny and talks about his life stories during class. Get ready to study though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funk is an acquired taste but is honestly the best. Is tricky to know the main takeaways of lectures but once you are familiar with his style, they are not bad. HWs can be pretty tough but exams are usually always fair. He offers a lot of review and practice exams to take advantage of. Awesome teacher and a hilarious person, absolutely recommend.

He's like a total old-school professor, He's all about that traditional stuff. You gotta print out all your homework and hand it in physically before class. Plus, he's not about this Canvas life, so there's no way you're getting any notes online. You gotta show up to class and squint at the board where he scribbles stuff that's as clear as mud.

He doesn't use any technology except for releasing hw every 2-3 weeks. Not much work outside class, but lectures are him standing and writing on a chalkboard for the entire hour- he will never end early. Funny guy get to know him he's awesome. Go to his exam reviews, except sometimes they're on weekends but never during a home game.

PART 2 CONT....Then, in class he will speak while writing so quickly on a chalk board and your only hopes of having hard to decipher notes is to get it all down fast enough before he erases the board or moves on to the next topic. You are only graded on 10 assignments: 6 homeworks, 3 exams, and 1 final.

Worst class I have ever taken. Yes, organic chemistry is a difficult topic, but this teaching style made learning nearly impossible. First, Funk only teaches by giving you a sheet to read before class that uses hard-to-understand language. There are no other notes provided to you besides the textbook. CONT......

Probably the worst teacher I have had. He does not use powerpoint so you are expected to learn organic chemistry from him speaking and writing on the chalkboard. I went to office hours with a TA every week, which is the only reason I passed this class. I genuinely learned next to nothing from his lectures.
He wants you to learn via the book. He uses lecture to talk about stuff not on the test. I learned more on youtube than I did in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Funk is old school - course is composed of 6 HWs and then the rest are exams. Lectures contain a decent amount of information that is not useful so you have to be good at deciding what is worth writing down, as he moves very quickly. Fair tests, HWs, and nice curve. By far the best professor I have had at Penn State, he is hilarious.

He's chill but the info is just a lot. I also wish he didn't use the chalk board as much because its really hard to read unless your like in the front row. At the start of the course I felt like I knew what was going on but half way through it felt like he just kept throwing new thing after new thing so its kinda easy to get lost.

Dr. Funk is a great guy but horrible teacher. He's not used to teaching the first orgo and it shows. He just doesn't teach the basics and spends class time on things that wont be on the exam. He ONLY uses the chalkboard, and everything including homework is done on paper. He is a fair grader. Just know you will have to teach yourself everything.

He really is passionate for chem and is very good at teaching the information. Make sure to show up to class if you want to do well. The practice exams and homework are very helpful for prepping for tests. The curve is very good.
Sweet man but made me Frel like an idiot when I asked a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Funk's exams are incredibly easy and mirror the practice exam quite a bit. Make sure to sit near the chalkboard to see his notes. His notes are not recorded, so you have to go to lecture, but a lot of the homework and exam are directly from the notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He was really funny and taught the material well for the most part. It really is just a tough class, and his homework grading is frustrating (4 pages of questions, but one question is randomly graded), but he does give a lot of materials to study. A good choice for a tough class
Oof

Dr. Funk is a funny and caring professor. The small honors section is definitely a huge plus. You'll only have a few quams (quiz/exam), (several in 210H, less in 212H) and no hw, so make sure to study often. People say "don't memorize organic chem", but you will have to memorize a few things to do well quickly on exams. I 100% suggest flashcards.

Dr. Funk is one of the best professors I've ever had. He explained exactly what material he wanted during the lecture, and never gave us any surprises. He's funny, and engaging, and I would take his class again!! There are few grades in the class, but as long as you pay attention and go to class, you'll be completely prepared for all exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk is one of the best professors at Penn State. He cracks several jokes during lectures and makes learning orgo II enjoyable. His exams are very similar to his HW's and Practice Exam, so pay attention to those. Make sure to sit close to the front of the classroom to read the board though! Enjoy your time with Dr. Funk - it goes by very fast!

This class is tough, but Funk is probably the best guy for the job. His lectures felt a little chaotic to me, and he was prone to blocking the board with his body which was frustrating. HW grading is stupid, but HW and the practice exams are pretty good prep for the exams. Be prepared to work hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Funk is best orgo teacher in my opinion. I learned so much better from him than my orgo 1 professor. His grading of HW is pretty unfair but his exams are always pretty close to practice exam. Very old school teacher but I recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Such a nice guy and a good teacher... Literally just go to class and do the homeworks and practice exams and you'll be fine. WAY better than the other orgo teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly loved him he was so funny!! He is very old school with his teaching style which I actually liked. Practice exams and homeworks are almost identical to the exams. Must put in work to learn the material but that's organic chem. take him over elaqua, our exam averages were consistently 20 points higher
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's old school to a point where he uses a small chalkboard instead of using Powerpoint and the pull-down screen provided by the school. If you do not get a seat in the first couple of rows, you better have binoculars to see what he is writing on the screen.
Dr. Funk does not understand how to teach those that chemistry does not come naturally to them. He is too smart and struggles to make the material at the level for a college student.

really liked him! the lectures are straightforward- he draws example reactions on a chalkboard. he does examples very similar to problems on homeworks. copy the examples down and make a quizlet to memorize the reactions for exams. if you know the reagents and what they do, youll be fine. show up to class and get. the. notes. and pay attention.

Ray funk is definitely passionate about chemistry and is a good teacher despite what people say. You just have to actually put in the work. The only thing is its really hard to see the board because he writes tiny on the chalkboards in forum.

Honestly he probably has become one of my favorite professors... Extremely reasonable. Exams are the exact same style as the practice exams. A really nice guy, even though he seems tough on the outside. Take him over the other one... Trust me

I thought Dr. Funk was awesome. You're so busy in his class that time passes quickly, everything you need for the HW is what he wrote on the board. Tests are an easier version of the HWs, know your HWA in the class. Make friends to do the HW with, its kinda fun. Also, I thought he was hilarious. All around a straight G, 10/10 recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Overall great professor. Very clear about the expectations and what will be on the exam. He is also funny but some don't understand his humor
Theres few grades in the grade book other than tests. The lectures are really boring. If you can take Masters I would.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: As a disclaimer I hate ochem and did very poorly in CHEM210. Funk was a good professor in my opinion, I just struggled with the material. His class was offered in-person and made it more engaging. The homework and practice exams are fantastic and prepare you really well for the exams if you study them and know what you're doing.

Funk is the best chem professor I've had at Penn State! His lectures are fairly easy to follow, and if you do the homework and practice exams the exams are not challenging. He takes questions directly off of homework and practice exams and puts them on the exams. I'm not finished his class yet but I currently have an A after two exams.

simply put, funk is too smart to be teaching. he's one of those profs that are there for research. the ta, lucas, however was wonderful. i did not learn a thing from funk, but learned a lot from lucas during his reviews. the lectures arent that helpful, the best way to learn and study is from the homework. format and content are very similar

Hate on him all you want, I thought Dr. Funk was a solid choice for 212. His lectures are intense, but extremely useful for the exams. Speaking of, the practice exams are almost exactly like the actual exams, so know those and you'll be fine. Even though it was hard to communicate with him outside of class, I still found myself doing well in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Horrid. A nightmare. Went off on tangents in class like it was actual material. If you don't arrive 15 min early you might as well not go because then the front seats are taken and you can't read the board. He doesn't explain why, just says things are the way they are. Made me want to become an art major.

Prof Funk does not answer emails and during online learning has done nothing to assist students learning from home. He just talks during class and you never know what is important and he has even said that the lecture points wont really help you which is his only form of "notes". Exams are the same as the homework and that is the only thing good.

I had Funk for 210 and 212 and got an A in both. His lectures are hard to follow because he just writes things on a chalkboard, and will talk for 20 minutes about something you do not need to know. Orgo is hard, you need to put in the work but just really study the topics on the homeworks and practice exams and the you will do well on the exams.

I had Dr. Funk for both Chem 210 and 212. He is an incredible professor and is so passionate about chemistry. This class is hard only if you don't put in the effort. Exams are very similar to the homework and practice exams, so if you do them and understand them you will be fine! Office hours are extremely helpful, I HIGHLY recommend going!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk is a very nice guy overall and is very passionate about organic chemistry. His examples in class and humor made it more enjoyable than the previous ochem prof I had. Tests are basically the homework, so if you can do those, you're set. Only thing he did not teach well was NMR. Practice outside of class and you'll be fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk is an amazing organic chemist (unbelievably smart). You MUST do work outside of class, but he provides you with everything you need to get an A. It's up to YOU to get the A by going to office/ TA hours. He will tell us in lecture exactly what's on the test and most the mechanism/ synthesis are directly from the notes/ textbook problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: By far the most interesting professor I have ever had. He is a great guy, very intelligent, and hilarious but his class is really hard. I like him as a person but he refuses to teach any other way than just drawing mechanisms all over his chalk board at lightening speed. Barely any homework assignments and basically only tests. Good luck!

Funk is a cool guy, but he takes all of his notes on the chalkboard and talks like Forrest Gump, sit at the front if possible! Go to all lectures, office hours and GSGs and put in the work. Exams are VERY similar to practice exams and homeworks; know those and youll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk is a great professor and really cares about his students. Class is difficult as will all organic chemistry classes, but if you put in the work you will do well. GSG sessions and office hours are extremely helpful.

Dr. Funk is by far my favorite professor at PSU. <3 You must go early to sit in the front because he writes everything in chalk, but he gives you all the resources necessary to succeed in the class and has a great sense of humor. You can tell he loves organic chemistry and you will succeed if you put in work and pay attention to his lectures!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk was very good at teaching the material even though it can be hard to understand. The people who complain about 210 or 212 being hard are also the ones who talk and don't pay attention in class. If you show up, take good notes, listen to the hints he gives about exams, do homeworks and practice exams, there's no reason you can't get an A.

reviews.comment: do not skip lecture. every single exam question is either EXACTLY or slightly modified from the notes, homework, or practice exam.
