reviews.comment: Funk is a quirky guy, but is a decent professor. Pay attention take good notes and study. I had him for 210 and 212. OChem is not easy but with work you will get a decent grade. His grade scale and policies make getting a decent grade attainable.

I had Funk for 210 and 212. Takes a long time to get used to his style. I learned most of the course through the textbook. Going to class is good for figuring out what specific things he wants you to know for the exam. Both classes are a ton of work. There's a pretty sweet curve at the end which is nice. was an OK-ish experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Dr Funk for both Chem 210 and 212. His teaching style takes some getting used to but just make sure to go to class & take as clear of notes as possible. The material is tough. He puts everything he thinks is important on the hw. He gives you last years exam as a practice exam. Study the heck out of those and you'll be fine. GO TO THE REVIEWS
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk was a very nice guy but his lectures are all over the pass, it's very hard to follow. I taught myself most of the material. Very mechanism heavy, but written exams and partial credit (if you're lucky). Homework assignments about every 2-3 weeks. Final exam grade can replace a midterm grade. He is still probably the best 210 prof PSU has.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Raymond Funk has the most substantial BDE ever recorded. His lectures are hilarious and you can tell Dr. Funk truly loves organic chemistry!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Felt like an honors level class. He gives examples in class for about 50 minutes and that sums up his teaching. Examples with a tiny bit of explanation. You have to figure the rest out on your own. He is a lenient grader and everything is open-ended. Replaces your worst grade with the final. The class average was prob a 60 and he curved minimally
Could not understand what he was saying, he made concepts harder than they were. Good guy who would help you a lot in office hours. You can see he is trying.

Overall A really amazing professor. Dr. Funk is super knowledgeable and legitimately funny. The tests were completely fair as they were problems you have seen before and he literally gives you 5-10% of what will be on it as long as you are paying attention. YOU HAVE TO SIT UP CLOSE otherwise you will have a hard time hearing/seeing.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He does not care about if students understand what he is talking about. So go to TA office hours! He is very hard to hear because he doesn't like the microphone and he only uses the chalkboard so sit close to the front. Even though he is not a good teacher he is a very easy grader and will give points where you don't really deserve it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Funk's lectures are extremely disorganized and sometimes can be tough to follow. He follows the textbook in sequential order, so definitely purchase that and read it. Funks exams are difficult but fair. His partial credit policy is more than reasonable, and homeworks/ practice exams/ textbook problems are all fair game. Sit in front of the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: 4 words to describe Funk's class: WAY BETTER THAN MASLAK. Unfortunately did not receive an A- because I had too many finals on one day but it is achievable if you are good at memorizing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Chem 212 is easier than chem 210 and you can actually understand it. None of the notes are online so you have to go to class unless you get nitanny notes. I got a B in 210 and an A- in 212, Funk isnt bad but this class is really just memorizing reactions and how the mechanisms work.

Dr. Funk seems like a great person. But not the best professor. He definitely knows what he is talking about but seems to have trouble conveying it in a simple way. He gets off track fairly often and I struggled to follow along sometimes. There is a ton of material and if you took CHEM 210 with Maslak you have no basis for success in 212.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: God, I hated this class so much. This class is so much harder than Chem 210. Get ready to memorize a ton of reactions and pKas. Funk is super rude and completely talks over you, however, he is still kinda funny. His teaching assistants do a better job of explaining the material. Would never take again. EVER.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk was a pretty chill professor. Be prepared to learn the most of the material on your own outside of class. I recommend the McMurry book as that's the only book I used, and it summarized the reactions nicely.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He's a funny guy and clearly knows what he's talking about. Makes the lectures more entertaining than the average professor. He probably jokes about questions you ask him as a defense mechanism to the stupid questions that have been asked to him over the years. Ochem is never going to be a easy A but he's fair, cares and loves his dogs. Dogsbest
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Literally impossible to ask questions to either inside or outside of class. He literally turns everything into a joke, however, the TAs are extremely helpful, and it is very hard work, but if you put the time in it's worth it in the long run.
Be careful when taking this class.....
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I LOVE Dr. Funk. He is an absolutely amazing professor and yeah organic chemistry isn't easy but he makes it 100000x more enjoyable, understandable, and manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: If you're interested in chemistry I'd strongly recommend taking this class. Dr. Funk is  a funny guy and his understanding of organic chemistry has incredible depth. If you've taken honors 110/112 (Gen Chem) at PSU, this class isn't graded quite as leniently but in my opinion the information is far and away more interesting to learn.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Funk is everything you hope a professor will be. Sure, his class is hard, but that is the nature of organic chemistry. This class is much easier than Chem 210 if you keep up with the work. Exams are free-response which provides ample opportunity for extra credit. Gives good practice exams. Curves grades in favor of those who go to office hours.

Funk is without a doubt a great professor. He skips a lot of key points in reactions and expects you to figure it out yourself, which is tough. 90% of your grade are exam based. Exams are incredibly tough. Be able to APPLY reactions and mechanisms as it is NOT straight memorization. I put a ton of work in and still did not get a decent grade.

The class is basically memorization on steroids. It covers a lot of material, but if you can commit the time to memorizing the reactions and pay attention in lectures to the names of the molecules it isn't the worst.

Grade was 90% exams and while averages for exams were low 60s he only curved the class minimally. If you don't get front row seat in lecture you wont see what's happening because he only uses chalkboard to write reactions. People said office hours helped. Assumes that you'll understand everything so quickly, dislike his arrogance.

Funk is an INCREDIBLE professor. Expect a challenge, as it's still organic chemistry, but he makes the subject as easy as it could ever possibly be. He's hilarious and keeps his lectures dynamic. If you stay on top of the material, you really should have no problem.

This guy knows and LOVES ochem. He is a good lecturer although they can get a little messy on the blackboard. Overall if you pay attention in class and go to office hours, it is not too difficult to succeed in this class. Also if you get an A in the class he hires you as a grader :) Which is nice.

Funk is an amazing 212 teacher. His notes are extremely scattered and it seems like each reaction has no rhyme or reason. But, you have to break down the reactions by type/functional group and it'll make sense. Whoever memorizes orgo reactions doesn't understand chemistry. Very good teacher.

I despised this class and the way he taught it. Just a bunch of raw memorization of reactions and their mechanisms. Literally classes were just drawing out reactions upon reactions with little to no explanation as to the reasonings behind what was happening. Worse is that Funk then asserted that he "doesn't focus on memorization". ...b.s.

Dr. Funk is a brilliant professor for a difficult class. It's really not his fault that the class is hard (it's organic chemistry). His material is very clear-cut, meaning he won't throw you a curveball on the test. If he covers it in lecture, it's fair game, but he'll never "surprise" you. By far my favorite professor I've ever had at Penn State.

Dr. Funk gives amazing lectures that are hilarious and informative. Instead of letting students get away with trying to memorize the material, he would do his best to teach his students how to understand it and apply these concepts to new scenarios. If you are interested in actually learning organic chemistry, take this class.
210 is a hard class but Funk makes it easy. He's super scattered with his lectures but if you rewrite your notes you should be okay. I def would take him over any other teacher.

Pros: Partial Credit, grades on a curve I averaged 50 and passed  Cons: No ppt slides If you're doing chem 210 for your first time just be sure to read the book and do the practice problems at the end of each section. The more practice you do(rent the solutions manual so you can get more practice) the better you'll do.

Dr. Funk is fantastic. He's very enthusiastic and always willing to help. All of his notes are done on the chalkboard during lectures, which I personally learn really well from. While the material is certainly difficult, Dr. Funk makes conceptual understanding easier and the course more fun overall.

Ochem is a really hard class but Dr. Funk does his best to explain concepts clearly. His exams are fair & all open-ended which actually works in your favor bc partial credit. I would def recommend taking him over Radosevich. You'll learn a lot more and actually understand what is going on in class!
Difficult class to say the least but if you keep up with the material you will do fine. What saved me is the final which is worth a large chunk of your grade.

honestly worst class i ever took at PSU. he uses a chalkboard for notes, which i found really hard to learn from. his hw are ok, but he only grades one problem. his exams are not multiple choice. very strict with partial credit. overall, not a bad person, just a bad teacher for me.
Worst class I have ever taken.  Avoid his section!!!

He uses examples from the textbook on exams. If you go to class, Listen, have good notes, and look at the text book, you will do well. He gives you a practice exam and if you go to the practice exam review sessions, he gives you pointers about what will actually be on the exam Monday. If you failed it's because you just didn't listen.

Scribbles all over a chalkboard during lecture. Poor preparations for exams. Puts one practice exam online with answers but no solutions or explanations. If you miss a lecture your only resource is the textbook but often he discusses topics not in the book. Avoid definitely
4 exams. Final grade replaces your lowest exam grade. Homework points are used to boost your grade. Not a bad pofessor but attend PSU know how sessions and you should be okay. Lots of memorization

His lectures are very incoherent. He only writes on the chalkboards, and he only writes disorganized mechanisms. He refuses to speak up so you can hardly hear him. He values strict memorization above learning concepts. The man knows his material, but he is terrible at teaching. If you take him, be sure to study the book and you'll be okay
Funk is an awesome teacher; easy to understand, very enthusiastic, and willing to help if a student shows initiative.
Funk is a def for chem212, all notes are hand written though so must go to class.  very straight forward of what he wants on the test, practice exams are the same questions as the test.

Very good teacher. Presents the material in an interesting way and if you take his advice and learn the underlying concepts of his class then you'll do well on his tests. Willing to help as long as you're willing to show up at his office hours and listen, his review sessions are extremely helpful.

Boring class. Not much you can do to make it better. I think I may retain some info as a result of Funk and his teaching style. Exams are fairly straightforward and requires strict memorization of ALL of the reactions.
Funk is a fair professor that actually makes the normally boring material interesting. Definitely take him if you have to take CHEM 212.

I had both funk and masters, hands down funk was a far better teacher of a different caliber. Masters insists on groups and gives too much homework often. Funk's tests are not only easy but his style of teaching helps you LEARN instead of just memorize. TAKE him instead, even if you have to walk far out of your way.

Avoid Funk and his classes if you can. I had him both for Chem 210H and 212. Both were very hard, and I could barely pay attention in class because I was too busy scribbling down his messy notes. He said he was going to equilibrate our Chem 212 grades since Masters' class is so much easier, but our grades came out before they even had their final.

Prof. Funk is a good teacher overall. His test are difficult and are all partial credit, not multiple choice. Lectures are mandatory since he likes to present the material in his own way. Overall, he is a funny guy and a good teacher, but the class is difficult.
Has the same mannerisms as Dr. Cox on Scrubs, but looks like David Lettermen. Not a bad Teacher
Overall, not a bad teacher. Although less mean than Maslak, his class is harder. 3 people are supposed to get an A out of the whole class. You have to go to lecture, cant just read th beek

This guy is fun, and enthusiastic about chem, no boring lectures here. Pretty clear in his explanations, and very helpful outside of class. The material is not that hard to understand, but there is a lot of it. Definitely read the text before coming to class, and you will succeed. The quizzes are harder than the final. Take it if you can.

Funk is the man   he loves what he teaches and it shows  class is interesting  he is a funny guy.  Organic chem is hard but if you study you can do well he also drops one low exam grade.  take organic chem with funk!!

Has quite a passion for organic chem.  Explanations are clear, although he does go through the material quickly.  Bi-weekly quizzes instead of midterms, giving you plenty of chances to bring up your grade.  A bit difficult to approach; he is very smart and can make you feel very small, but you can see the TA instead.  A must for any chem major.

I think Funk is a really good teacher. Ive learned so much this semester. Its a hard course so go to your TA's office hours and go to recitaton and youll be fine. you get practice tests that prepare you for the actual tests. Funk likes to make little asides that are actually kinda cool so you dont get bored.

The material is really tedious and takes awhile to learn. Reading the book and attending lecture are absolutely necessary to pass the class. But he makes it easier with free-response exams, in which partial credit is possible. The little bit of "extra-credit" homework can drop you a grade point though, as it did to me.

This man lives and breathes chemistry, you can tell he is passionate about the material.  His lectures and exams closely follow the text, and the exams aren't that bad if you've studied.  Take him if you can!
The class was very challenging but if you work hard you'll be fine.  Do as many practice mechanisms and synthesis as possible!
Great guy makes class interesting.  The tests are hard and you need to read the book a lot.  Also the tests are not multiple choice.  If you want/ need to learn Ochem take Funk!
Decent teacher, but OChem II is such a pain in the ass.  Why do they make Ch Es take it?
AMAZING teacher. Challenging class, but very interesting. He loves what he teaches.
Great professor, very motivating. Does not write recommendations so if you are planning to go to med/grad school, don't count on him
He keeps things interesting in class, and uses real world examples of why what we learn is useful.  He's great in an honors class where you have more interaction.
Very intelligent.  Did well explaining material.  Exams were difficult, but he prepared students well for them.  Overall he was a good teacher.  I learned quite a bit.

Funk teaches mainly by throwing examples on the chalkboard and expecting you to read about why it works.  He often defines terms once and then flings them around like we're familiar with them already.
He was a really good lecturer. He actually used the chalkboard! He knew what he was talking about and his lectures were interesting. If I had a chance to take him for another class; I would.

One of the best professors at Penn State, his lectures were very clear and easy to understand, and interesting! I fully recommend taking his class, and the written tests are not nearly as bad as people say they are (partial credit). You will learn a lot from him.
DEFINITELY looks like David Letterman.
could explain things really well but was arrogant

Awesome organic chem teacher, very clear and easy to understand. His tests are all written, but a lot easier than mulitple choice (but still not easy). If you can take his class, take it! (He also looks like David Letterman).
pretty good.  seems kinda full of himself which makes him unapproachable... but i learned a lot.  funny guy too.  i'd recommend him to others. just dont be scared to ask questions.
definitely the best organic chem professor at penn state. the course is interesting and he is entertaining. you have to put in a lot of work to come out with a good grade.

Dr. Funk is a great guy, he cracks jokes all the time and usually lecturs all class.  He can be intimidating and his exams are hard but you get what you put in, don't expect a cake walk but if u study hard, you can really end up with a good grade.  Best of all he speaks English so take him instead of Zhang whatever..
Professor Funk is the greatest organic teacher ever - helpful, clear, super intelligent, and HOT.

Dr. Funk is the only good organic teacher at Penn State. I rated him for 38H and I'm giving a higher rating now. He's better in a large lecture, and really gets the class involved. He leaves no stone unturned.
DO NOT TAKE HIM for chem 39. He was very disorganized and the tests are short answer!

Dr. Funk frequently uses real-world examples and recent discoveries to demonstrate the dynamics of organic chemistry.  His humor is a welcome addition to the class, but I must agree that sometimes it seems as though student questions are not appreciated.
No Comments

Dr. Funk's lectures are awesome, and he presents the material in an excellent way. You will not fall asleep in his class. He is also funny. The only problem is that he's not that great about answering your questions (he does try though). Ask your TA.
No Comments
Dr. Funk is very disorganized in class and refuses to be helpful.

One of the worst professors I have had. His lectures are boring and content-heavy, making it hard to actually learn anything in class. He is knowledgeable and passionate about the subject, but is just really bad at teaching. Going to office hours is a waste of time; more often than not, you will leave more confused.

I really enjoyed taking fin 406 with this professor. The class was very organized and the lectures were easy to follow. The professor did a good job using real world examples to explain the material, which helped me understand better
This professor is very good. The class is clear and easy to follow. I learned a lot and would recommend this course.
Would recommend. Study and you will do well. Tests are not that hard as I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Had to LD this class because it was going to tank my GPA. I had him during the fall semester and thought something was wrong with me because I have a pretty good GPA, but I bombed the first two exams in his class. Glad to know it's Freddy's incompetence as a professor, not a lack of intelligence on my part.
I am not sure what the school is doing, to be honest. He does not know how to teach. He has an ego that is unmatched.  smeal five in five, not with this guy
I mean, the rest of the reviews are very accurate....

The rest of the reviews don't lie, this is the worst finance professor at PSU. Have fun failing the exams. You will not do good. A+ students don't even do good in this class. One of those guys that has a class of failing students and blames it on them. Buddy, you're the common denominator, we all do great with other professors in finance.

reviews.comment: this guy does not CARE and just put tests as 100% of the grade. 4 tests during semester and he complains about not wanting to do work. do what you want with that info
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He was very nice when I had one-on-one interactions.  I stopped going to class because I genuinely did not know what was going on when I would try and pay attention.  I started trying to record him on AI to see if AI could help me.  Exams are so so hard.  The final was the easiest one because it was all MC.

I know some people have their thoughts about him but in my opinion, he was a great professor. He was always interested in what he was teaching and willing to help. He doesn't teach straight form the book, so I recommend going to class. Really nice guy and gave very generous curves and credit.

I never leave reviews but felt like I had to for him. He's a nice dude, but man is he not good at teaching. His lectures make no sense, and his exams are long and difficult. He curves but it's not worth it imo. I studied for hours upon hours for one of the exams and only got a B. That was with a 13 point curve and the avg was an 67 without it.

Doesn't teach or tell students what's on exams ended up blaming us because we did bad on an exam when he gave no specific expectations what we were supposed to know. Worst teacher I've ever had in 16 years of schooling.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: If I could leave an emoji here it would be the skull and bones. If you take this class you are just asking to have hours upon hours of extra work as you will have to teach yourself this class as he certainly doesnt. Safe yourself the trouble take someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE AT ANY COST! Exam times are too short (most students don't finish), and he does not articulate / format questions well at all. If you have a question about anything on the exam, he will ignore you. Teaches too many topics and tests on random details that don't actually matter. Does not give information about exam content.

In theory, this class should be easy, since Penn State students with other professors have excellent grades in it. Freddy, however, loves his bonds and wants to shove them down your throat. I have taken Calc 2 in high school, and have aced every class for the last 8 years. Freddy has plans to dump my GPA in the trash. I'll pray for you.

WORST PROFESSOR, he does not teach and his tests are not possible to finish in the time he gives. Does not care to actually teach and does not give any practice or exam prep. He is genuienly the worst prof

Worst professor I have ever had doesn't tell you what's on the exam posts review questions for the chapters that correlate with the textbook but after that your guessing what to study. 75% of the class is exams and he doesn't explain any of the concepts just talks about their real world relevance but none of the work we do has real world purpose.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a good chaotic man. He is a very caring man and gives great feedback. Very funny and is just a great man overall. He doesn't grade harshly, and is always willing to push back some due dates if you communicate your troubles. He is the prime example of someone who loves their job and what they do.

Inconsistent grading and did not follow clear grading rubric on syllabus. Graded according to how the wind blew and was incredibly inconsistent. Additionally was sassy to all students and wasted class time on irrelevant tangents.

Dr. Finch was a great professor. He challenged us but was very lenient about grades. I found the material interesting, and the class was stressful due to level of difficulty, but he explained everything and graded very easily.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Inspirational

reviews.comment: I loved Dr. Finch! I thought that his class was fairly easy and hard to do bad. The assignments weren't difficult as long as you can write decently in German. Some of the texts we read were hard to understand but I still found it to be easy overall. He is very flexible on assignments, and he is genuinely a fun guy that you can get along with.

I don't really know what to say. He knows what he is talking about but he's just a very odd man. Some days you leave class feeling berated and others he praises you. hot and cold but is always willing to give extensions and push back due dates. I kind of just feel indifferent, he was okay.

Sagan is amazing. Not sure why the other reviews say the class is boring, this class was the most interesting class I took this semester and made me WANT to go to class. Her slides are clear and the information you need for exams will be on them, make sure to take some notes during lectures even though she moves a little quickly. 10/10 recommend

I would absolutely never take this class again. Biggest waste of time learning about some irrelevant diseases. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS UNLESS YOU HAVE TO. Sagan is a sweet lady but she is impossible to reach outside of class and has a passion for the most boring subject on planet earth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class itself is easy, but attendance is *absolutely* mandatory and the lectures are very long. Dr Friant is very hard to reach outside of class, so if you need something urgently, you're on your own. All the notes are posted online, and there's options for extra credits, but grades get put in sporadically, so it'll tank unexpectedly. 6.5/10.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Friant's class is fascinating. If the subject is remotely interesting then I definitely recommend her class. It's a bit hard for a GenEd but very very interesting. Very relevant course material that changes perspectives. She is super sweet and is very funny as well. She also made some of the best cookies that I have ever consumed in my life.

Professor Foster is an amazing math professor. He really takes the time to explain everything and make sure you understand it. Go to his office hours if you have any questions, he's really helpful and just good at fully teaching the concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: hes the goat. Everything he says is gold. Very friendly and nice. Currently taking 141 with him and enjoying it.

His teaching is great. Textbook was not needed. He answered the nails sent quite on time. I didn't go for office hours but I'm pretty sure they were good. I've enrolled in his math 141 class again this semester
GOAT. Go to his office hours, as he helps a lot.

Professor Foster is the best! He teaches so well and takes time to make sure every student understands the material. Although it was his first semester this fall he did a phenomenal job. He would even you points back on exams if you just go talk to him about a specific problem during office hours.

Dr. Foster is an amazing professor. He encourages questions and ensures students understand the topic before he moves to the next topic. He is very receptive if you have qualms with the way your test was graded. If you are taking Calc 1/Calc 2, find a section taught by Dr. Foster.

Great professor and I highly recommend. The only thing I would say is that sometimes he gets very carried away with lectures and will explain topics too quickly. But if you ask him to explain he will sit with you and walk you through it.

Very good professor who cares about his students' success and makes sure to help anyone he can. Great lectures where he breaks down everything you need to know, and will happily walk you through something if you're confused. He makes sure you are well prepared for exams and tells you what will be on them and what you need to know.

He is a great professor who cares deeply about his students. For exams, he sends excellent review material, and his lectures reflect the exams well. He is always willing to provide help and explain content to his students. I would recommend his class to anyone.
He is the W
He is really good professor and he knows his content
Professor Foster is a very good professor and really cares about his students. He will do his best to help you and make sure you understand the material. I will be taking his classes again.
Pretty calm teacher, he lectures well. Attendance not really mandatory, and he is pretty easy to work with.

He never prepares or posts any notes on Canvas. The quizzes aren't based on the examples from class, and I hate that he showed us weird poses while teaching. He also always turns the question back to you instead of explaining it clearly.
Don't mind if you do calculation errors, he is very nice and easy to talk to. Knows a lot and answers any problems you ask. Homework is a bit heavy but grading isn't strict.

Had him at his first semester at teaching, good nonetheless. It was my first time consuming calc topics and he made it very easy to comprehend, seriously, he made calc A LOT easier. Attendance is not mandatory, but i highly encourage it as it made studying way quicker. Quizzes were easy and straightforward.
Very knowledgable on what he teaches, clearly explains the skills needed to succeed.

You must buy the course packet for the class that comes with the online textbook. Quizzes/homeworks where lower grades can be dropped. Overall easy but the exams can be very difficult. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you don't go there is no other way to get the notes unless you ask someone.
Honestly the GOAT for Econ 102.

Dave Brown is a really good teacher for Econ 102. He has you buy a note-taking book (you need it). The lectures are not mandatory, but they help a lot; they are really engaging, and as long as you take notes, you should be fine in the class. There are also lots of point oppurtunties with the homeworks and the GSG sessions.
If you study you should end with an A- or a B+. Super nice and funny guy. The exams can be tough but if you study and really try to understand the material you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Dave was my favorite instructor from my first semester here at PSU. After having him for Micro I made sure to take him again this semester for Macro.

Professor Brown is clearly very passionate about the material. His passion led me to minor in economics. He is funny, his classes are engaging, and the notes are easy to follow. I'd recommend going to every lecture, since I only missed a few and was confused when I missed, even with getting the notes from classmates. The second exam is the hardest.

I found the lectures to be quite engaging, and the content was relevant to our lives. The fact that he doesn't post the lecture notes is a little annoying, but if you go to every lecture (and actually pay attention), you should be fine. Also, the practice tests are helpful checks to make sure you know everything.

Class was very test heavy and overall grade was bascially your two midterm grades and the final. He drops the lowest two homework and quiz grades which is nice but overall doesnt significantly help your grade. I knew many people who struggled in this class even with attending lecture and the gsg sessions.

The people who say his class is too hard do no work and skip class all the time. If you show up and pay attention, you will do well. Three exams make up ~85% of your grade, so prepare for those if you want to do well. Some questions are tricky, but the test content is almost verbatim what the notes say. Get the notes packet, not the textbook.

I don't recommend this course to international students who are not yet fluent in english. Wait a semester. The questions are often tricky, so if your comprehension isn't perfect, it can be difficult. I especially experienced this on the first exam, which cost me the A in the course. Aside from that, it's a fairly easy class if you put in the work.

Dr. Dave is a good Econ teacher. You must buy a note pack created by him to really do good in classes. He doesn't take attendance, but it is still to not go to the lectures as that is literally where you get all the info. He gives homework's and quizzes like every 2 weeks, and the homework is graded pretty harshly. Tests can be confusing, it's ez
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Dave is a really good guy. He's funny and the lectures are manageable but can be boring. Good amount of homework and quizzes which are easy. 2 midterms and a final which were pretty difficult. If you put in the effort you will be fine. GSG is helpful. Overall it was an enjoyable course and he is definitely the best choice for 102
If you go to class and follow the notes you will be fine. Boring lectures but easy homework and quizzes and straightforward tests if you study.
Very cool guy. Sticks to the syllabus - show up and you'll do fine.

Getting A in phy 211 was easier than getting C+ in econ, exam is NOTHING like lecture!

80% of grade based on his hard exams, one exam goes wrong, u drop

He is so not understanding even tho lecture was light, I do not understand why is he acting like this, it's an intro class.

Dave Brown's class has probably been my favorite so far at PSU hands down. Microeconomics is a practical course, and Dave does a great job teaching it. He gives good lectures and has funny jokes. Take him for 102 and you're in for a treat.

I studied 3 weeks for the final and did worse then my Accounting 211 final that I spent 3 days on.. Even when you feel like you understand the material, the questions feel so tricky and far more difficult then they need to be. The prof seems enthusiastic during lectures, but isn't very nice when answering questions and is kinda short..

If you are taking any introductory econ class, he is your best option by far. His lectures are great, entertaining, and he is super funny. As long as you show up to class and pay attention you will do fine on the tests. There is not a lot of homework and he gives extra credit sometimes.

Not sure how some found this class so easy.  I am a straight A student that knows how to study and that wasn't enough for this class.  Dropped after 3rd exam before it tanked by GPA.  Would not recommend.

Dave is a great lecturer, funny too. Definitely get the course packet. He explains material well and makes it easy to take notes on the slides. Don't skip lectures because he doesn't post lecture anywhere. If you are paying attention in class, Dave makes it the easiest course you'll take in college. Concepts are easy, there's just a lot.

The concepts were not too difficult, but volume of material on each exam was overwhelming. Lectures were somewhat entertaining, but the instructor lacked gentleness answering questions. Office hours were inconvenient, with homework assigned Wednesday and due Monday and none in between. Exams were very tricky and required near perfect understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dave is a great professor. His lectures were interesting and not boring. The first exam is easy but the second is not. Exams make up about 80% of your grade. There is only a few homework assignments and at home quizzes throughout the semester. Overall, great class.
Really great professor, humorous, and makes class fun.  Very lecture-heavy, study guides are very similar to exams.
Buy the textbook, it helps. He goes fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He's a super nice guy! I would definitely recommend attending every class because a lot of the material on the exams is his exact words from class.

Dr Dave is fairly good at explaining things. It can be easy to get lost in the wording of economics, but he does a decent job breaking things back down into basics to make the content easier to understand. The tests and homework feel a bit easy compared to the confusion I sometimes feel during the lecture. He's the best Econ 102 prof, though.

Man, where do I begin.....When I arrived in August, I was sooooo nervous about economics, but Dave Brown changed my life forever. From the garbage truck example to the Natty Lite jokes, his class just clicked. I'll never see life the same. Thank you, Dave Brown, for the impact. I will never be the same again. You are my idol.

Dr. Dave is so funny! I don't find Econ very difficult and I could get by without going to lecture but I literally want to go to them anyway because he makes class so fun. Econ can be boring but he does a great job making class interesting. Decided to take his 104 class too! This guy should have 5 stars.

Dr. Dave is an amazing professor and makes classes very entertaining. You can tell he is very passionate and always makes class fun. As one of my first professors at PSU, he has been an amazing experience. But his exams suck and bring down your grade a lot—very hard exams, but he gives lots of materials to help.

Dr. Dave is def the best econ professor at psu and if you study and do well on the weekly quiz and homework, you'll get at least a B, but probably higher. Def do the review session the sunday before the exams and study the various study materials he provides for the exams. know the mutiple choice and just get through the first 2 exams(final online)

Dave Brown is the best econ professor. I've heard horror stories from friends about the other ones. I am curently taking this class and he makes the lectures super engaging. someone said that the final exam is online... but he never directly said that so I don't know. can anyone who took this class previously like this post if the final is online

TAs for this course have been disappointing. The Zoom links are consistently late for review. The grading has been unreasonably harsh. Dr. Dave needs to show more understanding of his students. I've worked hard to maintain a 4.0 GPA, and it's frustrating to think this class could jeopardize that in my final year simply because of poor instruction.

If you're an underclassman and comparing Econ teachers, Dr. Brown is the best option. His lectures are engaging and pretty easy to follow along with because he has a guided note packet for both Econ 102 and 104. There are plenty of grading opportunities because there are weekly online quizzes and homework assignments.

Dr. Brown is a really incredible econ professor. His lectures are engaging and interesting. You get guided notes to fill it so it is much easier to listen. His tests can be a little tough, but as long as you study and really try to understand the material, you will be totally fine.
He's very nice and wants students to succeed. Funny and entertaining lectures, fill in the blank notes!

Basically writing the entire class of notes . Your entire grade is basically exams and they're borderline unfair. First exam wasn't bad. Second Exam was extremely hard . Doesn't curve or offer extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is a fine professor and not super boring but lectures are very fast paced and it's just him talking and you writing the whole entire class. Exams are very difficult for no reason and you only get 50 minutes for 45 questions including open ended. I wouldn't take it with him again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: For econ being a hard subject he made it a lot easier to understand.
His lectures were really interesting and he was really passionate so it was easy to pay attention. The assignments were a little hard but all of them but a couple exams were take home.

Dr. Brown is the best Econ prof at PSU. His lectures are funny and engaging. He is super down to earth and makes a 350 person class feel much smaller. He is super knowlagable about econ and the real world connections it has. This class is very test-heavy, though it makes up 75% of your final grade. Just go to class and study and you will do great.

He is a really great professor and if you need any econ class TAKE IT WITH HIM. The other ones are significantly harder compared to him. As long as you go to class and look over the notes before a test it's easy to get an A or B in this class.

I took Econ 102 with Professor Dave Brown, and I can confidently say that he is the best economics professor. The homework he gives is amazing practice for exams. I recommend going to all his lectures. He teaches well and is always interesting. He takes feedback seriously and tries to improve every day! I will be taking Econ 104 with him as well!

Dave is an amazing professor! He always made lectures super engaging and fun by using video/movie clips, real-life examples, and current events (+ just had a great sense of humor). Exams make up ~80% of your grade, though the final was online. Textbook not required at all. I hope to take him again in future econ classes.

Dave was an awesome teacher and was very much engaged with the class. His class was meant to take very seriously as the exams are difficult and cover a lot of content. If you study and work hard, you will do good!

Dave's econ102 is the easiest by far, his teaching is awesome easy to follow along (guided notes) hw and quizzes dont really matter (20% of grade for like 20 assignments) 3 exams 3rd being your final, show up to class and take good notes, there is tons of resources to help you watch the gsg recordings before the tests and you will do awesome!

His lectures make a hard course and complex topics easier to understand. There is no participation grade, however, if you don't show up it will be more difficult for you. Will be taking him next semester too in another course!

Dr. Dave is great! The class is not bad at all if you actually go to class and watch the TA gsg review before the exams. He makes it impossible to not pass. He gives away answers to the homework's and quizzes every single time. There's also extra credit! Don't buy the text book you will not use it at all. Everyone that says he is hard is lazy asf

He trys to make the class fun he seems like such a nice guy, the tests are pretty hard. The homework is also, and there are not many points overall, so do well on all quizzes and homework. I wish the exams were just a little easier, then i would 100% take this course again.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Brown makes the lectures engaging, but the exams can be quite tricky. To do well, go to class, study the slides, and use resources like unstuckstudy ai for extra practice. The course is challenging, but worth it if you put in the effort.

Dr. Dave was very good at lecturing.  Super easy to learn from.  Exams could be difficult sometimes. Some questions were just confusing and did not feel like they connected well.  However, Dr. Dave is a great teacher.  Highly recommend any class he teaches.

Brown is an amazing professor. He clearly loves economics and teaching it. He explains everything he does without droning and is very engaging. You take all of your notes by filling out his note packet and nothing is posted online, so make sure you go to every lecture or at least have a friend who can send you notes!
Dr. Dave might be one of my favorite professors at PSU. No attendance was taken, but I still went to class because he makes class fun. First test was easy, but next 2 were bad.

I am not sure how people are saying he is amazing. His class is extremely difficult, the exams are extremely hard. I studied a lot and still never did good. A B+ is a 88 which is just extreme. The exams are super specific things from lectures and his lectures are super long. There is a lot of content and you tested on everything. DO NOT TAKE.

Overall he is a great professor and very accommodating. However, his tests are very difficult and he does not curve them. The online quizzes and homework help your grade though, but it is mostly test heavy. The 1st exam is easy but midterm 2 and the final are difficult even if you do the practice supplements.
Worst class ever. Doesnt curve and his averages are always below a 70. None of the professors for econ are good anyway so it doesnt even matter who you take.

Dave is a fantastic professor; he goes out of his way to make class interesting. I wish I had paid more attention and actually attended class when I had Dave, as I think my grade and understanding of economics would've been a lot better. Go to class, study the notes, and you will be fine.

Dr. Dave is such an econ nerd and sometimes it's hilarious the way he eagerly explains things. You can tell he enjoys teaching. He makes lectures tolerable and makes assignments as simple as possible for us. Going to GSG sessions and doing the supplements helps to study for the exams! Sometimes he does give extra points to help boost our grade.
So funny and interesting lectures.

Best Choice if you have to take this class. Made lectures interesting, but you NEED to do well on exams. if you're willing to spend Liontutors helps for exams, and the free exam reviews are also helpful. Nice guy and tried to make the boring material econ is at least a tiny bit interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dave Brown is a perfect teacher with a great personality. Lectures are engaging. My biggest complaint are the exams. The multiple choice on the exams have questions that are vaguely related to the notes. Many of the questions have answers that can barely be located as one sentence in the most random part of your notebook. Reread chapters daily.

Dr. Brown can explain the materials and the concepts in a very great and fun way. However, the exams were so difficult especially the first one which didn't have enough time to solve. At the end of the semester, he made the final online which helped us a lot. Dr. Brown made me love economics.

This guy is a great teacher during lecture and makes the class more enjoyable. He knows what he is talking about and engages with the class. Although, the exams he has are very difficult, the open-ended portions are very easy if you studied, however, the mcq section is very difficult regardless if you studied or not.

102 is tough, and the options for who teaches the class aren't any better Brown is your best option but this is not me boosting him. Extremely hard exams, tedious homework graded on accuracy, boring lectures. Notes packet isn't worth it, just type your notes from the slides, save yourself $40. He prob made final online because everyone was failing.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I would definitely take Dave again. His exams were moderately hard but he gave lots of extra credit and was engaging during class.

David Brown is a great professor who makes lectures interesting. However, I do think that the exams are a bit difficult though. I think the homework and quizzes are pretty easy and can bring your grade up a little bit. He doesn't really offer much extra credit, he's only given a maximum of 2 points. The course overall was good.

good professor, and made lectures interesting. attendance isnt mandatory, but he doesnt post notes, and some test questions are from class. grade depends on your exams. 2 midterms and then 1 final (open book). a little bit of homework and quizzes, but not a lot and like 2 points of extra credit.

great professor. attendance isn't mandatory, but i understood better the material i was in class & heard him teach.  you def have to show up to really do well. he makes lectures engaging!!  2 in person exams, 1 final that was online/open note. 6 hws, 8 quizzes, 2 drops each. they're the only grades so you have to do well on exams.

I loved Dr. Dave I'm not very good at ECON but he made this class fun and engaging. I would recommend going to all the classes or at least having a friend in the class to give you notes if you miss. He doesn't give out the notes from past classes. There were 3 exams and around 12 HW/quizzes. Just put in the work and try and you'll do great!

Dave Brown is among my favorite professors. The note packet he has is all you need, attend his class and you'll pass relatively easily. He brings humor and realism to a boring day and makes economics enjoyable to learn. Great professor and a go-to for any econ class.

Dave was a great professor considering ECON is already a very hard class he definitely made it easier. If you are taking ECON 102 I would 100% take it with Dave. Attendance is not mandatory, he gives a lot of extra credit, there were 2 exams and 1 final. I would definitely take a class by him again.

Dave was such a funny guy and did a lot to make his lectures memorable. You should buy the physical note packet. I bought the digital and never got it, which lead to my poor grade in the class. Ultimately he ended up rounding my grade.

Professor Brown is really nice and he tries his best to joke and relate the info to real-world scenarios. His homework and quizzes are hard, even with notes. The wording is weird and makes it hard to get correct. The exams are very difficult and most of the questions are vaguely related to what was taught in class. Buy the note packet, not the book
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: i had dave for 102 last semester and took him again because he is the best. go to class even though its not mandatory, he is so funny and tries to make the material interesting with videos. i will say that the exams were a little difficult, so go to class and take good notes. he drops the 2 lowest hw and quiz scores on canvas so that helped a lot

It's true, Dave Brown is the goat. Lectures are kinda mandatory as he does not post the notes online unless you get them from a friend. Great prof and does extra research when kids have questions. Homework and quizzes are all online. DO NOT be fooled by how easy the first exam is, the second exam and final are pretty brutal.

As someone who has previously struggled and just not enjoyed previous Econ classes, Professor Dave was a good change of pace. I found his lectures engaging and not a complete bore to sit through. I will say to not be fooled by the first exam as it was quite easy. The next two were incredibly difficult.

Dave Brown made lectures really interesting and you can tell he actually cares about what he is teaching. Exams are tricky so make sure you put in the work to study for them. He provided extra credit (which actually saved my grade) when people did bad on an exam. Definitely take him!

Amazing professor is passionate about economics and knows what he is talking about. He does research on questions he does not know the answer too and sends them to the class through emails. Gave extra credit and assigns a few homework's and quizzes. Exams are hard so study a lot and go to his office hours.

Easily one of if not the best professor I had at Penn State so far. He makes Economics interesting. It is all lecture but the way he teachers it is very easy to comprehend and pay attention to. Great Professor and class.

Dave's class is a good class and not too hard. Attendance is pretty much mandatory because the class is all notes. Take this class with a friend or two or make sure to make friends the first couple weeks so you won't miss notes and can rely on each other. Overall, a good class but make sure to be prepared for lots of notes and study for exams well.

Great professor. If he is asked any questions in class that he doesn't know the answer to, he will do research and send out an announcement to the class with the answer and his sources for the answer. Brought in bills, coins, whatever other forms of currency or precious metals and let students inspect them. 10/10 recommend.

Overall, Professor Dave is a great guy. Kinda funny to listen to in class. Exams get harder and the final is absolutely horrible. Took him for 102 in the Fall and taking him again for 104, overall decent experience.
great and funny guy, makes lectures interesting. still a fairly difficult class and tests get harder as year go on. Would recommend to take him over any other Econ teacher, for 102 or 104.

Took him for 102 and am glad I took him for 104. If you took 102, the class is set up the same way, except exams are in-person. Charismatic lecturer, but the content is much harder than 102. Tests (except the 1st) can be pretty hard, so study well for those (GSG reviews helps). Attendance isn't mandatory, but I'd go for the content & entertainment.

Dr. Dave is a great lecturer, but an okay professor. It's clear to me he is really uninvested in the class a minute before time starts and a minute after it ends. Of course, **every minute of class he is a fantastic lecturer and great presenter (10/10),** so make sure to go to class, since outside of it, he seems very apathetic towards teaching.

He is a funny guy, cares about his students, makes great lectures, and doesn't try to trick you on exams. he practically sets up success for you, all you have to do is take notes, pay attention, and care about you grade. The syllabus leaves room for dumb mistakes, just keep in mind you are better off not making them.

Dave Brown--at the time I took this class--was the only option other than Goff. From what I have heard, Goff was terrible; if you have a choice, avoid him at all costs and take Dr. Dave instead. He is super chill, plays lots of great videos, will answer questions (in person is recommended), and has a relaxed grading policy. READ THE SYLLABUS!

If you are reading this and debating whether to take him for Econ102 or Econ104, do it. He actually makes the lectures interesting unlike many other Econ professors. The notes packet was easy to follow along with and used as a good studying tool. Tests used to online but now they may be in person

Dave Brown taught me Econ 102 last semester. He is a good teacher and is clearly passionate about what he teaches. His exams are TOUGH. Often times I had a hard time studying because I knew what was on the exam most likely would not be in the note packet. His quizzes and homework help because there is a lot and they are decently easy.

Overall Dr. Dave is a great professor. We have guided notes during his lectures. There is no textbook required. But there is a good amount of homework and quizzes. The only reason i didn't give him a 5 is because of how heavy he has the final and midterms weighed into our final grade.

Dr. Dave is an incredible professor in almost all aspects. If you plan to take Econ 102, make it a priority to get Dave. You don't "need" to show up to class, but to get a good grade you definitely should. He makes lectures enjoyable and always plays videos. Not an easy course but if you do the work, expect to get at least a B

Very good professor, as long as you go to lectures and take notes you should be fine. I will admit lectures are sometimes boring buts its economics what do you expect?  I barely studied and ended up getting an A.  There are also guided study groups weekly that you can go to if you are struggling and exam reviews. Very little homework or quizzes.

Easy class except for the final exam, I had an A- that dropped to a B- from it. The other midterms were easy, some math but nothing past high school alg. The $40 packet is helpful, but not necessary if you can type fast (this also helped me on the final because of command F). Have access to a printer for hw's. All tests and hw are open note.

Dave is an extremely passionate professor and this is reflected in his lectures. He tries to help his students understand material in as many ways as possible by going over parts of the homework during class and creating practice exams and keys. Overall, he gives so many opportunities for his students to be successful if you pay attention and try!!

I am required to take econ as an engineering student, but really enjoyed this class this semester. His course is thoroughly outlines in the syllabus. All exams were online, and I didn't think the first two exams were too bad, but the final exam was honestly a little bit brutal. I would definitely recommend Brown over any ECON102 prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really liked Dr. Dave, but the final exam screwed me over. I had a 96 prior to it, and I studied like crazy. There were a ton of math questions and it brought my grade down to an 88. Other than the final, the class was not too bad and usually interesting to listen to. Make sure you take notes in the note packet and study for the tests.

Saw the ratings and thought he would be a great professor. Quickly realized he was the complete opposite. His lectures are insanely boring since you have to copy notes down the entire class. He also makes the exams IMPOSSIBLE. I have a 3.8 gpa and studied like crazy for the exam yet they were insanely hard. Everyone I know did horrible on every one
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Dave is the best ECON 102 professor at Penn State. It is a difficult class but if you pay attention it is very passable. Attendance is not mandatory but it benefits you to go. Overall great teacher.

dr. dave is awesome and tries to keep the material interesting with good examples and videos. definitely go to class even though attendance isn't required. the exams are online and doable, just pay attention in class and take notes. you have to buy his notes packet to bring to class everyday (like $50) that follows along with his powerpoint.

I really enjoyed this class but the tests were rather hard. I had never had econ before but I feel like the homework and online quizzes were doable. Overall Dr. Dave was a great professor and had a ton of amazing videos and examples to explain topics. Definitely the best econ professor offered for 102.
Dave Brown is the GOAT. Definitely take his class. Great professor. Online exams.

A very funny professor who makes you want to show up to lecture each day. The material is very interesting if you like econ. He shows a lot of videos that help you understand the material better. The midterms are extremely easy if you just show up to class. The final was online but quite difficult. Highly recommend this class to everyone.

Dr. Dave does is a passionate teacher who explains concepts in a very clear way and is always looking for ways to improve. The course is very graph and math heavy especially in the beginning, but if you show up to lectures and stay on track with work, you will succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dave Brown is the goat. If you're taking econ 102, take it with this man 100 percent. The class can get boring sometimes, but Dr. Dave makes it enjoyable. He drops the lowest 2 homeworks and quizzes, but it's very easy to fall behind on the course. Keep up with the material and you'll be fine.

Dr. Brown is the best professor I have had up to this point. His lectures are very intriguing and make you want to show up to class. This class can be a little difficult, especially the final, but if you go to every class and regularly review the material you are learning instead of cramming, it's not bad at all. Very enjoyable and I learned a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very funny, good videos during class. One of my favorite professors, made things easy to understand. Class should be easy if you actually study.

Dave is a GREAT profesor and for anyone wondering who to take ECON 102 with I would chose Dave. He makes the lectures understandable for people who have never taken economics before. His TAs are very helpful outside of class in the study groups. Overall if you want to do well in Daves class, go to the study groups and the classes.
He is a great guy. course material can be challenging. Exams are difficult and the wording is somewhat tricky. Attendance is not mandatory but go to class if you want to pass.

Dr. Dave is a great professor. Attendance is not graded, but going to the lectures really helps. He has detailed notes and explains everything well. The homeworks and quizzes aren't too hard, and the exams are online. He does a great job giving a base for future economics classes.

Dr. Dave is a really great professor. Econ 102 is pretty boring but he tries to make the class interesting and shows a lot of interesting videos. Exams make up pretty much all your grade, but they were open notes, online and really easy. He made a boring class, enjoyable to come to, so I would highly recommend taking his class.

Overall he was a really nice professor and kept class interesting and the lectures wasn't boring at all. On the other hand, the exams are very difficult and he doesn't provide enough practice questions prior to the exams in my opinion. The tests really make or break you so its important to study and take notes.

Dr Dave Brown is the best professor for ECON. Although his course is lecture heavy but the material and his way of explaining everything is just too good. The course packet is really helpful. His lectures are really engaging and have fun activities throughout the semester. HW and Quizzes aren't that bad. Exams are easy if you attend lectures daily.

Dr. Dave was awesome! Guided notes made reviewing easy and expectations for the class were clear. Not homework heavy at all, one or two assignments every few weeks. All the exams are online and open note, including the final exam. He is funny and engaging, I highly recommend!

Class is just going through a guided notes packet. he explains topics and gives good examples. he was really engaging and entertaining. I didn't study for this class until finals and I never found any content hard. just go over the notes briefly and you should be fine. always ready to answer questions at office hours or after class
Dr. Dave is a great teacher. He explains difficult-to-understand concepts in Econ very clearly and is a funny and genuine guy. I recommend to anyone taking the course

Dave is the greatest professor I've ever had. He's funny as hell and is great at explaining. All my friends that took other professors for the course were jealous. Economics isn't the most interesting topic, but Dave damn sure does everything to make it bearable. Exams were open note so show up and take notes and you're good.

You'll enjoy econ with Dr. Dave whether it's 102(micro) or 104(macro). He's really funny and tries to make an otherwise lecture-heavy class interesting including showing videos to keep the class engaging. All the exams including the final were online and open note so the class isn't really difficult. Make sure to use his note packet and take notes.

Dr. Dave is awesome.  He is funny and super excited to teach.  He uses a very helpful guided notes packet, and the class was easy to understand with no previous economics experience.  He has many memorable quotes and even deconstructed a sandwich in the middle of class.  He cared a lot and I recommend him to anyone that is taking an econ class.
Awesome teacher. Very easy to follow in class. His excitement about the material is passed down to his students. 10/10 recommend for everyone!

In case the other reviews didn't make it obvious enough, this man's really the GOAT. Class is all lecture and you fill in his note packet with fill in the blanks. Definitely don't need the textbook, just the course packet. Goes a little fast, but he's really passionate and entertaining to listen to. Not a lot of HW though, so study for the 3 tests.
All hail Dave Brown. Best teacher out there; would recommend taking him even if it's just as a gen-ed. Makes class super fun and the homeworks and tests are very easy.
DAVE BROWN THE GOAT
the goat

I looked at all of these reviews before taking his class and it gave me a false sense of hope. Although he is a nice guy and gave a couple points of extra credit from the exams, this was probably one of my hardest classes. The class is super boring and hard to pay attention to. There aren't that many assignments to boost your grade either.

I loved Dr Dave. He gives homework but always goes over it before its due. Very passionate about what he's teaching and very easy to pay attention to. Is a professor I would(and probably will) take again

Dave is one of the best lecturers I've ever had. He is intelligent, charismatic, and a great guy. I found the material covered in the class to be very interesting and information everybody should know. All being said, Dave's exams were very difficult. I wish his exams were more reasonable, however, I enjoyed going to his class very much.
He's a great professor. Really funny and easy to pay attention to. Make sure to look over the practice exams before the actuall exams. Overall, not too bad of a class.

Dave is a really nice guy and I find his lectures super helpful and informative. As long as you take the initiative to study for the exams you'll do well. He gives a bunch of sample MC questions and they aren't the same questions but it tells you what you need to know. He wants you to do well. Definitely recommend for 104.

Dave is a nice guy, he is just very boring. His lectures are long and boring but if you show up and do the work, you will be fine. Two tests and a non cumulative final. The second test had a low average which he curved by giving substantial extra credit on quizzes and homeworks. I went from a 92 to a 97 because of the extra credit. Boring but easy.

I would definitely not recommend Dr. Brown for any of your Econ classes. Listening to this guy talk gives me migraines. He goes way to fast during lectures and is a teacher who is too smart for his own job (not in a good way). Do yourself a favor and stay away from this guy making your semester a lot more stressful than it needs to b e.

Dr. Brown is an amazing lecturer and even plays music before class starts. Uses good examples and videos in lecture. Several homeworks/online Canvas quizzes (all open note & at home) with an extra credit assignment too. HW is directly related to lecture. Dr. Brown even does some of the HW in lecture with us! Needed note packet, never used textbook.

Dr. Brown is a really engaging professor and actually made economics interesting. Attendance is not graded, but go to class, otherwise you won't learn anything. I never used the required textbook, but the course pack of notes was extremely helpful.

I liked professor Brown a lot he was very engaging and knew what he was talking about. However I found it hard to understand sometimes and he goes kind of fast in class. There are study groups that you can go to that help a lot where you can get extra practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dave Brown is probably the best professor Ive had at PSU so far. Hes so funny and relates to everyone. Im a STEM major so Econ didnt relate to my major at all so honestly I stopped caring and didnt show up to lectures. I still passed with a C (thanks to him rounding my 68 up!). Buy the note packet, skip the textbook.

I went into this class, thinking that I would enjoy it and learn about something that I had never learned before; however, I was wrong. Dave Brown does not do a good job on preparing you for the final exams and midterms. Dave Brown's "textbook" where you fill in his notes is a waste of money. Save your time and money!!! SO MUCH UNNECESSARY STRESS!!

Dr. Brown's class is one of the classes that I look forward to attending every week. His lectures are inspirational and he gives out relevant examples that give the students goosebumps on how good it is. However, Dr. Brown is kinda cold when it comes to interaction with his students, making us feel like we are just one out of 400.

Dr. Dave is the best Econ 102 professor. Just make sure to attend the lectures and take good notes. Homeworks are super easy and he does give some extra credit. Just use the practice exams to prepare for the exams and you'll have an easy A.

Dr. Brown's lectures are incredibly engaging and interesting! As a person, I enjoyed listening to him and he made the subject interesting. However, the tests weren't like the practice supplements and often had obscure details on them. The exams also made up the great majority of your points. If you're looking for an easy A, don't take him.

Dr. Brown's lectures are very engaging and it is nice that he gives you the notes to write in. But, I would not take this class if you have no previous knowledge. Tests are very difficult and are nothing like the practice test supplements.

If you want to learn microeconomics, take this class. If you want an easy B-A, look elsewhere. Lectures are super enthusiastic, and you won't be tested on the information that you learn, but rather be forced to apply it to more intricate scenarios. Very test-heavy, and mind you the tests ARE difficult, but overall a great class.

Dr. Dave is an amazing, great guy who knows his stuff. Always has fun and interesting examples to help you learn the economic concepts. I enjoyed going to his class everyday and never skipped it. This is a class where you cannot get through by just attending lectures, do all supplemental practice work and attend GSGs and you will do just fine.

dr. dave is a really nice guy! his lectures were very interesting, and i have no interest in econ at all. i will say however, a lot of the class is exams (more than 70% of your grade) so if you arent the best test taker, i would possibly look into another prof.

He is the best econ 102 professor at Penn state, so pick him if you can. Your success in the class depends on your natural ability to understand the material. Some people get an easy A while others really struggle. Go to class and do not get behind.

Dave has great lectures and an engaging class. However, most of your grade comes from the exams. They aren't easy. The lectures and the note packet go by easy, then the exams f you over. Even with the help of lions tutors...

Dave Brown is a very great professor! I love his lectures and he is very engaging. However, I would not recommend taking this class if you aren't the best test taker. The exams are really hard but not impossible.

One of the best professors at Penn State. The people who say the exams are hard didnt study for more than 15 minutes. As long as you study for the exams for at least a couple hours you will do very well. Class is easy as well as the homeworks and quizzes.

Dave's class is very entertaining and he honestly is a good teacher. You only use the notes packet which is what you spend the whole class filling out. The tests are very difficult and most on your grade. My class averages were around a 62. The exams are worth 22% per midterm and 33% for final.

He's one of the best professors I've ever had. His lectures are interesting and people respect him. The only bad thing is that his packet of notes is too long to study from and exams are very hard. I recommend to have taken an high school class before because the material is too specific. Other than that, definetly go for it if you want to learn
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Personally, I don't see why this guy has so many positive reviews. He has a decent personality and his lectures are kind of interesting, but the exams are unnecessarily difficult. If you haven't taken econ previously, take someone else.
A very nice professor, but exams are overly hard and a lot of material.

Dr Dave is great. Lectures are always interesting, keeps material relevant which helps to understand the economical concepts. Tests are hard, some Econ knowledge would be good to have beforehand but dont worry, Dave makes it better. If you have to take Econ102 I recommend taking Dave

I am not even an Econ or business major and I loved this class all because of Dave. His classes where so much fun, he truly does care and wants to help you be successful. Going to class is a huge help because of the note packet which is amazing to help you study. He has been one of the b best professors I have had so far.

Dr. Dave's class is never boring. He puts a ton of effort to make the content relevant and entertaining to learn. He is accessible outside of class for extra help, and was the most clear Professor I have ever had in terms of what he expected from us. 10/10 would recommend

I have no interest in economics, but Dave made me excited to learn about it. He has great real-world examples that really helps you visualize these concepts. You don't need the textbook. Exams are pretty straightforward, but the Mapleton math practice text and Devil's Advocate text definitely help with a few of the exam questions. TAKE DAVE!

Really cool guy but not the best prof. If you've taken econ before you will do fine, but if not then I'd recommend another professor. Minimal work but going to class is necessary in order to do well. Averages were always pretty low and he didn't seem to care, so only take him if you're good at econ!
Favorite class I've taken this year. Lectures were never boring and the tests were very straightforward. If you study for the exams at least 3 days beforehand you'll do very well. 10/10 Recommend.

I loved Daves class! His notes packet is amazing and so helpful, it will help you on all the homework and quizzes. He goes over homework and quizzes in class, so make sure to attend. So far, one of my favorite professors at PSU!
Not a lot to say. Great guy with a great class!
He's a goat. If ur hood at math, you'll get an A. If you struggle with math, it would prob be a harder class but I found it to be a simple, easy course with Dave brown

Great teacher explains hard concepts very well and you can tell he has a real passion and joy for what he is teaching. Walkthroughs homeworks and quizzes during class so be sure to always attend. Overall really fun class and amazing professor.

Dave Brown is a Chad. PSU freshman flock to take his heavily coveted ECON 102 course. Jokes aside, really easy class if you put in the minimum effort to take notes, finish homeworks, and study prior to exams. For those with good handwriting, save your notes and pass them off to other PSU students who also want to take his course. Subway Sandwich.
his lectures are something else, amazing professor

Dr. Dave is an amazing professor. His expectations for grading are very clear. He also tells students exactly what to expect on the exams, and the questions are very fair. He kept lectures interesting and engaging over Zoom. Overall, a great class, would 100% pick him as your ECON 102 prof!

Dr. Dave was a good professor. Honestly, really didn't pay attention to most lectures and did high 70's and low 80's on exams, but still ended with an 89. He is funny and tries to make zoom university interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: As many people said before, professor Brown is awesome. His lectures are engaging. His explanations are clear. His examples and videos are vivid and easy to understand. He doesn't give tricky questions in quizzes, homework or exams. More importantly, he gives many chances of EXTRA CREDITS. If you enroll in his ECON102, lucky you!

Amazing prof. There's only three exams the entire year (including the final), and his lectures are engaging and informative. Even though class size is huge, he gets everyone involved. I bought the online textbook and didn't open it a single time. The only thing you need is the notes packet from the PSU bookstore, and you're set for an A.
Dr. Dave was really passionate about the class and he made it so engaging. He made it easy to take notes and the exams were exactly what I expected. If I had to take this class again, I would.

Dave Brown was by far my favorite professor yet. His lectures were engaging and fun despite a virtual format. Be careful on the homework and quizzes because they can be tricky and there are not many grades for the class. The notes packet is a lifesaver and study hard for the exams and you'll be fine! No textbook needed.

I got 100s in all the exams with a few hours of studying and I finished them in 30 min. Theyre easy is you work. Prof brown was great and kept stuff entertaining. HW and quizzes were annoying. Final was relatively easy. Spent maybe 3 hours and got a 95. Easy class but required effort.

Dr. Dave is an awesome professor. I didnt really know much about economics coming in and wasnt really interested in it, but you really do learn something in his class. Hes very straightforward and passionate, and his guided notes are great

Can't go wrong with Dr. Dave!! His lectures and notes are very clear. One time I just didn't pay attention during class but there was homework due and all I did was read over the notes and I instantly understood all of the content. He is very passionate and he tries to keep the class very engaged. The extra math workbook is helpful for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor to get for ECON 102. It is more conceptual than math-related. Not too much homework or quizzes. Exams are manageable if you study.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT
