Most boring and monotone professor I have had at Penn State. He is ridiculously tedious and is very stuck in his ways. He even likes to control how students, who pay to go here, how they are supposed to take notes and learn the material. It is ironic that a sociology professor does not account for a different method of learning.

Not a good professor. Lectures are really boring and he made many creepy comments during them. He wears two masks so hearing him is difficult. He also bans typed notes which is really inconvenient for the students who pay to go here. It is his way or the highway, he does not care about accommodating students needs

This guy is just about the most tedious and terrible professor I have ever seen. First, he wears two masks and speaks at the lowest level, making him seem underwater. Then, we have two weeks of classes, then he gets covid (two masks are worth it, though) and gives us an exam on materials we have not discussed in class. Absolute Joke.

If you see a bad rating on here its because the student probably didn't go to class or even try to read the textbook. Before a test he will give a exam review with all terms to focus on. Go into the textbook read those concepts and you will get an A in the class. Class can be boring but he tries to keep students active with his dad jokes. easy 5/5

Professor Fulton was awful. I was lucky to be able to drop the course. He assigned almost double the amount of work that my 400-level courses had for a very introductory course. When asked if he could make the homework visible sooner, he said I would be lucky to sleep with my course load (18 credits) so he wouldn't. He is all about his convenience.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: So monotone and boring and all you learn in soc1 is common sense but using sociology terms instead. Clicker questions in class so attendance is required, but study the homework and you will be fine on exams. Lectures aren't super important because you have to go through it all again for hw.

easiest class ever! as long as you read the textbook and come to most of the classes, its an easy A/B. class can be a little boring or slow sometimes, but overall still worth taking if you want a simple GH credit

He does not allow computers or technology while in class but he does go slow to allow for handwritten notes. The homework assignments are roughly once a week with a few extra credit opportunities during the semester. As long as you go to lecture and do the homework assignments it should be an A
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fulton is a fine professor if you like going to lectures where the professor just reads off of PowerPoints. He doesn't post the PowerPoints on Canvas which might compel you to show up to class, however, after a few weeks of going to class I quickly realized that the powerpoint lectures were simply reiterating what we read in the text book
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Fulton is a cool guy and he was able to make class entertaining most of the time. He says no devices but honestly he is pretty chill about it as long as you are still getting your work done.

he doesn't allow devices in lecture, but speaks very slowly to accommodate paper notetaking. expect lots of dad jokes. he was also pretty tech-savvy which was somewhat refreshing. if you need help, ATTEND OFFICE HOURS. even just directly asking after class is great. he's very willing to help and will take the time to talk with you if you need help.

It is very easy to get an A if you play the part. However, I wish the class would be named after what it really is, which is Critical Race Theory 101. You will be forced to learn radically leftist views, and you will be graded upon what they want you to believe is "correct." Google indoctrination before you sign up.

He is not the most enthusiastic person, but he attempts to deliver jokes, which never lands but he means well. Overall, his class is pretty easy as long as you show up and actually put in the work. Just keep in mind he doesn't allow phones or computers while Hes talking so prepare ti take notes on a loose leaf.

Lectures are boring and vague. Clicker questions for points and sometimes in class activities so you have to attend lectures. Posts notes on Canvas. Tests are pretty easy if you take notes and pay attention. Gives paper syllabus and sticks to it. Uses connect for homework and readings which are easy. Doesn't allow laptops, so paper notes only.

This class was supposed to be an easy gen ed, and it is not that.  My GPA last semester was like a 3.47, and this class brought it down so much.  He says you cannot approach the podium and gives a 20 minute mask lecture before getting to the material.  Showed lots of weird videos in class, creeped me out.  Not a fan, just not for me.

Just No. Prof Fulton was seriously one of the most boring people I've ever heard speak. Easy content, bland lectures, and pop up assignments. Idolize the syllabus or you won't pass. Did I mention every class you miss after your 3rd is a percent off your final grade? Yep. Have fun.
Dr. Fulton was super funny and made the lectures really enjoyable. Would definitely recommend him as a professor!

You have to go class as there are several assignments that he doesn't tell you about until that day so if you miss class you cannot get credit for those and he doesn't post the slides so you won't get the notes. Very lecture heavy and uses an online textbook, so that is where all the test questions come from. Need to study but it's not that bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Insane amount of homework for what is supposed to be an easy introduction class. Got roped into taking this because of an academic advisor and it ended up taking up much more of my time than I would have liked. The tests are based mostly on the textbook, but attendance is mandatory. Every absence after 3 is a percentage point off your final grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: A lot of the assignments would not be brought up until the day it's due. Studying for the exam is hard when you don't have a clear guide on what to study.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's an extremely unpleasant person who doesn't talk about upcoming assignments such as homework and aspects you to be up to date on random changes to the syllabus which he doesn't tell anyone about. Horrible communicator. The only excuse for not being in class is having Covid. Doesn't understand that students have other excuses to miss class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally does not tell you what you need for the tests and leaves you trying to memorize the smallest details for literally 3 to 4 chapters of the texbook. No one can get 100s on his exams. A sociology class shouldn't be this hard. Literally will study for 3 weeks and not score how I want. Take a different teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Easiest class taken so far. There is a decent volume of homework but it can all be completed within an hour each. Show up to lectures, take notes, and read the textbook readings every so often and this will be an easy A. Dr. Fulton is scarily in-touch and up to date with college culture, and sometimes has extremely funny lectures.

Honestly, it is a lot of homework, but the homework is meaningful and if you do it you will get an A on the exam. The exams aren't easy but if u do the readings you will pass. He's really funny and I feel like I'm actually learning so much. Such an interesting class and would definitely take it again.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His lectures are pretty engaging. There is a lot of textbook reading, but personally I liked the format of the class. There are questions online for each chapter that are just graded for completion and the textbook is good so it's not too bad. Try not to skip too much and study the book for tests.

He is a very funny and entertaining teacher but he doesn't tell u what you should study and has you rely on pages and pages of textbooks. Some of the questions on the tests are things you never heard. He needs to give you more guidance.

His classes are very boring & the exam material rarely covers the things he mentions in lectures. Hes very quiet (and wears 2 masks) so youll spend most of class trying to figure out what hes saying. As long as you do the textbook readings (theres lots of them) you should be fine. Exams are pretty easy and straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Fulton was helpful when it came to answering questions and always gave very detailed responses. As long as you do your work with proficiency and turn everything in on time, you will most likely be in the A- or A range. It is vital you read the book because his quizzes and discussions are heavily based on the chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Seemed like a pretty good prof. until he ghosted us two weeks into the semester. graded everything during finals week. literally didn't hear anything from February until May. The class was really easy though and the prof isn't a tough grader at all. Skim through the textbook and put 30 minutes into the weekly assignment and you'll get an easy A.

SOC 1 WEB wasn't hard but it did suck. All we did was read out of a long textbook the entire semester. Chapters were very long, with way too much information. Didn't grade the homework or chapter quizzes until the very end. Take a synchronous version instead, unless you want to bore yourself.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: This guy literally didn't grade anything until finals week. It's super annoying even though most of the assignments are easy. Read the book and you'll do just fine. Probably the only class I've really read for.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Really such an easy class, simple assignments that make it hard to not get full credit for them. Class weekly schedule is consistent which makes staying on top of work easy. Would recommend this class WEB.

No technology allowed and clicker questions are required in class to pass. He tries to make class interesting and it is! But he's a little dry and his exams are fairly tough. Homework is easy though. Honestly, clickers and studying for the exams are what you need to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Fulton is a great guy, but is so old-school with his teaching (which really sucked during quarantine when we barely had any actual lectures). Plus side, if you show up to class you get extra credit. However, if you miss more than two classes he starts deducting points which sucks. Really need to read the textbook for exams!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: His exams were easy and I should have ended with an a, but due to missing class he drops full percentage points. This brought me all the way down to a b. With a class as simple as soc1, its ridiculous to make attendance mandatory. On top of that his lectures are painfully boring, as hes practically going over common sense.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not a bad choice, not great but he's fine. Attendance is 100% mandatory. There's clickers and in class work. Points off final grade if you skip more than twice. Weekly hw, decently easy exams based off readings. Lecture is useless but mandatory. Class kinda just feels like busy work but who cares. Kinda a weird guy but you get used to it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Attendance being a requirement for this class is a joke. Tests arent bad, if you do the entire studyguide you wont have to worry about reading from the textbook. His lectures are painfully boring and he moves really slow, so it was a huge pain having to attend every class. Overall not a hard class just a really boring professor
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You have to read the book to do well but otherwise it is really easy. He is super boring and you do need to go to class for in class assignments and clicker points. He adds up to 4 percent extra credit to your grade so it is easy to do well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Okay - this man is hands down the worst Professor I have ever had. Miss class? Thats an ENTIRE % PER CLASS subtracted from your overall course grade. He rambles - focuses on useless topics & his grading makes no sense. You MUST read for exams: the exams YOU DONT GET BACK!!!! Impossible class. Impossible Professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: So where do I begin, His homework assignments are so simple and the exams are a joke (except he will throw in some questions that are like a random one liner from the text book). Besides him being really creepy, his homework late policy is absurd. If you come to class 3 minutes late, that homework assignment your typed and printed will NOT count
Make sure to do the readings - they're important for the exams but are never mentioned in class.
he make me wanna sleep during lecture
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty awkward guy. Reminds me of Danny Tanner. I came into the course expecting it to be easy, because the lectures were super basic. But, you HAVE to rad the book to exceed on exams, as most of the questions come from the readings. Lectures can get boring after a while.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: John is a great professor, yes you have to read the book to know whats on the exams but its close to 10 pages a week you have to read and when you do you can easily get a perfect on the exams. He also gives 4% bonus as long as you come to class everyday so there really is no reason to not get an A in here.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fun guy overall. Lectures are interesting but not too challenging. Exam questions mainly come from the textbook and covers material not taught in class. Great intro class that doesn't dive too deep into the subject.

Fulton is a real nice and caring guy, the only complaint I have about the class is that the lectures can put you to sleep some days. But sometimes he can be hilarious and he obviously cares deeply about his field of study. Advice: do the readings!!! They will help you a lot on exams. Overall easy and enjoyable class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Fulton seems weird at first but through the semester you will realize that he is actually hysterical. He actually wants to relate to students and the lectures are really chill and for the most part interesting. 1/2 the exams comes directly from the book but if you read it wont be a problem. You also get 4 absences without penalty which is cool
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Go to every class you get three percent added to your overall grade. Thats a whole letter grade!!! Do the readings ahead of time and study the lecture notes (which are very straight forward) and you will be perfectly fine on the exams! Also no final! Fulton made class interesting every day and is so funny and nice!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: lectures are actually interesting and relevant... John is funny and connects well with students tests are difficult and you really need to keep up with the readings but if you put in the work you will do ok on the tests. Also if you dont miss any classes you get three percents added to your final grade
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A lot of the course content is intuitive or just vocab. However! Skipping class will lose you a lot of points, while perfect (or near-perfect) attendance earns extra credit. So go to class. There are also a few long readings. You should properly read them at least once. Very specific questions will appear on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: John's lectures are super boring and is a complete waste of time. Nothing of what he says is related to the exam. The exam content is based on his readings so you must read the Core Concepts book. Learn from my mistake and do the readings! bc I got 73% on an exam without it and a 94% when I took the effort. Sociology is just not my forte
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is beyond easy. Not one thing from the lecture is on the exam which is severely annoying. He makes you go to class and takes points of your grade if you miss more than 2 classes. If you read to book and do the practice quizzes on canvas this class is an easy A. He offers 6% of extra credit which makes this class even easier to get an A.
A good choice for a GS. You do have to read to do well on exams, but there are multiple chances for extra credit. Go to class. He's a nice guy and a typical college professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Fulton is very nice and makes his lectures as engaging as possible. This class was harder than expected, but he gives you a significant amount of extra credit just for showing up. You definitely have to read the textbooks to be prepared for the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great way to fulfill GS requirement. 6 points extra credit available on final grade just for attending class and filling out 3 online quizzes. lectures can be interesting and exams are not too difficult. overall great teacher and class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, but his lectures are not very engaging. His clicker questions go towards your participation/attendance points which in turn become extra credit. The class is fairly based on common sense so studying for exams aren't too challenging. Although lectures are boring, some parts are engaging. Most definitely a GPA booster.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Fulton is a very boring lecturer, but he tries to make the class as engaging as possible. As long as you read the book, attend class and study for exams you will be fine. Don't expect your grade to be rounded up at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was super easy and very interesting & entertaining. Go to the lectures for attendance credit, and sometimes they're kinda funny/interesting. Definitely read and outline all of the readings and chapters assigned because that is the majority of the exam, but still a lot of this is common knowledge & the rest is super easy to understand

The only reason why you have to go to lecture is to get credit for attendance and the clicker questions. PLEASE DONT BOTHER PAYING ATTENTION TO THE LECTURE. The lecture slides are about 10% of whats on the exam. The other 90% come straight from the readings. Go to all the TA review sessions before the exam and they will tell you what to study

I say attendance mandatory because he literally adds 3% of extra credit on your final grade if you have perfect attendance. Don't even bother paying attention in lecture - read the readings and study the textbook and you'll get an A on every exam. A good number of extra credit opportunities, and the homeworks are not bad at all.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Lectures tend to be sort of useless. You need to read ALL of the readings for the exam. If you read everything and know it well, you will do just fine.

Easiest class at Penn state, if you are just looking for an easy elective, take soc 001 with fulton. Class is very boring and paying attention is not that important. Look at the terms on the study guide and you will get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Fulton is horrible at teaching this class. He gives lectures that do not prepare the students for exams. Attendance is very important even though going to class usually feels like a big waste of time. Just study the textbook to get an A. He fails to bring any substance to class discussions and makes everyone do silly exercises in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Fulton treats you like you are in high school but his tests are not that simple. However, the tests are completely opinion based. The questions I got wrong were because I did not agree with his views.  He was extremely rude as well.  I did not like this class at all, but if you read the text thoroughly and go to class it is easy to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Learned more about Sociology when I took it in high school. His lectures are pointless (but mandatory)  and his clicker questions are nothing like exam questions. His exams are based almost completely off the tedious readings he assigns. He does give a decent amount of extra credit though. I got a B without putting in too much effort.

Class was long... but overall Fulton made the class enjoyable with partner and individual assignments. Go to every class (if you go to all classes, you can receive 3% onto your overall grade) Exams are based on the readings. Do the study review guide. Fulton is funny and approachable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Super easy A. Read the book and the exams are fine. Lectures are boring, but attendance is required. Tons of extra credit.

Easy class. You can save money by just going to the library and reserving the books whenever you need them. The readings in the book are also all online. Tests are more difficult than expected but follow the study guide precisely and it becomes rather easy. LOTS OF EXTRA CREDIT, more than most professors on campus.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Gives a lot of extra credit. Attendance and clicker points count as extra credit. Easy in class assignments and homework assignments. His exams are 50 multiple choice questions, most of them from the readings and some from lecture notes. They are harder than you would think but gives so much extra credit that it's easy to do well in this class.

This by no means a hard class but it seems so pointless that it is a little bit hard. I never wanted to go to class and Im not that type of person but I had to bc you are only allowed to miss 3 classes. The lectures almost have nothing to do with the tests and they are basically common sense. I would only recommend if you have high self discipline.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Fulton makes the class so everyone can pass. Attendance is mandatory and is a big part of your grade. Class ins interesting and easy and repetitive.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Most boring class i've ever taken, also the easiest class. Don't bother doing the readings, just search the answers to the pre-test study guides online before the test. I never took a single note and got an A easily. 3 points extra credit for not missing a class and another 3 points for random stuff throughout the semester.

Great guy. lectures can be boring. attendance matters with clicker questions. exams are difficult. Must read to do well on the exams. only 3 exams that are 50 multiple choice questions and there is no final. On the last day of class there is a 25 question quiz with 3 extra questions for bonus points. Sit by someone you know.

Loves teaching. His lectures are boring. Clicker questions are easy and count as extra credit and attendance. He's very organized. Goes by his outline. Exams are difficult and must read. Two small books are required. 9 homework assignments and are easy. Sit next to someone you know because does a lot of interaction with the person next to you.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Easiest class i've taken at PSU. Barely studied for tests and got all A's. Most boring class also, but you have to show up to click in. 3 points extra credit for showing up to every class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I don't know why Dr. Fulton is so poorly rated on here but I LOVED him!! His lectures are hilarious and he really cares about his students. He gives super detailed study guides for exams and practice questions, although 90% of the questions come from the readings not from class material. No reason not to get an A.

If you don't have to take this class, DO NOT TAKE IT. It's not hard but it's probably the most boring class I've ever taken. He spends the whole class talking about things that don't pertain to the lesson and he has a horrible teaching style. Take any other class if you can. Seriously. Any. OTHER. Class.

Dr. Fulton is a really nice guy and the class isn't necessarily hard. However,  the exams are all reading while the lectures are absolutely useless. Usually this wouldn't be a problem, but class is absolutely mandatory. It occasionally felt like a waste of time, but there is plenty of extra credit and unique homework assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The test are based on what you read between the two books. The lectures barely matter and they are boring. You should go to class for clicker points and attendance, which also turn into extra credit at the end of the semester. Be careful who you sit by because he assigns group projects on Fridays and they are due on Mondays. The tests are hard

John Fulton is a goofball (in a good way I suppose). He looks like a very tall version of the voice actor for Spongebob, Tom Kenny. Seriously. Cram the night before the tests and you'll do fine. The final is a quiz. If you don't miss any classes you get 3% onto your grade. Be prepared to hear "here's today's goal guys.." every day.

Don't get me wrong, Fulton's a nice professor, but his lectures and tests don't add up. His tests are based more on the readings and films than his lectures. Some of his clicker questions are easy. Also, the clicker questions are used for attendance; it has no benefit to your grade. His lectures can get boring, but the homework assignments are fun.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Fulton is a great guy and I did enjoy his class. I thought his homework assignments were interesting and unique. Although keeping up with the readings is tough, it is necessary as the majority of the exams cover that material. He gives tons of extra credit just by going to class. Very easy A, I would recommend him for Soc 001
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr Fulton is pretty boring. He repeats the same things over and over again, and then his exams don't reflect what was discussed in lecture at all.  You will have to do a lot of reading, and attendance is mandatory/ will majorly affect your grade. The class is super easy, but attendance will most likely be the thing that will  trip most people up.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Fulton is awesome. He is very quirky, but funny-quirky. Lectures are interesting and relatable. Sometimes he'll even add memes to slides, and we watch a lot of videos. The exams are easy- just go to the review sessions and take the practice exams online beforehand. Not a bad class at all. Would definitely take again with Dr. Fulton.

John is a nice guy who wants you to do well, but the lectures suck. With that being said, attendance is mandatory, but the bright side is that he gives you an extra 3% for going to every lecture. When it comes to the exam, just do the study guide and go to the reading review sessions (even if you think you don't need to).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. John Fulton is an awesome guy. Makes all the material relatable to college students. Test can be difficult, make sure to attend review sessions and ask many questions as he gives test questions if you ask good questions. Definitely a good Gen Ed choice.
Great professor, strongly recommended. You will have practice exam before the real exam, and lots of class practices. As long as you prepare the exam properly, you will rock this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: This class overall was fairly easy. However, it becomes a challenge when you factor in attendance, which is mandatory. Why is this a problem? Because his lectures are SO BORING. Prof Fulton is pretty monotonous and redundant. He will spend 2 minutes per iClick to give everyone enough time to read the one-sentence question. Homework is easy.

I learned more in my high school sociology class than in this class. He was an okay professor but it felt like so little information was taught in the span of a week or so. I'd be interested in taking 207 with him but I was disappointed in how little ended up being taught. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities so it's easy to do well anyway

Fulton was a good professor, he gives a good amount of extra credit. Show up to class everyday and get 3% added to your final grade. Clickers are used to take attendance and his tests are based on the readings, so make sure you buy or rent the books.

Amazing professor. Many homework assignments, which are fun to do as they are out of the ordinary. Three exams, almost all book based - relatively tough. Do not miss class. Gives a lot of extra credit - attendance based and mandatory. Overall, not a tough course, and I would highly recommend.

Dr. Fulton is the man. He is one of the nicest guys ever. SOC 001 is very easy. All you have to do is show up to class to get clicker points and bonus for the class, do not miss class. The three tests are only on book material and are not difficult. He is very enthusiastic about what he does, and he is a role model for other teachers.

Most boring class I've ever taken. Professor Fulton's lectures drag on when he talks and the tests are all on readings in the book he never talks about in class. Do not take this class. It is very easy to just sit on your phone the whole time during class. The readings are long and boring, and you lose interest after the first page.

Gives a lot of extra credit, including 3% on final grade for perfect attendance. Don't need to pay attention in class since the exams are just on the book. Sometimes watch videos all class, and the material can be interesting. Homework once every week or two and 3 exams. It's not an easy A but if you work it's a very obtainable A.

Go to class for clicker points and extra credit. The 3 exams aren't easy but certainly not difficult by any means.  Lots of homework to bring your grade up.  Definitely an easy B or B+ but have to put in a little effort to get an A or A-.  Fulton is the nicest guy too.

Gives three exams that aren't that tough and no final. Classes can be interesting but you don't need to pay attention really since the exams are only on the book. If you attend every class you get a +3% boost on your final grade which is awesome, plus even more opportunities for extra credit. Not an easy A, but a very very obtainable A.
Only went for clicker points. Attendance is a must or you'll be penalized. Lectures are long and pretty self explanatory. Generally easy, but slightly boring.

I like Professor Fulton. The material in class is very easy to understand. The tests are based on lectures, chapter readings (which are discussed in class) and textbook readings. Don't read the textbook intensely. Definitions are important and basic concepts.

very boring lectures. only go to class for clicker points. goes over the same subject every single day (literally, last 5 mins is new material and 95% of the class is reveiw from past classes) and exams aren't even on the material he teaches in class but instead all based on the textbook. heard Nielson is a much better teacher for this class

Dr. Fulton seemed like a pretty cool guy.  He tried his hardest to make lectures appeal to students, but fell flat.  For someone interested in social sciences, he sure managed to bore the hell out of me.  There may be two or three things said in lecture that actually end up on an exam.  The rest is from the textbook and readings.
Read the passages, look over the textbook, study the lectures, and attend the exam review for the tests, and you'll be fine.
Gives 3% extra credit if you attend every lecture. His tests aren't too difficult, but he always has a handful of test questions that you need to read the textbook to get correct.
Very Dad-esque. Awkward and makes dad jokes.  Fairly easy class, but boring lecture.  Homework assignments were pretty interesting, though.  Attendance mandatory (clicker).
Funny lectures, you only need to go to class because of the clicker points and in class assignments.  He really cares about his students.

John Fulton was overall a great professor. His tests are not extremely difficult, nor extremely easy. If you have never taken Sociology before, this is a great introductory course. He is a pretty funny guy but his lectures can be long. And if you don't read the text book or do the homework assigned, you won't pass. I would take this class again.

soc with him is one of those simple classes that should be an easy A. that being said, it is a burden that you have to go to class because you lose a percentage from your final grade with each miss after 3 free misses. however, if you don't miss those 3 misses you get 3% bonus. lectures vary from extremely boring to funny cause he's such a goof

Fulton is a great guy, always cracking jokes but his lectures are usually extremely long. Tests are easy but based on ideas and topics in the readings and homework, not lectures. He makes you use a clicker for attendance and is constantly giving homework (expect it every weekend- sometimes group projects). I would take this class again.

Dr. Fulton is a good teacher and overall good guy. He gives lots of opportunities for points, is clear on topics, offers help, and is just quirky enough to make lectures kind of fun. Pretty cool and understanding. Just turn in your work on time!

Lectures are pretty useless - you will go over 1 simple concept for 5 classes in a row. Super nice guy though and means well! But you'll really end up teaching yourself.  Tests are based on the readings bc you don't cover much material in lecture... As long as you do the readings and understand them, you'll get an A on the test. Attendance is EC

Dr. Fulton's lectures were rather boring but you have to be there! If you miss more than 3 classes, your grade will lose a percent for every class missed but if you don't miss any, 3% will be added to your final grade. Read the books, do the study guide and you will do fine on his exams. 9 short, easy homework's, 3 exams and 1 quiz (no final).

Dr. Fulton's class is easy. Read the chapters, do the study guides, and go to class. You get 3% points added to the final grade if you don't miss plus extra credit on the final quiz. No final exam. Class is boringstupid, just play on your phone and click in. It's pretty simply. The kids who did poorly just neglected the class. Easy A, but boring.

Professor Fulton was by far the worst professor I've ever encountered at Penn State. His lectures are mandatory and he spends the whole class fixated on his suicide obsession. He never covers any relevant material and won't reply to any emails.

The concepts are pretty easy, however the class itself is maddening. He makes class mandatory yet doesn't even discuss any readings or many main concepts found on exams. I attended every class, yet when grades went out I didn't even receive an A for attendance. I emailed him, never heard back.

If you're going to take this class, GET READY TO READ. I thought the readings were pointless. I read all the materials. I still ended up with a B in his class. I expected better. His lectures are just long and plain old BORING. He puts me to sleep. He never replied to my e-mails. I even reminded him after class, and he never got around to it.

Dr. Fulton's class is pretty easy. Gives homework weekly, attendance is mandatory, gives 3 percentage points at the end of the semester towards your final grade if you dont miss a class (BIG HELP). The lectures aren't really related to the exams (3 exams); studying the book is very necessary for the test. I would take him again.

Don't let "Skip class? You won't pass" scare you away!! attendance is extra credit lectures are actually funny he tries to relate information to students in a way so that we can relate Small homework assignments (mostly interesting) 3 tests&a quiz no midterm no final easy to approach & works with you I would take it again! skim book before test!!
He gave an exam the day after Thanksgiving break. Enough said.

horrible horrible horrible horrible. DOES NOT TEACH. 80% of whats on exams is from the textbook. and that would be okay except attendance is mandatory... he is also just super boring. the absolute worst professor I had in my first year here at PSU. AVOID AT ALL COSTS.

A little goofy but he knows his stuff. Lectures can be boring but he tries to keep it interesting. Clickers used for attendance and if you don't miss any classes you get 3 percent added to your final grade. Relatively easy gen ed
Does not teach you anything the exam is based on outside of class readings.

Dr. Fulton is a great teacher. He is so passionate about the subject and would do anything to help his students. All you have to do is go to class, take notes and then read the book chapters when it comes time to the exam. He gives extra credit for just clicking in to class. No final, just a small quiz the last day of class. I recommend this class.
Dr. Fulton is a nice guy but an awful teacher. Does not teach what is on the exams. Love Soc but hated this class with him.

He's pretty easy. I'm the kind of person who doesn't pay attention during class, but still managed to get an A.  That's cuz I attended class everyday (3% EC if you do that added onto final grade) and I read the whole textbook. Know online quiz questions and you should be fine.

John Fulton is an extremely clear, passionate speaker. He knows his material well and his lectures cover most material for the exams. Additional readings are pretty mandatory for the tests, but if you do them the tests are so easy you could cry. Clickers are used for attendance which is pretty annoying, but the class is fun and I loved it.

Fulton is a weird guy. Unfortunately class is mandatory but if you don't miss a class all semester you get 3 whole percent added to your final grade. The course material was more boring than I expected which made it very painful. Exams are pretty straightforward if you've done the readings he assigns

Dr. Fulton is easily the most unintelligent teacher I've had in my entire life. His class is almost entirely based on his incredibly offensive and judgmental opinions. If you are even the slightest bit intelligent you will hate this class and this teacher. He talks to the students as if they are in 3rd grade. I have never hated a class more.

Dr. Fulton is okay at his job. It's the material that makes this course maddening. I like easy classes, but SOC 001 is so elementary that it is unbearable and attendance is mandatory for points. Other than that, only 3 exams, a quiz, and 8 15-minute homeworks are required. Fulton himself is a weird but good guy. You just won't walk away with much.

Somewhat interesting class. I just hated how attendance was mandatory. For everyday you miss he takes off 1% from your overall grade. So if you're the type of person who can manage to go to every single class everyday then take this class.
He is the nicest professor Ive had at Penn State. He is very understudying n teaches really well.Only thing is that he values attendance a lot. Definitely take his class!

He's awesome. Exams are easy as long as you do the readings and fill out the study guides he provides. I would definitely recommend this class. John is an easy going guy who genuinely cares about his students. He keeps things interesting in class, too. Make sure you attend for attendance points though.
Go to class, do the readings, and Fulton makes this GS an easy A. He's an overall good guy for sure, and you'll go over some interesting case studies.
Really easy class. Fulton is a good guy, cares about  his students. Gives you 3 points towards your final grade if you don't miss class. Exams are easy if you read. Overall a very good GS to take.
He is a really funny guy and makes class fun but he does not go over the readings at all. Whatever comes in the tests are from the reading and that makes it kinda hard to study.

He doesn't go over the readings in class, which are a large part of the tests.  It helps that if you go to every class you get extra credit, but I thought the material was so boring.  The tests shouldn't be that hard for a soc 001 class.
Very easy class, gives you 3 extra percentage points for attending all classes. Exams are easy if you review notes and study guide. Overall, good GPA booster
great teacher, easy class.  definetly recomend

Dr. Fulton has probably been my favorite teacher so far at PSU. Really goofy guy, and makes a lot of interesting points. Tests are incredibly easy. I got 90's on all 3 without owning the text book. He gives you online practice problems, and half of those are usually on the exam. Plus you can get up to 3 extra credit points just for going to class.
Fulton is a little odd but you just have to see through it.  He's a good professor, easy class.  The study guide he gives you for the exam is great.

Very easy gen ed! It is also rather interesting, I learned a lot. Fulton is very funny and keeps class interesting. Attendance is mandatory, but it can help your grade a lot. The readings are long but not boring.
easiest class ive ever taken. hes funny and makes awkward sexual jokes. very easy A, no work just review before exams

Good, you should take this class. It is very fair if you spend time for the exam, you will get A. And attendence is required for the extra credits. Some homeworks and projects and one-take home Exam are grade booster!

Took it as a GS Gen-ed! Had a lot of fun! Fulton is a really good teacher and makes every class very exciting and interesting! All exams are multiple choice and most readings are interesting :) Attendance is needed though because more than 3 absences can affect your grade. But definitely take this  class! The readings can be photocopied!
Great course. Great teacher. Fun and exciting.

Had a blast in this class. Dr. Fulton is so funny and easy going. The material is also really interesting, but he is a funny guy. It sucks that he added tests to the class, but there are only two. Very reasonable. Not that hard to get an A. Great professor.

Dr. Fulton is a good professor and really makes the material interesting for class. He can also be decently funny and likes to drop sexual jokes a few times a class. Toward the end of the semester he gave us assigned seats, and that was a tad annoying, but overall good class.

Really nice guy. If you need help with something, he is more than happy to meet with you. Can only miss three classes then takes a percentage point off your final grade for every class you miss which is too harsh. If you miss no class he adds those three points though to your final grade. If you pay attention and go to class it's an easy A. Take it

Not bad, about average difficulty. Fairly nice guy; class is sometimes interesting, but if the power points were posted online I probably would not attend. The quizzes were a little harder than they should have been for a 001 class, but the HW and in class ex's allow you to boost your grade.

The lectures are pretty boring, but you should probably go to them because you never know when we will have an in class assignment. Be prepared to work with partners (yeah, in a huge classroom, and it get's awkward. He can be funny at times, but is usually hard to hear.

Very nice professor, recieved a decent grade, but incredibly boring class. He is a strange professor and teaches accordingly. I personally would not want to take any other course with him. He is unorganized and most lessons are useless. Take someone else if your have a choice but if you must take him He's not toooo bad
it was easy, but you have to read and go to class to listen cause sometimes he'll put random things discussed in class in the weekly quizzes. the quizzes gradually get harder and harder

This professor mumbles when he talks and brings up very random topics in class that he thinks are relevent to the material.  The class was easy as long as you did the readings and paid attention in class.  Kinda an odd guy but a simple gen ed.

Class isn't mandatory, but he does ask some questions from class on quizzes. Only 10 quizzes, no exams. Assignments are easy but there is A LOT of reading for the quizzes. B+. Wasn't awful- he's an interesting guy

Awesome teacher. Shows lots of videos, but they really went well with what we learned. No exams or finals, just assignments and quizzes. But you really need to read the textbooks if you want to do well on the quizzes. Class isn't mandatory, but he does put questions on the quiz on stuff from class.

Dr.Fulton was a great lecturer. He relies heavily on video clips and discussion, but the class was very interesting. He does randomly call on people at times, but that's just to aid discussion. Reading is essential, but you need to read if you want to do well on the weekly quizzes. Not a lot of homework and NO MIDTERM OR FINAL. Easy class to take.
John Andre wasn't the best teacher when it came to interesting classes, but he's a very easy grader on projects and the tests aren't bad if you're prepared. Wholly inoffensive.

Dr. Fulton is a very nice and entertaining guy. In class: Big on videos and discussion, and it was probably my most fun class time. But be warned that there is HOURS of reading, and most of the test content will be on this reading and NOT what is discussed in class. Very interesting and about the right level for honors, take it if you like it.

Great guy. 4 quizes, 3 exams, 10 homeworks. Quizes are tedious and kind of hard. Exams and homework are easy. Fairly easy to do good if you go to class and do your work. I would recommend him to friends. He made class interesting and funny

He's a really nice guy. Cares about the students and is always willing to help. The tests are not that easy, but he gives extra credit at the end of the course. Its not a bad gen ed to take. Average student prob got a B plus in this class.
Fulton couldn't be a nicer guy. Tries to keep everyone interested and plans his lectures well. Test material is kind of ambiguous. Take this class for an easy gen ed.

Fulton is such a goober! This was a great Gen ed. You don't need to go to class, but I recommend it, in case he gives out an angel assignment (they are only for completion, 10% of grade) plus you will almost always laugh. Watched lots of videos overall NOT a hard class. take it, read the elementary textbook and get an easy A on tests/quizzes
Wonderful professor. Best I've ever had. Very approachable and extremely helpful and considerate. Thank you for everything, Dr. Fulton! :)

Extremely easy class. Good guy with good intentions, but so boring. Take your laptop and pay games during class. 2 extra credit points for attending every class. Read the small book and get an A. Take this class.
Pretty easy class if you read. Attendance is not completely mandatory, you can miss up to 6 classes. Class is kinda boring, Fulton doesn't really make it overly interesting, but still an easy gen-ed.
No Comments
Fairly easy subject, extremely easy class. A lot of opportunities to bring your grade up and depending on the class average you can even request for extra credit.
Really nice guy, was easy to contact and communicate with. If I missed classes always worked with me and helped me get on track. Allowed makeup speech's and moving due dates. Grades fairly.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Genuinely love his class so much. He's easy and fair but also genuinely teaches and gives great feedback. He's also very kind and understanding to those who are more anxious about public speaking and grades them fairly. Lastly, nothing funnier than a sarcastic british man.

Dr. Gilmore is such an amazing profess for CAS100. If you can take it with him, I HIGHLY recommend you do. He genuinely cares about every student he has and is always there to help you if you need it.

I took Dr. Gilmore's online class. Unlike many online professors, Dr. Gilmore was always available and happy to jump on video calls. The class isn't easy but his feedback has made me feel more confident when presenting

AG is genuinely the best. so kind, accommodating, and actually wants you to succeed. He's the most straight-up and helpful professor I've had. Take him for anything you can. I seriously love this guy.

If you have the option to take a class with Andy do it!! I hated public speaking before taking his class, but he is an amazing professor and is very clear and helpful in his instructions. He genuinely wants you to succeed in his class. On top of that he is always positive and funny, making his class enjoyable to be in.

Take CAS100 with Andy! Before the class, I was nervous, especially about public speaking, but Andy made it enjoyable and helped build my confidence. He creates a comfortable, supportive environment and gives great feedback. He's funny and genuinely cares about his students' success. One of my favorite professors at Penn State!
Professor Andy is a great guy and cares about his students.100% would recommend to anyone who needs a CAS100 class and really passionate about what he teaches. Would definitely take his class again.

I had Andy for CAS100C and genuinely have not enjoyed taking a class in my three years at Penn State as much as I did his. He was personable and caring and friendly and honestly one of the best professors at this school. He doesn't let you slack off but also will cut you a break when needed. I would highly recommend taking his class if you can.

Andy is actually the best professor I have ever had. I was not a good public speaker whatsoever coming into this class. His feedback is amazing and if you put in effort, you will get an A. This isnt a class where you only succeed if you are naturally good at something. His classroom environment was always welcoming and I always had a smile!

I completely adored Andy and loved taking this class with him! He truly wants you to be successful in his class and doesn't put pressure on you to become a perfect public speaker, rather he just wants to see you grow! Not only is he super funny and relatable, but he provides great feedback and creates a comfortable environment for all speakers.

It was a privilege to be in Andy's class! I read these reviews before enrolling and was convinced by the outstanding feedback. I was not disappointed! Truly a wonderful professor. He is funny, relaxed, and helpful. He takes the nerves out of speeches and creates such a calm environment. If you have to take public speaking take it with him!!!

I took 100C online with Dr Gilmore over the summer. it was the best experience I've had in an online class. He explained everything clearly, posted weekly overviews and was quick to grade. If only all online classes were this organized. Take thins class with Dr Gilmore!

Andy is the best professor I have ever had at PSU. I've never experienced a classroom environment like his class-i always wanted to go to class. None of use knew what rhetorical criticism was when we started this class but Andy is an expert, he explains everything so well and uses clear examples. Take a class with him.

I have never had a professor like Andy. I enjoyed every class and I would definitely recommend him as a professor for CAS 100A. He always knows how to make the class laugh but at the same time is very knowledgeable about public speaking and my confidence in my public speaking has definitely improved. I would take another class with him.

If you need to take CAS 100, take it with Dr. Gilmore. If his class is full, wait until the next semester. If it's full again, wait until the next semester! I was terrified of public speaking and had dropped this class twice before taking in with Dr. Gilmore. He cares about his students and is passionate about his research.
This guy is a beast. Funny and caring professor and makes sure everyone is comfortable given this is a public speaking class. Great British humor, overall awesome professor.

Andy is a phenomenal professor. He is knowledgable and at the same time deeply cares for the success of his students. I've never experienced a classroom quite like Andy's, he creates an environment in which we all got to know each other. Andy is funny and engaging but he also makes you think hard about rhetorical criticism and public speaking
hes seriously the best prof here and makes everyone feel so comfortable and caring, hes so personable and hes British haha, but srsly you won't regret it!!!! cannot recommend him enough
The lectures were super boring. The exams were also all over the place. It was his first semester teaching at Penn State, so he has probably gotten better since then.
great lectures interesting material learned alot
just wanted to say great lectures and very helpful
professor explains very clearly and helps you understand thank you
professor encourages you, liked that he cares about student, helpful with great feedback
lectures straight forward, assignments normal professor knows about the world and real life situations caring and inspirational
international professor knowledgable teaching and lectures great enjoyed the class
lectures and material given was good, learned about the course helped me understand better
Very boaring lectures do not take if you want to learn something

Woodman is a nice guy and cares about the subject but he just yaps for 99% of the class and there is never any clear learning topics. This is also the worst management of a class at PSU. Due dates are missing or unclear, directions to assignments make no sense and the TAs don't even have a clue what's going on. only positive is super easy grader.

If you're just looking for an easy grade, this isn't the class. The professor prioritizes life lessons over coursework, but expectations are unclear and inconsistent. Participation on assignments are flexible, yet assignments still impact grades. Overall, the structure is confusing—and that's exactly how the class feels daily.
He likes to make disparaging comments towards his TA's during class time. It is honestly awkward to witness. Outside of this, class is chaotic and hard to follow. Better off taking another course.

Greg Woodman is by far my favorite professor out of all of my years of education. He truly cares about everyone and will shape your outlook on life in such a positive way. Even if this class isn't required for your major, I reccomend you take it. Classes are interesting and fun to go to unlike any other class and he is so kind and caring

Absolute favorite professor I've had the privilege to learn from. I would love to keep in contact with him in the future as he has truly changed my life for the better. He values what every student has to say and is curious to learn about everyone. He sees potential in everyone and wants you to see it in yourself.

Greg is the best professor I have ever had and I would recommend him to anyone that has the opportunity to take his class. He is so caring and truly wants all of his students to succeed in and outside of the classroom. You will get 10x what you put into this class and make deep connections with those in the class. 1000% recommend if interested.

This is one of the best professors at Penn State! The class was super informative and instead of just learning outside things, the class is structured to the better understanding of yourself. Greg is amazing and so caring. His lectures were actually super entertaining and I made many friends in the class and through the group work. HIGHLY RECOMMEND

One of the best experiences of my life. There are 3 main assignments - personal business plan, startup case study and consultant case studies(personal and group). Greg helps you delve deeper into your swot analysis. He  is the epitome of entrepreneurial mindset. You need to  work hard but it gets amazing results. He is a guide than an instructor!

This was one of the most beneficial and impactful courses of my college career. Greg is an insightful and knowledgeable teacher and a great mentor. He creates a collaborative learning environment that simulates the real world of business. If you're willing to show up, engage, and be open to new ideas, this course can change your college experience.

This course is pointless. The lectures are just repeated and extremely shallow: you do a lot of work to learn nothing--expected to pay attention and participate in lectures that have no substance. The assignments are scattered, disorganized, and flawed. TA does all the grading, teaching, etc. Easy, mind-numbing class. Greg is a good guy.

Easily the best and most influential teacher ever! Just an overall amazing person with an awesome story who really cares about his students. You will learn so many important life lessons from him. His TA, Kayli, is also wonderful! Best class ever!

Really enjoyable lectures about things that students actually care about. I really enjoyed talking about our futures and how this class helped us create goals. Professor Woodman is great and really engages the class.
This is the best professor I have ever been taught by.
The professor is the best I have been taught by in my life.

Professor Woodman honestly changed my life and helped me view life in a different perspective. He was very personable and made me want to come to class everyday. Truly teaches you how to be successful in life and cares about each of his students. Genuinely an awesome person to be around, and even better teacher.

Greg is an awesome guy. Your performance will be directly correlated by how much you participate in class and if you are doing every assignment. The assignments are time-consuming but most of them are useful. Grading is very (very) generous and the only exam is easy. If you give the time it requires, this is an easy A and a enjoyable class.

Professor Woodman is very passionate about the topic. Yet, there is a clear disconnection between the student's learning experience and his expectation. If you do not have the time to spend at least ten hours a week on the class, you would have a very hard time to succeed academically. The assignments are very detailed and length savvy.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Amazing Professor with great insight. This class helped me plan my future as well as truly understand what a leader is. If you plan on ever having a leadership position of any sort please take this class!

Greg is a really nice guy. Lots of hands-on and group work- the group projects are a huge part of the grade, so make sure you get a good group! The homework is easy, and the exams are even easier. I'd definitely recommend him for ENGR 310, feels more like a fun elective than anything else. There is some cool stuff about personality/leadership types
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Caring

reviews.comment: It's very easy to succeed in this class as well as an enjoyable class in general. There's a good amount of writing for hw, but nothing truly difficult. Some public speaking, but it's a pretty relaxed environment. Be sure to keep on top of things for group projects and you'll be fine. Prof. Woodman is a really nice, understanding guy.

This class is an easy A, but not super informative. Most of the classes are spent on tangents with 20 minutes to cover the actual material, and the assignments are weird. Attendance and late work policy is very strict. Overall, easy class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Greg is a great professor and I learned a ton about entrepreneurship in his class. I appreciate the open environment and learning by doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Professor Woodman is a great professor, and a really nice guy. I learned so much from his class and had a lot of fun with the "fail fast, learn quickly" modus operandi of the class, much like how real entrepreneurship is. 10/10 would take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Very good professor. He clearly cares about students. It is also a really easy class, only once a week. Field trips are really nice, and you get to see parts of campus that not everyone gets to see. Almost no homework, the little homework he hands out is really easy. Be prepared for group projects and presentations. Not a tough grade at all.

Andrew is a great guy. He's always rooting for the students, and trying to inspire us to engineering more sustainable solutions to make the world a better place. Field trips are really fun as well. Super easy class as well, as expected out of a First Year Seminar.

Amazing professor. Lectures are interesting and field trips break up the day-to-day routine. Really cares and gets to know his students, will write rec letters if asked. Cares about teaching, lets class participate. There is a group presentation near the end, but your actual presentation skills aren't graded, just the info. No pressure at all.

This class is an intro to the concept of engineering, not anything technical. I really enjoyed it and that was mostly thanks to Andrew being so engaging and clearly caring about his job. He wants to be a support system for his students and makes it abundantly clear how important that is to him.

If you are an engineering major taking your first year seminar course, this is the professor to take it with. The class is half site visits, and half in class lectures. Andrew is a fantastic presenter and a lovely person. There is one group presentation, but all the other assignments are by yourself, and if you just simply do the work you'll pass.

Andrew is a great professor. He is an engineer for the university, not an academic. His seminar class meets once a week and consists of about half site visits to different places on campus related to different fields of engineering, and about half in-class lectures. A few small homework assignments too. Overall, great first-year seminar class.

Andrew is very chill and highly respects and cares about all of the students in the class. He is willing to help with literally anything from homework to recommendation letters. This class is very interesting and the site tours were my favorite experience this semester. I highly recommend this first-year seminar for incoming engineers.
He is a really good professor and will work with you outside of class if  you need help. He made this a very easy class all you have to do is show up.
Andrew is the man. Super chill and makes the class very easy going. He 100% is the best first year seminar that you can get. Definitely try to get him for your freshman year.

An amazing first year seminar. The class was about half classroom and half field trips to different places on campus. Andrew was great and learned all of our names after day 1. There are barely any assignments, and he is very forgiving for pretty much everything. He wants you to succeed. He also is happy to be a future reference.  Awesome class!

Prof Gutberlet teaches an amazing class that is easy to understand and gets you thinking. He is approachable, kind, and makes class super engaging. I could not recommend his class enough for a first year seminar, it'll be an easy A.

Very easy class, I probably had 2 hours of total homework for the whole semester. The class is about sustainable engineering, and was split between lectures and field trips to places around campus. He is a fun professor overall and tries to engage the class, friendly and easy to talk to. Show up and do the minimal work and you'll get an A.

Dr. Gutbelet is a solid choice for the engineering first-year seminar here at Penn State. For those who don't know, his special topics class is about engineering a sustainable future. He is a very lively person who wants to get to know you personally and he also likes it when you contribute to discussions. Super nice guy.

For his class, half of the time is building tours, and the other half is about how to present and sustainable options. There's barely any homework, only one presentation, and a final paper ( not super bad either). Super relaxed guy, a low stressful class. Definite choice if you want an easy A for a seminar.

Definitely the better of the two.  But doesn't excuse how difficult this class is.  Do not take this as a gen ed.  The class is all lecture-based, and the tests are spread far and wide and cover way too much for one to study.  The tests are also not open notes as some previous reviews said.

First off I would like to say that this class was very informative and interactive at times and the professors that teach this course are very knowledged and tried to make it very interesting. However, if you are looking for an easy elective to take, this is not the one. Homework is graded for accuracy and quiz/tests are closed notes.

I loved Dr. Grozinger's Honeybees class! She taught it with Harland Patch and they make a great duo. Her lectures are engaging and she does a good job of describing the material to all majors. As a math major who took her class as an elective, I thought she was great! You can tell she really loves her job! Tests and assignments are not hard at all.

It's a really interesting course. There's two online, open book exams and two paper exams (non-cumlative). and then 3 projects. The tests are reasonable and the projects are research papers and pretty easy.

I had to take this class for my major and I honestly underestimated how hard it was. It was a LOT of material for each exam and a lot of details that you need to know inside out. She only posts slides with blanks and attendance is a good chunk of your grade so you have to go to class.She has a accent and speaks really quietly which can make it hard

She talks very quietly, and even though she does seem as if she cares about the course and her students, no one seems to participate either. It's very hard to stay awake in this class, even when I take it in the afternoon; most of the time my energy is spent trying to understand what she said/went over, even if I sit near the front.

She was just ok. She has a very high pitched voice on top of an accent so that got annoying real quick. Her lecture slides are literally 75 slides long which is just ridiculous, but she does show you which ones are the most important before exams. As long as you do the out of class assignments and study for exams, you'll be fine.

You can tell Prof Hodges cares about her students, however it is extremely hard to hear her during lectures even with her mic on. She also goes through the slides pretty slowly and she just reads off of the slides. I ended up having to teach myself all of the material because of how quietly she speaks and reads.

She's very kind and definitely does try to make sure students understand the material. However, she does talk quietly and her accent sometimes makes it a little harder to understand her. Also, she is pretty weird and strange whenever she explains topics in her lectures in my opinion.

She actually talks and goes over the material at the speed of a sloth, even though she's reading off the slide. She talks VERY quietly and it's hard to hear her sometimes. There are probably 70-90 slides per chapter and there are about 3-4 chapters per exam. Exams can be worded weirdly imo. She does A LOT of Tophat. Good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is so sweet and a good professor but her lectures are pretty boring. She has gaps in the slides posted on canvas so the only way you can get this is by going to class. Use quizlet!!!! There is a LOT of memorisation, but put in the time and you will do well.

She is very nice and caring. Lectures are very boring. The exams were fairly easy in my opinion. The questions were not hard, if you study you'll do well. Other assignments are annoying but very easy. I would recommend her, just go to class and do the work and you'll be good.

She is the sweetest person ever and makes an effort to relate to students. She is quiet, often reads off her slides. Straight forward notes and easy assignments. Millions of things to memorize for the tests but she does reviews during class and basically tells you everything on the exam. AMD take a good chunk of time to complete.

She is the sweetest and has a great sense of humor. I underestimated this class; there was a lot of biochemistry and millions of things to memorize for the tests. AMD assignments take a good chunk of time to complete. Overall, I liked the class, but DO NOT RECOMMEND it to any non-STEM major.

so boring. she talks within the same 2 decibels for a full hour and 15 minutes. i go to most lectures and attendance is basically 20% of the grade....i do great on exams but the only thing keeping my grade down is attendance.

Dr. Hodges is a very sweet lady. You can tell she cares about her students and is passionate about this course. However, there is a lot of material and she essentially reads it off the slides. But, most of it isn't even on the exam. The assignments are easy A's, but you really need to study for the tests.

This class has a lot of information, but her notes have stuff in purple, which means you need to know it for the exam. She is very quiet, so it can be hard sometimes to hear her. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are top hats in each class that count towards a little percentage of your grade.

Talks very quiet. Reads off the notes, no explanations given. Tests have nothing to do with the notes. Does not respond back to emails or post lecture videos. Expects us to know the test information when they are things we have never discussed in class. Difficult learning environment. Doesn't know how to teach about the subject.

She is pretty quiet, but uses a microphone and is super passionate about her profession. Provides extra pieces of information for application and practical purposes. Very insightful and caring for her students.
Very caring and knowledgeable

She reads off the slides with some fill in notes. She is very quiet and the lectures are very boring. I had no idea what to expect for the first exam, but they are very specific and require a lot of memorization. She makes videos for review, but it is the same slides and she just rereads them. Do not take this as a GenEd!

Her lectures were very boring and long... all she really did was read off of the slides in a very quiet voice. She was very understanding of my circumstances though and let me take an exam a few weeks after it was originally scheduled. The info was just a lot of memorization. Exams were really hard if you did not study.

Overall, the lectures were long and boring. She talked very quietly so it was hard to hear her in the back, but you could tell she loves what she teaches and wants you to succeed. Very approachable and will answer any questions that you may have. If you're taking this as a gen ed, don't! Be prepared to go to every class as attendance matters!

Dr. Hodges is alright, if you have to take her it's not the end of the world. Her lectures are extremely boring, but you have to go in order to get the fill-in-the-blanks for the slides. TopHat is worth a lot too, and she does on average 5-6 questions per class. She's also a bit weird. Overall nice woman though, and does care for her students.

The lectures are mind numbingly boring and she will asks questions which are literally on the board for everyone to see and will wait for a poor sole to mumble out the answer which everyone already can read off the board. She does effectively teach the content and the slideshows are exactly like the test. Class is easy if you study a bit and notes.

she is very nice and you can tell she likes what she teaches. although attendance isnt mandatory, there are top hats that count for credit. you get .5 point if you get it right and .5 point for just answering. the exams are information directly from the slides and tophats so as long as you study those 2 things you will be good.

Dr. Hodges is amazing. She is so kind and sweet, and you can tell she truly loves what she is teaching. The class itself is a LOT of memorization (3 exams and 1 final), but overall not hard! She makes it very easy to learn and take notes, and the exams are just like the slides and TopHat questions. I highly recommend!

Professor Hodge's class is pretty great. Lectures revolve around TopHat for participation and fill-in-the-blank slides. Info for the exams (3 midterms + 1 Final) comes directly from the slides + usually a review session before each exam that goes over the relevant slides. Mcgraw Hill assignments every week. Extra credit research lab (2%).
Dr. Hodges' class is VERY easy if you go to class. in her powerpoint slides she leaves blanks in the notes though, so if you don't go you wont have all the info in the notes.

This class was good. She does not give too many homework assignments and they are really easy and not a waist of time. She is also not a tough grader on assignments either. The slides that we go over in class are exactly like the exam questions. I studied off of the slides and got Bs and As on the exams.

Easiest class ever. There are a lot of notes but I used an iPad and just downloaded everything, 99% of it was already done just a few words here or there needed filled in. The homework can get a little tedious but I'd do it again for the easy A. She basically told us what was all going to be on the exams and I only studied a day or two before them.

Dr. Hodges is my favorite professor I've had so far. She is very kind and her lectures are interesting and easy to follow. She has clear lecture slides, and does review for each exam. The homework assignments and case studies are very relevant to what you are studying.

This class is meh. She low-key does give us a lot of homework every week which sucks and the lectures are SO boring, but you do not have to go. There are a lot of tophat questions which you have to do. The exams are exactly like the slides, so if you study the color coated sentences you should be fine. I do recommend going to the TA for extra help

This class is easy if you show up to lecture. The review session she held at the beginning of the semester for the first exam was helpful, but as the semester continued the review sessions became less helpful as she didn't want to help as much when she noticed people not showing up to class. Thosewho regularly showed up to class were punished, too.

Dr. Hodges is the best professor I've had at Penn State. It's clear that she cares about her students and is always willing to further explain anything and answer questions. She's passionate about teaching and it's obvious in class. The enthusiasm she brings to class is unmatched by any other professor I've had. Her expectations are clear.

Dr. Hodges is the best professor I've ever had at Penn State. I enjoyed her lecture, and she was always passionate about teaching. Her PowerPoint was clear and easy to read. She would have review sessions before each exam, and she would point out the key materials. She was also more than happy to help her students outside the class.
Dr, Hodges is definitely the best professor in Nutrition. Her tests are straightforward. She gives detailed review sessions before tests. I love her so much.

Dr. Hodges does an amazing job of explaining the material. The information we learn in this class is complex and she does a great way of explaining it in a way that we can understand. She makes it clear what her expectations are and is always willing to help students out. She's one of the best professors I've had at Penn State.

This class was so hard that I had to drop it. Don't get me wrong, she's nice, but this class was impossible. I got 100s on almost all assignments except for the exams. I did so bad on the exams that it was impossible to get above a B in the class after the second exam. Be prepared to type. There's about 45-50 pages of doc notes for every exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Holness is AMAZING. He is super caring and so smart. His lectures are engaging. As long as you pay attention in class and participate during discussions, you will be totally fine. He is so funny too!

Just don't take him. Simple. He obviously doesn't know how to communicate or relate to students. Knows his stuff but expects his first or second year students to know as much as he does. Should be in another field not working with other people. Bad communication skills and overall just should not have a professor job
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had at PSU
