reviews.comment: never take this professor. point blank period
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: if i could go back in time to when i scheduled this class id slap myself. this has been the most frustrating experence of my life, if i could give 0 stars i would. whatever you do avoid this professor! he has a superiority complex and makes you feel stupid for asking questions
Dr Holness is tough but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: being completely honest, this professor is awful. he cannot do his job, nor is he a good person. i'm not trying to sound harsh but he seriously made me debate dropping out ever day. this man shouldn't be a professor. he's not kind of empathetic to his students.
very passionate lady, good w extensions. her daughter was in the hospital this sem so I'm giving her grace on her unorganized nature

Very unorganized and will yap with no end goal about her daughter instead of talking about actual class material. Will assign tons of notes you will never end up talking about in class. The final where you make puppets? You will not start it until like nine weeks in, while other classes started during week two. Need help? Good luck Charlie.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: My classmate whining in the comments didn't even try in class. Dr. Henward might be messy but she earned her position lol just don't blow off the class. she's so kind and lovely, not her fault people hate good profs

Worst professor I have had yet. Apparently the Head of ECE. She never even speaks a real sentence and stops it halfway through and begins another one. I leave the class more confused than when I went in. Penn State, do better. This isn't okay.
the GOAT of the education dept. so willing to help and really cares about what she's talking about
She is so kind and thoughtful. Take this class if you want to be challenged and inspired. Dr. Henward really cares.

Dr. Henward is very passionate about what she teaches. The class can be boring at times but is very easy. Not many assignments but you will work in groups often. She can be unorganized at times but is very forgiving with missing/late assignments. Overall, it is a pretty easy class and she definitely knows what she is talking about.

Dr. Henward is an amazing teacher!! I haven't finished the course yet but I can't wait to give her a 5/5. She is kind, loving, caring, knowledgeable. Her class does have a lot of reading but you will learn so much through those readings. Also, I loved the discussions in class because those are some great questions that we need to consider in educ.

Dr. Henward is absolutely amazing. Her class is extremely inspiring and it is very clear that she is passionate about what she teaches. She is open to questions and comments and loves to hear feedback from her students. Her syllabus is extremely detailed and the assignments are very interesting. I would highly recommend taking this course with her!

I loved Dr. Henward's class! There is a decent chunk of reading but you will discuss all of the reading in class. She has a lot of experience as an educator and is very knowledgable on what she is teaching. The only grades really come from the midterm exam, the final paper, book club project, and a few reading responses but they're all easy!

You will only be graded on quizzes which get harder with each attempt he claims to give amazing feedback and how helpful it is but the feedback doesn't even actually tell you how you went wrong in the problem the only way to do well in this class is to spend hours studying and going to office hour and working with the las
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I have ever had by far. No exams and quiz retakes sounds good until its not. You take min 3 quizzes every week and 6 or more if you dont pass the 1st try. He is hard to contact, condescending, and blames any misconceptions on students. The ONLY grades are quizzes. My mental health is in shambles. Dont do specs grading.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had him for 210 and 212 because he was the only professor available 210 was easier than 212, but he was condescending anytime you asked him a question. The material isn't the hardest, but the specs grading is annoying, after the first three weeks you have at least three quizzes a week and you can't make mistakes on the quizzes or you get a 0.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Are these reviews botted? Why did I just see Joseph Houck get called "the goat." I hated that guy, but the class was fine ig. Specs grading was easy but a waste of time and promoted regurgitation of information. Also, at an off-campus event, someone unprompted told me that this professor showed favoritism to muscular boys.

Houck is the goat. He just won the atherton teaching award. Having in in 210 and 212 has me acing the MCAT orgo questions. He really cares about his students learning which comes through not only during class but how the course is structured. Very flexible and may opportunities to demonstrate learning.

It was my first class that used specs grading and I really appreciated it. I felt like I actually learned and internalized the material rather than just memorizing for an exam. Love the class worksheets he uses with lots of examples.

The structure of this course improved my learning compared to other chem courses I have taken. Being offered optional assignments that can only boost your grade, along with the fact that you have all semester to complete some of them, was a major help. I really benefited from the spec grading system, and I am taking much more away from this course.

Dr. Houck made every effort to help his students learn chemistry, love chemistry, and be successful in his class. We had access to so many extra resources to practice. I could reach my TAs, professor, and peers outside of class easily.  Being able to take quizzes multiple times allowed me not only to learn more but also to do well overall.

My learning experience in this course was great. The assignments and feedback I received helped me further understand the material that was discussed in class. However, I would say Dr. Houck goes over material very quickly in class but I understand that there is a lot of material to over the semester.
do not let my grade fool you. i cried sm. you cannot afford to fall behind (sooo many quizzes per week). taking him again for 212 tho

Dr Houck is the best professor i've had for chemistry. This class is challenging but if you put in the effort and you show up to his office hours you will do good. Specs grading is the goat. So excited to have him for another semester
Graded by a few LTs every week which are very easy to slip up and fall behind on. He is very accessible in office hours and will help you go over whatever you missed, though.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not a bad guy. He has good resources that allow you to do well in the class. However, he's not very easy to get ahold of and he's a bit of a slow grader. Other than that, this wasn't a bad class if you put the time into it.

The only thing you are graded for in 210/212 are the LT quizzes; realistically you can skip all the lectures, homework, and outside of class material and get an A in the class. Keep up with quizzes or you will be taking 10 a week (no exaggeration). I missed two weeks of classes due to a family emergency and for the last month I took 10 a week.

This class brought SO much unnecessary stress and was not worth it. If you get behind on quizzes one week you'll take 6+ the next week which take hours to study for. He was also very condescending. Ochem is difficult, but he made it worse. My advice- take the exam section and be stressed for only the week of the exam and not the entire semester.

Dr. Houck is by far the worst professor I have ever had. He is condescending and rude & extremely hard to contact. By the middle of the semester, we were taking upwards of 8-9 quizzes a week all on different material, and it was near impossible to study for all of them and be successful. I would not wish this experience on my worst enemy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Had potential to be very well structured but fell short. Grading is extremely subjective and "all or nothing". I found myself taking ~8 quizzes a week which is virtually impossible to study for while taking other classes. Everything is basically optional but there is so much to do that it would be impossible to finish. Structure needs fixing.

Dr. Houck has been the best chemistry professor I have had my entire life. He explains concepts very well and is very understanding and willing to answer questions. Specs grading is for people who can handle studying on a weekly basis. It rewards consistent hard work. If you are a lazy student, it can be overwhelming.

"No exams" sounds so appealing til you're in the trenches in week 10 and taking 7 quizzes each week between recitation & quiz hours. The grading is subjective and dependent on the TA/LA who grades your LTQ, and they frequently make errors that need to be regraded. Houck is stubborn and condescending about his "revolutionary" grading scheme.

By far worst teacher I've ever had in my entire life. The curriculum he's teaching is all over the place. He uses an outdated website to teach and you'll never get in contact with him. I messaged at least 6x over the entire semester on different applications and never got a response. The practice and guides and hw are nothing like the test.

He is one of the least understanding professors I've ever had. He is often snarky or will rudely call out students if they are not understanding something in lecture. This course is not terribly difficult, but you will not enjoy your time with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Houck was the rudest and most uncaring professor I've ever had. A family emergency forced me to miss two weeks of school. I asked Houck multiple times if I should drop the class, as it was a lot of work I had missed. He told me we would figure it out, and then dodged every attempt to contact him for weeks before trying to defer my grade.

I've never taken more away from a class in my life. One of the only classes here where I actually pay attention during lecture because Dr. Houck explains concepts so well. He makes hard topics simple and supplements lecture with videos if he sees that the majority is struggling. You can see how much he cares. Prepares you well for 212, 213, & mcat.

I am all for Specs grading. Dr. Master's format was great in my experience. However in this course, the majority of its benefit is removed. 3-4 quizzes each week is an incredible burden, and there is virtually no partial credit. Get one wrong, you might sneak by with a 2 or 1, anything more, zero. With this structure, its 0% or 100%. Disappointing.

Houck is condescending and defensive. He thinks specs grading is great but the way he does it seems rushed and sloppy. The number of quizzes per week is insane, I feel so bad for whoever has to grade them. People get by in this class without knowing anything, and then he brags about how many people got an A. If you want to learn, don't take Houck.
BEST ORGANIC CHEMISTRY PROFESSOR AT PENN STATE
He took a class that notoriously tanks your gpa for med school and made it the easiest stem class I've taken here so far. It was so fun. Best professor I've ever had.

Specs grading is a joke. Replacing exams while expecting students to do a ridiculous amount of quizzes and other random stuff is so insanely silly. As someone else mentioned, He thinks he has the education system figured out but in reality, I found it much easier to learn the same content in Funk's exam-based class and the workload was much less.

Houck was always very caring and supportive in everything he did. Some people might not like the grading system, but I think it made me retain and understand information a lot better than an exam based course. Docked the point for how fast he goes through topics at times, and the harsh grading. Organic chem is hard, Houck makes it bearable.

Probably the most caring professor I have ever had on campus, and he will take the time to get to know you. Even though he is a great person, the way he grades is terrible. The grading system will have your entire grade almost based on 9 different "quizzes", I would prefer the 3 exams over this.

Houck's specs grading system takes some getting used to, but the tradeoff is a ton of support resources. The concepts can be tough, so definitely use office hours and tools like unstuck AI to stay on top of the material.

Joseph Daniel Houck thinks he has the education system figured out. He convinces himself that specs grading is a perfect system that helps students learn concepts rather than memorize them but doesn't realize that it achieves the exact opposite effect. Any given student would learn better from traditional grading than his "revolutionary" system.

Not a lot of good options for 212 professors, but Dr. Houck is still pretty bad. Class structure was just disorganized. The grading structure is the worst thing imaginable, would rather have 4 large exams. The grading itself is VERY subjective, and there is  no transparency in how to do well on a quiz. Lectures were useless. Nice guy, bad teacher.

Take this class with caution! If you ever have any questions to ask Dr. Houck, honestly do not even bother. He will not respond until weeks or months later. He assigned many quizzes with missing images and never bothered to fix them because he acted like it was not his problem. His extra credit(s) are basically pointless. All I can say is pray lol.

Make sure not to get admitted to the hospital or stay in the ER for a period of time because he doesn't allow any make-ups of anything. I was in and out of the hospital for several weeks due to a medical condition and he was the ONLY professor that gave me no help what so ever. He told me "sorry nothing I can do, its stated in the syllabus."

I thought this course was well structured. I liked that we had to take LT quizzes and we could better learn from our mistakes compared to just exams.  The quizzes he gives are straightforward and fair in terms of what we should be expected to know. Overall, I thought this course was a good learning experience for me.

Houck is a very smart professor but I do not think he is for everyone. He does specs grading, so if you fall behind you will never catch up. I fell behind because I had some things going on in my life and I never ended caught back up. I was taking 6 quizzes a week every week. Not a bad professor but make sure you can handle his type of teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Basically unapproachable outside of class if you're not doing well in the class. Seems passive aggressive if you ask for help from him and you basically have to rely on the TA/LA team to help you understand anything. He seems like a nice and friendly guy otherwise but would probably do better as a research scientist rather than a professor.

Lots of LA/TA/Instructor time outside of class that I highly suggest taking advantage of to do well in the class. I had Masters for 210 so it was a tough transition at first, but the most important thing is practicing and reviewing as much as possible. Watch the review videos for the individual quizzes, those helped me more than anything.

I had Houck for CHEM 210/212 and I liked the use of specs grading. While attendance is not mandatory, often direct examples from the notes will appear on the quizzes. He has a large LA/TA team making it easy to get help outside of class. He provides plenty of optional practice to prepare for the weekly quizzes.

I honestly liked Houck's teaching style overall. Specs grading was great - I felt like I learned all of the content well but was never stressed about the class. He does sometimes rush through important concepts during class, but if you take time to review notes and do the practice on Canvas you'll be fine. Overall enjoyed taking 210/212B with him.

Dr. Houck is definitely a great professor to take for Organic Chem. The specs grading took some time getting used to, but if you know what grade you wanted it is easily achievable when putting in the work. I had Houck for both 210B and 212B and got an A in 210 so its not too bad! Just beware that 212B is much harder concept wise!

Dr. Houck is very passionate about orgo. You either like him or you don't. Either way, he provides so many resources for us to do well in the class. Going to GSG and Learning Communities definitely helped me on the quizzes. Specs grading can sometimes be a tossup though, but you can take the same quiz up to 5 times.

For a guy teaching organic chemistry, he is the champion of champions. Not enough nice things can be said about Dr. Houck. I had him as a prof for a full year and never regretted that decision. Has a HUGE support staff that's really knowledgeable. Also, ignore the people who complain about him. They probably don't know the meaning of "work."

AVOID THIS PROFESSOR! Took CHEM 210B with him and enjoyed it, but 212B is 10x harder and the quizzes are graded so harshly. Specs grading can be nice sometimes, but you have to devote so much time to studying for ~6 quizzes every week. Dr. Houck is also not very approachable and isn't helpful outside of class. This class was painful to get through.
He does the specs grading but Ochem 2 is really hard and he's a nut compared to ochem 1. lowkey kinda sus
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: The grading for this course is a joke. They look for reasons to dock points. An example would be losing points "summary was too short"  or "missing data." What data was missing? I don't know. I answered every question on the lab? If I were you, I would take this class in-person because you sure won't be getting any answers to your questions here.

I took this class, because it was mandatory. I enjoyed the concepts, but it was not due to his material. Also, the study material was very disorganized and all over the place instead of consolidated to one area. He also offers to help with things, but does not respond promptly or if he does it is condescendingly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Houck is an ok teacher! He sometimes rushes through way too advanced concepts and teaches like we all have chemistry PhDs, but mostly he gets the point across. My good score is mostly for the specs grading format he uses - it makes approaching dense topics so much easier and leaves room for error! Everybody should use specs grading!
I took this class online summer 2022. I was retaking chem 110. It is a hard class. Luckily he gave partial credit on exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Hard subject but Specs Grading made it easy to get a good grade. Made minimum to get each letter grade so much harder than it needed to be, expect to take 4-8 quizzes a week after Week 4. Goes over the bare minimum to pass the LT quizzes in lectures in the most confusing way possible, you'll need to do a TON of work outside of lecture to pass LTs.

This class is the first time that I felt like I was learning and succeeding in a chemistry class. I credit Dr. Houck's dedication to education and students. In college I seldom see an instructor work to the degree he does with students to help them succeed.

Dr. Houck was a nice professor who explained concepts clearly for the most part. Specs grading system was a pain, to the point that I'd actually prefer exams (and that's saying a lot from someone who hates exams). Especially towards the second half, expect to take 4-8 difficult, in-person quizzes per week. There are many ways to get help though.

If you have to take organic chemistry at Penn State, take it with Dr. Houck. With the specs grading system, students are able to learn the material in small increments rather than taking large exams. He truly wants to see his students succeed and provides many opportunities to do so. TAs & LAs were amazing too & very knowledgeable in the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Houck is highly intelligent and knows what he's talking about; however, he comes off as condescending. He encourages discussing grades over emails but does not respond promptly. The specs grading is convenient and made it possible to get an A despite the difficulty of organic chem.

Houck did specs grading for the second semester this fall and it was lovely. In some ways it was overwhelming to have so many opportunities to succeed, because it felt like I HAD to get an A, but he's doing his best. I will say though the 210B felt very much more geared towards premed students and as a chem major I wasn't as engaged

I understand his approach to specs grading but the execution is downright atrocious. I think this class should be standardized more. The grading is unclear and hurried at some instances and Houck can be quite condescending. Despite this, this course is a good introduction to organic chemistry 1.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The SPECS grading system may be the reason for my hatred of this class. It requires you to take 4-8 quizzes a week which becomes very time-consuming because a lot are taken outside of class time. The answer keys for quizzes are also vague and confusing and Houck has given rude responses back if you ask questions about them.

Dr. Houck does an excellent job at providing scaffolding to allow students to be autonomous in their learning. I actually really liked the structure of this course. Dr. Houck provided a plethora of resources that varied in mode of learning that allowed students to customize their course to their strengths in order to be successful.

He was a really sweet and understanding professor! Genuinely cares about his students excelling in the class and had such a calm and chill personality with us which made the students feel more at ease with the class. He instructed the material with no doubts and even ensured us that there were no dumb questions that could be asked in the class.

I had high hopes for this class since spec grading seems ideal with having more time to learn the information. The reality of it is that as much as the quizzes overlap because topics in chemistry relate. In CHEM 212 especially different reactions vary slightly. Also much of my learning occurred out of lecture using master organic chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: If you have to take 210B or 212B, choose the B. No exams, course is run by specs grading in which you take quizzes every week that are pass/fail with 5+ attempts to pass them. Orgo is still hard, but specs grading gives you the chance to learn from your mistakes and improve. I think you're making a mistake if you take regular orgo with tests!

I am certain my peers write rude things on here because ochem is difficult and they turn their frustration onto Dr. Houck, as to absolve themselves of personal responsibility. I genuinely loved Dr. Houck's teaching style. The worksheets are such a good way methodically building on prior knowledge.  He teaches a sort of 'chemical intuition'. 10/10

The professor was responsive and kind, and that helped a great deal. The TAs were also kind. No one ever made me feel bad because I didn't know something, and that means a lot. The unlimited practice quizzes were amazing and extremely helpful! The practice exams were useful. The unlimited knowledge checks were very useful as well.

He is good with his lecture videos and explaining the material. 4 total exams, the final was optional but in a way, you could redeem yourself to achieve a higher grade. If you are a student who needs to speak with their professor to ask questions, this is not your guy. His communication is lacking greatly, expect an email reply over a week later.

Great lecturer and structured course so it is easy to get help. Specs grading is a net positive. The people complaining about it are just mad they didn't do well.Houck is a great prof that will actively help you learn. He would have a 5 star rating if he didn't teach such a difficult course.

Specs grading was so unique and I was able to show growth and progress over time, rather than on a few midterms. More professors should use specs grading, because it eliminates so much stress! There were so many resources and practice modules for each learning target. This truly made a difference in my understanding of the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Houck is a really great professor for OChem. There's a lot of people complaining about the specs grading with synthesis being difficult, but synthesis problems shouldn't be easy. There was a lot of time for office hours and LA/TA hours for help.

Would definitely recommend for Chem 210B, not for 212B. Specs grading was very difficult for this semester and you needed to basically get a 100% on every quiz to pass. I would have to take 3+ quizzes in quiz hours and then 4 more in recitation every week. It kind of felt like having two exams every week. TAs/LAs a great

His lectures are actually pretty good, but he is unreachable outside of class sometimes and the TAs can be downright rude when responding to regrade requests even if they made a mistake. Specs grading is a complete disaster and is very inconsistent. He also loses quizzes and forces you to retake them anyways.

Dr. Houck's specs grading system made 212B a nightmare. I spent 2+ hours taking quizzes each week, grading was harsh (100% to pass a quiz) and unorganized. My quizzes went "missing" in his office many times, and I received grades less than 24 hrs before my next attempt, sometimes not even until after. Also, reaching him over email is impossible.

The specs grading was definitely a game changer for me. As a student who took traditional-exam styled orgo I and transitioned into orgo II with specs grading, with confidence I can say I have learned far more from the quizzes and this style of learning compared to traditional orgo I. No exams, just weekly quizzes. Take Houck for 210B/212B!

Truly my favorite class at Penn State so far. Dr. Houck is an amazing teacher who cares about his students and has a great way of teaching. The teaching style is awesome with no exams. There is tons of help from the team and lots of practice problems available.

Specs grading is okay. It has so many faults and great aspects. However, he is so unorganized with this stuff. He doesn't keep to the deadlines he made. He is very lenient but it's often seen with a speck of favoritism. He doesn't teach very concisely and puts very difficult things on the quizzes which then leads to everyone failing. it's a mess.

Great professor. Course work is very challenging prepare to spend lots of time studying for the exams and practicing the material. Another thing about him is his horrible communication skills if you need anything from him make sure to reach out at least 3 days in advance.

I do not understand why he has a 5/5 rating. He uses 20 different sites for homework, making it overcomplicated. The tests are nothing like the practice. The lectures are so dull they can put someone with insomnia to sleep. This class is worse than EMCH 210, MATH 230, and MATH 251 combined, which is a miracle.

Specs grading with Houck is a game changer. He is very willing and eager to help students understand the material and genuinely wants everyone to succeed. The material is still very challenging but I don't think you could find a better professor than Dr. Houck.

Dr. Houck really cares about and invests in his students. New specs grading system had some hiccups, but this was a pilot, so understandable. The way he speaks can come off as condescending, but from speaking to him individually, I don't think this is intentional.  I never liked chem before and orgo is hard, but I loved it and feel I learned a lot.

The specs grading was good for the most part but expectations on the quizzes aren't always super clear and it only takes a few mistakes to not earn credit for a quiz. There's tons of help available outside of class but you are at a disadvantage if you don't have time to commit to seeking help frequently.

Not sure why people are praising him. I found him incredibly condescending and the only reason I got an A in this class was because of the specs grading system and going to every learning community and GSG I could. I learned more from the LAs and TAs than I did from him.

Dr. Houck used specifications grading (grade determined by number of mastered "learning targets"). I will say he had to deal with so much complaining from students. Orgo I is inherently a pain. He made it so there was so many office hours & time to ask questions. Prolly hardest working prof. This class made getting an A predictable and possible.

Dr. Houck is awesome and very cool. This was one of my first classes here at Penn State and already one of my favorites. OChem is naturally going to somewhat difficult, so you're going to have to put in effort to get a good grade. I liked the specs grading for the most part, but it seemed like we spent too much time on the easy stuff at the start.

The specs grading system provides you more flexibility in making mistakes and gives you chances to retake the quizzes until you are proficient. It can be tiring in the middle of the semester, but looking back now, I definitely learned more and understood the materials better. It makes me enjoy orgo chem (not a chem major), and feel successful.

I personally liked specs grading but if you'd prefer to have exams and homework I would not recommend Houck. We were the first class he used this method of grading on so we were kind of crash dummies and it was a bit disorganized BUT this class was much more enjoyable than my Gen Chem classes and I actually felt that I was learning.

I loved Dr. Houck! He used a specification grading scheme, which allowed for assessments to be retaken up to 6 times. There was no exams, making the class less stressful, especially because of the difficult topics expected organic chemistry. LA Casey was amazing!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The specs grading system was very poorly implemented. This class consists of anywhere between 4-10 challenging quizzes PER WEEK and they are graded with very little feedback. Houck is incredibly condescending and he does not seem to care about the success of his students. Upon multiple visits, he made me feel insecure about my academic abilities.
The class is very disorganized and very little feedback is provided on quizzes. The specs grading system has not been implemented well. The class structure also involves taking 4-8 quizzes per week.
He is amazing and really willing to help. Go talk to him if you have any concerns/difficulties, and he gives good feedback. The best chem professor ever!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: really good teacher

Advice: take this w/ World Campus; SO much better than in person. Still too much work for 1 credit, but at least deadlines are manageable + can use notes on exams. You get supplies in lab kit + do experiments/exams wherever/whenever you want. I've never met Dr. Houck, but he seems very chill. Asynch CHEM111 is the way to go if you need this course.

Dr. Houck was an amazing professor! His lectures were easy to understand, but he did just go through the course pack for the class. The homework was helpful in learning exam material even though the exams were much harder. If you can take Houck for this class, I would!

People like him since he's nice and a good lecturer. He makes the class harder than it already needs to be. A topic that was 10% of the unit will be 50% of unit exam. Exams are now in class (50 mins) but the same length and complexity as when they were outside of class in 90 min periods. Your grade depends on which LA grades it. GSG is very helpful

Dr. Houck is obviously here to help! Just consider all of the resources provided from supplemental readings/videos to frequent student hours. Houck is not a bad professor by any means. I think he truly cares for his students and explained the material well. Beware of the angry students commenting on here because they didnt get the grade they wanted.

The quizzes being every two weeks he says “puts less pressure” actually did the opposite for me i was always unprepared when they came around and it was the only class I was barely passing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a nice teacher but is very difficult to understand. I often find that he mumbles during the lectures and talks too quietly. There are quizzes every other week and are scheduled in the PTC. The quizzes require a lot of studying, but no midterms are given.

Prof. Goffe is an amazing professor. He clearly explains the topics & answers any of your questions very clearly. Coming from someone who had a difficult time in another economics class, I didn't have high hopes for Econ 104. However, he completely changed my stance on it. You can tell he's a caring person and only wants the best for his students.

Amazing. Talks a lot for long lectures but it is very clear how caring he is and how much he wants his students to learn and gain from his class. Study for the quizzes. Go to class/GSG sessions and be engaged. Your lowest quiz score (7 quizzes instead of midterms) is dropped. I would definitely take him again for another economics course!

My favorite professor I have had. His lectures are very easy to understand and he is very engaging and kind. He really cares about his students and he gives lots of resources to be able to help you study. The quizzes every 2 weeks makes it easier to keep up with learning. I really enjoyed his class.
Quiz every 2 weeks and he only teaches from slides with barely any homework, so you can't really have any hands on learning. If that isn't for you then don't take this class
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Good guy, class not too bad.
Prof. Goffe made a subject I did not want to take fun and enjoyable. Highly recommend taking a class with him, minus having to take a quiz every 2 weeks.

You can tell that Professor Goffe truly cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. Although his lectures can be boring from time to time he provides plenty of resources on canvas for studying. Do the reading assignments and study the quiz information that he releases before each quiz and you will be fine.

I try to shoot for A's and I got an A- in this class. However, it was very worth it. He is a very caring person and lays out everything very carefully and explains stuff well. The quizzes were sometimes a little confusing but overall a good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: I loved having Professor Goff for ECON 104! He cares so much about his students and truly wants everyone to succeed. He goes out of his way to provide his students opportunities to do well on the exams. His quizzes are really not hard if you study just a little bit and actually go to lecture. The GSG sessions are also huge. Overall one of the best!

Bill Goffe is an excellent teacher who, despite his monotone way of speaking, is very passionate about teaching and makes lectures interesting. He's very helpful with grading, the lowest quiz and 2nd stage are dropped, all homework is graded on completion, and a lenient participation grade only requiring you to answer 75% of in-class questions.

Having quizzes instead of exams seems nice, but I personally like to lock in and learn the material myself the week before exams. Having to do that 7 times and a final instead of the usual 3-4 exams kinda sucked. Having the drop quiz helps. Idk how the other 104 profs are but Goffe is probably similar,

Dawg there's so many freaking quizzes. When he first said we didn't have midterms and instead had seven quizzes, believe me, I was the first one jumping up and down from my seat. But bloody HECK, they're so difficult and time-consuming. Studying for the finals has been the worst thing I've done. Please help me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Goffe is one of the kindest professors I've ever encountered at Penn State. He is so accommodating when something comes up; he's very understanding and truly wants the best for his students. Slides are clear and easy to understand, and the quizzes are not difficult if you study the learning objectives. Attendance/participation through iClicker.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Goffe explains the content well except he is very monotone and the class can become very boring. He uses clicker questions for attendance and it has geolocation so you must attend class for it. He has 7 quizzes throughout the semester instead of midterms. If you take this course with professor Goffe, you basically have a quiz every week.

Prof Goffe is a great guy and he has a pretty structured system to help you learn and understand material.Tests are pretty easy, with a few challenging questions.Some questions are just straight common sense.Makes you do 2nd stage quizzes/reflections to help your understanding. I dont like the Perusal HW he gives
He is very monotone during his mandatory lectures and gives out quizzes every other week. The quizzes are somewhat challenging. Go to the GSG reviews.
Quizzes every two weeks were terrible—unclear, rushed, and didn't reflect the material well. The course felt disorganized, and grading seemed inconsistent. Overall, a very frustrating experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bill is a great guy and super friendly. He is also very helpful too and wants everyone to do well. There are bi-weekly quizzes in pollock which mostly make up your grade. There are also assignments on Perusall and Canvas. Definitely watch the GSGs because those were extremely helpful for each quiz. Instead of Tophat he uses iClicker.

Amazing chill professor. Very organized and easy to follow lectures which are posted to canvas. 7 quizzes instead of midterms and although the midterms are tough if you genuinely read the material AND WATCH THE GSG videos it is hard to do bad in this class. Very accessible outside of class and most importantly genuinely cares about his students.

He is an okay professor. In my opinion, he gives too much busy work and the quizzes he gives instead of midterms are not that easy. GO TO THE GSG REVIEWS, those help but sometimes they don't even help. I don't like the quizzes because you have to study for them as if they are exams since they are in pollock. I wouldn't take this class again w him

Dr. Goffe is a really nice professor who is very passionate about his subject. However, his lectures can be extremely dull and boring while containing information that isn't posted anywhere. The class is graded on 7 quizzes and a final which is less daunting than it sounds. Make sure to go to class and the GSG and you'll do well.

Professor Goffe really cares and you can see that through the lectures. He is a fantastic teacher and makes everything easy to understand. Only quizzes in Pollock Testing Center every other week - usually 20 questions. Get the course pack, skim the textbook, and take good lecture notes and you'll be fine.

I find his lectures to be very interesting, and you can tell he cares a lot about the subject and making students understand. The course consists of 7 biweekly quizzes, and a final. The worst quiz grade gets dropped. There is homework in the online textbook, but it is very simple. Definetely a good option of a professor for ECON 104.

I enjoyed his class. He clearly cares a lot about his students. Lectures could sometimes get a bit boring, but go to class because clicker questions are very important for understanding concepts. Biweekly quizzes were nice compared to midterms. Make sure to do the readings.

I genuinely enjoyed this class. The bi-weekly quizzes I had a love hate relationship with but they weren't bad. Watch the GSG videos, they help a lot and sometimes contain questions that are VERY similar to those on the exam. Classes feel long but he is passionate about what he teaches and you can tell he wants everyone to learn something.

Bill Goffe is honestly really chill, once you get past the really soft voice You should make sure you are taking clear notes since there are things he might mention once that can appear on the exam. GSG's are also super helpful. If you come in with no economic background and just give yourself a little time to study, then you should be fine.

I didn't do anything in this class, 99% of why i showed up was attendance, just watch the GSGs before exams and you will pass comfortably. He's a good professor but very quiet soft and monotone, makes it hard to focus during lectures.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr Goffe is a chill guy. Hardest issue is paying attention as he has a very soft voice and a low mic volume it makes it hard to pay attention. His notes are also not very direct and relate to real world events, therefore on occasion can be hard to understand a fine cut definition. Overall it was a fine class but the GSG sessions helped more.

Prof. Goffe gives great lectures and goes into detail on topics without being too complex. The class is structured very well, giving you plenty of time to study for quizzes. Also, the content of the course builds on itself, making it easier to retain knowledge and prepare for the final exam. Attendance is important so that you have good notes.

He is a very good professor. He cares a lot about his students and their success. He gives more than enough material to prepare for the bi-weekly quizzes (which does become a lot), and they can be easy if you put in the effort. I did struggle in this class, but I know that it was on my end and not his. He received an ovation on our last day.

The nicest professor at Penn state. if i had to marry a professor I'd marry Dr. Goffe. He is the nicest man I have ever met. the class was great, he is so caring. He does biweekly quizzes that help a lot. Watch the GSG videos and you'll have an easy time.
Bill is a great guy who cares about his students. Watch GSGs before every quiz.

not the worst but not the best
quizzes every 2 weeks in pollock instead of exams; not clear guidance on what each is on. busy work assignments but only open for short periods on canvas so theyre VERY easy to miss. lectures are so boring but iclicker questions for attendance w location. cumulative final but wasn't that bad. go to GSG for quiz help

Lectures can be a bit boring but a 3.9 rating is unfair he is a good professor who cares a lot and is a genuinely good guy. Lots of quizzes but study a bit and it will be fine. Could have finished with a better grade but that was my fault, not his or his classes fault.

Dr. Goffe is a very very good teacher so make sure to pay attention during lectures, he goes over concepts very well and he encourages students to ask questions. The biweekly quizzes are not easy for the most part but you can prepare for them by attending the GSG quiz reviews (these are extremely helpful).

Average experience. You get what you put into the class. He's extremely fair and respected for often awarding full credit for problems if majority of students got it wrong. Lectures are boring IMO and you have to attend 75% for full participation credit. Biweekly quizzes were annoying and difficultly definitely varied drastically. Final was easy

He was okay but I didn't like his grading scale, if you fail one quiz you're cooked and sometimes when you ask him questions it felt like he was talking down to you. The only thing that helped me were the GSGs so go to them pls.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Goffe is a great professor who cares about his class. He is a very statistical person and loves surveys. The class is not that hard, but stay on top of the biweekly quizzes because there are not many other assignments that boost your grade. Make sure to read the assigned articles and go over practice quizzes/learning goals to study for quizzes.

The only bad thing I can say about Goffe is that the 1.5 hour lectures were boring. His lectures were slow but very easily understandable. He also had no midterms which makes it nice replaced by 7 mini quizes which are easilyu manageable. Would reccomend.
The sweetest man ever. You can tell he really cares about his students and loves what he does. He is very understanding and tries to make the course as simple as possible.

Bill Goffe was kind and always willing to help when asked. While his lectures lacked energy and were a bit monotone, he taught the material well. The GSG sessions, however, were extremely beneficial for achieving a good grade

To be honest w u guys, he a good person, but the only thing wrong is the structure of this class, too many quizzes. Pretty stressful. And practice quizzes dont really help, I would say they help 50%. And you have to go to every class and write down every sentence he since any of those might be tested. However, Mr. Goffe read students comments a lot
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS WITH BILL GOFFE! He is very knowledgeable and passionate about macroeconomics. I am an engineering major and worried about econ, but the set up of this class is awesome (7 quizzes instead of big tests, homework for completion). Professor Goffe explains things so well with great examples and it is clear he cares about his students.

Lectures are worth going to, he adds important information not included in the slides. Not much outside homework other than some reading assignment and checkpoint homeworks. Quiz about every 2 weeks, lots of resources and guides for studying. Goffe is also super understanding and willing to make accommodations for missed assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Bill is a pretty good professor. He knows a lot about economics, is super nice, and wants everyone to succeed. Lectures can be boring but are important to attend if you want a good grade. Use the materials he gives (practice tests, textbook readings, etc.) and you should be fine.

Imagine watching Mr. Roger's neighborhood for 90 mins every other day. This is Econ 104 with Dr. Goffe.

Some people find it boring, dry, predictable, rudimentary, monotonous, etc.

Others will find it inspirational, helpful, insightful, and appreciate the guy's "wiseness" and obvious knowledge about the subject.

Which are you?

Bill Goffe really cares about his student's success. There are bi-weekly quizzes but if watch the GSG recordings they're easy. He is very understanding if you need to reschedule a quiz and helps you find a time that works best. I definitely recommend him.

Professor Goffe is overall a good professor. He explains the material clearly and uses examples to further help your understanding. The quizzes are relatively easy if you pay attention and attend the GSG sessions.
Truly a chill guy.
Just a chill guy

Professor Goffe is great - he really cares about students and makes the tough ECON material manageable. While the lectures can be dry, attending is key. The quizzes are better than midterms, and resources like GSG and Unstuck ai help a lot.

STRATEGIES- pasting slides into chatgpt for a better explanation, attending office hours if you have questions, doing the readings, maybe watching a YouTube video to better understand the concepts, and attending the GSG sessions. ATTEND THE GSG SESSIONS THEY ARE A LIFESAVER.

I initially had mixed views on this class as his teaching style didn't work for me; however, he is an amazing professor regardless. Strategies- pasting the slides into chatgpt for a deeper explanation, asking for help during office hours, watching YouTube videos on the concepts, and attending gsg sessions. Seriously, ATTEND THE GSG SESSIONS.

He is so nice and very accommodating to schedules and needs but sometimes his lectures can get very boring. The quizzes are also hard and a lot of application. get the textbook and packet bc he puts questions directly about the readings on the quizzes
He's just a really softspoken and chill guy

There are 7 quizzes, 20 questions; one gets dropped; if you don't want a mid-term, take him. Lectures are boring, confusing, and a lot of current events. Attendance is mandatory but can be worked around. Homework is easy, and everyone gets full credit. Not good at answering questions. Also a lot of resources. But overall, not that hard of a course.

10/10. He may be a bit monotone, but he seriously cares about his students! He is humble and always seeks out constructive criticism. He tailors his tests in a way that forces you to understand the material, rather than just memorize it, but he provides many materials so that you can succeed. Watch the GSGs and do the practice quizzes!

The class may seem difficult at the beginning, but as long as you complete the assignments given you will get so many extra points that help to boost your grade.  Bill Goffe truly cares about his students and works his best to make students be successful in the course.

Professor Goffe was constantly asking his students how he can improve his teaching styles and what he can do to help his students succeed. He genuinely cares about his students and is always looking to help them. Quizzes are every other week and aren't cumulative but there is no midterm, just a final exam.

Dude is boring, uses iclicker for attendance (geolocation), every person in class multitasks, and tests are broad. Just like the other guy said, uses 3 ipads on his arm and still can't make the class engaging. Voice is so annoying that I would rather listen to Stephen Hawking give a lecture for 1:15 minutes.

Dr. Goffe is probably one of the best lecturers at Penn State. Although a lot of students blame that there's lots of reading in this class, if you really dive into it, you can find that they are relevant to what you learned in the class, and you can have a better understanding of the class material.

I took Economics 104 in Spring 2024.  Dr. Goffe is a great professor, and really cares about his class.  He walks around to make sure everyone understands the material, and is very understanding.  The quizzes can be challenging, so make sure you study.  However, all of the studying and preparation material is clearly listed on his Canvas page!

I really liked Bill Goffe! For a class as big and tough as ECON can be, he really tried to help everyone find a way to succeed. I couldn't make it to every class, but as long as you find a way to get the notes and study the lectures, you will pass. I did not like the Pollock testing he gives, but overall he tries and that's all that matters.

I took this as a Gen Ed and it was quite fun. Dr. Goffe is very kind and very good at teaching a class. Instead of midterms, there are 7 quizzes, typically biweekly, some of them kinda suck, but as long as you study you will do fine in this class.

I loved Professor Goffe and plan to take a class with him again in the future. He really cares about his students and what he teaches. There are many resources you can use to study along with your notes. If you understand the topics, it is an easy class. Definitely take him if you can!

Bill Goffe is the Econ professor that you want. The lectures are sometimes long and boring, but you gotta suck it up. Go to the lectures because you will actually understand the concepts. 7 quizzes compared to tests IMO were so much better than having to take a midterm and the lowest one gets dropped. GSG reviews before each quiz help a lot.

Very caring and respectful professor. I ask questions every time after class and he answered my questions patiently and with relevant trending stories that helps me understand better. If you just want a good grade, just go to GSG session since they will break down and help you understand the concept, step by step.

Here's the only review you need:
Great guy & Genuinely cares. 7 Bi-weekly quizzes (69%), GSG's are all you need to do VERY well for them. HOWEVER: Quizzes DONT prepare you for a difficult Final (25%, it's still doable tho). He has Boring lectures, use GSG's too.
 
Other 104 Prof's will have Midterms, so figure out which you'd rather have.

Really kind man. His lectures are a little hard to sit through in all honesty, but his homework is graded on completion and drops a quiz. His quiz guidelines I felt reflected the quizzes pretty well (except for the 6th one). I would try to take him in the afternoon because 9am was not the move.

Nice professor but his classes are useless and boring. Just watch the GSG for the quizzes and you'll be fine. Look into other ECON professors before you take him. Weekly quizzes aren't as great as you think they are

Bill Goffe is the most caring professor I have ever had, he asks us if we want the lights adjusted, if we want a section in the auditorium for people who don't use computers so it can suit them better, and mentioned he hired a speech coach to help us hear him better. His lectures are clear and easy to follow, he elaborates and explains everything.

Probably one of the most respected profs at PSU. His lectures are clear and logical, drawing from real world examples to help you understand. If you have an interest in econ, you will enjoy this class. Tests are fair and accurate as long as you pay attention and take good notes. One of the most memorable classes I've taken in college.

We had a quiz on our fourth week and he still hasn't taught us anything. He uses 3 ipads on his arm and reminds me of iron man. His voice makes me want to sleep. Still haven't learned a single thing. Walmart Steve jobs.

Dr. Goffe clearly outlined what we studied and what the quizzes and final would be on.  He gave a lot of study materials including practice quizzes and was available in office hours to answer any questions we had.  Overall he did a great job teaching Econ.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof Goffe gave quizzes every week in which you would have to read pages of the online textbook to actually understand what is going on. His lectures are long and not really helpful when it comes to teaching material for the quizzes and final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: content itself isnt hard but its the way he phrases the questions on the quizzes that can be confusing. classes are dull and hard to stay awake at times but he truly cares. take detailed notes, attend GSG quiz reviews, get at least 75% of clicker points, write out learning goals, read articles, and do practice quizzes n you should be fine

Professor Goffe genuinely cares about his students success. His lectures are semi-repetitive which people are complaining about, but HELLO that is going to make you remember the content that will show up on the quizzes. Make sure to participate via clicker, but classes are recorded and posted. GSG sessions are EXTREMELY helpful. Super kind guy.

A very kind and caring professor. His lectures could be a bit long and dull, but you could tell he cared. He used real-life examples to apply concepts in class which I appreciated. There were seven quizzes spread throughout the semester (+ 1 final) which were nice to have instead of less large exams. Also, watch the GSG sessions for quiz studying!

Professor Goffe was a good professor. The class is structed in a way that you can come back from a bad grade to start the year and there is little homework which was nice. Grade is about 90% quizzes and the final.

Make sure to go to class to do the participate points. He is not a bad teacher, pretty average. He gives quizzes every two weeks. He also gives decent amount of extra credit. Make sure to do all the quiz reflections and go to the GSG (GUIDED STUDY SESSIONS) it is very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was awful. I always went to class but never understood what was going on. He speaks very softly and quickly making it so difficult to understand him. Quizzes are every two weeks and the wording is very tricky. You also never know what he will decide to put on the quiz and there is very little review or resources to do well in the course.

Teaches basically every lecture through iClicker questions. This course is nothing but filling as a business prereq, could've been summarized onto 4 pages of paper instead of wasting students' time. Explains everything 15 times over and is quite the drag. Stopped listening halfway through the semester. Nice guy, caring, but cannot ever hear him.

Dr Goffe gives you all the tools you need to succeed. The class itself is a little challenging but hes great. He's always willing to answer questions, he simplifies concepts without talking down to you, he provides outlines for all quizzes. He posts his lectures online and there are quizzes across the semester instead of a midterm. Love Dr Goffe!

Professor Goffe is a very nice person but the things he teaches just aren't exciting. He tries to relate the content to young students, but it can come across as boring. There are many ways to get credit but it's hard to remember when they're all due. Attend or watch the GSG sessions to help with the quizzes, which are usually every other week.

Professor Goffe is truly passionate about what he teaches but does not know how to keep a class engaged. His lectures are super boring. The class is made up for by the fact that most of it is simple material or easily learned in 5 minutes.
Absolutely horrible do not take this professor. Lectures are incredibly boring and impossible to sit through.
9ams with him were tough, but the man was fun to listen to, even when some parts of macro were so boring to learn. He cares, and I respect that as a student.

Goffe was frustrating to work with, not just because of his approach to teaching, but also because of his personality, ego, and conduct with students. He has a tendency to talk down to you, lecture students on their behavior or how they need to be better without practicing empathy or finding ways to speak kindly.
He cares a lot. Love him

Dr. Goffe is an amazing and caring professor. He does bi-weekly quizzes and no midterms, which were extremely helpful in preparing me for the final exam. If you go to class and take notes (also write down the clicker questions he shows in class) and attend the GSG sessions, you will be fine.

He's a great guy and very helpful, very passionate about what he's teaching and often experiments with different teaching methods. However, this class has been very confusing, he was trying new teaching methods, but it wasn't well organized, and he was having a rough semester. He's great when he's organized, like he was for 104, but 304 was tough.

Boring proffessor had to sit in the second row because he is a soft-spoken guy and I would get to distracted. Pollack testing center every other week which makes up 70% of your grade with small little quizzes. Plus a final. Don't take class unless you need it. Content itself is not too difficult if you have taken econ already.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the worst run and worst taught class in my college history thus far. Truly going to class was a waste of my time and I regret taking this class

One of the most challenging courses I've ever taken. Course material isn't even that difficult but he made it impossible, basically had to teach myself everything. Took 6 weeks to grade the first exam. The quizzes are all based on textbook we didn't even learn in class. Now about to take final cumulative exam, don't even know my grade in the class.

Bill Goffe is a nice guy who is passionate about economics, but he didn't lecture in this class. ALL OF the learning is done through individual reading. The team based idea was too much chaos for a lecture of 300, tests were weird and took forever to grade, no TA accessibility, and only grades are by weekly in class quizzes and 3 exams + final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sweet guy, but this class was rough. This semester was his first time teaching 304 and he tried doing a group structured class and ultimately failed. Not very clear expectations and very unorganized. He has the most boring lectures and multiple in class quizzes.

Look is this going to be the most fun and exciting class, no. But if you want a gruanted A, take this class. Yes it boring just put on headphones and listen to music during lecture. If you pay attention (like actually, not just online shopping) and study like 1hr MAX a week, you will get an A. Everyones complaning and IDK why. Hes broing but easy.

This class should not have been as difficult as it was. The lectures are long and boring. He repeats the same thing over and over again and yet that material never shows up on quizzes. The quizzes are next to impossible and will make or break your grade. Attend GSG sessions because those are the only things that can help you understand the material

Professor Goffe is a nice person & 104 wasn't too hard, however, exam grades are returned weeks after they have been taken & you're required to do a second stage quiz with the same questions as the first without correcting anything/learning anymore material- kind of pointless imo because you're probably just gonna get the same questions wrong.

New team-based learning method was rushed and unorganized. Didn't get exam grades back for entire month. No homework, all test-based. Lots of textbook reading to do. Lectures are boring. Includes trivial/dumb questions that are super specific on exams. You have no choice but to have him for 304, so good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a nice guy, the material is just hard. His lectures are long and his voice soothes you to sleep. He really does care and will reach out to you if you're struggling in the class, but the biweekly quizzes are very hard. No matter how hard I studied I couldn't get above a 75% on them. There were also a lot of trick questions.

he is a nice guy but his lectures are really boring and it is hard to follow along sometimes. there are quizzes every 2 weeks instead of midterms which is nice but they are difficult. GSG's saved my grade so I recommend attending the quiz reviews if you take this course. you have to spend a lot of time learning the material on your own

He's very dull, and staying concentrated in his lecture is hard because he frequently strays away from lecture topics each class. He's a nice person, I'm not going to lie, but his teaching style is so mind-numbing you're better off studying at home. Either way, this course is a weed-out class.

I love Professor Goffe. Great Guy. Sometimes the lectures can be kind of boring but whatever. There are 7 total quizzes in the class and then the final. The "quizzes" are basically short exams but if you listen to the lecture and take notes you should be just fine. I am someone who has horrible test anxiety but I have felt fine taking his quizzes.
Not a hard class as long as you take down notes. He connects materials to current issues and explains them well.

Was expecting better things with Bill. Really boring lecturer and his quizzes are very difficult. My friend and I spent 5+ hours on each quiz and we haven't seen the results we were expecting going into it. He gives broad topics to study and picks from the little details for each question. Not to mention the quizzes and final are worth 94% of grade
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures were pretty boring but Professor Goffe used iClicker to make you feel engaged. You get full participation if you show up and answer enough clicker questions and you get 100% on homework (graded on participation). The only thing that made this class difficult was the quizzes. They were too wordy and complex for an intro level class
Professor Goffe is amazing and a wonderful teacher. He is enthusiastic in what he teaches and believes in his students' success. 10/10

Honestly Mr. Goffe was pretty difficult, but he is a good guy. If you show up to lectures AND read the book and articles, you will be fine. His quizzes were pretty tough at times, but if you study and show up, you can get an A. In the beginning of the semester try to understand the basic concepts first (really understand them).

I played pokemon in this class, and was still able to get an A. It's not a hard class, just really boring at times because Prof. Goffe takes time to answer every question on GroupMe, so there are lulls in the class that get really repetitive. Studying for quizzes isn't hard, but the questions can be pretty different from the practice quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bill is a great teacher that cares about his students, even if it seems rough at first
Goffe is easy to fall asleep during but if you take good notes and attend GSGs then you should be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had a love hate relationship with Goffee. I honestly thought I was going to get a C in his class but managed to get a B. I thought he was going to be this amazing professor from what I heard from my friends, but they all took him when he had quizzes/exams online. If you want his real rate my professor rating, look up William Leo Goffee.

Goffe is a fantastic professor. His lectures are well organized and easy to follow and take notes on. Also, he keeps the class current by explaining how economic concepts connect to what we see in the economy. This class is fairly easy if you pay attention. There are lecture questions but they are small part of your grade and all lectures -> record

I loved having Dr. Groffe has my ECON 104 prof. It is very obvious that he is a very dedicated professor and deeply cares about the material he's teaching. If you miss a lecture, he uploads them to canvas so you don't have to stress about missing content. The lectures are extremely easy to follow and take notes on. 10/10 prof

Lectures are monotone and unproductive. Professor is obsessed with statistics and will spend a sizeable amount of the class saying things like "65% or the class rated this exam question as difficult" or collecting data from the class so he has more statistics for next year. Also he's extremely conceited about answering emails if he replies at all.

He tries his best to be engaging, but it is really hard to stay engaged when he talks to monotone. Considering it is a 100-level class, the exams are honestly a little difficult. It is a mix of open-ended and multiple choice, and the multiple choice can be tricky. Given it is a 100-level, I thought it was too much thinking. Use AP credit if you can
Despite being a difficult class Dr. Goffe makes it much easier to manage.

Professor Goffe is great. It is a information-heavy class, so you really need to pay attention and take good notes.  Quizzes have some difficult/unclear questions on them which I didn't like.  Professor is good at teaching the material, but it is pretty slow/boring.  I'm pretty sure that's just because its econ.
To be honest, Goffe is a best speaker, if you try to join the course, you will think it's very interesting. But the exam is hard, but he give you plenty of resources to review it. I enjoy his course
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mr. Goffe is very knowledgeable and can be a great presenter. This semester I dreaded going to his class in the back half of this semester because of the slow pace of his lectures and they get really repetitive. His quizzes can be very tricky as well. He does outline the quiz learning goals on his page and gives you plenty of resources, however.
Prof. is very boring during lectures

Professor Goffe's quizzes are definitely much harder than the material he presents, but they are manageable if you attend the GSG sessions (especially the ones right before the quiz) and take them seriously enough to study a little. He is a very interesting guy and his lectures are very relaxing and enjoyable compared to my other STEM classes.

You have to study if you want to do good on the quizzes, but there is multiple quizzes and homeworks to help you get your grade up. He is a super nice guy and is understanding. If you go to class and study, you will get a good grade in his class.
bill is ass
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had. There are a lot of in-class quizzes that count as a large part of the final grade, but many questions in the quizzes are not covered in the lecture and review material.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Explains material clearly.

Dr. Goffe's class consists primarily of long, boring lectures with biweekly quizzes that make up almost 70% of your grade. The quizzes are quite easy as long as you take good notes and read the assigned articles, but occasionally some questions can be poorly worded and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Goffe really cares about what he teaches, but most of your grade is made up of a few quizzes but you'll be fine as long as you take good notes and study.

His classes are 75 minutes long that are vey hard to sit through. You have quizzes every other week that barely contain any material you learned the past week. The questions are worded horribly and are somewhat difficult. The material learned in class is somewhat confusing. The biggest thing are the quizzes.

This man stinks. You have an in class quiz every other week and they are horribly worded. The questions make no sense. Also his voice makes me want to jump out a window. Impossible to sit through 75 minutes listening to this clown.

His quizzes are all in class and not open note. Despite having practice quizzes and group study sessions, much of the material in both isnt even beneficial for the quizzes. Quiz questions are often confusing and different from material you think to study. Quizzes are cumulative and the questions are broad, rather than applying what youve learned

The material he teaches in class is often glossed over and not on any of the tests/exams. He is nearly impossible to understand, not due to the difficulty of the course but rather his lack of seeming lack of interest in the subject and teaching as a whole. Most of the tests and exams are based entirely on material briefly talked about in the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes ate no open note. That was a covid thing. It is all in class close note quizzes. Many of his test questions are things he does not teach and that you have to teach yourself. Read the assigned articles all quizzes will have a question about them. Get ready to purchase them.
Bill was a good dude. Had some good dry humor and was very very helpful to anyone that asked

This guy is a legend. A little boring in class, but once you build a relationship with him, he is a kind and caring fellow. The grade is made up mostly of 7 open note quizzes which are bi-weekly. The quizzes are not too bad as long as you pay attention in class and review beforehand.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Make sure to be well prepared for the quizzes. Even though they are open notes, you definitely need to have a good understanding of the material to get a good grade on them. He was a great professor and made sure to fully explain all concepts.

JUST TAKE HIS SECTION. He cares about his student's learning. Would drop quiz questions if he thinks they're unfair based on Canvas discrimination index. The quiz questions will be VERY similar to the clicker questions so write those down. Also has practice quizzes posted and have a thorough explanation on why each answer is correct or incorrect.

Fully online course. You have a quiz every 2 weeks and just a final exam, which are all online and fairly easy. Lectures are a bit boring but do help you prepare for the quizzes and final. He also goes over each question the lecture after the quiz so if anything isn't clear he will help clear them up. Take him!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Quizzes were bi-weekly that were online and not too hard if you took notes. If the quizzes were in person I probably would have not done as well. Lectures were long and can get boring but are only twice a week.

Professor Goffe really wants his students to do well and understand the concepts. He gives many different options for preparing for quizzes. You will do well if you attend class, take thorough notes, and prepare for the quizzes using the practice quizzes and really looking through notes. Heavily conceptual so memorization is not the way to do well.
If you have the opportunity to take Goffe, please do. He is very caring and always willing to help. He always explains things in a way that makes sense.

Dr. Goffe is very nice and cares about his students deeply. He even gives out his personal phone number in case of emergency to all his students. He does not use exams and has small quizzes every other week as the main source of grades along with one cumulative final at the end of the year.

Was a really good and interesting lecture.  Stayed connected through email and groupme the entire time and always tries to answer questions.  Notes are very good and every quiz was online open note.  Did a quiz every two weeks instead of midterms and definitely worked better.

Open note/book quizzes online every other week. Could organize his powerpoints and topics a bit better. Attendance counts but you can attend online via livestream. Sometimes he has trouble understanding what you're asking. Quizzes are difficult and very application based. Hard for a 100 level class, but not impossible by any means.
love mr. goffe but his class was sort of hard - def had to do a ton of studying if i wanted to do well, doing alright was easy

I think the power points were hard to follow and take notes on, I think there are much better ways to present this information that would help the students understand the material better.  The lectures were long and boring but you must pay attention and learn from them since the class is lecture heavy.

Nice guy, just sometimes hard to hear because he doesn't speak loudly. The class is pretty straight forward, show up and take good notes and you will be fine. Exams are open notes and the grading criteria for the class is very straight forward.

Professor Goffe is hands down the best professor at Penn State. You can tell he really cares about his students and he has a true passion for teaching. Lectures aren't mandatory but you won't learn much if you skip. I loved the class and I cannot say enough good things about Goffe. Highly recommend - he's always willing to help!

Professor Goffe was great. The class was super easy and as long as you pay attention and write down what he says .There's online, open note quizzes every other week instead of midterms which was nice, and the final was online, open note as well. He really cares about his students. His lectures do get a tad slow boring, though.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: theres a quiz every other week so it's tiring, but manageable. Go to the TA's sessions (at least the review ones right before quizzes) and pay attention in class and you should be fine. He doesn't care about grades, & we had quizzes sometimes with 60% averages. I had an A all semester and finished with an 89 and he refused to round so study a lot!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Probably one of the best professors for ECON 104

Professor Goffe is a caring and helpful professor. There was lots of resources provided to help prepare for quizes including practice quizes with answer explanations. Professor Goffe is very patent with students and will curve questions that have a bad discrimination index. Overall I would highly recommend professor Goffe.

Class is beyond boring and hard to stay awake during. Even after going to class, the every-other-week quizzes are quite the challenge. Completely operated like a 100 level course - lots of homework, wants you to actually learn, graded on participation, etc. If you like econ, you make like this class. If not, you're out of luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: super nice guy. lectures are long and pretty boring. quizzes can be difficult if you don't study well or if you miss any class. he's very adaptable and willing to change things if you talk to him. really cares for the students. not a super easy course (i mean, it's an econ course it's not intended to be easy).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures are dragged out for being 75 minutes long, could fit it into a 20-30 minute lecture. He's very dry/boring and doesn't really go off-topic from the material, but cares a lot about his students and teaching the material and will help you whenever you need.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Goffe is by far one of my favorite professors! He is the sweetest man you'll ever meet, and always open to help his students. Attend his lectures - you'll learn the most and ask questions. He is super nice and always will help if you stay after and clear up any confusion you may have!
Really reasonable teacher. You can tell her wants the best for his students. I would really recommend taking his class.
