He tells really funny jokesstories and keeps the class very interesting and high-energy. Exams can be tough, but not surprising.
He is my favorite teacher at Penn State so far!!! no joke!! very articulate and hilarious!!!

Handzy is easily the best prof I've had at Penn State.  Entertaining so he is able to keep your attention during an otherwise boring class.  If you go to call I had no problem getting an A.  Incredibly helpful an great at explaining all concepts.  HW isn't bad either, only due once a week
He has really bad jokes but he makes math really easy to understand and the jokes are so bad you just have to laugh. He also learns everyones names which is different for classes like those.

Handzy is the man. Keeps the class engaged pretty much all the time regardless of the material. Not necessarily an easy class but if you have him you'll be a lot better off than people in other sections. Easy to talk to and would definitely recommend getting one of his sections if you can

He has really bad jokes which are kind of funny once you get used to them. The lectures are not boring and pretty straight forward. The material is not hard if you have taken Math 140 and Math 141 but the exams are not easy. There are two exams and the final. For me it was the best mandatory class I have taken so far.
Nice guy. Always there to help. Homework can be tough because he sometimes gives problems not covered in class.

This guy, probably the best math teacher there is at PSU. Explains things in huge amounts of clarifing detail, and hes wicked entertaining too so its easy to pay attention. Spoiler alert likes to talk about the walking dead and will ruin it for you.
Very clear lectures, does many examples in class, assigns a fair amount of homework. Quizzes are always on what was discussed in class. Overall a great teacher and highly recommended.

Nestor Handzy is a true gangster. In all honesty, the only person in the math department who is not completely arrogant. Great sense of humor, which definitely helped get through a subject as dry as differential equations. Actually made me WANT to go to class. Made everything so incredibly easy to understand. For the love of God, TAKE HIS CLASS!
BEST TEACHER AT PENNSTATE

This guy is the man!!! Very clear lectures, homework usually take along time. Short quizzes everyday, piece of cake. If you do all the homeworks, quizzes, this class is a breeze. Take this professor if you ca, I guarantee you will love math, and should get an easy passing grade. But, hes too slow with grading, and seems unorganized most of the time

By far one of the best math professors I've had. Even after all of his jokes and shark drawings, you somehow understand all of the material and have a blast doing it. If you have a question, he'll not only give an answer but the reasoning behind it. No math is easy, but this legen (wait for it) dary man makes it a good time.

Handzy is so awesome!!!!!!!!!!!!! You will actually never be sorry for taking him. He would also teach you how to draw very near sharks. I feel like my differential equations and drawing skills have progressed in this class ;) love you Nestor!

You will learn Differential Equations in this class, not just how to solve problems. He knows how to keep the class awake and guide it. His quizzes sometimes can get tough. WARNING : HIS JOKES WILL MAKE YOU CRY!!!
Handz down best teacher I've ever had.

By far the best math professor I've ever had. His quirky sense of humor can break up even the most boring topics. I will surely miss his teaching when I move on to other mass courses. My only complaint is that you are only given 5 minutes to take a quiz, which is sometimes not quite enough to feel comfortable.
The class is bearable, even likeable, with Dr. Handzy as the professor. He's funny, he communicates well, and he knows his stuff.

Seriously the BEST math teacher I've ever had. Hands down. He has a quirky sense of humor and everyone loves it. The class is well structured and follows the syllabus religiously. He not only knows the math, but he Knows The Math. He loves drawing pictures which are extremely helpful in understanding the material. THE BEST! Major: Computer Science.
He is very entertaining, knowledgable and helpful. Keep up with homework and ask questions in class or office hours.

IMO Dr. Handzy is the best math instructor at Penn State. He is very knowledgeable in the subject matter yet he can convey it on a level that is understandable. He also is very helpful during his office hours if you don't completely grasp something in class.
Excellent professor. Extremely clear explanations, and he makes the class interesting and funny. The exams are hard, but if you go to class you can learn everything you need to know.
Best teacher I've had at Penn State, taught me math 220 material better than my 220 teacher, and I was taking Math 250.

Great teacher. He knew the material very well and taught it with ease. Definitely show up for class. The sample exams are very helpful to doing well on the midterm and final. You should be able to get most of the points on homework/quizzes, and if you do fairly well on the exams, you'll get a good grade. I got an A with a decent amount of effort.

Like everyone said, he's the best math prof at PSU.  Knows the subject perfectly and super clear in his lectures.  And this is especially important in 250 because the textbook is worthless.  On top of that, he's a genuinely entertaining person, so even though  I didn't like the subject much, I still enjoyed my time in class.

Differential equations might just be the most advanced math i had to take, higher level operations than calc 3 and matricies, but handzy teaches everything so clearly that if you pay attention to him in class it is the easiest math class ive taken, and believe me im not very good at comprehending, so if i could keep up and understand him so can you

best math professor at penn stae.  somehow goes slow enough so everyone in the class can keep up but fast enough to cover all the material with more than enough examples.  cares about his students, speaks english, but doesn't like chalk.  he's pretty funny so you wont fall asleep, and he's made a chalk joke at every class.
Best math teacher I have ever had.  Office Hours are extremely useful.
Best math professor at Penn state, he cares about his students and is always available for office hours. The most clear on concepts and computation I've seen.

The best math professor I have had at Penn State. He knows the topic extremely well and is more than likely to help you learn it too. He is down-to-earth and a funny guy. Definitely go to his lectures and take his notes because they are 100x easier to follow than the textbook. The homework can be challenging because of the way the book was written.

Handzy is a great professor, he's funny and a good guy. his quizzes are pretty easy so they can help your grade. you definitely have to study for the tests but if you go to class and do the homeworks you'll be fine. class wont be any easier with anyone else so i would take this class with him

Such a good teacher! Really clear lectures. I never read the text book and only had to study an hour for the tests. Got high A's on every exam and it was my favorite class so far at penn state because of how easy and interesting he made it

Professor Handzy is a really great guy. He makes terrible math jokes that make you laugh on the inside. He really cares about his students and makes a lot of efforts to make sure you understand the material. I would recommend him to any and every student that enjoys math. This guy really is the real deal.

He's an awesome teacher!! He definitely knows the material and, unlike every other Math250 teacher, he actually speaks ENGLISH!! He made the material as easy as he could, but its definitely still a very challenging class.... DO HOMEWORKS AND STUDY FOR QUIZES, THEY WILL SAVE YOUR GRADE

It's really boring and you have to keep writing his blackboard notes until your hand get paralyzed :((( Also, VERY TOUGH. However, He's always ready to help you. if you attend the class, study and focus on that, you will be fine.

Nestor is a good professor, it just stinks that the math classes here at Penn State are so hard. He will try his hardest to make sure you get all of the 100 quiz and homework points, but it's up to you on the tests. Read ahead in the chapters, and do a lot of the practice tests before the exam.

A good professor, but hard course but you can't blame him for the exams because he didn't make them...(So study hard!) He seems to care about his students doing well and his 1st language is English, which I hear is rare for Math140 professors, and he's kind of funny (in a way that you laugh at the pathetic-ness of his jokes rather than the joke).

Great teacher but tests are REALLLLLLLY HARD!!! HE DOES NOT REVIEW ANYTHING ON THE TESTS ITS ALL FOR YOURSELF. Everything he teaches in class seems to be really easy, until you have to do the textbook homework where his notes DO NOT HELP WHATSOEVER!!!!! If you are good at calculus this might be an okay class for you

I take her Japanese 110. It's not very helpful. Many of her assignments were just about reciting textbook examples, which does not improve my Japanese linguistic skills. The most disappointing part was that when she called on me to answer questions, she often seemed to be impatient for waiting me to finish answering if I struggled.

I attend her Japanese 110. Her teaching isn't very supportive. Many assignments were just about reciting textbook contents, which had almost nothing to do with natural conversation skills. The most disappointing part was that when she called on me to answer questions, she seemed very impatient to wait for me to finish the answer if I struggled.

If you watch anime and you are familier with Japanese,(or you are Chinese or korean) i highly recommend this class.
the professor is very kind, and the class is interesting. 
if you do well in the preperation, you can easily pass this class.
Be careful every moment. If you don't, points will be taken away from you forever. I always wonder, even local Japanese in this class will be taken points off.

JAPNS1 should be very easy. But Iwami makes everything hard. Just let us talk about daily performance: Common satuation you just need to show up on time and you get full points(4/4). But here, in Iwami's class, you only have 3.5/4 except you doing very very well. Homeworks and tests are same. Frist week, 92% grade, from a student who good at JP

Iwami-sensei was a very solid teacher for japanese. She cares about your success; she asked to meet with me in the middle of the semester because my grade/performance was slipping and I didn't even realize, and she set me back on the right track from then on. If you put in the work outside of class, keeping up is very doable.
took japns2 this summer. She is sometimes a tough grader but kind & knowledgeable. Will take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: If you want to seriously learn Japanese, professor Iwami is great. The class is like trial by fire but in the end you actually learn a lot. Shes not malicious but she does expect you to speak coherently in every class. Its a crazy amount of hw but without it, you probably wouldnt learn the language. Shes a sweet woman and she means well.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Would not recommend taking this class with this specific professor. Moves entirely too quick and majority of it is you learning by yourself with the textbook then she quizzes you by randomly calling on people. Performance is the biggest part of your grade but she expects Intro learners to be fluent. No matter how hard you study, shell take points.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I recommend not to take this course unless you speak fine Japanese.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is the best Japanese professor I' ve ever met in Penn State. ALERT!!! She is a tough grader but if you prepared well you'll definitely be okay. Her class is interesting. If you wanna be good at Japanese, take her class. You won't regret it!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Iwami-sensei's class is a lot of fun, but she is very strict and can be a pretty tough grader. However, she is really helpful and will always try to help you out if you are confused. Despite all the people complaining about their participation grade with her, I actually did better on that front with her than any other Japanese prof I had.

You really need to prepare a lot before attending the class, she wants everyone in the class to understand she is talking about, however, she is really tough tough tough grader, she considers you know everything. And you have to answer her question rn, or you will not get the full participation grades. Six exams, one oral exam, there is no final.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Iwami is a strict professor but her class is not hard to take. If you did homework and preview every time before the class you can get full credit on the quiz and test. Good Luck.

Don't take this professor's class. I always couldn't get full credit in her class even I work really really hard. I like and want to learn Japanese but after I took her class I want to quit because even I work so hard I still couldn't get higher grade and she needs students be a prefect speaking and writing in Japan. So I do not recommend to take.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Worst teacher in my life ! Very Very STRICT, you dont get full credit even though you do well until you did perfectly perfect. And she also asks weird questions like guess the name of the person in the picture and if you answer wrongly you will lose points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Iwami sensei is an inspiration as she is very strict but also very smart and works hard to push you to do your best and help you learn the language. At this point if your in 401 you should be working to become fluent and that is exactly what her course helps you to do. It is very hard and there is a ton of work but it is rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Iwami is a fantastic Japanese teacher. She will constantly engage you during class, and limits English speaking to a minimum to give you good listening and speaking comprehension. This class is NOT, however, an easy A. Take this class if you want to learn Japanese, not get a GPA boost.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Iwami was my first teacher for Japanese, and while she was very strict, she was just what one looks for in a language teacher. She will push you unobtrusively to do your work, helping you to learn the language. This is NOT the language to take if your major requires it and you aren't interested in actually learning it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Professor Iwami is indeed strict and you have to pay attention to the class every time.

Fairly speaking, I can tell that she loves teaching. She is informative and supportive in and out of class. And one thing that coming students might care about is her attitude, and here's my good news: SHE HAS CHANGED A LOT. She is NOT as strict as she were in the past! Her exam's hard because, dude, you are in an upper level class!
It's just like taking test everyday...you have to be perfect all the time.

This class is so hard. She grades your performance in every class from points 1 to 4. Basically you have to study Japanese all on your own and be tested in class. She expects you to speak Japanese fluently in class. You will probably get a 2 out of 4 for your performance if you can't answer her questions fluently in Japanese.OMG its an intro class!

All of the Japanese professors want to challenge you and push you to do the best that you can. If you go along with it and prepare well and do everything you can to succeed, you will. Iwami-sensee is no different. She is very nice and helpful but tough as well. She makes classes fun and informative. You just have to try hard and do all the work.

Haruko Iwami is an extremely challenging teacher. She seems to have trouble realizing that she is teaching an intro class. There were 24 kids to begin and it dropped to 17 by the time the mid term was returned. If you put all of your effort into this class and no others, you will be able to get an A.
Very interesting class and great professor, keeps things interesting
Omg I actually cannot understand this guy. I stopped going to class because of his accent

FIN 305W is easy. This is simply the kind of class where its going to be easy to succeed for evry1 if you study. Iliev, however, doesnt explain these topics well at all. He'll just give you the basic math. With him, youll figure out the math to solve each problem but you wont learn the financial technicals cause he has a basic understanding himself

Peter is a great professor. He tries his best to make content as understandable as possible. If you attend class and do the homework you should be fine on his exams. I feel if I tried a little harder I could've gotten that A

Professor might mean well, but low quality teaching method. Expects you to understand the background of topics from get-go, moves fast, super brief. PowerPoints are not useful, math disorganized, hard to follow along his written notes when individually reviewing. Exam questions are confusing even if you pay attention in class.

Professor Iliev is a great professor. He has a lot of dry humor, keeping the class interesting. He is extremely knowledgeable and helpful. Practice exams are very similar to exams; with effort you can do very well in his class. Weekly homework's and 3 exams.

Although Prof. Ilieve seems tough, he's very fair. He grades based on weight (lowest grades weigh less, highest grades weigh more) and gives a project where he basically gave everyone over a 90. You'll definitely have to put a lot of work in but he's there to help. Go to review sessions and office hours!

I would not take this professor. Hard to understand and moves too fast through his lectures. He is a nice guy but not a great teacher. He gave us three online quizzes that weren't bad. The written project was not well explained (he gave everyone above 80%). The exams are similar to practice questions in class but more difficult and confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Love Professor Iliev. I let out at least 2 nose harsh nose exhales from his jokes each class. He gives you all the materials to succeed and if you study at all you will get an A

Professor Iliev, in my opinion, is one of the best professors at Penn State. He is extremely funny and makes the course content very interesting and relatable. Quizzes are easy, tests are pretty hard, final project is easy. The trick to exams is to do practice problems from textbook as well as from his course packet. Highly advise taking.

Peter is the man. Highly recommend for 305. Easy class, but don't take it lightly. Keys to an A are to do all of the practice problems on canvas and in the notes, and read the main points in the book and notes. He allows cheat sheets too. Tests are mainly problems and some concept questions.
Really awesome professor. Nothing bad to say about him. He really wants his students to succeed.

Not going to write a lot about Professor Iliev. I will say that Peter is one of the best professors I have had at Penn State and was one of the many students that was looking forward to going to class.
One of the best professors I've had. Gives extra credit and exams are short answer so he gives lots of partial credit. Really wants his students to succeed. Very nice and funny guy.

Peter is a legend. He's always cracking jokes in class and making the material interesting. Tests are challenging but fair. He also gives tons of extra credit with clicker points and final grade curving. He'll also give you test questions on angel to help prepare. Pretty impossible to not pass this class.

Peter is the man. Offers incredibly easy extra credit. Won't give a grade lower than a B unless you really deserve it. Doing the sample exam questions are a must and you'll do great on the exams. Also, basically a review of Finance 301.

Peter is a funny and nice guy. He provides ample opportunities and example/practice problems (that will be extremely similar to test questions) in class that count towards participation credit. He provides sample questions for each chapter covered and sample exams from previous years. You get what you put in; he provides all you need to do well.
Pretty funny and obviously smart. For two of the three exams I walked out thinking I had done very well only to find out later that I had not. Can be kind of tricky. Extra credit helps though.

Peter is a great guy, and teaches a fairly easy course. I would highly recommend taking his class as he is very reasonable and kind, and he has a great sense of humor. He is more than willing to help in office hours, and does whatever he can to help students prepare for exams. Great guy, not a terribly difficult class. Take Peter!

pretty good teacher..u have 4 assignments which he gives everyone 100..thats 20% of grade.then 3 exams. 20, 20, and 40 percent.can use a cheat sheet on exams b/c theyre a lot of equations. most people get an A or B. hes funny and sounds like borat..
Wow, worst I ever took

I found this course to be frustrating. Her teaching style was awful, and instructions were often unclear, and assignment feedback lacked the detail needed to understand how to improve. I also noticed that she was occasionally late to class but still penalized students for arriving late,which felt a bit unfair. We don't need her at Kean's University

The Professor barely projects her voice and you can't hear her. The grading is harsh even on your first assignment when you are unsure of the expectations first starting off. The class is also not engaging at all or interesting despite the topics being very interesting. I wish there was more engaging material than just papers and papers.
Instructions for assignments were usually pretty vague and would usually lead to a lot of unnecessary confusion.

Professor Iouri is a funny good professor who actually cares about students and personally improved my confidence in math.Although you might lose track of content because 251 is simply a challenging class, he has review sessions in class where past problems are similar to actual exam problems. Quiz scores can be changed to 10s if you do corrections
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: His lectures were not helpful at all. It was difficult to grasp the concept in class, which caused me to do poorly on exams. A lot of your studying has to be done outside of class, and make sure you get help from others earlier on! He is very respectful, and all of his quizzes are ONLINE!! Which is a huge plus, but homework is long and takes hours.

This class is easy as long as you attend and understand the pre-req, the take home quizzes weren't hard and he lets you correct them if you had mistakes, you also have a week to do each quiz. He'll tell you that the class is hard in the beginning of the semester but it is easier than that.  Prof soukhov is very knowledgable and tells funny jokes.

I like Iouri Soukhov's way of allowing us to complete quiz corrections. He teaches class by writing down content from the notes and differential equations textbook. I find certain parts of his lecture difficult to understand, but he cares about you to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Soukhov is a great professor for the honors class.  He is very smart but makes sure he is going at a pace that students in the class can follow.  His office hours are helpful and you can go over homework and quiz questions with him.  Definitely would recommend taking this class with him.

Professor Souhkov was my first math professor at Penn State and I must say I thoroughly enjoyed the experience. His accent is not detrimental to the class and if you're paying attention you will be fine. Grading was very laid back, HW was essentially completion, and there were quiz corrections. Don't take it too seriously and it'll be QED.

Iouri's lectures are insanely fast and difficult to follow, but he cares a lot about his students' success. Homeworks are extremely tedious but usually graded for completion. Quizzes are very difficult but take-home, and the lowest 1-2 get dropped. There's only 2 exams and a final, so get help ASAP. Highly recommend LionTutors for this course.
Great professor.

Prof S is a really cool lecturer. It's kind of up to you to figure out your own step by step problem solving guide sometimes but always manageable. Sometimes he does integration techniques really weird but other than that it's a smooth class that covers some cool content.

Exams make up a large portion of your grade, so plan accordingly. Prof is an interesting old man and talks to each student about their grades. Quizzes and HWs can get long and tough, so working in groups helps. Ask questions during the lecture as soon as you have them, because he will plow ahead otherwise. Amazing person, challenging class.

Dr. Soukhov cared about his students and did his best to help us do well. His lectures were fast-paced, sometimes confusing, but he always answered questions to try and clarify. His material for the honors class went beyond what was necessary for exams, which made tests seem pretty easy. His take-home quizzes were hard, but graded fairly easily.

He's a very nice guy who seems to truly care about his students' success. However, his lectures are complicated and go lightning fast, often times I left the class not understanding anything, though I think I was along in that. In my experience, even asking questions isn't that helpful. Very easy to get a high grade though.

Iouri cares about all of his students and usually learns everyone's name and helps give inspiration for tests and your overall grade. Online quizzes were very hard but he drops your lowest. He flies by on the lectures too, so avoid if you want to go at a slower pace. Gets insight from the dept. for exams too, which is nice.

Iouri is overall a good professor for MATH 251 and knows his stuff. If you don't understand something though, be persistent in asking questions since he's not the best with directly answering questions. The quizzes are pretty tough but if you can do them by yourself, you are good for the test. Also, do the sample exams as they parallel the tests.

Soukhov was a great 251 professor, he taught using a lot of examples and always asked for questions. Lots of memorization for tests (department decided) and he gets insider info to share with you on them, he also does reviews. Most quizzes are take home and he offers remediation for 1 extra point, if you go over hw w/him he gives credit back.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He means well but just isn't good at teaching material to students. He just starts writing examples and doesn't  say what the topic is called so that adds to the confusion. Each prof makes their own quizzes and his took HOURS, they were take home but nothing like the exams or even other classes' quizzes. Better have a good group to study with.

Just showing you some pdf. and teaching you some basic calculus instead of the new materials in Math 251. Rarely response to the emails asking for some questions. And the answer for homework changing all the time. And he made us retake the exam since he put the exam answer before we took the exam. Thanks Iouri. Choose Iouri making your life harder.

Iouri is great at math. So good that he doesn't understand the topics that students will struggle with and blows through them, while spending too much time on other topics, because it is all easy to Iouri. He's a good guy and means well, but he does not teach effectively and the lectures have so much unnecessary material. Must teach self to pass.

Just writes his notes on the board and when you ask questions he just says "because I decided to do it that way" without really explaining the theory behind it or why he solves the problems the way he does. Uses too many abbreviations and doesn't explain what they mean, just expects you to know. Also teaches way to hard and not to the test. Avoid.

Professor Soukhov is very nice with surprising sense of humor. He's very helpful if you ask him. His teaching may not seem fancy at first, but later at homework or tests I realize he really teaches the essential clearly. He also plans at least 2-3 review classes for each test, in which he modifies old tests into harder problems to better prepare us

Many people complain about Iouri, but he is not a bad professor at all. You just need to pay attention during his lectures, and participate during class. The exams are not too difficult, however, be prepared for some tricks from the math dept(as usual). My advice is to ask many questions during class, and to do a lot of the practice exams online.

He is a probably one of the worst professors I had to take a course from. Yes Math 251 is hard by itself, but this guy makes it even harder. Lectures I practically worthless, you won't understand what he is trying to teach because there is no order. If you want to pass go to liontutors, you won't "self teach" yourself through using the book.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Iouri is one of the nicest guys, but he is literally the worst math teacher I have ever had in my life. If you have to take MATH 251, do yourself a favor and switch into Tseng's class because whenever Iouri couldn't answer a question, he said "Look at Tseng's notes." Definitely bombed that final yesterday. Thanks Iouri.

Iouri is such a nice guy and means really well with his attitude towards his students. But his teach ability is not there and the homeworks are on things that were learned 2 weeks ago and dont help to reinforce the learning, theyre just very large and take up a lot of time.

Iouri is the type of professor to get annoyed when asked questions, call on you when you don't know the answer, put you on the spot, discuss your grades in front of the rest of the class. Can occasionally be funny or compassionate, but his lectures were all over the place. LionTutors was WAY more helpful, wouldn't have passed without tutoring.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: His accent makes it hard to understand and follow along with what he is trying to convey. He's a nice guy and can be helpful during office hours, but do not expect the class time to be super helpful unless you can follow along with what he is saying. I found going to LionTutors far more helpful and conducive to my learning .

Iouri (your-e) is Russian and has a small accent but nothing to worry about. He will repeat words many times as he writes them probably a speech problem. He also always breaks chalk in class. He is super helpful during office hours and his quines are take home. HW is about every week or so and usually not that hard. Use GroupMe with the whole class

I have never had a professor be so disrespectful. It was not a good experience overall, especially waiting for him to grade your working knowing he would find something wrong no matter how hard you worked on it. In emails and public responses he talks down on you if he disagrees or thinks you did not do enough.

***not a PoliSci major***

If you're not interested in the topic, don't bother because it will be obvious, and you won't do as well. Great class, interesting topics, very creative assignments. Grading rubric is very clear so your grade is really on you. Some of the reading can be a hard slog but still def worth it. Great class, cool professor.

Do not take this class if you hate learning.  I had no idea how valuable this class would be but I am so grateful I took it. Winham is brilliant and the assignments are so interesting and clever. He is very engaging in discussion posts, too. Super cool class!

Prof Winham is just extremely disrespectful when he doesn't agree with your take on a political thinker. He will delete your discussion posts if he doesn't like them and grades papers really hard. He gave me a 66 on a paper because I 'didn't quote Marx enough' - it was a 3 page paper and I quoted him twice and some other source materials as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Well-organized and good flowing lessons. The grading criteria is very obvious in the rubric. Some quiz questions are a little vague. The readings are extremely terse but they're pretty fundamental and necessary for the material. Took as an elective and enjoyed it. First professor I've seen actually contribute to discussion posts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Within the first week I dropped his class due to the first interaction I had with him. His response to my introduction came off as extremely sarcastic and rude.

Perhaps as others on here has said, Prof. Winham's courses are those you should only take if you are a political science major. I took this course as an integrative studies requirement and was genuinely interested in the content. 3 weeks in and I have never wanted to participate in a discussion less than the ones he aggressively jumped into.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Do not take this as a freshman. The teacher is rude, the test answers are subjective to his opinion. I had to argue my point in some of the tests to get more points. I have to take this class AGAIN with the same professor to graduate, A's and B's in all my other classes. Reading heavy class with little to no feedback.

took his web-based class, bought the textbook, and immediately understood this is a PHD level class at the very least. The textbook is not possible to comprehend if your vocabulary isn't that of a genius.

Worst professor I have ever had. This course was much more difficult than any 400 level I'd taken and I did not take anything away from the experience. If you ask him for feedback, he will be rude and does not give useful feedback. Avoid this professor at all costs.

Summer class was taken to fulfill the requirements of a gen-ed and for my plsc major (double major). Prof was not helpful at all. Lots of reading but quizzes were difficult because I felt like things could have been intercepted differently based on one's viewpoints. Be prepared for zero feedback and short responses. Lowest PLSC grade yet.

Quick preface: I DON'T recommend taking this class if you are not a political science major. That being said, I didn't have any issues with this professor being rude or being a tough grader on discussions. If you read his standards for discussion posts and you do the readings, you shouldn't have any problems. Be prepared for a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Prof. Winham is okay, but he has a very hard expectation for discussions. You better have good quotes, good structure in your discussion to get a good grade. His quizzes are very hard, so study up. He has at least six books for us to read, and always, read! Otherwise, he is kinda rude, when I asked him how the discussions/ reply system worked.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Grading is extremely difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Awful individual. Opinionated and gives zero feedback. Terrible.

I just finished this class. It was difficult and there was a ton of reading involved. If you are ready for that then you might enjoy it. There was too much social justice stuff and not enough actual political teaching. It's too bad, there is a lot of very interesting material to learn. felt it was overshadowed by peripheral rabbit hole material

I really enjoyed this class. A lot of people complained that he was too tough, but if you do the discussions like you know what youre talking about and read the syllabus to see what hes expecting, then youll do great in the class. Also, Prof. Winham helped me quickly every time I needed it and was and was never rude like the other reviews say.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This prof has an expectation that everyone in this class has experience with political analysis, its an intro course!! Dont bother engaging if you are unhappy with a grade, he will tell you it is your unexamined beliefs that are the problem, not his teaching. He should be serving burgers at Wendys, not teaching intro students. Hes a clown!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Prof Winham is passionate about engaging with students, but positive reinforcement is not in his playbook. He is a socratic professor who is very harsh, especially with grading. The course is also needlessly difficult, filled with high-level theory and tough exams with no mercy. As a PoliSci senior, this is my lowest grade yet. Not an intro class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is simply a very difficult intro course. Part due to the heady material and amount of reading, particularly conceptually difficult ideas, and partly the professors approach to the Socratic method. His attempt to be a gadfly often reads like highly critical commentary. Also, his personal political leanings are quite obvious...
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: intro level class with *extremely* dense reading material- mostly high level theory. wouldn't recommend unless you're dedicated to polisci and in at least your sophomore year. not impossible to pass, but get ready for tough grading/lots of ultra-specific open response questions/brusque (sometimes almost rude) responses from the prof.

Do not take this class with this Professor. His attitude towards students is negative. He's rude and belittles students. You literally can do nothing right in this class or live up to his expectations. Don't expect full marks on ANYTHING despite following all the instructions. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS, if you don't have to.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dont even try to engage this prof with your ideas, he doesnt care. He has obvious political leanings and is given to fringe and biased rhetoric. This is little more than a Marxism class disguised as an ideology course. I had multiple class wide emails discussing this profs harsh and demeaning tone. Should not be a teacher

Econ as a general is not that hard of a class, however professor Sean makes is intresting and fun. In order to get full participation, you will have to show up to a majority of the classes, however he will do fun little demonstration and he makes his notes really east to take. Just write down everything he writes down and read before exam.

Started off the class fine, but slowly got more and more strange. He would scream at people for talking when it was near dead silent in the class room. He taught the material well but his exams were very weird. You could completely understand a concept but still get a question wrong because of the wording of the question.

Made the material pretty easy to understand and was always available to answer questions if needed. Tests are very manageable if you study. Participation is graded on answering questions correctly in class, but even if you get every question wrong you will still have enough points as long as you go to all of the classes
The tests were hard and covered a lot of material. The final average was very low.
Went to class everyday, studied for hours, wasn't enough, avoid.
As far as Econ professors go, he's pretty good at explaining it and makes the lectures interesting. Go to class, take notes, pay attention, and you will do fine.
Good professor, but the exams were decently difficult and with the exception of participation and homework, exam grades essentially made up the entire final grade.
Don't think he was as bad as his rep is. Lectures were boring and confusing at times, but figured it out. Not too bad overall
Very odd guy. Teaches for the people that understand and are as passionate as him. Rambles
Loves to call out kids and the exams were really tough
Very interesting lectures and explains topics very well. If you study and take notes should be a easy A.

His lectures are just note taking from the smartboard, but he explains everything very well. Lots of information to cover throughout the course, but the exams aren't too hard. If you study you will get an A, and if you don't you won't get below a B if you go to class. Study for the final, it is a lot harder than the normal exams.

Pretty cool guy. He explains concepts well and shows plenty of examples for every topic. However, he does not provide notes outside of class, and participation is graded up until you hit a certain threshold (which is near the 2/3 mark of the semester).

participation is easy and only requires showing up to half of the classes, but they are mostly worth going to, homework is easy, don't buy the textbook, get the course pack tests are 80% similar to the practice tests in the course pack, do them every time.
Class participation has credits, so show up to lectures. Try scoring well in mids as it matters a lot.

No notes available outside of class, so even though attendance (outside of participation points) isnt required, it is still important for attaining a good grade. The practice tests are often very similar to actual exams, however the final exam had no comprehensive review besides the one the GSG leader provides. Final exam was much harder than avg.

As a student new to econ, the GSG sessions are the only reason I passed the class. Sean is so smart to the point where he doesn't realize he has to over explain it for the students. He will point you out in class if he sees or hears you whisper to someone. There are just better econ teachers for this course.

Though Professor Inoue's lectures are dull, he does provide homework assignments, which you can redo till the end of the semester, and bonus/extra credit opportunities. He would provide old and older exams for his students to practice, and the actual exam is pretty identical to the old ones. I would say his final exam was a bit difficult.

Good professor just a tough course if you don't try. If you spend 15 minutes really teaching yourself the material after each class you will be fine on the exams. You just need to have good study habits.

Just finished this professor's class. It was frustrating overall. Exams felt intentionally tricky, with confusing questions instead of clearly testing what we learned. Lectures weren't very helpful, and there were no study guides or clear direction on how to prepare, the class was more stressful than necessary. Take it with a different professor.

The amount of hate is honestly totally unjustified; Prof Inoue is an incredibly dedicated man who is willing to help you no matter what. He is truly passionate about economics and as long as you put even a LITTLE work into the course, you will do well, believe me. In case you have any more trouble, GO TO THE GSGs, trust me, you will thank me.

He's a good teacher and I would take his class again. He explains things well and gives lots of optional practice tests and practice assignments. The homework isn't a heavy load. He writes his own lecture notes which I personally preferred, since it's more engaging than a fill in the blank power point.

The reviews are v harsh and he's highkey a v brilliant man. He's def harder, but study (GSGS clutch up big time), go to lectures (his hand writing is truly bad I'll say), & do the HW (unlimited attempts & no late points). He's forgiving w TPS and HW points. Exams are 1,800 points tho. lol. But you'll see. not a bad guy. don't talk in class tho....

Inoue's test are difficult if you don't study enough for them, but that's any Econ class. There is a good amount of grade inflation from homework's which you can unlimited attempts and from think-pair-share points which there are lots of opportunities. If you go to class and take good notes and study a good amount you should do fine in this class.

guys he's not that bad u guys scared me so bad for no reason. just pay attention and take notes and make sure u actually prepare well for ur exams because ur grade is basically determined ONLY by ur exam grades. but like he's not that bad. also don't have conversations loudly in his class if u don't want him to publicly humiliate u.

Proffesor Inoue actually tries to do some fun activites to make lectures more intresting. He also gives you till the final to do all your hw for full points, which you can redo as many times as you want till than. However I agree that his handwriting is bad. Just show up to class and take notes, its an easy A.

You have to purchase your grade in addition to the tuition you already pay. Move your eyes 1 cm to the right, and he'll pull you from the middle row just to watch you (Diddy). You watch the professor (basically a confused toddler) struggle to write statements on the board. I'd rather watch paint dry. At least the paint knows what it's doing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm not an econ major, had to take this class to fulfill a credit (MechE). Class isn't as easy, takes serious effort and time. Exams are weighted super heavily so they basically determine everything. He takes lectures really seriously, never posts notes, and will call people out for not paying attention even though it's a 300 person hall.

Sean is a great guy but his handwriting is kinda bad. I would only go to class for the attendance, after completing your attendance grade then I would honestly self study that's what worked for me if that's how you like to study I would do that.
Easy to follow lectures, can do homework literally whenever you want with infinite attempts, good guy. Show up to class and take notes and you get an A.

Not the friendliest guy and all classes are fully lectures and note taking. Large class size and he moves fast through content. Content is relatively easy but I had to reteach myself most of it outside of class for full understanding. Put the work in outside of class you will get a good grade. Use practice tests they are exactly like the exams.

HE IS AN AMAZING PROFESSOR. Anyone who disagrees is just mad they didn't get the grade they wanted. If you are considering majoring in econ, taking 102 with him is a MUST. I am going to admit that his class is quite advanced for 102 and he goes into 300's level concepts sometimes, but this ended up being great preparation for econ 302.

Chill dude, if you took any economics in high school before than he is a fine option. If u didn't than take a different professor. Go to class and the gsg. Look over the old exams on canvas they are identical to the test, but you still need to study. Don't talk during class he will move you or ask you to leave, same goes for during the test.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Not bad but not great either. Very mediocre but a good guy, must attend lectures and exams are not too hard. Overall not bad but if you can find a better professor you should

Honestly, Inoue is a pretty chill professor. He is really lecture-heavy, but he keeps them pretty interesting . He does have a weird way of grading, though. He uses Econ Bucks; you buy your grade at the end of the year with money you've accumulated from attendance, homework, and exams. Other than that, he's a solid professor.

Sean is a really nice guy who is passionate about econ, but is the hardest of the 102 profs. The material is not very difficult, but lectures are just not great due to the ~300 person size. HW is super helpful and exams are near identical to the prior ones posted. Def go to the TA exam reviews, as they were my primary method of studying and great.

Inoue gives passionate lectures and gives a lot of content every lecture. Note taking is a must in his class because he DOES NOT post his notes on Canvas. In class participation counts as your attendance, and you only need to keep going until you have the "max points." (< you will learn about this in the class, Inoue has a special way of grading).

Prof. Inoue is an interesting individual but comes across as passive-aggressive and condescending. He is honestly quite bad at explaining even the most basic of concepts. Here is how I've gotten an A on the first two exams: I look at the two practice exams he posts for every exam and I solve the problems and check my work with ChatGPT. That's it.
Such a good teacher and the exams aren't that hard. He will call you out if you talk in class and can be rude but its really funny when it happens to other people
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The professor knows the content well but I lowkey learned more by doing the homework than listening in class. Inoue is quirky and disrespectful to students at times over nothing. Honestly for Econ 102 the professor doesn't matter because the content is incredibly easy, to study for tests just do the old exams on Canvas and use AI to check answers.

Professor Inoue is an amazing ECON 102 professor. I like the way he does notes in class because it is very beneficial if you write down notes on a notepad. Attendance is done via Think-Pair-Share. Do all the homework and attend the GSGs. You'll be prepared for any exam if you use the resources given to you.

An amazing professor who wants to help everyone as much as he can. He provides multiple examples for everything, and if you attend the GSGs, complete the practice tests, and finish your homework, the class is very easy. He can be passive aggressive, but it's when people deserve it and it's honestly hilarious.

Take a different econ 102 professor he is the hardest of them all. Very long lectures and there's basically no grades other than the exams (attendance). If you have him go to GSG they are the only thing that will help. He also has an exam on Halloween if you take it in the fall.

The econ department here has all the profs make their own exams so if you buy his book thing from the bookstore (its like $7), you'll be set. He also only requires a certain amount of attendance so knock it out early as possible, because it'll take down your grade if you don't do it in time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you use your resources it is a guaranteed good grade. GO TO THE GSG. I CAN NOT STRESS THIS ENOUGH. THEY WILL PREPARE YOU FOR 95% OF THE TEST QUESTIONS. Use his practice tests, use the old ones he posts. Find people that have had his old practice tests in the past and look at those.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Fun to listen to. Attendance is taken by daily questions in class that you write down on paper with the people around you and then write your names on the paper. I don't like Econ but he made it pretty easy to understand (especially with the examples he gives), you will do pass if you try at least a little. Clearly enjoys teaching and is helpful.

Dropped this course cause it's basically an extension of 304, but 304 is not a prereq, so it's hard to take it concurrently. He's a nice guy and I believe he cares, but he just needs some improvements in teaching. His answers to students' questions are dodgy. Often overcomplicate concepts. Handwriting sucks and class notes won't be posted.

Inoue is probably my favorite teacher I've ever had. All the material was super interesting, and he made class fun with interesting examples. It's obvious that Inoue has a true passion for teaching and the material. It's also easy to get a good grade, just go to class, do the participation questions, and pay attention; its not hard material

Very nice, funny professor. Very knowledgeable but can be a little strict on grading and how the class acts during lecture. Understood majority of the content, however there is very little to aid you in studying for exams.

Put in the work and study for a few days and you will do just fine on exams b/c you'll actually know the material. Idk why everyone hates on him so much. Everything is pretty straight forward, just take notes. Study old exams in Canvas. Don't save homework til the end, do them as he assigns them. Attend GSGs or watch them online they're so helpful!
the dynamic of his class is actually a game, makes things way more difficult than they need to be, never seen a professor like inoue before, watch gsg
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I think Inoue has unfair rankings from students who expect this to be an easy class. Put in the work outside of class, study for more than a day before the exam, attend class and GSG and you will literally do fine. Test 2 was the most difficult. Homeworks are hard but do them before the last possible day. Gives a lot of examples in class.

Take a different 300 Level Econ Class. Was not a fan of Sean teaching style he explains something once and expects you to know it. Also, no review or practice exam for tests. The tests are normally 5 question open response and its either you know it or don't.  Would not take this class again or a class with him.

Sean is such a nice guy and a good professor! However the exams are definetly difficult and even with 4 hours of studying I still struggle to get a C or B on the exams. Definetly watch the GSG exam review videos!

better than other econ profs
doesn't sell you overpriced homework softwares

Sean is frankly the boy. I see a lot of haters on here and idk why. His class is quite straight forward imo and you can max out your attendance grade while still missing half the classes. He's a good dude. If you're complaining about his handwriting you probably just weren't paying attention, I never had an issue taking notes.

Taking this class right now and it is extremely difficult. Exams have a ton of lecture material and information pulled from all over the place. Definitely avoid this class and if anybody who has taken it in the past and has any insights while I currently take it please help!
made my semester miserable. if you are taking this because you're required to and aren't good at math/economics, AVOID HIM AT ALL COSTS

The most confusing grading scale I've ever had, you have to "purchase" your grade. Also, unless you calculate your grade yourself with his weird grade calculator, you won't know your overall grade until the end of the semester. I broke my wrist, and the guy still made me take the exam because my excuse "was not valid"?
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good teacher, but bad with tests. Moreover, his grading criteria is unclear and feels very arbitrary. The papers are not given back and you won't be able to see what you did wrong, so it's not a good course when you're trying to improve yourself. Is also monotonous. Only plus side is he tries to care for his students.

Inoue is not the best Econ prof at Penn State. He has more tests than Dave Brown (3 vs Dave's 2, while Dave has an online final and Sean has an in person final). Get ready to be moved around in exams - even if you move your eyes an inch to the right (you are expected to look only up and down), he will make you change seats.
he should not be teaching in lectures, nor should he be teaching using his handwriting it is god awful

Nice guy and can tell he loves econ, but lectures are so boring and I fell asleep multiple times but luckily the content was not difficult at all. Wish he would post lecture notes but he refuses. Kind of difficult to get an A but not impossible, just need to prepare well for the exams. Overall his teaching style is just straight lecturing.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: he gets unnecessarily hated on, hes a good guy and he knows what he talks about. #justiceforinoue

Notes are not on canvas so attendance is "mandatory" so keep up with the lectures, don't fall behind and you will be fine. I found the later exams more difficult but still doable. Sean is okay at best, he teaches the material and there is a small percentage for in class participation which you can easily get full points for. Homework is mostly easy
handwriting is trash, material is easy, tests r interesting.

Tough to say. A good portion of the grade is easy to achieve just through participation, however Inoue sneaks in many trick questions on exams to try to mess you up. His lectures are good, however he tends to go on tangents. The exams were taken in the Forum which isn't ideal. I would avoid him for ECON 102, I have heard other professors are better

econ itself is hard, and I think inoue didn't explain as simply as he could've sometimes, but overall if you study and go to the GSG review sessions, you'll do well. he is also super nice and tries his best to make class fun!

Great guy, he genuinely cares about his students understanding the concepts while simultaneously managing a 200+ person class. YOU MUST go to lecture to expect a good grade. No published notes, if you miss a class, you must get notes from another student. Lots of opportunity to practice questions with online resources and previous exams

His notes were not accessible outside of class, and his handwriting was terrible. Also test questions were based on what he believed, and the test curves were awful, a couple of questions wrong and you move down to C or D. The GSG were much better than going to class, although it best to go the class because he gives these participation points.

Anyone who complains about Inoue's ECON 102 simply didn't go to lecture or study. If you take good notes, come to the majority of the classes, and utilize the GSG sessions, you should get an A. His tests are very application-based, so knowing definitions aren't enough for a good grade. First two tests are easy, third was bad, final was easy!

Econ is not an easy subject, so naturally the class is pretty difficult. Participation points are 15% of the overall grade which is clutch and can be maxed out shortly after the first exam. If you go to class, pay attention, and do minimal studying you will be able to get by. The gsg's are clutch and easily the best resource for studying.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I definitely do not recommend him for Econ 102. I ended up late dropping the class because I seriously struggled to stay attentive and understand the material with the every class being strictly lectures.

Dr. Inoue shifted my perspective on economics from a field I had little interest in, to a class which I enjoyed being a part of. The material itself is really easy to the point that with minimal studying you should be able to get a B or higher.

The professor does a good job of managing such a large class. Every class, we had think-pair-shares, where he would write a question on the board, and we would discuss it with our neighbors and submit an answer afterwards. He's very enthusiastic about economics and gives everyone a chance to participate in class activities.

Pretty regular class. Attendance and homework are easy to full credit for if you show up like half the time and spend the time doing the homework. The rest of the grade comes from exams which can be tricky. As everyone else mentioned his handwriting is super messy and lectures can be boring. Just go to GSG and you'll be fine in the class.

Probably one of the most useless classes I've taken here. Exam questions are super niche to his beliefs so you have to memorize what he "thinks" is correct. If you don't have good note-taking, you're screwed because the topics are so subjective. Prof cannot write if his life depended on it and notes aren't published. Fr the worst part of my day.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: :ectures are boring and npt as helpful as the gsgs,the gsgs are the best.  If you go to class and watch the gsgs you will definitely get at least a B.The final was harder than the other tests and brough my average down a little but the 3 other exams are easy.The homework is not helpful
The exam this guy writes is so hard you would think the riddler from batman would've wrote it. He speaks in riddles in lecture and wont curve grades. Would not recommend to a nearby solar system

Overall the class itself wasn't too hard. Lectures can be information heavy and fast-paced. The exams were easy. As long as you do the practice exams and listen to the GSG recordings you'll be fine. He'll literally put similar, if not the same, questions from the practice exams onto the real exams.

Great professor who liked to get students involved in discussions. Was definitely a more difficult course, but going to the GSG sessions was the biggest lifesaver and was the main reason I passed the class. You need to attend class because he does not post lecture slides. Reviewing old exams and practice problems before exams was super helpful.
Very strict about test dates and doesn't put up with mistakes you make. Not understanding in the slightest.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Terrible professor. The final was an IQ test not a Economics test

Professor Inoue knows is very knowledgable and is accessible outside of class. He is quite comical with his animated voice during lectures. I took notes all semester, yet mainly looked over the practice exams before exams and did fine.

He was fine. People who are complaining are just bad at economics. His notes this semester have changed and have gotten better from previous semesters. I do not think he is the problem; his lectures are engaging and interesting. However, going to the GSGs was a lifesaver, and I did very well in this class. Homeworks kind of sucks, but all online.

Doesn't take attendance, but you should still go to class. He gives out daily questions for a grade, and it's the only way to get notes. His tests are really hard, but the GSG sessions are super helpful. As long as you go to class and GSG, it's pretty easy to get a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance is not taken, but you are graded on in-class daily questions, so it's important to go to most lectures. Tests are somewhat difficult, but the GSGs are very helpful. Overall, the class is a bit harder than other economics professors who teach the same class. You also cannot see your grade until the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very very very lecture heavy. You will succeed if you go to GSG sessions and do practice tests. Homework's can all be re done for full credit. Attendance isn't taken, but there is a certain amount of participation questions you do each class to max out the grade. Tests are short but you have to study to do well. People who hates him are dramatic.

Professor Inoue is VERY lecture heavy. His course is manageable if you take notes, or have friends that will help you when you miss, but otherwise is super fine. No attendance taken, but you need to do enough questions for participation in class to get the attendance grade to be a 100%. Homework is fine too, he is really silly and I like his class.
GOATED professor

I actually loved Sean and thought he was a great professor. You NEED to go to class to get whats going on but if you show up the material is very clear. He gives you everything you need to do well on the exams, people just don't use it. The only things you need to do are go to class and look at the course book practice. No textbook needed.

Literally a terrible professor. I sit in his classes and have no idea whats going on. His homework is about a ton of things he doesn't cover in his hour long lectures. I don't look either way while crossing the street when Im walking to his class because I hope to get hit by a car. Rather do that than sit in a his class. Do not take this class bruh

Honestly, Dr. Inoue is a great professor, but the exam can be sometimes confusing. Take the final as an example, it has several questions that include the content he didn't cover in the lecture at all. So, his Econ 102 can't be a super easy class. If you do want to learn something, you can take it.
These comments are absolutely hilarious and a treat. Came here for course recs and stayed for the tr@ll humor. Thanks DB.
Go with david brown

This class was mostly comprised of lectures written on paper that were not posted online, so attendance is mandatory. Sometimes the homework does not line up with the lectures, but the answers are in the textbook or can be looked up, as you have infinite attempts on homework problems. The exams were easy if you did the homework and went to reviews.

Looks like the same tr@ll as Wooten's page is posting on here now.
Learned a lot about economics concepts with Sean. It can get dry but does his best to introduce examples. GSG sessions are extremely helpful. Would like extra office hours each month to better understand hws.

Never post any note on Canvas, you must go to class in person or you are going to miss the note. And never have a study guide or practice exam for ALL exams. There's no rubric for the group project and the presentation is not the most important part. His handwriting is horrible. Don't take his class, the worst professor I've ever met at PSU.

This guy doesn't teach content regarding what is on the actual exams, he speaks in pure concepts and doesn't show you what to do for exams. His handwriting is very difficult to read, he speaks and goes over content at way too fast of a pace. Go to the GSG sessions because they will make you understand it. Prepare for armpit stains as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sean is a great professor teaching a tough course. Attendance isn't enforced and participation points can be maxed out without attending all the lectures, but going to class and taking notes is important if you want to get a good grade. All the homework is due at the end of the semester but definitely do it as it's assigned, because there's a lot.

I absolutely loved Sean. He was such a great and insightful professor. His lectures were very well paced and he uploaded video lectures to Canvas. His exams were pretty difficult and involved some chemistry and some calculus, but he is a very generous when curving exams. The only downsides are frequent pop quizzes and a few group projects.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Beware of pop quizzes--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: If you have ever talked to Inoue in person he is such a nice guy. If you don't understand something go to office hours or watch the GSG, Collin is amazing! He posts practice exams on canvas and about 4 questions from the practice exam show up WORD FOR WORD on the actual exam. To succeed in this class you need to study your notes and attend GSG.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cannot wright on a piece of paper to save his life. Tests are just straight up not fair. EVEN THE GSG PEOPLE AGREE!

Say what you will but he really isn't a terrible prof. It's lecture/notes heavy and the tests are based on the notes so it's important you attend class. His notes helped me review and the GSG's helped me understand the concepts, they go hand-in-hand and I don't think people realize that so they complain ab the class. Study and you'll be fine!

His lectures will cover the exam, however, it can be very hard to study with lecture notes as you do not have anything to cross reference your notes with after the lecture is given due to him not posting lecture content. My recommendations are to do every Pearson activity thoroughly while taking notes and then watch GSG recordings. Exam 2 is rough.
The main issue with this class is the exams.

I wouldn't take 102 with him if I could go back. His tests are tricky and not at all like the practice exams. Homework piles up and doesn't help with the exams at all. He fully locks grades until the last day so nobody knows how they're doing in the class. The only thing getting me through is the GSG. Colin is the best. Love you Colin, you're a G!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor inoue moved very quickly through lectures and I don't recommend taking him if you have never taken any econ course before. If you have taken econ before, you should be ok

I usually don't think this website is a good measure of a professor, but this class is awful. He changes terms on the test to be a different name than in the lectures, can't read his handwriting, and the way he teaches some concepts is confusing. I have a relatively good grade in the class, and it's still one of the worst courses I've taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I honestly liked this class, I dont know why people dont like his class, Attendance isn't mandatory but he doesn't post notes on canvas so its best if you attend and everything you take in class is on the exam, he gives a quick classwork for participation and you get some points even if you answer incorrectly, he's incredibly kind, not a hard class

Genuinely the worst professor here at PSU. AVOID. AVOID. AVOID taking econ 102 with him if you can. Attendance is basically mandatory because he only writes out notes in his scribbly childlike handwriting and NEVER posts them online. He teaches incredibly fast. TA taught better. He also has horrid underarm sweat stains and only talks with his hands
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sean Inoue's handwriting is hard to read. The exams are not too hard if you study, but he does not curve the midterms. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives out participation points and the exams are only based on the notes he gives in lectures. I would not recommend him for Econ 102. The GSG sessions were much more helpful than attending class.

Everyone complaining about this class being difficult: 1.) didn't go to class, 2.) looked up the homework answers even though they are great practice for the exams, or 3.) did not go to the guided study review sessions. If you do all of these things and study independently, there is no reason this class should be difficult.

I would rather eat my poo and get intentional carpet burn than take that dudes class again. Bro is so boring and you can see his pit stains a mile away, it looks like a puddle underneath his arms. He jumps into a material faster than children at a Skyzone birthday party. His exams are alright i guess but overall he's doo doo with grading.
a lot the tests answers come from the old exams he provides you with so use those to study for the exam. If you do all of the homework and go to class, you should get a good grade
Do not take this professor whatever you do
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Attendance is not required but very much so recommended, as you will receive participation credit and the lectures are very informative. As long as you pay attention in class and complete your homework you should do good. Tests are short and worth a lot, but the content is covered well in class and an A is definitely achievable on each exam.

He is a very nice guy who definitely cares about what he is teaching. He makes the concepts very easy to understand. You get a free 30% by just going to class and getting done the homework which is nice. The tests aren't awful but they have so few questions that even if you get 3 wrong your score drops a ton.

He is a great teacher he explains concepts like you would to a child which is helpful in understanding. However, it is very homework heavy but you have the entire semester to do them and still get full credit. The tests only have 15 questions so getting even a few questions wrong will bring your grade down. Class participation gives you credit too.

He's a super nice guy, the tests are not too difficult but they're low in points so even if you get three questions wrong thats already down a letter grade. If you go to class you will get participation points. I would advise taking him, hes a chill guy but just make you understand the material.

What a king, he is so amazing. Go to lectures because every day in class you can earn points that go toward your final grade. The exams determine your grade, they're tough because they're heavily weighted and don't have a lot of questions.
Course is very heavily involved with game theory

literally do not take this class trust me. average on all the exams was a 65-75 and he refused to curve. genuinely the worst professor at psu. does not teach form the textbook, one unit half the unit was on health care? if you did well in micro in high school you wont do well in this class even if you go to it everyday.

This class was very organized and not hard at all.The exams are a little tough only because he grades them out of 1800 points and they aren't that many questions. Attendance isn't madetory but you have to go to class in order to not get behind on notes. Sean is such a great and nice professor I highly recommend taking it with him.

Cool professor, challenging class if you don't grasp the concept of econ. Attendance is not mandatory as long as you have your attendance points but you won't understand the homework/tests. He gives you the whole semester to do the homeworks. I found his tests to be hard because of how short they were so make you study because class average is low
You are essentially given 30% for showing up, so you can preform subpar on the tests and final and still pass/ receive a good grade.

He writes down notes and you copy them the whole class. Attendance is not manadorty but you have to go to at least half the classes to get all the TPS participation points. He makes econ concepts very easy to understand but lectures can tend to be boring and drag on. I would take this class again.
Online class is not recommended. Classmates are hidden.  Help is not available.

Seems like a decent person, but cannot explain anything at all. Homework is NOTHING like what she talks about in class, and her exams are insanely difficult. DO NOT take this with her if you have the choice, and you'll be better for it i promise you.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Kim is one of the most caring professors at Penn State. If you attend every lecture, you should have no problem in the class. Be sure to do well on the first two exams, as the material gets markedly more difficult after exam two. Spend a significant amount of time on the homework if you want to fully understand the class.

Wonderful professor. If you want a good grade, show up to every lecture and legitimately try on the homework. Engage with the lecture, and she will do everything within her power to give you the grade you deserve. The material after exam two is difficult, but she does her best to make it manageable. 100% would take again.
She's so nice and tried her best to get you though the class
Do better...

The course is structured fine, but the prof assigns problems like we're stats PhDs. Go with 414 or 401 instead. HW takes ~5 hrs/week. Attendance is “rewarded” with pop quizzes for extra credit—aka free points for whoever shows up. They somehow always happen when you miss class. Total trap. Exams are overtly difficult with the averages being ~ 60%.

Dr. Kim is phenomenal. I knew nothing about stats before taking this class, but if you go to lecture and listen, you will be golden. The homework is pretty easy, the midterms are completely fair, and she does give a few extra credit points throughout the semester for attending lectures/pop quizzes (they don't affect your grade if you do poorly).
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Kim is one of the most caring and helpful professors that I've had at Penn State. She always wants her students to do well and is very willing to help. She even had a snack for us at the final exam, which was very sweet of her. Would definitely recommend Dr. Kim.

This class is an easy A, but requires way too much work for a 2 credit course. Should be 3 credits. 2 'projects' due per week, each take 2-3 hours. Can easily be solved using examples in book. Lectures were optional, with 5% EC available if you attend all lectures. Midterm was brutal, final project was easy. Just be prepared to have a decent amt HW
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice professor, however it seemed like this was the first time teaching the course. A few times we were put into groups for team work but it wasn't enough for everyone to get to know each other so we barely did any work during these times anyway. I probably wouldn't take her class again but if I had to I wouldn't be upset.

As someone with no prior programming experience, this class was tough but doable. The lectures were easy to follow, and she was always willing to help if I had questions. That being said, the homework problems would often be far harder to do. However, if you take the time to figure it out, you will be all set for the midterm and final project.

Professor does not show any examples in class that even remotely match the complexity of the homework. If you have no prior coding experience, you will essentially have to get a tutor or find answers to the homework online. I believe that a "beginner" class should be passable for complete coding beginners, but that couldn't be further from truth.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: STAT 414 is definitely a hard course. However, Dr. Kim is a perfect instructor for it. She gives good feedback and detailed explanation with real life examples and analogies during lectures. She cares her students a lot.
