The lectures are interesting and she makes sure everyone is engaged in them. She is great and I am going to take her other classes because she is really one of my favorites!

If you like lots of busy work this is the class for you. I have never had an ELECTIVE with this much work and time required. Don't take this class as you will regret it. Weekly quizzes, discussions, and sometimes documents to complete. The professor is nice, but needs to realize not everyone is a HDFS major.

LOVE Professor KTP. She is so knowledgable and passionate about the course material, and I learned so much from her. She genuinely cares about her students and makes the class enjoyable even though the subject matter is often difficult to discuss. I highly recommend taking her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great prof and this is a great class! Class attendance is considered into your grade so technically isn't mandatory. She is very knowledgeable and keeps lecture interesting. I didn't get the book which I regret but I still am solid in the class. Highly recommend this course, but beware some of the content is sad.
She is very nice and can be very generous. She is very understanding and kind, only strict when it comes to exams. You need the textbook for class.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The sweetest professor! Genuinely cares about students. There are 6 pop quizzes but other then that all slides are posted online. 2 exams that are fairly easy as long as you read the information. A term paper at the end that also isn't that bad. Discussion posts each week. You actually learn in class without stressing the whole semester.

She is the best professor I've had so far. She is super sweet and really wants you to do well while also learning a lot. The exams are really straight forward if you go off the powerpoints. There's 6 random quizzes but she drops one or two so you don't have to go to every class. There's a term paper but it is not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Does random pop quizzes at end of class so need to be there. Some exam material is from the textbook. Super nice and interesting. No laptops allowed, need to write all the notes. Uses powerpoints and will post them after class on canvas. There are canvas discussions and need to post on it every week. Highly recommend her.

Super nice professor. Class is interesting on child maltreatment. Not a lot of rigorous assignments. No big paper. There are random quizzes and 3 exams. Need to post on the discussion board every week for credit. The last exam is cumulative given during finals week.

Dr. Briggs is a good professor. He makes outlines really clear and the course easier to understand. He is a slow grader and very picky and will take off points for small formatting mistakes. Overall he is funny and genuinely cares about teaching, but the grading can be frustrating at times. Worth it if you stay on all details and follow directions.

Overall, he was a great teacher, full of energy, and really wanted you to do well in English 15. He was a slower grader, but it didnt effect the timeline of the class at all. Lots of energy and rambles occasionally, but he makes it fun, and it makes you want to come to class every day.

Incredibly tough and slow grader. Takes forever to grade assignments and gives unclear feedback. Also weirdly energetic at 7:55am to the point of mental exhaustion. If you have him later than 8am the class is very easy but at the crack of dawn it's tough to say the least
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He grades assignments REALLY slowly and tough. Something that was frustrating: he would say my writing was well written and then my grade for the assignment would be a C+ and that confused me and then when i went to office hours to ask he told me again that my writing was good and that a C+ was good as well so idk but hes a really nice person

I really enjoyed takin Dr. Briggs class. He does talk a lot and loves to ramble on but he is very nice and wants to see us do well. English isn't my strong suit and I feel he does grade on the harder side but overall I liked his class.

Although at first it seems like he just keeps talking and will never stop, he actually has great advice to give regarding our work and is very passionate. He does tend to ramble all period but he has a corny sense of humor and tries his best to relate to his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I cannot say enough good things about Maurizio. Definitely one of the best and most caring professors I have ever had. He wants all his students to succeed and is overall just an amazing guy. SO funny too!
Is an awesome guy in general and a funny teacher. Make sure to go to lecture though where you get most of your class info from.
He's a really great professor, super funny, and I enjoyed being in his class a ton. Classes are two lectures a week and a discussion on Friday. Highly recommend taking his classes.

Awesome guy. He was super caring and wanted all students to succeed. Class itself just basic Western Civ history. Only grades are the weekly quizzes based on the textbook readings, participation, and the midterm/final. Very generous grader and reaches out regarding your progress. Would definitely recommend taking his class he's the goat.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Very down to earth & easy to approach, clearly passionate about what he teaches! Good amount of reading each week, but its pretty manageable. Besides exams only graded on quick weekly canvas quizzes and some (mostly) group presentations (those were very easy & he grades leniently). Exams weren't too hard, & essay portions were open note.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: hes just a chill guy

Dr. Murdock is a very nice and funny guy. I found this class really interesting! The only issue was that it was almost impossible to get an A on the quizzes. I attended every class, did all of the readings, and studied. It's graded on very few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE! He does not care about students doing well and even made an effort to say that in his lecture. His quizzes (50% of your grade) have NOTHING to do with his content, and his slides contradict his point constantly. I could go on and on, but honestly, I would get banned.

Professor murdock is a really good guy and u can tell he cares abt his students. He incorperates interesting stories into his lectures (they're often really funny or actually applicable to what we are learning). the downside is that there aren't many assignments and they're not worth a lot of points so if you do mid on them you will get a mid grade
No direction in course content. Conflicting information in notes compared to quiz answers. Doesn't reason with students, what he says goes. Would say much more but would probably get banned.

Kyle is a great guy, but there are limited assignments that make up your grade and the TA grades very harshly. There is always something you did wrong that wasn't on the rubric. He does not post slides, and it is unclear what exactly you're supposed to be writing down for notes.  This class is seemingly easy, until it's not. I struggle to keep a C

He's a nice guy but class was way to hard and much work. take this class with ANYONE else!!! No tech is allowed and he doesn't post anything on canvas, so you have to have hand written notes and can't miss class.  We had almost 2 quizzes every week. Almost everyone in my class would average C on every assignment, they were so hard for no reason.

the worst class i have taken at penn state! the assignments are all memorizing info with basically no guidelines. TA grades hard and doesnt match the rubric. prof doesnt post anything on canvas so your handwritten notes need to be perfect. only 3 types of assignments so if u mess up 1 thing ur done for. average on every assignment is C or D
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: TAKE THIS CLASS WITH ANOTHER PROFESSOR! Genuinely the worst class, there are only quizzes, in class written assignments (essays without notes), and reading comprehensions. The TA is the harshest grader and will not give a 100%. No matter the amount of studying and memorization of notes I do, I am still barley holding onto a B. Thumbs down!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS. We basically have either a quiz, a reading comprehension quiz, or in class writing ever single week. Thats all your grade is made of no outside of class assignments. His TA grades everything and takes points off for stuff outside of the rubric. nice guy but the structure of his class sucks and he does not seem to care.

Worst class ever. He changed how he did this class, and it is now extremely hard. You take notes by hand, and every assignment is done in class with zero notes allowed. His TA grades WAY too harsh, and will never give you 100%, despite following the rubric. Zero resources to study with besides your notes. Extremely unpredictable assignments. 0/10
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I heard from some students that since FALL 25 Murdock had to make his class a bit more difficult since too many people before this semester were getting As.Notes are now hand written quizzes are now closed book & are alot of info & different topics. the average was around 75 after the first quiz.He is a GREAT prof but class itself has become harder

lectures are enjoyable and engaging when you're there. He doesn't post lecture slides or recordings, so class attendance is basically required. The TA who graded our papers focused way too harshly on grammar, almost to the point of ignoring content. I've never had even my English teachers grade that hard.

Definitely take this class with Professor Murdock!! Great professor, and the class itself is structured very well. If you go to class, you'll get good grades on the exams (they are taken on Canvas and open notes). He also makes class super fun and enjoyable, usually everyone shows up despite attendance not being mandatory.

Dr. Murdock is an amazing professor. I have so many great things I could say. All we had were tests on Canvas that we took at home, reading guides (but you only need to do 8/17), and a final paper. You have to do a good bit of note taking and I would definitely recommend making a friend in the class if you miss notes.

Kyle is absolutely fantastic! His lectures are hilarious, and he does a Kahoot at the beginning of each class to review from the previous lecture. These questions are typically on the quizzes (no exams) which are all open note! He does not post his slides, so if you don't know anybody in the class SHOW UP! The quizzes are directly from the slides.

Kyle was one of the best professors I have had at Penn State. He genuinely cares about his students and is a really down to earth guy. The topics are interesting and there is 5 case studies where the topics are given for 4 of them and they are very interesting. Online quizzes are not bad as long as you go to class and take notes. Loved him.

Great professor. You learn about very interesting topics, and he makes the lectures easy to understand. If you take good notes in this class it is not difficult to get a good grade. I can tell he wants his students to succeed.
No exams, some readings, a few short essays, and one long one at the end. Overall, it was an easy class. Quizzes were open note. He cares for us as students and tried to make lecture interesting.

Really enjoyed having this professor and the class topics were very interesting. He is really involved with his work and the material + you can tell he is very knowledgeable about each topic. He is very open to questions and keeps the content interesting. Even though attendance was not mandatory he does not post the lectures, so go to his class!!
Luckily there are no tests, a lot of the grade come from pop up in class assignments & projects. If anything the TA will be the reason you don't get an A in the class.

Most of the work was done with reading and some essays. Was not hard, but can get tiring if you do not like writing. His course should be listed as BBH 311W lol. But he was seriously so kind and easy to pay attention to. I had his 9:05 class, and even though I always showed up late he never seemed to have a problem with it. I'm not a morning person
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --So many papers

reviews.comment: He was so sweet and knows what he is talking about and has great connections in the biobheavioral health world! Love Dr. Kyle!

Kyle is one of the best professors I've had. He is very intelligent and you can tell how much he cares about the topics we go over in class. The lectures have a lot of information and he doesn't post the slides so be prepared to show up to class for notes.

Kyle is the best. He is very passionate about BBH; it's very reassuring that I'm in the right major. He is absolutely hilarious and gives extremely relevant examples from his medical experience and personal life. The ONLY con (if that) is that he doesn't post notes so you have to go to class to get them. But I don't care about that bc I go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Murdock is awesome. He has so much experience and really knows what he's talking about. His class was super fun (even the work) and he used Tophat to ask questions (most of them were funny). I LOVE when professors share a bit about their personal life and relate it to the class. He was super personable and really wanted students to succeed. 11/10!

Kyle is literally AMAZING. He is so sweet and funny. He often talks about his personal life and shows the class pictures and funny stories to take the edge off after concentrating for so long. He is super easygoing, and anyone can easily earn an A in this class if you keep in contact with him and the TA based on their expectations.
He is absolutely awesome and really just makes your life easy with the way he runs his class!
Love the professor but the class was easy but annoying. No exams but quizzes can be very detailed. He goes through notes very fast and does not post slides.

Dr. Murdock is easily one of the best professor's I've had. The lectures cover a lot of broad material, but he adds in fun stories and explains things really well. He also spent an entire class talking about how to get into grad school, which is something that I've never heard of any other prof doing. Highly recommend taking him!!

Professor Murdock is one of the coolest professors I have had in my 4 years at Penn State. He really cares about his students, and made the transition back to in person classes great for his students. His lectures are broad, but the way he teaches it is good, and he tells funny stories throughout the semester too. Totally recommend taking his class

One of the best professors ive had. Take Professor Murdock is you have the chance he is very knowledgeable and makes the lectures interesting. I learned so much and he grades very fair. One of the classes I actually enjoyed going to.

I took this class in FA 2020 while the course was a hybrid model of in person and online. Kyle's stories from his time as a clinical psychologist help to make the class interesting and the material easier to remember. Although there are many quizzes and no exams, you need to take thorough notes for the quizzes.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Kyle is literally the best professor I've had at Penn State. He's funny, caring, and very knowledgable. All the quiz questions come directly from the notes so if you pay attention during class they're easy. He's very open with his students and wants them to succeed. I find the material to be interesting and useful. Take 311 with Kyle he's the goat

Dr. Kyle Murdock is the man. He clearly knows what hes talking about and makes class so fun and interesting. Hes also very accommodating as long as you communicate with him respectively. I had him for BBH 311 and 416 and couldnt have asked for a better, more caring teacher. Take a class with him hes helpful with more than just class content.

Kyle unfortunately went through a life changing experience during our semester with him. He returned a couple weeks later & inspired me by how well he managed to still make us all laugh and continued his career here after. Makes dry, known material in class more fun and goes by fast. I'm taking 416 with him & can't wait to see where his career goes

Dr. Murdock is a great and down-to-earth professor and his class is a little repetitive of other BBH classes i have taken before. There are only quizzes, reading guides and case studies which are not too bad if you go to class and review. The TA, Mariah, is an extremely harsh grader which I think is the only down side of this class

Always responds to emails quickly and is very helpful. He clearly cares about his students' future and is willing to do what it takes to help them achieve their goals. The class is a little awkward because it is so broad, but I highly recommend taking it from him.
don't listen to the bad comments those people are idiots, most lectures are interesting and he tells funny stories that are relatable to the material

Im gonna be real with yall so u can avoid this Professor. YES, there are no exams and YES, he gives out extra credit for speaking in class but NO it isnt not worth sitting through these lonnnnggg boring lectures where the slides consist of google photos and no other text to study off of. I would rather be in a class I learn than an easy one.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Kyle is such an entertaining professor. His lectures are long but he adds funny stories and breaks and gives extra credit if you talk in class. Homework only takes about 40 minutes a week and the quizzes are fair and made up mostly of clicker questions. You can tell he has a lot of life experience and actually cares about students and their futures

So I am currently in Kyles class this semester, and unlike his classes last semester, he isn't as easy as before. It isn't impossible, but if you don't try, you won't do well. Don't expect to not do anything and still get an A. Various tests/case studies/reading guides due, grading is a bit tough, but still very possible to get an A if you do work.

Dr. Murdock is a new professor, and he does a really great job. The material taught in this class can be really boring but Kyle is a great professor. You don't have to go to class, but you're guaranteed an A if you do. Everything is easy and doesn't take much time to complete, and your lowest score for each category of assignments is dropped.

Dr. Murdock is one of my favorite professors. He is always very kind and helpful. He gives you the answers to the quizzes before the quiz. There are no exams and he drops the lowest of each assignment. He talks about himself a lot which is kind of comical, but he's a good guy. I highly recommend this class. ***PLUS!!! NO BOOK IS NEEDED*** YAY!

great professor. funnest professor i've had so far at penn state. I highly recommend his class. 5 case studies and 5 quizzes but lowest for each is dropped. and a final paper. there is no final exam just the final paper. definitely take this class with kyle
Kyle is a great professor. There are 5 "exams" and 5 papers but he drops the lowest grade. very understanding and very helpful. bottom line definitely take this class
HW takes forever. Expects the same from exams, except you only have an hour and a half.
does not grade your assignments. we are about one month away from finals and he has not graded a single assignment for the whole class

Not sure why there are so many complaints about Dr. Kifer. If you go to class and do everything that he says, the class is not that bad. He explains concepts pretty well and sets you up for success. Like most classes, if you attend the lectures, listen, and work hard on the homework, you will succeed.

two exams worth 60% of our grade, but you have to code in the terminal, and if any line is wrong, you lose an ungodly amount of points.  While Similar to the assignments, those took up to 7 hours to complete, and you only get an hour and a half for the exams. 
Very bad lecturer as well, reads entirely off slides, vague office hours. Do not take.

He puts minimal effort into actually teaching students about concepts. He reads directly off of slides during lectures, and half the time he is talking too quietly for you to even hear. We have already had our last class and have the final in two days, but I wouldn't know what my current grade is because half our assignments aren't even graded yet.

This is the most difficult and time-consuming class I have taken at Penn State. The concepts should be easier to learn than they actually are. Homework assignments will make you want to drop the class for how long they take you to do. The exams are terrible and almost everyone fails to complete them.

Fair class. The effort you put in is the grade you'll get back. Long assignments some over 4h but given with more than enough time (Daniel will even give you time in class to do them) you have unlimited tries in gradescope so its up to you if you want to risk it on the exams. The exams are fair to the content and hwks with open notes and gradescope

Kifer's class is arguably the worst run class I've ever been in. Exam's are unreasonably long, and while the concepts are super easy, he decides to try and cram 6 hours of work into a 1 hour exam. Only about 5 / 50 kids finished the final within the time frame. He purposely makes the class difficult to stroke his ego.

Exams were extremely difficult. The homework was also challenging, with me spending nearly 10 hours to complete it. It does not get any better on the exams, with them being the same as the HWs, and now you only get an hour to complete them. Also makes you code in terminal for 0 reason when IDE's exist. WOULD NEVER TAKE THIS PROF!!!!!

Midterm is 30% of your grade and only one question. Homeworks take 6-8 hours but you're expected to do the same in 1 hour on an exam without any errors. Partial credit is never implemented, and the difference of one line of code can turn your grade from 100% to 40%. Weird superiority complex and doesn't follow AI reporting guidelines. Unreasonable.

Class is easy. He explains stuff on the slide well. You wouldn't even need to spend time out of class doing the assignments because he provides many lab days that act like office hours! Everything on the HW will be solely from the slides, so its easy as long as you understand the slides. You have access to Github (all hw) and slides during exams!

Class is difficult. Homeworks often take 12-20 hours outside of class time and oftentimes require many days in advance to get working. However, probably the class I learned the most, and the final grade was curved generously. Be prepared to spend a lot of time and to feel a little out of your depth throughout the course, but it may turn out okay

Class is Entirely Unorganized: You don't know how many assignments you will receive and dues dates are impossibly close to the date they're assigned. 

Exams are the Entire Course (60%): You get a short amount of time to write code that must be "optimized" and run perfectly on GradeScope or else you're screwed. 

Unprofessional and Unreasonable.

WARNING:
Easily the worst professor I've had at school. Labs/HW would take on average up to 8-12 hours a week outside of class, and you are expected to do the same level of work on a single exam. You feel highly inferior in office hours, partial credit was promised in the syllabus but NEVER implemented, and grading is insanely strict on top of that

Horrible teacher. I was very familiar with a cluster environment and linux before coming into the class, so it less difficult; but, he was probably the worst teacher I have ever had. He is not helpful at all and his exam structure is completely absurd. The assignments are easy, but the final and midterm are horrible.

The class is challenging but you have plenty of time for the assignments on Gradescope so you can know what grade you will get. Lectures are unorganized and not very helpful, but there he is always available for questions. Get familiar with Linux at the start of the class to be prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Honestly, Dr. Kifer has a difficult CMPSC/DS 410 class. However, I feel like I learned the most in his class out of other CMPSC classes I have taken before and he was very generous with grading and understanding his classes' needs. Take him if you want to learn Scala! However, know that it will be difficult to get an A!
Although the class is difficult, but professor Daniel is great. He will answer the questions. And he is generous with giving the final letter grade.

Probably one of the better CMPSC teachers here. If you pay attention in lectures he gives you everything you need to succeed in the class. He responds to messages quickly, but his responses are usually very short and not the most helpful. It is a hard class but if you pay attention and work hard it's pretty easy to pass.

By week 5, nearly half the class had dropped this course. Kifer expects the whole class to be completely comfortable with new programs, packages, and systems by the end of syllabus week and offers little to no help when encountering issues, simply telling you to "read the instructions" which are already ambiguous enough.

Dr. Kifer is always well prepared for class, and his lectures are clearly well thought out and informative. While the homework can get difficult, it is still extremely fun and rewarding to figure things out. His office hours are also extremely helpful. I would definitely recommend taking one of his classes-it is fun and very informative.

Went on and on the first day about how important reading the instructions is, and stated that as long as we are literate enough to read through each assignment we will pass without issue. He then proceeds to give entirely incorrect instructions, and completely ambiguous assignments that are impossible to understand on the first reads through.

Many students complain about the difficulty of the class contents he designs. Honestly, it's one of the most informative classes I took at PSU. You definitely can learn some things new that you can add to your resume from this class if you put in some effort. If you want to learn Scala, choose him!
No partial credit for not running code. Perfect code without detailed comments are graded harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Half the class seemed to drop after the midterm (avg score  50). Homeworks weren't too difficult. Midterm/Final coding based and aren't taken on your personal computer even though screen is recorded. He does have a line in the syllabus that if your code doesn't run you won't receive a passing grade...
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: To be fairly, Dr. Kifer's lecture is one of best in the CSE dept, definitely could learn something useful. Homework is challenging but not that hard. However, the exams are hard and weird, especially in the midterm there's lot of questions that the lectures not covered.
Exams are completely different from what he teaches. He just makes everything very very hard. Do not take him.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Kifer gave amazing lectures that really helped me understand machine learning, ranging from the intuition behind certain algorithms to their applications to the underlying math. However, some of the assignments and criteria was unclear (especially after covid)

I've taken both of Prof. Kifer's course, CMPSC 448 and CMPSC 410, at Penn State. His lectures are intuitive and inspirational, which shows that he did care about teaching and how to make students understand the content.

This man is one of the most savage profs I've had. He made us obsess over matrix calcs, and barely put it in the midterm. He made us obsess over the entire syllabus, and then the final was bayes theorem. That being said, his lectures are pretty descriptive and I preferred his lectures once we were able to record it.
Do not have any course with him, this guy is a much worse lecturer than Yanling Wang. He will never answer your question directly and friendly, and the course is just graded by few things.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Toughest professor I have ever met in my college life. Like 50% people dropped this course after midterm.
Avoid him at any cost. Since COVID-19, we cannot have a normal final exam, he changes the weight of midterm which average socre is about 52/96 from 35% to 52.5%.

Dan actually cares that students understand the course content, and he makes an effort to explain concepts well. He did a good job emphasizing the basics of mapreduce and spark. The class is not conceptually difficult, but it can be challenging to get used to new programming frameworks. Also, he does programming exams.

The professor was somewhat awkward when giving lectures. I do not think he was comfortable with public speaking. We used clicker questions for attendance in class, but considering it was only a 40 person class, I think it was a little unnecessary. The labs are challenging simply because we had to use absurd systems to run our program.
The class itself is interesting and he cares about teaching his students.

I see a ton of hate here, but Simon is a great professor. You actually learn about different parts of the sports industry, including those outside of America. It is a good eye-opener for someone looking for ways to enter the industry. Exams are open-book and easy. The homework does require work, but as long as you put in the time, it's an easy A

This teacher is horrendous. Was told I would be getting a great professor in this class named Mike Poorman who everyone loves. Instead I got a flaming bag on coal. Simon treats this class like a 400 level class. The TA and him were the harshest graders i've ever seen. Nit picking things that were not big deals.

100 level class with the most busy work and dumbest assignments possible. Attendance is only required for guest speakers, and exams are online. Not a difficult class, but dude is a tool and a clear step down from what I heard about this class when Poorman taught it.

I did not enjoy Simon's class whatsoever, and it didn't make learning about the Sports Industry fun. He assigned multiple papers with strict formatting rules and would lose points if even a small thing was wrong. This should be a class about sports and shouldn't be like an AP English class. Don't take this if you want an enjoyable sports course.

Simon is one of the worst professors I have ever had!!! All he does is assign papers with strict formatting directions like it's a AP high school class. He complains every single lecture about people not participating when it's 9am and a room of 150 people. He forces you to attended guest speaker lectures and write about them. Worst teacher.

This is the nicest, most caring man in the world. I never write reviews but I just hope he reads this so he knows how much everyone likes him. He turns a somewhat boring topic into an engaging lesson and he genuinely wants you to learn. He will change things around and accommodate just so we succeed. If u have him, ur so lucky!

I'm not even done with the class yet but want to post this for people considering - take this class! This man is the nicest man I have ever met and genuinely cares. He is so experienced yet humble. He is the only professor that genuinely makes me feel respected and accounted for.

He's really funny and wants all his students to succeed. Attendance is taken randomly and if you're there for 5 of the times he takes it, you get a 100% on attendance. Exams make up 60% of your grade. Homeworks make up 30% and they're graded as pass/fail. Not sure at all how this related to risk management honestly
Excellent professor and he tries to help each student to get good grades.

I can really learn something from his class. He really want every student to learn something. He is an amazing professor. The best professor in University. If you study during class, you will get an A.

Professor Peng is the nicest professor I have met in my time here at Penn State. He genuinely cares about his students and prioritizes making sure his students understand what is going on over exam grades. He's super helpful in office hours, is constantly giving extra credit, and curves exams when needed. Pay attention to lectures and ask questions

Professor Peng is the best one I met at university, he is very kind and he can explain some tough things in a simple and easy understanding way! I recommended every RM major student to take this course, R language is useful and the professor won't disappoint you!!
Dr. Peng is intelligent, caring, and eager to help his students. The later of this class is way harder than the beginning, so take each class seriously and be prepared to learn.

great prof!! so encouraging at office hours, class is semi optional, tests are straight forward, and most importantly he is the most caring prof ive ever had, understands any difficulties, and is so fair in grading and how he conducts the class. TAKE HIM if you want an A *and* an amazing prof who is a joy to be around!!!

The best professor I have ever met. He cares if students understand topics, and he cold calls students but it really helps to understand the topics. Every time you answer his question correctly he will encourage you which makes you feel confident. Exams are not tricky at all-you need to understand the knowledge.
Dr. Liang is an awesome guy who actually cares about his students. He always makes sure that everyone is understanding the topic. The material is hard but he makes it easy for you. Great experience!

If you're looking for a class to look forward to, this is the one! He makes class so entertaining and makes sure everyone feels included, whether you want to be or not. I'm so glad I took his class, I've learned so much from him. Pay attention and participate to get the most out of class--this is not your stereotypical teaching style.

One of my fav professors. He's a kooky guy, and will give you a good grade if you put effort into your assignments and do the outside readings. PMK is a very kind soul, and just loves to talk. If you go to class wanting to sit quietly in the back, you'll hate his class. He's a super chatty guy and an amazing writer himself. Learned tons from him

Please take Professor Kellermann. Really easy professor, extremely funny (even if people don't laugh at his jokes enough). His only vice is being a very slow grader, but you'll enjoy him as a professor.

What a guy. You will never have a teacher like him. He teaches not only grammar but life lessons. Class is never boring because he'll always do some random thing to get everyone's attention. My class was dry, so nobody laughed at his jokes, but they were funny. Papers are light, he's not a tough grader. It's a fun class.

Your grade is basically weekly discussion posts, a 350 word essay, a video reading this essay, a group essay, and a persuasive essay. Not a lot of things to do, and he's pretty accessible outside of class. He takes forever to grade things though. Overall pretty easy, show up to class, participate a little in his questions, and you'll be fine
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Average instructor, you will need to read and write and go to class. He is very bad at communication and late on grading papers, and not clear about what he wants for writing assignments.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--So many papers

reviews.comment: The readings and videos required supported writing growth and bettered our lives to make us well-rounded college students. Peer reviews were structured to be helpful, and the class felt more connected through the intriguing attendance questions. This professor cares, makes puns, and encourages open-minded discussion.

Paul's class is a fun ride - expect some quirks but his engaging personality makes it a blast. Short assignments, helpful feedback, and unstuckstudy made prepping a breeze. Definitely recommend for an easy A!

After my first year at Penn State, Professor Kellermann was the best professor I had. Ending the days with his class was the best decision I've ever made. He does a great job at getting his students to be engaged in his class everyday. He also never failed to make me laugh in that class. I would highly recommend taking his class.

After finishing my freshman year at Penn State, Professor Kellermann was my favorite professor across the two semesters. Ending the day with his class was the best decision I've ever made. He knows how to always get his students engaged and is always there with a smile on his face. He never failed to make me laugh in that class. Highly Recommend.

Paul Kellerman was an okay instructor. 

You need to go to class, read, and he can be confusing about what he wants done for assignments and papers. Very slow grader and he takes forever to grade papers and assignments. Not a bad instructor but his feedback about what he wants done for papers and projects is not always clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I was not looking forward to taking this class, but he made it very enjoyable. There are only a few big papers to write, and they're graded relatively lightly. He also facilitates peer review discussions and instructor conferences for essays, which I found very helpful. There can be a lot of stuff to read prior to each class, but it was manageable.

Best english 15 professor at Penn State. I was dreading this class and it ended up being my favorite class during the semester. His personality made class enjoyable and his assignments were very easy.

Best English 15 teacher at PSU. He is an interesting guy but makes class very fun. There are weekly discussion posts and replies that don't take more than 5-10 minutes. You are graded on that and three essays. His class is fun and interesting. There are weekly readings as well. He provides lots of help to his students, and he cares a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Probably one of the worst english "professors" I've ever had.  You wouldn't know english was his first language but how bad he was at speaking it, let alone teaching it.

There were two papers worth 70% of our grade, and he never graded them. He inexplicably lowered my grade by 10 points after the semester was already over, after having an A the entire semester, yet those two papers were NEVER graded. It was really unprofessional and made his class stressful. The writing homework and readings were really helpful.

At first, I was concerned about him because he is a bit strange but after a week, I really began to enjoy having him. He is super caring and funny and definitely makes sure there's never a dull moment in class. His assignments are about 3 essays and one is a group essay and weekly meditations. He is a slow grader but you should get at least a B+.

HE SUCKS! It's finals week and he still hasn't graded assignments from the first week! There's only 2 large assignments, and he just put in the first one FROM EARLY OCTOBER!! And on top of that, he's a harsh grader!! 

At the late drop deadline there were only 2 small grades in. Unacceptable!!

I thought he was literally insane my first day of class but his humor and chaos makes class fun. He assigns online readings before every class but you can just skim through them or read during class. One discussion post a week and 3 essays total(500 words ish). He takes a while to grade but if you do the work and show up to class you will get an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Kellermann will be one of my most memorable professors at PSU. Yes, he takes forever to grade assignments. But as long as you participate and do what he asks, you should easily get a B+ or higher (depending on your writing skills). He is definitely easy on you compared to other English professors here (especially for ENGL 15A).
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only take this professor if you're not concerned about your assignments being graded until months after you submitted them! I had to e-mail Mr. Kellerman three times to get him to post my final grade. I'm sorry, but this is completely unacceptable! Every student deserves to have his or her grades submitted in a timely and professional manner.

Professor Kellerman is the greatest professor I've ever had. He's the most chaotic guy around but boy is he incredible at keeping a class engaged. I would marry this man if I could. I've never been more excited to go to class! TAKE HIS CLASS, You simply won't regret it.

Good professor who cares about his students. This class is very much 'get out what you put in.' You can get a good grade without much effort but the class is much more enjoyable if you participate in discussion. 3 papers and weekly discussion posts were graded. He does take a long time to grade but leaves high quality feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There were only three "big" assignments that were maximum of 1,000 words so it was not that hard to write. Weekly discussion posts that were actually enjoyable.

He's easy-going and his classes are pretty laid back. There are readings but you really don't need to do them. He only gives us three essays, and one of them is a group essay. Compared to what I've heard about other classes, I'd say his would be the easiest. By the end of the semester, the entire class is pretty tight.

Prof. Kellermann is such an amazing professor. On the first day of class, I thought he was a literal psychopath because he's so strange, but he's so funny and made me excited to come to class everyday. He cracks a lot of jokes, and only gives 3 major writing assignments on top of weekly discussion posts for the entire semester. 11/10 recommend.
Taking 15A was my best decision! Prof truly cares and is so funny. I always enjoyed coming to class. He takes the time to conference with students and always gave good inout. I def recommend him!

Paul is an awesome guy. Hes super kind and compassionate towards his students. He made the class environment comfortable. He did take a long time to grade essays, but I bet it takes a while to get through them all. We wrote 3 essays during the semester and only one was graded when the semester ended. So, revisions arent really a thing.

Paul is the kind of professor that makes you want to come to class again and again. He makes class fun and painless. He is very knowledgeable, down to earth, and cares a lot about his students. Take his classes!!

The dude tries to be really nice to his students, which I can completely respect. But man, this dude does not grade assignments. So it's almost impossible to get feedback on what he likes/dislikes about your writing until the semester is already over, by which point you can't make any changes to it. Which kinda defeats the point of a writing class.

Loved this class and the professor! He was so hilarious and we would barely learn in the class and he would just talk about his life. A few short papers and the only thing is he really cares about attendance!

Classes are fun and assignments are, too. You'll never get feedback or grades on your big assignments (of which there are three), but he's not a very harsh grader. Lots of reading, but the material is high-quality and you can probably get by without doing most of it. I know people who did that.

There are no words to describe how amazing of a professor Paul Kellerman is, there is no single teacher in Penn State that has inspired me as much as him. He talks about real issues, and genuinely cares about the world around us. The lectures are interesting and interactive. Do the readings before class!! He takes a while to grade, but you'll pass.

its been three weeks and he hasn't graded a single assignment throughout the semester or now, he tricks lionpath by putting NG. The class itself was okay, but he doesn't grade any assignments throughout the semester. If you want a funny teacher that gives you extensions but won't grade anything, go for it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Although he takes forever to get grade backs, Paul is absolutely hilarious and a great professor. I always enjoyed going to class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He's a fun teacher in that he makes you laugh a lot, but beyond that I would not recommend him. My class did not get a single grade until after the late drop period had passed. No papers were given back, no discussion or attendance points were graded, it was a very stressful experience honestly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Paul truly is a gem. He's a hilarious dude who makes coming to class way more enjoyable. The class was really easy and as long as you show up and make an effort you can easily get an A. Highly recommend him as a professor.

You'll learn a lot from this class. He expects you to do the lessons and assignments. He's timely with responding and grading. Some have said it's a lot of reading and writing but in reality, it's just the right amount. I've had other classes where it was worse. Plus, the assignments aren't even hard! Just do the class! It was my favorite.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: This guy is fun in lecture, if you can even call it that. We don't always make much progress in class, but what he does say is very well said. His written descriptions of assignments are very clear if you read them well. Try to get all his jokes, they can be subtle. His grading is incredibly fair, always gives very valid and constructive feedback.

I found his online class to be confusing and difficult. There were two due dates every week with multiple assignements-reading (from 3 books) , a writing piece and an in depth discussion with two replies. He even had a hard time keeping up with grading and feedback. Group projects were a nightmare-people disappeared-had to be reassigned twice.

If you don't take a class with Paul, you are wrong. He is so amazing and funny! Puns just roll off of his tongue. Papers were really easy. As long as you try your best, you will pass them all. He sees things from multiple perspectives and gives good feedback. He takes a while to grade, but it's totally worth it. Such a sweet, caring man. Take him!

PMK is a cool professor and a great guy. Get ready for classes full of the best puns you've ever heard. On the first day of class you'll think he's crazy, by the last day you'll know he is. PMK will show you a good time and make you think while you're at it. He's not an easy A but it's possible. TAKE HIM IF YOU CAN!

PMK didn't really teach me much about writing. He had good discussions that kept me thinking, but for a composition class, I would've rather had another teacher. He didn't get anything back to us on time so I didn't get any constructive criticism, and grading criteria was always very vague. Good guy, not the best prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Love prof K! He has such a kind heart and really wants the best for all of his students. If you can't stand puns he isn't the professor for you. He doesn't lecture, but makes class more of a discussion. We didn't need any books. He references them a few times but you never need them in class. Lots of reading homework but you don't have to do it.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: P. Kellermann is such a great guy! He's hysterical and his class was pretty interesting. There's a lot of homework, but it's a writing class so you should expect that. He grades fairly, just make sure you put in effort. I would definitely take this class again, highly recommend him!

This is a writing class, so you will be writing, but the assignments are not that hard.  The professor really wants you to do well and he helps you with ideas, and how to improve.  Great class.  Good Professor.
He's a great professor. One of the best i've had, to be honest. Besides being funny and original, Professor Kellerman is definitely one of the few people I can honestly call a "good human being".

Paul Kellermann is not that good of an instructor.  He's extremely rude to students, opinionated, one of those instructors who wants to hear what he says and his opinions parroted back to him, and he's not clear on what he wants for papers.
Professor Kellerman is a unique and authentic personality. His wit will keep you laughing and engaged. You will become a better writer and have fun with it. Awesome professor and awesome class

Amazing professor. He's hilarious, but may offend some people. His will to help is highly evident. A LOT of readings to do. Peer edits are mandatory, and effort counts. A lot of assignments, so be prepared to work almost every day. Fail to be clear with him, and he'll send an angry e-mail. Overall, not a bad grader and a fun class to attend.

Professor Kellerman is by far one of my favorite professors. His sense of humor may offend some, but he made class interesting to attend. He is a tough grader but if you ask him to read your rough draft, he tells you exactly what to change. Overall, it was an easy class. There was only a few essays which he gave plenty of time to complete.

PMK is great. The first day of class was a shock because his teaching style was different than anything I had experienced. He's hilarious and his pun game is absurd. If you attend class and put effort in to your papers, you're golden. He's always there to meet w you and help, and I really learned a lot in his class. Hands down best prof I've had.
great professor, takes time to get used to his teaching style but its worth it. weekly meditations are not difficult and add to participation. i recommend this professor.

Tries to be casual by cursing and making jokes. Overuses terrible puns. Mandatory peer reviews. Group essays where everyone gets the same grade regardless of individual effort. Mandatory visits to museums outside of class. Limited criticism on papers but not a tough grader. Attempts to make it engaging but just sits there awkwardly if it fails.

The absolute man, makes class interesting. Curses, messes around; promotes an informal setting. Grading isnt too bad. Just make if your serious work and you should do fine. I get A- on my papers. TAKE HIM, the only class I took this semester that I didnt want to skip.

Paul is the best professor I've had at Penn State! He wants every student to succeed, and is great at helping your writing. He makes class fun and makes you think. Don't be scared of his "tough grading" - it's totally fair! Do the meditations and take advantage of office hours and peer review, and you're sure to get an A, no doubt. PMK FOREVER.
Paul is a great guy.  He really wants all of his students to be successful.

Paul is a great guy. He really cares about students and their lives here at Penn State. He's great at making you think and rethink your beliefs, and he also has a way of making writing fun, even for those who hate it. Overall, he is the best professor I've had, and I definitely recommend.
Paul was a great professor that genuinely cared about his students. GO TO OFFICE HOURS. He will read over your essay and tell you what to add to get an A.

I took Paul's class 6-9 and it was probably one of the best classes I've taken. Even though it was 3 hours it never felt that way. He's great! I've been trying to find more classes of his to take. I highly recommend taking one of his classes!

Paul is an amazing teacher. I took this as a night class (W 6-9) and always looked forward to going. He is funny and entertaining. He gives helpful, thoughtful feedback on papers. The assigned readings are some of the best stories I've read. He has a great teaching philosophy-- I hope to take another class with him in the future.

Paul is the best professor I've had a Penn State. If you go to his office hours, he will tell you everything you need to add to your essay to get an A on it. Totally recommend him; he's an awesome guy.
Class is fun but hes a really tough grader

Mr. Kellermann is a great teacher and person. He is entertaining and really makes class enjoyable. There are not many papers to write and the reading assignments are not a big deal. Take his class if you can!

Paul Kellermann is a fantastic English teacher, you'll leave his class with much more then you came in with. plus, he makes classes fun to go to, so you'll never want to skip. You'll be lucky if you get him and he grades very fair.
Awesome teacher. Highly recommend him. He makes you want to go to class every week.

Paul is what professors should be.  You learn alot, but it isn't painful at all.  Instead it's really fun.  He gets everyone involved. I have a terrible memory but writing tips he gave stuck with me.  He's dedicated, too.  You will be glad you took his class.

PMK is a great professor with a funny sense of humor. If you need help he is very helpful and is easy to understand. However, he is not the easiest grader and you need to work for the grade you want...whatever that may be. I got a B+ in this class and was devastated; there are definitely no brownie points in this class.
Taken him for several courses.  Absolutely love him.
Such a legend at Penn State! Paul has an interesting sense of humor and it won't take long before it rubs off on you. Great guy in general.

Paul is the man. He is very straight-forward and has a great sense of humor. If you can take his once a week 6-9 class its the most fun I have ever ha at PSU in a class. One quiz every week and minor assignments once or twice a week along with 3 main projects. One fiction, one non-fiction, and one poetry! Paul is GREAT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH HIM!!!!!
Kellermann is easily one of the best professors I have ever had.  He's engaging, has dogs with clever names and he's funny.  It's a winning situation all around.

PMK is so awesome! He's very unorthodox but that's what makes him so cool! You definitely need to do the readings, but they really help. You can also do as many drafts of a paper as you want--which is really helpful! PMK is so cool. Take him, you won't regret it!
I love this guy!! For a class that is notoriously boring and annoying, he makes things much more entertaining. Always willing to provide extra help, too. Definitely take this class with him!

Sir Paul is the man. Gotta keep up with his jokes and sarcasm. Attendance topics are the best part of the class, always fun and entertaining. He's basically a hippie Engl. teacher from the 60s, but that's what makes him great. One of the best teachers I've had at PSU. Highly recommend his class.

One of my favorite professors so far.  Classes are laid-back and you never know what joke he is gonna throw at you.  He doesn't give grades until the end, so you have to go to his office to find out how you're doing.  The class wasn't too hard and my writing definitely improved.

PMK is great at keeping class interesting and fostering an open learning environment. A lot of classmates became close friends during the course of the semester. Fair grader who always has an interesting take on your ideas. Not a lot of comments on papers. Not sure my writing improved too much. He is someone I will stay in touch with.

Interesting man. Conducts class in a way that makes you hate him one day but you cannot make yourself miss that class on the next day. Grades very hard on the papers and is very subjective in his comments, he thinks it is ENGL 400. I'm not to worried about my GPA but this definitely is not the prof for a PreMed.

PMK is the man! The class is interesting and he definitely has a teaching style that draws attention and builds interaction between students. Grading on papers is a bit tough, but it is definitely worth it. You will benefit from taking any one of his classes, and I highly recommend it.

pmk is the craziest, most eccentric professor I have had to date, but teaches with a lot of passion and knows his stuff. Asks tough questions that require thought, picks good reading material, and puts comments on papers that allow to truly improve. Kind of reminds me of the professor from Back to the Future...but definitely a great professor

Paul creates a fun atmosphere and is constantly laughing with his odd sense of humor. He is very reasonable and grades fairly easy. He knows the subject well and gets his points across. I would definitely take a class with him again, don't pass him up!

pretty cool professor. great class! it's kind of boring at times but the material is really interesting. he's a crazy guy who loves to drink coke. tests are pretty easy as long as you read the material. overall, if you need an easy A-B gen ed, take this class.
amazing and fun
pk was a great teacher. although we had weekly paragraphs due and 4 big papers, he was funny and class went by quickly
Entertaining teacher, knows his stuff. Very hard to get A's on papers. I enjoyed this class a lot, just not my grade.

What can I say about Paul. He's crazy; but for the most part in a good way. Very eccentric prof. Attendance is the most random thing ever. He doesn't give out grades throughout the semester but it's okay because It turns out he's a pretty easy grader. Loves wearing doc. martins, jeans and a leather jacket to teach.

I really enjoyed having Paul as a teacher. The writing assignments were interesting, engaging, and manageable because they were spaced out nicely. I found the informal nature of the class to be very interesting and thought provoking. If you are willing to step back and realize that you can always improve your writing, take ENG30.

I AM IN LOVE WITH THIS MAN. Seriously. He kicks ass. I'm only over 1/2 way through the semester and I've already scheduled to take him again in the Spring. He is AMAZING. His class has been my best expierence at PSU so far.

This was an enjoyable class. You read a lot from the textbooks for homework, but it pretty much all goes to good use later in class. The homework assignments are inventive and really get the gears turning for when you have to hand in your long papers. The teacher is very laid back (hawaiian shirt, shorts, comfy/no shoes) and willing to help.
wonderful

A difficult professor to evaluate.  The assignments could be easy, but he makes them difficult... but ultimately for your benefit.  His attitude is a simultaneous strength and flaw.  I had difficulty taking him seriously sometimes, but by and large he was enjoyable to be taught by.  Jokes are usually funny and (at the end) a fair grader.

Paul is the only adult from college that I keep in contact with.  He is a true friend and will go to bat for you again and again.  Years after graduation, I still feel like he is the only person at PSU who took the time to encourage me.

P. Kellerman will challenge the expectations of what an English class can be, and if you choose he can guide you to a more rewarding experience at PSU. Be sure to check him out when he plays Webster's, but leave your irony at the door.
An excellent professor, his standards are high, but very entertaining class

First day was scary, since he made a kid apologize for using his cell phone 10 minutes before class started, but after that, he was excellent.  Very entertaining and made you think creatively.  Great professor to take, so find a course he is teaching and sign up.
My favorite professor at Penn State. Bizarre and brilliant. Great syllabi, great assignments, very accessible and interesting.
Kellermann is excellent.  Never forget the extra "n" at the end.  Definitely my favorite teacher.
excellent professor, very kind, understanding, and helpful.  Can be a hard grader and a bit of a perfectionist though.
This class is really interesting, but the exams are hard as hell. I think he expects too much for a gened. :(
This man is incredible. Schedule him now. NOW! You will not regret your decision. His classes are so much fun and he will literally do anything in his power to help you. Trust me.

Kind of an odd ball, but entertaining nonetheless.  Only complaint is that I wasn't quite sure what I was doing in the class, or rather the relevance to some of the assignments we did.  Fairly easy teacher.
He is the ****ing man.
He bables alot, but the class is interesting enough that it is worth taking.

I look forward to going to every class. It's the only class I have perfect attendance in this year and if he is ever an option for a class you want or need, take it with him!  He could make a boring class great and a good class excellent. My favorite yet.
Really fun professor!
great teacher, makes everything fun
he is such a good teacher.  i actually look foreward to going to class because class is so interesting.
Fantastic!

Paul is an example of what professors should be. After putting up with the crap that passes for education at Penn State, you will find his class like a healthy draught of refreshing, high quality H20.
The coolest guy ever! Joe Gould was the best!
AMAZING. Take him whenever you can. You can tell he TRULEY likes to teach AND he does it very well. Also, he likes cool music and is really funny.
No Comments
Paul rocked my world!
He is just awesome!  Take his class if you can!
Paul can make you laugh whenever.  Also, he helps you to write a steller paper.

The professor grades very tough, especially for a 100-level class, and the professor is very vague on feedback. And if you correct your work from the feedback given, you'll still lose points. There's also so many assignments for the course, save your time and do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Im a history major, do not take her. I would rather several interesting essays than take her class where she grades discussion posts with F's like she's giving out candy. Meanwhile discussions are most of the grade. You would think she would be more compassionate towards people who need to take school online because of other obligations.
She grades discussion posts more harshly than other teachers, especially for a 100 level course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Class structure is simple; read one chapter weekly, write one post, respond to two posts, & hit the assigned word count. Correct editions of textbooks were available on thriftbooks and one was available at my local library. She responded to questions out of class with kindness and good humor. More than fair with grading, and I loved her class!

I found the grading hard to follow, as feedback often didn't clearly explain point deductions or expectations. Assignment instructions felt vague, making it difficult to know what was required even when following directions. Due to the uncertainty around evaluation, I chose to drop the course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Spare yourself headaches and hours of work put into a 100 level class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I am taking this class in the asynchronous form and it is THE most work I have ever had to do for an online class. If you are looking for an easy online class to satisfy a requirement, this is NOT it. She grades discussion posts so incredibly tough. It is currently the lowest grade I currently have and it is an ONLINE class.

She actually treats this class like a 400-level course. The grading on her discussion posts is actually absurd. No professor should be assigning this much coursework to students who are obviously only taking the class because they have to. The discussion posts take about 3 hours to do in total, which is just stupid. DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS.

This simple class was made incredibly brutal- not at all because of the material, but rather this professor's inconsistent and harsh grading, terrible communication, and shifting expectations. This class was stressful and miserable. I don't recommend taking this class if you're looking for a fair or transparent experience, find another professor.

Dr. Sapelly is the greatest professor at Penn State that you'll come across...all she requires you do is make an effort, and complete your assignments. If you miss an assignment or ask for an extension she will almost always give you one. Her assignment descriptions are easy to understand, and she gives succinct feedback.
Don't take this class with this professor!

This professor is probably one of the worst I have ever had. She is a very tough grader but doesn't express what she wants very well. She gave very harsh reviews after only one assignment at the begging of the semester. A lot of work for the class. Do not recommend!

She was so nice! I used a source I shouldn't have and she gave me feedback and I was able to resubmit using the correct sources and did not get penalized. There is lots of writing involved and a 10 question quiz almost every week. Interesting class and I liked debating other students. If you like writing easy A.

Very great course on a wide range of subjects. Dr. Sapelly cares deeply about both the students and the content of the course. Grades are based on a mix of discussion posts, reading quizzes, and essays, but the difficulty feels right for a 100 level course. Content challenges assumptions without being demeaning--it's a great space to learn.
TAKE HER!!! She's the nicest person and more than fair. Wants her students to succeed. Class is super predictable and fair. No exams, just mini reading quizzes.

Really great professor. Super sweet every time I messaged her and very understanding about life situations impacting my ability to complete work on time. Class was really easy as long as you put in the expected effort. She so genuinely wants to see her students succeed, which I really appreciate. Online courses are hard, but Dr. S' was enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Skip Her!Don't Take This Class with Laura! She's very demanding and requires 3 expensive books to read. You will be writing and reading forever in a day. She shows no mercy! You ask questions and her responses are short, so basically figure it out yourself. Her comments for assignments are rude and she's not encouraging. Worse class I've ever had.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: If you have questions about anything, Dr. Sapelly replies quickly and is very friendly. There is one group project at the end of the class but it consists of a lot more independent work than group work and it's a fun project where you get to listen to your favorite musicians. Overall, she's a laid-back professor and easy grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. Laura will make this class a great learning experience. She was always accessible outside of class and ready to help and answer questions. There was a lot of reading but it went along with the assignments and did not take long. The course material is outdated and boring but Laura recognizes this and is doing her best to change it.

Take this professor if you can. Her course content is interesting and relevant and she supplements the content with videos. Weekly discussions, 3 short essays, and a group project made up course with a few quizzes and a mid term. She did not give feedback on grading but I got A's in everything so it wasn't a concern. Would take again.
Dr. Sapelly was very easy to work with. Her history class was fun, easy and you learn a lot.

Easy class with only 1-2 hours of work per week and she will give 100s on everything. You have two discussions each week and they are easy. You'll have one or two small quizzes per week, but you don't need to study because you can find the answers. You also get two attempts and most of the questions are T/F. I got the textbook, but I never use it.

Great class through World Campus. Only 2 quizzes, kind of hard, but if you don't do well, the essays really bring you up. She grades quite fast and a nice grader. Everything is straight forward. There isn't a lot of work to do, so just do the essays well and you'll pass. Just make sure to not write just one paragraph for essays.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Lots of reading to do, but Laura clearly explains what she's looking for on HW and exam papers, making it easy to get an A if you pay attention to the material, her rubrics, and assignment questions. Also sends weekly emails which are helpful/encouraging to read, grades promptly, & can be very understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Caring

reviews.comment: Took sapelly's accelerated hist 021 class online. There was multiple discussions due every week and 3 exam papers, I believe. It was a lot of writing, but if you do the work you should get a good grade. Actually feel like I learned something from this class which was nice. Also, liked that Sapelly emailed us each week, which was motivating
She is so so so so friendly and sweet. If you do the readings and weekly posts you'll do well

This is an enjoyable and easy class. Every week there are readings, a discussion, and a quiz, all of which probably took me only 2-3 hours out of my week. If you do the readings and do the assignments on time you will be fine. I would definitely recommend this class to anyone looking for an easy gen ed with an interesting subject matter.

Easiest college course Ive ever taken, I cant imagine anyone in my class not getting an A. Laura is super friendly and helpful! History is my least fav subject but I love love love this course, I would so take this course again!

Laura is definitely.... unique, but she's so sweet and really cares about her students. She's also brilliant and see every angle to an argument. First  15 minutes of every class is spent sewing (it sounds lame but it's fun). The discussion posts for homework are a ton of reading and writing, but the discussions are worth it. No exams.

Laziest teaching style of all time. I stopped going to lectures after the first exam and got an A. The class is not difficult, but you are going to have to teach yourself the entire thing if you want to do well.

She is a very sweet and kind professor, but in lecture we would go over what we were already  expected to know. We spend 5-10 per question so most of the lecture you sit there just answering simple questions. I usually like bio, but it was way too slow paced for my liking and it did not prepare me for the exams. I would leave lecture more confused.
You teach yourself the entire course and learn NOTHING in lectures.

Worst part about this class was the group work. Groups are chosen at the beginning of the semester and if you get a bad group you're kind of screwed. Professor McCarthy is very nice though, and she cares about your success. It is very easy to skip class and still keep up using the weekly assignments, which I recommend if bio is your strong suit.
Professor McCarthy seemed like a very nice person, but the slides and visual classroom questions that we did in class were mainly trick questions and honestly confused me more than anything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. McCarthy is a helpful professor, and her lectures and LA review sessions are great. However, the lab was frustrating—my TA, Laurel Moyse, graded harshly and unfairly. My grade dropped from an A to an A- due to the lab, while others with different TAs received much higher grades. Unrealistic standards for an entry level class.
Is a flipped class, lectures are well explained. As long as you know everything from the tutorials you're good.

I honestly don't know why Dr. McCarthy is rated so low. I really liked her, I found lecture to be helpful (only sometimes boring), her exams were very straight forward, office hours were helpful, and she offers extra credit. She's very nice and so are the LA's. The lab is annoying but boosts your grade. I'd recommend taking her!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This class was so ridiculous. She expects you to learn everything before hand. For material quite difficult she teaches so little. The La's were amazing though. But at this point I should also be getting paid 100k a year for the amount of teaching I did to myself.

Not quite sure how this woman has a job. She uses the Learning Guides as an excuse to not lecture. And when she does attempt to lecture, she just talks in a circle until you want to get up and leave. You'll probably be better off in the course if you just do not go to lecture and spend that time teaching yourself the concepts.

Dr. McCarthy uses a "reverse classroom" method which, you basically teach yourself the material in class and she reviews it outside of class. In my opinion, that's not something I want to pay for. Her lectures are boring and she is very monotone. A lot of people I know skipped and still did well. Dont take Laurel Moyse as a TA in the lab section!!
She is very nice and genuinely wants you to succeed. Her lectures were not that helpful, but if you go to her office hours they help a lot and she's willing to explain things.
I did not find the lectures to be helpful. Lectures weren't very engaging. Exams were hard and worth most of your grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. McCarthy is a good professor but can be a bit monotonous sometimes. She is good at explaining the answers and is very available during class for questions. She is also helpful when it comes to lab work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Even though I got an A in this class, I don't think going to lectures is 'helpful' and 'motivating' at all. You can easily pass or even get an A in this class by reading off the online Learning Guides and fill out the Learning Guide sheet. The LG sheets pretty much cover everything from the online reading materials.

She's such a nice person and genuinely wants everyone to do well. All BIOL 110 sections are structured the same and exams are the same. IF you actually go to lecture (unlike 70% of the class) and use the practice questions on canvas, you'll be good. Lab is a lot of work but ends up being a booster to final grade. She uses the reverse classroom.

The exams are overly complicated and the majority of the material must be taught to yourself outside of class, but the TAs do offer lots of office hours and help which is great. She uses the reverse classroom technique and I could not have strongly disliked it more. There are 4 exams (1 drop) and a cumulative final worth 2x the amt of points

I honestly don't know why her ratings are so bad, shes honestly amazing. She was very helpful when I needed help on what I got wrong on my exams. I had her 8am lecture, and while nobody wanted to really be there, she was still able to make it fun in a way. I really liked her class and I plan on taking her for 220w.

One word: EH. She was okay. I had her for 8am bio and everyone could tell she didn't wanna be there...but then again, who does? Lectures were informative but boring, and material on exams was not covered in class. Only got a B+ thanks to my lab TA
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I seriously don't know why McCarthy has such bad reviews. First off, shes like the sweetest lady I've ever met in my life. She a sweet person but a horrible professor. 

What you need to know:

1. Assignments never have clear due date with little to no instructions.

2. She never reply to emails. She also blamed us for her lack of communication. 

3. Do not take ENGL50 if you hate social media! tech heavy class.

4. It an easy A but not worth the mental energy.

She is a gem of a human. Class was interesting and worthwhile.

reviews.comment: Another amazing semester with Maria. I take her as much as I can each semester. One of the greatest psychology professors at Penn State hands down. I can never say enough about her. I love Maria! She uses real world examples and makes it so easy to learn. She gives you 8 assignments that are not hard at all due by the end of the semester. If you have a chance to have her as a professor, please take her!!

Maria is a great professor, and she really cares about her students. The late work policy is fair, but the assignments are manageable even without it.
