Overly easy course, I took it online just make sure to set a reminder for when assignments are due so you don't miss any
This class wasn't the most interesting. I definitely learned a lot, but some of it was boring. Professor Obringer is easy to get a hold of, though, and is understanding and caring.
THIS IS FOR EGEE 102. Basically the same exact thing as EGEE 101 (might be easiest gen ed), just take this class for an easy A and do the assignments. It is all asynchronous, the class is a free A.
Renee is absolutely fantastic. She does a good job explaining material and is abundantly helpful and willing to clarify things.

Professor O'Shea's online class was great. As she allowed us to learn through readings and then reflect through weekly questions. Each week we were responsible to write 200-800 word responses. Lack of stability and structure in this course and her LA's do most of the work.

Dr. Ocker gets a hard rep from the lower classman classes, but she's a good professor. She tries to make her lectures entertaining. There are quizzes in every class but the worst 3 are dropped and they aren't that hard. The TA's graded most things and mine were easy graders. Overall, you have to go to class and pay attention and you will be fine.

You have to teach yourself using the Zybooks, she doesn't really teach much at all in class. She also doesn't respond to emails and her TA's do almost all of the work. She can also be rude to students at times for no reason.
She is an okay teacher. Her TAs did most of the work. Wasn't really accessible out of class, either she responded to your emails or didn't at all.

Overall, Doc Ock is one of the best IST professors. She is very sarcastic and may have tones, but she cares about her students and wants people to pass. Most of the course is easy to get an A in, however, the final is difficult and weighted heavy. Do the homework and zybooks, and you will be fine. TA's do the grading and most of the work too.

I was excited to take this course and really dive into java but this professor made me hate java. She was extremely condescending at times if a student had a question and had extremely high expectations for students as if this isn't an introductory course.

never again.

Doc Ock is a sweet lady who genuinely cares about her students. She's always willing to work with you, especially if you form a relationship w/ her. Very nice lady and overall knowledgeable professor.

Ocker is a great option for IST 210 I felt like I learned a lot in this course and can actually do SQL very well. 6 unit quizzes and 6 labs are the biggest thing but may small assignments that help your grade. the LAs are very helpful and good graders I would highly recommend Ocker for 210 she is also so funny. it made the class fun!!

Very good professor, I feel like I have finished this course with a solid understanding of SQL. Professor Ocker usually made her TA's do everything for her. She's not to good at explaining things that clearly and if you have no prior coding experience, get ready to work hard in this class as it will not be easy for you. She definitely cares about her students, but I'd rather her care about my grade. If she's the only option, that's okay

I did not have any coding experience before taking this class and I was so scared I would fail. I got a high A and never felt like I was struggling. Doc Ock is a great teacher and prepares you well for the quizzes and finals.

If you have an option of taking this class with another professor, just go ahead and do that. This class has a quiz every class, no extra credit. LA's are not of much help. In addition, you won't know what went wrong in your exams, as the professor mutes them.

I loved Dr. Ocker she is definitely one of my favorite professors. It feels like she truly cares if you do well or not. Most of the assignments are dependent on the TAs though, they were a big part of the course. It seems like she hires good TAs though because they were very helpful and also seemed to want the best for you.

This professor is the worst I've ever had, so I'm not sure why she's receiving such positive reviews. She just reads from ppt. Tons of hw. Doc Ock is definitely my favorite professor I have taken so far.  She did her best to connect with students and she made this class a great experience, as long as you put the work in and understand the material you should do very well.  I could not recommend her enough for this class!  I hope to have her again in some of the higher-level courses.

Doc Ock is amazing, she clearly cares about everyone and her personality and teaching really shined whenever the mask mandate dropped. She obviously loves being in the classroom and teaching. Subject progression is a bit of a trainwreck but regardless, a good class. Lazy and unreachable TAs who belittle you; don't expect to get any leniency on HW.

My favorite professor at Penn State! Goes over everything in class for you to follow along with and the quizzes/tests are very easy if you pay attention in class. Most work can get done in class as well, as I rarely had homework. Totally recommend.

Doc is the perfect professor for IST 210. We use zybooks for learning SQL. What makes her great is that teaches content during class as well. Goes through the material slowly. Professor Ocker is an amazing teacher, and it really shows in IST210. If you pay attention and come to class, you should be able to get an A in this class with relative ease!

Professor Ocker, is one of the best professors I have had here at Penn State so far. Her classes are focused on learning and understanding the material, the problem sets which were due before the tests often laid out exactly what you needed to know for the test, and I never felt lost in the class. Take this class if you can, easy but great class!

Doc is amazing. I understand the downvotes, but I feel like its because they didn't understand the dynamic of the class or try at all, NOT EASY A

Professor Ocker, or Doc Ock, as she likes to be called, is a great professor. This is a team based class so whoever you get put with in the beginning is with you until the end. Doc is great though, take a course with her!!!

Doc Oak is the sweetest professor I have had at PSU. Her classes can be quite tough, though, so make sure you THOROUGHLY read through the syllabus so you know what's going on. She is the most lively and bubbly teacher and her classes are always a blast to attend. Cannot recommend Doc Ock enough. Take her courses! You'll love her!

I agree with the 1 star rating but I do understand it was hard to transition bec COVID. The prof just reads off the slides and says out loud what code the TA's should type w/o really explaining it well. The slides she presents are all inconsistent and like my peers, I still dont know what im doing and I still have an A. Switched major bec of this.

She was a semi easy grader but i didn't learn much coding in the class.

She has quizzes at the beginning of each class and requires her students to participate in class to earn points. It can be a lot of work, but she does this to ensure her students are engaged and actually read the material. Her lectures are great though, and she's hilarious. She's either someone you'll hate or love.

reviews.comment: Dr. Ocker is a gem. She's an incredibly nice person who wants students to succeed. While I do not like programming, I actually enjoyed this course. I had to go to the TAs for a lot of help on the homework, but Dr. Ocker lets you use a page of notes for exams, which were similar to hw/projects. She's also hilarious and keeps class entertaining.

She was my first professor to meet in U Park and remained one of my favorites. Although she might look very tough but She is extremely nice to you if you go to her office hours. She might be strict on some coding staff like the name of an attribute or methods, you will find that very helpful when you take higher-level classes like IST 242.

Really awesome professor who obviously cares for her students. She made my first coding class a breeze, and she is a very fair teacher with a fun personality. I will say she's not always available outside of class and you will definitely need to stay on top of all the topics to get a good grade.

reviews.comment: This was the best programming class I've taken at Penn State because it was actually designed for beginners. Each class is guided programming practice and the hw and quizzes are based on the in-class work. It might take some effort if you don't get programming but you're given lots of resources and the TAs are very accessible outside of class.

I have previously taken coding classes,not specifically java & thought this class was a breeze. If you have never coded before this will be rough, more than a third of my class dropped & the average on last test was a 56%. There is a TON of help available, class has 3 TAs who have office hours constantly & want to help you. Def better than others

She is the worst teacher I have ever met. Huge tons of homework. Get ready to read 2 journals, 1 packet of cases and write lots of assigned questions every week. Get ready to memory lots of definitions for 3 tests. Also, she has somewhat racial discrimination especially for Asians. If you don't want such a burden, maybe online 301 is better choice

reviews.comment: Although I  wasn't a fan in the beginning of the semester, Doc Ock ended up being a great professor who I recommend. She really does take an interest in her students, and is such a nice person. However,  so many reading quizzes (at least once a week) sucks, and u really have to pay attention in class due to the huge emphasis on participation points

reviews.comment: Professor Ocker is one of a kind. She is a very lively person, and will make you participate. She will call you out if you're not (humorously). Absolutely, the most entertaining class I've ever taken. There was not one dull moment in the entire semester. The class is not hard, but a good amount of work. There are a ton or points, she does give EC

Doc Ock is a great teacher that seems to care about her students. She always adds humor to the class and makes things more interesting than they really are. If you are one that doesn't like to speak up in class, then don't take her. Her teaching style thrives on participation in class which most people seem to like, but some may not.

Doc Ock is great. I had her for 301 right after I transferred from a branch campus back in Fall 2014 and she has been the only professor i've met that cares more about students learning something and putting in actual effort rather than constant examination and memorization. My favorite prof at PSU University Park so far.

It's a pain that you have to use your name tag and she can call you out (and will!) if you're distracted or doing something she's not happy with. Her assignments are fairly easy and her class is pretty entertaining. She gives tons of extra credit! Definitely take her over the other options.
Great teacher, helps your learn material quite effectively and helps those who need help. If she sees the class is struggling as a whole, she will try her hardest to get everyone back on track.
One of the funniest professors I've ever had. Very clear about whats on exams. Lots of assignments to boost your grade and a fairly easy class while learning a lot. Highly recommend.

Dr. Ocker was great. I was a little intimidated at first, but she is super cool. Don't be too worried about participation points, she gives them out every now and then. I didn't raise my hand once and got a 2830. If you have any issues just tell the TA's and they'll help you with whatever you need. Definitely choose to take the class with her.

Participation is required to receive credit, however it is beneficial to learning in this class.  Assignments are easy if you pay attention, first exam is hard.

Ocker is a very fun professor who is very knowledgeable about this course. She put us in groups with people from around the world and had us devise a solution to a bioterrorism threat. Along the way, she helped us troubleshoot any issues pertaining to the project's content as well as any issues with our global teams. Great professor, great course!

Awesome professor who really loves what she does.  The class is both fun and interesting.  I highly recommend this professor for any class she teaches.  You will honestly look forward to going to class, no joke.

One of my favorite professors ever. She's awesome, definitely take her. You won't regret it. Attendance ins't mandatory but sometimes she'll give an attendance pin and you'll get some extra points for showing up!

She is a very good prof. She uses a lot of T.A.s, but she teaches great. She explains things very clearly. The in an attendence pin every once in a while, mostly when half of the class is not there due to weather to a upcoming holiday. If you speak at discussions you get extra credit points! You don't even have to be correct just open your mouth!

She is an easy, fun teacher. This class is an easy A class. All you have to do is the readings (not along 10 pages max) answer the short questions and there is your quiz. She gives weekly quizzes, assignments, and final project. All easy! Recommend.

Doc Ocker is an amazing professor.  I learned a lot from her and she was very helpful.  I would always take her if you had the chance to.  She makes class fun and easy.  We didn't have a final, a final or project, or even the last week of class. She said we did enough work and let us have the last week of class off.
Really nice. Helpful. Easy grader.

My favorite professor at PSU.  She keeps class interesting with humor and you will learn a lot in this course.  The material is easy, but she makes you do a lot of work so the course isn't overall easy.  She'll also bake you cookies if you're good.  Definitely take her.
Not a fan of her personality, or style, but if you go to class every day there's literally no excuse for not getting an A in her class.  It's basically A for effort.

She is funny and has a mature sense of humor. Think of a librarian on crack.  She's been around the block and her lectures are straight forward. Make sure when you explain yourself you give clear and concise questions or you'll loose her.  Wacky, but makes class all the more fun.

She is AWESOME!!!  If you put in an effort and she knows it, you are not going to fail.  I've had her twice and both times the class was so much fun!  She's like that really cool, hot mom of one of your friends.  Always choose her class if you can!  If you get a bad grade in there... you DEFINITELY deserve it!

Doc Ock is one of my favorite PSU professors! She's so funny and fun to be around. I thoroughly enjoyed going to class. She also often brings in cookies :) HIGHLY recommend for IST 301 - Doc Ock is the best!
Really nice professor and fun. Class is pretty chill. There is work but she will work with you if it gets too difficult.

excellent professor. very good at implementing unique teaching methods including snack time (brings in cookies), play time (outside activities), story time (random real life stories). A little eccentric overall, but that keeps the interest level high. A++
Dr. Ocker has to be one of the nicest professors in IST.  She has a unique style of teaching and cares about her students.  She bakes some great cookies too!  I recommend taking her.

Dr. Ocker is a strange professor, quite possibly one of the strangest you will ever meet. She teaches at a steady pace, and is willing to compromise for her students. She is a lot of fun in class but if you don't listen to her, or you're off topic she gives you a glare that could kill bunnies then moves on. Highly recommend her, taking her for 420.
avoid her by all means!

At first I thought she was a bit crazy (first IST course at PSU) but once the class got rolling everything was smooth.  Also took Ocker for IST420 which is a path I would highly recommend.  I would recommend her to anyone who wants to learn and work with someone who integrates "story time" (real world knowledge) into the class.
AMAZING

One of the easiest teachers I have ever had.  Quite helpful and easy going.  A bit rigid on representation of both sexes in all assignments though...  The professor is recommended you won't be disapointed.

Dr. Ocker was one of the best IST professors I've had. She is very high energy and makes class enjoyable with her activities. She has real world knowledge and works in into her coursework. If you approach her she will go out of her way to help or accommodate you. I'd recommend taking her over another professor.
Dr. Ocker was really high energy, and she made the material (which was sometimes boring) seem alot more interesting.

weirdo..Knows nothing but thinks knows all. Doesn't teach anything in class. Only pulls her hairs and acts crazy..Only collects data for her stupid research which has no value at all...do not take any of her classes by any means if you have choices..

Dr. O was AWESOME for IST110.  Since it was her first time teaching it in Spring '06, she wasn't too clear at first in her instructions, but as the semester progressed, she definitely made great improvment.  She has a good personality and is always open to class feedback.  I would definitely recommend taking her class.
I'd rather have my toe nails pulled out with a wrench.

Lets see there was a schedule of lectures, but that got tossed in favor of doing nothing each class. Then, There were grade weights, but she changed those. Oh yeah and there were her grad students who made out like little research bandits at my expense. avoid like ebola.
She is genuinely the best professor I've had at Penn State. Her class is actually interesting and she is not a harsh grader. 10/10.

Has a required textbook but she has the lectures on canvas summarized of each chapter so you don't need to but it. Weekly discussion posts and a project due at the end of the semester. Responds to messages fairly quickly. Gives good encouraging feedback on all discussion posts. Class is definitely worth taking.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Owens is so sweet and caring. She provides really meaningful feedback on assignments. The weekly workload consists of a discussion post, replies to others, and sometimes a research project. All of the smaller research projects contribute to the "final" which is a complete research project. I would definitely take Dr. Owens again.

Lydia is truly an angel. The class is intro-level and she understands that, but she really appreciates people showing up and engaging. She offers in-class participation assignments sporadically and doesn't tell you when they'll be beforehand to encourage attending lecture. She is always open to feedback and is so so kind and understanding. Love her

Very sweet and caring! Randomly took attendance throughout the semester using google forms. 3 quizzes throughout the semester but they were online and taken outside of class. Concept checks were given for homework through the online textbook (which you have to pay for). Lydia is very kind and you can tell that she really cares for her students.

The sweetest professor ever! You do not have many assignments just a few group projects and that is it but they are pretty simple. You will have in class participation but only 12 times but you can miss 2 classes, although she does not announce them. If you have to take Soc 1 or even if you need an easy gen ed definitely take it with her!

Dr. Owens is so so nice!! This class is so easy, she does in class participation points every once in awhile, but not all the time and they don't make up a lot of your grade. No exams or final, just 3 online 40 question quizzes which are easy. One group project and one book/podcast project but I did embedded and it was pretty interesting! TAKE HER!

I took her class a while ago and learned a lot from her. She has the most beautiful slides and an extremely clear course structure. You won't regret taking her class! Lydia is a great sociologist and a kind professor.
Very kind professor. I will take her course again.

The best professor and kindest professor I have ever seen! I must give her a thumbs-up. If every professor is just like her, I am sure this world will be better! We need to support a professor like her. I will give five stars to her. Trust me, you will always be safe in her class because she is the best sociologist who is saving her people.

I took her at 9am so obviously I never showed up. This really didn't affect my grade even though there is participation points. Tests and exams are online and are main parts of grade. The other percent was based off the paper and the group project. Do the concept checks and pack backs it takes 5 seconds.

Lecture was chaotic at times but this was her first time teaching so that will probably improve with time. Extremely responsive to emails and is very helpful with issues. The way she does in class attendance is unusual (only 6 random classes count for participation) but you can make up one of these if you miss it.

The class was super easy to follow and as long as you do the in-class participation and do the work, you get plenty of time to do it, and you will be fine. The professor is super understanding and caring. she is responsive too so you can count on her reply.

Very straightforward class. The lectures were decent and I definitely feel like this course does a good job at introducing sociology to a general audience (most students take it as a GenEd). Lectures at times were a bit disorganized but the class was interesting and the participation activities were very unique and fun. Do packbacks and you're set
Lydia Owens is very sweet and her lectures are very easy to understand. She's very laid back and classwork is easy. Just do the packback every week and you will be set.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was so unresponsive. Incredibly unhelpful.
Good class, show up and do the work you'll get an A
She switched to being my professor like half way through the semester. Honestly an easy A. I dont care about this class so it was boring to me. Taken as a gen Ed

I really really enjoyed this class. It's definitely a lecture-heavy class, but she throws in a lot of videos and some class discussions. The exams aren't hard if you pay attention in class and study a little. She uploads powerpoints and does clicker participation points so you really don't have to go. A few projects & groupwork.
Best professor I've had in a while. Super understanding, and always wants you to do well. Ruth is the best.

Ruth is funny, understanding, and fair. Attendance was not mandatory and if you accidentally missed an assignment, she always gave you more time to submit it. This class was low maintenance which helped because I had a tough course load. I did put in effort though and showed up to class daily and honestly did homework there. Super easy and fun

She was awesome. It's rare that I can put a teacher at 5 and put difficulty at 1, because usually that means you didn't learn, but here she really helps you grow as a speaker and with forming arguments. Super kind but doesn't BS things, gives great feedback, grades very generously and is just real. Doesn't expect the world of you and encourages you
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I took this class during Summer Session, she was super funny and we got out of class early a lot of days. I feel like I can more confidently present in front of large groups of people and the way the speeches are created is like how you write an essay so her class helps you to improve your essay writing too.

She was a good professor who gave easy grades as long as you met her requirements, which were super easy to find and follow. Super detailed, super nice, awesome to reach out of class. Show up and do the work and you're guaranteed at least a B+. Probably the best professor for CAS100A
Ruth was great, she really wanted to see people get better through the course. As long as you do the work, attend class, and do your best in the speeches, you will do good in her class.

Ruth was very nice. Since it was a summer semester, she had to cover a lot of material in a short time, but she made it easy to manage. She was strict when grading outlines, but if you asked for help, she spent time working with you to improve them. She did take a while to grade speeches, which was a downside, but I really enjoyed the class.
Ruth is the goat bro

It is hard to review her because most of it is from the department. However she can be a really harsh grader on outlines and does not use common sense on the obvious because of language barriers. She doesn't really have clear criteria and will tell you your work is awful without any explanations. She will give 0 if she finds 1 mistake.

She gives generic copy pasted feedback on what you turn in that is good and if you do poor on assignment she doesn't give any. Her assignments are often unclear of what the students are supposed to have. She doesn't help students become better, but often just tries to find weaknesses and that you need to redo it. Her lectures are extremely boring.
Attend class and try participating she gives free marks whenever possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Ruth is a passionate professor who cares about each individual student and cares about their success in the class. Ruth was an easy going professor and extremely easy to get in contact with. If Ruth taught more classes I would take all of them.

Ruth is the GOAT. She's cool and easy to talk to. Nobody loves CAS but she helps her students get through it. This was her first semester teaching and it felt like she had been doing it a long time. She lets you out of class early if you get stuff done, keeps it lighthearted and knows how to crack a joke.

I had him for Cyber 262, and he was the professor for only half the semester. Every class begins with him walking around and greeting every single student in the class. Even though some classes only have 5-8 kids, he will still have the same attitude and teaching method, no matter the student. I would 100% say he is the best professor in IST.
Saved our class. Shows he cares for the students

He taught me Cyber100, and he's absolutely wonderful. Professor Price is always so helpful, down to earth, hilarious, and care for his students a lot. He hands out a lot of EC which helps a ton. He's always cracking jokes and posts weekly about seminars and internships. The best professor ever easily.

Dr. Price is the best professor. I had him for Cyber 100 and could not have made the class any easier. It's just online quizzes every week along with a lab every week but they are mostly done in class and are very easy. Definitely take a class with Dr. Price.

Dr. Price is one of the best professors I have taken. He is very hilarious and can make a boring class into a fun class. He really cares about his students and will help you as much as he can. There is a lab and an easy online quiz each 2 weeks. He cares about feedback from students. I would really recommend taking any course that he teaches.
Best professor I ever had at Penn State!! I was nervous going into the class as I am a business major, but he was super helpful with assignments and asked for our feedback for exams.

Dr. Price is the best professor I have ever taken. He makes class very entertaining and is hilarious. He is also very understanding and grades very easily. I would recommend taking ANY course that he teaches, you will never have to struggle. He cares a lot for his students and is always there for you if needed. Weekly easy quiz and lab

Hands down, the best professor I've ever had. Super funny, understanding, and even one time bought the whole class ice cream. He's super chill and as long as you try, you'll get basically a 100% for the class. He also would give encouraging feedback and compliments when he graded the assessments, overall the best professor at PSU there is.
Honestly an amazing prof, definitely try and get him!

Professor Price is the best professor I have ever taken a class with. He is very caring and so fun. He understands the struggle of college students and is very nice and easy. He cares about the students and makes class very fun and enjoyable. He is also easy to reach and gets grades done very quickly. Quizzes are easy and group project is fun.

Dr. Gall is a great professor. He gives students a lot of flexibility in how they want to run their projects. He definitely does not micromanage and instead allows students to work directly with their sponsor. A lot of times our meetings would run late, so he would let us meet with him via Zoom. He is overall a super nice guy and very flexible.

Easy class bad teacher, he does not teach in depth and just skips over important ideas and then barley does any examples making homework and exams harder than they need to be. Plus no annotated lecture slides so he is basically forcing you to go to a class he does nothing in
I was paid to write this review.

This class requires lots of work. Oren and the TAs were helpful. I did buy the product he recommends the DEB. And it was helpful for the Design Projects and HW. It is a challenging class but if you stay on top of HW you will be fine. He does offer extra credit which is good. And class was mandatory

Prof. Gall is friendly, but his lectures are unhelpful and unclear. Doesn't post annotated notes. HW and exams are long and difficult, grading is harsh for no reason. No credit for projects if circuits are correct but don't work. However, grading scale is adjusted at the end and lots of extra credit. Don't buy DEB! Use bredboards in lab for free.

Lectures are to the point and everything is explained clearly. Homework problems, labs and design projects reinforce what has been taught in class. One receives all the support needed to excel in this course.

As you may have seen, Dr. Gall wants to sell you his DEB really bad. It is technically optional, but it is really useful especially for the Design Projects and HW. I had a bad experience with the TAs grading my assignment, who frequently gave me bad grades randomly without explanation. The material is not easy to catch up on if you skip.

Lab was fun with materials to complete some example questions to understand more about the lecture. 
If went to class then it is easy to get a good score.

The class is tough but Professor Gall is helpful. He helped me a lot in office hours and also the LAs were very helpful too. I did buy the DEB he recommended and it was helpful to learn on. Even though the assignments are tough but there is extra credit
I've accomplished so much in this course and feel super prepared and motivated for my next semester. I can't thank Dr. Gall enough for this experience!
This guy is just incompetent nuff said

Oren Gall definitely wants your money; the class is 100000% harder without the breadboard his company makes for 160. He says it's "optional," but it definitely isn't, and you will buy it to make your life easier. That being said, he's a solid professor, and the class is set up so that you will learn, but he'll put in minimal effort to help you.

This man is lazy, he once understood the material he is teaching no doubt but those days are past and he often relies on having a virtual day to cram in ill used class times. He rushes through complex material and does a lot of hand waving, not a fan.

The worst professor and human I have ever interacted with at Penn State. I know it's a required class for most so this won't do much but I just want him to see this and know that nobody loves him and that he would not be missed in the world. Oren I despise you will all of my heart and wish for nothing but the worst to you.

Do. Not. Buy. The. DEB. Don't give him more money than you already do. Just learn to breadboard and do your labs the old-fashioned way. Other than his business tactics, not a bad prof. Just do the design projects early since he never provides enough ICs/LEDs/etc. and the lab WILL run out if you do try to do it last-minute.

Oren. Oren, i dont know where to start. There's so much i want to say but so little i am permitted to. I love you Oren. I often walked up to your podium at the end of class, but was too shy to ask any questions. Oren, I would wait in front of 314C leonard just so we could "coincidentally" see each other. I often imagine a life together with you.

Oren gall is so handsome, so caring, so so so beautiful. The only thing that got me out of bed MWF at 9 AM was just thinking about Oren. I highly recommend you fail this course at least 2 times so you get to see him more often. Additionally, please buy the DEB, it makes labs so much easier, it makes life so much easier, and I sleep with it.

Really good lectures. The lectures flow week to week very logically, so make sure you catch up as fast as you can if you miss a class. Be prepared to review the coursework a ton, especially around the second half of the course, as the homework problems build directly from earlier chapters. Definitely recommend taking this with Professor Gall.

CMPEN 270 with Professor Gall was one of the most useful classes I've taken. The material was challenging but well explained, and the support we got made a big difference. It gave me a solid foundation in computer systems and helped me feel more prepared for research and advanced work.

Professor Gall has engaging lectures that really helped me to learn a lot and care about the field of computer engineering as a whole. The grading was rather challenging but fair, really making me work for my grade in the class.

Took his class last semester. The tests are tough but overall he gives you extra credit opportunities. I bought the DEB and it was very helpful. The LAs will help you in office hours. Overall not a bad class

I had this professor a few years ago and his predatory practices have only grown since then. I was able to purchase the "kit" of components on my own back then ($10 in components sold for $100), and now he requires his "deb kit" which costs $169 for a glorified breadboard. Aside from that, the class is extremely easy.

Gall uses you for money that's all he milks you dry and hopes for you to fail. He doesn't make anything for his class he ends everything out of no where cause he has specific parts of class recorded that he'll use for you to do online by yourself you can ask him about anything and he won't know.
the extra credit is behind paywall

He's not a very good teacher and only cares about the cheque. There's a reason he's had a few ethics complaints filed against him already.

TAs are in charge and don't know what they're doing. I've had to get 30-40% of my work regraded. The DEB is useful, but try and get a parts list and put it together yourself. You'll save $130

I took CMPEN 270 last semester w Dr. Oren is a kind and friendly teacher who really cares about his students. He makes class fun and keeps things easy to understand. His lessons are not stressful, and he creates a calm and happy place to learn. The homework and projects he gives help students understand important ideas in a simple and helpful way.

Dr.Gall doesn't care i'll be honest he's there for money makes u buy his textbook and DEB board which is owned by his company. The projects never make sense and you ask him about it and he doesn't even know. so who does know? The Ta's don't he doesn't then who. he speaks in class just revising the video lectures but not even well. make a study bud

He's alright. Pretty good lectures, and Fridays were all remote. Content came at you extremely fast, he did a decent job at making it understandable. Assignments weren't too bad (lots of extra credit) but exams were mega brutal. Class grade boundaries were very generous.

He started well, but then I realized that the TAs run the whole class, from homework to projects to exams, the whole nine yards. All this guy does is lecture two times a week and one online lecture on Fridays. The exams can be very long and are worded very poorly. Massive curve so if you stay with it you'll be fine. DEB helps, textbook does not.

A lot of people complained about this teacher throughout the semester but most of the information needed was given in the slides and videos. The real help was at office hours. Shoutout Kevin the goat for always helping. Without the TAs, I'm sure most of the people in this class would've done much worse

Oren Gall is a mid professor. He required us to buy a textbook to just have a single question on the Homework. It feels like he does not know what is happening in his class with the LA's doing most of the work. Kevin is the goat.
I really enjoyed taking this class. The professor was very helpful and learned a lot
Labs and projects were disorganized. Textbook was expensive and never used.

The class costs an additional $169 because the labs are prohibitively difficult without the kit that his company sells. He sees the class as a way to generate revenue and negatively affects me as a low income student.

This course was required for my major (BME with focus in Medical Imaging and Devices) but I would recommend it for anyone who needs an engineering elective etc. Professor is great and super approachable and the material was straight forward when it came to assignments and tests!

Dr. Oren is a great, approachable and one of the most friendly professors with an understanding demeanor and care for the students. He maintains the stress-free and relaxing vibe of the lectures and the coursework throughout a semester. The assignments & projects designed are a great starter for understanding the importance of the concepts taught.

ehhh he's alright. lectures are nothing special. most of your learning will be from the LAs/TAs. Doesnt do much tbh, class itself is quite predatory on students such as selling his own textbook and breadboard catered towards assignments.

Pleaseeeeeee, pleaseeeee do not take him. He uses student's tears to fuel his protein powder. Made us buy a textbook for one question for 70 dollars. I need some refund. DEBs are too expensive. Shout out to soumya he is a G. Does not bother to explain any concept, does everything surface level.

Please do not take this class with him. The content is a lot but he makes it impossible to understand. His tests are nothing like his lectures, which are useless as he talks without saying much. Over that he made us buy a textbook that he created for one question in our first HW and never again. the TAs are the only reason anything gets done.

I don't understand the Oren Gall glazing in the ratings. He is a pretty average professor, but he does not understand the structure of his own course. He forced everyone to buy the textbook to only include ONE homework problem, and he doesn't ever know what's on the homeworks or labs. His office hours are useless. I learned mostly through TAs.

I took this class in my fourth semester in Fall 2023 and was my first entry into my track in BME. I found the class very interesting and thus easy. Oren is an amazing professor who is always ready to help students with the class material. The exams have questions that are discussed in the homeworks and class as well. The LA is also very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I took Dr Gall's course this semester, and it was great. He has a remarkable ability to make complex concepts accessible and engaging. Dr Gall encourages critical thinking and fosters a supportive learning environment, making every class both challenging and rewarding. A truly outstanding professor!

I recommend starting HW's a WEEK in advanced! Also, I recommend you treat this class not like a traditional class where you learn from the prof but more of a tutoring session, you essentially have to teach yourself the material. You would think he has no input in HW's or exams the way the material dosen't even remotely follow the lectures.

This class requires you to work a lot! Be ready to spend a lot of time for everything(HWs, Design Projects, Exams, Extra Credit HW, LABs). Start everything early. TAs are very helpful. Ask help whenever stuck. They have enough office hours. And yes getting his $180 kit is important because that will get things done more efficiently. Solve all pyq.

Oren Gall is a pretty solid professor who makes lectures pretty entertaining. Tests are graded a little harshly: One timing hazard diagram was worth 25%, I brain-farted and failed the midterm. Grades are curved pretty nicely. Says you don't need a 180$ breadboard his company makes but he makes the labs almost impossible without it.
Useless lecture only got knowledge from TA, he does make the curve scale low but he is still bad

I hate hardware and dont care to learn it. Oren Gal just yaps at lecture and rewatching the lectures don;t even teach me anyhting. A c is a 59% but I needed that or else I would fail. I don't like the class structure and he doesn't teach. He's a nice ripped man but find peers who can teach the content to you if you struggle like me.

Overall quite the enjoyable class. A couple of things I personally struggled with. If you are unsure about something, best option by far is office hours, I was misled by online resources many times. Homework often reflects the exam more accurately than the actual practice exam, take this with a grain of salt. Also, playing catch up is not fun here.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: oren charges students $150+ to do homeworks by structuring assignments such that they are impossible to do without the DEB kit sold by HIS company... he has basically no involvement other than lecturing (which I guess he's fine at), but the TA's write all the homeworks and exams which is unfortunate as they usually have errors.

Prof. Gall doesn't really do much outside of lecturing, it's mostly just the TAs. An example of how that works out, I went to office hours because they changed the directions for a homework question the day it was due, and even they were still trying to figure out the answer to their own homework question. Basically, it sucks, poor overworked Tas.

All Oren does is lecture(which he's pretty decent at). The class is run by TA's, they make the HW, the tests, everything. Often there are reworks for HW questions only announced the day it's due.The wording on everything is awful. The hardest part about this class isn't the content, it's trying to understand the directions written on the Hws/Tests.

I took this class when it was Dr. Gall's first time teaching it, so we were learning the material together. Lecture is boring, but go to it anyway. The book seems outdated and published without being reviewed for the amount of errors in it. Exams are based on homeworks and Exam Reviews.

1. You have to buy an expensive lab kit from his company, otherwise you cannot complete labs and homework. 

2. Useless lectures. Maybe 10% of the class bothers to attend. 

3. Homework questions consistently have errors.

4. Tests are not hard, but there is no way to prepare without sample questions. 

Not sure what these good reviews are about.
Very good lectures. The exams are definitely harder than homeworks, make sure you practice the review. Even though problems may seem easy, but there is a very high probability of making mistakes.

Course was competently taught, and most concepts (other than ones we did not need to focus on) were handled with care and given ample intuition and practice through homeworks. Exams are also simply procedures from HWs, with some curveballs to test whether you truly understand. Main issue was unclear instructions from TAs on HWs and labs.

OZG knows what's up. An incredible introduction to the CMPEN degree. The TAs are kinda bad at grading, but they do their best to make corrections when you push them to. Be sure to stay aware of those sneaky weekly quizes.

while most of the class is run by the ta's, oren gall is a good instructor and a really good guy. he explains things well and holds good office hours. the problem with this class is that the exams have nothing to do with the review material, which is the course coordinators fault, not the professor.

Professor Gall excels in making complex topics clear and engaging. He uses relevant examples that aid in understanding the material. The assignments and labs are well-aligned with lectures, deepening comprehension. Studying the sample exams is beneficial. With dedication, achieving a high grade is very feasible.

Professor Gall is a good teacher, he is accommodating to student's needs and will help you outside of class. The class itself is also relatively easy if you have seen the material before. However, there is something evil about selling your $300 breadboard kit to students as required material. Good professor, but I have no respect for his business.
He is fine as a professor. The tests are harder than they should be, but with some studying you will do okay.
exam questions are much harder than the homework and lecture examples, and the question type never appeared before

The professor is nice but the tests are insanely long and hard, some design projects are confusing and ambiguously worded too. Don't bother emailing him, he won't respond. Make sure you go to the office hours if you have ANY doubts. Prepare VERY well for the tests go to the office hours for the design projects and you should be good. GO TO CLASS!
No comments needed. Dr Gall is one of the few professors that actually cares about the success of every single student.
I can not stress enough how good he is. Just take the class. Show up and do the work and you will do amazing.
Dr Gall is an amazing lecturer. G-d damn best professor. Do yourself a favor and take his class

Gives extra credit 
is accessible outside class
Teaches pretty good
is very caring, nice and helpful
Is very smart guy
I love Dr Gall. Take his class. You won't regret. Amazing guy that cares about his students
Dr Gall is a gem for this school. I was so lucky I was able to have him for this course. I improved so much and all the hard work paid off !
Dr Gall is amazing. Excellent professor. He knows what he is talking about.

It is impossible to do bad in his class as long as you put the effort. He is there for you. He is so inspiring and caring. This class motivated me to do better in my other classes as well. Dr Gal is really amazing and helpful.
I love Dr Gall. This class is worth the hard work. At the end, you will be so happy and proud.

Class participation actually helped me remember the concepts and do well on the exam because when you talk to him about the topics one on one everything starts to click in your head and made the exam much easier. Make sure you participate in the class conversation. He doesn't judge and he will help you understand things better. He gets you thinking

I usually struggle a lot with my classes but I was going just fine in Dr Gall class mainly because he explains the concepts in a way that you get it. He really breaks it down and repeats the concepts. grading is clear on the syllabus. Includes extra credit opportunities in case you needed a boost.

G-d I love this professor ! He is so funny. I truly enjoy this class. He teaches so well. Exams are fair and makes perfect sense. He is also super cute so its a plus lololol Just take ittttttttttttttt
I did pretty well personally in his class just listening during lectures to be honest. He is extremely sweet and respectful to all TA and students.
Exams are easy. They are not hard. I went to class and did the homework. I clarifies some topics with the TA and I also asked him for help during office hours. So, the exam made perfect sense.
He gives tons of extra credit opportunities. He wants people to do very well. All you have to do is show up to class and be willing to put the effort and do your best.

Dr Gall taught me that I have to figure out the answer to the problems and the answer is not always obvious. He taught me critical thinking. This is something that I can always use in my life and in my field to solve problems. Amazing lecturer. Very kind professor
He is super funny. He is not like average boring professors. He is so professional and knowledgable. Take his class
He is super understanding. I never had a professor as nice as him. If you show him that you are working and putting the effort, he is there for you and helps you. You can get an A if you do the work.

Dr Gall is one of the best professors I ever had. He makes the lectures crystal clear. Exams are fair and easy after just doing the homework and just attending class. He is super caring and makes himself available to students during office hours. He is so nice and helpful. I learned so much from his class. He is the best. Definitely take him.

Gall is a good professor IMO. Despite the material of the class being hard, he's very willing to offer his hand to help outside of class if his lectures don't help you fully understand the material. The TAs are also very helpful in the same sense. The lectures being posted online is also a very convenient plus.
Exams in this class aim to trick you up

Tough class with good informative lectures. Exams felt a bit unfair, given that the questions on them were always significantly more complicated than what was on practice exams. The estimated weighting of topics for the exams did not match the actual exam content at all. Be sure to study EVERYTHING before exams, not just the most weighted topics.

Hides bad teaching and unfair exams with a curve. Made the class somehow harder this semester. Exams are very unfair, practice exams given are much easier than the real exam. On actual exams, you will be given problems you have never seen and are expected to know the question and finish it correctly within time frame. Too many questions on exams.

Gall is a nice guy and cares about his student but he is not made for lecturing; watch the recordings on 2x speed thank me later. Gives some good opportunities for extra credit and curves the final grades very heavily, so it is still pretty easy to do well if you put the effort in.

Gall is a nice professor, but what's horrible in this class is his graders. They are utterly lazy and irresponsible. I needed to regrade my midterms every time and each time, I got 5+ credits back Imao. What a joke!

I took his class last semester. His lectures were amazing as he was very excited on the material he teaches to the students. VL every Friday is very nice. Labs and design projects aren't bad if you pay attention. Tests are the hardest part of this class, ngl. He did curve heavily at the end though. Cutoff for A: 89 and Cutoff for C: 59

Not the best professor out there as his explanations aren't good, but the class is heavily curved and there are a lot of resources available online, mainly on youtube. Office hours are a must as he always manages to have good TAs and LAs. Overall not the best, but gets the job done.
He's obviously very passionate about what he teaches and wants everyone to do well in the class. Class lectures aren't a snooze fest and the projects really help you understand the material.

I took Professor Gall's class in Fall 2017.
Difficult class can't deny it, however, Professor Gall is always there for you if you ask questions and visit his office hours.
I also took and passed the FE exam thanks for his advice.

Professor Gall gives great lectures. They may be a bit hard to follow, but I recommend watching the recordings when doing homework. The design projects are interesting, and I highly recommend going to office hours to get help early. Also, do the optional homework if you want to do well on the exams!!!
Exams are painful....hate hate hate.
Exam takes weeks to be graded.

I learned a lot from this class, the professor teaches the course material really well and takes what the students do outside of class into consideration a lot. He has done online video lectures every Friday and sometimes ends the class early for us to do our projects or to student which I have found very helpful.

Very warm and jubilant personality. Loved going to lectures because he actually sounded excited about what he was teaching. Lectures were very clear and easy to understand. The only negatives were that he was hard to contact through email and the tests were very hard. Although, he curved generously.

Gall is an amazing and enthusiastic professor who always tries to make the topic fun and enjoys helping his students. you don't have to attend and can watch lectures over zoom but its inconvenient and I don't recommend it. VL every Friday is also a nice add on too. The grading he does is also super kind and makes getting an A much more feasible.

Recorded Friday lectures are the only good lectures in my opinion but its still smart to go to class. Gall is one of those guys who is very nice, great at office hours and in online lectures but in person lectures leave you wondering what just happened. Do the homework and you'll be fine for exams. I can promise you wont get them graded for a month

The course leans toward the easier side; although, it becomes a little rigorous once sequential circuits is introduced. To do well on the exams, know how to do all the HW and complete all the practice exams given. Design projects were doable. Friday recorded lectures are better than Oren's in-person lectures. Go to office hours if you need help.

He is a nice person and cares about his students. His lecture slides are clear for the most part, but as time goes on he becomes unclear when teaching. This is not much of a problem if you keep up with lectures. The homework, labs, and quizzes are very helpful in teaching the material.

As long as you understand the material and can do the homework through comprehension, the class is very straightforward and easy. The exams are just past homework problems and the exact same questions as the review (especially the conceptual questions), so going to class or lab isn't exactly necessary, especially since the lab can be done at home.

Professor Gall is a good teacher who does his best to be fair and engaging. Exams are rough, design projects are to the point and only difficult if you don't pay attention, and homework is due every week... I recommend going to class. Friday classes are video lectures, so that's nice. Lots of available office hours. Study for those exams tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was clear and recordings were available online, making studying easy. Lots of examples given in slides (also provided in modules) and he explains concepts very well. TA's and Dr. Gall very accessible outside of class. Though the class is difficult, Dr, Gall makes it as easy as it can be.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: This class and professor were very helpful in building the foundations of computer science and engineering.

Overall decent professor. Lectures covered most of the material fairly, although some outside reading and help may be required. Exams are quite difficult, but usually doing and understanding the practice exams is sufficient for a C on the exam. Projects can take a long time to complete, too. He curves VERY HEAVILY. A C was a 57 this semester!

Lectures are boring, but they are all recorded. Lot of content to cover because it's a fundamental class, so I don't blame him for going fast. He curves the course by a lot (only need 86-87% for an A) and drops lowest HW/labs so your grade won't tank. Make sure to carefully review assignments for regrades because the TA's WILL mess up grading.

Lectures can sometimes be boring and slow, exams are very tough, but material is understandable and Gall is easy to reach outside of class. As long as you pay attention in class you should be fine. He normally applies a huge curve at the end of the semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a very nice professor that I have a lot of respect for. However, the grading by some of the TAs is a nightmare. I failed the first two homeworks (even though I got everything correct) because I did not select the right pages on Gradescope which tanked my grade. On exams, there were times that I got points off even though I got the same as key
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: follow instruction and will be good

He is such a nice guy, and he will try his best to save your grade. I got 82.3 at the end of the semester, and he boost me to an A-. I truly think I do not deserve this grade, but he thinks I do. Super nice guy. Take his class!!!!
Best professor among all the CMPEN classes I have taken so far.

Dr. Gall is one of the most supportive professors I have ever met at Penn State. He gave us lots of activities to do in the classroom and great experiments in labs which helped me REALLY understand what I was doing. I really appreciated the way the professor was always there after class to answer questions and always responded to my e-mails.

Professor Gall is fine, but most of the problem is in how the class grading system. You will be dealing with TAs 98% of the time, and I find none of them to be very reachable and responsive when it comes to grading. The graders give no forgiveness for minor errors so get ready to meet the professor every week to tell the grade to correct them.

As a professor, he's alright. Lectures were recorded so you could always go back and watch them. Too bad none of that matters when the homework assignments are 100 times harder than what is done in lecture. And it's graded on accuracy with no forgiveness for slight errors. Tests are do-able. Textbook is a joke, google is your friend in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I found CMPEN 270 to be a great and fair class. It wasn't easy, but anybody could succeed in this class if they studied the given material well. The design projects helped me learn a lot about the subject, and the tests were not harder than anything we went over in class. Overall, if you studied and put in effort, you did well.

Spends way too much time telling jokes and having "discussions" where we talk about very arbitrary topics during lectures. Then, he skims over important concepts that you would actually need to know for the homework and tests. Design projects had unclear instructions.

His class was a mess. The professor is too cold and cant manage this course. The grading isnt consistent on exams and homeworks and they take time to grade them. Also the course grading wasnt scaled heavily as in past semesters. The exams were harder than past exams and we had 3 projects.

He definitely tried his best to do it online, and I found lectures to be great (I found his jokes ironically funny and those made the lectures so much better). He curved fine imo. However, the labs were absolutely terrible, we had to teach ourselves how to do them and were at the mercy of TA's to give us answers.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Hilarious

reviews.comment: You don't have much of a choice on who you take this class with, but I thought he did a decent job overall. Sometimes his jokes were definite misses, other times I thought he was pretty amusing, it was a mixed bag. Only actual bad thing about him is that he can't seem to motivate his TAs to grade anything/organize labs properly.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The course is difficult by nature, 3 exams count for 75% of the grade, all other activities count for the last 25%. Professor Gall's lectures are very informative and detailed, and he is very accessible for students. To succeed in this class you need to keep up with the material, as it all builds on itself. Do not be afraid to ask questions.

Oren comes across as a lazy professor in the way he has the class set up and the way he goes through the material. Seems like he has no communication with the TA's throughout the semester. It takes weeks to get assignments graded. Needed to learn Verilog completely on my own for labs. Unclear terms for grading and weighting scale. Not a fun class.

My main issue with Oren is his inability to properly manage, set grading standards, and pressure his TAs to do their job. The TAs frequently take several weeks to grade homework. The exams were written by the 'head' TA who made them vry difficult and disorganized, and we have to TEACH OURSELVES Verilog, a notoriously difficult programming language.

Teacher is awesome, main complaint are the TA's. Often grade incorrectly, take weeks to grade assignments, one TA missed or postponed nearly every study session they hosted, etc. On the first test half the class failed. The teacher is funny, caring, and willing to work with the students but the TA's seriously ruined the class for me.

Dr. Gall is a funny, easy-going guy. Very accessible to questions in office hours and immediately after class. The material can be difficult and tricky, but Dr. Gall's lectures are pretty straightforward about what you need to know. The exams did have a tendency to be difficult and the labs were not organized in the best way possible.

Gall makes tons of lame jokes, but they still manage to spice up his lectures. He teaches decently, though his handwriting is atrocious. Doing HW is crucial for doing well on exams; the 2nd midterm is especially hard. He curves generously. However, his TA/LA team often contradicts itself and makes grading errors.

Dr. Gall is a real stand up guy. I enjoyed both his humor and his lecture. These will be the main way that you are exposed to the class material and the HW is how you actually learn it. Exams are quite difficult tbh, but curved usually. The labs suck and have nothing to due with the rest of the class. Overall, this class was hard, but fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Curves grades after each exam, but exams are extremely difficult unless you really know the material. He tries to be funny but isn't, and TA's/LA's are inconsistent with grading. Also, if you don't know verilog going into the class you are screwed because half the semester's labs are done in verilog but he does not give instruction on how to code.
Dr. Gall is a great lecturer, and he really cares about his material. Definitely would take this class again. Online lectures weren't bad either.

Dr. Gall isn't a great lecturer, but he wants you to succeed. Exams were curved heavily, and so was the overall course grading scale. Here's how you succeed in this class: Take time to do the homework without using the internet, and go to all possible office hours. If you do the above, you should end up with a decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Gall was a great professors. The hw was very challenging compared to lecture but it prepared you well for exams. Taking advantage of hw help sessions from HKN that he promoted helped me tremendously. Gall was easy to work with, really nice guy, good lectures, video lecture to miss Friday class was great. An A ended up being an 88 and that was easy

Professor Gall is a pretty decent professor. Video lectures are super important. You have to listen to every word that he says in his videos because you will be surprised by how many tiny topics you will be tested. One of the exams is harder than the other two. The in-person lecture is useless, and the focus should be all targeted towards videos
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Gall is nice and caring as a person, but his lectures are not helpful at all and will not prepare you for hw assignments, let alone midterms and final. His way of changing 2/3 of the in-person lectures each week to online is not helpful, although I get that he wants to use those times for extended office hours. Nice person but terrible lecturer
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He's a really caring guy that will curve grades to your benefit. He really will go into detail about anything you have trouble with. He also has a lot of LAs that are extremely helpful. He creates exams very close to practice tests so it is not hard to do well. Recommend

Oren Gall is a solid professor, for an introductory computer engineering course he does a great job explaining things. My only gripe with him would be I emailed him twice throughout the semester and both times he ghosted me.

Awesome guy his lectures were very good but not mandatory. Video lectures every Friday instead of in person class. Just study and do the practice exams and youll get a good grade. There was a generous curve in my semester. He really cares about you learning the material and is an overall great guy.
Good guy, understands well, teaches well, very very polite and kind.
he srsly is a GOAT. his lecture videos are awesome. one of the very few, good cmpeng/cmpsci professors at PSU

Oren is the best guy ever! He really cares about his students and if you put in the right efforts, this class is not that bad. The LA office hours are the best bet to actually learn the material in the class.

I didn't find his office hours as helpful as everyone else is saying, but I did find the LA office hours very helpful. If you do well on the HWs, you'll do well in the midterms and final. The optional HWs before the midterms are VERY helpful so remember to make time for them! MT2 is definitely harder than MT1, but totally manageable

Great guy. Understands the material very well and is pretty decent at explaining it. The class however was very time consuming and sometimes felt too abstract and pointless. Office hours will save your life in this course 1 on 1 time with him is worth your weight in gold.
Great class. You will learn a lot with some initiative and practice. Don't expect too much hand-holding, but office hours/help is available and very useful. LA's are awesome too.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Oren's lectures weren't very informative, honestly I wouldn't bother attending. The labs also didn't really teach information helpful to the class. The biggest part is the homework, if you do that well each week then you should be fine for the exams.

Oren was a good professor and a great guy. He generally explained material well, and allowed students to ask questions in class. First midterm and the final weren't bad, but the second midterm was tough. I didn't use the textbook once --do not buy it.

I did not find Oren's lectures to be very useful throughout the semester. You are probably going to be better off turning to an online resource and using it to work through homework. Labs aren't that bad, but Oren doesn't really keep in touch with his TAs about them, so there are some inconsistencies. Not a fun class.

He is good at explaining the conceptual material, but his lectures are lacking solid examples that you would see on an exam. Exams can be difficult be there is a curve. TA office hours are the best bet for homeworks. Labs are easy but pointless. He is not good at announcing important info and he can be very short in emails asking for clarification.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a great guy with a strong background, however some of the material was not explained well in lecture. The labs are not to bad, but the homework can take ages to complete. The exams were not too challenging, depending if you got a firm grip on the material.
The professor is very sweet but you won't learn much in class. The homeworks take forever to do and the exams are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Oren is a very nice and friendly guy, but his lectures are very vague and do not help you in the scheme of things. The only learning done in this course is from the homework and exam solutions that are posted. Wouldnt have done well at all without them. Also takes forever for anything to get graded.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Oren is a likable guy and his lectures are straightforward, however they moved too slow for me and I would lose focus, making it hard for me to benefit from them. But if the pace is okay, then they're really helpful and clear. Exams are difficult, but he curves really fairly. Do they homework and get help to understand it and you'll be good.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: One of the best teachers I've ever had. Exams are pretty hard especially the final but all of them were given high curves. Must take notes in class as he only puts slides online but writes on them in class. HW takes a while but teaches u pretty well. I ended up skipping a bunch of classes, not going to OH, but still easy A.

Some of the people really don't prefer him and I honestly don't understand why. My friends warned me before taking this class but I honestly had a great time with it. He's pretty good with the lectures. Exam 1 was pretty easy. But exam 2 honestly was tough. I'd suggest you to prepare well and get your concepts super clear. Not as hard to score an A
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: CMPEN 270 is constructed so that there are office hours,  labs, or class from like 9-5 every week day, so getting help isn't tough at all. It's basically all binary code, so if you're good with finding patterns and using the techniques he demonstrates in class, it's a very obtainable A

Friendly, but bad at lecturing. It's only his second semester teaching, so I think he'll improve. Speaks perfect English. His slides are not complete, so you must take notes if you want to reference lecture slides to study/do homework. Material is hard to find online, so take notes. Allegedly, he curves the class heavily at the end. Exams are hard.
flexible grading scales

This guy's lectures are solid. Clear examples, time to ask questions (none are dumb), and he goes at a steady pace. Anything you might not understand gets cleared up in HW and OH. Exams have curveballs in them (long af, questions may seem ridiculous at first), but he curves A LOT. Labs are dumb, but just finish them and don't worry too much.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: When I took his class it was his first time teaching it, so there were organizational problems that made it difficult. But f you read the textbook you should be fine, plus he had a pretty good curve. He really cares and is helpful if you go to office hours. When I took it, the course was a little frustrating, but I think it will improve.

Genuinely the nicest professor I've met at Penn State. Really tries hard to make sure everybody (who tries) does well. Lectures can be a little dry, but he's a huge help in office hours and the exams are usually easier than the often challenging homework. That said, start your homework early. The concepts are new and you'll want office hours help.

I'm not sure that last student was very motivated.  The homework is long and also challenging, and that's how it should be.  I just took the first exam and felt VERY prepared.  This course is not so bad if you're willing to work hard (welcome to engineering).

He is very bad at explaining, not the best professor in lectures. The homework is super long and better off learning on your own. CmPen students have it better since they have labs, for CmpSc not so much.

Dr. Packer is one of the professors that makes you want to go back to school and easily one of the most knowledgeable people I've ever been around. 3 essays, very difficult to clear a C. Remember you're in college to learn, not just for GPA. In a Packer class, you will learn to think of the world in a unique way that many others will never get to.

This is not a 1st-year or even 2nd-year level class. Professor Packer does a great job of covering content in a way that forces his students to interact with the content and lecture which is new for many. He will not spoon-feed you the answers or make a neat powerpoint for you to copy and paste later. Taking active notes and participating is big.

. Harshest grader I have ever seen. Highest grade in the class was a B-. About a 3rd of the class dropped if not more. He is also super unfriendly, demeaning towards students and doesn't answer emails. Stay away if possible.

Not only is even the single hardest greater I've ever seen. He also gives the worst instructions as well. He is down right mean too. You won't learn anything in this class unless you teach yourself. He is a waste of time and sanity. Do not take any of his classes. Pretty much every student agrees he should be fired.

This class is a very challenging class, but Dr. Packer does his best to get us to understand. There is 3 1900 word essays which are graded very strictly,  but if you want to actually learn something from a political science class this is the class to go.

reviews.comment: Professor Packer is not only one of the most egotistical professors I've ever met, but one of the most insufferable and disgustingly haughty for someone who's job is to educated students who are learning material for the first time. He is impossible to please and is extremely degrading. I hope one day he's fired in the worst way possible.

reviews.comment: As a Dean's list you'd assume I could get higher than a C on my papers but no. Never saw a grade higher than a C everyone gets D's or Fs. Worse teacher I have ever seen. He is also incredibly rude to his students. The fact the Penn state hasn't fired him blows my mind.

Almost half the class dropped the other half got C's and below. The devil works hard but Robert packer works harder.
In all seriousness don't take any of his classes. He is probably the worst professor in the country and I am not exaggerating. Most people get a D in his classes. He's just a horrible professor.

Do not take this course under ANY circumstance. Pain and despair is all you will feel in this class, with it being IMPOSSIBLE to get above a B on any paper (most of the time receiving much less). If you don't have a religion, GET ONE and pray.

reviews.comment: Attending every class can get you a D in participation. His grading is unfair and his directions are so vague. If you want to talk you have to attend office hours where he will demean you.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'm a Dean's List student and got a D in my paper, and my academic advisor tell me this is "normal" for his class. as a senior I have taken many courses with strict professors and ended up with good grades, but the problem of Packer is that his strictness is not to push student to succeed but rather to fulfill his personal ego.
I love dr packer but his essay gradings are way too harsh

As a pre-med major, I have never felt that a class was so unfair. His directions are vague and even contradictory, and if you have a question, he will rudely brush you off. He refuses to answer emails and grades harder than any professor in state college. Stay away!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you're reading this, this is your warning. I wish someone would've warned me. This is the worst class ever.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This was the absolute worst class and professor I have ever taken and had. Graded by 3 papers and attendance. He graded my papers so harshly and didn't give me them back until 2 weeks before school ended. He was also so rude in his comments and would never respond to emails. PLEASE AVOID IF U CAN.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS!!!!! You might think you can "beat" the system and get a good grade, but you can't! He literally just rambles the entire time. There are no lecture slides, no notes—nothing to follow along with. Every class, he asks students to remind him where he left off. It's completely disorganized and frustrating.
Clearly knows what he is talking about but is not able to trach it!

Took him PLSC 442. His lectures could sometimes be dry but he explained everything you needed to know for the essays. The class was 3 take home essays about 2000 words. Attendence was also graded. Every essay he assigned he also gave an outline with that explained everything you needed to cover. Took a long time grade but still a good class.

Packer is the WORST professor I have ever taken. ZERO guidelines or structure to the course, no feedback, unnecessarily hard grader. Didn't give me ANY of my grades back until the last week of class and ignored all my emails requesting them over weeks. Very rude to his students and speaks down on people who do feel brave enough to speak in class.

This class with Professor Packer is no easy feat, but if you're up for a challenge, it's worth it. The workload is intense, but using tools like unstuck study alongside the lectures can really help. Stay on top of the essays and you'll learn a ton.

Dr.Packer is one of the smartest men I have ever met. However, I think he fails to recognize that his students are studying these topics for the very first time. He is not very receptive to questions and his tone is very condescending if you do not understand the concept the first time around.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The grade is based on attendence, which if you don't email you lose 1/3 of your attendence points. As well as three 1800 word essays, which do not have concrete guidelines or grading criteria. Syllabus didn't have due dates for any of the essays, he just pulled out the pdf assignment one day and said its due in a week.

reviews.comment: Don't take don't take don't take. Unless you already know everything on the subject he's talking about this class is not for you. The grade consists of attendance and 3 1800-word essays. Save yourself.
Took a third of my grade for one wrong citation

reviews.comment: He is a very intelligent man, but an extremely tough professor. He is the hardest grader at this college and also gives zero feedback. Your entire grade is only based on 3 1800-word essays that are graded so hard. If you fail the first one (most do) it is impossible to come back.

Avoid classes with him if at all possible. He never responded to emails when inquiring about my paper. Very vague about what he expects but then absolutely destroys your paper. Hard to come back from a D on the first essay exam when there are only three grades. You do not learn useful information in class and it is a waste of time
