Dr. Packer is a very knowledgeable academic, this does not equate to being a good professor. True to the word lecturing is all class is, with expert-level knowledge of all world events seems to be expected. Seemingly no structure to what may be covered in class, and only vague explanation of expectations for his exams. Good luck.

ALL THE RUMORS ARE TRUE - LIZZO,

No rubric or clear expectations for assignments. He expects all of his students to know everything already and doesn't actually teach it to you. do not take his class.
This is the worst professor at Penn State. Condescending and expects everyone to know everything about the world. Should stop teaching and work for as a political analyst.

impossible class. extremely hard grader, leaves no useable feedback if any. lectures are him rambling off hundreds of years of history then is condescending when the class can't answer his questions even though he doesn't actually teach any terms or concepts. I'm expecting to fail this class just don't take it man its horrid

reviews.comment: Packer is an incredibly intelligent man and he has a real way of thing course content to the real world, but he often gets caught up in tangents making class hard to follow at times.

Do not take this class unless you want a GPA drop. It is graded off three papers and he does not give constructive feedback. IN fact, his feedback is rather rude and he does not offer help. Lectures are based off his own notes and are not helpful. I have been a great writer my whole academic career and he gave me D's with NO feedback to go off of.

This class was extremely difficult and it did not help that Professor Packer was extremely slow in giving feedback along with responding to emails and answering questions. It felt like we were completely left on our own to work through very difficult course material. Would not recommend taking one of his classes.

I personally liked his class a lot. He was an extremely hard grader, but as long as you go to his office hours and asked for clarification on things you did not fully understand then you'll be alright. If he gives you the ability to get your outline checked, DO IT. Make it as detailed as possible and he'll tell you what to fix and what to take off.
This class will make you wonder if you're mentally retarded.

The man is a straight up encyclopedia. Will ramble off exact dates of any treaty like its nothing. But he is one of the professors who are too smart to convey information to students. Will grade your papers as if your in your last year of law school. Save yourself the stress and your GPA. Take someone else!!!

AVOID!

reviews.comment: If you want to learn anything useful or interesting, do not take this class. If you want to maintain a good GPA, do not take this class. If you want to listen to the incoherent ramblings of a man whose personal attributes cannot be adequately described without the use of derogatory terms (as forbidden by RMP) - by all means, take this class.

Robert Packer is the worst professor I've ever dealt with at Penn State. He gave zero constructive feedback on papers (which are the only assignments) and belittle any argument we tried to piece together based on vague and incoherent prompts. He doesn't respond to emails nor listen to students. Please save yourself, do not take a class with him.

I hate this man. So much.

reviews.comment: You will never see the tougher grading than him. I dont know if its my own problem but I cant accept this way of teaching. This man just reads off the word docs and takes notes in the ZOOM Chat. THE MOST BORING AND THE HARDEST CLASS I HAVE EVER TAKE. Please DON'T take any courses he teaches.

I hate this man. I am taking his class for the second time, but not by choice. I have never hated a professor as much as him. He teaches the class as if we are all PhD graduates. He is an extremely tough grader and its nearly impossible to pass his class. if you have any other option, DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS !!!!

reviews.comment: Any class taught by Packer is going to be your worst nightmare. Prepare for the most boring lectures of your life followed by working on papers for weeks just to get C's and D's. He is very smart but condescending towards students and grades undergraduate students as if they are going for a Ph.D. Stay away from any class that he teaches, seriously.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This professor grades HARD. He has ridiculous expectations for undergrad students and grades solely off three take-home essay exams. Gives students nothing over a B and most classmates received Cs and Ds on exams. If you dont have to, do not take this class! He also did not give any leniency because of COVID if you had technical issues!!!!!!!!!!

Was my professor for POLISCI438. Professor was extremely harsh when grading papers. Left rude comments that were not helpful and had unreasonable expectations for our papers. Was not lenient with technology issues and took off points for very inappropriate reasons even with COVID circumstances. Only lecturing, nothing else. Hard to stay focused.

Professor Packer is insanely knowledgeable about foreign affairs. The man is a living encyclopedia. However his classes are impossible. Your grade is 3 papers which nobody will get above a B on and expect most people to get Cs and D plus. His lectures are insanely boring and his essay prompts are insane. If you can take any other course do it.

He is the WORST professor I've had at Penn State. He reads off of a Word document for his class lectures and is likely the most boring professor I've ever listened to. But his lectures aren't even the worst part. His grading is unrealistically tough. On the 3 essays we had, his expectations were well beyond those explicitly asked in the prompts.

Not going to sugar coat it- if youre not passionate about the class or poli sci in general, youre going to struggle. Tough grader but can give you plenty of feedback before the essay is due to bump it up. Go to office hours and write down as much as possible
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Packer is one of the best international politics professors I had in my life in terms of lectures. He is deeply knowledgeable in his field and teaches the class fairly well. HOWEVER, he grades you based only on 3 take-home essay exams, which nobody gets better than a B. If you want to get a good grade STAY AWAY from him. x

reviews.comment: Professor Packer is the smartest teacher I ever had. His knowledge of international politics is absolutely impressive. However, this is, without a doubt, the hardest first-year seminar you can choose. There are 3 papers and attendance. A great paper will get a B, a good one will get a C. If you are not into politics, run.

I have to start by dispelling a lot of the reviews here. If you come to office hours and ask the right questions, as well as don't wait till the last minute to start the essay exams, will you will do well! Rely on in-class notes as your sources on the essays, follow his arguments, reiterate and examine his arguments on paper, and you will be fine.

Packer is probably the best professor I had at Penn State. He is an encyclopedia on history and politics. He is a tough grader. Camp in his office hours and you will learn a lot and likely earn above a C. Don't take his class expecting an easy A, because you won't get it. Take his class if you want to learn, and you will. Packer doesn't mess around

Professor Packer is really smart and his classes will teach you a ton. The problem is you're graded on three exams, and you won't do anywhere near well on them unless you do to office hours. Between the first two exams he gave out a single A-. Additionally, the topics for these essays are extremely difficult to understand.

reviews.comment: Dr. Packer has been getting a lot of hate on here for being a tough grader and challenging his students. Fight for feedback and go to office hours; you'll learn!

This is the only first year seminar I've seen where people consistently fail.

Save yourself the trouble. Packer is a horrible professor. Lectures consist of him reading directly off the notes, asking random/obscure questions, then acting surprised when nobody knows the answers. reviews.comment: Not professional at all. Found his lecture notes that are supposedly 'written by him', online under another author's name. He's incredibly knowledgeable but expects everyone to be at his level and doesn't give straight answers to questions. The entire grade came from 3 essays, which were essentially summaries of his class lectures & personal opinions. Prepare to get Ds and Fs on his essay exams, I have heard him make fun of students before for the questions they ask. He is awful, PSU should be ashamed that they have him on their payroll.
If you want a good grade. do not take this class. He grades based off of three take-home essays that nobody gets higher than a C on. He only holds office hours on Friday in the middle of the day.

Professor Packer is the worst instructor I have ever had. His classes consist of him asking obscure questions about various historical events and mocking the class for not knowing the answer. Also, if you spend six hours or six days on a paper, it will not make a difference. He grades harshly to the point of absurdity.

DONT TAKE!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Where to begin? He can't be  a professor. Yes he is smart. Yes he is knowledgeable. but if you go to his office hours, you are guaranteed a lower grade in the next exam. I know that doesn't make sense but ever since i have asked him questions in his office hours, i have gotten lower grades!!!

He's been my favorite teacher so far! Very interesting lectures, and he knows pretty much everything. If your are engaged in the lectures your fine. I have learned a lot from him and he's the reason why I love talking about War and international politics

Dr. Packer is a brilliant man and knows everything there is to know about world history but can be a bit dry. You certainly have to be interested in the topic to enjoy class. You are graded on three essays that are fairly in depth but if you can write half-decent and don't mind reading a little, you will be fine. Attendance never is taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Packer is very unwilling to help his students. If you ask a question whether its during class or in office hours he will let you squirm and scramble to explain to him what you need help with, and will offer help in the form of useless "clues" and tell you to figure it out. Didn't take attendance a single time throughout semester.
Packer is very smart, but does not know how to teach what he knows. He doesn't break anything down. It's too bad because I was interested in the material. Very boring, complicated lectures.

I learned SO much from Dr. Packer. He truly is a wealth of knowledge on anything surrounding economics, politics, and international finance. His main drawback is that he is a tough grader and his grading methodology is not very clear. Go to office hours to figure out what he's looking for. But more importantly, go to class and soak up the goodness.

I know that the fact that I received a C+ in this class might make it seem as though I am bitter -- but I'm not. The grade are received was not a surprise, Dr. Packer is brilliant, yet expects you to be brilliant too. Due to this, his grading on each of your papers is hard. I put a lot of blood, sweat, and tears into this class yet still got a C+.

This class is very analyitcal.  There's a small book, and over 10 long articles you will need to devote a lot of time to reading and put in a lot of effort on your papers.  Dr Packer is a genius without question, but some people are not meant to teach. If you are really into the subject though it may be easier.

Packer takes a lot of heat on these boards, but I thought he was a great professor. Just use your notes on the essays and talk to him in office hours and you will do fine. The class is tough, but what do you expect for a 400 level class.

Dr. Packer's class will not necessarily be easy.  Most of your grade is based off of 3 strictly graded papers. However, Dr. Packer will help you during office hours.  Keep in mind though, if you didn't do the reading, pay attention in class, and read his notes, then office hours will not be helpful.

He may be a genius, but guess what? Geniuses make bad professors. Students apologize for him because he's goofy and innocent, but  at the end of the day if you want a reasonably easy A you should look elsewhere. Went to office hours 3 TIMES for a paper and got a C. I'm an A- student. Avoid the frustration it's not worth it.

This is honestly one of the best professor's I had at Penn State. I had him for PL SC 007, and now for PL SC 412. If I could take another class with him I could. I never met a teacher more intelligent and willing to help teach students . Anyone who gave him a bad review is just a freshman who does not know what they are talking about.
This class was terrible honestly for a freshman seminar. I would not suggest to take this course. He does not clarify the topics and even at office hours he is confusing.

Honestly Packer is not helpful at all. he is not punctual with the grade assignments. he literally assigned the essays and then gave us like two days to write them each time. he is highly confusing because he is too into his work. I went to his office hours as well and it wasn't helpful; he doesn't understand how to teach this subject

Came into class with high expectations. All fell with Packer. Lectures are pointless, babbling rants, goes way to fast and doesn't care about you. I don't know what realm this guy is from... Only way I learned was from writing the papers where I learned myself.He's a love or hate prof, definitely hated his unorganized/sporadic way of "teaching"

Yes, your Packer class will be extremely hard, but he will make sure you understand it. Show up to class, take notes, do your 3 essays, and go to office hours. Taking my 3rd class in 4 semesters with him...if you love the subject he will just encourage you even more. Never learned so much in my life, but you're going to have to work for the grade.

Packer may have boring lectures but he is a genius that can really challenge your thinking if you pay attention. I never read or went to the TAs but just went to class and got an A. All you need are his slides and if you have half a brain and can write you'll be fine.

incredibly boring lectures. i was interested in the subject matter and could not ever remained focused on what he was saying. he chooses to go over extremely dense stuff. i didnt go to class after awhile and still got a b. the TAs were extremely difficult graders in my class but theyll raise your grade if you visit with them afterwards.

Robert Packer is by far the worst professor I have had in my experience at Penn State thus far. As an honors student and political science major I anticipated this class to be easy (like all my other intro level poli sci) it was not and worst of all it was utterly boring. It's too bad he has tenure because this man should be fired right on the spot

Only 3 Exams & attendance quizzes determine your final grade. TA's grade your paper-somewhat flexible with changing grades. LOTS OF READING-but I only did reading for the specific essay exam questions and still got an A. How to get an A? Go to office hours religiously(Talk to TA & Professor about clarifications)& study group to discuss questions.

Very challenging and essay questions can be quite confusing. Take notes in class and GO TO HIS OFFICE HOURS and do not procrastinate. Tough but possible to get an A and very possible to get a B. Were only 3 essay/exam questions and 1 quiz. Do the readings he assigns though. Don't take the class if you aren't interested in the subject.

Extremely hard grader, but if you go to him for help he'll do his best to assist you. The TAs grade your papers, so it's up in the air on how hard they'll be. Unfortunately for my class they're insufferably difficult and love to give people Cs and lower. You can always argue your grade with Packer (TAs gave me and F and he bumped it to a B).
He is terribly boring and has no interest in helping the students. Prefers to show off his own knowledge rather than make sure the students understood what he was "teaching."

I had absolutely no experience in International Political Economy before I came to the class, and although it was the most difficult class I had ever taken, I earned an A and I learned so much! Packer is so nice and willing to help (go to his office hours!) One of my favorite classes and favorite professors. Take on the challenge!

Though I got an A-, I had no idea what was going on.  It's easy to get lost, but you can use his notes on angel to write the take-home essay exams.  The TA's grade the papers. They're pretty easy graders if you include everything.  This class is hard, but do-able.  I failed every single quiz, and still got an A-, so no worries there.

Probably the hardest class I've ever taken. I had absolutely no experience in economics prior to taking this class. I struggled a lot and barely pulled off a B. Though I disagree with his tough grading and high expectations, I have to admit I've never learned more in a single class than I have in this one.
He is a genius, which makes his class hard. He grades very harshly.

I am an International Politics major and he definetely made me loose interest in the topic. His lectures are really boring and he makes no effort into keeping us interested. There are no exams, just 3 papers but they are very hard and most people are clueless by the time we have to start the paper.

Don't believe *everything* you read here. Yes his exams are very subjective, yes he reads right off his Word document slides, but as long as you basically do the readings as clarification of the lectures you'll do fine. I didn't do the readings at all except the week of the exams and still managed a B. I would take it again if given the chance.

I have Professor Packer for Turbulence and Arab Israeli conflict.  The fact of the matter is as follows; if you are interested in pursuing IR in any way shape or form, take professor Packers classes. Everyone says he is a bad teacher but he pushes you to learn more than any other professor will.  Pursuit of Knowledge here.....
Really hard class, he's a hard grader. 3 papers no exams but the papers are really hard!
Not a good Professor for an Intro-level course and leaves too much to often unfair TAs. Expects around 100 pages per week of reading for a 0 level course. Very knowledgable though.

Packer's a genius, but explains nothing.  He reads notes word for word off of a powerpoint. His TAs grade the 3 essays that determine your whole grade, which sucks if the TAs are unfair.  In my class A-K always had MUCH lower grades that L-Z.

Not *as* bad as everyone here says. Three papers, graded by TAs. Occasional quizzes really only taken for attendance and if your average is high he'll bump you up a letter grade. Just string the notes and readings into an essay and pray to whatever deity you believe in that the TAs are fair graders, and it's a fairly easy A. DON'T BUY THE BOOK!!!
He should NOT be teaching an intro level course. Like others have said, he's very smart but he's not a very good teacher.

He's nice to talk to one-on-one, but he is NOT a good teacher for a 014 level class! He's VERY smart, but does more bragging than teaching. IF you can avoid this class do. But it also depends on your writing abilities because it is just THREE essays and if you have good TA's, you'll be fine. ADVICE: Try to bond with your TAs. (They are the ones gra

Packer is brilliant, but he teaches way above gen ed level. He expects students to have background knowledge in the subject, and he doesn't explain his notes. He just reads through them and expects you to get it. The grade is mostly based on three essays, so if you're struggling, you're screwed. Don't take it unless you have a love for IR.

Smart guy, terrible teacher. Class is hideously disorganized, and just because he knows details about every single war ever fought since the beginning of time doesn't mean everybody else does. Would make an outstanding grad school professor, but really shouldn't be teaching undergrads, especially as an introductory course.

Most unorganized class I have ever taken. He is incredibly intelligent, but isn't a good teacher. Also he expects you to have background information that shouldn't be required for an introductory course.

Packer is extremely smart and has devoted his life to following both economics and polisci. That being said, he will likely make you feel dumb for asking questions and he rushes through his notes making it hard to keep up. If you can stay awake then you can learn a lot. Very hard grader. Never answers emails.

He is the most intelligent professor I have ever had at Penn State.  I took his Int'l Political Economy class and it was extremely insightful.  If you are interested in IPE or Political Science, you have to take Dr. Packer.  Is a very difficult grader though.

robert packer was so smart! his class is fun because he knows so much and loves class participation. he was also so helpful. i would def take this class again. no tests, just 3, 5-7 page papers. dont buy the book though

Confusing if you are not a plsc major. took a course of his as a first semester freshman which probably wasn't a good idea. his course, though described to be entry level, was taught with the expectation of vast international knowledge. if you can stand his ego and disorganization though, its an easy A though because of TA grading. the book helps.

No doubt Packer is a smart guy, but that was one of the most disorganized classes I've ever been in. I never knew what we were talking out, come day to day. He teaches this Intro class like everyone in it has been doing nothing else for years. I still got away with a B, but it was a painful class.

He is extremely smart, but he is also one of the most pretentious I have ever met. Its intimidating to talk to him because he makes you feel like you don't know what your talking about. He is way too broad when he lectures and he goes off topic way too often. Don't take his class.

Robert Packer was one of the best professors I had this semester. He is really interesting and amazingly intelligent.I don't know what everyone else is talking about this class was not that hard. Yeah it was 3 essays, but they came straight from the notes. If you rephrase the notes into an essay you will get an A. I highly recommend PACKER!
Very Smart

He is extremely smart, though his grading is extremely harsh. He will help with questions, and attendance is not mandatory in any class. Entire grade is made up of 3 papers which are graded HARSHLY. The graduate student graders are out to simply deny any A's they can.

There is no doubt he is super smart, but the class was honestly a joke. The lectures jump around, there is no organization to the class what so over, and your grade is based off 3 papers graded by graduate students who refuse to give out A's for the most part. NOT A GOOD PROF!
He's so smart that he almost makes it hard to understand him.

if you are not a poli sci major, stay farrrr away from packer. i took this class thinking i might be interested in international relations as a major & i had 0 idea what he was talking about at any given time. he talks completely over students' heads, has no structured lecture material & is a pompous ass. how this is an intro class is beyond me

By far the smartest teacher I have ever had at Penn State. Im a Poli Sci major and I thoroughly enjoyed the class. He knows more about the subject matter than you could possibly imagine. As for people saying he should teach grad school, don't you want your professors to be intelligent so as to make you even more intelligent?
awful. avoid this class and this professor.  His lectures are ridiculous and he should not be teaching undergrads.  very smart man, but simply can not teach.

He is a pedant and a fool.  He thinks he is incredibly intelligent and yet he cannot understand the extremely simple concepts involved in teaching a class.  He gives essay exams, but don't be fooled, he doesn't want an essay (as in an academic paper with a thesis and support), he wants you to simply parrot back everything he said in class.

He teaches waay over students heads and spams your inbox daily with articles. I'm an international relations major with a concentration in economics and I thought this class was awful. I went to office hours several times and still couldn't explain things clearly. He's strictly an academic who should be teaching grad school.
Boring lectures, unfair grading, unorganized, know-it-all attitude..what more do you need to know? good part is he doesn't expect a lot of work.

This professor gives you the worst of both worlds. On one hand, his lectures are boring and consist of him reading his notes off a computer--not as smart as he fancies himself. On the other hand, he grades assignments very harshly. I would avoid at all costs--there are much better professors in the department.

material is tough to understand, especially if you didn't take an intl econ class before. only 3 take home tests (essays) but they are graded hard. i was having trouble and went into his office hours and he definitely was a help. one of the most intelligent professors. bottom line, tough but fair grader, don't miss class, you miss too much info

The most knowledgeable professor I've ever had.  Material is enjoyable though difficult to understand at times.  Visit his office hours and he will be more than willing to help and is a very interesting guy to get to know.

This guy is smart but teaches WAY over students heads. Maybe he should be a Grad school prof. He has a hard time simply explaining course material and often goes off on confusing tangents. I almost immediately dropped this class.
awesome.i want his brain, he is so smart

A very nice guy however too smart to be teaching an entry level course. Talks over the students heads and expects them to know everything he knows. He will explain things better if asked but still confusing. Only 3 essays for the class however he grades them really hard and subjectively. I honestly did not understand a thing we learned in class.

smart, nice guy, but not a good teacher for a gen ed class. If you are a pl sci or history major u will be fine, but he often assumes the class knows historical/political situations that arent in the book. also there are only 3 essays the whole class, which sounds nice but grading is very subjective. would def not recommend to a non pl sci major.

Very bright man, knows the topics inside and out and delivers the information clearly. Occasionally talks over the students' heads but has no problem going over the information again and will answer any question. No textbook, but a lot of online readings. He provides his notes on the readings though.

Awesome teacher. Very intelligent. He is really clear and understandable. Also, there are no exams in his class. Only a few take home essays that you have a week to complete. Once in awhile he gives a quiz for attendance that doesn't hurt your grade. I completely recommend taking his class!
Not as bad as I thought it'd be when I seen his ratings. Pretty mid overall, he has a heavy accent and pretty bad handwriting during lectures but the work is easy.

I've been a student here for 3 years and this is the worst professor I have ever had at Penn State. If you have the choice, do NOT take him. Exams are worth like 80% of your grade and he barely even teaches anything thats on them. He also has the worst handwritting and chooses to hand-write all his slides, so good luck trying to read anything. 0/10
If you take this professor, you will lose interest in econ. hard to understand his accent.

If this is your first econ class, it will be very difficult. His lectures are long and drag on, while he is moving through content very quickly. Much learning will have to take place outside of the class. I did not have a hard time understanding him, but his handwriting on slides was messy. Much harder than any other Econ102 professor.
A little hard to understand at times but he's super nice and all of the tests are based right off the homework. He's definitely trying so if you're having trouble you just have to ask.

He is genuinely a kind/caring person, making accommodations for students throughout the semester. His accent isn't bad, but the class is very lecture heavy and can be boring. I struggled with the material and had to re-teach myself a few topics. Great guy, the format of the class was just difficult for me. Tests are based directly off homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Pecheu is very nice and understanding. That being said, he can be hard to understand at times and his lectures are very long and tend to be boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very little practice available, lectures with super messy slides and just a lot going on. Have to learn all outside of class. #WouldNOTrecommend
Professor Pecheu is probably the worst Econ102 teacher you can get. Can't speak English, writes like a 2nd grader, overall sucks, don't take him. Looking out for future students.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I don't think his accent was that bad. His lectures he just writes on his ipad and progresses through the material very quickly. I looked down at my phone for 5 minutes and I look up completely lost. If you look at the problem sets you'll be fine. Be prepared to teach yourself a lot of the content if not all of it.

He is a good guy I am sure, but his lectures are extremely difficult to follow along with and his hand writing is atrocious. He is a VERY TOUGH grade and his midterm average was a 60%. On top of his boring lectures, he fills his slides with tons of nonsense and makes it even harder to read whats going on. Plus he moves through his slides too fast.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good guy...

Vladimir is a great guy and you can tell that immediately. But the way he teaches the course is very hard to follow. The lectures lack engagement and are just him talking the entire time which isn't a big incentive to go to class. The material isn't very hard but you will be teaching yourself.

He is genuinely a great person. He cares about how his students do. However, his accent and lack of participation in lectures makes it difficult to understand the material. Reviewing the problem sets definitely helps. Going to his office hours was more helpful to me than attending the lectures, but I did both.

Professor Pecheu seems like a very kind person from going to his office hours. However, his lectures are extremely confusing and it is very hard to actually learn. His handwriting is hard to read, and he only explains concepts with complex graphs. He is also a very strict grader-- first midterm average was %60 with a small curve.
i hate this class. he's such a bad professor, you can't understand what he says. he goes so fast. all he does is talk instead of teach. don't recommend at all.
Nice guy, hard to understand. Tests are not too bad if you study.

He is a very nice professor on the humane side, but hasn't grasped that since he is French, we as a class struggled to understand him. My grade I feel has reflected the misunderstanding. He really wants to see us succeed but he has struggled to find that balance without addressing the real issue. It's so hard cause it's not his fault. HEAVY ACCENT!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is hard to understand, however, he made his midterms so they are based off of the homework. You just have to study the solutions to the homework and the class is not bad at all. Vlad is a great guy.

Very hard to understand with his accent and handwriting. He is very kind and retypes much of the study material. I takes time to relearn the subjects because content in class is confusing. But speaking with him, you can tell he is a kind person who cares about his students. The exams are difficult, and there are usually many grading errors as well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Hard to understand, study guide would just be a test outline rather than actual information, and would not prepare us well for the test. Simply every test was a guessing game, sometimes I would know a section or two, but mainly I was lost 100% of the time.

Professor Vladimir is a very flexible and caring individual. Talking to him or emailing him one-on-one shows he is a very caring teacher and happy to help. However, as a teacher, he is very difficult. He is a hard grader and his test are difficult. Lectures are hard to get through and long. I have to teach myself because I can't learn in his class.

Seems like a really good dude but I can't stand those lectures. No type of class participation and he just lectures the whole class. If you take the class, Get ready to learn most stuff by yourself. Focus on problem sets as they are the same weight as the midterms.
The worst professor I've ever taken. If you are interested in ECON take another professor, this guy will make you loose interest and get bored in lectures.

He seems like a really nice guy and is clearly really knowledgeable on international economics. I find his lectures to be very boring, as he reads from the board and writes with handwriting that is difficult to read.  There aren't very many grades. He does post his slides from class, which is really helpful if you miss.

Clearly does not care about teaching. The course is completely graded with very few pearson automatically generated assignments and tests. The pearson homework is the most tedious and irrelevant content. The tests have nothing to do with the lectures. She doesnt even show up for the exam days. The entire class uses AI, it is a joke.

Borning lectures. She just talks to herself. Exams are not directly related to lectures. You need to learn notes from former professor by yourself for exam. Participation accounts for 20% that you need to provide "quality discussion" that is very subjective. No homework. Exams are all multiple choices. 1 question lose 1% course grade.
You have to do well on both exams and the presentation.

Easiest ECON class at PSU. Sweet teacher. Just attend 10 classes and ask question in each class. No need to pay attention. Easy two mid terms with no finals. One group project with 5 people and a 5-10 min presentation. TAKE THIS CLASS.

Toughest class ever taken in terms of course material difficulty. Be prepared to do mathematical proofs MIT math majors and 160 Genius friends find challenging. However, caring professor, do the work, put in effort and you will receive a good great. She does curve! 70 > B- / 85 > A
Overall good prof for a tough subject. Show up to class as much as possible, take notes, go to office hours, and you'll be fine. Also very helpful in office hours.
Dr. Wang not as bad as people say but to do well show up to lecture, do homework, and go to office hours. Subject itself is pretty difficult so be prepared for that.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She's a minimal effort professor. She writes out all her notes in class on a blank paper and is not organized. Her homework is graded by adding points for parts completed. I would often lose points and have no idea why with no explanation. Same is true for the exams and practice exams. She tries as little as possible when teaching a class.

She is currently the only ME450 prof. If there were any other option I may recommend it, but Wang isn't as bad as some say. She is hard to understand and each class is a test of one's patience, but she doesn't make it harder than need be - online notes, straightforward tests, optional attendance. Get into the class groupme and get through it.

She does not put any lecture notes online. If you do not show up to class or do not have someone in class to give you the notes you will not have access to them. Exams are fair and similar to homework assignments. Her lectures can be boring sometimes as they are all derivations of equations found on the equation sheet for each exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: ME 555 is might be useful to study higher-level Controls.   Her lecture is way too fast. She talks fast, which is understandable, but she skips a lot of steps. She assumes you to have a very solid background in linear algebra. If you need to take it, find Jake Abbott's online lectures on Youtube.  Homework is not that tough, though.

Dr. Wang isn't always the best at explaining the things in class, but her online notes are great. The class itself wasn't too hard, but I feel like I didn't actually learn how to design control systems and what half of the concepts actually meant.
No Comments
Totally agree with the last post.  The only bright side is the notes are better than lectures and available online so you really dont have to go to class.

as unhelpful as anyother chinese professor. a terrible teacher for a hard class. lectures are just her recopying note printouts on the board. doesnt provide help in preparing for exams. DONT TAKE A CLASS WITH HER

Dr. Minnich explains Calculus concepts very clearly and gives solid instruction. The homework/tests are controlled by the department, but he writes his own quizzes - they are tough, but there are opportunities to improve your grade.

I personally enjoyed Dr. Minnich's class. I thought the overall material got pretty difficult towards the end of the semester but he did a great job of explaining things. He's very understanding and caring towards his students and accessible out of class. He's young so he tires to connect and be funny with his students which I think can help.
Quizzes super hard, exams are easier than quizzes. Overall good professor, except he makes quizzes too hard.

His quizzes are way harder than the mids he would give u 4/10 even if u answer all questions correctly cuz he didn't want you to use this method 

His questions literally be like
Solve this without using the department's rule for it use the harder way

Stopped going to quizzes half way through the term

Dr. Minnich really knows what he's talking about. He does a good job at explaining things intuitively, and he understands when topics might be hard for students, elaborating when necessary. It's a shame they give him so much to teach in such a short amount of time. He does a good job with it though. Stay engaged, ask questions, and you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice guy, did not enjoy this class. He enjoys making his quizzes overly hard and they will kill your grade. I've talked with peers and you are much better off taking a different professor. That being said, Minnich is a good teacher of the material and you will do well on the exams, however he added more stress to my sem than it was worth.

Dr. Minnich is a good professor and person. You WILL find his quizzes hard, no matter prior experience; the strict 15 minute time constraints make them challenging. This is my only true criticism, though. He is articulate and eager to help others. He is a unique guy but it makes him interesting to listen to. Expect a rewarding, not easy, class.

Although his class is challenging, he would give examples of very challenging problems so exams were much easier to figure out. I was able to understand most topics he taught well, gave useful tricks and shortcuts, and was very helpful. Quizzes can be difficult, but attending LA sessions would get some low-scoring quizzes dropped.
Very good lectures, he'll clearly breakdown what you're learning simply. You just need to show up and always be engaged, content is just naturally difficult. Go to office hours he will help you.

He gets excited by making difficult quizzes we couldn't understand. The rest of the course (homework and exams) were well regulated and a lot more doable. Kills your confidence a little to fail so many quizzes but I did fine on the exams. Definitely quirky but I think he means well.

Minnich was my favorite professor, but very difficult. He is notoriously more challenging than other professors. The weekly quizzes are much harder and higher stakes than what other professors provide. A lot of people I knew had far lower quiz averages than exam averages for this class, whereas other classes, their quizzes boosted their grades.

His quizzes were way were harder than any other section of Math 141. I would score near perfect on exams and still get below 4/10 every week on his quizzes. While he's not a bad teacher, he has very snarky attitude to him that makes it hard to communicate with. You are much better taking a different professor.

Will give you 15 minutes for 6 question quizzes when every other class does 2 questions. He laughs about the quizzes he gives because he knows you can't solve them. He talks about everything you don't get tested on all class then brushes over everything on the test. Not the worst, super nice but don't expect to get better than a 2/10 on a quiz.

He is a great teacher, Very good at explaining complex topics simply. Overall structures class and resources well. Quizzes get very difficult at the end, and I think he enjoys giving out difficult tests/quizzes. He is a caring and good teacher though, stays on track with the course and doesn't fall behind the other teachers. He does his job well.

Lectured all class, with a few individual practice problems at the end. Not a lot of individual help, but that is hard to do in a big class. Quizzes were unnecessarily hard but if you attend LA Sessions you can get quiz drops.
He teaches too fast and barley explains.
Wouldn't take again, taught too fast and barely helped when asked questions.
Lectured styled, lots of notes, not much individual help

Dr. Minnich is a good professor stuck teaching a bad class. The format of Math 141 is not great and very quiz and exam heavy but there is nothing any professor can really do to stop that. Overall lectures were helpful and he does exam reviews too which are somewhat helpful for exams.

Prof Minnich is a great professor. I had never taken Calc II before, but he explained everything very thoroughly and made the class easy. The weekly quizzes can be difficult, but they are much harder than the exam questions. The exams aren't bad and are just like the practice exams. He does not accept any late work but is a great guy.

He is fine at teaching the material but gives unnecessarily hard quizzes while also giving zero slack Often you will get an answer right but he will mark it wrong for formatting issues He will also refuse to review something before an exam because "it's a waste of time and we did it in class" Don't take his class he doesn't help the student succeed

My time with Dr. Minnich was amazing taking MATH 140.  To be fair I did take both AB and BC in high school, but he taught calc better than my high school teachers and I thought they were amazing.  He is truly an awesome guy when you get to meet him.  100/10

This class is what you make of it, Prof Minnich is super helpful in office hours and cares. I suggest getting head starts on the achieves and written as some of them take a long time to do. Also, beware of the weekly quizzes!!! Attend LA sessions too for quiz drops:)

Good professor 
Beware of weekly quizzes
Ez class if you go to office hour
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Minnich was such a great professor and really cared about his students. He was always willing to meet with you in office hours and answer your questions. He gives you quizzes every Monday and they are hard, but he offers 3 quiz drops (replacing lowest grade with 100%) if you attend review sessions.

I took Math 250 with him at 8am. I did attend every lecture, but he did post notes when he finished a topic. Homework was manageable. He would finish the content for an upcoming exam a few days before that exam, and then he would do practice problems. Before the final we finished the content a week before finals week.

Qitong Jiang is maybe the most genuine professor I've ever had. He's a great guy and is trying his absolute darndest to make this class doable. He gives excellent explanations of the concepts and will always answer questions. If you go to class and ask questions when you're confused it'll be fine. You might also catch him at the gym ballin' up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Great guy. He was super helpful in office hours, and he clearly cares about his students. Unfortunately, he just hasn't gotten the hang of teaching yet. I'm sure the following semesters will be better, as he is a very hard worker. The class is difficult by nature, and if you don't put in the effort to learn on your own, you won't pass.
Meh
My man is trying everything he can....

Qile is one of the best lecturers I've ever had—kind, supportive, and truly inspirational. He consistently made challenging material feel accessible and easy to understand and always willing to support students and genuinely want the best for his students!

He teaches at Minnesota now, I took MATH 2243 with him. The worst professor I've had my freshman year. His lectures didn't make sense and he would often skip around, question himself, and get practice problems wrong. I could barely understand his lectures so I ended up not going after the first month and taught myself everything with YouTube.
I had him for MATH 4242. The worst lecturer I've ever had. I had to teach myself the entire course via textbook, and my grade reflects that. Avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: MATH4242. Do not take him. I came out of MATH2373 and took this as an elective. His lectures were unclear. He posted illegible notes 2 weeks into the semester, but he just used the whiteboard. He was nice enough to do a one-on-one meeting, but he did not help explain the homework material. Three midterms were 80% of the grade if I remember right.

Professor Yans lectures are very confusing and many of us has no idea whats going on half the time. He does answer questions, but so poorly that it just makes it more confusing. There is online and written homework every week that is so difficult it does not reflect the material he teaches in class. The written homework is graded so meticulously.

Professor Yan is OK. He can give clear explanations on those concepts and theorems. He would answer any question you have in class. But his lectures are kind of boring because of his flat tone. Also, I don't know if he's on purpose, he often makes mistakes when solving example problems.

Not too much to say about prof since she was rarely there, TAs helped with labs a lot more. Be sure to choose a good lab partner and read up on all the labs ahead of time so you pick good ones, especially for the long lab at the end. Presentation was just chatting with prof for 5min, explaining the long experiment setup, methods, and any results.
Awful. Just... awful explanations, awful tests, awful everything. Only positive is that some test questions are taken directly from the sample test.
Material covered in lecture had no relevance to exam material- I still attended class for conceptual material. Need to learn everything on exam by yourself.

As with the rest of the physics department, what she focuses on in lecture has very little to do with the material covered on the exam. She spends entirely too much time with the derivation of equations. Her examples are overly simplified, brief, poorly explained, and utterly unhelpful.

Ok its quantum physics, its gonna be confusing but she does a pretty good job at explaining things. Shes really nice and theres no problem with her accent at all. Some people didnt like her but I honestly think its because of the material.
She's a nice lady and she's willing to help, but she just isn't good at explaining things. The tests were pretty difficult compared to homework assignments, almost to the point of being unfair.

Seminar class. The lectures were interesting, but didn't cover enough topics. Jenny is amazingly unhelpful and the assignments were unclear. The grading is easy enough I guess but it was too much work for a 2 credit "easy" class.
Couldnt understand her, homeworks and tests were too hard, and classes were dull.
I didn't attend much class, and when I did, it was incomprehensible.
shes pretty cool

You will think you know what's going on, and then you'll take the exam and realize you know NOTHING. Lecture time is more like nap time, just print the notes out from the internet. You're grade will probably depend on how good of a mult. choice guesser you are. Good Luck
lectures very boring, exams way too difficult - very different from sample exams and book material, curve small compared to other profs
Not incredibly interesting.  Not the best at explaining stuff, but the course isn't really hard imo.  Lots of people around to help you.
She's very nice and the class isn't too difficult, but the exams seemed to be unfair.  The averages AFTER the curves were in the 60's.  Explanations can be a little confusing too.

Great guy. The bad reviews are entirely unwarranted. Genuinely wants everyone to do well and get an A. No curve so unlike other EE classes but the material is well organized and easy to study for with appropriate cheat sheets. Exams are fair. Sit in the front and he will care to be nicer and talk to you in class

He is a very kind old man who wants to see people succeed. Sit in front, ask questions, and absolutely go to office hours (he will clarify questions and basically give you the answers to homework). Hes a little disorganized and hard to understand at first but he is hilarious.

The class itself isn't hard. He also wants everyone to get an A, doing the homework does help for the exams. The only issue is that he doesn't give enough practice, glides over practice problems on the lectures then they turn up on the exams. The practice exams he gives are relatively easy, the actual exams are opposite. He does allow cheat sheets.
Very boring lectures. You have to read and learn on your own. He does not know anything but behaves like he is a master.
He is the master x3. Seriously, do the homework and you'll be fine. Gives As to kids who make an effort.

This is the first time I have had a professor who has said out loud "I'm glad that the averages are lower because I don't want all my students to get As". As a student who has consistently struggled in his class, it was hurtful and demoralizing. In class he is all smiles, in office hours he acts like he is a superior being and belittles his student
HE IS DEFINITELY THE MASTER
he is the master

Professor Chen is an amazing professor who really cares about his students. If you go to class and office hours he will get to know you and he is always willing to answer questions. He doesn't just give you the answers to questions, he will make you think and learn. He also gives a lot of extra credit, but it is hard and you have to work for it.

Seems a little too smart at times to convey the material properly and can be rude at times when it comes to "simpler" questions. I think the web version of this class was a lot easier, but I took it in person. Class average was a 58% for the first exam and he blamed us completely for that.

Great professor! This class was pretty tough/stressful at points but the lectures and posted notes are very helpful and there are so many opportunities to raise your grade if you do poorly on tests. There is a lot of homework but if you can do the problems well then tests are straightforward. Overall I would still 100% recommend.

Have two projects, two home works, and a quiz all during finals week. Take with anyone else - its actually an interesting class but this teacher may just be too smart for his own good. Unreasonable course load.
He's the freaking man! Likes to crack jokes and is always willing to answer questions. Really just wants you to do well and provides all the materials you could need (:
This professor sucks. Avoid him if you can. He does not explain anything clearly and is least helpful. Does not respect his students.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Amazing professor! The first bit of the material can be difficult, but if you hang on through the conceptual stuff and GO TO HIS RECITATION(!!!), Qiushi will take care of you.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was an awesome professor who provides clear and organized lectures and notes. He also provided extra recitation for helping students to do hw. Thus, my experience was super nice. Even if this is a hard class, his teaching and helping make the contents much easier to understand. He is my nan shen teacher. Recommend.

She does not respond to emails, TA grades everything, an assignment is due almost every other day, and unclear instructions. She does not teach CAD at all and makes you learn it yourself. AVOID taking this section; the other EDSGN is so much better. Plus, every absence afte 3 docks 2% from your final grade.
Follows the curriculum EXACTLY for a class that teaches nothing besides busywork and navigating bureaucracy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She tells you the first day of class that there will be no homework but then assigns tons of it through the semester. The class is not meant to be difficult, but she makes it way harder than it needs to be. I'm lucky I already knew how to use Fusion because her explanations and tutorials were atrocious. Do not take this professor!!

She's not the best—long lectures and confusing assignments—but many negative reviews are overblown. Easy grader (I got 99 without much effort) and was very kind when I asked for help. This class is tough no matter who teaches it, she's not the worst option.

Get ready for poor student/educator communication in this class. Instruction in class and in canvas is always unclear, and I did not look forward to going to this class three times a week. Attendance policy is strict too.

I was sick for a group project, emailed her the day before with a doctors note, and I got 30 points docked for not being there. When I followed up the email a week later, she said she couldn't change the grade because it was too late. I asked why she didn't respond and she said "You can't expect me to respond to everything." Class was 25 kids max.

Horrible. Reads word for word off of slide show and doesn't explain anything further. Nobody in the class ever understands assignments and then she gets mad when you ask questions about anything. One time she said "you are trying to pin your misunderstandings on me" to a girl who asked a question.
good luck on your 2nd attempt

Do not take EDSGN100 with her. The TA determines your grade because she never grades HW/assignments, and she is harsh when it comes to grading the group projects. She hardly teaches how to do the CAD modeling assignments, and assigns more HW than other professors. Above all, she can be very rude and uninterested in helping her students.

Such an annoying teacher.. said we would have no homework at the beginning of the semester but we had a ton over the semester. My TA was terrible and graded super harshly

If you've never done busy work before be prepared to do an insane amount of it.

She was a nice teacher but constantly yapped all class so everything had to be done for homework
Terrible teacher!

Professor Takaghaj is inconsiderate in the sense that she will never tolerate any excuse for a late submission or be understanding to any inconveniences. She talks low, and she will not welcome questions in class. She is the sole reason anyone can struggle in this course because with any other instructor it's a guaranteed A.

For the sake of your sanity, please do not take this professor. Unless you want to be full of stress during and outside of class, take it with a different professor. Every project in this class is very useless and boring. The professor doesn't talk loud enough or speak clearly. Grading takes forever and just overall this class/professor is bad.ㅗㅗㅗㅗ

Boring lectures and does not speak loud enough. Unclear instructions for assignments. Does not help you when you need advice or have an issue. Takes a long time to put grades in, and doesn't respond to emails. Does not help with CAD. Waste of time being class after lecture as she sits on her phone and you do work you could do outside of it.

Her lectures are pretty boring and it feels like a waste of time to sit through a 1h50min class. Her grading criteria is pretty bad. And trying to communicate with her is really difficult cause she wont care
She is very strict with grading even though she is not able to clearly communicate her expectations.

Most useless and boring professor I've had. The only important thing we learned was Solidworks, which she didn't even teach in class and made us watch tutorials on weekends. Instead, she decides to yap for two hours and gets mad when people fall asleep.

Shes a completely intolerable human being incapable of having a respectful or competent conversation. She shouldn't be a teacher and the only reason she hasn't been fired is because she teaches an introductory course to engineering freshman who don't have time or confidence to stand up for the quality of their education.

During one group project, I ended up doing all of the work. I asked for an extension to finish the work on time,she denied claiming there was time, knowing that I was doing everything alone. Another time, I almost fainted,and I asked if it was okay if I had left after I presented, she denied asking for medical documentation that I was feeling ill.
just don't. I hate her in every way.

This class is supposed to be a fun introductory level course, but she makes everything more difficult than it needs to be. There would be multiple times where my classmates and I lost points because the TA and the professor had different requirements/rubrics. If the professor doesn't like you, good luck because she will make your grade suffer.

Prof. Takaghaj is one of if not the worst teacher I have ever had. She overexplains simple tasks to the point where everyone tunes out, and then she will say something important and everyone will miss it. What she says in class frequently contradicts the rubric. She is also a tougher grader than all the other edsgn 100 profs.
One of the worst professors that I have taken a course with, if your taking EDSGN 100 Make sure to look for another professor
RUN. TAKE EDSGN 100 WITH ANY OTHER PROFESSOR.

She will often misunderstand what you are saying and assume that you're being passive-aggressive by asking questions. Her explanations are awful, usually very vague and leaves the students questioning the assignment. She also tells students to seek TAs instead of her when they have questions. Her teaching skills are next to none, do NOT recommend.
She antagonizes her students and is vindictive. Fails to be understanding and always needs to be right. Once she doesn't like you, you will receive unprecedented bs and your grades WILL fall.

She is a very stubborn and tough grading person. She takes everything seriously and shows no mercy towards students that submit assignments. She takes everything as a personal matter and isn't open-minded to people's troubles and problems. Lastly, she doesn't explain properly at all her voice is very low-pitched. TAKE EDSGN WITH ANYOTHER PROFESSOR!

She's a nice person, but I just got agitated in class bc she speaks so quietly and high pitched. She wasn't clear when she explained the projects so the TA would have to reexplain after. She wld drill a lot of people with questions during presentations too, so make sure you are prepared and read the rubrics. Solidworks is used for class- HATE IT
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice professor but she is very unorganized and is sometimes hard to understand what she is asking from us for an assignment. I would not recommend taking her section.
Tim Kelsey is hands down one of the best professors I've ever had.

AMAZING! Loved this honors class. Group project whole sem. Lots of work, but fine if you balance with the group. Short readings before every class. Minimal allowed absences. Very kind and understanding of mental health absences. Interesting class if you get a topic you like. Lets you revise your writing to receive a better grade.

Tim was an absolutely amazing teacher! His CED 102N class was taught exceptionally well, the lectures were highly organized, and the subjects discussed were meaningful and useful for our lives. His teaching style is very concise, and I know the lessons he taught in the class will be very influential in my life. I would definitely recommend him!
Very caring, easy to get a good grade, just keep up with the work. group projects focus on real world problems

Prof. Kelsey was by far my favorite professor last semester (SP25). I enjoyed the lecture material. It wasn't as much of a lecture class either per se. It was much more of ongoing group discussions. Be ready to discuss in small groups and with the class. Group project is worth the large bulk of your grade, get a good team 1st then just do the proj.

Tim is a great guy and a great professor. The lectures are mandatory, but he is very understanding if you are sick or have special circumstances. Make sure you pick a topic that you actually like, or else your semester will be boring. The homework is easy, and as long as your group is decent, you'll do fine on the papers.
Class is great for CED majors, really helps us understand certain things. Very kind & accessible outside of class, 10/10!

He's a really nice guy and cares for his students. I did learn things through my group project but I felt that a lot of the things we did in class were not meaningful. You don't need to buy the books. He was always accessible and you can get a good grade if you go to class and do assignments.

I cannot stress enough how phenomenal of a professor Tim is. The guy is super caring and truly cares about his students and wants them to succeed, the class is great and very discussion focused, with problems that people are interested in. I would take this class a hundred times if I could, he is a really great guy and will help out no question
I took this class as a GenEd and tbh very boring and group-based work. But fairly simple and easy! Very cool teacher and professor.

This class was alright. It's basically one semester-long group project with other smaller things in between. No actual exams. Lectures are really boring and you have only 3 unexcused absences. This class will be a lot worse if you get a bad group. Lots of writing and the the material is really boring. Really bad gen ed to take, find something else.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: One of the easiest classes I have taken at PSU, however dropped my grade on the last day of class because of attendance even though I completed all my work and had an A in the class he dropped me to a C because of it.

I definitely suggest taking this course as easy A for a gen ed. You work on a project the whole semester with a group and you have some other assignments. Mostly busy work but very manageable. Tim really cared about his students and let you revise your work after receiving feedback from him to get a better score.

CED 102N was just a boring class in general, the the professor was pretty okay. there is a lot of unnecessary stuff needed to be done for this class def would not take it again just cause it doesn't match my interest.

The class itself wasn't my favorite since it's essentially just one giant group project, but Tim is a super nice and understanding guy. He'll always respond to your emails and cares a lot about his students. Easy to get an A if you put in a reasonable amount of effort (he also lets you submit revised assignments for a better grade).
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I think that it is an easy A course, there is just a lot of homework. Tim really is a great guy and cares about what he teaches. I think there is a lot of busy work but nothing that is too crazy. A big group project that lasts the whole semester and takes a lot of work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Professor Kelsey is the best professor I've had!  He is truly the nicest man and really cares about all his students.  The CED102N course was new this semester so I decided to try it and I have no regrets at all.  WOULD RECOMMEND HIM TO EVERYONE!!!!! He's awesome!!!
Great teacher, highly recommend

I took his class for interdomain credit. Most of the assignments are in a learning team to research all semester. Interviews are required for this course, lots of readings with check points every day of class, and lots of writing. Tim is very flexible with grading and due dates. Great person and very kind professor. I recommend CED102N for ID creds
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Tim is a fantastic professor, and it's clear he cares a lot about the material and whether the students understand it. He's super easy to get ahold of outside of the classroom too. I can't recommend him enough. If you are even considering CED, take 275.

Tim is the best professor I've had at Penn State and I can't believe his department is not supported on this website solely because of how great he is. He is great at giving back helpful and meaningful feedback to students on anything and everything. Accompanied by his grading system that makes it incredibly difficult to not Ace one of his classes.

The class was hard for me, the exams are all short response but you get a study sheet, labs were the hardest part. She also will reach out if you are doing poorly. Overall just come to class and take detailed notes and you'll be fine.

LITERALLY THE BEST PROF EVER AND I'M A COMPLETELY DIFF MAJOR. PLEASE TAKE HER CLASSES SHES SO SWEET. 

It is ur fault if you dont do the work, its just one homework a week with one reading that shouldn't be an issue to do. 
A group project at the end of the sem which is also super easy. 

She's an amazing professor and truly a good person.
Guaranteed A if you show up and do homework on time. The grading for the homeworks and final grade is a little unclear though.

Extremely kind professor. If you show up, an A is basically guaranteed. A few long reading assignments and a handful of questions—no exams and no final. Lecture content isn't really tested, but attending and showing you're engaged helps. Easy Gen Ed that is actually pretty interesting. I sat front, participated, and never lost points!!

EARTH105N is an easy GenEd as long as you show up and do the work. Directions for assignments can be unclear at times but she's a really lenient grader and willing to help (even though sometimes her help isn't all that helpful and a little dismissive). The class is interesting for a non major. Would recommend just be prepared to do the work.

This is definitely a pretty easy A if you go to class and ask questions. However, sometimes I felt like when I asked questions she would give me really passive aggressive responses. Overall it's fine if you need to fill a gen ed requirement. Does the job.
Decent and very easy going

Although the class isn't bad it would be infinitely easier if there were proper directions to the excel assignments. Honestly it sometimes feels like she makes the directions terrible on purpose so everyone is forced to come to class. However if you're willig to come to class and ask questions this should be an easy A.

She was very nice at first, but when it came to the Excel assignments, she became less helpful and didn't explain them clearly. I hope this improves in the future because it's frustrating to ask for help and receive passive-aggressive responses or no response at all.

Dr. Furman is a great professor! Exams cover ALL topics we did in class, so take good/detailed notes during lecture and you'll be set. She lets the class vote on syllabus percentages to see what's best for everyone throughout the semester. Labs are a bit tricky but not impossible. Overall the class is pretty nice, and she's very caring.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Horrible tests. Lower average in these tests than chemistry and math weeder classes. Doesn't believe in multiple choice or proper teaching. Will mark everything wrong on tests because it wasn't exactly "what she was looking for". Labs were extremely boring and unnecessary

This class is lecture heavy, and is based on labs, a few HW assignments, and 2 midterms. If you attend class regularly, take notes, and study for exams, then you'll do well. Make sure to attend labs and work hard on them, because they account for a good portion of your grade. Dr. Furman is kind, friendly, and often makes funny remarks.

Hi everyone. I am actively on my hands and knees begging you to not take a Tanya Furman taught class. I am a third-year civil engineer and this was by far my hardest class... as a level 1 geoscience prerequisite. She grades hard, impossible dare I say, and the mandatory labs every week are graded even harder. STAY AWAY FROM TANYA FURMAN. PLEASE.

She is amazing for Geosci001. The tests were based on the slides and the book, but you have a study sheet to bring to the exam. She is super caring and will allow you to submit late work with little penalty. The tests are hard, but they are curved. The labs are fun, but it depends on the TA. Just go to the lab and class, and you will be fine.
She makes you buy the book for barely any homework. She's the only one who requires it. She makes this class way harder than it needs to be the other teachers understand it's geoscience 1

Professor Furman was one of my favorites this Fall 2024 semester. Her Earth Science 105 course has to be one of the easiest courses I have ever taken. The course work is easy and manageable and she is a very fair grader. I would definitely recommend this class as a NS Gen-Ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Furman is very caring and compassionate. I took this class for gen-ed to fulfill both interdomain and international culture course. This class is a bit boring and the journals may be hard to read. But this is not to say it's a bad class, just not my personal interests. Furman grades thing quite light and this class is not hard overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great teacher, hardly had homework. Every so often had to write a journal with a few prompts off of a few readings, but overall super easy. A few group projects and a major one at the end but she provides so much feedback and help throughout with plenty of time to get assignment and projects done in class although can be unclear at times.

Dr. Furman was great. Make sure you at least go to class like 2 times a week as well as the labs. She gave points in this class if you did well in the labs and that raised my grade a whole bunch. Her lectures are so long and boring but you get a sheet for exams and honestly you can make one just repeating the slides, you will pass the class.

This woman does not get the credit she deserves! She has a great personality and is easy to talk to! Lectures can be a lot sometimes, but trust the process and skim the book to get more information. Tests are atrociously hard, but she curves them. I got a 68 on one and it was a B. You get a sheet of notes to take in for the exam.

Took geoscience the Spring semester and had a miserable time. She is not only a tough grader but is very selective on answers for midterms which are 15-20 short answer responses. The questions on midterms require a deep level overview even for being allowed a one page study sheet. She explains concepts in long tangents that leave you more confused.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor is really passionate about what she is teaching. She has a great sense of humour and I thoroughly enjoyed her class. She is very accommodating and genuinely cares about students. The class is not work heavy at all. Best of all it has not exams just in class activities journal entries and a final project.
Very easy Gen Ed, Dr Furman is great and very accessible. Put in a little bit of work and you can easily receive an A.

if you really want to be a geoscientist or whatever perfect teacher, but otherwise take someone else. she doesn't believe in multiple choice and gives up to 20 open ended questions in a hour for midterms, and is specifically looking for certain answers. she does curve very well though and answer emails very fast.
Never take Geosc 1 with her

Super cool professor, one of my favs. Had 3 exams, and the final was optional. The only hw is like 4 projects throughout the semester. Labs are fine as long as you work with ppl. Easy to get an A. Funny professor, and the lectures are interesting.

Grades were made up of labs, assignments, and exams. The exams were challenging, but I felt as long as I went to lectures and paid attention I could do fairly well. Dr. Furman was great, it is obvious that she is dedicated to this topic and wants others to feel this excitement she has. One of the best teachers I have had so far at Penn State!

Dr. Furman is very understanding. She accepts late work and does not take attendance. There are no tests in this class, just "journals" which consist of answering a few questions from a reading. At the end of the semester there is a group project and presentation, but its done all in class.

Easy A class. Basically put in an hour for journal writings (there are 5), show up in class to do the activities, and she will tell you the answer if you don't know, then you'll get A. No exams. She also makes stuff easy to understand. Just put in some effort and this guarantees an A.

A lot of people did not like her, but they just did not want to do the work. 50% of the class is non exams, so it you will do well. Easy to pass hard to get an A. A lot of confusing content, but she explains it well. Felt lucky to have her as my teacher. Exam questions are pulled directly from her slides, and her slide notes.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had. I had her through zoom and she did not care whether she had good or bad connection or if her students could ever hear her. She was constantly rude when people asked questions and straight up said in a study session she wrote us a bad exam because she was in a bad mood. Horrible professor, doesn't care
Professor Furman is great. Many dislike her course due to the difficult exams, but she curves them so it's not hard to get an A or B. Very intelligent and her sarcasm makes the class more enjoyable.

I really liked Dr. Furman. She was very understanding. The lectures were easy to follow along, and matches mostly what's on the exams. She tells you what you should read, skim, or skip in the book, and goes over what type of questions she asks on the exams.

Worst professor I have ever had to date. She is absolutely atrocious. This is a LEVEL ONE CLASS. There was no need for the ridiculous grading and tests she gave. If you want a true level one class experience, do not take this class with this professor. Unbelievable.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Do NOT look at the old reviews for Dr. Furman. Earth 105 has changed. No exams. One class she gives a presentation, next you do a work sheet. About six easy 1 page papers (1 hour). I'm not a great writer but still did well. A final project. Interesting class but not overwhelming on an engineering schedule and she gets that. A Hidden Gem Prof
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Tanya is super fair! Many do not like her because she gives challenging exams, but the class average is curved, so it is not hard to get an A/B. She wants you to get something out of the class and not give pointless MC exams.
Not recommended, lots of extra work, exams are extremely difficult, in a 001 level course
Great teacher, great person. I loved her class. She is a tough grader, but there is a curve. I would take her again.

This class is pretty easy..it is full of work but as you know you make the class what you want it to be...as for Tanya she is a very nice lady and is very willing to help out where you don't understand so I kind of recommend taking this class as long as your willin to work for your grade.

AAAS/Earth 105 is a terrible class.There are bunch of online activities that take forever and don't usually pertain to what you're learning in class.You have to read a lot of articles too and answer study questions which you usually can't find in the articles.There are three tests that aren't too hard, but difficult to study for.

Most painful class ever. It is full of busy work and takes no effort, the busy work also is painfully boring. Don't take this class unless you are ready for a class on the level of 8th grade classes.  You realllllllly shouldn't take this class unless you don't wanna learn anything except a few tediously worthless facts.

this class is annoying. im thinking of dropping it.  it's changed a lot since what the other students were commenting.  we have lots of questions that we need to answer for each activity, and all the answers take a lot of time to write and think about.  there's a lot of busy work - not worth it

I did not like the class at all--there were no tests, but some of the projects were rediculous.  And sadly, I really didn't learn a whole lot.  She is a good teacher though.  She's a little bit nutty, but she'll help you out a lot if you just talk to her.  She usually responds to e-mails within 5 minutes.
Tanya is the greatest. She is always willing to help, and as long as you pay attention and give it a good try, you will do just fine in any of her classes.
No Comments

Really willing to give help if you ask her.  No tests but a group project at the end which wasn't too bad.  But you have to come to class everyday b/c there are alot of in class activities (which are very easy).
