Dr. Furman is excellent! She doesn't make her assignments hard, and she is quite amusing. She is the perfect First-Year Seminar professor. She really helped me to adjust to Penn State and for that I am grateful. Thank you, Dr. Furman.

Very easy class.  Primary emphasis was on a group project that we were given 6 weeks to work on and took about an hour to actually do.  Also, we had to write "journal entries" based on assigned readings from the course pack.  This class couldn't
She's good at being a geologist, bad at being a teacher. She made an intro to geology class hard with her complicated lectures and difficult assignments.  Avoid.

Whoever left the comment above must be Dr. Furman's daughter.  She is unclear, disorganized, and rarely comes to class prepared.  Her lectures are pointless because the quizzes have nothing to do with them.  Avoid her if possible.
Furman is awesome. Take her classes now.

This guy was great. He is very nice, a little hard to understand but the class content is not difficult. Kinda a lot of outside of class work, but manageable. One morning I had a pretty bad bike accident on the way to class and he took the time out of class to drive me to university health services. So yeah, good guy.

Professor Yu was awesome. Very easy grader, teaches skills actually valuable to engineering, and was very easily accessible outside of class. Group projects are very dependent on the quality of your teammates, so try to meet people in your class the first couple of days. Only complaint would be that he was often late and took forever to grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The most respectful and caring professor you'd have. He is a lenient grader, can be funny sometimes. considers everyone's problems just be clear with him. Very friendly. However, work might feel too much, but the professor would still help if you are submitting late or had any other problems without hesitation. I'm glad I took this class with him.

He was a great and caring guy. Very understanding, I hated the class though. Some instructions are fairly confusing but he is always willing to answer questions and will extend deadlines. Don't judge the course based on the first few weeks.

Dr. Yu is a decent professor. However, he often cancels with less than 30 minutes notice, which is frustrating if you commute from off campus. Assignment instructions are vague, but putting in effort usually leads to good grades. He's very slow to grade; it's currently Sunday of finals week with assignments ungraded and no final grades submitted.

A respectable religous man. He is funny, explains material well, answers questions well, easily understood, and down to earth. This class is very heavily hands on where lectures don't really matter but they are mandatory but he makes them entertaining. Class is easy and fun and you can get by doing almost the bare minimum or enjoy participating

Dr. Yu is a very nice teacher who really cares about his students. However, he takes a very long time to grade assignments (most were not graded until after finals week). He also canceled class or arrived late on very short notice on several occasions. Some of the assignments are repetitive and tedious, but the class itself is not that difficult.

Didn't grade anything for months until the end of finals week... upholds attendance but canceled class on very short notice (many people were already at the classroom) on several occasions. Lectures are longer than they need to be. Nice guy though, not an awful class, pretty easy.

Dr. Yu is an amazing EDSGN professor. His TA will grade most things under 35 points, but anything over that will likely take Dr. Yu a while to grade, but he does almost always give 100%. He gives helpful and constructive feedback for projects, and he is very easy to joke around with.

Never graded anything until the absolute last day of the grade deadline (after finals) and took off points for assignments I was given an extension on for being late. This guy is genuinely the worst professor I've had at Penn State, and that is saying a lot considering the professors in the engineering department. Avoid at all costs, very bad prof.

Tianliang is a very good guy. He is very understanding, and he will give you extensions as long as you have a valid reason. Where he falls short is grading assignments on time. It's finals week and he's only graded FIVE assignments. This makes it difficult to know what your actual grade is. Other than not grading anything, he is okay.
You have to do a lot of work and go to class, but it's not hard to get an A. Dr. Yu teaches everything well and loves enjoying a Coca Cola everyday.
This professor was a genuine guy who cared about his class and the projects he presented. Assignments are very easy and can be done within 30 minutes tops. Just be ready to use SolidWorks.

Tianliang Yu is very kind and caring. Although his accent limits his lectures, he always portrays his message and explains it very well. He is a very smart man and always wants the best for his students.

Dr. Yu is an amazing professor and truly cares about his students. He learned my name in the first week and is a very considerate person. He knows how to answer questions and is always willing to help his students.
Dr. Yu is great. He keeps lectures short, is always available to help, and is happy to be teaching. The grading is easy, and he can keep the class fun.
Dr. Yu is an amazing professor that always made sure everyone was comfortable and learning. There are many group projects but Dr. Yu makes it fun and interesting every day in class.

Dr. Yu is a great professor, and I would recommend him for EDSGN 100.
He explains things clearly, and includes light humor into his lectures.
His grading rubrics are very clear and easy to understand, and is relatively easy-going on grading as well.
He truly cares about his students, too, and is quite flexible.
literally going through my first heartbreak when I took this class and I still did good, Taoli my goat
Take him if you can
Nice guy with a good taste in fashion. Has a tendency to go over class time, but does a good job explaining the content.
Great teacher and super nice. He knows his stuff and will answer any questions. This class is really easy if you go to lectures and do the homework. Practice exams are super helpful.

Tough class, but he did a great job teaching it and cared about his students. Was super cool and held extra office hours before exams. Provided helpful responses to emails quickly and always took any questions after class. Take him!

This professor is fairly good at teaching the class and knows how to explain the class concepts reasonably well. The course itself is fairly difficult but he explains everything the best that anyone can. Would recommend him as a professor if you are interested in just getting through the class.
RUFF GRR ARF ARF GRRRRR WOOF WOOF RUFF WOOF ARF ARF GRR WOOF
He talks about his love for the nature and his dog so much during class, would take again
RUFF RUFF WOOF GRRRR WOOF RUFF WOOF GRRRR ARRRRFFF ARRRRFFF GROWLFF.

Prof Matsoukas is a very esteemed and respected professor, he works like a dog in and out of the classroom. HE truly pushes us to be the best students we can. The class is hard but but if you work hard you will be rewarded. His office hours are kind of difficult to make, but you will almost always find him in his lab.

Professor Matsaukas is a very interesting guy. He was a tough grader and textbook reading were mandatory. He does give extra credit opportunities such as sending pics of you walking your dog and nature reserves by your house. He does seem quite stressed and distracted in class so he should blow off more steam in nature but aside from that he's good

By far my favorite professor and loved to take walks through the woods with his dog to blow off steam. I don't know what happened to him but he was one of my favorite professors at Penn State. By the end of the semester I really felt like I got to know him inside and out.

Dr.matsoukas cares and about his students and you can tell he is very invested into the course.Since, the course very organized and he breaks down the concepts in a much simpler way. His exams were fair but they are not easy not too difficult either. I would overall 100% recommend taking thermo 1 with Themis.

Matsoukas clearly cares about his students and the topic. His lectures are not mandatory but you need to go to understand the material. He does have a bunch of typos/algebra mistakes but does give EC if you are the first one to point them out. Pretty forgiving with HW/exam grading too (gives partial credit). Overall, a good intro prof for ChemEs.
He cares about his students. He introduces the concepts on Cheme very well. YOU HAVE TO GO TO CLASS. THIS IS NOT A TEXTBOOK READING TYPA THING. JUST GO.

professor Matsoukas had pretty fair exams and his lectures were pretty good. He does make a ton of typos and algebra mistakes but he said algebra is easy or hire a math intern which is kind of funny. He will not round your grade if you are .1% away from a grade cut off. He can be rude sometimes but he is usually friendly.

I had Prof. Matsoukas for both Che 220 and 320 and I really have nothing bad to say about him. He is extremely fair with his assignments and exams, and is very knowledgable. He is also very accommodating to his students and his class was by far the best in terms of adapting to zoom classes during the pandemic. Take classes with him if you can.
Prof. Matsoukas is a true gem in the chemical engineering department i loved the subject.

I took the class online over the summer, however I was on campus and visited him a bunch, not the best with question help and his homework is super hard. His test compared to the HW is a walk in the park, Def easier than the average professor so I would highly recommend. Similar to Pester if you had him before.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Matsoukas makes a LOT of algebra mistakes during lecture, and it often leads to confusion. Exams were only 2 questions and pretty tough. Also, he doesn't have a timer during exams, so be sure to bring a watch, or else you won't know how much time you have left to finish. He teaches by lots of examples, and you can learn a lot if you pay attention.
Clear, concise, organized, and kind
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Matsoukas was meh. Don't bother going to class, he just reads off a powerpoint that he posts later so you can just read that and get the same information. The class isn't easy, and it especially doesn't help that he makes soooo many mistakes in his notes that you don't really know what you can trust. Definitely could have been a lot better.

Really great professor who wants you to learn. Exams are very straight forward and similar to the in class problems. If you do enough practice problems and pay attention in class, it shouldn't be too difficult

Matsoukas is a great guy, but he makes thermo way easier than it really needs to be. The exams are exactly like the homework/in-class problems, so they're pretty much cake. I strongly recommend forming a study with people around you as soon as possible. The homeworks can be tricky to work through solo. Attending lecture isn't all that important.

Themis is the kind of guy who knows and loves what he teaches. He explains the material in a very precise and understandable manner. Don't expect to not try and understand everything and get an A. Go be a business major then. But if you want to learn and understand, then this class is for you. Any questions he also explains in his office hours.

This class is like a foreign language. If you do not read the textbook you will fall behind in the first week. He expects you to know a lot. His examples in class are not the best and the test are 10 times harder than the homework.

If you learn by doing lots of examples, then Themis is your guy. He goes through examples step by step but he does move quickly. My advice is to read the book before lectures and write as many notes in it as you can before the exams . Exams push your thinking, but if you write notes that summarize the equations you might need, you will pass.
His exams are easy as long as you follow lectures, keep up with the book and understand the homework. I like him and his class

Professor Matsoukas is so arrogant he refuses to admit when he makes a mistake, or in the case of his textbook about 200 mistakes. If you confront him about a mistake he gets angry and refuses to answer any other questions you may have for the rest of the semester. Avoid his class if you can

Dr. Matsoukas is a great professor of thermodynamics. He wrote the textbook, so he teaches it in a very linear fashion. He's extremely helpful and clear when teaching difficult concepts (looking at you, fugacity). Overall, he's a very accommodating professor. Take his classes whenever possible, especially for any level of thermo.

Not an easy professor, but if you actually want to learn how to solve problems rather than memorize them, he is the best professor to have. He teaches you to think like an eningeer and the problem solving skills you learn from him you will utilize the rest of your chemical engineering career. Also had him for Ch E 210 and felt the same.

Class operates on a very straight-forward schedule: Homework every week and roughly 10 lectures of material to a test. Tests are just like homework problems with an added twist. Lecture is full of example problems which are often full of mistakes since Themis isn't the best at algebra. But nevertheless, you get used to it and will learn a lot.
Very well spoken. You can tell he loves teaching.

Matsoukas is an okay guy but as far as a professor he falls short.  Dont expect him to spend time on preparing his lectures because he uses examples from thirty years ago where he still hasn't fixed the errors.  Expect nearly all of his examples in class to lead to a dead end due to his mistakes.

Course is hard at the beginning and gets easier with each succesive test.  Matsoukas makes alot of mistakes but cares about the students and what their opinions are.  Not a bad class on the whole.  Though if your in it you probably don't have a choice of prof. anyway.

A good teacher. Presents material well and tests it fairly with tests and homework. Still a challenging course, keeps you on you toes. Makes ALOT of mistakes on the board, you just have to be patient.

Prof. Matsoukas always had interesting lectures. I wish all my chem engr profs could be this good. Always willing to answer questions and one could tell he had a deep interest in seeing students succeed.
This guy is my honors advisor. He is the man. Teaches well and advises very well and in a timely fashion both. Gotta love him and his insight!
Great professor. Very clear presentations in class. He does make a fair share of mistakes doing problems in class, but he knows his material.
He sucks at teaching and makes mistakes on the board all the time.

Good:  Verygood lecturer.  Extremely clear, concise.  Teaches you how to think; not to memorize.  Bad: Often makes mistake on problems during class.  Very harsh grading -> But then again this is a "weed out" course designed to get rid of the weaker Chem Es.
makes mistakes all the time because apparently he is "too close to the board". Isn't forgiving at all with grading. doesn't do review sessions, and not very helpful at all during office hours either.

great ChE prof! teaches you how to think, not memorize. breaks problems down into steps. challenging hw assignments/tests. makes you work hard. notes clear. graded hws/tests with detailed comments. fun refrig. cycle project. ALWAYS in office if help is needed! responds to e-mails very quickly. seems to love teaching. most rewarding A- I received!

Very good teacher.  Makes clear presentations and makes hard material somewhat easier.  Is very interested in teaching the students to problem solve, not to solve a set of problems.  He is very helpful, and always responded to emails in a timely fashion.
Tough class, but fair grading. The professor really knows his subject and he's accessible after class. Participation matters a lot as the exams are based on his notes.
Canvas won't contain the new materials, only Lectures and Duderstadt. Tests are simple, don't overthink it. Homeworks are long and very beneficial.

This professor expected the class to prioritize the work for his class over that of all of our other classes (other 400 level NUCE classes).
Only returned half of the students HW before an exam where a third of the exam was directly copied HW questions.
Difficult to approach, didn't answer questions related to course structure or clarifications.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Great professor. He is available to provide help and discuss results. This was his first year teaching NUCE403.
Skibs loved being condescending to students.
Lectures are snoozefests. Horrible exam grading system

While attendance isn't necessary, there were lots of things covered in class that are missing from the material provided. That said, the lectures were great and heavily informative, though often extremely long.
how about that?
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Skibinski can seem tough but once you get used to his teaching style he's one of the better profs in CE. He's very knowledgeable about the real-world practices of engineering. 432 is a great class to take even if you aren't going into Construction Management

Professor Skibinski is a really nice and highly knowledgeable about what's going on in the industry. There are only six homework assignments for the whole semester, and he gives plenty of extra credit opportunities. The tests can be rather tedious to study for (especially the quantitative material) but there not too bad.

Professor Skibinski provides great material and truly teaches pretty well. His quizzes are quite tough so I recommend spending a good amount of time studying. The group project at the end of the semester was quite enjoyable. I recommend taking him if you don't mind studying PowerPoints.
He doesn't care about his students and will make you retake the course even if your a few percentage off from the grade you need. Doesn't give any exam outline to study from.

Was pretty surprised seeing all the negativity here. He's one of my favorite teachers I've had, very genuine and knowledgeable. Class is not hard - just get ready to read through some long powerpoints to study

After having taken Mr. Skibinski for CE332 a few years back, I was apprehensive at taking another class with him. However, he is a much better teacher and personality in front of small groups and classes instead of the large lecture that 332 was. He graded the final project a little tough but gave great advice and anecdotal examples.
Does not take into consideration students circumstances . Can honestly be very disrespectful at times.. Don't recommend taking this class.

Throughout this class we have done 2 major assignments, first being a time management which I got a 80 on and the second assignment being a career research paper which I got 100 on. Overall, I received a D! Felt like he was very un-friendly and un-approachable. Also, replied with the same exact same answer to two long emails. Late 15 mins15/100
Very rude professor, very by the book. If you wanna pass you better study the slides.

Seems like a good guy. The class is only a quiz, 5 assignments, and 3 exams. So messing up one thing can hurt your grade. The multiple choice on the exams is insanely difficult. Youre expected to know pretty much everything from the class powerpoints. Class is pretty interesting tho

Skibs is pretty rude as a professor, if you ask a question instead of answering it he goes along the lines of "you should know that" or "pay better attention". the class isn't difficult but the exams do ask for specifics so make sure to pay attention to the slides. Homework is easy.
Professor is well educated and speaks clearly. My minor complaint is he seems a bit condescending and the lectures are very very dry similarl to a prune thats been sitting in the sun for way to long.

Extremely haphazard with project formatting. His grading does not make any sense. Unbelievably condescending. Lectures are boring and he just emphatically reads off of the power point slides. Very inflexible refuses to accommodate anyone. Only positive is that he makes us aware us of internship opportunities.

I had Tom for two classes as an adult learner several years ago. He is a class act who preaches practical knowledge. A great guy who cares as much as you care.�� The classes aren't too difficult if you show up for class, study a little and patictipate in the group projects. Oh yeah, and wear nice shoes...��
Great guy and very helpful and friendly also loves to take about real world application which makes the material interesting
Great guy. Doesn't pull any tricks and the material presented in class is very practical.

Literally just reads from the power point slides which gets a bit boring, but he pulls tests Q's from them. Exams aren't bad if you go to class, group projects suck. He is very arrogant which is annoying, also, he clearly does not have the time to teach the class due to his own engineering firm taking up his time which isn't fair to students
Great guy really fair and loves being an engineer and definitely loves life

I would strongly advise anyone to think carefully before joining her lab for an MS or PhD. Mentorship was very limited, with an expectation to self-teach and work independently with little guidance. She also expected makeup hours on weekends for sick days, and several PhD students have left the lab. Consider this before joining for your MS or PhD.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is the easiest class I have ever taken at Penn State I ended up with a 113%. She gives so much extra credit but most of the assignments are group based and she does take random attendance towards the end of the semester.

This class is extremely easy to get an A in as she gives a ton of extra credit.  Lectures are veryyy boring tho (she is a yapper), and she takes attendance so you have to attend.  2/4 of the homeworks and the final project is with groups. Overall, super easy BME elective.
The teacher says derogatory comments about America students

Very knowledgeable professor. Dr. Hasegawa's lectures were very interesting, and she is obviously very passionate about the subject. All of the homework took the form of group projects, but she was very accessible in case of conflicts within groups. Dr. Hasegawa gave a lot of extra credit, so it's pretty easy to get a good grade in this class.

DROP THIS CLASS IMMEDIATELY. She is a nice woman outside of class but she is so unorganized and unprepared. Expects you to be there every class but will cancel class randomly two hours before with no explanation. Unclear explanations of assignments and expectations. She clearly doesn't know how to use Canvas, blames things on us as students.

Gives the bare minimum explanation for all assignments and expects you to be able to figure out what she wants from you. When she does give instructions, they're extremely unclear and just cause more confusion. Loves to not put assignments on the calendar or to-do. Rambles during lecture and says very little that actually pertains to the class.
Doesn't explain any assignments and expects us to be professional public speakers

Not as harsh of a grader as it seems, she'll give scary feedback but then give you an A on your speech. The feedback is also useful to improve on your next speech. You can only miss three classes per semester, but I think that's pretty standard across all CAS100 courses. Definitely not bad to the point where you should drop if she's your professor.

A public speaking teacher that stands at the front of the class and reads slides for fifty minutes. Listen to her feedback; she will grade you on your improvement specifically in those areas. She often is unprepared for class, but seemingly expects a perfect attendance from her students. Not the greatest learning experience, would not take again.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. She is consistently unprepared and puts the bare minimum into teaching, yet expects the maximum from you. Her teaching in this class genuinely made me wonder if she was qualified to teach this at all. She will assign work with little instructions and grade with little explanation. Would not recommend

If you are kind and get your work done, you will be fine. The class is ok, kind of annoying, but whatever. Her feedback on speeches is great, so you know what to do better, but she is a very harsh grader. Just don't try too hard in the beginning, and it will look like you make amazing improvements through the semester.

There were tons of lectures, textbook readings, and lectures that felt unnecessary. She graded unclearly, too. The assignments weren't properly addressed/explained at times, so I had to give it my best shot and hope she wouldn't take off points. I usually enjoy public speaking, but she made the class not very enjoyable.
She may come off as tough but she genuinely cares about her students. Simply do what she asks and she will allow you space to grow.

Sister Judith is a solid teacher who you can tell knows what they are talking about. She gives genuine, honest advice and it is easy to grow and develop in that class. The more you take that class, the easier it gets and the better you do.
If you are fun in this class and everyone participates she is a very fun teacher but if everyone is silent it will just be boring lectures.
Sister Judith may come off as strict and rigid but she is incredibly honest with her advice on improvement and she genuinely cares.

She was very nice and you could definitely tell that she cared about all of her students. She definitely does have high standards but they are reachable standards and I saw improvement within myself because of her.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Professor Judith is very unwelcoming and does not accommodate her students who have accommodations. She is a very hard grader and has a very strict attendance policy. She is not a nice teacher and there are way better teachers out there for this class. I would never take this class again.

Bad teacher there are so many better ones, I would just drop immediately and get on the waiting list for another easier teacher. Don't waste your time with this class most likely you will get lower grades than you expect

Professor Udechukwu is a nun that shows up to her class everyday in a habit, but she has no empathy or care. She's cold to the students and refused to excuse my absences when I went to the hospital.

Horrible feedback on assignments. Takes forever to grade so good luck having a good understanding of your grade.

Do not take her.

DROP THE CLASS BEFORE IT IS TOO LATE. She is a really hard grader and assigns an excessive amount of work. Some days she canceled class and assigned a lot of work at 2pm that was due 6pm, the same day. There are many other easier teachers that grade easier and assign less work. but definitely drop and get out of there.
don't take it. take another teacher it will be easier
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Sister Udechukwu chooses favorites and grades unreasonably harsh for a CAS100 class. She is unclear about the guidelines of the speech, assignments, and when things are due. I attended all but three classes and worked hard to prepare for each one of my speeches, but only received subpar grades. Overall frustrating class.

Sister Judith was AMAZING, anyone who says otherwise is lazy and isn't capable of putting the bare minimum into the courses they pay for. CAS100A can be a tough class, especially for someone who doesn't love public speaking, but Sister Judith made such a comfortable and relaxed environment that it was easy for me and my classmates.

This professor is very moody with her grading and attitude towards students. She is not very accessible outside of class, often grades unfairly, treats students differently, and gives incredibly boring presentations. She's not tech savvy and is quite ignorant to students, doesn't even know our names. Do not take her!!

If you don't go to class, this class isn't for you. If you do, she explains the criteria for the speeches really well and gives good feedback. If you actually try in this class, she'll be really encouraging. But if you don't, she's going to return that energy.

She responds to all emails in timely fashion. The reading tests online are extremely boring but a majority of the grade is in the four main speeches. She is big on creating an inclusive community within the class. She is a lovely human being and does a lot of in class group work. Grading criteria is not clear. Make sure to attend class as well.

Professor Udechukwu's lack of concern is evident in her refusal to support students. Unnecessarily harsh grading scales and unfair assignment weighting increase frustration. Her unwillingness to assist reflects a lack of dedication. Overall, my experience was marked by indifference, harsh grading, and a lack of support. Absolutely not recommended.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am rating this professor again because I gave him a 1/5 when I was upset, so now I am giving him a 3/5 because overall I would say he was a 2/5. I didn't love his teaching style, but his grading was very generous which was his saving grace.

University of Utah Foundations of Analysis 2. I got an A+ in Foundations 1, but barely grasp it now. Cons: Lectures seem extremely disorganized. Does not follow the textbook, so if you don't understand what he's teaching, you're lost. The homework questions are ridiculously hard. Pros: records lectures and posts them on Youtube. Grading is lenient.

Uzman at the University of Utah is a fantastic teacher. His lectures are great and you can tell he is absolutely brilliant. The homework can get quite difficult, however, the exams were very easy comparatively. Overall, one of my favorite math classes so far.

The dude obviously cares deeply about math. Nice guy but this wasnt an easy class. If you figure out how to ask the right questions hell go into full detail and lay it all out for you. That was really helpful. Glad I took 251 with prof uzman.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: I fully taught myself this class. It could've been taken through mylabmath with no guidance from a person at all and there wouldn't have been a difference. Nice guy, horrible professor.
Nice guy. Has trouble actually explaining concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Knows his stuff but he doesn't explain it well sometimes. However, he's a good and funny dude. All grades came from exams and quizzes. Didn't teach us directly during COVID but provided lecture videos which was better IMO. Sometimes he uses weird notation and goes way too in depth, which is cool but confusing. Overall, not the best but far from bad

He is definitely the worst math "professor" (grad student) I've had at Penn State and if you know anything about them they all aren't good. He didn't teach us for half the semester when covid happened. The final practice exams went from 12 questions to having 24 and no one finished. He also gave an exam the day after THON worth 20% of our grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The most caring and understanding teacher. Get ready to read as that is the main homework along with responding to questions but its always the same structure which makes it easy and not stressful.

My favorite Spanish professor at Penn State. Although this class required a lot of reading, I learned how to become a better analyzer while also improving my Spanish. You can tell Juan cares about what he's teaching which makes class more engaging. The SEEQ closed before our class ended, and I wasn't able to complete one :( Take his class!

Juan is a caring professor. We covered lots of material on the textbook, but he made sure we understood everything. Apart from readings and comprehension questions... be ready to participate. This class will for sure help you learn while encouraging you out of your comfort zone.
I enjoyed Dr. Udaondo Alegres course quite a bit. I couldnt have had a better professor to teach me Don Quijote from beginning to end!

One of the best classes I have taken so far. As a native spanish speaker I was still challenged by the material and the discussions were amazing. It is not too hard, even for non-native speakers, as long as you participate and show enthusiasm for the literature. The books chosen were really good, and I loved the class and the teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Great professor! There is a lot of reading and homework, but you review the summary in class. Two papers and two tests that are mostly composed of free response questions. He's super nice and approachable. During COVID-19, he was very prepared for zoom classes and kept them engaging.
Extremely boring class. He reads exactly from the PowerPoint and will go over class time because he is too busy speaking. Attendance IS mandatory.

Professor Ulmer is a solid option for this course. You'll have 4 papers and 1 longer final paper throughout the semester, along with 3 exams and no final exam. He can be a little confusing during lectures since he has a tendency to say pickup words like “ya know” every 5 seconds, but he gives out study guides that are usually spot on for exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You would think that someone with a PhD would have enough intelligence to accurately teach information about his field. Nope. Dr. Ulmer is a horrible instructor and spends every class reading word for word off the slides or rambling about some irrelevant side story. Also, theres so little points in this course so one bad grade screws you over.

Professor Ulmer is a very nice guy, but I wouldn't take him again. This class was too much for a 200 level. There was only 500 points in a semester, so if you mess up one thing it really affects your grade. You have to write 5 papers throughout the year, and the last one is 10 pages. 3 exams and the mean was usually a 70%. No final though.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: You get clicker points for attending class, so it's worth it to go. Not very exciting, but he gets really into his lectures and knows what he's talking about. It's a basic crim course and there's a lot to over so you can't expect too much. 4 tests and if you study lecture notes and book chapters you'll do well!

Professor Ulmer is a nice guy, and he will help you out if you need it. There are 4 exams, and each tests you on the lectures (PowerPoint) and the book; exams are not hard if you study. Clicker questions are used for attendance, and are scored based off of participation, not accuracy of the answer. Overall a good class and a good professor!
He is soooooo boring, but the class is pretty easy as long as you study the book AND class notes.
A good professor over. His lectures can get boring. I took it as a GenEd and I learned a bunch. Take it how you will.

This class is pretty self explanatory from day one, I like Dr. Ulmer because he has a lot of credentials and really promotes his honors students. You need to read the book cover to back, his test aren't horrible and no cummulative final...I got an 89, 79, and 95 and got an A-. It's not that bad if you're a student who does the reading

The class itself is not that hard. However, it is painfully boring. Sit back and listen to him go through powerpoints over and over. Btw, the material on the slides are 'quote on quote' out of the book. Writing assignments get very repetitive and quite annoying by the end of the year. I don't recommend this class if you're looking for honors credit
A bit of writing, but nothing unmanageable. Great class

Very easy and flexible professor. Notes were straight out of the book. Very informal, discussion based class. Weekly assignments online which were fairly easy. Multiple choice and take home essay tests. Although it was not the most compelling class I've had in SOC, I did learn quite a bit. I would more highly recommend one of his crime classes!

He is such a nice guy and he loves Criminology. Yeah, lectures can be a bit dry and there were a lot of writing assignments, but exams were not bad and he was an easy grader. I learned so much in this class.

Can't really speak and present well, many random tangents and very difficult to listen to for a while. Good teacher though, but the book he uses is horrible and the notes and the book don't always have the answer which make you go looking elsewhere or ****ting the paper.

Ulmer is  a nice guy and if you pay attention teh quizes and tests arent bad its just really hard to pay attention.  There are a lot of ways to bring up your grade though if you do bad on the quizes.  the midterm was all essay and hard and the final was either essay or you could write a paper.

Dr. Ulmer's a nice guy, but I agree with the consensus on his boredom level. Since my class was a freshman seminar, he frequently talked down to us... and while I know he was just trying to be helpful, he mostly just lulled us to sleep. In short: takes interesting material and dumbs it down.

I thought this class was going to be interesting, and it is, it's just that he's the boring one.  Everything he said went through one ear and out the other, b/c he can litterally knock you right to sleep once he starts talking.  If you like clj, take another teacher unless u like sleeping in class.

They didn't post the final or even made it available to be seen until the day it was due for an online course. If you are taking an online course you have a full time job and have to plan your assignments ahead of time and that is what the calendar in Canvas is for. She decided to not post it and I never saw it dropping me from an A to a B

Professor Vora is a very sweet person but her teaching style is very jumpy and disjointed. Was corrected by students many times and often doesn't explain what she's doing when coding which can be really confusing. Also often misunderstand student's questions and provides unrelated answers. Sweet person but really frustrating class to learn in.

Professor Vora is nice, but she doesn't really know how to teach a class well. Classes are spent with her just writing code and you copying it because she doesn't teach any of the concepts very well. If you go to class, she will basically give you the answers to most of the assignments. It's also difficult to understand her sometimes.

Absolute waste of a class. Each assignment was the equivalent of doing one leetcode problem once a week and have another person posting video lectures that are not thought out at all prior to them beginning it. This legit feels like a 100 level class with a student teaching it. I am online student btw. Do not take a class with this professor
Just don't. Whatever you do PICK A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR.

Professor Vora is a sweetheart. I had never done programming before so I was intimidated by the class, but she lead us step by step. There is a language barrier, but she is a good listener and wants us to succeed. She had great TA's that helped with questions. I never missed a class and did my work on time, I think that contributed to my success.

about a week before the final, she dropped nearly everyone's grade by 4 points because we didn't complete a programming competition in time. she ended up dropping the grade as it was the lowest score of the semester for almost anyone in the class. sucks because i was hoping she would drop a new previous assignment  in the semester. DO NOT TAKE HER.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is a good person, easy to reach outside of class. But, her grading is terrible and she grades really tough. I would never take her class again. I can barely understand her and her teaching is all over the place.
If you have a chance to take a section without Urja - do it. I lost my sanity in her abomination of a class
no, just no
She's rude and she doesn't provide clear directions. Would love to Kirk Colbain myself than take another class with her

I genuinely cannot stress enough how much of a DISGRACE Vora is to the college of IST. I entered my first semester of freshman year having no idea of how to code. I will most likely have to drop out of the college due to the fact that I simply cannot learn anything from her. PSU setting their students up for failure by employing her. simply unfair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: she barely speak english
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Was good teacher tbh. I did fine with her and I have no prior knowledge of java.

Was a pretty good professor honestly. This was my second time taking java and it was so much better this time around. She drops a-lot of assignments that are your lowest grades. She always posts the lectures and powerpoints with videos attached.

By far the worst professor I have ever had in my time at Penn State. She is impossible to understand and her grading criteria are unclear. Her lectures are extremely boring and you can't follow along to what she is saying pretty much all the time. She will meet with you but she is no help. I seriously do not understand how she is still employed.
She is a very kind person, however class is often confusing and assignments don't correspond to classwork.
Please never take this professor. If you don't know how to code find a different teacher. Do not make my mistake. She is awful at teaching.

THE WORST. Has no idea how to teach or explain anything. ZERO classroom control/management. She is so hard to understand and if you've never coded before, or don't know Java, DO NOT take IST140 w/ her. She just talks and types and does nothing else. Textbook readings are USELESS. DO NOT TAKE IST 140 WITH HER - there are many other professors.

If you want to salvage your mental and physical health, do not take this class. No clear grading criteria, no clear feedback, lecture slides are useless + no programming is taught, 12+ hours of work each week. She'll meet outside of class but is no help. I've never been so distraught, discouraged, and exhausted. 
Goodbye to my GPA and my wellbeing.

There is a very strong language barrier, making it difficult to understand the information. She makes mistakes in almost every single line of code we do and does not tell us what she is changing, so we have to find it ourselves. Whenever we have questions, she usually says something like "how do you solve this" like idk.

I can not understand a single word that is said during class. When she presents the information in class, she routinely messes up and then starts the topic over, only to mess up again, which leads to incredible confusion. It is very difficult to know what she is asking for in assignments. The textbook is the savior of my grade. Very nice lady.

MASSIVE AMOUNT of HOMEWORK and no idea what she is looking for. Supposedly, the assignments are not supposed to take that long but you will most likely spend at least 2-3 hours/assignment not including the work on the group project. She will say one thing in class but then when you do that, she will take points off or give vague answer to questions

Class wasn't difficult; but it was very confusing and chaotic which was really annoying. She has trouble differentiating the boundry between the actual requirements in a real world project and what she expects students. For example she'll say something like "you need to log this info, it is crucial" but doesn't actually expect you to code it.

Hands down worst class I have taken at Penn State. Lectures are extremely dull & she never covers assignment concepts. I never understood assignment instructions & she gives no feedback. Ask questions & she provides vague and unhelpful answers. Sometimes LAs & professor didn't show up to their own office hours. I was just confused & overwhelmed.

Grading is harsh & I was accused of cheating on an assignment that I did not cheat on. I denied cheating and offered to show her whatever she wanted to prove that fact, she claimed I had copied someone else's code and gave me a zero. You're basically teaching yourself through zybooks. Her english is very difficult to follow as well in emails

Kind professor but does not know how to teach. There are four programming assignments that weigh half of the entire grade so you don't wanna mess up. Had to learn everything outside the class myself. Her assignment instructions are vague so you NEED to ask her how to do the assignments or you will probably be screwed. HARD class try to avoid.

Her reviews for IST 311 sum it up. I do not learn anything in this class and never really show up anymore because all she does in class is type code. We have to teach ourselves if we want to succeed in this class. The professor is a very sweet person but she is one of the worst teachers that I have ever experienced during my 3 years at Penn State.

One of the worst classes I have ever taken so far. (11th week) New professor who just doesn't know how to teach correctly. Stands in the front of the class and codes silently most of the time. Also never respects the students time and goes over the class period by 3-4 mins every single time.  Do not take this professor if you do not have to.

All she does is code silently in front of the class, and once in a while talks about something but does not explain the code. Only 1/3 of the class shows up anymore (Writing during week 10). Her programming assignments take a lot of time because you have to teach yourself what you are doing while doing them. I haven't learned anything in this class

I had her during her second semester teaching. She is still learning how to be a professor. Expect 8-12 hrs of group-based hw per week. To succeed, ask her questions after class regarding how to do the assignments. Ask her to give examples so you know exactly what she is looking for. Her canvas instructions can be vague and unclear.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Was I the biggest fan? No. However, she helped outside of class, recognized genuine efforts, made many accommodations (deadline extensions, reducing final exam weight), and dealt with the growing pains as a first-semester professor while also handling a poorly-designed/vaguely-specified course. However, she also added unneeded difficulty at times.

She does not explain the material were expected to know. A typically class day consists of her doing a program and not explaining any aspects of it. In addition to this, we were quizzed on material that we did not learn. To pass this class, I had to seek the help of the teaching assistants and teach myself everything I needed to know.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
If you are looking to enter into a class where you can learn absolutely nothing and secure a decent grade this is where you should go! 

Group projects are available so that you can suffer together and engage in group catharsis!

The exams were very difficult too and the TAs never seem to give any partial credit at all. But the curve was insane, 50 for a C and a 55 for a B-. He is the most caring Professor and he tried to help all his students as much as possible with the projects.

Projects were way too hard and the guidance we were given on them ranged from unhelpful to making things even more confusing. Project 3 sample code was a mess, had to be revised multiple times, and barely anyone could do it. Avoid

Gives decent lectures and pretty willing to help students with extensions/accommodations, however the class was not well organized. One project (worth 20% of our grade) had very unclear instructions and multiple code updates and significant changes to submission/grading after being released

This man told me to repeat a class that I got an A in. He said this to me because I spoke out on zoom when he expected us to know something that we were not explicitly taught. This was a terribly unorganized class.

Hardest class I've taken at this school and I hope and pray I don't take harder, makes 311 feel like a joke. Gives grad level projects for an undergrad CMPSC class. CSE-511 with Prof. Urgaonkar was the defining course of my graduate degree. He makes the course as interesting as it is difficult. The exams were way too challenging and needed big curves to get people to pass. Bhuvan is very knowledgeable, but the lectures got boring and he was not of big help in office hours.,

Easily one of the best CSE professors here at Penn State, especially for a class like CMPSC 473 which could turn out to be one of the hardest materials you will learn if not taken by a good professor. Never miss any class taught by him. This was one of the very few classes where I couldn't ever take my attention off the lectures. SO GOOD!

reviews.comment: One of the best professors in the CSE department you'll ever take. His lectures are so amazing. He's great at explaining everything with great examples.
Nice professor with strong conceptual background.

Professor Bhuvan tried his best to teach. He is also knowledgeable, but he did not make his grading clear. In the first lecture, he said 90% overall grade will be an A with a small change. it turned out 95% is A. I dont consider it as a small change. He gave 10% bonus which was very hard to save your grade, but I prefer not do it with 90%.

While he's very smart and makes topics interesting, some of the explanations can go over your head. Textbook is fantastic (and free). Tries his best to be fair.

reviews.comment: He is really good. The course is definitely worth taking. He introduced everything in a clear manner.

Dr. Bhuvan is a great professor. His class is relatively tough but there is a lot to gain from it. There are only 4 projects but each is worth 15% of the grade and are pretty challenging.  He is always ready to help you out and will also allow you to replace the projects with any project idea that you want to work on

Homeworks were really long but each were only worth 2.5% of your grade. I really enjoyed his lectures and the course material. The book was fantastic and easy to read. However, he did not do a good job preparing students for the exams. The questions would not have been as difficult had he spent more time on it in class. TA's did the grading.

Don't take this class if you want to be spoon-fed. But if you want to be exposed to real OS stuff, great collection of papers. Great exams and projects. Disorganized but I had great meetings during office hours and learnt a lot!

No planning for class, no proper course structure. Very unclear lectures, very boring and bad jokes, very useless slides and hard-to-read papers! I learnt simply nothing in this course. As a grad student, I had more expectations. Extremely difficult exams, 4 papers to read every week, incessant and pointless questioning in class with no answer!
too cool

Dr. Abaci is an amazing Professor. His lectures are entertaining, and during discussions heavily questions your point of view on certain things, in a good way.

Really good professor, great lectures. Not a ton of assignments -- dropped some from the syllabus entirely -- but you learn a lot about the five or so philosophers he covers in the class. Gives you the set of possible exam questions in advance so exams are pretty easy.

reviews.comment: I am a senior philosophy major and Dr. Abaci's class was by far the best I have taken at Penn State. He clearly outlines what is expected of his students. He has a really good sense of humor and gives you warnings before pop quizzes. He also has helpful review sessions before the midterm and final.

Really great professor, with interesting subject material, make sure you go to class or you won't do as well as you want to. Class is 80% discussion and 20% lecture, he will absolutely make you question your beliefs.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Abaci is an amazing lecturer. I had never been too interested in moral philosophy until I took this class with Dr. Abaci. The class was almost completely discussion based with a few quizzes, homework, and two tests. The class is a lot more interesting if you actively participate in the discussions because he takes everyone's ideas into account.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

awesome class. i do not recommend if you're not into philosophy  or reading a lot.

I tried to give him a chance but it's an unequivocal no. He is not who I want to be learning from and has no lived experience in the subject of Black Freedom Movements. And the lectures do not capture interest.

The weird thing is I think he thinks the class is going well. It's not. On top of all my other grievances, he does not return our assignments in a timely fashion. It's bad enough having to do the assignments, let alone wait forever to get the assignment back. I do not recommend.

Going to this class makes me feel so depressed. I don't think he's a good teacher because he's constantly fumbling around and doesn't do a good job lecturing. Assignments are a headache and I want to let everyone know they are better off studying this subject on their own and not taking the class.

I am not happy with this guy. He seems out of place teaching us and honestly other students in the class seem to know more about the topic than him. Why is he here? It feels like a waste taking this class but I cant drop it due to schedule issues.

This guy desn't know anything about the subject, where did they get him from? It's obvious he's uncomfortable and lacks expertise. Also, his assignments are not explained well. What a horrible experience going to class is.
Guy is so awful and disappointing. I almost cried on day 1 when I realized he was the prof. I think there is still time to drop this course. I hope.

I took his class over the summer, and he did a good job of not stressing us out.  There's a pop quiz once a week, but if you do the readings, you should be fine.  He loves what he teaches and he's great to have a conversation with. He gives good feedback on work. As long as you go to class and to the readings, you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Respected

reviews.comment: Wouter is a great professor, very humble and willing to work with students. The pop quizzes are generally very easy if you pay attention to his lecture he emphasizes what is going to put on the tests, you don't have to do the readings if you pay attention in class but they will help your quiz grades. The reflections are easy points.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Made well organized handouts that outlined what we did in class. Was willing to give feedback on essay outlines which was very helpful. Helped me become a better writer.

Dr. Umar seems like a good guy. The class is REALLY hard. He also has a heavy accent which makes it hard to understand especially when all the topics are pretty much just glazed over. I wish there were more detailed explanations for the topics covered. I get it's a “weed out class” but it's so difficult. If you don't NEET the class, DON'T TAKE

Lectures are boring and often times they don't cover all the material needed to get through the HW. Labs suck, recitations are boring but somewhat helpful. Dr. Umar is nice and really smart, but can't seem to dumb material down for everyone. I took AP physics in HS and it absolutely carried me. Most exam averages were in the 60s..

He is a very sweet and intelligent guy however he is not good at teaching. The lectures were very boring with very few examples to prepare for the exam. The labs were pointless and a waste of time. Most students learned from the GSG leader in the fall semester. Would recommend lion tutors if lectures do not make sense.

Dr. Umar does not deserve the hate he receives. His exams were much easier than last semester's and still got curved 5-10 points each time. Phys 250 is a hard class to begin with and if you come into it with zero understanding of physics then you are already behind. The GSGs w/ Nero were most helpful and the practice exams were just like the exams
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Physics is hard but he doesn't make it worse than it has to be. Lectures aren't great but they're not mandatory. You do have to teach yourself a lot. 1 homework assignment/week, lab & recitation, 3 exams. The exams are hard but he curves so the average is 70 (we had 10-15 point curves). Cumulative final hurt my grade but the class is not terrible.

He's grown on me a little bit. He can be hard to understand, but in general his lectures are useful and concise, even if they aren't delivered in the most engaging way. Exams are tough, but can be passed. Homework can also be difficult (1 assignment per week). Class overall is time consuming because of the lectures plus lab and recitation.

He's not terrible. Yes, his lectures can be a bit dull/inaudible at times, and he covers material quickly, but Dr. Umar himself is a pretty decent person. If you go to office hours, he's willing to help and make himself available. There are only 2 exams and 1 final, so not much room for error there. YOU WILL HAVE TO PUT IN WORK, but you can pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Exams with questions that don't even have correct answers, TAs that don't show up to office hours, oversimplified lecture slides with insane exams (averages in the 50s), this class is a nightmare. Dr. Umar is also disorganized and is not the best instructor for this class. I studied through the orgo tutor and got an A, never went to class.

He isn't as bad as people say he is in the reviews. He can mumble at time during the lectures, but he had demos during the lecture to help you understand. He was a nice guy who gave extra credit and allowed me to retake an old assignment. If you've taken physics 1 before, you'll be fine.

This class was extremely difficult. He went through lectures very quickly and I felt like they were really oversimplified. Recitations and labs were really easy and boost your grade but in no way did I find them helpful for exams in the slightest. To give Umar credit, when I went into office hours he helped me out.

DO. NOT. TAKE. DR. UMAR. This man is the absolute worst. His lectures are so ungodly boring and his mumbling is the cherry on top. He's condescending and rude when you speak to him. Recitation is a waste of time and lab never has anything to do with lecture. Exams are super tough, nothing like class, and both had failing averages. He deserves a 0/5

For example, on a practice exam it said, "What is the amplitude of the net wave to the right of both speakers are identical sources?" He claimed it was not grammatically correct, but understandable.

Dr.Umar is a nice man, but horrible instructor. He would not explain concepts, asked many theoretical questions on exams, and skipped steps which confused students. Our first class average he lied saying it was a 55, when it was a 37.5 in which he gave 17.5 points of partial credit, then curved by 15% to get it to a 70 average. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful professor. The exams were so difficult too. They never lined up with what we did in class. I don't think he realized that half of the people in this class need a good grade in physics to get into PT or med school, he simply doesn't care.

Professor Umar may have been one of the worst professors I have ever had. He always seemed like he didn't have time to teach or help out his students and rushed lectures. He was also very rude and sassy and always thought he was right. DO NOT TAKE HIS CLASS RUN IF YOU CAN. The average for exams was also almost always in the 40s. live love Umar!!!!!

THE LECTURE NOTES ARE SO OVERSIMPLIFIED AND THE EXAM QUESTIONS AREN'T. You would think the exams were written by a completely different person. You might as well use your basic level high school notes instead of going to class.   
2 MID TERMS + FINAL btw
Oh and the equation sheet is so useless. Clearly hasn't been updated with the notes.

Awful. Avoid him at all cost. He covers the bare minimum in lecture and expects you to understand how to apply it to harder problems. The averages on the exams are so low he has to add a huge curve or else everybody would fail the class. Be ready to teach yourself everything. He can't teach at all.

Been at Penn State for 3 years and he is by far the worst professor I have ever had. Never answers any questions, the first exam average was a 48% and he lied saying it was a 55%. He doesn't seem to really understand physics at all and how he is employed is beyond me. The "extra" credit he offered wasn't actually extra and is mandatory.

I think he was an OK professor. He is helpful when you need it but he should improve in explaining concepts and formulas. Practice is so helpful for this class. The labs and recitations help a lot, though.

Mumbles through his lectures, and bails on his office hours at least once a week. GSG sessions are also available.

reviews.comment: Professor Umar is one of the worst professors I have had in my time at Penn State. His accent along with the terrible explanations of concepts and practice problems has made my time in physics miserable. He rushes through everything, does not explain any steps in detail. I have had to teach myself all the concepts online through other sources.
Terrible at explaining things in his own words on physics concepts. Avoid taking physics with him at all costs.

Probably one of the worst professors I've had. He doesn't explain anything well and you basically have to teach yourself. I recommend going to GSG (guided study group) because you don't learn anything during lectures. There are two exams and a final, the averages were 55% and 58%. Take another professor if you can because you will be suffering.

He only reads off of the slides and expects you to know everything before you even show up to class. He gives sample exams before tests to help you study, but somehow the actual test is the complete opposite of the material he tells you to practice. Literally cannot teach, only thing that helped was GSG, but the professor himself is nonexistent.

DO NOT TAKE DR. UMAR. This man is the absolute worst. His lectures are so ungodly boring and his mumbling is the cherry on top. He's condescending and rude when you speak to him. Recitation is a waste of time and lab never has anything to do with lecture. Exams are super tough. If you can take any other professor, do it.

He rushes through the lectures and provides little help even in office hours. He does not post solutions to practice exams, only puts the letter answers. The first exam average was a 55%, with a 15 point curve, and he told us as the students he was disappointed in the score, even though he admitted he made the exam too difficult.

Horrible. His lecture slides are full of material that he quickly goes over and then moves on to the next slide with no explanation. He attempts to do work on the "Whiteboard" of his iPad but his handwriting is so messy you cannot read it and it makes no sense. The average of the first exam was a 55 and had to be curved 15%.

Extremely easy class as long as you go to class and do the work. At-home quizzes every week, along with some easy group projects, make up most of the grade. There is graded attendance based on participation, but it isn't that hard. Should definitly take this class for a free A.

This class was one of the easiest GenEds I've taken. Her lectures are easy and everything is mostly online. There are only a few projects which determine your grade so as long as you attend those lecutres you can get an easy A. You can get away with not attending most lecutres though.

reviews.comment: Took as an online class and it was a great gen ed. Super easy to understand and not too much work. At times, the assignments were confusing/worded weirdly, but none of them were too hard too complete. There is a weekly quiz and reflection, and then a couple bigger projects every few weeks to help prepare for your final project. Would take again.
Really cool class and Professor Nimmo's lectures are always very interesting. As long as you go to class and put in some effort you should be fine.
This class was relatively easy to take online and provided a lot of info about geology in general. Weekly reflections and assessments, along with bigger projects every couple of weeks.
Lectures are boring, mostly content that can be found on online portion, hard to hear and very saturated content, dry reads

reviews.comment: I liked her a lot! Her class was easy (I'm not sure why most people are saying it's way too difficult), and the group project was easy too. Considering you show up to class and have decent partners for the project, you will get an A.
Honestly one of the best classes/ professors i've taken. show up once a week and you will get an A. She's so understanding and straight forward
Pretty good class. Professor was very nice and understanding if students had issues. Do your work and you'll get an easy A.

This class is far too challenging for a Gen Ed. Compared to my 400 level classes, this class has been the hardest of the semester. It is challenging to receive assistance outside of class. Additionally, you have a group project with randomly assigned students. All of the material is graded harshly, and weekly quizzes are hard to get 100% on.

Way too tough of a grader for a 1 level class. Grades things and will take off points with very little feedback and an undescriptive rubric. It is not hard, just a ton of work for a 1N class.

reviews.comment: Lectures are long and dry. She thinks this class is a 400-level class and not a Gen Ed. There are weekly quizzes, sometimes 2, that require you to read pages and pages of uploaded documents. There are also in-depth papers you have to write that are single-spaced.

reviews.comment: Worst class of my life,not because of the topic (immunology is amazing) but because of Dr. W. Take it with ANYONE ELSE. She was passive aggressive and couldn't teach. Exams were extremely detail-oriented, had to memorize ~200 protein abbreviations each time. She also said the final was cumulative a week before; average was in the 60s with no curve

Dr. Wacleche made MICRO 410 a forgiving course. She offered about 20% of extra credit which really saves your overall grade since exams are tough. If you go to her group study sessions, meet with her one on one and show you want to do well, she will work for you. Overall, a very challenging class but you will pass if you attend lecture!

Dr. Wacleche made Immunology a very forgiving course. The exams were difficult and application, but she offered 4 open-note extra credit pop quizzes that were worth 5% extra credit each; in theory, you could get 20% ec, plus she gives 2% ec for doing the SEEQ and 1% for doing in-class practice. There are 4 HWs that have 2 attempts each (5% each).

Dr. Wacleche is funny and genuinely caring. She offers a lot of extra credit through random in-class quizzes, making attendance crucial. However, lectures rely on dense slides read quickly, so you'll need to self-teach. All 4 exams are much, much harder than lectures. Show up to class and never fall behind. Take it with someone else if you can.

Definitely a caring professor, but goes through the material too quickly to understand in depth (+thick accent). Grade is just quizzes/ exams (+ a few ec quizzes). Exams were pretty difficult as they were application based when we were basically taught definitions. Generous grading system (75 = B). Overall, not a great class, avoid if possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: 100% of the grade is exams and quizzes. A few EC quizzes with very hard questions. She does a decent good job of teaching the material but does rush through slides and cannot explain everything in depth. This is a problem because of how in depth this class is. No homework or in class questions, just straight yap for 50 minutes very hard to focus.
Has yet to teach a class. Class is taught by the ta.

His syllabus is a bit lengthy, but he is very great about it. The concepts are very practical and easily relatable to actual research. It's suggested you actually put in the work and study for the course.
He's an amazing professor. Always ready to explain any of the concepts we don't understand. Very friendly and caring.

This professor never show up. He hands lecture to a PhD student. I couldn't believe some PhD student was teaching a 400 level class. All he did was reading the slides and no examples to help us to understand.

The class is purely memorization which suck because even if you are struggling and go to him for help he will tell you to just study harder. the homework have nothing to do with the exam, lectures are boring he just reads the notes barely explains them avoid him if memory and a professor who doesn't care about your progress is not your thing

Although attendance is not taken or graded and the lectures are very boring, you MUST show up to class if you want to succeed. The exam reviews are also helpful for connecting lecture and exam content. You need to review the entire chapter front to back to do well on exams! Write chemical structures and create flashcards to drill the concepts.

reviews.comment: This class is mostly a memorization game, so it will range in difficulty person-by-person. Randy is awesome and he cares so much about his subject. The homework kind of sucks bc they aren't relevant to the tests, but the in class review sessions are so helpful. This class becomes very hard the minute you stop attending class, even tho its tempting.

This class is completely unfair. The whole thing is memory but what he does now is he completely changes the exam from the review. I have gone over the review millions of times but still failed the exam. To base a class completely off memory is unfair and if you even wanted to learn anything, his lectures are boring and at 9/10 AM.
Pure memory test. Very exam heavy. Homeworks are cakewalks compared to most other STEM courses, but watch out for the quizzes, they tended to destroy people's avg. grades when I took the class.

Your grade is based on 5 exams and one project. Your lowest exam grade gets dropped. I didn't show up to class after the first week and only attended the TA lead review sessions. Memorizing everything covered at the review session is pretty much a guaranteed A.

This professor always make things complicated and he is a tough grader. You have to do the film analysis quiz in class and also plot quiz every week.

Took ASIA 404Y. Super boring, unresponsive to emails. Doesn't even sound like he knows what he's talking about. Class time is dependent on whether or not you know random facts about the poet. At first glance you may think Dr. Volland's class is going to be boring and uninteresting, but give it a few classes. The more deep you get into the texts, the more interesting the in-class discussions become. Make sure to read every text assigned and be prepared to write 8 response papers throughout the semester. Overall easy class.

Do not take his class. His class is awful and worthless.
Don't take this class. The teacher is awful and boring. I fell asleep almost every class.
He is a tough grader. It doesn't matter if you go to class or not, but if you don't a participate in class, you will get poor participation grade. I will never take his class again.

Personally I found him to be a great professor. When you get past his stuttering and accent, you'll be fine. He expects you to do the readings and come to class to participate. He only gives credit for what's right for him. You can never have your own thoughts, and if you do that, he will take off points.
Good, nice teacher
If you just do the weekly extra credit you can get literally get A. I finished this class with overall 111%.

If you consider this class as an easy general education course, you will regret. Passionate about AI. Highly knowledgeable. Deeply cares about helping students master the core ideas, strengths and limitations of AI. Course covers not just technical stuff but also ethical considerations and impacts of AI. Great course. Amazing prof.

I course was amazing. Dr. Vasant is an amazing teacher.  He covered the philosophical roots, concepts, and ethical considerations of AI. I feel ready to explore AI in greater depth in follow-up courses. Great course from a highly knowledgeable professor.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. Class is all lectures, but his voice is so monotone that you cannot understand a single thing. LAs are not helpful as well. They are very bad with emails. There's a midterm and a final, which are worth less in the gradebook than the homework (hw is worth 50% of your grade). Overall, I would advise against taking the class.

reviews.comment: Professor Honavar's course was very difficult. lectures were long and boring, he would read off his 100 slide powerpoints. The material was very complex and hard for an introductory level class. do not take AI100 as a gen ed. there are much easier classes.

The lectures were great. The lecture notes which he provided were really great. They explained the core concepts really well. I have printed them out so I have them as reference. Great course. Amazing instructor.

I am an Econ major. I had very little exposure to computing before I took this course. I learned a lot. I had to work hard. I showed up in Dr. Honavar's office hours often. He was always patient with me and answered even the most basic questions. I am expecting a hard-earned A
If you want to learn about AI and are not allergic to thinking, reading or math, this is a fantastic course. I loved it.

The course covers basics of AI really well. It is not a coding course. It covers concepts. It has no programming prerequisites, so that makes sense. It is not a cookbook course. Completing assigned readings and homework is really important. If you try to use chatGPT to do your homework, or try to cram the material before the exam you will fail.

If you want to learn about AI, take this course. The professor is extremely knowledgeable and breaks down complex concepts into easy-to-understand pieces. The lecture notes he provided and the slides were extremely helpful. He is accessible outside of class, and welcomes questions in class.

Honestly, this was the worst class I've ever taken in the IST school, and I'm an IST major. He was insanely boring and monotone and just talked about the same thing over and over again. He literally talked about the Turing Test for a month straight. For an  AI-related clas,s IST130 is 100% better than this.

we learned about the history of computation and then got into depth about coding and agents. His lectures are a snooze fest. He is very monotone and hard to understand. We do not do a single practice problem in class, there is no teaching, just talking. I would end up spending the whole week before an exam teaching myself the whole curriculum.

I am a freshman taking this AI course. I was nervous because I did not have advanced math or programming coming in. Dr. Honavar makes difficult concepts really easy to understand. The course notes and slides really help. His lectures are amazing. After taking this class, I am really excited about AI and want major in AI.

I never expected to have the opportunity to take such an amazing course about AI from a top AI researcher in my freshman year. I compared notes with friends taking senior undergrad course in AI. Dr. Honavar makes topics that even seniors struggle with accessible to freshmen. I am loving this course and would highly recommend it to everyone.

I took this course as a freshman. Seniors in computer science told me it is impossible to learn about AI before I took a lot of CS and Math courses. But Dr. Honavar demystifies AI and shows how to build systems that behave as if they have minds. The study guide walks you through readings and useful resources. Great course.
Great professor

I took this course to learn about causal modeling and causal inference. Prof. Honavar's knowledge of the topic is encyclopedic. He had a great way to motivate the problems, the theory, approaches, and pitfalls of causal inference from observations. The lectures offered examples and deep insights that are hard to find elsewhere. Great professor.

Prof. Honavar is a great professor, with his lectures being among the best I have seen at PSU. He knows what he is talking about and explains all classroom topics with ease. The homeworks in 197G are all you need to study for the exams, along with paying attention to lectures. This class is structured to help you learn, not crush you with exams.

Lectures aren't very engaging, it was mostly boring, although I thought that the topics were interesting. Much of the material could be taught in a faster manner. Questions are worded ambiguously, very hard to understand what he wants you to answer.

Prof. Honavar's course demystifies AI, teaches the core elements of AI  to first year students without much background. The course connects AI to philosophy and brain science which I found really cool. I took  the course when it was taught for the first time. I believe it will be taught regularly as A-I 100. I hope Dr. Honavar will teach it.

The prof. is simply great. Very knowledgeable, passionate about AI, and makes AI really fun and exciting to learn about. I really loved how he connected AI to philosophy and computing. If you can take only one course on AI, take this course. Prof. Honavar provided very detailed (350+ pages) of typed up lecture notes. I hope he publishes it.

I took this course in my freshman year. I could not have had a better way to begin my studies at Penn State. Dr. Honavar is a top Ai researcher. This was an amazing introduction that demystified AI and computing. I loved every minute of it. I hope to take more courses from Dr. Honavar before I graduate. I can't wait for the new AI major to launch.

This is a new introductory freshman level general education course on artificial intelligence. I was unsure how such an advanced topic could be taught to students with little or no computing background.
