reviews.comment: Only good thing about the class ,she is an interesting lecturer. Everything else is a mess. Assignments either not graded or graded months later. Exams are openbook because she takes points off for random reasons. Same goes for group projects where TA's are also harsh graders. Dont take this class seriously, and youll probably get a better grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: she seems like a nice person, but this class stressed me out, even tho I'm really into corrections. she provides no rubrics for tests/assignments, and no feedback explaining why she took off points on essay question responses. she also spends a lot of class time showing videos that could easily be watched outside class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Had such a great time this class. It is a lot of work if you care about you grade and want to get an A. Quiz on canvas for every chapter every weekend (very easy). exams are also easy but make sure to read the chapters.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Yevchak gives a very interesting lecture, I have had her from CRIM 12 and 100, you can tell she is passionate about what she does which in turn makes you genuinely interested in her teaching, if you are having difficulty she generally has office hours that are very accessible to clear things up, use your resources shes definitely one of them
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Does not post announcements or interact with the online class at all.  Her participation was the bare minimum.

This class is very discussion based. There aren't many powerpoint slides, but write down everything you see in her class because she doesn't post the notes. If you take the exams based on the lectures, you'll get at least a B. But if you add material from the book, you'll get an A. She goes on tangents often, but covers all necessary material.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: I had Mrs. Yevchak as a Crim/Soc 012 instructor and CRIM 100 instructor. Her lectures are very discussion based and her notes are very sparse. Her exams are lecture heavy and videos we watched in class. Her attendance policy doesn't match with her syllabus and I managed to a get C. She doesn't respond to emails quickly and gets side tracked
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I enjoyed the class in Soc 12 but not so much in crim 100. The attendance policy is a lie on the syllabus. It says if you're absence 2 or less you get the full 10%. But then the last week when it was graded, she said it was more than attendance. So you might have to answer a few questions in class. Lectures are slow and reading is a MUST.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: While she seems to be passionate about her teaching, she is terrible at it. Many lectures consisted of her talking about her experience on the EMS or watching videos. While attendance is mandatory, tests were based entirely from the textbook. Can honestly say this this was the worst class I've ever taken and Yevchak is the worst CRIM prof at PSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: She takes way too much time away from actual lecturing to encourage class discussion. The same 4 students talk each class. I personally found this insufferable. Easy quizzes, hard tests. The tests are filled with unclear questions where multiple answers could be correct. She doesn't post lecture slides and gets off track during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I honestly didn't mind Dr. Yevchak. Her lectures definitely didn't cover all necessary material, but in place you have interesting and thorough class discussions about the topic at hand, and you learn the rest from the textbook. You get on her good side if you participate. Outside of class, she genuinely cares about her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: If you do not fit her reasoning or agenda, she will give you a horrid grade.  Such in the case of the death penalty, if your answer is not to her liking with evidence; she will maintain a chip and will slowly lower your grade.  Hint, know her agenda.  She will respond late to your questions, but wont except late work.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She barely gives notes during class and the things she talks about during class are irrelevant half the time.  If you don't read the book you'll fail the exam. You only get 2 skips for class even though you could literally never show up and just read the book and get an A.

Worst class I have ever had to take for my major.  I didnt learn any relevant info from the lectures because she goes on tangents & tells stories about her friends who apparently have a lot of trouble with the law. We were very behind in class. She isnt clear on assignments &  test questions, then takes points off because it's not what she wanted
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Have to go to every class and it's a good way to boost your grade up. Must read every chapter assigned for the homework quizzes. Tests are very tricky and a lot of questions that weren't in the textbook or talked about it class. Class is somewhat boring and mostly discussion based.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: None of her lectures make sense. She repeats stuff so many times in class in a way that is not useful. There is no review for exams,  and the only way she slightly helps you out is by dropping the two lowest quiz grades. She also says um often. If you skip more than twice you lose points. Wouldn't recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: good class
She is very passionate about teaching and truly enjoys asking the class questions to get our perspective.

I read the textbook, I highlight the book, I take good notes in class, and I have regular attendance to her lectures. So why am I not doing as well as I want to in her class? The answer: she has a TERRIBLE structure of exams and quizzes. Double questions, grammatical errors, and irrelevant questions highlight her way of "teaching". Do not take.

I'm going into my senior year next semester and this was so far my LEAST favorite class I have taken yet at Penn state. The class itself was very watered-down and chaotic; for example when I got home my notes made no sense even copied verbatim. She prides herself on not using any "quizlet questions" but they end up being either idiotic or very hard

Horrible lecturer, slides have absolutely no information and rather than expand on them she goes off on a tangent and talks about herself and all the friends she has who have been arrested.  Tests are grammatically incorrect and have so many repeat questions it's nauseating.  Seriously made me consider switching out of this major. Avoid if you can.
She is very passionate about sociology. She's also a very quirky person but she's funny and very likeable.

Let me start with the positivity of the class. She is nice, talkative, illustrative. I learned alot in this class. On the other hand, her exams are tough. You have to study the book, outside reading, lectures she presented. I study alot and got 90 on the first and 82 on the second. You can get 100s in quizes if you studied the book prior the quiz.
Worst class I have ever taken. Bring your butt and your clicker to class every day. Her slides are stupid and unorganized and never relevant to the lesson. Read the book thats your only hope.
The exam and quiz questions are often trick questions and do not test your knowledge of the material. The class is very slow and boring and she spends a lot of time explaining simple concepts.

If you're looking for an interesting, basic gen. ed class this isn't it. Lectures are boring , tend to go off topic, and are not online to look over. Exams are poorly constructed and test no knowledge of the overall understanding of the chapter. Quizzes are weekly and you're given 20 minutes no matter how many questions are given. DO NOT TAKE THIS.

Let me put it this way, I would have dropped the class if there were any other 400-level CRIM classes available.  I've learned more about her EMT career and dogs than I have about Corrections.  Her exams are ridiculous and when the class average is a 70, there's an obvious issue or disconnect.  DO NOT TAKE UNLESS YOU HAVE TO.

DO NOT TAKE. Lectures are boring and Yevchak often goes off on a tangent. Exams are poorly constructed (frequent spelling/grammar mistakes) and test students on extremely specific material. Furthermore, she is not receptive at all towards students' concerns.  I strongly discourage anyone from taking her as a professor.

Very nice, awesome teacher. Very caring and helpful if you have questions. She does tend to get boring when she is lecturing, but she has a lot of material to get through. Really interesting stuff she teaches. Textbook is necessary!
Not a great teacher even though she is very knowledgable.  lectures are painful and drone on and on. unclear major themes make exams difficult to prepare for. Recommend to take a different Professor.

If you're looking for a fairly easy elective I would recommend taking this class. The only drawback is that attendance is under intense scrutiny and she is clicker happy.  If you take decent notes and read the book her test are not very difficult.  Easiest class my first semester.  -semi-interesting -likes to rant

Relatively easy class if you attend every class, read the textbook, and study. Quizzes (Sometimes unannounced) are based on long reading assignments and often ask random irrelevant questions. Test questions can also be on insignificant information mentioned once in a class and not in the textbook. Would not recommend someone to take her class.

Avoid taking this professor at all costs. Rather than actually teaching the important subjects of criminology, her tests and quizzes focus on irrelevant and minor details that require you to memorize almost every detail. She drones on for the entire lecture, and during "review days" before tests, she allocates a whopping 1-2 minutes to questions.

You have 4 tests and no final. She has readings due every class. Sometimes there are either a pop quiz or online ANGEL quiz. She will not send a reminder email to read or to do quiz so you are responsible for yourself. She is really into lectures and can ramble but really knows her information and has good examples/stories.

Professor Yevchak is a great teacher, and her class is interesting and engaging. It's not an easy A, though. You'll have to do a lot of reading (which can be quite dry) and you should always expect to be quizzed on it the next day in class. The tests are pretty challenging, too. But overall, this you'll be glad you took this class.

I love crim, but this class made me question going forward it. This professor is terrible, do everything in your power to avoid her. Her powerpoints have 2 words on them and she goes on rants that are so hard to fully pay attention to. Her tests are so hard and way to specific, what she says to study for it isn't even correct. She loves clickers.
She's the worst professor in the world. AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Had her twice as last resort. Want to die.
Very passionate about what she does. Just too much reading and time that is required to get an A on a gen ed I presumed was going to be a joke. I was wrong. Don't make the same mistake I made.
Made me love Criminology. She's passionate and loves what she is talking about. Exams are somehow rough but not that difficult.

Awesome lady. I wish I would have taken other classes with her. She cares about her students and takes the time to learn your names.  Tests are not very hard. Attendance is required and you can miss 2 classes to receive the full 10%
Great professor, will talk about anything going on in the world with you for as long as you want to and then some. Very interesting person to talk with. Taking her again next semester.

Professor Yevchak is a good professor, but can be confusing at times. Her notes she uses in class are good, but normally need to be accompanied by the readings. She posts many, long, readings to read over the semester that you often get quizzed on, so make sure you read. Don't underestimate exams and make sure you know her slides and the book.
good teacher but talks on and on about crim. can make you lose interest but overall I've had worst so id say toughin up if you need her class.

Yevchak is very nice, but usually she stumbles into class 5-10 minutes after the lecture was supposed to begin, which means she never gets through the material and usually crams it in.  She goes on rants a lot.  Tests are pretty easy. All multiple choice on the computer, but they are poorly wordedweird. Mandatory is a must since she uses clickers.

Very good professor, clearly interested in criminology and in teaching. Was very approachable if I had any questions regarding assignments. It's clear she takes the material seriously. I definitely recommend her for  any 400-level CRIM course.

She rants a bit, but it's so easy, how can you give her a bad rating?? You look at the slideshows before the exam, and you have to be stupid to get a poor grade. No lie, easiest actual class I've ever taken at PSU.

The class material is interesting, but it is extremely poorly taught. Yevchak's powerpoints are really underdeveloped and she stands at the front of the class and goes on rants that don't always connect. She isn't receptive to emails or other concerns. The exam questions are poorly written and are too specific for the amount of material. Avoid!
she is an easy grade if you listen well in lectures

I dont get why everyone disliked her so much. i took her for 100&12 and she is easy. all u have to do is make flashcards based on the slides and you will get at least a B+ (if not an A). she does ramble, & shes not very understanding about mistakes but so are most professors. i think too many people took this as an easy A and didn't expect to work

Possibly the worst class you could take at Penn State. Lecture is BRUTAL and boring because she doensn't know how to teach. Her exams are irrelevant and she picks questions that are so damn specific. Ended with a 79.8 and she won't round and she doesn't help in office hours either so avoid at all costs.

Lecinda is horrible. Do not take her class unless you want to claw your eyes out after 1 hour and 15 minutes of boringness. She gets off topic really easily and is unreasonably strict. Exams have extreme specifics that should not be relevant to an introductory course.

DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES!! Like everyone else has said on here she does not help give a better understanding of material going into an exam. It is really a free for all there could be questions from anywhere. Defiantly not looking into CRIM anymore...
DO NOT TAKE ANY OF HER CLASSES! She gets off topic very easily, her exams are extremely vague, and she is really no help. She doesn't help condense the information for the exams at all.

I was a criminology major and she made me switch. Hard tests that forced us to remember minuscule details, more like a grad school class than an entrance-to-major class. Very inflexible, generally unfriendly, & confusing. Goes off on tangents and Powerpoints don't help to prepare for tests. Doesnt do any activities to make sure students understand.

Awful professor, made me completely lose interest in criminology. Lectures are boring and she goes through them too quickly to write everything down. Still though, she barely puts up any power points. Also expects students to always show up and basically acts like no one has any other classes. Take this with any other professor.

I took this as a gen ed with a general interest in crime and HATED it. This professor is awful. She's impossible to work with, doesn't give any leeway, and the quizzes and tests are nothing like what was discussed in class. You're expected to take your own notes, can't makeup quizzes or exams, and NEVER forget your clicker.
you only get 2 missed classes.  If you forget your clicker she says its not her problem and that this is what the two days are for.  She rambles on and classes are generally not engaging.

Tests are no way shape or form what she talks about. She rambles like crazy during class then pushes through 6 slides at the end of the lecture. Her tests seem to be written by a 10 year old. Lack of basic grammar, are you kidding me?? As if her tests weren't hard enough you can't understand 20% of the questions regardless. Avoid. Avoid. Avoid.

DO NOT TAKE CRIM WITH HER. I am a Criminology major and she made this class unbearable. She talks about pointless, boring things that have nothing to do with the test and you can only miss two classes without being penalized. Also, if you need help do not expect to get it from her

Beginning of the semester she purposely said slides won't be online b/c she "believes students learn better from writing notes". She rushes thru slides, no one can finish and she eventually realized how stupid her theory was b/c no one has time to pay attention what she says since they rush to write everything down. Too bad her slides arent helpful
Awful. Tests are incredibly hard and a good majority are not on the slides. It's a 100 level course, she acts as though we're graduate students. Avoid this prof. Like the plague.

Honestly, she almost made me want to change my major out of criminology. Very boring; drags out each powerpoint slide and discusses pointless information. Also incredibly strict and not willing to help anyone, especially with make up exams. Also promised to put slides up, then decided last minute not to. Take with another professor!

If you are taking hard classes do not take her classes for an gen ed. She gives long assigned readings. And she just does way too much. I am a straight A student, a Biochem major and this class was suppose to be my fun easy class. But nope. I did not like it overall. And attendance is a must!!!

She's really nice but can be a little strict at times. The class is easy but attendance is mandatory because she uses the clickers every day. Tests are pretty straight forward. Overall it's not a bad class.
Really dry class and a bit of a pain to sit through. But keep up with notes and put in minimal effort and it's easy. She's a really nice person and easy going.

Absolutely loved this class. The material is a bit dry, but for being a 1st year professor, she did exceptionally well with trying to make it entertaining. She is also an extremely nice and easy person to get along with if you took the time to get to know her and ask her questions. Would repeat this class if given the chance.

Lecinda is an awesome person. Her positive attitude adds to the class. The materiel is a bit dry but she tries her best. The classes got a lot harder than they were last semester. I'm assuming she read these. If you read and go to class it is not too hard to get an A. I would recommend, just do the work though.
Nice women, 3 exams,8 quiz(3 lowest drop). No final. Exams are a little bit difficult. Overall, very good teacher..
not a fan. boring. easy material with difficult tests

I personally loved her as a person. She's cool,and made me consider CRIM as a major. Interesting, exams are fair, not so easy but just study. She tells you whats on it if you go to class. Go to class. Clicker points for attendance! that was my downfall, being a lazy college kid and not waking up. get up and go. worth it to get a good grade.

She is a good professor and the class is really easy. The quizzes can be challenging I found but the exams weren't bad at all. 3 drops for quizzes helps if you miss class and really she gives you exam questions every class so it's good to go. She is nice and my only complaint is she talks about one slide for 30 minutes occasionally

There are now clicker points in class so you have to go to get attendance points. There are three exams (no final) and there are 8 quizzes - three lowest quiz grades drop. The class is pretty easy, but it's a little dry. If you have no interest in criminology you may not want to take this. The professor is very nice.

Lectures are a little dry but she is an awesome person. She reads these rating because since last semester classes got twice as difficult. Over all better professor than some others in the department.

Boring, Put me back to sleep at 9:45 in the morning.  Class is optional so its tempting so skip.  2 Exams and 2 papers.  So if you don't do well on one of them you can screw yourself over.  Reads right off the slides (which are online)  barely used the book if at all.   She is young and needs to work on her teaching style

literally went to class 3 times this semester and expect an A or A- in the class. All you have to do is go over the notes she posts online and briefly skim the text. The two papers you're required to write are an easy 200 points all together. The exams are INSANELY easy.  Great woman, very accommodating and understanding. The class is just dull

Class is not mandatory at all, she posts all the slides online.  The only benefit is she will explicitly tell you certain things that are on the exams.  There are only two tests, both of which are basically common sense.  Overall easy course and a boring but nice women.

She is a very nice lady. However, the class is really boring and there are only a few opportunities to earn grades (2 papers, 2 tests, and a final) so you have to do good on the papers and tests or else you will get a bad grade. The class is easy if you go to class and pay attention. Also there is no extra credit.

This professor....uhhh...reads off...uhh...the....uhhh..slides...uhh and she constantly..uhh..says "uhh" . It get to a point where listen to the lecture becomes agonizingly annoying! Like the previous rater said the only reason to go to class is because she tells you or at least gives you tips on what will be on the exams. Needs better lectures...
Its a lecture she just reads the slides. The only reason to go to class is because she will tell you exactly what will be on the Exam. Nice teacher Easy Class. Common sence is half of it.

She is a great teacher but her heavy russian accent makes it very difficult to understand how she is explaining things. Her practice and homework makes it easy enough to learn the content without attending or being able to learn in class.

Math 230 is a very difficult course. Prof. Zikatanova seems to know her stuff, but many times she spends a lot on semantics of how to derive something, and very little on how to apply it. She can also be pretty abrasive, and sort of shame people for asking "bad" questions if they don't understand. The in class quizzes are nice for less stress.
pretty helpful office hours, good professor but the difficulty of the class itself jumps in the last 3 weeks
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Zikatanova enjoys teaching this class, but her lectures can be difficult to understand conceptually. Especially later in the semester, watching YouTube videos and finding other material is extremely helpful. She does have a generous outlook on grading and the in-class quizzes are not that bad.

She's a great professor. She understands the material well and really explains the concepts in-depth with proofs and derivations of the formulas. The course itself is very dense, homework assignments are long but necessary. DO NOT SKIP LECTURE! Since the class combines 231 and 232 it moves fast, missing one lecture could set you back ALOT.

I am glad I took her class. She posts organized notes with practice problems for each lesson and wants her students to succeed, though she can be abrasive at times. When I had conflicts she was very understanding. If you regularly attend lecture and are respectful you will have a similar experience. I highly recommend taking Math 230 with her.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She's a bit tough to understand, and teaches at the board in the front of the class. Quiz, written hw, and about 2 online hw assignments per week. 3 midterm exams and a final, all of which are standardized and unreasonably difficult, and they don't curve. You need to have a strong foundation in calculus if you want a chance in this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Zikatanova is very smart, but doesn't convey the lectures very well. Teaches on white board, get a seat in front of class. 1 written assignment with 3 ebook assignments per week, on average 15-20 hours hw / week. Quizzes every week. Hard class, but not her fault, exams are tough. Do well on exam 1 and 2, they are cake compared to exam 3.

Her lectures have a bit of a learning curve to them since you need to pay a lot of attention to understand her accent, but then she over-explains a lot of things which just makes it super confusing. Biggest problem is the exams though. Pay extra attention to the practice questions on the notes, not just the hw. Also, bring a tablet for notes

I love Prof. Zikatanova. She is very kind and funny, and truly wants all of her students to succeed. The class itself is the problem. The coordinators make the worst exams that are nothing like the reviews, and no matter how much Prof. Zikatanova gives us as review, the exams are still ridiculously hard. I would recommend her for MATH230.
Doesn't know how to explain and her accent makes it difficult to understand. If you take her class be prepared to self taught the whole semester. Avoid her at all costs!!
She sucks. All you need to know

She's incredibly tough but cares about her students. The classload itself is a LOT. Get ready for this to be the main class you think about during your semester. Quizzes on Mondays, homework on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and a lot of information given at once. The workload is doable if you're really ready for it. Review information, use your resources

Albena to me is a good professor. As long as you show up to class go to office hours when needed and email her about any issues in the class she is usually understanding. She cares about you if you care enough about the class.If you show up and are ready to learn she's a great professor to have.

Dropped during sylly week when she started putting in failing review quiz grades for every student in the class with no explanation and screamed at a student. Very demeaning and teaches solely off worksheets.
This class is going to be very hard if you  never learned calculus before.

All of her "lectures" are just going through worksheets and doing problems on the board. You are provided no extra exam study material. You will be expected to make your own practice problems. She does have office hours but as some others have mentioned she has a very degrading tone when you don't understand something

STAY AWAY! One of the worst professors I've had. She lectures off of work sheets, and just reviews conceps. There is no "teaching" of content. One must learn solely out of class. Office hours are accessible and can be helpful but her tone of voice makes you feel belittled. Albena makes you feel belittled in class she's the made me change my major.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Lecture heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: CAUTION: AVOID AT ALL COST. Albena's quizzes are so ridiculous and do not prepare you for the exam AT ALL! This lady is ATROCIOUS at teaching and gets mad at you for not knowing anything. Read the textbook if you have her that thing is more useful than she will be at teaching. Exams are easy if you read the book but do not depend on that lady
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Honestly no professors at Penn State for Math 140 are outstanding. It is a weed out class and therefore very difficult. She is not a good teacher. She will write through new problems once in front of the class and you are expected to learn from that. Class is hardly worth attending to pass exams, I suggest study groups & lion tutors to pass.

Although Math140 may be a very challenging class, Dr. Zikatanova tried her best to make it possible for all her students. She was very kind and was always made herself available to questions I may have had. There is a slight accent that takes some time to get used to, but nothing impossible. I would say she is one of the best professors for Math140

Mediocre professor, hard class. Thick accent but you get used to it. Will criticize you for not doing things correctly rather than guiding you in the right direction. Lots of homework it becomes routine. She really does care but isn't great at expressing it. Notes are also hard to follow. Exams are big part of grade. GO TO THE LA SESSIONS!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Albena teaches well and you can tell that she genuinely cares about students and their success. Note that college calculus is usually a lot harder than people expect, even if they took AP in hs. It takes a lot of work to do well. In terms of the heavy online hw: that is out of the prof's control. You will get swamped no matter which prof you get.

She is extremely unhelpful and condescending. She wants people to participate in class, but when people do, she ridicules them. Her lectures are very confusing. I already took AP Calculus AB and BC and she still confuses me, so if you haven't taken a calculus class before, do not take her.

Likely the worst teacher I have ever encountered. It is an exaggeration calling her a teacher. Good luck passing this class if you yourself are not a Math 140 teacher. Absurd amount of homework and very confusing "notes". She will tell you the wrong answer and why it is wrong but will never clarify the correct answer she got. Irrationally angry!!
forget how to do a problem? get ready for a scolding. she will ask for your feedback... don't give negative feedback or she will blame you.

Accessible outside of class, but her explanations aren't the best. Notes are also messy. Otherwise, very organized and willing to help. Use the practice exams and follow her lectures to get an A. Also, use her office hours for difficult homework questions.

The class in itself isnt too bad, but Professor Zikatanova isnt the best teacher. Her notes are, truly, terrible. Youll probably find yourself teaching yourself the material at some point during the course. Objectively, she also talks to her students in a slightly condescending way  as if its not her job to help you understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Math 141 is a tough class and you definitely have to put in the work to do well, but Prof Zikatanova very obviously cares about her students and does everything she can to help you succeed. Assigns a lot of homework but most due dates are flexible if you tell her you need more time/help. Always offers to stay after class and office hours for help.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She assigns lot of homework, and requires you to write in detail, otherwise you will lose points. Be sure to listen carefully to the content of the class. If you don't understand anything, you should make it clear in time. Otherwise, it's hard to keep up. Examination time is not enough, generally you can only write the answer without check.

She speaks with a slight accent but is easily understood. Homework is turned in on paper and must show work. Math 141 is a difficult course at Penn Sate but Albena is a great teacher and is willing to help you if you struggle. I recommend doing all the homework and going to office hours.

Albena is the best professor I have ever met. She is very intelligent and explains everything with proof. Her lectures make it so easy for anyone to understand the difficult concepts. Her explanations are fantastic and she is always ready and willing to help outside of class. She gives us many opportunities to increase our grades. She is amazing!

Albena is a nice professor even though she comes off as harsh at first. She is very helpful during office hours if you choose to go. She can be a very tough grader when it comes to quizzes and exams, but homework is an easy way to get your grade up in the class. She's a good teacher if you had a calculus class before, or else she is confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is the worst math teacher I ever had. I learned absolutely nothing from her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I couldn't understand anything she was saying and she was rude to students when they asked questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She is smart, but she doesn't really know how to explain the idea to students, especially in such an important and hard course. Lots of HW but that's how you learn the content. Exams are hard in the course, can't change that.

Very mean, calls out individual students if they make a mistake. I didn't understand somethings, went to her office hours, was told that I didn't understand and should stop wasting her time! Toxic class environment. Quizzes were 15% of grade, homework 5%. Read over my shoulder during tests and made me too nervous to finish. 8/52 students finished.

Regardless of who you professor is for MATH140 at Penn State, you are in for a rude awakening. This is a tough class. Albena Zikantova does a great job (in my opinion) of presenting the material, but it is really only how you review/study that material that matters when it comes time for the test. Never give up in this class, push hard all semester

I don't think her lectures are very clear, but her office hours are REALLY helpful!! I would recommend going to them as soon as you get stuck in homeworks and quizzes. She's kind and appreciates it when students work hard. I did bad on both of my midterms but I worked hard for the final with her help and I managed to get a a B-
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: She is a nice lady, I think she is trying to make her lecture helpful but she is really not helping at all at most of the times. She makes me feel stupid when I ask her questions which she did not fully explain. She kind of wanting you to understand everything ahead of time and she thinks her lectures is extremely clear.....
She is a great teacher just pay attention and put in work

She is an OK professor. You will be fine taking her class if you have a solid calculus background. After the first week, you won't notice her accent anymore. She gets upset when you skip class; she called me out for skipping one time.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She has the most monotone and boring voice which makes it very difficult to pay attention. Also, the notes that she writes on the board are always un-organized and hard to follow.

She is a ridiculously difficult grader. I got an 85 on a quiz because I made a sign error earlier in the problem, but finished with the same final answer. During class, if you ask a question she becomes upset and aggressive which doesn't help anyone understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Albena is super intelligent and she is a very good math instructor. She is lenient and very helpful. You won't even notice her accent after the first week of class. She gives a lot of homework, but it really helps nail down the concepts. Make sure you pay attention in class because she doesn't respond well when you ask a redundant question.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Albena won't be very specific when you ask questions in class for sake of time but if you have any questions about homework or anything, she is more than willing to help in office hours or by appt. Talking to her 1 on 1 is easy because she has a great sense of humor. She has a slight accent but it's really easy to understand compared to others.
She is tough but good.

Overall Albena is a nice lady, I could really see where her compassion could shine through at some points.  I found it REALLY tough to understand her lectures as she just talks to herself while writing the notes on the board.  She gets aggressive when you ask questions and/or don't understand what she's doing.

This is easily the worst teacher I have ever had. She literally talks to herself when she is going over topics. You rarely do practice problems and she makes everything so confusing. Also, her accent is so annoying. Math 140 is a tough class do not take this teacher. You will be pissed off every single day in class because she sucks so much.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Honestly this teacher was my only sub-par teacher my freshman year. She has an accent but it isnt too bad, but my main problem is she would get angry at you if you asked a question. She only answered maybe 15 questions this year and she would make the person asking feel like an idiot. She is also an odd grader, a little bit strick, but mostly odd .
hard

Albena's accent isn't bad, you can manage if you pay attention. She tries to make you understand the material rather than learn how to do the problems, sometimes lectures are entirely spent proving a theorem or law and no practice problems. Exams are weighted a lot, studying is necessary. If you put the work in you can get a good grade with Albena.

Albena is the nicest teacher I had this semester. If you make the effort, she will know your name and help you the best way possible. Good person to go to for recommendation letters for scholarships. One time I woke up sick the day of an exam and left class early, SHE handed ME the makeup exam for without me even asking- it really meant a lot!

I really like Albena, she is a nice woman. However, I took Calculus 1 and 2 and struggled in this class. She is too concerned with proving WHY the math makes sense, and not concerned enough with helping you learn new material. She is a very nice woman, very funny but I would chose a different teacher for Math 141
She has a very hard time communicating to the students due to a lack of communication skills and a strong accent.  The tests are tough and is not really based off the study guide.

honestly do not take her.. i used to be really good in math until i got to her class and I was confused every single day. its like she speaks to herself when she teaches. good woman, but do not take her. makes the class harder. the accent is not bad though.

She's a pretty good teacher.  MATH 141 was challenging for a number of people but you really only NEED to go to class once a week to turn in homework and take the weekly quiz if you are able to learn the material outside of class.

Math 140 is a hard class;I struggled for an A an took AP Honors calc. If you can take another professor, I would have done so. She is very much into describing HOW and WHY proofs are they way they are and doesn't go over a lot of practice problems in class, which is what the exam is. Also grades quizzes hard. But go to office hours, she likes that.

Albena is a very brilliant calc professor, but has trouble portraying her thoughts to her students. I had to spend many hours outside of class getting extra help at lion tutors and what not. Penn State Learning is also a great place to get help with homework. It is a difficult class but if you put in the effort, you can manage at least a B.
Very hard to understand with her accent.  She doesn't explain things clearly and you basically have to go by what she writes on the board.

She is funny and fiery.  She has an accent but you stop noticing after the first day.  It's a hard class, and her sense of humor is at least a relief.  She gets mad at stupid questions, but this is entertaining as well.  She is helpful and really knows her stuff.
Very passionate instructor, and she really cares about her students, especially the ones who regularly come to class.

Albena is a great professor. Gives you all the tools you need to succeed in math with her typed up notes and resources on angel. Her accent is thick sometimes but you really do get over it in 30 seconds. You will not find a better professor for this class. If you're serious about succeeding, she'll make sure you will. Best Prof I've had so far here

Albena is a wonderful professor. She's very helpful, and actually cares about each student. She used the book for homework. And her accent was never a problem. She is passionate about mathematics and is very good at teaching. Best Calc prof I've ever had.

Albena is a wonderful Bulgarian woman, and yes she has an accent. At times she is hard to understand, but you get used to it. She is very helpful and welcoming to come talk to. No matter who you take the class with, it is going to be hard, but if you study hard and do the hw, you will do fine. Albena does not do online hw, she uses the book for hw.

I took Albena for 140 and 141. She's a fierce Calc instructor who knows her stuff and really cares about her students. Don't let other people's ratings fool you, she is great and more than willing to help you. Calc is hard and requires your effort. You definitely earn your grade for this class.

Albena WANTS you to do well.  She always wants somebody to do a problem on the board but if you get it wrong she gets mad. Kinda contradicting but oh well.  I've heard a lot of things about the math department but Albena seems like she wants you to succeed in her class.

I had her a while back and I must say; it was horrid. And don't take my dropping of this class to be faulted to me, I hated her as a prof. I took 141 again next semester and got an A-. Avoid at all costs.

She is really smart and helpful, but at times it is hard to learn because the classroom is so big. It is best to get additional instruction to complement the class. If you go to the TAs, attend a Lion Tutors session (the weekly reviews are really good too) and read the book you should do well.

Albena was a solid Calc II professor. She knew everything with math inside and out and conveyed everything extremely well, even with a heavy accent. Her homework and quizzes prepped us for the exams well.  At times she was firey, but that's fine, I think it was funny at times.  Overall, a solid professor.  Take her.

Terrible teacher. She doesnt give you credit for things you earned. my quiz and homework average were bringing down my exam average. Shes a tough grader and is not very helpful. I taught myself this class.

Accent isn't a problem at all.  Extremely nice, and unintentionally humorous.  Her teaching isn't anything special, however.  Nice lady, and not a nightmare...a safe, but not perfect bet for Math140.  Overall, pleased (not thrilled) with my experience.
Very thick accent.  She is a very nice lady but is hard to understand.  I got a good grade but had to teach much of it to myself to do so. I would try to find someone else.
ALTHOUGH SHE GIVES ALOT OF HOMEWORK AND AN ALOMOST WEEKLY QUIZ , THIS WHAT MAKES YOUR MARK GO UP ESPECIALLY IN A COURSE LIKE THIS ONE, WHERE THE MATERIAL IS NOT EASY ... RECOMMENDED !
Good teacher, thick accent but able to understand after a few classes.  Examples help to clarify difficult concepts.

Great teacher for Math 141.  Thick accent, but not hard to understand.  She is always willing to help.  Go to office hours if you are lost.  She gfoes relatively quickly in class, but attendance isn't mandatory.  The first midtermn was cake.  I recommend taking Albena.

She is very nice and helpful, but her thick accent is often hard to understand. If you do the homework and go to her office hours when you're having trouble you should be able to get through the class.
Very smart teacher, she understand the subject material very well. If you go to class, study the material and get on her good side, you should have no problem getting an A.
Not so bad if you have patience with her accent. She's a nice lady but hard to understand sometimes. If you know math then you shouldn't have to hard of a time in the class.

Terrible teacher...thick accent and unfair grader! She picks her favorites.  I got A's on all my papers in class, she gave me an A- in the class...a friend of mine got C's on projects and somehow managed an A in the class. Does that make sense to you?

Actually a great professor. Slides are easy to read and understand, content is presented in an easily digestible manner, and no handwritten code on exams is a HUGE plus. The labs take a bit of work, get them done earlier rather than later. His slides and content contain everything you need. There's no need for AI. PLENTY of great study resources.

Professor Zhu is the definition of a fair professor. I have never felt hard done by grading and have consistently gotten out what I put in. It is difficult material, and his slides explain it decently well. The practice questions he provides are also great for covering all of your bases before exams. The homework isn't too bad either.
oh boi can't wait this man teaching CMPSC 311 again.

lazy teacher he uses someone else's slides and read straight off. no point in going to class. In order to pass, YOU NEED FRIENDS. The labs are confusing so go to office hours and talk to your classmates. He flexes giving people AI's and failing people, so don't copy code. It's normal to fail the midterms and annotate the slides &u pass good luck
As one of the most difficult courses in cs major, you need to devote time to it and work hard, so that you can get an A. There is no magic.
Horrible

INCREDIBLY DIFFICULT TO UNDERSTAND LECTURES. 5 LABS (cumulative), 3 Exams (non-cumulative). LABS ARE INCREDIBLE DIFFICULT, GO TO OH and START EARLY! Literally need to study every single lecture slide to do well on the exams, because it is literal memorization of the lecture slides. Piazza Discussion was somewhat helpful. Prof also mumbles.

I highly suggest taking any other professor for this class.

For tests, lectures are your only viable resource, and Professor Zhu speaks softly, stutters, and mumbles through them all with little clarification. I got front row seats to all his lectures from day one until midterm 2: I always left with little to no understanding and wasted time.

Uses someone else's slides and just reads them in lecture. Very heavy accent. Couldn't understand ever what he said. It is a good class and is great for learning purpose. Please try to take with some other professor. Very disappointed from Penn State for having such a professor.
Terrible
Bro looks like a turtle but literally talks like a turtle
Learn how to teach
Get ready to live in office hours

It's irritating that an important course like this is taught by Professor Zhu. The exams are hard but not entirely unreasonable. However, the labs are unnecessarily confusing, have incomplete test cases, are tedious/impossible to debug, and use content only briefly mentioned in class. If you have to take this course, use TA sessions for your labs.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Legitimately the worst instructor I have ever had. Cannot follow his lectures in the slightest, and then get hit with extremely difficult fully open-ended exams. Take this class over the summer with a different professor if possible.
People are too harsh. If you simply watch his lectures and study the slides the midterms should be a breeze. Only homework are lab assignments that take a couple hours tops if you are a decent coder.

complete mumbler. could not understand almost anything he said because of he annunciation. class is in C it difficult but not impossible. did not attend very many classes because I could barely understand his instructions. just if you are going to be a teacher you should probably learn how to effectively publicly speak and now mumble.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Learn how to speak English. As a Chinese student, I felt awkward listening to your class. And self-reflection will save you in your future career.

By far the worst professor I have ever had. It feels like he wants you to fail and will go out of his way to set you back. Surprised the school allows this class: grade is composed of 5 labs and 3 exams including final. If you make any mistake you will just be another statistic that he will brag about. Refused to curve a midterm with 49% average.

He has been one of the worst professors I have ever had. During lecture, all he does is read off the slideshow. The labs are very difficult and when you go to office hours, there is one TA with many people waiting. I have rarely received help. The exams are very difficult with hardly any extra credit. Worst taught and managed course I ever took.
The hardest class i've ever taken
Some people are not meant to be a teacher, and he is one of them :)
Horrible professor. Reluctant to curve exams when averages were in the 40s, and barely gave out any chances of extra credit. He wants you to fail.

The professor talks more about the difficulty rather than teaching. Projects are a huge part of your grade but little time during class is dedicated to help you get started. You just teach this class to your self. Lectures are vague and hard to understand. Terrible structure and bad reflection on the computer science department at Penn State.

"I don't have intent to make you fail this class. I will give you easy questions. It's not my fault, just because you didn't work hard and attend class." If you really care about the students that should not be the reason why there is an average below 49. PLEASE GIVE YOURSELF A REFLECTION ABOUT YOUR TEACHING!!!
Terrible representation of the CS department unfortunately.
Bad lectures and way too difficult exams. Actual assignments are not too bad at all but the exams make this class very difficult.
bro doesnt stop for a second to consider that he might be the problem
"I know I am not a good teacher"

Heavy accent, only read the slides. Makes the exam hard and enjoys threatening students to fail the class.

Best line he said, "Now it is NOT my job to curve the grades for you to pass, but your own decision whether to take this course seriously or not."

First exam, the average grade was 49. No curve. Professor complained that people didn't show up to class. Of course, the reason is because his lectures are incredibly difficult to understand. Exam questions were based on details he barely mentioned in lectures. Exam grading was extremely strict. Good luck if you need to take this class.
So horrible
bro thought he were teaching in china
best class for masochist who loves getting academic depression

He has a ton of citations on Google Scholar, yes. Wish that made him a good teacher though cause he's definitely not even a 1/5. 0/5, if I could. Hard to understand, terrible lectures, impossible exams. The mean for Exam 1 was 47.5 and he is not even curving it. No extra credit. Stressful, depressing, frustrating. Some TAs could be helpful.

You will never understand what he said. He will post confusing sample exams. He just read it with the heaviest accent so nobody understand no matter where you came from. 
He doesn't require attendance but he will send you email or announcement to complain about absence and tell you that's the reason of your fail. HE IS THE REASON!!!!
Worse than Dan Kahn

He just stumbles through the lectures, The practice tests are from YEARS ago with no explanations to questions. You cant even take the time to give us the answers so we know what is expected? You are paying to waste hours learning the material your self. He keeps mentioning the failure rate as if the previous points weren't clues as to why...

How did bro even became a professor though...Simple slides but extra heavy lab works and tests, and I had to learn all he mentioned in class with online videos on YTB. Gave us materials for exams that are without answers and told us 'dont ask us because we dont know'. Actually no one gives a sht to your awkward jokes in class...

He speaks slowly and almost like he does not know the material himself because he does not, the course was built entirely by his predecessors and he simply reads slides. He obviously does not have ill intent toward any students but he loves bragging about failure rates and how hard the course is. Avoid him if you can.
No words.

Professor Zhu knows the ins & outs of computer security, but his course structure could use some rework. He assigns lengthy unguided lab reports due every week. The course contains only one cumulative final exam where you have to remember every little detail taught from day 1 (no cheat sheets). He makes attendance mandatory with canvas quizzes.

Not great in 311, great in 443. Clearly he is more passionate about the computer security topic. Attendance is mandatory and graded. About 6 labs that aren't necessarily difficult, but take some time to do. Some hws, no exams, just 1 final exam worth 20%.  Definitely take this course if you are interested in cybersecurity, you will do quite well.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: TBH couldnt pay attention during lectures cause they were quite dry. However, material for this class is interesting and reasonably easy. Showed up, did my homeworks and my labs in a timely manner and the class flew by. No midterms, only a final which was not tricky at all. Sencun is pretty laid back except for counting participation.

I cannot learn anything from his lecture. But I have to watch it because there might be important shell commands. Do not copy anything in your code. Be sure to remember everything they told you. Yes, EVERYTHING!!! There are many tricky questions on the exam. Even though it is not important, it could on the exam.
This clown only read from the slides and scared us off with AI warnings every week and assignment.

All the stuff taught was material from professors that taught the class previously. Zhu would just read off of slides. 50% of the grade is labs that are extremely challenging that you will struggle to find help with due to booked office hours and bad answers on Piazza. Exams are unfair, averages were 50%. No mentioned curve
BEST QUOTE OF 2022 BY SENCUN: Certainly you need to change something about the way you teach the course. There is no magic here.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Has a heavy accent and reads from slides. Exams are very difficult (50% avg) and the projects get progressively more difficult (avg in 70s, 50s on the last project). About 50% project heavy and 50% exam heavy. He didn't provide any exam study resources, simply said "review the slides". No mention of a curve and it's 2 days from finals.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Come on Prof. Zhu, 380 of people are waiting for you give a juicy curve though. We been waiting for the entire semester and looking at the labs average is like 70 and the exams average is like 60. We all need to pass this class and go on with our lives with CMPSC 473 though. Come on, a juicy curve like 10% solves everything.

Boring lectures from a previous professor, added nothing to them. Did not answer student questions and usually said to refer to slides or recorded lectures, and had difficult labs and exams that had about a failing avg for both.
the semester is finished, and where's the curve Prof. Zhu??

The best 311 professor is Abutalib Aghayev, avoid everyone else. Exams are needless hard. Projects are needless hard. Penn State honestly only wants the top students to get a degree in cmpsc/cmpen, the rest are being farmed outta money, forced to change major or retake the class which adds more semester to their 4 year degree.

To be honest, the best answer he has ever given on piazza was "certainly you need to change something as you mentioned. There is no magic here.". Other than that, he is a paid robot that monotonously reads word by word from the slides used in class and which were zero helpful for the labs.

Basically spends all lecture reading the text on a lecture slide (which was made by another professor). If you ask him a question, he will either outright dismiss the question or give a non-answer. Does not give sufficient information for you to be able to complete HW. Asks extremely unfair questions on exams (and then makes then 50% of the grade)

Lectures are completely irrelevant to the course until the last 2 weeks when they suddenly make or break your understanding of the labs. Very (read: VERY VERY VERY) difficult to understand; speaks very fast, mumbles, heavy accent. TA's unhelpful, main form of help is Piazza (main help is "see lecture slides"). Used another professor's slides. BAD!

Very strong tone when lecturing. Labs and slides are taken from Prof. McDaniel and Prof. Abutalib and with minor modifications.

On top of those, HE DOES NOT CURVE! The average for the midterms are 55 and he kept his promise where he won't curve said beginning of the semester. Nice one.
He does not know how to teach at all and you will learn almost nothing from lectures. Assignments are at best loosely related to what we learn in class. Do not take if you want to learn.
He doesn't know how to make students understand what he wants us to learn. Like what is network.

I simply did not understand him during lectures. I believe one of the reasons is his accent, but also it always felt that he was trying to understand the topic himself during the lectures. Further, there was just one lab that had something to do with what we learnt in the class, while others were simply to be done with the help of TAs.

Not a difficult class to pass. Homeworks are very doable. Just have the textbook handy. Lab assignments are tricky but by no means impossible. Just show all your steps and you'll get credit. The only exam is the final and there is a ton of material to remember. Lectures can be difficult to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures can be boring, but cares about his students. Homework and labs aren't too bad and office hours can be very helpful. Provides additional help on the labs and dropped one of the labs to lessen the workload. This class isn't for everyone, but personally I thought the material was interesting and mostly easy to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Its not just his accent that makes him hard to understand, but also his presentation skills. His slides are overloaded with information and is a mess at times. Not very good at tying overall concepts together and his explanations are all over the place. He clearly has a lot to learn about teaching.

From the lecture side, Sencun has a very thick accent and his long lectures put you to sleep. The information is interesting, but the way he presents makes you not pay attention or even show up. However, the homework and labs teach you a ton and make up most of the grade. The final exam was also fair so even though he is boring, he is fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Man's one of the worst lecturers I've seen and that's saying a lot. Never worked so hard to just pay attention in class and learn so little. Use the textbook, use Google, use Youtube. This guy is useless.

Someone, please ask him if he even knows what teaching means. He doesn't know how to teach, doesn't know how to give lectures, doesn't know how to even create a database, never coded a single line in a class that was coding-based, doesn't put in any effort, and doesn't work hard enough to make students understand the basics of the course syllabus.

One of the worst professors I have ever had. He knows the material well, but he does not know how to teach. His English is also not the best and he has a very thick accent. He is a lenient grader, labs are relatively easy and well explained in the lab documents so it is easy to get a decent grade, but I feel that I left this class without learning

Such a nice guy and is willing to help you during office hours. He definitely knows what he's talking about, and his tests are basically from the homeworks and quizzes. As long as you attend class (which only about 1/2-1/3 of the class did), it will make understanding the information a lot easier because he was pretty good at explaining things.

This professor is worthless.  I've never had to rank anyone on here as terrible as this guy.  Cannot speak English, spent 8 weeks just covering cryptography at binary detail, barely scratched the surface with actual network security (Firewalls, IDS, Pentesting, etc).  The average exam score for 50+ students was a 45%.  Terrible.

Nice guy, bad class. Terrible English, grading inconsistent with rubrics, and review for exams is misleading. He's always willing to help you, but you're going to have to do a lot of work outside of class to succeed. I was lucky enough to have a hard-working group, and with great effort, managed an A. Not an easy class, but not impossible.

Dr. Zhu is an awesome professor! He is extremely smart and really wants to help students. His class is very challenging but not impossible. His English is also not the best but not horrible by any means and if you attend class you will do good. Just understand the concepts and put in the effort and you will do fine.

Great guy but misunderstood with his intentions and his english. When IST students get a teacher who expects you to put forth a good amount of work and effort they naturally flare up and throw their arms into the air and grumble. And that's what this class takes, you actually have to understand it. His English is awful but not his teaching.

He knows what he's talking about, but his English and teaching skills aren't at the point where you can really understand him. He will try to explain/help, but he isn't very good at it. Class is just him lecturing, which gets very boring. That being said, his class isn't impossible. I still picked up enough to do well - he also does some curving.

His test is easy as long as you do the homeworks and understand his slides. His english is hard to understand. You have to pay extra attention during class. His lecture can be boring, maybe due to the way he talks. But as long as you do the work, it's easy to get a good grade.

As other posters have said  - he is somewhat hard to understand because he talks fast. He definately knows his subjects 110%. Willing to help if you need it. All you have to do is pay attention and review the slides and you'll get a good grade in the class.  55% of your grade comes from labs and homeworks which are easy to get 100%'s on.

You can tell this guy is here for research only, because he is a bad teacher. Impossible to understand, so his lectures did nothing for me. His office hours is where I learned everything, and he is very willing to help. Tests are unfair, but once you understand how he tests, they get better.

This guy really sucks.  His tests are from another planet.  He is very hard to understand, but that is the least of your worries once you get one of his tests.  Labs are easy, thankfully, and participation isnt factored very much into your grade.  Nice guy, but horrible teacher.

He has only been in the country for 8 months so his english is very bad.  He is passionate about the subject but has very little experience teaching.  It took us half the semester to convince him to use powerpoint. before he taught everything on the board in really poorly done examples.

Everyone on here is overreacting. Professor Zhao is great, and her class is not very difficult if you have a basic understanding of Excel. I recommend taking this class with a friend so that after the 4th HW, you can work together. 1 HW Excel sheet a week and 2 exams overall. Professor Zhao is very smart and nice as well.

Zhao Hui is a nice person, don't get me wrong. Even though that's the case, her class is a torture. It is horrendous. I would recommend you avoid her at all costs. You should look for a clear instructor and easier grader.
This class is horrendous. Taking it with her is a nightmare. Avoid her at all costs. NOT WORTH THE STRUGGLE. Better take it with a clear instructor. !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
Horrendous class. Taking it with her is a nightmare! Avoid at all cost!

SCM 421 is gonna be horrible no matter what Professor you have, Hui is one of the smartest professors at smeal, however is not great at teaching material. She is willing to always help and is easy to reach outside of class. Group homeworks are huge so make sure you get a good group and do ALL extra credits. Exams are nearly impossible, but curved.

Hui is a very difficult professor and makes what is already a difficult course, even more difficult. When you go to her office hours for help, she makes the impression that she wants to help, but then proceeds to tell you she cannot help because it is graded. So when you feel lost and stumped in this class, there is really no where to go for help.
If you're really on this because she's your professor, good luck. Try anything possible to get any other professor.

NEVER TAKE THIS TEACHER UNDER ANY CONDITION!!!!!!! I never write these and I had to for this awful teacher. hard to understand, doesnt care about the students. just awful. very hard class. do whatever you can to stay away. absolute worst teacher and class at penn state i promise you

The material for the course itself isn't the most difficult, but Professor Zhao does a fairly bad job trying to teach the material in class. She will try to trick and confuse you on the midterm, final exam, and weekly homework quizzes. If possible, try to find another professor for SCM 421. No offense to her, but I do not recommend her at all.

SCM421 is gonna be awful no matter what, so she's probably better than other professors. It's still super hard, the weekly homeworks take hours, the quizzes are all excel, and she gave us homework over spring break. She goes super fast so use online sources to help with homework. She's very accessible outside of class and genuinely wants to help.
Love
Don't take her if you have other choices; her course is extremely hard. Tests and quizzes are heavy!

Effort doesn't matter. Attended every class and I have a C after the mid term. Hui is the best professor I have ever met. She is very inspirational and tries her best to make the hard class enjoyable. By the way she's my mom.

SCM421 is the toughest SCM class in general - but Hui *tries* to make it okay. She has a great sense of humor and is so kind and understanding. The homeworks are tough, quizzes are just the homeworks verbatim, and the exams are HARD. There's a ton of extra credit, tho. There's huge curves on the final exam & final grade, tho. Love Hui!

Hui is a great teacher and wants students to learn. The course is extremely hard, and sometimes she gets carried away and does not teach it directly. The first exam is doable, but the final is impossible (mostly cause the material is harder). Take her in the spring.

reviews.comment: Dr. Lei is a fascinating individual. He is by far the most intelligent professor I've had (two PhDs) and is clearly extremely passionate about what he teaches. The Professor & TA are very helpful so don't be afraid to reach out to them. Attendance wasn't mandatory but you need to be there for the quizzes of course. I am definitely glad I took this class with him!
Take notes, turn up to class for quiz and solve HW and exam prep problems and you can get a B or above.
reviews.rating_tags: BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof Zhen is a friendly and lenient grader. He believes in discipline and attention. Show up to class and do all the quizzes well, you will get an A.

reviews.comment: Not a tough class. The material has the potential to be interesting but Professor Lei is a horrible lecturer. This is the one of the easiest class I've took at Upark. Not a well structured class.. Homework assignments are incredibly frustrating. Exams are easy.

Do not buy the book; it will not be used. Dr. Lei is a nice guy and his English is satisfactory. Homeworks are hard, but the TA was very helpful. Tests are challenging, but make sure you understand the homework completely and you shall do OK. Lei will help his students in any capacity necessary. reviews.comment: He is a nice guy and knows what he's talking about, but the structure of the class makes it really difficult for me to learn. We have class 1 day a week where he gives a lecture, and we don't get to go over the material we watched in the videos. So basically, you teach yourself half the class and then you go to the exams and they're hard!

Exams are impossible. The wording is nothing like the practice exams. You think you studied enough? News flash you didn't. You could live and breathe this class and not be able to get an A on the exams. DO NOT take this as a science elective for all u engineers. I would've much rather taken chem 112.

I promise if you don't have a religion, you will by the final with how hard the tests are, you'll be praying on your walks to the pollock testing center. reviews.comment: This class was impossible. I've never gotten below an A in any bio class, as a pre-med student and I ended with a C+ in this class. The tests were completely unreasonable and the LA exam review sessions covered anything but what was actually going to be on the exams.

Professor really knows his stuff but so much information thrown at you. Many topics in each exam - very difficult to understand each topic as thorough as needed. Exams are extremely challenging because most of the questions are "multiple select" and very detailed. Extra credit opportunities given, but grade is heavily dependent on exam scores.

Genuinely one of the worst classes I've taken. all midterms have 'multiple select' and the questions are so insanely different from the notes in lecture that it makes it hard to apply what you've learned to the exams. There are so many concepts that you need to know every single minute detail about everything. Do not take this class.

human anatomy always gives me a tough time but he made it bearable. he gives really good detail in lectures and also has online lectures on canvas that you can go back and watch anytime. the extra credit in this class is the sole reason i have a C+. those exams whooped me but thats just cause i didnt study enough. hes very easily accessible.

The definition of useless professor, has 0 capabilites to teach, extremely boring, horrible slides, hard exams and the only thing that saves your grade is the extra credit. LA's are also uselles they are awful. If you want to struggle a lot with what is supposed to be an 'introductory class' go ahead. But I could not recommend it less.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: A lot of borderline "introductory" information loaded into a bunch of slide shows. Get's confusing trying to remember the specific definitions of each term. You basically have to gamble on what information to internalize before the exam because the questions are so specific there's no way to remember them all. Lectures just repeat slide shows.
The worst professor I've ever had.
ANNOYING!! very few points. not beginner level. only graded on quizzes and exams
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He is not qualified to teach this material and it shows in lecture. He also changes the grading criteria so you need an additional percentage point to get the same grade according to Penn States grading policy, and says that asking him to round your grade is "unethical." The only reason he has high ratings is because he gives extra credit.

Michael Zeman changes his grading policy and does not round, so be careful of your score. He is a horrible lecturer, but decent at making slideshows. For how much content this class has, he displays it well, though you could never attend a lecture (besides the extra credit ones!) and still get a good grade in his class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Only 1 in person lecture a week- and it covers the lectures that are pre-recorded online anyway. Lectures are insanely boring but not difficult. All recorded from covid-so can go at your own speed throughout the week. Exams aren't that hard-review the LA's practice exams. Lots of extra credit throughout the semester that make it hard to fail.

The class was okay. In person lectures were pretty useless since he just repeats what's said in the videos. Tests are pretty tough and super specific. He offers a good amount of extra credit which is really clutch.

The good reviews are fake. He would have awfully formatted slides that are difficult to read. The exams were extremely hard even if you study and go to each lecture. He was awful at actually teaching the material rather than just reading off the slides. Reviews were 10x easier than the exams. Extra credit keeps everyone from failing his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Zeman provides the welcoming feeling you need when going into a large class like Bio 141. The class itself is tough because there is lots of content to go over, if you don't have a "bio brain" that makes it harder. But if you give Professor Zeman the attention in class and listen you will do fine in the class and on exams.

I took 141 with no history in biology and left it completely enthralled with the subject matter. Prof Zeman helped with this, as half the class was online and even the videos were involved/interesting. He's easy to reach and understanding, even for small assignments. He makes the topics easy to digest. I recommend 141 to those with a curious mind.

Going to class is not necessary at all for this course. Your grade for the class is completely dependent on the tests you take and nothing else matters. This course is pretty much just memorize all of the PowerPoints and then try to apply them in the exam. The exam reviews are way easier than the tests so keep that in mind before taking them.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: PPT is your best friend in this class. Remember them and do the exam. That's all.

Cool and funny guy. Lectures go fast, so be ready for that. He re-explains most of the material in take-home lectures, though. No homework but weekly quizzes. Do your best on the quizzes and watch the recorded lectures.

Prof Zeman is a nice man. he cares a lot about his students. There are few extra credit opportunities but all grades are from weekly quizes and exams. I'm so glad the exams were online my semester because they were rough.
reviews.rating_tags: Test heavy--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He had decent lectures but they were sometimes so boring as it was just repeating the online lectures. The course was only graded on a few exams and a few small assignments, so once you mess up on one exam, its over for you. Try to take this course online with someone else if you have to take it.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Zeman is an OK Professor. Nice guy, but he has somewhat of a lazy teaching style which can render boring. The class itself isn't too hard, but the material is very dense (like any other BIO class). Grades are only from quizzes (easy) and VERY DETAILED exams. Only take this class if you plan to be serious about it; it's not a simple "filler" course.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Zeman is a great professor. Although lectures were very fast paced, and exams were a little hard, he provided countless opportunities for extra credit. The exams were very similar to the material in class and you will be fine if you pay attention. Overall great professor and great class!

Prof Zeman is great. This class isn't bad at all, especially with recorded lectures. Kinda annoying to meet Tues night, but lectures are not that boring. Quizzes are super easy each week and on quizlet. Exams are much harder, and have many detailed, application questions. So you have to study everything from the slides and know how to apply it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I took this as a sci elective for my major. Very lecture heavy that it can be difficult to stay interested in if you don't like bio. Meets once a week for just over an hour and then three weekly video lectures with a (pretty easy) weekly quiz too. Exams are very specific so you can't just memorize the material, you have to learn and understand it.

This is honestly not a bad class. It's a tonnnn of memorization and reading from slides and diagrams. The class meets once/week on Tues nights and has 3 other lectures per week that are easy to watch in 2x speed. One easy quiz per week. Exams are pretty hard and extremely detailed, so study the specifics. Prof is a great guy and offers extra credit
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I liked Zeman's class, whether that's because it was easy or because of him, I have no idea. Quizzes are basically free points and his in-person lectures are actually pretty good.
