reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is average. Class was not that hard compared to other classes in biochem major that I took. It was like biochem but a little easier because not memorize pathways. If you are good at science it won't be that much different than any other class. He is kinda boring. Half online/ half in person which is kinda weird.

I took bio 141 as a gen ed class. It is very hard to keep up with, as the lectures have so much information and you don't have enough time ever to write or type everything down. Exams cover a lot of difficult material. If you don't need this class for your major specifically do not take it.

Literally avoid this class at all cost the exams are 10 times harder than the study guides/lecture material that he barely teaches. This is really a do it yourself course and you better pray you have a strong study group. And your entire grade is basically exams. If you have to take this class good luck Charlie!

Professor Zeman has pretty interesting lectures, but it is hard to find material to study; he does reuse some of his quiz questions and in-lecture questions on exams. The fourth exam was much harder than the other three exams even though it technically was not a final and not cumulative. He gives a few chances for extra credit which is nice.
The exams are extremely hard. Half of the questions don't make sense. It's one of those classes where you start the exam and think "We never went over this?" Class left me frustrated and burnt out.

Exam was not even close to what we had in the study guide. 6-8 hour pre-recorded lectures a week that are 1 hour long each so you gotta be consistent if you're not it's hard to catch up because they all have an overwhelming amount of info that if you keep pausing you can sit in your room all day just watching them. Don't take if you overthink.

final was much harder than any exam/practice we've ever seen, you couldnt go back to a question after submitting and a lot of them had multiple answers because of cheating, he was also very rude about rounding grades evn tho an a in this class is a 94, we are in a PANDEMIC and his lectures were prerecorded so its not like he taught us anything
Lectures were prerecorded and somehow he sped through the material but the videos seemed excessively long. If this class would have been in person I probably wouldn't have passed.
His lectures are fun and he truly cares about what he's teaching. The class is really hard sadly so prepare for a lot of studying.

He's friendly and nice and chill but I was not expecting the difference of the exam compared to the practice questions to be that big. I'm not saying exams are hard, it's basically memorization with context. But jesus the practice questions was like "what is homeostasis". and exam was like "what happens if the sodium litaged pumps stopped working"

Um, he's funny. But he has no clue what he's talking about. He's the typical middle-school teacher. He likes to appeal to kids. Heck, he's a coach of a 4th grade girls volleyball team. My main problem was the exam was NOTHING like the review questions. I got a perfect on the review and was confident, comes to exam and it's all specific stuff.

This wasn't an easy course, but if you go for extra help, study the material, do the online quizzes and take advantage of the extra credit given. You can easily pass this class. The exams are very application based and sometimes he includes clicker questions from his lectures. My advice would be to take notes on the important information. GOOD LUCK

Nice guy. Tests aren't bad just study the slides and watch crash course videos.

Prof. Zeman is hilarious in his lectures. I didn't read the textbook too much but its a good resource to have if you need something explained more. reviews.comment: Zeman is adorable, and one of my favorite professors. Answers any question you could have, and is very straightforward. Exams are easy, I highly recommend.

Professor Zeman was a really good professor. He seems to be really interested in the subject matter and always uses real-world applications in his lectures. Though tests are challenging, he is accessible outside class during office hours and his learning assistants are very helpful.

I loved this professor, he's somewhat strict with grading and participation. However as long as you show up to class and participate, he will be more than willing to help you whenever he can. good professor, actually looks for feedback and listens to it which not many professors do. pretty useful class to learn cad and 3d printing

just dont enroll
would not recommend

This professor is really  unfair and not caring about students. He teaches one thing but acts the opposite. He puts you under unnecessary pressure, even though it can be fun sometimes. Be aware, all other professors ( no matter how bad they are ), cannot reach this professors level. He literally doesn't care if he gives you a zero, even if you deserve better. THE CLASS WILL BE MUCH MORE FUN AND YOU WILL GET BETTER GRADES WITH ANOTHER PROFESSOR.

Great guy, very engaging with students and is willing to help. Participate in class. Fluctuating homework loads, but all manageable. His grading habits are pretty average and he is willing to take revised work for more credit.
Nico was awesome and always very uplifting, just come to class and pay attention and you won't have any problems.
If you want an A in this class don't take him. Or be ready to work A LOT, even more then other classes like math or chemistry

he cares about students but he is really awful with the grading, he sees how the students work hard but he isn't as caring as he should be if I had a chance to retake the class I wouldn't choose him to be my professor, I always do the work on time.

Nico is a great teacher and is always there to help you learn. he is kind and jokes around. He can grade a little harshly but by paying attention and doing your work you'll get an A. What an awesome prof. Take him if you can. I learned soooo much about CATIA V5. CAD work seemed scary  at first, but I just put effort into doing it and it wasn't bad. Funny guy, respects you coming to class and participating, and overall just a great prof. Take his class, do well, and learn a whole bunch in the process.
Nico is great professor that cares about his students and it show

Nico is an amazing professor! He is always willing to help with projects and even life advice. He makes the class very fun and is so kind and funny. There is quite a large amount of homework, but not very time consuming. This is one of my favorite classes and Nico makes it 1000x better! Take any course you can with Nico.

Let me be real with yall for two minutes. This man is an absolute dawg of a human. Niko is fr a great a guy and I am giving you guys my honest truth. Excellent Professor, good sense of humor
Nico is very passionate and truly cares his students. It is mostly group work and projects. He wants to get everyone excited for engineering
Nico is an awesome teacher with a real passion for engineering. Most of the work is group work and he really tries to inspire people to enjoy engineering.

I have never put so much effort into a class and seen such little return. Spent at minimum 7 hours reading, annotating, and reviewing readings every week, never got more than 3/5 on quizzes if lucky. reviews.comment: I made a RMP account JUST to give Dr Reg a rating. He's by far my favorite psychology professor I've had between UP and a commonwealth campus. He's kind, passionate about his subject, knowledgable yet humble, very helpful (though not *always* the most timely with email responses, totally overlookable though), everything you'd want in a professor!

Very caring professor. He is so kind and respectful. He is not a harsh grader so that's definitely a plus. Attendance is mandatory. The lectures are very interesting and he is not boring at all! I would recommend taking him for Psych 243. If I could take another one of his classes I would!
Overall a very nice professor and guy, but the speed at which he goes through slides is just impossible to keep up with when trying to take notes.

Prof. Adams was literally the best. I took this class MWF at 9am. Attendance was not mandatory, he says that it is and sends around a roll but will not affect your grade as long as you are doing well on the quick quizzes and exams. I never read any articles for the quick quizzes and did fine on them exams were also really easy.

Adams is very research article heavy, so many of his lectures are very scientific, which is very interesting. Readings can be long for quick quizzes, but exams not too bad and only one project. Fun class recommend it

Professor Adams seems like a nice guy but lacks compassion when it comes to grading. He forced me to do a project that I HAD CONTRIBUTED WORK FOR on my own without hearing my side of the story first. He acted like a total mean girl. Would not recommend. Pick ANYONE else.

Dr. Adams Psych 490 provide a very welcoming environment for idea expression and discussion. So it's definitely better to go to class in person. Be prepare for the exams, go to review sessions and you will be fine.

Dr. Adams is the sweetest human being ever and is super understanding. I went to almost none of the lectures this semester and still passed with an A- so it's definitely an easy A. There are no tests, just quizzes on readings that you don't even really have to read. There are a few thought papers and one project too but they're all really easy.

Reg is a really caring and nice prof. While his lectures are dry and readings required for the quick quizzes are really long, the exams are pretty easy. 3 exams all finished before thanksgiving. The content was interesting to learn but Im not sure if I want to take another class with him bec of long readings. Overall, good content but just a dry.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Caring--So many papers

reviews.comment: Favorite professor! He genuinely cares about YOUR well-being. go to class on Tuesdays bc there are 5 question quizzes on readings. Learn to skim them. GO TO HIS PRE EXAM REVIEW-- it helps so much!! When I went to them I'd get a 90-100 on the exam. (it's such a good review that you'll ace it even if you didn't pay good attention in lecture)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Adam's has been my favorite here at Penn State. I highly suggest taking any psych class you can with him. He makes sure lectures are interesting, weekly quizzes on readings, and provides exam reviews which are extremely helpful before exams. The final exam is optional and group presentation at the end of semester

Dr. Adams is a great professor - very knowledgeable and cares about you getting something out of the class, both academically and personally. The syllabus and grading were clear. Review sessions before exams very helpful!! Would highly recommend PSYCH425, and I would take a class with him again for sure if I wasn't graduating.

I honestly adore Reg. He is awesome. His class is not "easy" but if you put in the work its not bad at all. You have quick quizzes every week that you must read like 40 pages for - thats the worst part. His exam reviews are VERY HELPFUL so make sure you go. He is very thorough. he is very bad at answering emails sometimes takes days.

reviews.comment: I HIGHLY recommend not taking both of his classes at the same time (currently taking 425&490). It's honestly torture. He has these stupid thought papers that he wants you to do, and they're so time consuming. His exams are the worst as well, he pretty much test you with every method possible. Multiple choice, Short answer, fill in the blank.

reviews.comment: professor knows his stuff and really cares.

test grades wont determine fate. I got a C,C, B plus, in that order and still finished with A plus.  Argue test questions u got wrong, if youre right he'll give the point. Hes a caring dude whos passionate, wants u to learn and have fun. Im taking him for psych 490 next semester.  Also  Easy 5 ques quizs each wk. just read chapters. take the class.

Gives long winded and poor lectures that drone on, which seem like he just gets to class and wings it without any semblance of preparation or forethought. The TA made/graded all tests and quizzes. He's incredibly hard to reach by e-mail, even if he says multiple times after class that he'll e-mail you or respond. I would avoid taking his classes.
The class is really interesting and the in-class activities are easy points. The exams were easy too.
The class was fascinating, and as long as you paid attention and did the readings before the exam you'll be fine. He's a good professor, and very interested in your input.

Don't listen to what these other people said about Reg's class, it was a piece of cake. If you take the time to read the textbook like you should anyways, you will do well on the exams.  Then Reg gives his students the opportunity to argue back questions you missed on the exam. By arguing I got 2 exams that I got Bs on changed to As. Take the class
His lectures are useless, he's very unclear about basically everything in the class, he has his TA do all of the work, and his in class exercises are pointless.

Doesn't respond to emails all the time, gives ambiguous/ very little clear information about the exams making it extremely hard to know what to actually study, all in class exercises are given the last month of school, has trouble explaining material, would suggest taking a different professor

Reg is a great teacher! He keeps things interesting & encourages discussion. The readings don't take long and the quizzes are made by the TA so its not Reg's fault if they're hard. If you're unsure of something during the test ASK! He will help you as much as he can! Go to class-do the readings-and you'll be fine. Be interested in the subject tho.

I had difficulty with his lack of clarity- his answers are very round-about and hard to decipher. Tests are tough, a LOT of reading. Quizzes almost every class, and doesn't drop any. Just not as interesting as I thought it would be.
Good professor. Very helpful. Grading methods are really unclear, but the class was really fun. I learned a lot. Not easy, but really great class. I would recommend taking him.

Really knows what he's talking about, and loves what he teaches.  Lots of reading and material to know, but exams are fair.  Really nice guy.  Loves answering questions and doesn't mind getting off track for class discussions.  Not an easy A, but I recommend taking a class from him.
Awesome teacher, tough but fair, will take more classes from him for sure.  Cool guy, for sure.

Reg is a great guy, very helpful. He even took time to do review sessions before the test. He's very passionate about what he teaches, but he expects you to know A LOT of info. and his slides are complicated and do not allow for note taking. Expect a lot of reading as well.

Professor Socoski is a fair graders and truly wants to see her student succeed, she made all of her lessons really entertaining and did a great job bringing the class together and work collaboratively. I recommend getting your assignments in on time and you'll have no problems with the class.

Professor Socoski was very kind and funny. On essays you need to follow the rubric exactly but if you do you can get 100%. Lots of discussion and interaction with classmates. I do think we did one more major essay/project than other professors who my friends had at the same time, so you can't necessarily put this class on the back-burner.
Bro just let me write the essay, she literally expands it into a month with different checkpoints… like come on bro. But the workload is pretty light because of how she breaks it up.

reviews.comment: 50/50 feelings towards prof, she has a very millennial mindset, so often when submitting papers or discussing them with her, she doesn't really understand ideas and can immediately give criticism without actually hearing you out, which was pretty irksome. try to participate since it takes a really big chunk out of your grade

Professor Socoski was very cute and quirky and you can tell she really loves English! The lectures could sometimes get boring but ultimately they were helpful for papers. Only 4 papers the whole semester broken down into very manageable parts. Got an A on all of my papers and she gave good feedback.

English 50 is by far the easiest class I have taken and is such an underrated Gen ED! Adriana is super quirky and a great leader in making the class come together! You should easily get an A as long as you submit all assignments on time it's that easy. Great people in the class, and great professor! Gonna miss my creative writing squad!

reviews.comment: This was an amazing class, Adriana was such an amazing professor. Sometimes Essays get a little boring to write and the peer reviews do sometimes get boring. Don't buy the textbook we barely used it. I didn't have problems with my Essays Ive gotten A's on them but if you are worried just go to Office Hours, I 100% recommend taking her for English

Adriana is such an amazing professor. She can sometimes be a tough grader but if you are worried about an essay, please just go to her office hours, she can really help. Peer reviews get boring at times, and it's 4 major essays, but they weren't too bad. You have to buy a textbook (dont buy the textbook you barely use it) 100% take her.

Professor Socoski is a great person, but an extremely hard grader. With most of the grades coming from the 4 major papers, every grade matters. I am not the best writer, but while my work got better, the grade didn't reflect it at all.

reviews.comment: Very nice and understanding but a very very tough grader. There are 4 major papers that she grades very strictly and makes it impossible to get an A. Professor is a bit inconsistent. Semester starts easy, but gets much harder. Pop quizzes given but allowed to solve in groups, with due dates often being EOD. reviews.comment: Good professor, definitely cares about the labs. The labs are more dependent on TA's but its an easy enough class to get an A in.

reviews.comment: He's a fairly new professor, but still good at teaching considering the track record of the EMCH department. The first exam was graded terribly, but there was enough extra credit to bump anyone's grade up a letter throughout the semester. His lectures were not bad at all, and he made a hard course kind of easier. Room to improve, but a great start.

Overall, the class was easy. The lab directions may be unclear some times, but always do able in the time period. The grading was very easy and generous, and the final was straight forward from the practice exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I'd say that he is overall a good professor. He is very passionate about the material and clearly knows a lot. The lectures could be structured better, but his literal explanations of concepts are great. He also is very receptive to all types of questions. Grading during the first exam was terrible but then it got much better.
The man is just starting out, however he's not off to greatest start. He was reading through the lecture slides without explaining the material that well. Homeworks were near impossible.
Would take this class with him. I was nervous from chem but he made it very friendly and simple to understand. He really cares about his students.

Really enjoy the class. Professor is always available and trying to help you as much as possible. Only negative thing, the price of the lab course. Tuition is already extremely expensive and the lab materials are $300+. I wish I'd know about this and would've definitely find an alternative
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Great teacher! He gave lots of opportunities for extra credit and graded fairly.

Prof. Herring is an amazing chemistry professor who genuinely cares about your success. The repetition from pre-lectures to lectures, recitation, and homework helps lock in the concepts. Definitely go to office hours, few attend, so you might get one-on-one time, which is incredibly helpful.

Professor Herring is truly one of a kind. He truly cares about his students and their success in his class. Chem130 was tough but he breaks it down into simpler terms and his grading is super fair. There's also a lot of filler points that can booster your grade and the exams are similar to his practice exams.
I would take this professor if given the chance. He makes you want to try and do well because of how upbeat he is

Probably the best professor I have had so far at Penn State! Chemistry isn't my best subject, but he always did his best to try and make the learning fun. He offers many opportunities for extra credit. If you have to take Chem 130, take it with him if you can!

Probably the best prof I've had at Penn State. Don't be freaked out by the flipped learning style, it's different, but I think many have issues with it because they aren't open to change. Tons of LA's there to help you in class, held after-class office hours for help, and material was so much easier to understand than any CHEM110 professor could do

Professor Herring made chemistry fun again. I truly enjoyed his class and I hope to take a class with him again. Many complain about the flipped classroom he utilizes, however he also teaches in depth in class and reaches out to you if you need help. Also if you ever need someone to talk to, he loves to talk. He makes sure his students do well!

Adam Herring was one of the best so try to get him. I had an 87 in the class the entire semester, but I didn't study too much for the final because of other classes so I finished with a C+. I know a lot of people who got B+ or A- in his class. He was extremely helpful in and out of class, always reachable, and took time to explain information.

Adam Herring as a person alone is great, he is helpful and truly cares for his students, however the course structure is a FLIPPED CLASSROOM. If you can't learn by watching 30 minute videos on the off days and doing virtually nothing in class, take this course with another professor. I truly regret my choice in professor.
professor Adam is great!!! He is so kind and really cares about his students. He wanted us to get good grades and have fun during the course.

Professor Herring was the best. He made this extremely difficult class so fun that I went to every lecture. I really enjoyed having him. Obviously, Chem 110 is really tough, but the TAs and Professor Herring have many office hours and are very helpful. Make sure you go to recitation, it really helps in this class!

Did not like his teaching style at all. rather than teaching in class like usual, he had students and watch 2-4 videos 3 times a week outside of class explaining new material. very time consuming, very tiring.

Professor Herring is amazing I highly recommend taking his class. He gives so many extra credit opportunities and you can always pop by his office hours with questions. The TAs were also very helpful and I liked the flipped classroom because he made in depth videos about each topic we learned (not just reading from the textbook)

Chem 110 is a hard class but Dr Herring is a great professor who cares about his student's success and will do whatever it takes to help them succeed. He is accessible outside of class and his flipped classroom model was great. Lectures are more about reviewing and understanding the material than learning it. He had great TAs which also helped.

reviews.comment: Overall engaging-lecture professor, load is fine and he helps make material easier with demonstration/ system of teaching with flipped class.
he slayed. honestly feel bad i didn't do better

Dr. Herring makes class very education and sometime includes fun demonstrations. He likes to blow things up! If you need help or are concerned about you grade, go to him! He is very helpful and inspiring. I went to him after I wasn't doing well on exams and the next one I got a B+. Utilize teachers like him who want to help and care. Take his class

If you know you tend to struggle with flipped classroom setting make sure to go to office hours as soon as you start and GSG !! Chem 110 can be difficult, but Herring does a great job at preparing his students for the exams. He'll try his best to keep the class engaged and is pretty funny, but his strength is how much he cares about his students.

TAKE PROFESSOR HERRING. He is so caring about students and their capability to learn, always going above  and beyond. He in engaging in lecture and is easy to meet with outside of class. His section has had the best averages for all three exams for a reason. Some people are adverse to the flipped classroom but he makes amazing videos.

He is awesome I highly recommend him for CHEM 110. He truly cares about his students and his classes have the highest averages on exams. He does a flipped classroom where you watch videos to learn the material before the lecture. He makes the videos himself and they are much more helpful than just reading a textbook. And gives tons of extra credit!
Prof Herring is amazing and so funny. He makes lectures very enjoyable and has an amazing energy. He is very helpful in aiding understanding of difficult chemistry concepts.
Amazing teacher, take him!

This was a fantastic course! I felt very successful and comfortable in class. Prof. Herring made this a great experience. He genuinely wanted us to learn and succeed. I've never felt more encouraged as a student. The best professor I've had at Penn State by far! He is a very kind and truly loves teaching! 12/10
Take this professor if you have the option.

He teaches with a flipped classroom. Though I understand the idea behind it, everyone in my study group hated it. We ended up having to teach ourselves basically everything, the TAs either did not give clear answers or they would give wrong ones. Tons of extra credit opportunities, exams in 3 parts, easy to study for.

Adam Herring is one of the best chem professors ever. He hosted so many office hours and generally wanted to help his students. The flipped classroom style was amazing because it allowed for people to ask questions and get genuine help during the class and recitation. Buy the textbook to supplement the videos. TAKE CHEM 110  WITH HIM.

He is a good prof, but the flipped style he uses NEEDS GOOD LAs. His LAs for my semester were not helpful at all, and the grading they did on things like packback (also was a waste of time) was not consistent. His classroom was frustrating with deadlines being changed without notice and the inconsistency in the grading.

Adam was by far one of the best professors I have ever had. I am not good at chemistry nor interested in it at all, so this class was challenging. However, Adam offers A TON of extra credit and is always there to help. He genuinely cares about his students and will do whatever he can to help them.

Adam Herring was a very good teacher and most definitely a very nice man. The only reason I didn't love this class was due to this flipped style of it along with the fact that I was mistakenly put into Chem110B, not Chem110 which meant I had to take this semi bio class for a major in which I would never use bio. Grade forgiveness and curves occur.

Your lab will be led by a TA so you won't interact with the professor much. However Adam always pops into classes and is always so nice and fun and makes everyone feel great. The class itself is fairly easy if you pay attention and put in the work. The lab final is worth 25% of your grade so keep up with the review sheet!

Adam is a great professor. I suck at chemistry, so I would never take another one of his classes, but Adam himself is super dedicated to his students, his content, and his classes. 10/10 I would recommend him to anyone. He'll work with you if you need it and as long as you keep up on your responsibilities it's impossible to feel helpless with him.

Chem 110 sucks. I won't say he was great, but he did the job. He was nice enough, but the class is just hard. Exams are super tough, so know the material. He was definitely better than other professors, but not the greatest. I would take him if you can, because he is the best probably

Professor Herring is one of the best professors I have ever had. I have never seen a professor care about their students as much as he does. He genuinely wants to see his students succeed. He provides plenty of resources for exam prep and there are office hours every day. I can't recommend him enough. If you have the option to take him, DO IT!!

I was scared coming into this class because I heard it was a weed out class & Im not big on bio. I ended up finishing with a 100, but that definitely didn't come w/o effort. Adam gives you everything you need to succeed & more, its really up to your effort and utilizing TA office hours. the average grade was 75.8 (Low being 2 and high 102.)

Best professor ever! He genuinely cares about his students and gives so much extra credit that I ended with a 103%. Chem itself is a tough subject but if you don't pass with Adam then that's on you because he genuinely makes it hard to fail if you put in at least some amount of work outside of class.

The class is difficult content-wise, but Herring makes it enjoyable. He offers a lot of extra credit opportunities and tests have group portions. It's a big lecture and you will need to put in work if you aren't chem oriented like me. He gave me an opportunity to bring up my final grade because I formed a relationship with him throughout the year.

Go to office hour
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Class was taught in a flipped manner (learn content beforehand & then do problems in class). If you dont have a good understanding of chem or did bad in high school I wouldnt recommend taking it with him.  Professor Garner is another great choice & he lectures in class so take him if you learn better that way. Both are great and are super nice!

Adam Herring is a real gem. My Chem110B was a flipped classroom and I really believed that is why I did so well in the class. At home, you will watch the lectures and then apply them during class through practice problems and demos. You can bring a cheat sheet to exams, and do a group portion. Moderately difficult so you have to put in the work!
The flipped classroom was extremely difficult and not helpful. If you struggled during Covid with online school, do not take this class. Only reason I passed was because of extra credit and homework.

I personally didn't enjoy this class a lot as Adam didn't teach a lot in the lectures. We were just asked to do the study guide and watch lectures that he posted before hand. He is an amazing professor but just does teach so it would have been better if he taught the stuff in class rather than posting the videos. Also, I ended up dropping the class
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Beware of pop quizzes--So many papers

reviews.comment: Personally, I'm not a fan of flipped classrooms. If you're not someone who did well learning online, this may not be the best option for you. The exams are pretty difficult and if you misunderstand the material the first time, you fall down a rabbit hole of falling behind. If you don't learn over videos, you will put in more than you get out of it

If you are taking CHEM 110B take Adam Herring!!!! CHEM 110 is a hard class but Adam is always willing to work with students to help them raise their grades and understand the content. He is funny and almost always has cool things to show during class.

Chem 110 is a very hard course, but the style that Adam teaches really helped when tasked with learning a wide spectrum of material in the course. The reverse classroom is good, but I do wish he did a little more lecture, but it was fine if you read the PLA material. His team of TAs and LAs is fantastic and helps a lot.

Worst teacher I've ever had. He makes us watch videos from years ago so the content we learn isnt complete. Taking this chem professor will put you at a disadvantage academically as the other chem professor is just better.
He sends you videos of lectures from years ago and then in lecture all you do is busy work. Leaves you to learning it all by yourself.

Adam is the nicest prof I've ever had. You can tell he really cares about you doing well and actually taking something useful away from the class. Sometimes after lectures I would stay with some people to clear up some confusion and he would always come over to sit and explain. Hes the best. Lots of work, but you'll get that with any chem class.
The flipped classroom works with Herring and he is very caring towards students.

His lectures a great and really detailed, he usually covers most things that will probably come in the exams however the exam pattern and the way questions are asked are very different from the sample papers and practice questions. He gives a lot of homework, otherwise he is a great professor and really approachable.

If you want to pass Chem 110, take Adam Herring. I was on the brink of getting a D, but his curve and extra credit got me to a C. He is by far the best Chem 110 professor. Without him, I wouldn't have passed this class. Everyone knows this class is an extreme amount of work. If you're taking 15+ credits like I was, good luck.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Herring is such a kind and funny professor! He cares about the students and really wanted everyone to understand the concepts in the course. Easy class and you get a ton out of it.

Chem is a really hard class but Prof. Herring is a really good professor, he really tries to get all his students to understand the topics and to do well in classes, when getting bad grades on quizzes, he would try to contact you to find ways to improve the class. Chem is very demanding as it has a lot of homewor s and quizzes, the exams are hard!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Herring is amazing!! He's considerate and explains the material well. You def need to do more work outside of lecture in order to fully understand the work but Herring does a great job teaching. Adam is amazing! When it comes to chem, it's hard no matter what, but his lectures and class set up is super helpful.

reviews.comment: I am so so glad I took Professor Herring this semester! Naturally, Chem 110 is a class that requires effort but Professor Herring made this class much more doable. Prof. Herring was amazing - he worked so hard to help students do well in the class. No matter what, Chem 110 is a fair amount of work, but he made it much more enjoyable and was always willing to help.

Herring was a great professor he really cares about his students understanding of the material. He also provides various options on what you need to focus on most during the lecture (by creating break out rooms for various topics). Would reccomend Herring out of any of the chem professors!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Herring was great!! He really cares about his students and wants everyone to succeed. He is very encouraging and motivating. I really liked him.

Adam was extremely kind and willing to reach out to students to show his support. He was keen and understanding when it came to knowing what material individuals typically have difficulties grasping. His energy is contagious which pushes you to do better/work harder.

Dr. Herring is the best chem 110 professor you will find. I took it as in covid a reverse class ( which I honestly wish my next chem class was this way too). The way that this class is mandated to be by the department (with exams and HW) kind of sucks, but Dr. Herring is the best. He would send us individual emails and always showed he really cared

Professor Herring is absolutely amazing!! I was so nervous for CHEM 110 but Prof. Herring made the class much less intimidating and did a great job teaching online. His lectures were always easy to understand and he had a sense of humor that made the class more enjoyable. He really cares about his students and makes himself available for help!!
Really cares about teaching and helping others in SC220 to understand about studying strategies, learning,motivation, etc. so they can improve not only their own habits but those of other students.

Professor Herring holds office hours during your assigned lecture period where he helps you with your hw, practice tests, and quiz questions. He responds to emails fast and tries to get to know the students. When concepts are difficult to understand he relates the concepts to our majors so we get a better understanding.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I loved this class. I took it online and dreaded learning chemistry in an online setting but Professor Herring created a positive learning environment through zoom. He had us watch the lectures before class and then go to class only if you had questions. I would recommend taking this Professor if you have to take Chem 112 because you will learn!

Adam is the kindest and most helpful professor I have ever worked with before. I took the SC220 course lead by Adam in order to serve as a CHEM110 LA for him. He is very good at communicating and is extremely understanding. He does a great job at explaining difficult chemistry concepts to students, and I look forward to being an LA for him again!

Professor Herring was a great instructor because he let us watch lectures on our own time due to COVID which was really helpful. The lectures were really detailed and the post-lecture quizzes helped with if you understood the content on not. Having a help session every class was also beneficial. The professor was friendly, he was accessible ALWAYS.
Love this man. I suck at chem but he made it doable and he genuinely wanted everyone to do good. Recommend x 10000

Assignments and HW were kinda heavy, but that's expected across all chem courses. Exams were a little difficult, but you should be fine if you put in the effort. Prof Herring and his TAs/LAs were extremely helpful and always provided access to help. Did a great job even with the online circumstances.

it was an online class so we had the lecture prerecorded and during class time there is a meeting where you can all your questions. Also the professor were very caring and and understanding. Chemistry is not my favorite subject but they made it easy and enjoyable Definitely recommended.
Professor Herring was a great CHEM110 instructor! He made the class enjoyable and his asynchronous lecture videos were really great and easy to follow.

Adam is just 111 or 113 supervisor, youll prob have a TA instead and thats what decides your grade. 1 credit class takes 4 hours out of your day and studying for the prelab quiz is necessary but not hard, can start the day before. If you were an A student in high school itll probably be a close A/A-. Class is just a hoop to jump for stem majors

Ive had Adam for both CHEM 108 and CHEM 113FC. Adam is one of the, if not the, most caring instructors I've ever had in college. It's no secret that Adam's a very tough instructor & grader; he expects a lot out of his students, but it's only bc he truly wants his students to do great things. So easy to tell how passionate he is about his work.
I had Adam for 111 and 113FC and he was very helpful. He usually answers questions with a question, only to make you think. He was great at explaining and reviewing topics we struggled with.

Mr. Herring is a good and friendly teacher. His Chem 108B class helps with Chem 110B if you pay attention to him and do in the in-class work. He gives a lot of online chapter quizzes but most of the answers are in the E-Book (if you purchased it). Easy A if you do all of the assignments but the point of the class is to help with Chem 110B.

If you got Adrienne for CAS you are so lucky. She is the BEST professor ever! You can tell she wants all of her students to succeed. She is also one of those professors that is so personable and kind she makes you want to show up to class. Yes, learning about public speaking is boring. However, she makes it fun and she gives great lectures.

reviews.comment: Adrienne IS THE GOAT! This is hands down the CAS you want to take. There is a decent amount of work but it can be done quickly and she is an easy grader. There is group work also, but honestly not too much. I took Cas100A last semester and it was bad, so I dropped it and took this and im very glad I came to this class.
As long as you show up to class and do the work you'll be fine. Dr. Darrah is a caring professor who wants her students to succeed.
Awesome. seriously if you need cas100 take her. Especially if you can take cas 100b. If you need an extension she was so gracious.

Adrienne was probably the best professor I've had at Penn State. Although you can't use notes during your speeches it makes you a better speaker. She gives you great feedback to help with future speeches. 10000000000000/10 would take this class with her again.
top 3 professors all time

AMAZING PROFESSOR!!! Course materials are all basically free here. She provided amazing lectures which were resourceful, understandable, and conversational with classmates for a morning class. On almost every speech assignment, she gave me personalized notes for improvement.

reviews.comment: I've ever written a review before, but adrienne darrah is the absolute GOAT. Attendance isn't mandatory, but super recommended. Her classes are quick and easy, you can do other work in them if you want too. If you struggle with ANY assignment in the class besides the major speeches, she'll help u out, give extra credit, or give an alternative GOAT

Extremely helpful, especially towards the exams the department forces... I think your experience might vary depending on your class. Ours had a bunch of great people which made speaking in front of them a lot easier!
Mrs. Darrah is very nice. She teaches a first-year seminar class so it is not very difficult. Make sure that you stay on top of your work so that you do not stupidly miss an assignment.

You can tell he is very passionate about what he teaches. While you may not find the material all that interesting, he makes connections to it in which students are also able to. Essentially a book club, we are assigned books to read outside of class then are graded on our participation (ability to discuss the chapters in class). 3 absences.

202-B is essentially a book club. 3 books throughout the semester and have lengthy in-depth discussions on them in class. Participation by answering in class is a large part of your grade. No tests or quizzes. But the class is dragged out/ annoying. Only allowed 2 absences all semester and for every extra, your FINAL grade decreases by 5 points
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He may seem intimidating the first few weeks of class but is actually a very nice professor. If you attend class and go to him for help during office hours, he is willing to be flexible and help you with your grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: It's a lil boring and there are readings for every class. Adam is cool and passionate about the class and makes discussions interesting. Graded on class participation, 7 one-page papers, and a final paper. There are worse professors to take than Adam and he makes the class laugh throughout the semester!

Lupo is super easy-going and just cares about getting a good class discussion going. He is honestly really funny, too. There are readings every class, but never more than 20 pages, they are usually way shorter. Two of the books are actually really inspirational and thought-provoking. I have gotten so much out of this class. Also, an easy grader.

Material was boring and professor was not inspiring. For a class that is required for all students in some capacity, it doesn't make sense that different sections are learning different material. Lupo provided a class that no other ENGL 202b professor was doing. The class was barely helpful; content was irrelevant to me. Grading was tough at times.

The coursework was unbelievably repetitive and uninspired. I understand that it's a course mandatory for most students, but the instructor's method of lecturing was drawn out and tedious. I would personally not recommend taking this specific class with this instructor, although he was a nice guy with pretty lenient grading.

Well, I'm not super fond of the material as it's basically four books written as an excuse for keeping gen-eds at college campuses but at least he made it somewhat tolerable. Participation is super critical and you will fail if you don't add to class discussion at least once a day. There's small papers due biweekly but they're only a page long.

The worst part of this class was that you had to attend every single class and you had to read the material. I was confused with his curriculum because none of my friends were doing the same material. He relied heavily on participation for your grade and there is a paper due every two weeks. would not take again

I took this class as a summer course so it moved pretty quickly but it was very easy to manage during the six weeks. there's a paper each week but you have freedom to write about what you want and whatever format based on the readings. discussions were very intriguing but sometimes long. this is definitely an easy A even if you skim readings

Lupo is super nice and cares a lot about the topic he teaches. He allows two absences because participation does matter and can help your grade. 
There are four essays, all pretty easy if you have a decent knowledge already on how to write essays.

Professor Lupo was by far my favorite Professor at Penn State University. Im a senior this year and having the ability to learn from him was awesome! Hes great at class engagement, allowing students to understand material and very fair with grading. Show up, speak in class and feel accepted! Explains everything thoroughly. In ur favor to get an A

I took this class during COVID in SP2021 and it was very easy. There were weekly assignments clearly laid out, and you could easily get by with just skimming the readings. It's really an easy class to manage, especially with Professor Lupo.

Adam wears the same grey shirt and black pants every day, and the very first day of class before saying a word, everybody thinks the same thing. He looks intimidating. Don't be quick to judge because you will quickly learn how amazing of a professor and person Adam is. He cares about his students very much and is a great grader. He is the best.

I literally ended this course with a 98%. He is the BEST to have for Eng202B! I had him for Engl 30 freshman year and he graded harder for that class but for Eng202b if you just try you will get an A, don't miss the weekly discussion posts/ replies and you're golden. The books are actually good to read, take him for eng202 and you won't regret it

Lupo was hilarious, he acted strange and wore the same clothes everyday. He seemed mean, but turned out to be nice and a fun guy to talk to. Participation matters, but you can talk about literally anything in his class as long as it somewhat connects to the textbook reading, which is essential. His class was so fun I actually miss having him.

You need two books for this class that are not very expensive. Professor Lupo is amazing. There are 5 one page homeworks throughout the semester and a research essay. there are no exams and no quizzes. He is an amazing person who is super understanding. he may seem intimidating in the beginning, but he is a really nice guy.

Adam is a really good professor at Penn State. He may seem super cold and uncaring the first day of class; however, he is a very nice guy and fantastic teacher once the class gets started. Most of the class time is group discussion on readings from the textbook. He is a lenient grader for the essays. He is probably the best professor for ENGL15.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The first day he seems harsh and unkind, but he warms up a lot and is actually pretty funny. He does not grade harshly on essays (5 essays). Attendance is mandatory, but class is not painful to go to... lots of group discussion and you really don't need to do the homework readings. He wears the same black pants and gray button up to class everyday.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Adam Lupo comes across harsh and cold on the first day, but Engl 15 turned out to be one of my favorite classes. His discussions are interesting, and most of your responses are opinion based. He cares about his students and wants them to succeed, and the essays in his class are much easier than most other Engl 15 classes.

At 1st he seems a little cold with his policies however he warms up throughout the semester. He is funny, and caring. He wears the same gray polo and black pants & switches to a gray button down when it gets colder. I'd recommend him over other English profs because from what I've heard he's a lot easier of a grader. make sure to participate!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious

reviews.comment: He is an average prof. He teaches and leaves and that's it. I did NOT like him at first (because he is kind of cold when you first meet him) but in the end, he was fine. Also, he wears the same grey shirt and black pants every day for some reason... but he can be kind of funny. Make sure you participate from day one.

reviews.comment: I normally dislike English classes, but professor Lupo made this class bearable. Participation is mandatory in class, but it is easy to contribute to the discussions even without reading. Total of five 4-5 page essays that make up your grade for the course, plus easy points for revision workshops and participation. Fair grader, definitely take him.

Mr. Lupo is a chill guy, great prof who gives good feedback. There's a total of 5 essays, but it's not that demanding. Participation is necessary, but you don't really have to read to join in on the discussions in class. he encourages you to not structure your essay traditionally, and is open minded
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is the best! He makes discussions interesting and is very caring toward students. Go to class if you want to do well since attendance counts a lot. Books are interesting and not a heavy course load. He is a fair grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor Adam is my favorite that now I have to make phrase for him on this website. I'm a natural science major and this class is designed for humanity students. It seems hard to me at the very beginning, but you got engaged very soon. He's great in talking about his lectures and making connection with students. A class that you can really learn.

reviews.comment: You need to go to class. the quizzes every week are difficult because the questions are very obscure. No exams just the quizzes, final paper, and 5 short one page essays. nothing is online so you don't know you're grade unless you see him. loves class discussions. doesn't take excuses for absences you only get 3 free before he deducts

reviews.comment: Class discussions were interesting. Not an unfair grader for essays. You don't really know what your final grade will be until you get it; he doesn't upload grades.

Professor Lupo is a bit of an eccentric lecturer and an easy essay grader. The entire course is about literacy and it is not very relevant to a career, unless you are specifically going into education policy. His weekly quizzes are graded on rote memorization on obscure topics from a dictionary of cultural literacy. I didn't gain much from it.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: He never graded my paper. It was an incredible poignant paper describing the importance of bilingualism in society and how it contributes to both identity and literacy, to answer his main topic for the course. He refused to critique or provide me with a good response to help me improve my writing. His personality gleans arrogance.  bliiind

This page may have some of the most accurate descriptions of Adam. When I first met him I automatically thought he was going to be my worst teacher but honestly he ended up being my favorite. An hour and twenty minute class flew by with him because he was very engaging and excited about his lectures. Also a very funny great guy and good grader
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of my favorite professors at penn state. The first class he seemed very rigorous, but once we got into the lecture, he really opened up. he's a phenomenal lecturer and open to the classes opinion.  Probably one of the only classes where I really learned something of value.

Positively brilliant. Mr. Lupo at first appears a little eccentric, almost robotic, but don't let that daunt you. As soon as you begin class discussions and he begins engaging with you as a student, he is so animated and passionate. His layout of this class was truly eye-opening, and I don't say that lightly. I couldn't recommend him enough.

My favorite professor at PSU. I came into the class with low expectations as I am a science student in a humanities based English class.  This class inspired me and opened my eyes towards many topics. Adam is engaging and his lectures and discussion based lectures make you want to class not to just get attendance but to learn something new.
Adam was my favorite professor at Penn State. He is a true gentleman, very helpful to his students, an interesting, respectful, funny, and intelligent person. I recommend his class to everyone.

English 15 was a boring class, but Mr. Lupo did his best to make it interesting and help us get something out of it. He really wants to make us better writers. He was easy-going about turning essays in, too. Just do the work and you'll be fine.

Adam is passionate about writing and he will instill that passion in you. He gives excellent homework that he grades on effort more than on quality. He helped me overcome my writer's block and got me back into writing. Easy class but you've gotta be a sucker for creative writing. If you are, then you'll most definitely get an A with minimal effort.
Great!

He seemed really weird at first but he's a great prof to take eng202 with. He's actually funny and loves everything he's trying to teach you, which makes this genEd, dare I say, enjoyable. I actually went out of my way to buy the books for the class out of respect for him. Definitely take him.

Adam seemed intimidating the first day, but he?s actually not and he?s a nice guy. It?s easy to tell that he?s really passionate about this subject. This was a very easy, relaxing class which made it enjoyable to go to. As long as you turn in all of your assignments on time, participate, and don?t miss more than 3 classes, you?ll get an A

Mr. Lupo reminds me of what Vonnegut wrote,"The very best thing you can be in life is a teacher,provided you are crazy in love with what you teach...."On days that I wanted to go through the motions, Mr. Lupo, every time, engaged me and the rest of the class with insightful and thoughtful comments.

Great Teacher. Helpful and fun, leaves students up to workshop responsibilities for 2nd half of the year. no final, just an edited short story (c. 10pgs) Fun guy and very interactive. Enjoyable class.
he really made an effort to make this class engaging. his comments on essays were neutral yet poignant.
This is a great class for students who are open to new thought, and what their minds to be opened a little more.

He kind of scared me on the first day of class, comes off kind of harsh but he really is a cool guy. You have to do the readings to get a good grade but the readings are overall pretty interesting. If you have a chance to take the class with Adam I would suggest you take it. He's very willing to meet with you and help you out if you need it.

He seemed weird at first, but he ended up being one of the best professors I've ever taken.  Adam really gets you to think.  You read a lot but class discussion is really interesting. I usually don't talk at all, but I spoke up almost ever class. Def take English 202B with Lupo, awesome guy.

I was unsure what to think after the first day of class, he came off as intimidating.  After I was in the class for a couple days I became comfortable.  Great class, you will learn a lot, converse with the other students, and cover some interesting intellectual topics.  Great class.  Possibly one of the best I have had here.

Not even finished with his class yet and I think he's a great guy.  He seemed scary at first but is very witty and wants his students to converse and succeed. He is funny and The readings are really interesting and make you think. I would recommend him.

He is the worst teacher i have ever had in my entire life. He does not help students and he is very biased. I like the overall class reading. He is really bad when it comes to helping and making you better. he sucks!!!! I hate Him!!! Do not take his class!!!

He would be better as a high school teacher.  His class is dry, too formal, and he comes off an unapproachable.  He believes he is superior to his students.  He thinks it is acceptable to require an insane amount of memorization in an Liberal Arts class and does not see the need to discuss ideas that deviate from his Extremist Right-Wing views.

Best english professor and my favorite class of the semester.  He may seem condescending, but he is worth taking because you learn a lot and its fairly easy.  Study for the weekly quizes and youll especially do fine
love him.  can't say enough good things about him.

At first, I was a little frightened by his domineering personality, but eventually his class became my favorite of the semester. He is a really great thinker and I found the class to be very intellectually stimulating, which is actually refreshing. He gave papers back promptly was consistent in writing comments. I would definitely take this one.
Egomanical and cold but it's an easy class if you go and complete all of the assignments.

He's ok if you like weird sarcastic people.  He expects a lot of participation, which is not my thing, but it didnt hurt my grade much.  It was annoying that he didnt return ANY papers to us all semester, and if we wanted them back we were supposed to go to his office sometime the following semester.

I didn't have this guy in a class but I had him for an advising session and he was completely unhelpful and kind of a jerk.  He could answer none of my questions.  I ended up going to see someone else.  Waste of my time, rude, condescending.

First I hated the class and was really mad that he didn't hand a single thing back all semester and I had no idea what my grade was. If you come to class, participate in the discussions, and do the work you'll be fine. I got an A. I think I would rather have him for this class than anyone else.

pretty cool class. a little unconventional but still fun. it was a real change from being in a class of 30 kids and not saying anything to a class of 20 kids and actually having your opinions heard. fun class. good discussions.

He NEVER hands back papers so you have no idea how you are doing.  The majority of his readings are boring and he takes attendance so you have to just go and sit there. Kinda a sarcastic and humurous guy though, probably not that bad out of class.

He's ok. Not my favorite class at all. He gets on my nerves and makes you feel stupid for having an opinion that's different from his. He never hands anything back so you never know how you're doing in the class. The books are sooo boring sometimes you want to shoot yourself. He's pretty lame too.
Real good teacher. You def wanna get him over other english teachers.

This guy was great.  He gave back papers at least a month after he said they would 'definetely' have been finished.  Really easy grader though and uses current events to keep the class really fresh.  Take him!

He focuses on rhetoric of pop culture, which means the material is fresh. Great sense of humor, fun discussions, and enjoyable writing assignments. His favorite band is Guided By Voices, you'll notice that in his office. I actually enjoyed english 15 because of Lupo. Get his section if you can.
It's fun class, but he doesn't hand back papers or let you know how you are doing in the class.
Not a good teacher. He didn't seem very knowledgeable and he gave virtually no feedback or clear instructions on assigments.

I'm going to have to disagree with my classmate.  While this class was fun at times, overall it got to be tedious to read everyone else's.  And the workload was really extravagant for anyone who's a non-major.  I wouldn't recommend this.

Adam was a great teacher and was very helpful.  We had an awesome workshop class that was a lot of fun.  Adam was very knowledgable and he helped us become great writers.  This is a fun and interesting class!
He's pretty monotonous and hardly EVER hands back papers. The class isn't too bad though (sometimes boring)- it's mostly a discussion class, and the grading isn't too hard.

He demands an unusual amount of work for a Gen Ed.  I was looking to take an easy arts class, definetly didnt get it but did learn a lot about writing.  If you dont mind writing, go ahead and take it, but it isnt an easy GA.

This guy is LAME.His classes are so boring and a waste of time.He never returns your papers and never has anything significant to say about them.You will not learn much in this class, if anything. He is an easy teacher though!
awesome teacher. nice to look at. fun class.
Good teacher, mostly a fun discussion class.

I took this course for an easy Gen Ed and it was for the most part. You get one lengthy assignment every week and you cannot procrastinate on it. It takes up a lot of time. He also grades werid. I mainly got 3/5 on all my assignments and still ended with an A-. As long as you turn in all the assignments, you will be fine.

I've never met him, but his lecture videos were really informative, and he seems passionate about design. The assignments were also super fun. There were several small activities worth 3-5 points, and a final project where we make a simple prototype, and discuss the process. There were also 3 easy quizzes. If you need a gen ed, take this!

Great guy and knows what he's talking about. Lectures are chopped up into smaller sections so you can easily come back later. Grading is pretty lean as long as you put in the effort and feedback is quite useful. Deadlines are very forgiving, just don't abuse them. If you're looking for a Gen Ed to fill the requirement, then look no further.
The lectures are interesting, but the assignments in the class can be very frustrating if you're not an artistic person.

Professor Aeschbacher is a gem of a professor. He is very knowledgeable in his field yet relatable. He cares about the material and about inspiring people through this course. I wasn't sure what to expect when I signed up for the course, but I finished with not only a ton of valuable tools but also a perspective I never imagined. Excellent!

I really hated this class. Theres no clear rubric for the designs you have to make. The TAs grade the assignments insanely hard and they are only out of 7. So you get a 4/7 and that can tank your grade pretty fast. I wouldnt have taken this class if I had known how difficult these projects wouldve been. Pass on this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Aeschbacher does a good job of making this class interesting for everyone, whether you're into design/art or not. Assignments have normal due dates and grace periods (3 weeks) where you can resubmit for a higher grade or just submit later. End of Lesson check-ins involve choosing favorite resources from online lectures & opinion replies.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Good
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Peter is very passionate about this subject. However, his TAs sometimes don't follow the grading criteria and Peter would have to grade the paper himself. A cool thing about this class is that you can resubmit the assignment as many times as you want.
He provided insightful lectures, engaging activities, and help where other professors might be apathetic.

Prof. Aeschbacher was one of my best professors! If you submit assignments early, he'd give you feedback to improve and re-submit. There is also a one week window to turn in assignments so you have plenty of time to complete them. He is extremely compassionate and kind and will take the time to hear you out if you have a question about anything!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Online class is very doable with flexible due dates. Just don't fall behind. Final Project has a strict deadline. Don't need to watch lectures to do the assignments. Easy Online Class Overall

Had Peter for Intro into Architectural Planning Theories. Easily the most interesting class I've ever taken, his lectures break down and rebuild everything you think you know about architecture, planning, and society as we know it. Attendance is not mandatory, but you should go because you will benefit.

One of my favorite teachers, very enthusiastic and makes you think. Funny and approachable. Somewhat lenient with grading, just know the general idea and you'll do fine. Lots of hard-to-understand online readings but you'll get it when he goes over them in lectures. Overall a great and interesting prof, if I could take him every year I would.

Took this as a web class. No tests/quizzes/exams. The content may feel extremely fluffy to non-design/art majors, but it's interesting nonetheless. Assignments and online lectures all have flexible due dates which really helps.
He knows so much about everything and very easy to talk to. You learn so much from him and he's just an interesting person.

Peter was my favorite first year studio professor. I feel that he was a little vague but on purpose. Some students didn't like it because it wasn't obvious but it made you think about design and form thoughts of your own.
Extremely smart and knows his stuff, he expects you to know your stuff too. Don't slack off-if you do he won't be helpful to you or take you seriously.
I love Prof. Aeschbacher! He can come across as arrogant sometimes, but he really isn't, esp. if you meet with him for individual help. He'll make you think and work but it really helps!

One of the most refreshing professors I've had. He'll make you work but the work is relevant and the assignments are intelligent. He can be a hard-ass during crits, but it's to your benefit. If you do anything half-assed or try to b.s. him he'll see right through it. Really knows his stuff, very intelligent man in all areas.

Dr. Nye is a good professor. The class is challenging at first, but once you figure out how to study you'll be fine. 3 quizzes/3 exams (lowest quiz dropped), & no hw. Tests are very specific to textbook, lectures, and videos. Go to class and participate—it really matters & will affect your grade in the end, he's not very understanding w/ absences.

I love this professor so much. The class is super easy if you just go to the lecture and take notes. Lots of questions are similar to practice exams/in class questions. Required attendance but he's understanding if you email him ahead of time. No homework, grades are quizzes, tests, attendance, and participation. So funny & seems to cares about us.

really super nice, cracks awkward jokes and they're lowkey funny. my biggest problem was his lecture style. so monotone. so slow. so hard to focus. other than that, really easy class; participate, study for the quizzes and exams, you'll be fine.
Objectively the best professor at PSU. Expectations are clear, material is taught thoroughly, and you just can't help but like him. Avid wildlife enthusiast.

Such a sweet professor. His quiz/exams are very specific. Attendance and participation is mandatory but gives the option to email him your thoughts on the lecture for credit, which I loved. He does in class assignments at least once a week and you literally just answer questions from a video he shows. One of the best poli sci profs I have had here.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof. has definitely changed compared to previous reviews; he is not reflected accurately. Tests are incredible ambiguous and vague. Super subjective and cherry picks when grading. Doesn't use a rubric when grading. Unnecessarily hard for a 200 level class. Will grade major papers late and give vague feedback. Heed the warning- will kill your GPA.
