All he did was showed videos, assigned presentations and switched on/off lights throughout the semester. Take this class for the easy A. You don't learn anything. You only learn the tolerance to control sleep.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Great guy! Follow his rules and you will get an A. Don't worry about the quizzes, they are all curved. You can't keep track of your grades, but if you just go an talk to him, you are sure to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Do your readings, participate in class, and go to office hours. You will most likely fail every single quiz (I literally did not pass one!!) but sit in the front, don't use your phone, and go to office hours. If you show that you're trying, you will get an A. Don't worry about quiz grades. He cares about his students that make an effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Probably the least useful class I have ever taken. You get out anywhere from 8-8:20 every class, depending on how much he rambles. There is a short paper during the semester and a "term" paper at the end instead of a final that was 8+ pages. The quiz grades I don't think even matter, just DO NOT skip class because I think that's all that matters.

Class  quizzes, participation & a group project. I failed (50%) every single quiz & bombed the group project yet ended up with an A. He cares about his students and will help if you show him that you care. Quizzes are tough but truly don't count towards your grade. Just answer questions during class, go to office hours once or twice, & youre good

This guys is a disgrace to Penn State. He does not support critical thinking or have any idea of academic principles. Very ignorant, arrogant, and thinks he knows all. Take his class only if you want the A grade. You will most likely not learn much from this class.
nice guy, quiz grades doesn't even matter, no cellphone during class, turning in homework and follow directions you will mostly like get an A.

Only take it if you want an easy A. I'm interested in African Studies, so I took this class and was very disappointed. You will not be introduced to new information in the class, except for the videos.  He has so many made up facts to support his claims. And you do not want to argue with him. He actually says that he is always right!
You can't track or predict your grade; grades are almost randomly distributed. Avoid him if you are an A student cuz he might hurt your GPA
Great class. Easy A!! Attended every class. The quizzes were tricky but You will still get an A as long as you are at class.

This was my first class I took and Penn State and I'm so glad it was. Became very close with Prof Abrokwaa over the (summer) semester. I can tell you based off of my quiz grades I should not have had an A, but if you attend every class your grade will jump. If he knows your name from your particpation in class you are on the right track. Take this!

Attendence is a MUST!! go to class and be involved in the final project! quiz are not as important as those two. This is an easy A class if you show you care. Professor is awesome. He really cares about his students. He want students to be involved in the class.

clemente is the man. if you go to his class (and i can't stress this enough, if you don't, you won't get an A) and you do his few assignments, you'll get an A. he is also a really cool and funny guy too. definitely recommend this as an easy GH

great teacher easy A with very little effort don't have to stress in this class even though he act like you should be stressed, very very very nice guy and funny too can get a lil boring but youll get an A reguardless

Dr. Abrokwaa seems like a good man. His quizzes are extremely tricky and he's very detail-oriented. If you put forth effort in the term paper and the shorter paper, as well as sign the attendance sheet every class, you'll get an A. Seriously. I thought I would get a B based on quiz grades and ended up with an A.

He is an amazing person, both inside and out of his classroom. I took AFR192 the spring of freshman year and he inspired me to become an African Studies major. He is very easy going and wonderful to talk to. He doesn't really use his text book but he chooses good books so it may be helpful to read them time to time. Overall, a great professor.

He is a nice and funny guy. His lecture is clear but boring. Quizzes are easy and no exams, but one paper and two presentations. But all of them are easy. Don't buy a textbook it's useless. I recommend you go to class he checks attendance every class. An easy A course.
Sweetest professor I have ever seen at PSU

Lecture is pretty boring so try to take the class with friends. Never keeps you more than 2 hours. Have perfect attendance and you're guaranteed an A. It's like "Whose Line Is It Anyway?" where everything is made up and the points don't matter.

TAKE THIS CLASS! ABROKWAA's goal is to both have you learn about respecting culture as a western individual and getting you an A in the course.  If you go to class and show that you read through participation, you will get an A even if you struggle with the papers. There is only a final paper and project due the last class. NO FINAL EXAM!

Funny professor. Lectures ca be boring at times. Grade mostly based on attendance, so come to every class! 3 quizzes and 2 large group presentations (every gets an A on). As long as you come to class, and somewhat participate in during lectures, you should get an A. I didn't say a word all semester, and still did.

I was really appalled by this professor. He gives you an A if you come to every class. He uses this class to push his political agenda and tell you why western society is evil. You can literally do nothing but come to class and do the quizzes he gives you. No notes required he doesn't use your quiz grades to make your final grade just attendance.
I could ramble on for paragraphs on how he was one of the best professors ever, but i wont. Take him and you will not be disappointed.
Great guy- boring teacher- easy A if you come to class
Easy online class without a huge workload. Great if you have a heavy workload and want to learn a thing or two about Africa on your own time.

He is The Best! You do have to do a few papers.. but there really not that important to overall grade if you go to class and participate.. The class does get a little dry at times.. but it worth it bc some of the topics are interesting and get a good grade as "A" bonus.

Took this course online over the summer and it was awesome. I learned interesting material about Africa. The quizzes were really easy. He is a lenient grader on projects and discussions. Basically just get the assignments done on time and do a decent job and it should be an easy A. The grading scale is ridiculous 90-100 is an A
This Professor was very helpful. Quizzes and tests are easy because they come right from the readings(No surprises). He gives extra credit at the end if you participate. I got an A in the class.

He is an AWESOME teacher! He is so funny and honest. He really cares about his students and makes an effort to reach out to every one of us--he is 1 of the few professors that truly shows his passion for his career.His office hrs r really fun and he takes time to talk to you, like a friend would speak to you. ]I'm signing up 4 more of his classes!

You will be a better person and student if you take him, one of the best professors I've ever had. The person below me is a moron who likely has a single digit IQ, he let us out early every single time. The class isn't that difficult, you learn more than you realize about Africa and life, getting an A is very possible, take him.

Do yourself a favor and DO NOT take this class. It does last the full 3 hours and is the most boring class I have ever taken in my life. There is work and he does actually grade it. The worst decision i've ever made was taking this course.
Awesome teacher.  Very easy course and keeps the class interesting.  Really cares about all of his students.  Just come to lecture and you should get a good grade in this course.

His "3 hour" class is on average and hour and a half and never goes past an hour and 45 min.  This class consists of 2 3 page papers, 2 quizes, a project, and a 7-13 page paper. I studied for 10 min on the 1st quiz and got an A, the project-everyone who showed up got an A, and overall he's an easy grader.  Can't beat a 1.5hr a week 3 cred gen ed

Very easy class and nice teacher. Class got boring at times. No test, but only 2 10 question quizzes. Papers didn't take much thought. Except for the term paper which was 10 pages, but he grades easily. Oh yea also a group project that is hard to motivate yourself to do. Easy A.
One of the most laid back and understanding professors at this campus. He stresses learning rather than grades. Great person.

boring class.  bad teacher, we never talk about african related topics.  we talk about things like the girl sitting next to me who cheated on her b/f, seriously that was a topic of dicussion for over an hour one day.  group project of 16 people!  doesn't follow syllabus.  not very knowledgable.  no tests though.
If you're looking for an easy gen-ed here it is, Dr. Abrokwaa is a really cool guy....just make sure you go to every class he's really big on attendance.
No Comments
No Comments

Abrokwwa has got to be the most awesome teacher ever at Penn State! Very easy, considering there is one major paper and one group presentation. I don't think I know anybody that got less than an A grade. I liked this class so much I went on to major in the field. There is a lot of reading though, but the learning is the better than examinations.

Very nice, smart professor.  The class is interesting if you want to know more about Africa.  It relates well to other classes, too.  He reminds me of Dr. Hibbert when he laughs all the time, even after something sad.  Good guy, though.
Great class, great lectures, easy going class, great professor, also likes to join a disscusion and argue your point of view.

He is a great guy, and knowledgeable in his field, but he tends to be redundant.Furthermore, makes people uncomfortable when he uses them as examples to the class no how "not" to be, and is scared of tackling current issues.Good intentions, surprised that no one  has pointed out the other issues tho

He is a great guy.  Easy to understand and doesant have an ego about him.  He is also very entertaining but thought provoking.  I would definately recommend him to anyone and will take another class with him.

Absoultey amazing class.  Great lectures.  Its a real class based on real life.  Abrowkwaa provides amazing poise in lectures as well.  I will definintely take him again for an elective.  He makes you think.
No Comments

You feel peaceful just being around the man; he exudes a sort of understanding and calm that is completely admirable and worth striving to reach yourself.  How appropriate that he teaches peace and conflict studies!
he is an amazing person.Just being in the same room with him is a gift- he has sooo much knowledge and wisdom to share. I strongly recommend him as a professor. One of my favorite professors at PSU

David is a very nice professor. He gives a handful of homework exercises per unit that are due on exam day for completion points. Exams are worth 72% across four of them. Attendance is only worth 2% so you can skip if you need to but you will struggle without attending. He gives so many simple extra credit opportunities so take advantage of those!

David is such a caring and funny professor. He really wants everyone in the class to succeed. He gave so much extra credit and was willing to work with you if you needed extra help. Overall, he really cared about his students and explained the content really well. As long as you show up to class and pay attention you will do great!

Amazing professor. Extremely hard class, but he makes it seem easy. Go to class and pay attention and you will do fine in this class. . Can't say enough great things about David. He is funny, a very clear explainer, and is always available to help outside of class. He genuinely wants everyone to succeed and recognizes that this is a hard course.

Absolutely the only professor you can take to pass this class. This is one of the hardest classes to take at PSU especially in regards to completing your major requirements. He is by far the best teacher to take due to how material heavy this class is. He is accessible outside of class and gives so many resources to be able to do well. Funny guy
Tough grader, never take his class again.
So annoying, every class has DQ which is the mandatory attendance. So annoying.

I took this class for the spring 2023 semester but never had the chance to write a review. Professor Agler was one of my favorite professors here at Penn State. He was always very funny and wanted his students to succeed. He was very helpful with answering any questions and made this class fun to go to. Highly recommend if you need a GH credit.

Dr. Agler is a fantastic professor. PHIL12 is an extremely hard course, however he explains the topics very well and wants students to succeed. He is very intelligent and has so many resources in order to help students of all levels. You definitely have to put in effort for this class, but its worth it.

Professor Agler is a fantastic individual.  He is a little socially awkward but such a nice guy.  He is very understandable and acceptable for all students' circumstances.  And he does a good job trying to relate the topics of discussion to the class.  I would really recommend this class and this teacher.

I came into this class thinking it would be easy but it was the hardest class I took. I showed up everyday and always failed every exam despite the average grade per exam was a B. If you do decide to take this class keep in mind to start the homework at least two weeks in advance. Great guy but extremely tough class.
Amazing at teaching. Eager to help you learn. If you need to take this course take it with him. I was afraid it would be very hard, but he is such a good teacher he makes it seem easy. Take him!!!

I took this for a GH, and it ended up being one of my favorite courses ever taken! Professor Agler's class is set up so clearly, and what you have to do each week is consistent. The discussion posts were thought provoking. The quizzes and exams were never really a surprise. I definitely recommend this course, and professor :)

Professor Agler really is a great guy. The class itself is super difficult - if you skip one class you will be extremely lost for a majority of the rest of the course - but Professor Agler does an amazing job at making a difficult class pretty easy. Lots of extra credit like I'm talking almost every day we get extra credit. Attendance is only 1%
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult. He stated that leading up to the Final Exam the average stood at a 73 - keep in mind no attend grade. His syllabus also said that an 89 was necessary for a B+, but that may have been a typo. His book is very helpful, online lectures less so but worthwhile. Still, he gave practice quizzes, Extra Credit, and tutoring.
Provide amazing lectures that always articulate all things clearly. He is the BEST.

I have taken PHIL12 and PHIL126H with Prof. Agler, and will take his PHIL426W in fall. He provides amazingly clear classes, and puts all things in ppt thus you don't have to write any. He gives a lot of opportunity for bonus credits. I got 100.18% for this class and finished it 2 weeks BEFORE the final. It is almost impossible to not have an A.

David is such a cool guy. Very relaxed and understands life gets in the way. Class isn't mandatory but going always helps. Not much work and it is fairly easy work. Final is not cumulative. Always, always, always willing to help however he can. He is pretty funny too. Being it's a 9am was scary but he makes it fairly interesting. Take this class!

I had this class at an 9am and showed up a few times. Attendance isn't mandatory, but if you email and tell him you're not coming, he will count you as present. There were three exams in this course and were heavily weighted. He tells you what's going to be on the exam, too. DO the study guides and you will be set.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: David's a person who would try to do anything to clarify your doubts. His lectures are very easy to understand and also, he's a hilarious guy :)

Professor Agler is one of my favorite professors to date. He goes out of his way to accommodate students, whether it be going over problems again and again, or providing countless opportunities to take exams. He is very straight forward about how the course will go (third exam being the toughest) and omits topics that he thinks are pointless.

You won't have any complaints on his expectations of the course. He thoroughly goes over anything you missed and does not make you feel stupid for asking simple questions , unlike many professors. Very direct approach and will exclude things he feels is useless.

David is such an amazing professor and has actually made me want to minor in philosophy. PHILS012 is definitely a hard class but if you show up and have questions he'll be more than happy to help you.

He is truly a very personable good professor, if you need help he will help you, but the books you read are difficult to understand. I spent hours writing short papers for his class because I could not for all that I tried understand the material. He is not a tough grader, come to class do the assignments and you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: PHIL 12 was interesting and Prof Agler is a very good teacher, going the extra mile to help students understand. It's a tough subject but he really does all he can to help you learn and earn your grade. Appreciated the responsiveness. With logic, once you understand the material, it's simple. So read and read again until you understand.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: David was an amazing professor. 4 online quizzes and five exams (1 final) the multiple choice questions are DIRECT definitions from handout. He explains the material well  but you either understand it or you don't. If you like math or logic, information will come very easy for you. I'm a finance major who accidentally ended up in here and got a 97
Great guy very honest and fair grader. He is very smart and funny if you contribute intelligently to the class you will get a lot out of him.
Great professor! Super flexible and approachable. Take his course.

Took Dr. Agler online and really enjoyed his course. He has 3 or 4 papers with a couple assignments in between so I didn't feel overburdened even with 2 other classes. His last paper is worth 20% of grade so theres pressure there and he's a very thorough but fair grader so just make sure you answer all of his questions. I'd highly recommend him.

This course started out nice and easy until you reached the 3rd lesson, but do not fear, Dr. Agler made learning symbolic logic both interesting and easy. You have to put in an effort into this course but an A is easily attainable if you stay on top of the work. Nice prep course for LSAT takers too!

Took this course online and while hesitant to take it to begin with, it ended up being one of my favorite courses. Dr. Agler grades fair and is always available to help answer questions. The homeworkstudy load is not too intense either. Would highly recommend his course.!

Awesome professor!  It helps that the textbook used is written by him, so everything is crystal clear. It's not an easy course on the GPA, but it seems that recent classes have been made easier.  I think our class was his first 012 online class.  He's very engaging and takes a vested interest in how well his students are doing.

Had to take this class as a major requirement.  It was extremely boring and Agler has very one-sided opinions.  It was an easy class, and an easy A, but there's a lot of those out there.  Find one that doesn't take attendance and won't make you write 4 papers.  Don't take this class if you don't have to.
I would definitely take Dr. Agler again. He takes a personal interest in how his class is helpful to students.

Dave lets you call him Dave, so he is the man, his notes can sometimes be a bit unorganized but as long as you are paying attention, the notes are pretty easy to understand.  If you can take one of Dave's classes, do it.

Hands down favorite professor! The subject isn't the easiest to grasp at the first attempt but going to class definately helps. Clarifications and perfect and extremely comprehensible. Very nice and funny. Not a dull class. Highly suggest taking it.
Great professor. The class I took with him was very relaxed and easy, but I still learned what I was expecting to. He gives detailed feedback on exams, papers, and homework.

I LOVE HIM! He is really funny and gives good feedback on everything! I was very motivated to do well in his class and I really enjoy his teaching style which is very visually based... I will be taking another class of his in the future. He cracks up all the time bc he is high on life... he also likes to run a lot... and he has a nice smile :D<3<3
good guy, philosophy is weird to begin with and he articulates the theories well, and won't hesitate to spend time on any question.
Awesome guy. Great class for a GPA booster, all the tests were open note.  Interesting material and very funny in class.  Cool drawings on the board

If you go see him during his office hours, he will help you.  In class, he's kind of incomprehensible and scribbles on the board.  He's funny though.  And he's a nice guy.  I got an A because I went out of my way to ask for his help and studied what he told me to.

Currently a senior and normally wouldn't go to class as much, but I don't think a missed a single one of her lectures. She makes it so worth it showing up to class. You learn a ton. Best 3 problem sets, best 1 exam, and a group project and presentation. Awesome class with an awesome professor.

She cares a lot about your learning and development throughout the course. Class is graded by best 3/4 problem sets, best 1 of 3 exams, and a class project. The problem sets and project is with a group, which makes it a little easier. Great professor, and will learn a ton regarding valuation and M&A deals.
The GOAT!!! Very nice and makes every effort to have everyone learning the material and be on the same page. If you're going into corporate finance, it's a great class to take!

Professor Agnosteva is extremely intelligent and very passionate about finance. Truly cares about her students and the learning experience and took the time in class to go over each problem and allowed time for questions and clarification. Although the exams are challenging, we have a lot of materials, notes, and homework problems to review from.

So caring, wants to know everybody's name and get everyone involved in class. Willing to help and will respond to emails at all hours. Lectures are very good and in-class questions + practice exams are great prep for the real exams, which aren't too hard. Keeps up with the times and encourages AI for learning within bounds of academic integrity.

Professor Delina is the best professor I've ever had in Smeal. She does a great job at teaching and preparing you for the exams. As long as you put in the time and do the homework's and review Tophat questions, you should be fine in her class. She truly values each and one of her students and I never had any professors in Smeal like her.
The best. The class was at 8am but I was motivated to go only because of her. You will learn if you are interested in finance.

She made this class way harder than it needed to be. No flexibility around deadlines even if it is in regard to your own physical or mental health. Lectures are hard to follow, and her exams are extremely tough with no curve.

This is my favorite professor at Penn State. She makes an effort to learn everyone's names and genuinely cares about her students. Her classes are engaging and easy to follow, and the content we learn is consistent with the exams. And she is open to accommodations/adjustments to make sure her students learn and perform well.
The worst possible Finance professor you could take at Smeal!

This class was very challenging but also one of the only finance courses I took at Penn State where I feel like I actually learned despite being difficult. She really cares about her students understanding the concepts and not just memorizing.The MyLab questions did a great job at matching up with the in-class problems and prepared me for exams.

I thought this course was extremely well run and taught. I learned a significant amount of new material that I did not know before and can take with me into the corporate finance world. The exams were fair and we were more than properly prepared for them.

had Delina for 306. one of the best professor's I've ever had. really knows the material and wants everyone to succeed. i don't think she teaches econ still but I highly recommend taking any of her classes. for 306 you just had to attend the lectures and actively engage and you would be fine on any exam.

If you're looking for a sign to take this class, this is it. Professor Agnosteva has to be the nicest professor in Smeal and she wants to help! She curves most exams, weighs your best exam more, and offers plenty of extra credit. HW is easy and she provides practice exams that prepare you for the real exam.
Delina is so sweet.  306 is a difficult course, but if you attend lectures you will do well.

Professor Agnosteva is the best professor I have had in my time at Penn State. She teaches the material in a manner that is easy to understand. She always goes out of the way to help students who display a motivation to learn and is understanding when answering questions.

Words dont do justice to Dr. Delina. Best econ professor Ive ever had. This class itself is hard but she definitely makes it easier and gives a TON of extra credit. Her sample exams are formatted the same as the actual ones but questions do change and vary a lot. Studying is a must but best professor hands down.
Dr. Delina is the GOAT!
306 is supposed to be hard but she made it easy. Lots of extra credit opportunities and very helpful study guides before tests

Dr. Agnosteva is one of my favorite professors ever. She lectures are extremely clear, and if you are confused and go to office hours she is helpful and cares about how you do in the course. This is a mundane topic, but she does her best to make it interesting and fun to learn. If you attend class and study, you will be completely fine.

PLEASE take 306 with Delina! She is one of the best professors I have had at Penn State! She is a great teacher (she knows the material well), she is always willing to help, she offers a good amount of extra credit, and she is an overwhelmingly kind person. I couldn't imagine a better Econ 306 professor.
One of the best professors at Penn State. Dr. Agnosteva has a black belt in economics and knows how to teach what she's mastered. 11/10

This class is not that easy, but is basic statistics class. All content is taught in lectures so go. Graded on 10 myeconlabs, 4 stata coding assignments (somewhat challenging), and the three exams. There was about 6-10% of extra credit per exam which was awesome, all given in class. She is an amazing professor and wants everyone to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I think professor Delina did a fantastic job preparing us for the tests with weekly announcements! The professor was very kind and responded to any questions faster than any professor I have had. There were also some technical errors in the course I think she handled with professionalism and poise.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Delina is one of the best professors I've had at Penn State. She is brilliant, she is overwhelmingly kind to her students, and she does an overall great job of teaching. She is obviously passionate about her job which makes for a great experience for the students. Also, she genuinely tries to make connections with her students .

Professor Agnosteva is an awesome, caring professor. Although the lectures can be a bit of a drag and require you to take a lot of notes, Econometrics can only be so fun. It is a particularly difficult class, but if you show up to every lecture, take notes, and study for several hours you will succeed. STATA/MyEconLab assignments are easy points.

Delina Agnosteva is probably the worst professor i have ever had at penn state. I am a math major so this class shouldn't necessarily be challenging, but it was because she doesn't accommodate you when youre sick, gives zero extensions, her teaching sucks and her exams are nothing like the practice problems. Ruined my mental health and life forreal
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Delina Agnosteva is my favorite Econ professor Ive ever had I would take anything and everything you can with her.
Best Prof ever, definitely take her class

Professor Agnosteva is nice, but she was not impressive. Her class is heavily math based with little instruction. She uses vague videos made by another professor to "teach" math concepts. Barely learned anything the entire semester, just struggled to pass her curveball tests/quizzes. Seems to me she places her online class on the back burner.

Professor Agnosteva really makes you want to go to class. And really tries to make this tough class easy to understand and succeed in. Watch out for the Stata assignments as they are the most difficult part in the course.
She is the best professor at penn state. Very helpful and cares about the work and the students. She will go out of her way to help you understand the subject. Awesome teacher!

Dr. Agnosteva is incredibly helpful at answering any questions. Usually within just a couple of hours (if not less at times), she was ready to help with clear examples (any day of the week). This support system was incredibly helpful. In addition, the course is well-organized and closely connects the content in the textbook to online content.

She is easily one of the best professors I've had in PSU. She is very nice and wishes best for students, and very helpful when student approaches for help. She is also very knowledgeable in the matter, and very organized when delivering the lecture.

Professor Agnosteva is great. I was scared going into 306 as I suck at stat, but she teaches great lectures, and the exams are very doable if you go to class and do the homeworks. The Stata assignments suck, but you only have a few. Overall made a very difficult subject easy and I could not recommend her enough.
the best prof ever 10/10

Dr. Delina is truly one of the best professors at Penn State. She makes the material so much easier to comprehend as she's able to describe complex econometric material in everyday terms. She's absolutely amazing! Still though, this is a hard class. Exam averages are low so be prepared coming in for a very challenging course, it's no cake walk
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Agnosteva tries to make the lesson easy for students. She is reachable outside class and she offers help with the concepts and the STATA assignments. The only thing you need to pay attention to is that she won't help you much with the extra credit STATA projects.

Dr. Delina is amazing, hands down best econ professor at Penn State. Econometrics is genuinely difficult but Delina will do everything in her power to make sure you get it. She's so open to suggestions, so kind, and a really good professor. She wants to be the best version of her self for her students. She really is the best.

Dr. Delina is truly great. She shows how much she cares about her students and makes sure we understand the material and can apply it. Stata is a pain in the beginning, but she always helps, and then it gets better. Read the lecture notes for the exams.

Dr. Delina did a review of statistics in the beginning of the semester and even thought she taught things we already covered in 106, the way she teaches makes the material so, so much clearer. She is organized and her lectures are well-structured, seems willing to help, and ties the material really well together. Definitely take her!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Prof. Agnotsteva care in making sure all her students understood the material really encouraged me to keep trying when I didn't understand something. She is a fantastic professor. Presented clearly and gave lots of opportunities for students to ask questions! Study guides for the exams and homework on MyEconLab were extremely helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Agnosteva was the best professor I have had at Penn State. She cares about you as a person and a student. There were about 100 kids in my class and she still took the time to learn almost everyones name. Her exams were difficult but fair. She also offered extra credit assignments that added 5% to your final grade.

I took this on World Campus. Coursework wasn't incredibly difficult. Sometimes the lesson examples didn't match the way the quiz/test would ask the same question. Quizzes were very similar to midterms and final. Formula heavy so make sure you have good notes. Weekly quizzes (10q) and a homework assignment every other week.

She is good, responds to emails fast & willing to help. The class is bad, this is not a 100 level class, there is pretty in depth calculations and analysis every week. The online videos are not helpful at all. Final is purposely difficult & misleading, 50% math with curveballs. Quizzes & homeworks are unnecessarily difficult. No Extra credit on WC
She is cool take that.

made 311 a lot easier than other profs- even gave us code to get started off on assignments. exam was also a lot easier than previous semesters, and had reasonable content from the review. just pay attention to lectures and go to office hours.

Learn everything there is to know about Bash before this class and attend Office Hours. It will make this class so much easier. Professor is great: if you want to see him flip out say "Vim is better than Emacs" or "I use Arch btw".

Go to Office Hours and treat them like mandatory class periods. There are other people in the class who know a lot more than you so try to make friends with them. The professor is great at LLP but that doesn't make the class any easier. Pray to God.

The best professor I had at PSU, I honestly don't know why he's at PSU with his credentials. He is a brilliant computer scientist and professor, he knows EVERYTHING about systems programming. I started the assignments same day they were assigned and finished them within a week, office hours are really helpful. Tests are easy if you pay attention.

Man flexes by using emacs and a native linux system. Drawing the JBOD layer does not make the code any easier. Professor, please try giving constuctive feedback and hints in the Piazza like you did for assignment 2,3. We are used to coding in IDEs and languages where most of the work is done by the black box compiler.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: I was really hoping there would be a curve but there was not! The class is tough and the professor is not helpful. The homeworks are insanely difficult,some not even related to what we were learning. If you have to take this class, take it with him because he knows his stuff, but go to as many office hours as you can. Prepare concurrent for final.
The worst instructor I've ever met.  If you did not develop good programming skills from past classes, it will be extremely difficult. The course has good content but exams are tough.
Difficult course. He was not helpful.

This is a hard course, but the professor's lectures are pretty clear and gives at least 3 weeks on each of the 5 assignments. He also gave extra credit so even though I got 80% on one of the assignments the extra credit helped recover the lost partial credit so I ended up getting over 100% on all 5 assignments on average. Tests hard if unprepared.

Prof. Talib is extremely qualified to teach what he does. His lectures are very clear cut and if you go you will learn. He wants all of his students to do well. The assignments can be tough but he give plenty of time to complete them. Only negative I can think of is no curves. The class average should be a C, not a static 70-79%. Tests were hard.

Prof. Talib is great. He is very nice and helpful and offers extra credit too. If you go to lectures and office hours, you will do fine. Midterms and the final are based on the slides. The 5 assignments are doable, but the documentation sucks, so you may need to go to office hours. Talib also gives a lot of help on the assignments on Piazza too.
Great guy, very funny and knowledgeable. I will take him again if I could.

If you go to lectures and office hours for the homework you will be okay. Prof is very funny and knowledgeable. Get ready to be roasted as a class for not knowing answers. Exams are difficult but memorize slides and concepts and you should be good. Prof gives many hints for homeworks during lectures and on piazza. Lectures are interesting.

For me the most difficult part of the class was the exams... get ready to memorize useless information most people would just look up. If you attend all the lectures this will be made easier. The other half of the class is 5 HW assignments which build off each other. I found them relatively easy, OH are also really helpful. Great guy!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Gives an extension to the whole class because over half of the class weren't able to finish their coding assignment before the due date. What about those who did finish on time? Nothing! I bombed a midterm of another class for this bro:( He is a nice person though.

The samples he gave for the test were all over the top and didn't give answers or any explanations, it was very confusing. Everyone was very confused before the test I couldn't understand why he did that

The exams are quite hard for me, But prof Aghayev is able to deliver really nice lecture that I could have actually learned something. If there is any question just post it on the piazza, or email him if anything personal involved. He works really hard and tries to be a nice professor. I cannot recommend him highly enough.

Dr. Aghayev is by far my favorite professor at University Park. He may be a bit monotone, but he is so clear and actually a really funny guy. 311 is overall not an easy class, but if you pay attention he teaches everything. He even took time in his office hours to help me prepare for an internship which i ended up getting! Love this man 10000/10 :)

This professor is a GOAT. He plays music at the start of every lecture to get you warmed up. The coding assignments are difficult, but there is plenty of time to work on them. He will always give extra credit and extensions when needed. Definitely recommend.

BEST PROFESSOR. This is a difficult class, but he cares so much about his students and gives a lot of effort to explain each concept and hw. Gives extensions on hws whenever needed and offers extra credit. If you put in effort, you're gonna get 100% on all of the hws.

He's one of those professors that genuinely cares about his students learning the material. He also used to work at Google so he really knew what he was teaching and knew how to answer questions in a way everyone could understand. Held help sessions for homework and didn't want to overwork us. Played banger music before class too.

not the easiest CS class but Talib is good at explaining in lectures. grades are 50% from HW, which build upon each other. he also gives lots of help for HW. exams are the other 50% for grades and can be tough if behind on lectures, but he's lenient in grading. I've heard 311 is one of the hardest, but he made this fun and easier than I expected.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: Not an easy course by any means but he is there to help you and it's more than doable. Homeworks build off of each other. E.g. if you struggled with homework 2, you'll struggle with homework 3. He has office hours and will even post help videos for each homework. Pay attention to lecture, doubly important because there's no textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Talib is one of the best professors in the penn state EECS department. He makes sure everyone understands the material and is a very caring professor. Take a class with him!

Talib made Cmpsc 311 enjoyable and ensures that we actually learn the material. It was clearly evident that he cared about what he was teaching about. One of the best professors I've taken a class with. Highly recommend taking a class with him if you get a chance.

Professor Aghayev is easily my favorite compsci professor I've had at Penn State. The way he taught the material made sense, he'd give background on a concept, teach its syntax, and give code examples at a minimum. You felt stupid asking a question and he'd always give a great response. All in all he created an awesome learning environment, 10/10.

He is a fantastic teacher that genuinely cares about the students and making sure the topics are understood, he also likes to add some fun to the course with his "Supply Chain Around Campus" videos. He is very available and responds quickly to emails with any questions you may have. A lot of reading but helps drives the subject home. Recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment:
Norm continuously talks to everyone in his graduate level courses like children. The number of group projects is atrocious and if you can't improve a team members work, he will just insult you rather than trying to help.
Overally SCM850 also managed to teach nothing new as the capstone which is incredibly disappointing
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Challenging professor but pushes you to think through your work. Personally enjoyed his classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Norm is an awesome professor! I've had him for two classes and he's been one of the best professors I've had as far as feedback and help with an issue. Now, I will say, he has a TON of reading within his modules. You truly don't have to read most of it but it does help you understand the module better. He does use Harvard publishing $40-$80.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolute horrible professor. All the reviews here are right. He is extremely difficult to work with and pretends to be jolly while ripping anything you submit to him. His rubrics are more complicated than the cases.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Very dislikable person. Socially awkward. No real work experience in operational logistics or if he does it is definitely outdated. What a waste of my money earned in the real world to pay for tuition. He should go to middle school and teach an English class because he like to talks to as if you were a kid. Unmemorable.

This man is squirrely. Extremely tough and subjective. Knowledgeable yet useless. Way too many outside sources required, to study but pointless for grades. He will critique your work without reason, without fairness. No mercy. He veils his dagger with jokey messages. A real fake. Beware ! Dot your i's and be prepared to dispute up the chain.

This professor is a absolute rogue. He take whatever liberties he wants with your grade, and will critique you on things that are not in the grading rubric. You can easily lose 15% on an assignment over formatting. When you appeal he will completely ignore you and even insult your attempt to challenge. He is that professor everyone hates.

Pain in the neck. TONS of reading. Very difficult grader. I am not being biased, this is a truth honest review. Very knowledgeable and interesting course work but expect to spend 12 hours reading per week or you will not do well. Assignments are weighted heavily so once you do poorly on one, very difficult to catch back up.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: complicating the issues
Easy A.....NOT

Aggon is a nice professor who wants his students to leave class learning something. He tried to make the class interesting, but many of the time the material was still boring. There were 3 exams, homeworks, and extra-credit quizes. I never really felt confident walking out of exams, but must of gotten lucky each time because I still ended w/ an A
More or less a boilerplate lazy professor. Any questions on the material are immediately directed to the TAs - would recommend taking this class with another professor.
Great teacher. Makes class interesting and relevant.
Really GREAT TEACHER! HA!

talks at a million mph.  no good way to study for the exams because 40% of the questions come from nowhere. highly recommend getting a different teacher if you can because his exams are the hardest compared to other BA302 teachers. if you have him... GO TO CLASS otherwise you'll do awful on the exams!
Awesome guy, funny, makes a good-hearted attempt to make his class enjoyable, but also provides knowledge and experience that he brings to the classroom

Norm is a great guy and is always there to help. The lectures are a little boring, but I've had worse. Overall the class isn't too difficult, but the tests are a little tricky. I don't have any reason to say not to take him - other than it isn't a joke of a class.

Lectures are incredibly boring so you'll never want to go to class. He'll make exam questions from something that he said one time in class so people actually show up. Wording on exams are always confusing and questions are mostly case based. If you are not a supply chain major, definitely try another professor for a 2 credit joke class.

Norm is a great guy. Supply chain as a subject is pretty boring but he tried to make class fun and interesting. The tests were hard and the questions were worded very confusingly, but the extra credit really helps. Go to class, do the homework and quizzes, and read the book and you'll be fine!
good professor.  can be dull at times but a really nice guy & tries to mix up the class with videos & jokes.  easy class overall.  do the hw and quizzes to help boost your grade :)

Norm was really, really easy. Tests were just common sense, and homework and quizzes brought the grades up even more. If you had a hard time with this class, you should just drop out. He's a nice guy, albeit a little strange. Second half of the class is very repetitive (ie. shorter lead times, reduce costs, be lean).
Tests were extremely difficult
Aggon is a good guy and makes class interesting.  Tests are extremely hard however quizes/homework will bring up your grade.

Subject matter is bland, but Norm did what he could to make it interesting.  Tests were impossible, but had a ton of quizzes/extra credit stuff to help pick up the grade. Could have been a much worse class with a different teacher.
He is a nice guy and pretty cool as far as teachers go. The tests are unnecessarily hard and his lectured jump around in the book so bad it is hard to study. Not easy.

if he spent more time on writing a decent exam instead of saying how the football season wasnt bad, he would be a good teacher.  multiple choice questions had up 8 choices!  the last quesiton on the final was "how will supply chain impact your careers" and there were 6 choices and the answers were "1 2 5 are correct, 1 2 6 are correct"

I can't tell you much about the prof because i went to the first class and haven't gone to one since.  you can learn everything from the lecture slides(posted online) and the book. exams are relatively easy and he curves to keep a solid avg. don't believe the other comments about needing to go to class. it aint true. recommended.
He is very energetic
tests are hard. you need to go to class.

Aggon is a nice guy, and I suppose better than other lecturers for supply chain from what I've heard. However he wasnt very willing to help. The material is boring, not always clear, and doesn't follow the book. Be careful with the book, he asks questions about it not covered in class.
I liked him. Class was straight-forward, information was clear and the material was fairly easy. Go to class and you're set.

Norm is the man! The info is not that exciting but he tries his best to make it interesting with his little jokes and funny studies like the Oreo study.  It is a good idea to attend class, take good notes, and read the book and you can get a good grade.  The tests are a little hard but he is there to help and he is very approachable.
Norm is a great professor.  He makes this class fun.  If you study for the exams and do all the easy assignments you will get a good grade in the class.  If you take BA 302, make sure its with Norm!

Norm is a wonderful human being.  The jokes are corny but add variety to the class.  On a human level, Norm is one of those guys who are here to help.  He's enthusiastic about the subject and presents it in a direct, yet borring, manner.  Read the book, go to class, write the words he says, and you'll get an A.  Highly Recommended.

Norm is the man. One of the nicest guys I have ever met. When I was in a car accident the summer i had him, he was really cool about everything and gave me extra time on assignments. He looked out for me and asked how I was doing with my rehab. The best professor at Penn State.
Extremely nice guy.  Class material isn't my favorite subject but he tried to make it interesting.  Class isn't too bad and he's such a nice guy but I've heard it's one of the harder BA302 sections.

The class material is very boring and not interesting but prof aggon really makes the attempt to reach every student, he is a good prof. Go to class and pay attention and also a plus you get to see the quick combover routine right before class..but in all serious on a personal level, he is very approachable and there to help
Norms a great guy...fun class, def a good teacher to have

Corny jokes but an extremely nice guy.  Tests can be a little difficult but he's willing to help anyone that needs it.  Possibly a bit harder than other BA302 professors but definitely not impossible.

I actually really liked him.  The exams were kind of difficult, but if you study the notes and read the book, you should do OK.  Do the preview quizzes, and show up to class...because there will be random extra credit problems (that are simple, because it was on the topic that was introduced that day).  I'd say take it with him.

Norm is energetic and knowledgeable, but for some reason, I didn't like his teaching style; felt like his class was harder than the other B A 302 professors; grade composed of 3 tests & 4 homework assignments; there is extra credit up to 3.5% points; got an A in the class; probably wouldn't take a class from him again
The class material is boring, but Professor Aggon makes it seem interesting. Very nice guy and helpful.
Nice guy but very unclear and confusing lectures/exams
Like all BA's, this is an absolute waste of a class.  It's the worst BA too.  Anyway, Norm's tests are kind of tough and the material is terrible.  Hardest (and unnecessarily so) BA 302 prof.

Like everyone said, he's a great teacher but the class material really sucks. I have great appreciation for all those supply chain majors out there, I couldnt imagine having to take another 5 or 6 classes like this but again AGGON really means well, go to class and pay attention and a "B" is very attainable in the class
A tough class, but Norm does a good job explaining everything.  A really great guy.

very, very good prof works hard. tests can be difficult but fairly easy if you attend class, pay attention, and study your notes. i thought he was an excellent prof and has a lot to do for the size of the class.. a great class!

Class is very boring. Out of all the BA's this has got to be the worst. Aggon isn't to bad, just the course content sucks. HW is tough. Tip: get alot of friends and work on it together. Test are kinda tricky.  Just do well on h/w's and quizzes to get ur extra points at the end of the semester.

not an interesting subject and he's really not an interesting guy. but he knows his stuff and he challenges you. the tests are straightforward if you go to the class, take good notes, and study hard. the test questions are taken from the notes, not the text. pay attention and the class isn't difficult. but you gotta show up.
Great class.  Easiest prof on campus.
Stormin Norman was a fun teach and made the class much more interesting!

The key to any junior core course is getting a study guide that's filled out from someone who already took the course. I didn't go to class at all from mid-February up to the final in early May (not even the review, cause it's all on ANGEL)... I got a "B".
sucks for you if you have to take it--worst part of the junior core by far

Aagon is an ok guy. The class is not as bad as everyone is saying. Tests are straight from the notes, nothing really from the text at all. The HW is alil hard but you can drop the lowest one. It's def not the best class but it's not the worst either.
Aggon fails to stress the main points clearly.  The first 10 minutes of the class are a waste of time.
he could explain hard concepts better
where do I start....hmmmmmm the information is useless...it's a bunch of b.s. and not to mention that the ****en exams and homeworks are hard as****..hmmmmm one more thing I hate the class!!!! :-)
lectures aren't too bad but the hmwrk quizes are tough and so are the tests....it sux that this is required
As if i didn't hate supply chains enough before this class, it made it much worse... Beware of the exams, they're WAAAAYYYy harder than you could ever imagine, so study like crazy.
Aggon's a weird guy who loves supply chain management.  Tries to make jokes, but they usually suck a big one.  He's alright but his class is horrrrible.

Nice guy, but EXTREMELY BORING teacher. The material is often common sense- but exams are ridiculously hard, uses lots of "except" and "none of the above" questions in the tests. Also requiring quizzes to be taken in computer labs is outrageous- not to mention they're hard as ****
OK... material is ridiculous and tests sucked my balls.  He is an awesome guy and always willing to help.  class was pointless, all common sense... but not easy at all..
YOU COULD HAVE A MONKEY TEACH THE CLASS, AND I WOULD HAVE LEARNED JUST AS MUCH!  HE HAD NO PERSONALITY.
very nice guy. though the material is not the most interesting, he makes class very enjoyable. A+
No Comments
very lively person which makes class interesting.  very helpful advice in preparing for college life through first year seminar
good class
No Comments
SOOOO BORING

Normy is nice, but the tests are like the SAT vocab section.  Supply chain is common sense, but you will no doubt get a 'C' in the class thanks to P. Alex Thompson (The rudest and most ignorant T.A. I've ever had).
he is such a nice guy and even though class may be a little boring it is super easy

Class is incredibly boring, but very easy if you pay attention.  No offense to Norm, who does the best he can with the material.  Norm is pretty funny, and he's nice to everyone, and he will help you out.  He's pretty cool.
The class is way too indepth for 2 credits.  The tests are very tricky.  They test your knowledge of word comprehension rather than subject matter.
Makes this class entirely too much work for 2 credits.  Thinks he's funny.  Nice guy, not funny.  Not always so clear on explaining things but tries hard.
No Comments

He is a very nice teacher who actually knows something about what he is teaching.  He relates the material to everyone's major and explains the relation.  He is funny because every morning he says "Good morning, good morning, good morning!"
No Comments
he loves to repeat things three times in a row...good morning, good morning, good morning! i miss norm! he is such a nice guy, friendly and and always willing to help you out.
Very nice guy.  You can tell he enjoys his job.  He is very helpful to students who want help.  I would highly recommend taking one of his classes.

Dr. A is one of the best professors I've ever had. She genuinely cares about all of her students and provides great feedback on projects that are applicable to real life and can lead to success. Dr. A is a great example of a professor who is both a great professor and a good person outside of the classroom.
Emily is amazing and super passionate about her work! She is very caring and is open to having great discussions in class. She is very flexible and always willing to work with you.
Dr. Perez is a very caring professor who is willing to work with you. She makes time for her students if they need help and provides great feedback which results in well written papers.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Aguilo-Perez's English 15 class was great! It was definitely a good amount of work, but the majority of the essays and projects are flexible and have a wide variety of topics to work with. She is always open to help you with your papers, as well as work with you on your ideas in a positive way. You have to take ENG15 at some point, take her!

Agnieszka isn't that difficult but the Math 230 overall is. She assigns 4 quizzes with a couple questions but you get the whole class time to work on it. You will only work in the textbook for homework problems. They aren't difficult as long as you do not put them off.

I was scared at first that she wouldn't be a great teacher because she's a grad student, but she was one of the best teachers I've had so far! She really seems to care about her students doing well and understanding the information. She can also be pretty funny and is very good with answering questions. Highly recommend.

There are some homework from textbook every week, it is a lot but it helps you keep track of the class. She has a little bit of accent but good enough to understand. She is also really patient and the exams are not that hard. One of the amazing class I've ever taken.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Aaryan is the GOAT.
all around solid guy. easygoing, authentic, and funny. i just wish his handwriting was neater
He can have my children

Great TA. Very fun guy and actually host useful recitations that reviews key points from the main lecture as well as going over practice problems. Also he gave us donuts on the last recitation. Pick him.
Super nice guy and a really easy class. Just pay attention and take notes and you should be fine. Aaron is always telling stories which makes things more personal and more engaging.

Super super nice guy and very understanding of all situations. He is just an overall good person and his classes reflect that. If you read and use the textbook, you will do well in his classes. Could not recommend enough!!!
One of my favorite profs at PSU. He is funny and understands that we have other classes to focus on. Easy exams and they're all online.

Dr. Miller was awesome! Exams are all online which is really nice. Assignments are minimal and very easy. Lecture slides aren't posting and there are reading quizzes in class but they're very easy. I'd recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Hilarious--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller was such a great professor, he explained in lectures very well and gave great examples. Such a fun class and he made learning enjoyable.

He is a super chill guy who knows a lot about Health and Human Development. He understands you are a kid too not just a student. Take this class, it is not very demanding at all and you learn some interesting things. He also cancels class sort of frequently/that or lets you out early. Attendance contributes a lot to your grade so go.
His class was so easy! A very interesting class and a really nice teacher

This professor would always go through the slides very quickly and would never post them. It is essential to be a fast note taker, or, if not, to make friends who will share their notes with you. Attendance is not mandatory; however, there are random questions that are done once a week that can only be done in class and are unannounced.
Very nice and obviously cares about the topics he is teaching. Sometimes lecture heavy.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This guy is the best. I mean idk if it was only how he runs this course or what, but I've genuinely never taken an easier course. Don't even think I went once for the last month of the semester and still got an 100. All tests are online, very few homework assignments, attendance never mandatory. Funny guy too. Totally recommend for an easy gen ed.

Liked this class more than I thought I would. Dr. Miller gives a lot of good personal anecdotes that actually help with understanding, though he can be a bit monotone at times. I thought the textbook helped, but it's not needed. Exams are on canvas and open note/book so as long as you show up to lecture and pay attention its a fairly easy class.

Aaron is definitely much better at teaching 239 than 229. It was his first time teaching 229, but you could tell that he was unfamiliar with the material. His lectures can be monotone, and I enjoyed 239 because he had funny personal anecdotes to include. I was fairly disappointed with 229 because I thought I would like it more. Easy class though.

Dr. Miller is a great professor. I have taken two of his classes and would take more. The exams are easy and there are occasional attendance papers to boost your grade. He relates topics to his own life and makes frequent "dad jokes".

Dr.Miller's lectures are boring, and you have to attend to get the notes bc he doesn't post the slides. He does not answer emails, and neither does his TA, so you must talk to him in person. His exams are easy. He also has reflection papers occasionally in class, but you don't know til the day of, so if you're not in class, you can't do them.
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: While lectures aren't the most interesting, he is a nice guy and as long as you do the assignments & show up to class you should do fine. There is a semester long group project, but it's not hard and you get class time to work on it. There are quizzes, but they're open note, and engaged learning hours that aren't too bad if you keep track of it.

HDFS 315 with Aaron Miller was the easiest class at Penn State I've taken. Attendance isn't mandatory, lecture is note heavy but is interesting. He gives extra credit, and all tests are online. He grades his tests super easy (if there is a small writing portion). Final is optional, but if you do take it, replaces your lowest exam score. Very chill.
Quizzes and test are pretty easy, lectures are interesting, and occasional papers.

My favorite professor this semester! So funny, down to earth, and facilitates just a calm, relaxed classroom environment. This class was extremely interesting and was taught using slides and occasionally videos/documentaries. There are 4 exams, 3 student choice assignments, and often short  reflection papers for participation so go to class!

Professor Miller was very sweet and caring! There aren't many things that are graded in this class, but as long as you attend most of the classes, you will do well. He does some attendance papers, so just make sure you attend regularly. Exams were online due to TA shortage but may be back in class depending on how that looks. Would recommend! :)

Dr. Miller is so great! All exams are open note, and he usually gives a day or two to complete them. His lectures are interesting and he always brings in his own personal experience with his kids which makes lectures funnier! There are very few assignments for this class--just taking notes and coming to class because he doesn't post slides.

Canceled class at least once every 2 weeks. Not passionate about teaching. Said ppl in working/lower class "work low skill jobs" & "have children before marriage if they get married at all" after asking students to raise their hands to identify which class they're in. 60-80ish ppl attend out of 120-140 ppl enrolled. Ppl walk out of class regularly.

Easiest class I have ever taken. No exams. Only projects and you don't even have to present. The only difficult thing was getting 20 hours of community service, but he let me use my THON committee hours. He is so chill, and the quizzes were stupid easy. He is also super nice and funny and half the time I did other work in his class.

Professor Miller is a great guy and genuinely cares about his students. I recommend going to class even though it is not mandatory. Some days he will give out extra credit for being in class when not many people are there and the in class videos are often on his exams. His exams suck though, half of the questions aren't in the notes.

Maybe 5 homework assignments, 3 exams and a final (bulk of your grade). BUT, everything is online. Yes, he is boring to listen to, but he tells some great stories and can be pretty funny. Attendance is not mandatory (and also not needed, he posts the slides) but if you show up he gives you extra credit. Says to buy the textbook but I never used it.

Test heavy, doesn't answer emails, TA does all the grading and is very harsh. Dr. Miller is very boring and does not grade attendance but the in class videos and discussions will be on the test. I would avoid him if possible.

Dr. Miller was very funny and a great professor. Provided entertaining lectures. Loved his class! Class is often let out early and attendance is not mandatory.  Easy assignments and tests (online) are based on the content in the slides.  100% recommend this class with Dr. Miller.
Super nice guy, seems interested in what he's teaching. Has a boring voice and his slides have not much on them, class often canceled or let out early. Take him but don't fall asleep

I've had Dr Miller for a few classes in the past, and always enjoy his lectures. Not many assignments for 315, and attendance isn't mandatory, but still recommend going to class. Gives extra credit but on days when few people are there. You get out of what you put into the class, so participate and ask questions because it makes all the difference.

Dr. Miller is kinda boring, but he allows cheat sheets for exams, a couple outside of class papers & quizzes, so other this class was very easy and honestly didn't require much. He takes attendance for XC randomly but only annoying thing would be that videos shown in class are often on exams.

Not much work, do all the assignments (quizzes and short papers). I got by fine without reading the textbook, but probably would have bumped my grade up to an A if I had read it.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I attended every lecture and took notes, however the exams were very textbook heavy that it caught me off guard. He provides different assignments and quizzes during the semester so it's not just based on exams. He also provided extra credit when you were in class. He was entertaining and the lectures were interesting.

Few things to know: they are hard graders, he takes a lot of questions from the slides, he reads off the slides, kinda boring, and test heavy class. Gives out some XC for attendance. Not a super hard class if you go to the lectures
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr.Miller is overall a great person, but tries too hard to be funny at times. The tests are fair, but make sure you read the textbook and take detailed notes from lecture.

reviews.comment: A really nice guy. Gives out random extra credit (not a lot, but still helpful). Also, go to classes, although attendance isn't mandatory, there're 6 reflection papers given in class. The tests are simply based on the TEXTBOOK, not the lecture, so read the book. Then you will know where to find the answers during the test (it's open-book).

Professor Miller is a great professor. He offers extra credit and in-class reflection papers that can really boost your grade. His exams are quite challenging however, they are online and open notes. He also gives an option if we want to take the final exam or not based on our previous exam grades.

He is a really nice guy. The tests and quizzes are super easy if you have your notes and textbook pulled up. The exam questions come mostly from the book however they arent hard to find with a simple command F. I definitely would recommend him
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is okay. I would not take this class if I didn't have to. The tests are worded weirdly and asks a lot of questions he never went over. He never responded to my emails, and they were about if he was going to open up the test to see which ones I got wrong. I did not think that was too much to ask for. So I never got to see what I did wrong

Reading through some of the other reviews from this semester, I was confused because the tests were relatively easy. Just go to class and you wont miss a reflection paper. He also gives a bonus one at the end of the semester if you missed one. The worst part is probably the Youth MHFA and some of the quizzes were difficult but you get 3 attempts.

All exams and quizzes. Reflection papers are random but still, loads of points are missed if you do not go. He reads from just slides that are on canvas. The tests- just read the book. He gives no clear answer in slides.

reviews.comment: he never answers his email ever. also he doesn't take attendance but instead does random in class assignments and you never know when they will be. the tests are impossible and the questions are so confusing. he has little to no energy either so how am I supposed to be interested in class when he isn't?
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Miller is hilarious, so it makes each class pass by quickly. The information is pretty basic and you can kind of figure it out on your own, but the class itself is really interesting. In order to do well, you have to read the textbook outside of the class which is a lot of reading if you fall behind.

This is not a hard course by any means but if you care about your major and are hoping to gain serious insight and meaning from this class, don't take it with Aaron. He does not even scratch the surface of these topics and expects memorization. READ THE BOOK. Some of the test and quiz questions are literally plucked from the text.

We have quizzes every sunday and 7 one page papers due throughout the semester. There's only two exams but they're based mostly on the textbook and not lecture. Honestly, going to lecture was useless because it would conflict with the textbook information and he never knew the answer to any of our questions. But, he did tell a lot of great stories.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: took this course for GHW - super easy! love this professor, he makes zoom lectures fun. He cancels them often. quizzes and written assignments due each week but takes max 30-45 minutes to complete both. easy A if you just do the work. highly recommend!!

I took the hybrid course, where we met in person once a week and the rest was online. Attendance wasn't mandatory in person, but those lectures were a good addition to the lesson material he posted online. There were weekly homework assignments and short quizzes. Not all of them counted toward the final grade, though.

The majority of this class was taken online, with in-class meetings happening once a week every two to three weeks. His online lessons are easy to comprehend and the textbook isn't overly necessary to do well. The assignments, quizzes, and papers are also really easy as long as you apply some effort. This class does have a mandatory field trip.

Dr. Miller was one of the best professors I've had. He is so funny and he makes lectures so relatable. The test are very hard, but if you read the book and come to class you should get at least a B. You can skip, but he has random reflection papers that are 10 points. He was a very nice guy and I would take his class again.

Professor Miller was engaging throughout his lectures. His tests are difficult and reading the book for the tests are a must! Even with studying out of the book and slides it can be difficult to get an A on the exams. He gives graded reflection papers without any heads up so attend class regularly, the reflection papers are an easy 10/10 tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: i really enjoyed the class and Dr Miller is funny and personable and tells stories that relate to content which make it easier to remember. attendance isnt mandatory but there are random reflection papers due for credit in lectures sometimes. posts slides online but there are reading quizzes (he tells you in advance) so you do have to read the book

pwpts are heavy w/ notes. incorporates his personal life into lecture. great professor. sometimes can be boring. exams are pretty difficult & cumulative. exams 35 multiple choice & 2 essays. txtbk isn't required but can help for exams. gives out random reflection papers tht count towards grade. passed around a sign in attendance paper evry class

I have never had a professor like this in my life. He is so rude and expected so much out of an intro level class. I thought I was coming here to learn how to use Adobe, not be critiqued like I was in a professional client meeting. Nothing is ever good enough for him and don't expect to hear a compliment. Literally don't put yourself through it.

Decided to take this 1 credit class because I thought it could be useful. He is rude, disrespectful, and grades hard. It seemed like he would make sure to yell at someone at least every class. Get ready to spend hours on a 10 point homework assignment every week. Don't take this class unless it's necessary for your major.

He makes it impossible to succeed & contradicts himself so you never know what to do. He is mean, doesn't know how to teach, and makes students feel dumb. Do not put yourself through this.
would rather not get student football tickets, miss the white loop and have -$200 in my lioncash then have to take this class. worst prof & class I've had to take in my life. I am 21.

Worst professor I have had at Penn State. Monotone lectures and very boring. Attendance is mandatory probably becuase no one would come if it wasn't. He is very unclear with directions. His lectures are also super unorganized and slow. Seems like he is just filling the time because he is somewhat unprepared. Extremely harsh grader.

Ron contradicts himself in every class critique. He will tell you to do something, and then when you do, he will complain and tell you its wrong. He is a Harsh grader. If you don't follow his instructions perfectly he will find a way to take points off. He assigns an absurd amount of work each class and expects perfection.
Ron will give you a lot of professional insight, he's picky but the industry is also picky. It's more like a job than a class, but you can learn a lot. very strict in his grading

I would never ever advise taking professor smith. This class caused everyone constant stress. He was not helpful and would often dismiss you if you did not do things his way. and then he would throw more and more work on top of it.Most of the work was just unnecessary and you have to visit him outside of class or go to his office

I was really excited about this class but ended up being very stressed about it every week. The content isn't too hard, but it will not be an easy class if you have no knowledge of Photoshop or InDesign. I went in for extra help and felt he was quizzing me instead of helping me. When I wouldn't know something he would belittle me.

The other reviews are bad, but I liked Professor Smith. Attendance was mandatory, but since we only met once a week for 10 weeks, that makes perfect sense. He was always very kind to me, and it was easy to get a good grade when you follow the notes. I did come in with lots of knowledge already with Photoshop and InDesign so that prob helped.
Had Ron for two classes and would not take another with him. He is not a bad man, but his grading is ridiculous and there group projects are extreme. I dread this class every week

I have taken two courses with him and pray to god that I dont have to take any others. He is the worst teacher I have ever had. Brutally harsh and only does group projects. Tomorrow is my last day of class, and since he has shot down our classes' project ideas for the last month everyone is less than half done their final projects. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
He is extremely strict and mean. Every single class is mandatory.

This professor grades extremely hard. I went to office hours at least once a week looking for feedback and would change everything he told me to, however, I would still get a ton of points off for aspects of my design for things he never mentioned. It is very frustrating getting points off for things I did not even know I needed to fix.

Ron does his best to exclude individuals and make them feel small. This class could be a lot of fun and very creative yet people sit in silence as he spews his negativity. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The class could be so fun but it sadly made me very stressed. Incredibly confusing class structure that does not use canvas. Instructions for all assignments were very unclear. Ron is a very tough grader. I went into this course not having any knowledge of graphic design and that would normally be okay, because it's supposed to be a beginners course. Although, it is not. reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: HORRIBLE and I mean HORRIBLE. The worst professor I have ever had. Penn State do better.
