If I learned anything from Ron, it is that I inspire to be nothing like him. DO NOT TAKE HIM.

Stay far away. Extremely condescending and rude. Belittles students publicly to the point of embarrassment. He should not be allowed to be a professor, considering the way that he treats students. Constantly talking down to students, which makes them afraid to ask or answer questions in the first place, because they know he will treat them horribly

Even when we did word for word what he told us to do, we were heavily penalized & ridiculed to the point of tears. No directions were clear and we were talked down to constantly. I genuinely have never felt as angry, frustrated and disrespected as I did in this class. The worst part is it felt like he genuinely did not want us to succeed. STAY AWAY

Seriously do not take this class. If you are one of the people who reads these and thinks, "Eh... Whatever, I should be fine!" Nope. No one ever knew what was going on in this class. Ron is not a good professor and actually gets angry when students are confused or ask questions. Wait until another prof is available. Just do not take. Sorry Ron.

I've never taken a comm class but my roommate complains about it every day, I feel like I'm in the class. He gives no feedback, yet will give the class failing grades. Doesn't give clear instructions and when asked to be more specific he MAKES FUN OF YOU. Unprofessional. Mean man and terrible teacher. Does not want students to succeed. Do not take.
Professor Ron is kind and knowledgable. He gave everyone good suggestions to improve on the projects. But he is very strict on your work so you won't receive high grades on your assignments.

He's an okay guy, but instructions on projects are extremely unclear and messy. reviews.comment: easily the worst teacher I have ever had including high school and my entire life. Tells you to do one thing, you do it and then says its wrong. Doesn't deserve the title of being a professor. If you have him, switch ASAP.

reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The worst class I have ever taken at Penn State. Please save yourself never take his class!

reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

Ron is awesome! I am currently taking his comm421w class (on Monday and Wednesday only- so it is kind of long, but he always gives a break after an hour and makes it interesting so it doesn't feel like it drags on). reviews.comment: Literally worst class experience I've had at Penn State. Class itself seems fun but Ron makes it positively awful. All group work (&no opp. for peer review), and an obscene amount of work for 3 credit class in between classes + 4 hrs of class/week. Little to no positive feedback which gets very discouraging. "Unfortunately" is his favorite word.

He was the worst. We had to do many group projects in a very short period of time and he hated all of our ideas. Terrible teacher. Gives vague instructions but expects a very specific result and if you don't give him exactly that then you're wrong. Condescending, rude, and inconsiderate on top of being an awful teacher. Not constructive in his criticism at all. Tons of projects and seems to assume that his is the only class we have to do work for.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Took Ron for a one credit seminar on Photoshop and InDesign overall he seemed chill, but the homework assignments were tough and assumed you knew more than you did. I felt I could have learned more in this class if Ron gave more instruction and he can be kind of harsh sometimes.

Really slow-paced class; he takes longer to teach something than he should (very repetitive). Is never clear on what he wants the 1st time you have to do an assignment, so he'll make you edit it over and over while adding more criteria each time instead of doing that all in the beginning. His attitude is condescending & rude.

Lectures are long and repetitive. Classes seem to go on forever.  Some of the projects seem silly.  You have a lot of projects to do. He will help you if you need it.  He is EXTREMELY specific and can never be wrong.

Really helpful class to prepare you for a career. Expect a good deal of feedback on projects and don't get offended.  There are a lot of fun projects in this class, the instruction is just very unclear. Ask for help. I found it helpful to ask random students in the library for feedback(this keeps it unbiased). Lots of writing, get a Google drive!

He is so rude and he has no patient towards his students. He goes through all of the steps in the softwares in class very fast and doesn't repeat himself when you ask him to. All he does is talk about ad club and on top of that he expects you to do all of the work he didn't give at the beginning of the semester to do it at the end in one day!!
Ron is a great guy and super creative! Take him if you want a career with the creative side of advertising. Yeah class isn't easy but he is preparing you for the real world.

This class was really hard because it pushes you in a way that you never are in classes. There are 7 projects crammed into a semester, and he expects a lot. If you go talk to him or show you are struggling, he will help. He isn't a bad guy, he just wants to make the class as real life as possible. If you have time for group projects, take the class

he really isn't a terrible teacher.. i really liked him. i participated in class and did the projects to the best of my ability and i had no trouble getting an A. if you're creative and show him that you care you should be fine in this class.

This guy is awful! rude and inconsiderate. condescending and not understanding of students. Please listen to me Penn Staters, I'm trying to look out for you. Do not take this professor if you can avoid him. I could go on for hours but I am fuming as a think about him. I find this man hard to have any respect for.

This guy is awful! inconsiderate and rude. condescending and not understanding of students. Please listen to me Penn Staters, I am looking out for you. Do not take his class if you can avoid it. I could go on for hours about this guy but I am fuming as I think about him.

To everyone who is thinking about taking this class: DONT. I am dead serious, this guy is boring, doesn't know how to teach and plays favorites. If you belong on his favorite list then you get an A if not you get a B or whatever. Do NOT take this class with him unless you absolutely have to. HE IS NOT YOUR TYPICAL COOL FUN COMMS PROFESSOR.

Difficult course. Not an easy grader, but you do get several chances to improve projects before final gradings. Ron is very vague during critiques, but I recommend listening to his advice if you want to get a good grade. Very very egotistical. He does curve grading, so all in all you should be able to get an A or B if you put in the effort

Very tough course.  Many projects to do crammed into one semester.  Like other people have said, it's basically the experience of working at an Advertising firm.  Except for the fact that those people have that as their only job and we have 4+ other classes and a job to do around it.  Valuable experience gained, but very stressful course.

Ron's class will make you crazy,and its very frustrating, but his high expectations are a GOOD thing because you're forced to go above and beyond. I hated it at the time, but when I compared my work to that of Ken's students, it was better in nearly every way. The class is hard but that's how it is on the job for creative.

Ron is an extremely unpredictable grader and in my opinion is very egotistical because of his previous work experience.  I can hardly stand to sit through his lectures.  Wish I would have signed up for this course with another professor.  He doesn't realize that not all Ad majors want to be creatives and that all is students are creatively inclined

He is a very difficult teacher but he is a VERY VERY good teacher.  He makes you think outside the box, and take your ideas to a whole new level.  Don't listen to these people they are probably just bitter they suck at advertising and him giving them a bad grade was his nice way of telling them they should switch majors.

Terrible teacher. Lectures are boring, repetitive and uninformative. He does not allow individual creativity in projects, but pushes his ideas on you. Suck up or join Ad Club and you'll get a better grade.

Ron is a nice guy but his grading is VERY critical, he took off a point on a project because my storyboard wasn't glued exactly in the lines! Join Ad Club, he may like you better. But he knows his stuff just not very good at giving direction in what he wants on projects...If possible take Ken.

Ron made us spend too much time drawing in a notebook instead of teaching us InDesign and Photoshop, which is what we really should be learing. He made us waste money on expensive supplies, and I hated how he assigned projects, and then before the first assign. was due, we had to start working on another. It was ridiculous.

I don't agree with the other comments. He is not a tough grader. I've never gotten below an 88% on anything in his class. He takes time out of his weekend to be in the lab to meet with students and offer extra help which most profs would never do. I enjoy his class a lot and he gives you out of class oppurtunities to work on ads for your portfolio

ron is very narrowminded with his view of what is creative advertising. the class would be very fun, however his grading is very unpredictable and he does not give much useful help. i think he just makes up grades. p.s. do not buy the text book or half the supplies he tells you that you will need for this course, you will never use them
HATED HIM AS A PROF.!!!!!!!!!!! NEVER TAKE RON. HE IS UNCLEAR AND DOESN'T ALLOW YOU 2 BE CREATIVE! DON'T WASTE YOUR TIME!

He's the worst teacher I have had at penn state.  He's so unorganized and spends half the class getting his stuff together.  He gives you instructions and changes his mind many times and punishes you for not understanding.  He forces his bad ideas on you when you should be allowed to be creative since it is a creative class. NEVER TAKE HIS CLASS!

I've never had such a bad teacher in my entire life.  He is really unhelpful and uncreative.  If he doesn't like your creative ideas, you have to act like you like his, and then use his ideas... which SUCK.  This man should not be considered an educator.  If you are thinking about taking this class with him, DON'T.

ron is a terrible instructor.  he does not explain himself and expects students to simply know what he is talking about.  421w is a creative course, but he does not allow you to actually be creative.  he wants your ideas to be his ideas, and the only way to get a good grade is to use his ideas and not your own.
No Comments

I learned a lot from this class and it gave me great insight into the major. The professor is very caring, kind, and always willing to help students. Class lecture is very heavy. Her lectures and PowerPoints have a tone of information each class so you need to take notes. Doesn't answer her emails. Class is made up of 4 exams and 2 papers. Doesn't like you if you don't participate
reads straight off slides - boring and hard to focus

This class is very informative and very lecture heavy, be prepared to take notes. There are a few assignments and papers along with TopHat questions randomly. Because of this, I would say attendance matters!! They will affect your grade. 
Overall, I really enjoyed this class!

Dr. Madhavan was a great professor; her class is an easy 100-level class for those who choose to study. It is majority memorization, but the tests are very straightforward. Going to class matters. Nobody tells you this, but the tophat questions during class affect your grade and are based on accuracy.

This class is very informative and very lecture heavy. You will literally be writing for the entire class, my hand would be burning after class. Definitely have the slides open next to you while in class. She uses a lot of videos to help you better understand the content, which was nice. All the exams including final are online and multiple choice.

This class is so lecture-heavy. Be prepared to sit in class for an hour and 20 minutes and listen to lectures the entire time. Also, she goes so fast so make sure you either take notes before or have the PowerPoint up next to you. She was very kind and did a lot of participation in class so make sure to go.

Professor Madhavan was a pretty good professor, but she often was inaccessible outside of class or was not able to answer certain questions, handing them off to the TAs. Her lectures practically came directly from the powerpoints, which got boring, but overall I felt like I learned a lot from her class, and it was a good introductory class for CSD.

reviews.comment: class can be pretty boring but tests are so straightforward (online tests and every question comes straight from the powerpoints). i thought it was an easy a but also didnt try to fully learn the material, there was also not much homework. shes a nice professor, i would recommend

Dr. Madhavan is a very nice professor. She is a good teacher and uses homework to really help you apply the lectures. However, there is a lot of content in the lectures slides, so make sure to study before exams.

reviews.comment: Dr. Madhavan is so sweet and caring! She is very knowledgeable on what she is teaching and cares very much about her students. She is kind and will help you with anything you need! As long as you study her slides she gives out you will be fine!

she can be hard to reach outside of class. However the exams are very straight forward and all the answers can be found in the notes. She goes really fast through the notes powerpoint so make sure you take notes before class and fill in blanks during class.

study a lot to do well on the exams. class is pretty boring but you watch videos that support the information on the powerpoints which helped me internalize the info, clicker questions for attendance, do all the extra credit she gives you, hw isn't hard and a good grade booster. final isn't cumulative but found it to be harder than the other exams

Her study guides are useless because they are so vague and she takes forever to grade exams and papers. Go to class to get clicker points even though it is mad boring.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I'm a junior but I could see first year students struggling with the past pace and her inability to elaborate. She also takes forever to respond to emails and grade papers. We took a scantron exam once and she took two weeks to grade it. This class isn't bad but she's not the greatest professor.

She's very lecture heavy, and goes to power points way too fast. You have to go to class because there are clicker questions. She's not good at answering questions and explaining things. A lot of her examples are the same things over and over again. She doesn't grade things in a timely fashion. Don't take her unless you really like lectures.

Reads directly off the powerpoint. Goes thorough material super fast and expects you to know so much information for the tests. Lectures are very boring, but make sure you go to class to get your clicker points.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She's a very nice person. However, she does tend to give a lot of lectures, which are varying in levels of engagement. She does clicker questions in my class I have with her, so you have to be in class. Beware, she goes through her powerpoints at the speed of light, but they are online. Her tests are fairly easy.

Prof. P really knows his stuff, and I enjoy his lectures. My only gripe is the homework, the assignments get pretty dull since they mostly have you clicking through different websites to answer questions. I think turning some of those writing tasks into weekly Canvas quizzes would make the workload way less repetitive.

Took PSYCH481. As a person, Dr. Pincus is incredible. He's knowledgable, funny, and caring. His lectures are dry but if you do the bare minimum and pay attention you will get an A. He is also a therapist and applies a lot of his own experiences to the course content, and a lot of his stories are very interesting.

Took 481 not 490. Boring. Reads directly from the posted slides with little elaboration. Little to no class discussion/activities/interaction. Exams are overly specific on details that don't matter much making studying difficult. Lowest exam averages of any psych class I have taken at PSU in my four years. Easy weekly assignments.

Probably one of the most interesting psych courses out there, especially if you plan on becoming a therapist. You don't have to do any readings (even though he says to) because he goes over everything you need to know. Grades consist of a few in class activities and 5 short quizzes. They're open ended but really straightforward.

Professor Pincus is a great professor with a lot of experience and can relate everything discussed in class to real world application. The material is not easy but extremely interesting and if you ask for help he will be happy and enthusiastic about giving it. Great professor would recommend the class to anyone.

Dr. Pinus is an awesome teacher and a cool guy.  He bases the class on his great deal of experience in the field of personality disorder therapy.  The class is all hands-on and application-based.  We had papers and assignments but no exams. It's a great choice for a psych seminar class!

Great class. Dr. Pincus knows what he is talking about and presents the information in a exciting and interesting way. Watch a lot of unique movies and read books about mental illnesses. Easy A if you work well with your group.

This class was my favorite class last semester. It is interesting and Aaron introduces and teaches the material in a interesting and engageing manner.  learning is done through discussion. The only annoying part is web participation. Don't forget to post several (at least 4) good post for each unit and you'll do fine. I highly recommend this class!

This class was my favorite of the semester.  If you want a really interesting seminar class take this one. Pincus really knows what he is talking about and has interesting stories to tell. He is a really cool guy and I learned a lot from this class.  We read several interesting books having to do with mental disorders and I liked most of them

This class is awful. It's all Freudian and Psychoanalytic. I don't know one person who likes this class. It's my biggest regret that I took it. The lectures are boring. The tests are difficult. He assigns 10 papers that are due on test days. No extra credit. One of the worst classes I've ever taken.
SUCH a good teacher. I absolutely loved going to class because it was so interesting and relaxed. Everyone else hated their first year seminar and mine was my fav. class!
Nice guy, easy class
Easy class.. and it's really interesting. Pincus really knows what he's talking about.
cool guy, nice class... fun.

Pretentious man. I asked for clarification on one thing halfway through the semester, and he had a problem with me the rest of the semester. Additionally, he is incompetent when it comes to using Canvas. He put in our Canvas attendance, making them artificially increase grades. He didn't realize this until the last week of classes, grade dropped 6%

Okay. Look, he's a nice guy, but he grades atrociously. He's a bit awkward in class, which is fine, but often class wouls come to a standstill. It's reading heavy, lots of very obscure books, but it fit the class. I wouldn't take it again because he was too harsh of a grader. Especially for the smallest assignemnts literallly worth 5 points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Did more reading for this class then some of my 400 level ENG classes. Despite doing well on most assignments he would make a note to disagree with my perspectives without any helpful feedback or commentary. Because of this i did not feel comfortable participating which docked my grade from an A to an A-. Would never recommend this prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He's a really nice guy but his class is so boring. No one pays attention but you don't really need to because the material is self explanatory. He is also an extremely tough grader and you are only graded on 6 things.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Montalvo cares about his students and gets to know our names while passionately lecturing and giving valuable feedback. He is a good person who is exited to educate effectively! (I am in his ENG202D class)
If Aaron would communicate more on why he grades the way he does maybe the class would be better. A one sentence answer is a big joke coming from someone who calls themself an English professor.

Professor Montalvo was okay as a professor. I was a bit concerned about the reviews but if you put in effort and show you care, he will care too. My biggest problem was that he was a bit pretentious about things, but it can be easily overlooked as well
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Almost did not take Prof. Montalvo due to previous reviews but so glad I did! Learned so much! He is very organized (everything is on Canvas: detailed assignments, class PPPs, work samples) and he truly cares. Plenty of time for assignments, detailed and encouraging feedback. You have to put in a strong effort but expectations are reasonable.

Professor Montalvo really made an effort to make this boring class interesting and engaging. He always made an effort to be there for his students which showed he cared. I realize this isn't exactly his area of expertise as he is a PhD student but I enjoyed having him in this class.

Aaron had expectations so high that the average grade for every assignment was 75% or below. I had to ask him to regrade one of my papers because I believed that it was harsh and he agreed he was grading unfair. No student should have to correct a professors grading. Avoid taking him if you can. I took AP English in high school and this was harder

I took Montalvo's class as a freshman. He is a very nice person, but I strongly recommend avoiding his class. I took AP English classes in high school and got A+'s on nearly every essay I ever wrote. When I took his class, I didn't score over a C on any of the major projects. I have concluded that it's impossible to meet his expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The format of the class can be somewhat hectic, lots of reading assigned on similar dates if not the exact date writing assignments are due. The grading scale is kind of ambiguous considering, you never really know why you received the grade you did. It is incredibly difficult to earn an A. However, Aaron is a good guy; I wish him the best.
Seems like a good guy, but grades things very harshly.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Literally the worst English teacher you can have at Penn State. DO NOT TAKE HIM. Super boring so it is hard to participate and he grades SO harshly. Was always a very strong writer in high school, finishing with As in AP English classes and I am struggling to get by with a C in his class.

You can never do anything right. Did not learn much in this class. Super boring. Again did not learn anything. Super hard grader. I have talked to multiple people in my class and they all say the same thing. He said in the beginning of the semester that he will not tell you why you received the grade you did. So there is no way to improve.
Extremely hard grader. No matter how much time you put in still get low grades. Has no specific grading rubric. Hardest english class I've been in.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Boring lectures, never learn anything, not clear on what he wants in papers. It is way past the middle of the semester and I still have an N/A for my grade. Posts things on Canvas a day before they are due. Choose literally any other professor but this one.

He's very nice but he gets sidetracked easily and yaps a lot about random topics that have nothing to do with the class. The textbook is "mandatory" but you don't really need it except for a quiz or two. He is very good at giving feedback and extensions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Furgiuele is the best ENGL 15 professor you could take. His assignments are straightforward and the instructions are always clear. He is more than helpful if you need to reach out to him via email or during office hours. For essays, he explains why you got the grade you did and gives exceptional feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He actually explains why you got the grade you got.  He does take attendance and he doesn't like phones.  Sometimes he has everyone close their laptops and wants everyone to talk and give their opinion on what ever the topic is.  But he never puts anyone down for what they say.He always makes you feel comfortable even if you don't know the answers.
The best professor I have ever had at UP. Bro was so chill and always understanding. If you ever take ESL15, take it with my man right here.

You will regret your decision if you do not take Aaron as your ESL15 lecturer. He is such a nice and lovely guy, and he always accept everyone's opinion. I would take him again if I have a chance. He once brought doughnuts and drinks for his students. I really admire him.

Professor Ahern is very nice, and I like him as a person. In terms of the class, it's important to show up. He's very forgiving of an absence if you email him ahead of time. He does love to talk, and it's always a journey following him to the point of his sentence, as he's a little long-winded, but the overall course is simple and easy.

He is a very caring professor who wants his students to succeed. The labs are beneficial because you are doing real world stuff that you need to know. Even though the points are low for attendance, go to class because they really do add up in the end.

Very easy class but lectures tend to drag on. Only half of the class would show up and it felt like he was talking to himself since he just reads off slides. Attendance isn't mandatory and just turns into extra credit. 2 exams that are fairly easy and most comes from slides that are posted. Little hw and it doesn't take long.

Prof Ahern is so kind and one of those prof's who works on brownie points-- go to him after he releases exam grades and he'll give you points back, in other words show him that you care about the class and want to do well and he will reward you for that... He's down to earth, chill and wants you to succeed. Just go to lab and class and try
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is so boring, this guy just reads off his slides and he posts them online so there's no point in paying attention but you have to go to clickers. His exams are really easy and he gives a lot of extra credit, but I literally did not learn one thing in this class. Only 3 exams and clickers, no homework but wish I didn't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This is the most boring class I have ever taken in my entire life. He reads directly from the slides and takes attendance based on clicker questions. He shows SO MUCH MAD MEN and does nothing to make this basic common sense material more interesting. Class is solely based on tests, clicker questions, and extra credit.

Stanley Tucci could be this guys twin. Awesome professor, he is extremely understanding and he just wants his students to do well. His love for advertising is so cute! Definitely recommend taking a class with Professor Ahern. Easy A as long as you put in effort and study for the exams.

You really only come to class for clicker points; otherwise, he posts his slides on CANVAS. His lectures are dry and tries to make it interesting with watching clips from Mad Men. As long as you study (1 hour a day 3-4 days before the exam), his tests are relatively straight forward. He also offers a good amount of extra credit.

This was a required class for my major and it was the worst class I've had to take so far. The lectures are him reading straight from PowerPoints which are uploaded online, but he uses clickers to force you into coming to an 8am lecture. The exams are extremely difficult (MC & short answer) and there is no textbook to study from.

Lee was a great professor who really understood the schedules of students and catered his presentations to what he felt would benefit us in our future careers. Lectures were interesting and exams were not hard if you came to class and knew how to do basic algebra. Learned a lot and made me more interested in this area of advertising.

This is a teach yourself class. It is so easy on a weekly basis: chapter reading and 2 posts comments that he will never read. Tests are hard and some have more math (yes, I said math) problems than relevant material; better be good at memorizing chapters and lesson notes because there is no guidance on test content. Horrible excuse for a class.
Class is dry but the exams are easy. There are not many points so complete all extra credit. He also considers an A as a 95%... annoying. Easy to get all clicker points.

What could have been a fascinating class was fairly dry with no discussion; the course consists of Dr. Ahern reading from his slides at a lightning pace. Very difficult to keep up. Class average on all three tests was around 30/40. Course is just too much info to cram without much peripheral activity, except for video examples.
Easy, interesting class. Need to attend class to get clicker points but you can miss a few. Tons of extra credit opportunities. Nice professor. I enjoyed it.
Overall easy class, but professor is useless and doesn't help at all.  He's very passionate but appears fairly ditzy

I took his comm-seminar class this past semester. He was a GREAT teacher! The only homework he assigned were blogs which were fun to write about and really easy to do. I loved going to his class even though it was at 9am every Monday, Wednesday and Friday. He's really a cool guy! If you're a comm or in DUS major...take this seminar!!

He is a nice guy, but his class a bit dry. You don't have to buy textbook, just study lecture slides for exams. Only 3 exams including final, and clicker points. He gives extra credit work. An easy A class.

BEST PROFESSOR EVER! Always there to help you, material is sometimes boring, but he tries his best to help you understand it. I would def. take a class with him again. A lot of comm professors are not the best at PSU, but I would recommend this man to anyone!
Really interesting guy, very chill. Lectures can be dry, but he knows his stuff a lot better than most -- definitely star professor material.
Dr. Ahern is awesome! He's extremely nice and tries to make class engaging and fun. I would definitely take another class with him!

He's a good teacher. Sometimes class can get a little slow sometimes but he has a lot of videos that relate to the material. The only grades is 3 tests and 4 quizzes. So while you cant really miss many points he offers a ton of bonus. I wasn't very interested in advertising and rarely went to class but still pulled an A-. I'd recommend Lee

I thought Ahern was boring, I can tell he really loves advertising but maybe because I wasn't interested, I did not enjoy the class. The tests are also kind of hard, he sometimes words questions in a weird way.

Such a nice guy! His class was interesting and he always had review games and review classes for tests. He gives you study guides and uploads powerpoint slides. If you need to take this class take it with him! He's awesome and would usually let us out early a lot. He also gives a lot of extra credit so take advantage of it!

This class is very easy but very boring.  Ahern is a very nice guy but his lectures are very dry.  You don't need a book and if you go to class and fill in the blanks on his powerpoints then you'll do fine.  In my opinion the class  wasn't the best for an intro course.

The class is very easy, the only reason to come to class is because he leaves blanks in his ANGEL notes you have to fill in. He reads off the notes and sometimes rambles about things not on the notes. The class is boring but exams are easy.

Very easy class! Prof ahern is so nice, even though he posted the powerpoints online I still tried to go to class simply because he is a good teacher. You can tell he wants everyone to do well and he tries to make everyone understand what he is saying. that said- very easy class.. don't buy the book. learn the study guide and you will get an a!

Very easy! Prof Ahern is very nice and tries to make everyone understand. He is very good about answering questions and the tests are incredibly easy even without going to class every day. Powerpoints are posted online, and as long as you know the study guide you will get an a on the exam. Very good, easy class!
Great great great professor! this class is easiler than what i thought, no hw, exam questions come straight from his ppt, which is always on angel! super easy class

Literally the worst professor I've ever had. Is always late to class, doesn't teach anything. Spent 30 minutes explaining how to drop the zero in calculations for an intro to advertising class. Never responds to emails, was late to my final exam. Is a bad person and a bad teacher. I would recommend staying as far away as possible from this joke.

He's a good professor, knowledgeable in his material and he tries to keep the class interested by showing us clips from commercials, advertisements, etc. He provides a lot of examples, which is good. Attendance doesn't matter.Grades based on 3 exams only but he gives out extra credit.highly recommended& easy class!

Dr. Ahern is such a nice man. Not many people showed up to class, but I still think it was worth it to go. He knew what he was talking about and he was a teacher that actually cared about his students.
just go and get the nittny notes!!!! just study before each exam its gonna be an A!!!!!!!!!

Prof Ahern knew what he was talking about! And you could see his excitement in class, he always wants to teach you how things work out in the world, not just what the book says.  Not to mention, he showed quite a few movies.  Even if you don't like to attend class (which I recommend you do) make a friend - he'll give pop extra credit
Amazing guy who really cares about his students. No need to go to lectures and the tests are easy if you study the slides. Don't buy the book. Easy A!

Loves Mad Men but can't teach advertising.  You don't have to attend the boriing lectures bc all the slides are on Angel.  Exams are kind of tough but he gives loads of extra credit.  Don't buy the overly priced book.
good teacher, attendance is not mandatory. I missed class for 2 weeks in a row right before finals and got an A on the final by just going over the slides and the book.
This class was so easy.  He gives tons of extra credit and 4 quizzes on angel to boost your grade.  There's a study guide for every test that is exactly what the test is.  Easy, easy A!

Didnt open my text book once, he posts the slides online even though they arent clear. you dont have to go to class unless you look for the occasional extra credit. he gives you a study guide before every tests with literally everything on it- easy A
this professor is extremely boring. Go to the classes if you want extra credit. There is no need to by the textbook he doesn't use it.
Shez cool! Very clear course & very interactive classes.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Teaches good. Very clear & nice. Enjoyed the class.

She is very polite and explains things so everyone in class can understand. Also very responsive to questions & always listens to problems and finds ways to make the theory course more fun and engaging.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: easy art gen ed consisting of 3 exams, weekly discussions, reading activities, quizzes, and very long lecture videos. she communicates a lot and is understanding and easy to talk to. recommend staying on top of the videos bc they are time consuming. photos are pretty
Take advantage of the extra credit. The class isn't hard just a lot of lectures to watch.
Very understanding and you can reach out to her if you are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Online arch class for gen ed. Open book open note. some questions on exams are weird but u can find them (in ur online notes).
Chem is a hard class but he makes it tolerable.

He is the best professor I have ever had. So sweet and makes class so enjoyable. Literally look forward to his class every day. 112B is said to be "harder" than regular 112, but he makes it very bearable and gives extra credit. He even tries to learn everyone's name in a 300-person lecture, which is so sweet. TAKE HIS CLASS.

Used his office hours and sat up front, which helped a lot. The class is naturally hard, so an A takes real work, but he's the professor you want: very nice, supportive, and gives tons of practice exams that mostly match the tests. Exam 3 deviated a lot from the practice set, but he curved to account for it. Clear explanations and willing to help.

Dr. Garner teaches well and the class is organized. I struggled with chemistry before, so it felt difficult, but looking back I could've done better with more consistent effort. There's a decent amount of extra credit available (around 5%), and the grading felt fair overall. Hard class, but doable.
Dr. Garner is so nice and really wants everyone to succeed. Choose him and good luck!

Professor Garner cared about every single person in the huge lecture hall. He made an attempt to memorize everyone's name. The class itself is moderately challenging, with three exams and a case study that brought up grades. There is lots of extra credit that makes this class super manageable.

Dr. Garner is the best professor I have been In a class with. His class is difficult, and it is very easy to fail, but he is so good at his job it would be an insult to him if you do. He gives a lot of extra credit, drops your lowest test grade, and gives you multiple opportunities to get your grade back up. He also makes sure you learn.

I loved Dr. Garner. This class is very hard in general but he made these hard topics really easy to understand. He gives lots of extra credit and the case study is free points. He is very nice and tried to learn almost everyones name in a 300 person lecture. If you are taking the 110b version take it with him you will not regret it.

super nice and funny teacher. his lectures were all great and decently interesting given it was a lecture. id say he was the best of the teachers in chem 110. his canvas is beautifully made and insanely organized. overall, he's a super good teacher and nice person. he made an effort to to try to learn everyone's name in a 300 person lecture

Super genuine and caring professer. He goes through the effort of learning the names of almost everyone in his several 300 person lecture halls. goes in depth on the slides and does a good job of explaining the depth. class is hard but has a TON of resources to do well. Case study is a free 100%. 15ish hours of studying per exam, but got 90%+ per

Wonderful professor and human. Literally went out of my way to make sure I had him for 112B. He's really smart and clearly wants you to succeed. His office hours are very valuable and he has a great instructional team. Simplifies what is still a really tough course!

Dr. Garner is probably one of the best chemistry professors you'll find here at Penn State. Despite the large class size, he is very quick with responding to emails and will take his time with his students. He provides so many resources. As a person who struggles with chemistry, this is the best I've done in a chemistry course. If you can, get him!
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: This class was very difficult just in general but Dr. Garner may be the best professor I've ever had. Such an amazing guy who cares a lot about everyone and actually learns students names in a 300 person lecture which says a lot. Great teaching style and easy to understand. Good resources in the class but chem 112 is just hard.

Way too reliant on tophat for the lectures.  He does not explain the content of the lecture very much, he just briefly glazes over it and immediately starts giving tophat questions all class long. Otherwise, a nice and approachable guy.

He is a very nice person and his lectures are not boring. However, I don't think he helps you prepare enough for the final exam. The content he taught leading up to the final exam wasn't enough to prepare students for the difficulty. I believe that the course was hard within itself, but you can find other professors who teach the material better.

The Lectures contain all the information you need to succeed and Garner explains the content at its most fundamental level and does not over complicate anything. He provides lots of opportunities to study and to complete extra credit. Take advantage of everything and you will do great.

I took his class this past semester and I can easily say he is one of the best professors I have had. He provides lots of resources and in the times I have emailed him or spoke with him he has been very kind and helpful. Chem 110B is somewhat of a hard class and he made it a little easier by being a great professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Garner is a wonderful professor, he explains concepts extremely well and it is evident he cares about his students. The class is extremely hard by nature and he understands this which is why he offers so much extra credit (5% in total I think). If you are struggling definitely attend his office hours, it will help. I would 100% him again.

Chem is hard but somehow Dr. Garner manages to teach the material in such a way that it becomes second nature for the exams. Very caring and memorized everyones names in an entire lecture hall. Gives tons of materials for tests and makes sure you are prepared. If tou are taking Chem 110B you would be making a mistake to not take it with Dr. Garner.

Chem is hard but taking it with garner is the easiest. He explains things so well, is so smart that he takes time to memorize everyone's names, and the TA/LAs are really helpful. You're given past exams to study for the midterms as well so if you actually try you shouldn't have a problem getting an A

Garner is such a great professor with interesting lectures and not too much homework. Chem is hard but I feel I didn't do as awful as I could've thanks to Garner. He cares about his students (memorized almost everyone's names in the 350 person lecture hall) and is always willing to help outside of class time as well.

Professor Garner makes a complex course manageable with his clear explanations and helpful office hours. While the class is challenging, the case study and support from TAs like Alexa make it doable. unstuck ai was a great study aid alongside the textbook.

To this day Dr. Garner is one of the best professors I have ever had. He manages to teach complex topics without being verbose and adds humor into his lectures at just the right times. This class is difficult, but if you pay attention and come to lecture, Dr. Garner will make sure you succeed. I highly, highly recommend you take his class.
Clear and rewarding lectures, always gets through the lecture slides, enjoys what he does, explains course material in an understandable way, tells you everything you need to know for the exams.

My favorite professor of all time - my second semester with Aaron (AKA Ronald). I could not recommend someone more for such a difficult course. He made Chemistry SO easy and understandable, and Piazza is the most amazing forum. Take 110B/112B regardless of your major because it is worth it! Best TAs and always responded to questions within minutes.

Garner is such a great chemistry professor. I wish I had taken him for Chem 110B as well because he is amazing at simplifying topics for his students and makes such an effort to get to know every single student he teaches. I would highly recommend taking him for this course.

I would literally DIE for this man. No exaggeration. He is such a sweet, understanding man. He is also really good at teaching the material. He is my FAVORITE professor ever. His class times are usually later in the day (3:35), but it is so worth it. PLEASE take his class if you need to take CHEM 110 and CHEM 112.

Garner is amazing, he really cares about his students learning the material. He will break everything down step by step if you need it. Definitely go to his office hours. The week of test he always extends his office hours unlike most professors! The class chem 110B and 112B (he teaches both) are hard but taking it with him is worth it!

I had Dr. Garner in my first semester at Penn State, and I do not believe any other professor will best him in quality, care, and resources. There is something special about a professor that takes the time to learn everybody's name in a 350 person lecture hall. The case study takes grading weight off the exams, so 110B is more forgiving than 110.

Do not choose 112B if you are not a chemistry genius. Dr. Garner's classes are great, but the exams are very difficult, and the difficulty of the official exams has nothing to do with the difficulty of the PRACTICE exams!

Chem 110 is a hard class, but 110B is even harder. Dr. Garner is very smart, almost too smart. He used to teach at Harvard if that tells you anything. He seems nice at first, but at the end of the class it was getting difficult for me,  and he was reluctant to help me in office hours. I ended up with a D when I could have had a C if I had help.

Professor Garner (Ronald in the course catalog) is the best teacher I've ever had. He has a special gift in making difficult course concepts very easily understandable in his amazing lectures. With Garner as opposed to my friends with other professors, I had significantly less assigned work but greater comprehension. Exams matched practice tests.

Outstanding lectures! It is almost like he is predicting what questions students might have and answers them before they are even asked. His team of TAs and LAs is also awesome. Both him and the group of TAs and LAs clearly care whether you learn. You will have to put in the work, but it is not anything crazy. Alexa Budman as a TA is also awesome!

GREAT PROFESSOR CANNOT RECOMMEND HIM ENOUGH! CHEM 110B can be a tough course, but Dr. Garner made it much more bearable. Seriously the best, so easy to talk to and never makes students feel like they're dumb. Very approachable and caring professor, I loved this class and plan to take him as much as possible with Chemistry sources.

The class itself is difficult, so there is not much room for diff between profs. Garner however is super caring and learns everyone's names. He also is the best at explaining concepts from what I've seen. Although the class is hard, if you make an effort you should get an A. I got 104% and I'm pretty dumb.

Doesn't overwhelm or pressure student for studying.
You will not do or study anything in the recitation, but is good for free grade.

The case study at semester end is a difficult to understand if you are not familiar with bio chemistry, so this course is not recommended if you are not familiar with that or have an option for 110 instead of 110B
Lots of recources, Fun proffessor, lots of TAs to help out. Dr. Garner made Chem 110B fun, although it was a challenge.

Already made my schedule to have him for next semester. Chem could be confusing, but he makes the content so much more understandable. Professor Garner is the best chemistry teacher I've had in my life! Definitely take his class if you have the opportunity, it's well worth it

Dr. Garner is amazing and I would take his class if you can. The class is slightly more difficult than normal Chem 110 but he offers a good amount of extra credit to help you out.

Great teacher for intro to chem. Always available to help. Overall a great teacher, easy to understand and a nice guy.

He's the man.

Chem 110 is already an extremely rigorous course for those like me who haven't taken Chemistry since their sophomore year of high school. Professor Garner is very caring and genuine. He reaches out and does his best to get to know his students. You can tell that he truly hopes everyone will succeed in his class!
He is the best professor you can ever have.

Dr. Garner is by far one of my favorites profs at PSU. I previously got a D in Chem 110 with another prof and had to retake it and I ended up getting an A. He makes sure everyone understands to his best ability and tries to learn everyone's name. He genuinely cares and wants you to understand chemistry.

The class is amazing and he does a lot of in-class experiments, especially with the hydrogen ballons. As long as you attend classes and do the Homeworks this course would be an easy A course, also before submitting the quizzes check with prof. Garner, he would gladly help you. Asn, also he gives extra credit on recitation, by doing pre-lecture asse

Dr. Garner was a fantastic chem professor. I had previously taken Chem 110 with another prof and got a D, but taking it with Dr. Garner made the course so much easier to understand and he was always willing to explain things in new ways. reviews.comment: Dr. Garner is so great. He's so nice and so helpful in office hours. He's a great teacher and does what he can to make sure everyone in the room understands before he moves on. He is a little awkward but he's a genius. I would definitely take him again if I could. Highly recommend!

Personally, I found his lecture slides very text heavy which sometimes left me lost and confused! He is a very caring person though and does a lot to help if you reach out to him! His clicker questions are styled very similar to exam questions. Exams are tough (not his fault) and manageable! TA resource room is a gem!

This is a very tough class for only being a 100 level Chemistry. The exams are very very difficult. However, Garner is an awesome professor and does everything he can to prepare you. Every class there are multiple clicker questions so you have to come to get participation points/a better understanding of the material. Hated the class, loved him.

reviews.comment: Dr. Garner is hands down one of the best chemistry professors at Penn State. He truly cares about his students and makes sure to explain everything clearly so that his students understand the material. I recommend printing the lecture slides before class so you can focus more on the material and example/clicker questions.

Aaron Garner is an excellent teacher. I took him for Chem 110 and was disappointed to find I couldn't find him for Chem 112. Every class has at least one clicker question so make sure you show up (they're a small but extremely easy bonus to your grade!). Highly recommend.
great instructor

Dr. Garner is a great teacher. He makes it easy to understand hard topics and is always willing to help during office hours. When he does demos he makes them fun to watch. He will leave clicker polls open and talk about it if the majority doesn't agree on an answer. He is also really smart! Like he went to Harvard and has a PhD so there's that too.
Dr. Garner is an excellent professor that genuinely cares about his students. He's approachable and tries his hardest to make sure that all of his students succeed.
He is great. He obviously cares about each students progress and is always willing to help out.
Literally the best professor at Penn state. she is so caring and wants you to succeed, if you have the opportunity to take her do it!

Arabic can seem insurmountable, but Lameese makes it possible. By far the nicest and most helpful prof I've had at Penn State. I'm scheduling to have her for a third semester. I look forward to her class the most.

The best language teacher I have ever had, very caring and nice to everyone. Class is really easy to keep up with and as long as you put in your work it is impossible to fail. Arabic is a very daunting language to start but with the right teacher it is doable.

Arabic is an extremely hard language and without the right professor I imagine that it would be a rough course to take. Lameese Ahmad was amazing and genuinely cares about all of her students. I would highly recommend that anyone who decides to take Arabic take her; you won't regret it.

reviews.comment: Doc was by far my favorite professor in the entire Hospitality program. He really goes the extra mile with his students, and will do anything to make sure you are successful. With that being said, do not take that for he is a push over. He is very stern and will respect you if you respect him. Do the work, show up to class, you will do well.
He does not explain anything. He is extremely boring. If you don't go to class you will not pass.
As long as you show up and pay attention it is an easy A. He goes over everything that will be on the test and the pop quizzes are very easy points.
good teacher, can help people out if you need any kinds of advice, no matter studies, careers in gaming industry or a recommendation to any gaming field internships

Dr. Ahlgren is an extremely valuable asset to the Hospitality Management major. He is without a doubt one of the top professors in the country in this field of study. He is extremely knowledgeable and I love attending his classes. If you don't go to class, don't bother signing up for his classes. He is very approachable  and an all around great guy
One of his pet peves is not attending class.

He is a really nice guy. The class is easy if you go. He doesn't take attendance but go if you can because he goes over everything you need to know. Get the final project done early and you'll be set.

Dr. Ahlgren is hands down one of the best professors at Penn State. If you have any interest whatsoever in the gaming industry, take the gaming emphasis with him. He teaches HRIM 386, 387, 388, and 336. He is extremely smart, laid back, and willing to help with any situation or coursework. A true asset to the school of hospitality management.
Great guy who makes sure you learn without overdoing anything.

Super nice and fun. IST110 with him was one of the easiest classes I took here. Online textbook with a few sections of reading due a week. And a few group projects on canvas throughout the semester. Attendance was only mandatory for the first half of semester and then he took it away. Understands that this isn't peoples majors and was really nice.
You learn everything on your own which is expected. The content really wasn't enough to self-teach. The labs and the project was not clear.

reviews.comment: Could not have taught us any less. Had to teach ourselves. Any question you have will be referred to students or someone else. Just there to cash a paycheck.

reviews.comment: The group project is labor intensive. However, he is very accessible and will answer all your questions. Also, he provides resources so that students can help each other and work through issues on labs together - This was a nice addition to an online class.

Nice guy doesn't equal a good teacher, even if he's an easy grader. He routinely skipped class and left his TA to teach. Also, he never really taught how to code SQL, he just kinda jumped into it and left a ton of us confused, I learned SQL eventually but it was significantly on my own time. TAKE THIS CLASS ONLINE!

Prof. Aileo is good and responsive. This class is group project heavy so make sure you have a good group or you will run into problems. The Professor will try to help you out if you have a bad group but there is only so much he can do.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: The best professor. The easiest class. Take it

Very easy going and willing to help to make sure you understand the material. Attendance is not mandatory, but it was often useful to go and we got to hear funny life stories before class started. chill guy. if you do the homework you get full credit for it.

(SOC19 is the class I took with Dr. A) Dr. A is a hillarious professor who is energetic and engaging with his students. My only drawback with his teaching is that his rubrics are a little vague, so there is room for error. Attendance was graded with a daily packback poll, but overall the class was very easy. Hes a cool dude

do not take this class. prof a is the strictest grader ever and there is no structure in his class at all. you can go to every class and will still never get a perfect score on anything. we talk about random stuff every time and expected to memorize how he feels about it. do not take!

Easy A class. Attendance is 'mandatory' but he takes it on packback during class so as long as you remember to log in and take the poll, you don't need to be in class. You need a textbook and packback for this class, but honestly, I just bought the packback and have had no issue at all.

Lectures are fun but I ended up not going as you can do attendance online. Quizzes and deep dives are graded as if you have been a sociologist for years. He's a funny guy and lectures are pretty enjoyable. Most of the assignments are pretty easy and straight forward. Attendance is taken through "polls" that you can take online. reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Overall nice guy, but grades unnecessarily hard. The quizzes are impossible to understand. If you want to pass the quizzes, you need to read and pay serious attention in class. Also, Pack Back sucks. That was the worst part of the class. Found the class material to be interesting, but the work to be hard.

Although he is a funny guy, some of these reviews are not up to date. He does now take attendance and it will gravely drop your grade if you miss days. On top of this he gives a lot of homework, weirdly organized quizzes, and is a tough grader. Nice guy overall tho.

Super funny guy, but this class was difficult. LOTS of HW and reading-based material so be prepared. Bonus is there's no final or class on Fridays.

Professor Ahlkvist was an amazing professor overall. His SOC 5 class was entertaining. He uses packback for almost everything, except quizzes. reviews.comment: No class on Fridays. Moderate workload. Easy to get an A if you attend class and read the textbook. Tests were fair and you can ask for feedback. He was very nice and responded to questions quickly.

Professor Ahlkavist provides a learning environment that is engaging and entertaining. His SOC 5 class was fun, interesting and not graded harshly at all. Dr. A is a really tough grader. Attendance isn't mandatory, but there are in class polls in order to obtain attendance grade. There are no classes Friday. Easy class, need to buy textbook and discussion post platform. Funny lectures, no class friday!

TAKE THIS CLASS IF YOU NEED CREDITS!

An easy GenEd for those looking for something in the SOC field. There are weekly quizzes but as long as you take notes on the lectures you'll be fine. Professor Ahlkvist is a tough grader. He does not set clear expectations for research assignments and it makes it difficult to understand exactly what he is looking for. Quiz questions are wordy and confusing.

Professor A talks in circles during his lecture so if you didn't show up to class, your grade would still be fine. There are very minimal assignments and no exams. The only large assignment is the research assignment which you only have to do one if you did good on the first one. I only read the textbook for the packbacks. Don't buy the book!

Took this class thinking itd be interesting because we discuss stuff happening in todays world. Unfortunately, Professor Ahlkvist is talented at making this class depressing. Hes a tough grader wholl never give full points. Dont waste time reading the book and going to lectures! Focus on projects and Weekly Reviews instead.

Whether its one of the weekly packback assignments or one of the three projects that count for your entire grade, expect unclear and drawn out directions that lead you misunderstnding the entire assignment. Professor Ahlkvist will meet you with little empathy when this happens and a long comment on canvas stating its just not enough.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Don't get me wrong, he seems like a nice guy; however, the class is so hard to get an A/B. The grade was partially based off of 4 exams that were 3 open ended questions. Professor Ahlkvist was a great professor. I took his SOC5 class as a gen-ed and I'm glad I chose this course over many others I could have taken. His lectures are engaging and fun. He shows a lot of videos and films to help put his lessons into context in the real world. He's also very funny. I would take this class again.

Ahlkvist is a good guy. My problem was the amount of effort it takes in this gen ed to get an A. We had four quizzes that are all open ended with only three questions. Regardless of reading the rubric he will never give you full points and is a very hard grader. He also treats this class like a writing class and makes content confusing.
no exams and easy assignments. didnt read the textbook once and got an A. Dont have to try too hard in the class except on research projects

Professor Ahlkvist's class taught me absolutely nothing. I did not take away anything meaningful from my semester, except to avoid Voicethread at all costs. Somehow I Manage, By Michael Scott. Somehow I managed to get a B+ in this class even though this dude is a very difficult grader. For one of the group projects the TA looked at our paper and said it was very good, a week later the grade came back and she gave us a 74. I put a ton of work into an individual project and somehow got a 67.

4 projects no exams. Have to go to class to get clicker points and they count for correctness not participation. You also use packback and the textbook but the homework is easy. Lectures the whole class but since there are no exams as long as you answer the clickers right you are fine. Grades a little tough on the projects but easy A otherwise.

This class has no tests, you will have 4-5 projects, some will be with a group. If you just go with it, you can get an A. I never read and still got an A, but it definitely helps to read. If you speak up and participate he will like you a lot. This class can get really boring but overall it's not bad.

The lecture material was interesting and easy to understand, however projects were hard and Dr. Ahlkvist is a tough grader. He also assigns group projects. Most points are clicker points. reviews.comment: SOC5 was awful. Getting an A- in the class was a true effort, and although I did all the homework and went to almost every class I felt like I was fighting an uphill battle. Alhkvist is a great teacher and is super knowledgeable on the topic. He didn't give us any exams and his grading criteria for the Case study sections was super clear.

But beware of the tests they are no joke.

Do NOT take Soc 005 with him. Worst professor I've ever had. His lectures are ridiculous and he doesn't even stay on topic. You get bonus points on the tests by using the clicker, but that won't even help your grade. The tests are weird and mostly based on current articles than the textbook. The class is very awkward and his 'sense of humor'? No.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: This guy sucks so bad he made me want to change my major. The lectures teach you nothing, so you have to read the book if you want to do well on exams. If there is any way for you to take another professor, I highly recommend it.

DO NOT TAKE SOC 005 WITH HIM!! The tests are impossible! You can study all you want from the textbook and notes in class but his questions are ridiculous. His powerpoints are unclear as well and I had no idea what he was talking about during class.

So if your taking Soc 5 because you want an easy A don't take it with Jarl. He's a nice dude and stuff but can be really unclear on certain grading criteria. Also his exams aren't that hard but a lot of questions are based on  examples or obscure current events he touches on in lecture. So even though you dont have to go to lecture, you have to go

Prof Jarl is a really funny guy who keeps lectures somewhat interesting. But the way he grades assignments is quite unclear and inconsistent. I read the whole book for the final and only 1 out of 25 questions were (i feel) sociology related. Got me down 2 grades. Kmn :(

I really liked Professor Ahlkvist. He's pretty funny and has a dry sense of humor so I didn't mind attending class. Only 3 exams, Pinterest posts, and journal entries so it's pretty easy. Reading is important for the exams, but you get extra credit points for every 10 clicker points. It's an easy class if you do the readings and attend the lectures

This class has two components, weekly lectures and one class with a grad student. Most learning will come from your grad student who provides an assignment every other week. The lectures can be boring but there are clicker questions which earn you bonus points on exams. Follow directions & read-- you'll be fine.

Probably the worst professor i have had at Penn State.  I took this class as a gen head and ended up getting a D in the class because of his unclear assignments and grading.  He does not respond to emails and his classes literally suck. Do not take this class

Overall, this class isn't too bad. Response papers are easy, Pinterest assignments weren't horrible, exams are doable. Sitting through his lectures was excruciating at times. If you go to class for clicker points and do the other work, then you should get a B+ at worst. Study the slides and skim the book to do well on exams.
This class is a class you will dread. The TA's really can only help you if you beg them,Grading is not clear neither is this class.

Taking this class was simply a waste of my time. I never attended class because it was pointless when I could just read the textbook and retain the same amount of information. Only attended Friday sections to turn in and receive new assignments. Work on a research proposal all semester. Tough grading, would not advise if you do not have to take.

This class used to be easy but he changed the course. You now have 3 tests, 5 papers, clickers, and a bunch more random stuff. The tests are pretty hard and he gives no exam reviews or study guides. The best way to prepare for this class is to come and listen to his boring lectures and try to get as many clickers as you can.  Also study the ppts.

Took this class as a freshman last year and was super easy. Clicker questions every day in class and that is about 80-85% of your grade I believe. The other percentage is from short, one-page response papers. I went and read a leisure book the whole time and got an easy A.

Took this class to fulfill requirements for my major, not interested in Sociology, and I took it because I heard this was one of the easiest classes at PSU. To get a good grade you will need to come to class and get clicker points, spend time on response papers and do the pinterest assignments. Dumb class in my opinion, lectures are super boring.

Lectures are kind of boring, but he's makes random jokes and plays videos. There's a clicker quiz every few weeks on chapters in the book. You don't have to read, it's all common knowledge. If you show up to class, make an attempt to answer clicker questions, and write the biweekly response papers you'll be fine. There's no tests or a final!

Jarl is a decent professor. His lectures are very long and boring. The unfortunate part is that you MUST attend lectures for iClicker points. If you can get past that however this class is an easy A. There are response papers that are due periodically throughout the semester, but they are very simple and easily graded. Also, NO EXAMS!
Show up do clicker you pass no test no quiz

reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Akiyoshi is a great professor and person in general, but held back by his bosses in the English department. He is very understanding about absences (with good excuse) and that English class is a low priority for many. Assignments get pushed back a lot too. Great professor, would take again!

He was a super cool professor. The issue with the class is that the English department sucks and runs a tight ship. He was always super cool and upbeat even with it being a 9 am class and he pushed deadlines back a lot. I feel like he would be an amazing professor if he didn't have to follow all of the English department's rules.

Clearly its an english class so there are a lot of writing assignment but he is very understanding and offers extensions when needed for students.the one MAJOR issue is that you will NOT know your grade until the semester end. IDK why, also he is very strict on attendence and participation. days missed=letter grade dropped.
Great professor. Very knowledgeable on the material. Entertaining lectures. Reasonable grader. Highly recommend.
I really enjoyed Professor Lakhtakia's class. He is very knowledgeable in his field and goes into great detail while teaching. I would highly recommend taking 400 with him.

My personal opinion is he is a great professor. The course material is ridiculous to begin with and there are times when you have no idea what's going on in the class, but he'll help you out and try to make sure you know the material. Also used an older edition of the text and saved me about $90. often held sessions on weekend to review/do problems

Lakhtakia is in my top 3 professors I've ever had at PSU. His passion and enthusiasm for learning really makes for a great class. His analogies make the beast that is E&M theory a manageable topic. The subject matter is extremely difficult, and there's no way around it. Laktahkia knows this and helps the students through it. 10/10
Oh God... he's teaching ESC 400H in the spring??  I just had him for 407H and there is NO WAY IN HELL I'm taking him again.  *drop*

I absolutely HATE this man! You won't learn anything in this class, you will spend 12 hours+ on homework per week, and you will be on the verge of suicide when you attempt the final. He expects you to be an expert programmer coming into the class because he won't help you at all with that. If you took CMPSC 201, good luck.... you're gonna need it

Not going to be on my list of favorite professors anytime soon.  I know two people already used the word, but it fits him perfectly: ARROGANT.  He thinks he's a god among men, but in fact he's nothing more than a lousy professor.  I liked most ESC professors, but NOT this one.  I would say "stay away," but unfortunately you don't have a choice

So far this class is pretty hard.. much harder than it needs to be.  He doesn't teach very much and yet expects you to know everything.  I agree with the other comment, he is very arrogant.  "God among men" ?? don't make me laugh

Lakhtakia is good-natured and wants his students to learn.  He is also exceedingly arrogant.  He is very nit-picky.  I wouldn't recommend taking a class with him, nor would I recommend against it.  One could have a very good or a very bad time in his class.  In either case it will be a lot of work.

He knows his subject well but he's a bit arrogant...prone to go on tangents in class that dont help in your understanding...the material isnt hard, just his explanations  and the way he solves problems make it seem that way sometimes...as long as you do the homework problems you should be ok...i think he is used to teaching upper level classes.

He knows his subject well but he's a bit arrogant...prone to go on tangents in class that dont really help your understanding at all...if you do the homework you should be ok though...the material isnt hard, just his way of solving problems and his explanations make it seem difficult sometimes...i think he's used to teaching upper level classes.
Akhlesh Lakhtakia is a god among men
Extremely intelligent, yet showed a lot of interest in his students and making sure that they understood even those concepts that were not easily understood.  Excellent professor on all levels.
Take his courses!
Boy, does he love to tell stories! He connects programming with real-life issues.

It's like he's a particularly bad teacher, he's average, it's just he gave so much homework that everyone drowned in that class, that it has soured my opinion of him too much. It seemed like he used mathlab because it was easy, but he didn't understand what it was assigning to us. A lot of homework problems weren't reflective of the classwork.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Lectures were thorough and organized, and he would always ask if the class understood each topic and encouraged questions. He makes himself very accessible after class and for office hours. A lot of homework, but he is flexible with due dates. He also dropped some homework grades depending on how well the class was doing collectively. Great teacher

He's a terrible professor. In class when you ask him a question he's unprepared for, he won't give you a definitive answer. He will go through it partly, and then tell you to finish it yourself. He makes constant mistakes, and is easily confused by his own material. The homework teaches you more than actually attending lectures

Often not clear with his expectations for assignments and then fails to provide useful feedback so that you can improve. Often unclear where and why points were removed from assignments. Most of his feedback is clearly copy pasted that he sends to every single student yet still he takes 6-7 days to grade assignments for a tiny class.
Great professor! Would definitely take this professor again.
Great teacher.

He always gives good feedback and breaks down exactly what he was looking for and if you hit all the points. You are never left wondering why he removed points. He also grades really fairly. Also was very empathetic to a natural disaster in the area even though most student's were affected and gave extra time on homework which was great
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--SO MANY PAPERS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Two books written, over 30 articles published. Heavy hitter for sure. But we all don't aspire to go that far. Some just want to pass the class. Expectations of students are unrealistic. Subject matter is not easy, especially for those with no int'l experience. Tough grader without much empathy. Not pity, empathy!

Its a hard class, his lectures are extremely long and difficult to understand (accent too). He teaches a program called R Studios, and you take more time learning a dead program that nobody uses anymore than actually learning any form of statistics. Every assignment is graded harshly, and the exams are soul-crushing. Good luck.

If you show up to class and actually listen the course is very easy. He does have an accent but its easy to understand. He let us retake every single exam at the end of the semester and is giving us a 20% extra bonus on the final. I was able to learn very easy and get a good grade in this class.
Rude and horrible lecturer

I honestly do not understand all the negative reviews. The professor is a nice guy and his class isn't hard at all if you just attend class and do the readings. Yes, he does have an accent but it's very easy to understand.

Amazing! The course isnt the best but this guy is soo passionate. He is very understanding if you show interest and interact with him. One of the best classes of DS I have taken. TAs are not the best though.

I loved my conversations with him about the course and out of course projects!

His accent isnt that hard to understand in my opinion.

Worst professor I've ever had. Spends most classes ranting about AI instead of teaching and gives pointless AIparticipation quizzes. Three exams worth 35% of your grade plus tons of unfairly graded homework and labs. Constant grading mistakes. When you ask for help, he talks down and yells. Avoid this classit's a complete waste of time and energy.

I've had to email him and his team multiple times throughout the semester to fix inaccurate grades for assignments. Half the time he doesn't respond and the other half I'm left even more confused. Lectures are not helpful at all, since the modules cover everything you need to know, and there is so much work for this class and seems unnecessary.

It is professors like Mahir that make me wonder how he's able to teach here at Penn State, and for this long. Lectures are often rambles about the readings that you've already done, his research project that has us learning from AI (yes, that's right), and so many busy work assignments. Take ANY class with literally anybody else, and save your time
Bro assigned homework on Whiteout Weekend.

Honestly I do not understand all of these negative reviews. Yes, he is cold but the class is structured in a way where you really learn the material and can do well on the exams if you study your homework, labs and in class activities. His accent is bearable and you can understand him, he also gives extra credit on the exams sometimes.
The class was relatively easy if you went to the lectures. His accent isn't as bad as some are saying it is, but the deduction I gave was due to the lucrative amount of busy work we had to do.

the course does take effort and if you don't understand one aspect you will be lost for the rest of the semester. attendance is mandatory on days you have in-class assignments. the exams are a bit different from the labs/hw, however you do get the chance to re-do the exams and the exam redos are similar. hw/labs are tedious and TA are very helpful

Honestly don't understand why Mahir has such a low rating. I was expecting this class to be 10x harder than it actually is. He gives you everything you need in order to be successful, and although he comes off as dry sometimes, you can tell he cares about his students. Small things like asking if anyone has any questions before every class.
It's hard to understand him. Exams were nothing like exam reviews. Terrible.
