i dont attend class, unless I need to for graded in-person assignments. If you did fine in stat 200 you'll be fine for this because I think it's much easier than stat200. The 2 graded assignments are tedious (about 1 hour each), but not too bad. lecture video and powerpoints were what I used to learn the material. prof is chill

Great professor. The coursework for this class can be challenging, but he posts step-for-step videos for each lesson. If you take the time to understand the material and watch the videos, you will do fine. He also allows you to have a cheat sheet with formulas and the code so you don't need to memorize for the exams.
He along with the teaching team is so bad at answering emails. The final is tomorrow and he literally won't answer my emails.

I took this class as a straight A student and it was not easy. The commands used were very specific despite there being different ways of doing the same thing. There is are two tests due every Sunday at 11:59 that take at least 1 hour a piece but thats the only assignments. Then there are 3 Exams and are not very similar to the course work.

WORST. rambly lectures and unreachable. structure of class is awful, unclear on what he expects. easy enough material but god does he suck. TA gave As on group project I did alone (group ignored me) Akgun never answered emails ab it. last week of class Akgun changed grades to Fs bc "TA was wrong/ I never reached out." sent proof but still failed me

If you ask for help on something, don't count on him or the LAs to help you. They're all equally clueless. Participation is key, attendance is mandatory. Bad lecturer, can't give directions in a cohesive, straightforward way. Lots of homework due Sunday nights. Exams are never actually based on the HW, be careful on those.

Nothing in this course is really homework. Attendance is basically mandatory even though he claims it isn't, labs every Thursday have attendance taken. Not the best at giving a lecture; really repetitive and seems like he doesn't know what he's teaching most of the time.

The review sessions he does for Labs are really good, which help completing the homework assignments. I do not like how heavy the exams weigh on the final grade. You can do extremely well on every lab and homework, but majorly screw up your grade due to a bad exam. His unique method blocking script answers is also very easy to screw up in Canvas.

He understands that the material is tough to grasp and makes it very hard to fail. There are 3 exams in total and you get to retake the first 2 and almost all of the homeworks. If you show up to class you will be just fine.

The material is tough but it's consistent with what he says in his online recorded lectures, and the assignments are directly relevant to the content to what you see on his exams. AND at the end of the semester he gave the option to retake any of the first 2 midterms and any of the homework. Lots of opportunity to get a good grade here guys.

Honestly, I don't know why he gets such bad reviews. He is such a great professor and he gives so many opportunities to boost your grade. If you go to class you'll be totally fine, and even if you miss sometimes he posts video lectures. If you work in the class and actually try you'll get at least a B

Professor means well and wants to see his students thrive in class. However, the course material is very hard and he's not the strongest teacher for this course. Take someone else if you can. He records videos of his lectures and has review assignments the week leading up to each exam. Noncumulative exams (3), homeworks and labs every Sunday (10).
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The course material is just hard. This is probably the hardest class you will take in your 4 years here. He's a nice teacher, answers any and every question. The recordings are your lifeline, without them it would be impossible to do labs or projects. PLEASE DO NOT WAIT UNTIL SUNDAY TO START LABS/PROJECTS! You will not finish I am warning you!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor stresses group communication for all projects but does do anything when students don't communicate or contribute to group work and one person is left doing a majority of the work. Sends out information regarding assignments and then changes his mind 2 days later so assignments have to be changed and resubmitted. Do not take him.

His recorded lectures are a lifesaver, he posts videos for every homework and lab on what a 100% looks like. Attendance wasn't mandatory, tests are 40% but with the videos that have good explanation you should be fine. No clue how his rating is low on here I loved this class.

AWFUL - this course wasn't a lot of work at all. What made the course so hard is the fact that the Professor doesn't explain any of the assignments. You must attend class because if you don't you wont be able to do the labs. He also won't respond to your emails either so the confusion continues throughout the semester.

Mahir is a god. The videos he sent out for this class were amazing and sometimes funny. Every time I emailed him, he answered within 24 hrs. Would highly recommend taking SRA365 with him. The class builds off itself and fixing your own mistakes which is very helpful. Labs are 10%, hw is 50% and tests are 40% of grade. Should be easy to get an A!
He is a nice man. Lots of labs that he doesnt explain very well.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: It is hard to understand him sometimes. If he is talking to you prepare to be confused a bit. Class was 50% tests (midterm and final) and 50% labs. Some days you could go in person but most people if not all would just stay online. He is not a tough grader when it comes to the tests, but labs he is tougher.

Professor Akgun did a good job making sure we understood the material and even posted multiple videos after lectures explaining everything again. I dont know how his rating is so low but he did state multiple times that he recently changed how he teaches his class and I think that really showed this semester. I recommend him.

I took SRA 365 as an online summer course. The course material can be difficult, but the work load is very reasonable (weekly quiz + 3 exams). The quiz questions would be pulled directly from his lecture videos. Almost every quiz had an optional retake and only your highest grade would be counted.

He is super focused on your group discussion. We would receive feedback with detailed analysis of our conversation, without clear information regarding the feedback. "this sentence is an example of that type of discussion" without explaining whether that was desired or not.

I had the class summer online. The class is just 1 quiz a week and 3 exams. He speaks very slowly in the lectures but he's a nice guy. You can offers a second attempt for everything the week after being due. His lecture code can often be reworked for the quiz. Submitting r code is fill in the blanks on canvas. Overall super easy and awesome guy.

I think most people who didn't like Akgun were the ones who sat on their phones all class and did not pay attention. SRA 365 is a hard class and you need to show up, pay attention, and put in the work. He explained things thoroughly in class, repeating himself often to make sure we understood. However, labs are only open for two days which sucks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Akgun is the worst professors I ever had at Penn State. He doesn't tell you the grading criteria and he rambles most of the lectures about concepts that aren't even tested. He never answers emails. You have to teach yourself pretty much everything. Focus on the labs cause thats the only way you'll learn anything. (1 day to work on them.)

Mahir is an incredible intelligent person, he simply isn't a good professor. He constantly contradicts himself in during class saying one thing but then when you come in the next class he says something else. Never gives clear cut directions for assignments and then when you don't do it the way he expected, you get it wrong. Overall a rough class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He goes at the pace of your class to make sure that everyone actually understands the material. He goes out of his way to make sure grading is fair and there are no questions in the class. Even if you forget STAT 200 you'll be fine in this class- just go to class because he doesn't post the lecture slides. If you go to class you'll do well.
Never answer emails, lectures boring as hell, labs are confusing at most
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This guy should never be trusted teaching. Hard to understand, the whole class has to teach themselves almost every aspect of the course, lectures about pointless conceptual details that aren't covered on exams. Unfortunately SRA365 is only taught by him so try to take the STAT option if you can. I'd give him a 0 if I could

I am now a senior at PSU and have never been more dissatisfied with a professor. This guy shows now care for students (you can tell he's only employed by Penn State to do research). Never answers emails, makes TAs teach classes a lot of the time, uses other professor's assignments. Penn State should be ashamed to call this guy a professor
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Spends the entire class lecturing about concepts not even covered on exams. Disorganized, half of the labs could not be completed because of technical difficulties. We were supposed to have 3 midterms and a final and we got so behind that we had to skip one. Makes us sign a form the first day of class so he can use our survey responses for research

Do not take IST110 with this man, especially the three hour lecture. It is the biggest waste of time, and I am not joking when I say I have not learned one thing. It is generally an easy class, just all group work. He is the most boring lecturer in the world. Everyone in my class just watches videos and do HW for other classes while he talks. AVOID
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: If you want to take IST 110 (6-9pm class), I strongly recommend that you take anyone but this guy. He will almost always keep you for the full 3 hours, because he will repeat the same things over and over. His expectations and grading are kinda vague (so the assignments can be annoying), but it is still relatively easy to get an A in the class.

Okay. The class is passable but he doesn't really help much. Hard to understand and lectures don't help you understand the material. The whole class struggles and is collectively confused 99% of the time. My advice is to focus on the labs (which you have like a day to work on lolz) if you understand the labs you can pass the exam most likely.
He sucks.

You can't really understand what he is saying half the time, even though he will go over the same thing in class 5 or 6 times. The class periods would be half the time if he didn't repeat everything. The grading is very tough and the exams are filled with trick questions. Least favorite class I have ever taken and I enjoyed stat 200.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you have to take SRA365 take STAT460 instead. you're welcome
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you took the prerequisites, they wont help. He is the most unclear professor I've ever taken. He babbles on with the answers to the last lab/exam the first hour of class, then doesn't release your submission until after. Take literally anyone else in any way. I've taken classes where I learn literally nothing, and I still prefer them.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Mahir has got to be one of the worst professors at PSU. Bottom line is if you have to take SRA365, or any of his classes. DO NOT take it with him. Lectures are barebones, arbitrary and make no sense. You are given less than 48 hours to work on labs. Not sure who let him be a prof at a school like PSU.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Beware of pop quizzes--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This class made me unlearn statistics

Powerpoints he provides hardly give you any help in understanding the homework assignments. He doesn't really even teach. The videos of the powerpoints are outdated and not done by him. Prepare to do a lot of learning on your own outside of the materials you're given. Otherwise, you won't do very well. If you can, just take someone else.

The TAs were the absolute worst they were so unnecessarily mean and biased in their grading. I could not understand the professor's lectures at all the concepts weren't important or well worded and his accent was difficult to decipher. I never knew what we were supposed to be doing and would never ever take this prof again. Save yourself.
He does not teach almost at all. Just references to some videos. No lectures! A power point of like 12 slides per week. That he didn't even make. Toughest grader I have ever seen.

This class by far was one of the worst classes I have taken at Penn State. Professor Akgun made the grading unclear which confused a lot of students. He also changed the syllabus (assignments, grading weight, attendance) multiple times throughout the semester. The class itself was not hard but the strict grading made it harder than it had to be.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: I have this class Tuesdays from 6-9 and he keeps you the entire class unlike other IST110 classes. I still have no idea what his grading criteria is because he is so unclear. There are no exams so the lectures are pointless and boring.

Have this class Thursdays from 6-9pm and it's the slowest thing ever. Grading is not very clear and there are papers due every week. It's not a hard class but it's definitely not an easy class either (lots of work).

Professor Ali is an amazing teacher and is very passionate and knowledgeable about telecommunications. Attendance is not mandatory and he posts slides on canvas. Class lectures were engaging and helpful so I always attended. I rarely did weekly readings and 3 exams and a final all in Pollock. Exams were easy as long as you study and know the terms.

Professor Ali is amazing and a great teacher. He is also so beyond understanding and kind. I wish I could say the same for the TA's, she grades like she is trying to make everyone just not do their work because they know they will get zeros anyways so she doesn't have to grade it! Good luck!

the course was pretty easy, textbook and packback required which sucks. He himself was a little mean in my unpopular opinion. But the class itself is easy. Just study, go to class, you'll do fine. Exams are online but in class and are heavily proctored.

Dr. Ali is super passionate about telecommunications. The lectures are engaging and informative. Show up and take notes and you'll be good. Weekly Packbacks take 30 minutes and are easy points. He prepares students well for tests and is always willing to re-explain topics or terms mid lecture.

Go to class. He is very passionate about what he talks about, which makes the lectures interesting. He made me want to go to class because of how amazing his lectures were. You are graded on a weekly packback and study guide for each of the exams which you are pretty much guaranteed a 100%. There are 4 exams with the final not being cumulative.

Attend the lectures and you will be fine. The study guides and packbacks are super easy to get 100% on. He gives away a TON of the exam answers in class. Very engaging and interesting lectures. Great Professor.

Great professor. Especially towards the end of the semester not many people showed up to lecture but he still made lectures engaging. Questions in class were encouraged and if you are really interested in the topics being discussed the lectures are actually great.

Dr. Ali is probably my favorite professor here at Penn State. He is so knowledgeable about what he's teaching and also passionate, which makes his lectures so much fun to listen do. You do have to get packback which is a bit pricey but as long as you do them you'll probably at least pass. I do suggest going to class. Definitely would take again!!

Professor Ali is one of my favorite professors. There are 4 exams, the 4th exam is during finals week & not cumulative. Lectures are interesting & information is clear. If you have questions he's available & happy to help. There's a weekly coffee hour, where you can talk about anything, it's a great way to get to know Professor Ali.
Great teacher. Professor Ali was always there for us, and would listen if we needed anything.

I love prof Ali! He is so sweet and genuine. He clearly cares about the topic and his students. He is so sweet, and his class was easy. There are 4 exams, but none of them are terribly hard if you study well. He holds coffee hours during the week, where you can just go in and talk to him. I love him; great prof, great guy overall. Take his class!

I adore this man so much. Lectures are always interesting and Professor Ali's passion for what he's teaching is so contagious. The topics were really interesting, however you might have to do a bit of reading. Weekly homework is essentially completion and tests can be challenging, but study guide is super helpful if you complete it. Great class!

Ali is an engaging lecturer and caring professor. Weekly TopHats, but it's not too bad bc you only need 60 pts. Usually have an easy 3 question quiz on Canvas during class each week. Exams are in Pollock and can be challenging but easy to do well if you study (esp if u use the study guide). Didn't buy the textbook or do readings and did fine.
Unpopular opinion but he was pretty annoying; he tried to be relatable but it was clear he put himself on a pedestal.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Bombed every exam, and forgot to do so many packbacks and still ended with a B+. I found that the exams were hard but it didn't really matter. There are other ways to bring your grade up. Really great guy and super engaged in his teaching. I want to shrink him and carry him around in my pocket.

Professor Ali is one of my favorite professors. He is very knowledgable and cares about his students. I loved the material we learned in this class and he made it very interesting to learn. If you can take his class, do it. The class had four exams, packback and extra credit. If I can take another class of his I would in a heartbeat.

Professor Ali has been the best professor I have ever had, he understands the importance of teaching good and also his topics are very interesting. He gave tons of extra credit opportunities. Class consists of packback every week and 3 exams that all are easy. This class is an easy A.

Prof Ali is a great professor. His lectures are very engaging, but attendance isn't mandatory and he posts all the slides on canvas. He offers extra credit and curves the exam grades if they are under a 78% average. Easy class if you study for his exams and do the weekly packbacks. I highly recommend taking his class.

Professor Ali is a great professor, he is new to PSU, but I would take him again. His COMM 180 class was graded off packbacks and 4 major tests. Great professor, great lectures, focus in class, take notes, and study for his tests and you'll be fine.

I took GWS 350: Human Rights and Global Lit at UW-Madison. Needless to say, Hanan is amazing. Her lectures are so insightful and well-structured. It's a discussion-heavy class, but she does an amazing job at keeping the flow. I definitely encourage you to take a class with her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Guys, I love Hanan! I had her for Arabic 1 & 2 over this school year. She creates such a safe environment to speak freely. Hanan also has a great sense of humor, is very light-hearted, soft-spoken, and is sooooooo understanding. I wish I could have Hanan for Arabic 3! She's just so excellent at what she does. Please take her class if you can!!!
very interesting class, and very kind and understanding professor, gives great lectures and good feedback. is clear about what she expects. class is worthwhile if humans rights means something to you

So much work for 2 & 3 point assignments. You can do everything the instructions say, but she will still take points off and then tell you it was because you didnt do something that you werent even told to do. You literally have to write essays to get credit for 2 point assignments and but they prob still wont be good enough. Don't take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Worst professor I have ever had

Very difficult to understand. Practically whispering at the front of the classroom. Reads every lecture off of a PowerPoint and offers no useful additional information. Nice man but there is such a lack of communication that it makes going to class almost useless.
Dont take horrible teacher
reviews.rating_tags: Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Very hard to follow along with what is going on in class. Lectures are very boring and dry. Homework was difficult and labs were as well. Was not a fan of R.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He lectures directly from the textbook that he wrote(and that said book is awful), so it's extremely boring and hard to pay attention in class. Also speaks quietly and with an accent, so that makes it even worse. At least he lets you have cheat sheets for the exams and final. To do well, you'll either need to teach yourself or find a good tutor.

Terrible professor, teaches what he thinks is important, and then good luck figuring out everything else for yourself! Teaches the basics for R coding and then you have to figure out how to make everything else work for yourself even if it doesn't make any sense!

Super quiet can barley hear anything he says, so you better read up on that text book he wrote and makes you get. All the homework is done in that book, and some of the labs too. If you can pay attention in that class and not fall sleep I commend you, he is a nice guy though, he will help you out, if you can hear him that is.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: The course is actually easy, if you have a decent professor. Akritas is a nice guy, but his teaching style is dry, the textbook sucks, he writes really small on a blackboard that takes up half of the classroom! If you have him, prepare to put in a lot of hours learning th material on your own. The only upside is that midterms are open book.

First off, I love stats.  I loved my AP Stats teacher in high school and got an A.  That being said, avoid this professor at all costs.  He wrote his own book and it seems like he uses his own made up equations.  The only redeeming quality is that he is eager to help but it doesn't matter cause the material makes no sense.  Good guy, awful teacher.

He is by far one of the worst professors I have ever had. He wrote his own textbook, which is the worst textbook written by mankind. I can have a third grader write a better textbook than him. University does not check on the material because I am pretty sure most of it is made up. Goes over a stupid program instead of actually teaching the materal

Bottom-line, he is extremely difficult to understand and the TA, Ye Yu, was equally as hardtop understand. The only way to learn the material was to spend countless hours reading the textbook. I credit myself and myself alone for my acceptable grade in this class.
he speaks Greek in classes, my knowledge of permutation combination got screwd big time after taking this course. But never the less a helpful guy. Choice is yours, to take this course.
really good teacher. very helpful in office hours. extremely patient and understanding that statistics is hard to learn and comprehend.

This was his first semester teaching this course so I cut him a little slack for not having great material organization. TA help was dreadful, his help was decent. If you have to take this class, Akritas lectures fluently and does know his stuff. Far too much use of math jargon/symbols, though, so read up on all that stuff.

He is helpful and wants to make sure that you understand the material. However, the slide shows are the same as the book and they are very boring, so you won't be able to stay alert during the whole class unless you are extremely interested.

The worst professor I've ever had at Penn State. Going to class was a waste of time, since the lecture notes are poorly written and badly explained. Awful textbook. In the end, almost all of my HW assignments were lost by him or the TA, and when I asked about them I was flat-out called a liar. Just unprofessional in the worst. Avoid at all costs.
he reads right off of his slides and the homework is rediculous.  There are very few examples, yet a ton of information...
not helpful

. His class isn't that hard, you get a sheet of notes for your quizzes and I thought the grading on the HW was fair.  The book could use more examples, but its def enough to do the homeworks. I don't really think you can make statistics exciting. but he drops the lowest HW (8 tot) and qz(3) score, it makes it easy to have a good grade b4 the final.

Terrible class. The book (if you want to call it that) is a piece of what I flush everyday. Lectures are mind boggling you jump through the book like you're in Quantum Leap. The TA is a nazi with grading hw, I'd rather have Himmler looking at it. The quizzes can be bsed though with the cheat sheets. I'd steer clear if you could.

What a clown, this guy totally blows as a teacher.  He wants you to buy this stupid textbook he supposedly wrote, and then all he does is read directly from it durring class.  My advise to you is either find a different professor or do what I did and buy Probability and Statistics by Jay L. Devore and read that instead of going to class.
This guy strait sucks at teaching.  This year he created his own textbook, made you buy it and it pretty much was worthless.  Stay away from this clown.

Dr Akritas was helpfull, knowledgabe, more than happy to help students, takes time as need to solve hw in class. in his note concentrate on the importatn things for us as engineers.Exam are reasonable.he need to find a way to make the class more active and get the attention of the students.

all these positive posts are falsified.  as of three days ago there were a bunch of posts.  none of them with anything good to say.  this guy doesn't care to teach and it shows.  he also looks like jesus from the big lebowski.

Dr. Akritas was a very fair instructor - he takes class time to answer homework questions, which doesn't happen too often.  The accent is no problem, and his English is excellent.  The course is tough, but not enough that an A is unattainable.  And a chance to waive the final exam is always a good thing.

Prof Akritas's course allowed me to learn a lot about statistics in a painless manner.  He focused on the material we were likely to need later as engineers.  His presentations were clear and his grading policy was fair.  He was always more than happy to help out a student outside of class.

Prof Akritas provided a good amount of examples for application of the equations.  He created his own notes, which is commendable, but it would help if the pertinent equations were put in a summary section (possibly at the end of each chapter).  The homework is challenging, but he is more than willing to give assistance = very understanding.
Prof. Akritas is pretty good.  He is always more than happy to help people outside of class.  With a little effort you can get a good grade and learn something.

Dr. Akritas makes STAT401 very reasonable for students.  He doesn't require a book, and doesn't require you to come to class. He gives 3-4 relatively easy quizzes, and also the opportunity to exempt the final. If you go to class, and put forth the effort, it should be an easy A. He is very fair, and kind towards students.  HIGHLY RECOMMENDED!!!!

Dr. Akritas is a good professor, but you must put forth an effort and show that you care about his class. Provided you read the chapter b4 class, his explanations are reinforcing and make perfect sense. The hmwk can be tough, but its do-able. He's always more than willing to help students outside of class (whether during his office hours or not).

Reads from the pdf's. The problem is, he wrote them so they don't make sense because nothing he says or does makes sense. He mumbles and is hard to understand or follow. DONT TAKE THIS CLASS. The hw is impossible because he teaches nothing so he ends up doing SOME of it in class and moving the due-date back. Worst teacher ever!

This guy is rediculously bad at everything in life.  I know this because there's no way he could be this horrible at teaching stat and be any good at anything else.  Except maybe evading responsibility.  He also looks like Jesus from The Big Lebowski.
All he did was read proofs and theorems.  Occasionaly he'd do an example that was 10 times simpler than anything on an exam.  Without the curve 2/3 of the class failed

"Mr. Akritas, what you've just said is one of the most insanely idiotic things I have ever heard. At no point in your rambling, incoherent semester were you even close to anything that could be considered a rational thought. Everyone in this room is now dumber for having listened to it. I award you
Horrible teacher.He does not explain anything and reads straight from the PDF that is exactly from the book.I learned nothing from his class

Teaches right from the PDF files and he jumps around so it's impossible to understand.  Tells you not to study his notes or from the book so all you have to study from is the hw, but those questions are easy compared his quizzes.  HW is the only help you'll get in this class.  Accent is horrible.

Confusing class, and his accent is tough to understand. He teaches off of pdf files, which sucks; but then again because of that you don't have to bother coming to class except for quizzes. Homework is a great grade-booster.

Easy class. Some of the grading is unreasonable, but lots of extra credit and weekly quizzes that you can take twice. Her lectures are really boring and she talks a lot about her perfect parenting style which is kind of annoying. Going to class is such a waste of time, but there are Tophats.

Easy class. Some of the grades are kind of unreasonable, but lots of extra credit and weekly quizzes that you can take twice. Her lectures are really boring and she constantly is uplifting her parenting style in a kind of annoying way. Going is kind of a waste of time, but there is Tophat.

Best professor EVER! I took this class for my minor and so happy I did. Dr. DP is one of the coolest professors ever. You can tell she wants all of her students to succeed. There is extra credit...do it becasue it helps you out. Assignments are not difficult, you get multiple attempts to learn and get a good grade. I recommend this class to anyone

Professor DP is great! Homework assignments are easy to complete, with many opportunities for make-ups. Top hat is used in class, but you can also make those up too. Plenty of extra-credit work, exams are open-note and open-textbook, so just by going to class and doing the homework on time, you're pretty much guaranteed an A.
Keeps the class moving and makes its fun. She makes the class interesting so you want to be present instead of staying in your dorm.

Dr. D-P was amazing! It's really impossible to fail in her class. She gives so much extra credit, will reopen any assignment and will given you partial credit if you complete something late. The exams were difficult but you can work in groups and they were all open not. Take her if you need an easy psych course!

Best professor found at Penn State. I've taken 2 of courses PSYCH 423 and 432. She will use Top Hat for attendance and assign in-class activities. If you were to get full credit for these sections of the class plus the 10 extra credit points she provides you are guaranteed to get a good grade. Exams: MC, 2-3 essay questions chosen from exam pool.

She is a great professor. Very approachable and friendly. PSYCH212 really is not all that hard - she makes the readings managable but I still feel like I'm learning a lot from her. I can tell she has a lot of experience and knows what she's doing 100%. I would take her class again!

Dr. DP is one of my favorite professors I have taken a class with in the Psych department here. She is super funny in lecture and has TONS of extra credit opportunities throughout the year. Its almost impossible to get a bad grade. She does use TopHat for in class participation points but will reopen the questions if you miss class.

Professor DP is a very nice professor, and allows you to make up anything in the class. I enjoyed taking this course and she makes sure you will do well. The exams are hard but if you do all the homework and textbook quizzes you will get an A.

Dr. DP was great this semester! She is extremely understanding and wants you to succeed. She gives a bunch of extra credit. There are tophats everyday for attendance purposes but you can make them up. Her quizzes are very textbook heavy but once you understand how the coursework is you will get good grades no problem.

Professor DP is a great person and wants her students to succeed. She gives a ton of extra credit and allows you to make up anything at anytime. I personally was not a fan of the teaching style and it just didn't suit me, but I recommend trying out one of her courses. Test are difficult but do not count for a lot of your grade. Lots of homework.

she really cares about her students doing well in her class. she is more than reasonable when it comes to making up working, meeting for office hours, and basically any assistance you may need. she is funny and her lectures are enjoyable. the content can be confusing but she is there to answer any question you may have!
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Absolute W of a professor. Really cares for her students.
Awesome teacher. Makes class interesting and really cares about her students!

She is the sweetest lady, however; there can be up to 7 hw assignments a week with additional in class activities. If you like psych, it is interesting, but work can become overwhelming and feel like busy work. She is happy to work with students and is good at her job. But if you have a busy schedule already, take this a different semester.

Dr. DP was always very engaging in lectures and made the class interesting so I really enjoyed it although it was optional in person at the time due to COVID. There are two required textbooks but they don't seem like textbooks and are easy reads. She was very understanding and offers extensions on practically any assignment if you need.

ADP was my favorite professor across all four years at PSU. Quick overview. Important to participate, come to class, take decent notes. Often too many class activities. Provides consistent, engaging anecdotes. Encourages people to share their opinions. Genuinely cares about you learning the material. I took her for 3 separate classes & would again.

Dr. DP is a good professor and teaches interesting stuff in class, but it doesn't really relate to the quizzes we have to take. All the info for the quizzes comes from the textbook, which isn't awful to navigate. This class is an easy A once you find out how to make the work load very manageable and minmal. I only went to class less than 8 times.

Caring, understanding, and will definitely hear you out. She teaches the material very well and uses personal connections to effectively explain the material. She also gives a ton of extra credit. However, group work is constant and tests are very hard (however they aren't worth much). Assigns an insane number of assignments (2-5 a week).
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Dr. DP is one of the sweetest professors. She cares about her students and cares more about learning than anything. She is very clear about what she expects from you and the tests are really easy if you use all the resources available to you. Also, there is quite a bit of extra credit so I didn't spend too much time stressing about this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. DP is really sweet but she assigns a lot of in-class work and homework. You would be doing multiple in-class group assignments during one class period and then would have case study and homework assessments to do aside. There's a lot of busywork that you really don't get much time to actually study the course material on your own.

The class design is simple in nature. If you do not read the assigned readings or watch the videos, you will miss questions on the quizzes and exams. The course content is interesting. Overall, I would take the class again. Prof Drais-Parrillo is a fair grader and gives quality feedback.

I have never been poorly graded as in this class. I applied my personal perspective on topics and she came back and said that this was not right so therefore my grade suffered. Online professors that teach online classes should be more interactive. She explained assignments after they were submitted.

The most caring professor I've ever had. She conveys information so clearly and the work is not hard a all. She understand that students are individual and is very patient and understanding in class in a way I've never seen.

She is super sweet! She cares about you and your grades. If you need extra time, she is willing to give it! She is understanding about work load. She is clear (sometimes) about her explanations but she mumbles sometimes. If you need clarification ask! Exams are on canvas - quizzes for each chapter. Case studies are sometimes in groups HW is simple

She really knows her stuff and provide clear explanations on the topics. There are 4 non-cumulative exams and no finals. Clicker points are for attendance and in class exercises. Bunch of works and group works to do but it will definitely help your grades. Flipd can supplement your clicker points. A lot of extra credits so come to class!

Human sexuality is a super interesting topic, so lectures and textbook readings were almost enjoyable. Her assignments however had little to no relation to the course material (very research methods oriented). Her grading criteria is also extremely confusing and there are too many assignments to be done in one class period.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Parillo is really sweet, but her lectures are really boring. It is not a hard class, as most of it is online. However, there are multiple assignments every week and the content is tricky. Loved the teacher, hated the class!

Dr. DP is awesome and makes lecture super interesting and funny. Exams are online, essay questions but she gives you the exact essay questions a week ahead of time. So much in class work. You will fail the class if you don't go.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: She is a great person and class seems easy but exams can be hard and extremelly confusing. Clicker grades are huge and Flipd gives you extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: Would 10/10 take a class with Dr. Parrillo! Shes amazing and honestly if you actually listen to her lectures she's pretty funny! She does a great job of making the material interesting. Use Flipd for extra points!!! If you use it for a certain number of hours she adds points to your grade and since I had more hours than her she gave me 6 points!

Let me start off by saying that I've never been so poorly graded on discussion in my life(7s-9s/10). However, things are different with this prof. She's not clear and she gives me the vibe that she's going through a lot at the moment and punishing her students about. She grades late and will always find something negative to say. Take another prof.

Let me start off by saying that whomever said she no exams, it's a LIE. She has many and piles up your exams, quizzes and web assignments to make up for spring break week. WTH LADY! Why not just give out work instead of letting us focus on your already long and annoying exams? It's like she's trying to prove something with a SOCIAL PSYCH course!!!

She's an easy professor, but she has exams back to back. Her exams are long and boring and we had to do 2 exams for two weeks in a row. The exams have 2 parts each. I don't understand why she would give us 2 exams back to back. Online classes annoy me, because we're literally paying for a degree and to teach ourselves off the book. No lectures.

Drais-Parrillo is amazing. A lovely human being who allows for a clear understanding of the material she presents. Super easy to work with and understands what students go through. Truly my favorite professor so far.
A relatively easy class, the prof is okay. Nothing much to talk about.

Dr. Parillo is a wonderful professor, she's understanding and really knows her stuff. She makes the lectures interesting by breaking it up with short group assignments. They are a good opportunity to learn the info more effectively. The class isn't heavily focused on exams. Overall, she's really sweet and interesting to learn from.

This is one of the easiest classes I've taken here. No tests, the answers for the online quizzes are on quizlet and an online final. Pretty much your whole grade is in class participation. If you don't get an A in this class you should quit your life.

Awesome class with a unique exams. Gives 10-13 essay options that could be on the exam. Do them all before hand and she'll go through them to make sure you got everything right. If you dont do them exams would be very hard. WORK AND REWARD. I loved this class, shes great, makes things fun, very personable. Reading quizzes are tough if you dont read
Very clear and to the point with lectures and directives for assignments. Always there to help and provide clarity

Alex is one of my favorite professors! He cares so much about his students, and will bend over backwards to make sure you have he support you need in his classes. He has readings, and much of class is discussion/lecture on the readings themselves. Great guy, 100% recommend, please take class with him!

Professor Host was very understanding and helpful. Some of his in-class essays can be difficult, but I always went to office hours beforehand and he was very helpful. You definitely have to do the readings and attend class to get a good grade in his class. He also grades pretty heavily on participation, so make sure to participate frequently.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Host is the best teacher I have had in my time at Penn State, coming from a non-Philosophy student. He makes the content accessible, the lectures are engaging, and he clearly cares about the success of each student. Could not recommend more. Take any of his classes if you get the chance.
Tests are extremely hard and ask about the smallest things. Quizzes are even harder and worth 25% of grade.

Once again he cancels class. Probably 8th time this semester.

I've heard grades are rounded at the end, I need it.
Since every comment doesn't meet the guidelines ill just say: Bad in every attribute, will miss class within first weeks, exam average is super super low.

He is one of the best professors in the Engineering department. He truly cares about his students and supports us in both the course and our career decisions. Although the class is challenging, he explains concepts clearly, never rushes his recorded lectures, and uses real-life examples that make learning easier and more memorable.
there should be a rating of 0 on the scale for this guy
bad class, bad communication
this professor needs to go
no one should have to deal with this professor

The only thing that helped me on the tests and quizzes was reading his slides; I had no idea what I had learned in class SP25. Since quizzes were far more difficult than exams, I honestly had no idea what to do. You can achieve an A if you simply place in the top 10% of the class; it's not impossible if you work hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Almekkawy explains the material clearly and keeps the lectures well organized. He is approachable and helpful when students have questions, and overall the course was a positive learning experience.
Took this class in SP25. The only reason he gets a 2 is because he curved the class a good bit. Otherwise, class is very disorganized and communication is not the best.

Class is very disorganized and communication not great. Expectations for labs are not clear but the help videos are clarifying. Quizzes (worth decent amount of grade) just test you on tiny details. Very second-half heavy course. First half of semester, you do like nothing. Second half, lab due every other week, quizzes weekly, etc.

Those quizzes were brutal to be honest, and sometimes it felt like it was quizzing the niche areas of the lectures at times. Overall this class was difficult but otherwise manageable, but don't expect your grade to look pretty until the end of the semester.

CMPEN 331 is a challenging, work-intensive course, but Prof. Almekkawy teaches it in a clear and structured way. He explains complex architecture concepts well, is approachable, and values consistent effort. The workload is heavy, but he applies a very good curve at the end citing the students' efforts, making the course fair and rewarding.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This is one of those classes where your grade will be under 80% the whole year unless you spend all your time on it, but there will be a big curve anyway. Don't be surprised if an exam average is
Good professor. Weekly quizzes so you are kind of forced to keep up with the material which is kind of a good thing. Quizzes and exams are most of the grade. Video lectures weekly. Important class.

Great lectures, he explains concepts with analogies. However, none of the lectures, slides, or review material prepares you for the Exams and Quizzes. You must find a way to have an in-depth fundamental understanding of the concepts to build off and infer on the spot for the quizzes.

Mohamed Almekkawy is one of the best professor I have ever met. His lecture is very clear and informative. He always explains those tricky concepts more than one time to make sure you really understand it. Meanwhile, he also gives good advices in career and life.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment:
His quizzes are either impossible or easy so studying is just useless.
He shows up late.
We have quizzes almost half the classes, sometimes back-to-back classes we have quizzes.
He doesn't give back your quizzes or exams so if you get a grade, you can't see what you even did.
His exams are alright but a little hard, but its still fine.

Prof. Almekkawy seems like a nice person but his teaching style isn't the best. He often arrives 20–30 minutes late to classes. Quizzes and exams are tough but manageable if you study well using his reviews and slides. The class is heavily curved as he mentions so grades usually balance out.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Weekly quizzes that are impossible, says that "You will be screaming by the end" On exams and quizzes (Which is crazy to say on its own). It's a gamble if you'll pass or fail. Always comes in late, reuses lectures from YouTube done like 8 years ago. Exams are very hard you have to quite literally understand as if you did this for your entire life

I had him in Spring 2025. nice guy, dropped 4quiz, 2lab and 1mid in the end, and the avg grade for an A was around 90. However, he was normally 30 minutes late for classes, and probably not showing up on Thurdays when we had quizzes. And the exams and quizzes were really hard. Labs were also hard. I got an A and had no idea what I learnt. Good luck
never responds to emails

He never replies to emails at all, regardless of whether there is a grading mistake or if you had a medical emergency. I took this class twice, once in the spring and once in the summer, and he never responded to a single email during either semester.

Trying and not trying in this class will get you about the SAME grade. Since everything is so heavily curved. Eventually he gives a speech with what's dropped and that sometimes you have to learn even if you don't like it. While also giving an excuse that this class is hard to teach....as a Professor.....as a introduction course.

People only like him because of curves, it's almost impossible to do well. Tests and quizzes are so difficult that studying for them feels like a waste of time. Online lectures get stale after a while. Even the study materials are rough, the answer keys are at times tricky to decipher and understand. If you only care about passing, you're fine.

Professor Almekkawy genuinely cares about his students and wants them to succeed. He explains difficult concepts well, drops the lowest grades, and even pushes the deadlines when needed. Although the labs are difficult at first, once you get a good grasp of Verilog, they get much easier. Overall, Professor Almekkawy does a great job with the class.

Class was on Tuesday and Thursday, with a test every Thursday. Lectures were recorded on Canvas, and I found them to be very helpful when studying. Drops a test and a few quizzes, and also gives an opportunity for some labs and homework to be dropped as well. Tests/quizzes were unnecessarily hard, but labs really help improve your grade.

He makes sure you understand, and answers questions in class. He uses analogies, which helps. Quizzes&exams are hard, but you just need to study slides&practice qs. For labs, he has tutorial videos that you can just follow. Grading isn't too harsh, and you get quiz, exam, homework and lab drops on top of a curve so there's no reason you don't pass.

Reuses old online lectures from years ago and regularly cancels class. Most weeks, you're only showing up once to take a quiz run by the TAs - quizzes that everyone fails (seriously, the last one had an average score of 4/10). Then you're out the door 40 minutes into what's supposed to be a 75-minute class. Awful.

Weekly quizzes and exams are based on lectures/book readings and are very difficult. I felt like I failed almost every one. There are labs and reading assingments where you can make up points. Try to hit slightly above averatge for each assignment and you will get a decent grade. He drops 3/8 quizzes, 2/5 labs, etc. Final project is easy too.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Quizzes were pretty brutal and I didn't pass most of them, you just have to do the labs, try to be about average on exams, and the curve should take care of you. The professor genuinely wants everyone to succeed and pass so just do the work and he'll make sure you pass. "You have to try to fail this class", in his words.

He is a bad professor, but his grading scale makes the class passable. He drops a lot of things. Don't get me wrong, the class is very hard. It's hard to know if you will pass the class or not and to trust the curve. Super hard labs. Quizzes every week.

The lab is my favorite part of this course, he drop many stuff at the end of the semester, so you won't fail on this class. But the really annoying things are that midterm 3 grade and final grade scale are determined in final week.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Beware of pop quizzes--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Even if you mess up the exams, submit labs late, or miss quizzes, you can easily pass.

I'm not a CMPENG student, but this was still one of my favorite courses I had to take. Professor Almekkay puts great effort into keeping his lectures engaging / interesting and is really looking for his students to succeed, so the grading is fairly forgiving. The labs and exams are challenging, but by no means unreasonable.
even if you put limited amount of work you'll still get a decent grade; he drops one exam (usually the 2nd since it's the hardest) but doesn't tell you until the end of the course.
class is difficult but the professor cares about the students. overall just good professor.

Professor Almekkawy will throw a lot of content at you and the labs, exams, and quizzes will be pretty difficult. However, I feel like this forced me to learn a lot and develop a strong understanding of the course material. He drops a lot of your lowest grades at the end of the semester so if you put in effort you'll finish with a good grade.

Never went to a single class through the semester, only showed up to quizzes (which are announced a couple weeks before). Truthfully, I had no business passing. Scoring 30s across every exam he handed out, skipping over half the quizzes. My only saving grace was the labs which I only did because they were fun and is a good resume builder.

Prof Almekkawy is awesome. Ensures you learn through a rigorous course, but then makes sure your grade does not suffer unfairly bc the difficulty of the course. He is a very likable person, who does a good job overall with the class.

This class is very difficult and will force you to learn a lot. However, mo ensures that everyone will pass the class with how much he drops. Just be sure to start all the labs early and the zybooks are very helpful. He gives some career advice at the end which is cool.
bro is a master of mailboxes and hotels management
Not the easiest class but everything was heavily curved.

The homework was not very difficult, although the projects were explained incredibly poorly and lazily., He didn't grade anything until the last week so I was unable to know my grade at all until then. Didn't respond to emails for weeks and some emails I sent got no response at all. Would not recommend taking a class with him as professor. Avoid.

DO NOT TAKE A ONLINE CLASS WITH HIM. He never responds to email, his TA's often skip their own office hours, it is impossible to reach out and receive assistance. You will be COMPLETELY on your own in the class, and he will only bother to grade assignments in the final week.

All of the lectures were recorded years ago and the material hasn't been touched since. Some lecture recordings have poor audio quality. One lecture has no audio whatsoever. The professor took far too long to reply to emails and the TAs did most of the work. It feels like the professor put zero effort into managing this course.

He gives very hard quizzes and exams that the averages were so low, but he understands and drops the lowest 3 quizzes and lowest exam to save people's grades. Labs start to get harder during the 2nd half of the semester,  and the project builds up on those labs. Also gives a curve such that the minimum for a passing C is around a 55, but A is 89.

Extremely qualified to teach. Cares greatly about his students. Labs, tests, quizzes were fair. Drops stuff to make the grading fairer. You will learn a lot if you keep up to date on lectures and go to office hours when you are stuck. He is good at explaining tough concepts. The only negative is that the lab instructions can be hard to understand.

For those that are currently enrolled in CMPEN 331 this semester, please do the SRTEs ASAP! Need to do them by Sunday 4/30 11:59pm. If 90% of CMPEN 331 students complete them, he will drop lowest exam, lowest 3 hws, lowest 3 quizzes, and lowest 2 quizzes. A lot of people really need the grade bump and doing the SRTEs would be very helpful to them.

Sometimes the grading can be harsh and the material is confusing but Almekkawy understands. He drops many exams, quizzes, and labs and pushes back deadlines when necessary. His lectures are good but the textbook is even better in my opinion. The exams are generally much harder than the practice exams but he provides a great variety in examples.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The course content is difficult but the professor definitely cares about his students doing well. Lectures are very good. Start the labs ahead of time to use office hours. There is also a generous curve at the end of the semester so don't feel discouraged if you do poorly on a quiz or exam.

One of the best professor in the CSE department. CMPEN 331 is a hard course, but there will be a huge curve at the end. So just take this course seriously, go to the lectures and prepare for the exam and you will be fine.

Professor Mohamed Almekkawy is one of the best professors in the computer engineering department. His lecture is pretty detailed. Even if the topic is hard, you will study a lot if you pay close attention. I super enjoy his computer vision class. It's pretty useful.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Almekkawy is a great professor. He provides excellent lectures and I learnt a lot about Computer Vision techniques in this course. One can get a good grade if sincere efforts are made by attending all lectures and solving all homework problems diligently. Projects are very interesting. I definitely recommend this class to everyone.

Dr. Almekkawy is a fairly good professor. He provides advice on how to succeed in this course, as well as in your future career/studies. The lab assignments are easy if you work to learn Verilog. He drops a lot of the grades, but I did not see the effect of the additional curve at all. His quizzes could have been more spread out over the semester.
Very good teacher.

Peace Be Upon Him.

Drops lowest exam, 3 lowest quizzes, 3 lowest labs, and some lowest HWs. All of this AND a curve. The course is pretty difficult but if you put in effort, he will give you a passing grade.

Professor Almekkawy is genuinely a good guy and professor. He really wants his students to succeed and gives them good advice. He dropped 1/3 exams, 3/7 quizzes, 3/9 homeworks, and 2/7 labs. Labs are pretty easy if you've had previous Verilog experience, so be sure to review it before taking this class! The cutoff for an A was around an 85%
Professor Almekkawy is a good professor, he is very helpful and mild, I like his lecture and I got A in CMPEN 331 course. Believe me, take his course!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: All the slides were from other professors, all of the lectures were prerecorded readings off the slides, he didn't answer any questions I asked through Canvas or email, he did not attend the office hour sessions that he posted (at least when I tried), and he didn't grade any of my work, the TA's did. Never had a teacher do literally nothing before.

He saved a lot of people's grades by dropping 1/3 exams, 2/5 labs, and 4/7 quizzes. The tests were insanely difficult but the top 10% cutoff (which is around the cutoff for an A) is only a 58% on exams. He definitely cares about his students, though, and if you put in the effort you'll do well. And try to attempt the project extra credit!

This class was one of the only courses in Penn State that I found to be genuinely worth it. You design a processor in this course, which is challenging but boy do you feel like a bad ass when it's finished. The curve is nice and the professor offered valuable advice to his students at the end of the semester.

If you are taking CMPSC 331, do not take it with any other professor other than Professor Almekkawy. He is the man. He is very understanding and with a very good curve and I mean a very very good curve. He is the man no doubt. As long as you do the work and try, you will not fail.

Sure he drops an exam, lowest 4 quizzes, 2 labs, and 2 homeworks. It does not make a difference because the averages for those are very high and for me I had a 100% in all of those categories (not including exam). Getting slightly above average on all of the exams I still will probably end up with a C+ in the class with his tentative 8-9% curve.
A real living Buddha! Drops 1 of 3 exams, 4 of 7 quizzes, 2 of 5 labs and 2 of weekly Zybook homework! CS and CE and EE students if you want to pass this class take it with him!!!

Prof. Mohamed Almekkawy is good at explaining lecture materiel. Lecture ppt and sample exam are helpful. Make sure to understand the sample exams before taking the midterms. Projects are very interesting but time consuming, so start the project early.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Prof. Almekkawy's lectures and topics of this class are very interesting. Projects are not easy, but the professor is very helpful and always give us more time to work on the projects. Exams are similar to the homework and review problem, which is manageable. I learned a lot about computer vision in this class.

Professor Mohamed Almekkawy is a great professor in teaching. Projects are carefully designed and interesting. His classes are very interesting, he interacts with students often to make sure everyone understand, and explains his knowledge very well. Recommend his classes.
Do the quizzes again and remember the formula then you will get good grades. Projects are hard but enough time. He sometimes gave extra credit during the lecture so remember to attend the class.
The projects are hard but he drop the lowest one and gave 5 free days for late submission in total, so that wasn't bad. Also drop the lowest midterm. 3 midterms and no finals.

Professor Almekkawy is the most considerate teacher I've ever had. He will always be there for you if you have concerns. He cares about students well being and will constantly check on us about both life and course work. He even gave amazing opportunities to drop projects and exams. The lectures are awesome and detailed as well.
I enjoyed this class for the most part. Projects were difficult, but grading seemed lenient and one got dropped. An exam also gets dropped so your grade at the end is pretty decent.

One of the best selective courses I took. The course is well-designed and gives you a good introduction to computer vision. 4 labs (1 optional) of interesting and practical topics, hard but at a reasonable difficulty level.

The class is hard no doubt, but there were curves and lots of low scores were dropped. Prof. Almekkawy is patient and really tries his best to help students with course materials. TAs in this class are very knowledgeable and helpful. Class overall is less time-consuming than other required 300&400-level courses.

This course is tough, so get ready to find TA and come to the office hour. Everything in class is important. Professor is nice and patient, he will explain whatever you ask. If you pay attention on class you will find the same questions appear on midterm exam and final
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: My CMPEN331 was the hardest class in all the 8 semesters but due to the level of hardness I had to push my boundaries which ultimately resulted into great knowledge of the subject which I am applying at work. Professor Almekkawy is a workaholic person and he is always available for students for any problems. He is very friendly and gem of a person

Professor Almekkawy may be a decent teacher for 331, but absolutely ran down this class. Class was poorly organized, professor just read off the slides (or rather breezed through them), with no context or examples whatsoever. Class was often cancelled and TAs cancelled office hours too. Too many projects and very little help.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Worst organized course material. Trust me, you will not be able to understand the material through his lecture.

Worst organized CS course at Penn State. Professor could be replaced by a wallnut tree and you would not feel the differerence in the course. Available only once a week for office hours which he keeps cancelling and rescheduling. He has put zero effort in actually teaching the material. TAs are no help either. Skip this one if you value your sanity

Do not get me wrong. This class is hard. One of the hardest classes that I have ever taken. However, thats why the professors are here, to help mitigate some of the difficult content. Professor is very very very passionate about these topics, he gives you good examples to help with the content. Labs are super easy if you get the content in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Inspirational--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: The stuff we learned was cool and the curve at the end was good, but it was one of the most stressful/time-consuming classes I've ever taken. Not sure if it's because of the prof or the amount of material there was. Exams were much harder than anything we've practiced in class and some of the labs took up way too much time.

Good person at least made you felt that way, his personality towards to the politician more than a professor. Which means when he promise you good future, good grade, curve up, those things were never guranteed to be real. It could goes either way.

Most hilarious and memeworthy professor I've ever had in the EECS department. Though not the best lecturer, he's caring, and his strategies push you to learn and digest materials by yourself, which is a really important skill to have in the industry and beyond. 100% recommend

He teaches by scribbling all over a powerpoint; I learned way more from doing Zybooks exercises. His exams were challenging, but since it was much easier to cheat online, exam averages were double the usual score. As a result, the curve was almost nonexistent in Fall 2020 (only 2-3%).

Prof. Almekkawy taught the Computer Vision class really well. Labs are very interesting and help you learn the concepts better, 2 exams both reasonably easy. Lectures are recorded which are helpful and the professor is very approachable outside of class.
A lot of stuff is covered during lecture, labs are very interesting and helpful for understanding. Exams are easy, would definitely take again.

Honest after taking some of 400 level CMPSC courses and CMPSC 311, Dr. Mohamed Almekkawy is one of the best instructers in CSE department. Although his exam is super hard, but he drops 3 out of 7 quizes, 2 out of 5 coding labs and gave about 10% cruve( heard from friends because I only need 5% to get A) in the semester I took.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is one of the better professors you will have in your time at Penn State, makes the exams very difficult but the rest of the class is given as easy points and there is a large grade. Homework is setup in a way you actually learn and benefit from.

He's okay. Nice person, but mediocre as a professor. The online textbook zyBooks is required as homework reading, but it is really helpful and will teach you the entire course if you take the time to understand it. His labs have cryptic instructions that will leave you guessing most of the time, and his lectures are pretty useless.

Gives us a final project assigned on Tuesday of the last week of classes that is very long and hard. This is due the Saturday after finals. TAs are busy, students are busy and the project lacks a lot of details.

Good class, but would not suggest take it online. The video lectures are fine, but the labs are really hard if you don't have a TA to help you. Big curve till the end though, I have 69% and got curved to a B+

Mohamed does everything he can to try and explain the course material. The class was very difficult but mohamed curved the course at the end. He himself said that if you put effort into the class, there is no way you will fail. Quizzes and homework are a nice grade boost for the hard exams. Exams averaged in the 50s.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Do not take this class online. There are "video lectures" from years ago that are not up to date. The labs are very difficult and vague, review questions do not reflect quiz, exam has randomly scattered material that is difficult to do taking this online. Its difficult and weird to access office hours b/c no ones ever present. No idea whats going o

This class has brutal exams and quizzes, but you can tell Mohamed only does this to force you to learn. You wouldn't push yourself if you were getting 100% on every test, right? Work hard, get help, and it will pay off in the end with a generous curve. Mohamed is a great professor, as he truly cares about his students' success even beyond his class

He's a great professor. He very clearly cares about your success in both the class and in your future. He has a great energy which makes the classes more interesting to follow and uses many easily accessible analogies to clarify difficult concepts. It's a hard class but he's rooting for you.

Dr. Almekkawy was good at teaching, but the material and tests were pretty hard. Thankfully, if a certain percentage of your class does SRTE's, he drop a ton of stuff which makes it a relatively easy pass.

Professor Almekkawy gives great lectures and breaks concepts simply with great analogies. Lectures are recorded and posted online, as well. Exams are VERY LONG, but not worth that much. Averages are always low. STUDY FOR QUIZZES. Labs aren't too hard. There is a curve at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Mohamed is an awesome professor that really cares about his students education and grades. As long as you try you are going to be fine. He dropped 4 quizzes, 2 labs, and 2 HWs at the very end of the semester. The quizzes and exams are graded extremely generously and there is a curve at the end. My only complaint is that the lectures aren't the best

He is a really awesome professor!! Interesting lectures with lots of opportunities to get extra credit in lecture, and he is pretty funny. He also posts recordings of the lectures online in case you miss class or want to review the material later. A genuinely nice guy, and one of my favorite professors here at Penn State.

Mohamed is a great professor. You could really tell he cared about his students and their success. His grading policy is well thought out. He tries to insert some humor and real-world knowledge occasionally with jokes, personal stories and analogies which keeps a light atmosphere. Would highly recommend taking a course with him.

Dr. Mohammed is hands down the best professor in the EECS department, and the best professor I've ever had in my life. His lectures are articulate and well crafted, the analogies he uses makes difficult concepts easy to grasp. If you stick through the lectures and the labs you will truly understand how a computer works from the ground up.

He makes the class hard to prepare students for the work out of college. The tests are extremely difficult but not weighed as heavily. There are tons of assignments and labs. The labs make up a big part of the grade so you need to pay attention and learn for the labs. If you try your hardest and stay on top of the class, you will earn the A.

The labs / final project are challenging, but worthwhile. The exams are 40% of the grade and averages are < 50% so there is always a substantial curve. However it isn't applied until the end so your grade remains unclear. He cares, but his approach isn't always appreciated, like opting for Friday night exams or soul crushing exams.

The professor is very articulate during lectures and puts in a great effort to make sure every student understands the topic. The labs are challenging, but if they are started early enough, students should not have difficulty completing them. Attending the professor's and TA/LA's office hours is very helpful for labs and subject learning.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Overall, not a bad professor. Class is tough and it requires effort but the professor does try to make it more interesting. The class was timed awkwardly and so his lectures can make you drowsy, but if you pay attention, its not a bad class. Beware though, MT1 avg was 67 and MT2 avg was 38. He curves
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He cares about his students and replies to emails very fast. His lectures are kinda boring but will learn a lot if you pay attention. Labs are time-consuming. Exams can be challenging but he gives good grades.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--Caring

reviews.comment: First half of semester you will learn MIPS assembly, and the other half Verilog. If you have previous experience with either of the topics, you will do well. In my case I had experience with x86 assembly so I didn't struggle as much as others. Labs can be hard but there are enough resources online you can look up to.

He is amusing and seems to generally want people to do well. He explains things okay, but between the accent, questionably organized course material and mediocre lectures. Exams are much, much, much harder than the labs, homework, quizzes - Only the top 5 people in each class got above a 'C' on the exams.   Study hard for those.

Lectures are terrible. Claims to be accessible and helpful in office hours but every time I went, he told me to go to the TA's and would not help me. He posts review questions that have nothing to do with the quizzes. He tells you about labs one week in advanced, but it is always after office hours are no longer available. Poorly prepared
You will have the tough time on the lab but you will survive if you try.

Literally the best professor I've had here. First of all, he REALLY cares about the students. Even at the end of the course, I had a discussion about the course and how it could be improved and he still was interested in how much we all learned. He also does his best to give everyone good grades. TAKE HIM if you can, he's amazing.

Professor Almekkawy really cares about students. He understands the difficulties  that students face, so he tries his best to help students learn and give students good grades. Do what you are supposed to do then you will get good marks.

He's a really good guy, and he cares about his students. Sometimes, he'll tie in real world advice that isn't related to the class to prepare you for the future. You won't do well in the class without learning the material. But, if you do make an effort, the test(s) and quizzes are very fair. I'd recommend scheduling him over an alternative.
This is an easy A. You learned a lot by doing the labs and the project. The exam is pretty tough, but he will curve it. You'll learn a lot about computers in his class!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Sanders gets a lot of flack for being a tough grader or giving an intense course load, but her ability to genuinely teach a classroom is amazing. Incredibly personable, funny, insightful and always ready to help and discuss anything you bring to her office hours. If you just buck up a little bit, you'll find that she is an amazing professor.
Didn't read emails, unclear instructions, nice lady seemingly, strict..
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: She is very very tough, however I really enjoyed the material and lectures. She's was nice but didn't do much to help students. I did learn a lot about the First Amendment but definitely struggled at times. She only grades off of quizzes with 7-10 questions, give on paper with a limit of 10 minutes. A lot of what I learned stuck with me.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Awful. When you go to her office hours for help, she'd waste your time talking about herself, like how her mom wrote a book and we should read it and whatnots. Doesn't help the students at all. Tests have a 10 min time limit and there are lots of written responses, most don't have a clear answer so be ready to get points docked off for no reason
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The worst professor I've had. She forces students to buy a textbook SHE WROTE which costs $100+ and ends up barely using it in class. 50% of what she said during lectures won't show up on the tests. Tests are full of questions that don't even come up in the notes and videos we watched. No HW, grading is split into weekly tests and a final project.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: She was a nice lady but a terrible teacher. I firmly believe that she doesn't care if her students pass or fail….

I would not recommend taking this course. I will give her credit for being nice every time I have had to talk to her, even though she gives no structure or feedback. She basically wants everyone to figure out things on their own. Half of the class dropped, and the rest are struggling, which I don't think she cares.
The type of professor that doesn't want you to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Group projects

reviews.comment: Professor Sanders is top 3 worst profs I have ever had. She is rude, lazy, and does not help you in any way. Her feedback is often vague, and docs you points on papers without explanation. Every assignment has a template which you must use or she will doc 10 pts before even starting. She finds every way to doc pts on assignments rather than help.

AVOID HER PLEASE I BEG EVERYONE! This class was by far the hardest class I have had in undergrad. There are only two grades she enters in the gradebook, 60% exams and 40% final project and thats it. You have an exam EVERY WEEK that are not easy at all and you have to come to class or you are screwed. She treats you like you are a law student so RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
Amy Sanders was one of the worst professors I've had at Penn State. She was extremely unresponsive outside of class she never replied to a single email.
