What little feedback was provided was minimal and subjective. Also just a mean lady outside of class.

If you end up taking her, good luck and be prepared to figure most things out on your own.

I had a love/hate relationship with this course and this professor. Sanders is very nice in class, but as soon as class is over, she is rude. Any feedback received was mean and not constructive. She was impossible to reach out of class unless you go to her office hours which are usually only once a week. Expect many unnecessary papers due for class

She is really smart, but her intelligence doesn't translate to her teaching prowess. Tests are absurd, with class averages around a high D/low C range. No curve. Blames it on students. 95% overall is required for an A. The class high has never even reached a 95. Getting an A took luck and sleepless nights. Avoid if you can.

She's fine but not a very personable person. If you do the homework's and study for exams you'll be fine. She's not flexible with deadlines or anything so just make sure you follow the syllabus and do everything on time and correctly.

She genuinely cares about her students and what she does. If you do good on exam 1 and 2 you can average it out for your final which is good. Up to 15 points of extra credit. 5 homework, 1 presentation, and a team debate at the end of the semester. Every encounter is kind and caring. Flies through PowerPoints and it is hard to get everything down.
Prof. Amaya is excellent,idk why her ratings are so low. If you study well you can get good grades easily.

She is tough but honestly I respect it. Her lectures are fast but you get a cheat sheet on the exam, so they weren't bad in my opinion. Just graded on exams, homeworks, and a presentation and group debate. I don't think the reviews should scare you off

I was extremely nervous to take this class with Johanna Amaya by reading these reviews. But, with a week left in the semester I am confident to say I would recommend taking her. Don't get me wrong I struggled in the beginning of the semester, but I found my way and you easily can too. She cares for her students and the class is not bad at all.

Going to class does absolutely nothing, had to teach myself everything. You get a cheat sheet to use during exams and this saved me. No final if you do well on Exams 1 and 2 which is nice. Her lectures are way too fast and so much content. There are a lot of extra credit opportunities which help. Would take a different professor if available.
Knows her stuff, just goes rly fast

This professor is awful and is not clear on her instructions and she makes it difficult to do every project and has ruined my drive for the supply chain. Don't understand how she can't make the assignments more clear. Also don't even try to email her cause all of her emails will be rude and backhanded.  AVOID AVOID AVOID.

One of the hardest classes I've taken at Penn State. The tests were nearly impossible due to having to gather information yourself from 2-3 slide decks of at least 100 slides. She does give a study guide but it is basically the slides without the detail. I've heard other professors are better I'd take them.

Probably one of the worst professors I have had at Penn State. She flies through the slides and is unclear with information on the tests (For each test, there were around 150-200 slides of information). She is rude and seems like she does not want her students to succeed. Try to stay away.

I don't agree with these other ratings of Dr. Amaya. She is very accessible outside of class.  I went to office hours before every homework was due, and received a 105/100 on ever one. She is TOUGH, but if you try you should succeed. Not required to take final if you get above a 60 on first 2 exams, you can average grades for final.

I'm a Dean's List student and have never dropped a class (I'm a junior currently). This was the first time I have had to drop a class. Homework comprises of things she didn't go over in class. She flies through the slides and the exams have nothing to do with the slides. She also does not do exam reviews and is downright rude towards students.
She does not seem like her priority is for her students to do well. She flies through slides during class and often times comes across as just rude. Stay away.
Her lectures are pretty boring and she stops them if you go on your phone. Exams are super hard. Be careful to follow homework instructions perfectly.

She is really terrible. She's one of those professors who reminds you of a high school sub teacher.. she pauses when someone is on their phone and waits for them to finish (like what???). She zooms through the lectures with slides that don't even make sense and the homework assignments have content that were never mentioned in class. Stay away!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: she's dog water seriously like she can't take criticism and she easily is one of the most frustrating teachers ever. lectures are like unbearable because she goes so fast so you basically have to learn the content yourself. if you see her name, run away

I do not recommend this teacher for learning public speaking. Although the assignments are creative and engaging, the classroom environment feels discouraging due to harsh grading and sometimes rude feedback. The instructor often spends class time talking about himself or already skilled students, which doesn't help with growing skills.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Curtis was my very first professor at PSU and is still in my top 3. He gave me incredibly helpful feeback after every speech. I was incredibly intimidated by this class and I actually succeeded and probably wouldn't have done as well with a different professor.
This guy is the best professor I've ever had at Penn State, and it's not even close. Made me a better speaker and student.
Dr. Curtis is a legend. Miss this man.

- Very quirky and energetic professor, definitely cares for his students
- tough but not harsh grader, and in return he gives you very in-depth feedback after each speech
- quizzes every week or two but they are asynchronous and pretty simple
- just show up to class, make sure you practice your speeches beforehand, and you're good
never responds to emails

Dr. Curtis seemed intimidating at first but that is just because he is so passionate about what he does. I truly got better at public speaking and enjoyed going to class. He is clear with his expectations and not as harsh of a grader as I expected. He is open and shows he cares about his students.

I love this guy. He gives great feedback and personalizes responses to every student. He is such a funny and charismatic guy, and knows how to make you feel good about your presentation. Definitely take him!

Dr. Curtis is a great professor to have for a public speaking class. He exhibits all of the techniques he teaches throughout his own lectures. He is engaging and personable. He gives constructive, yet encouraging feedback on speeches. He wants so see you succeed if you put in the work. The class itself is easy if you do as you are supposed to.
Do your work properly and show up to class, you will do good in this class, make sure you practice your speeches overall great guy, super funny, definitely recommend him
Dr. Curtis has been my favorite professor here at Penn State so far! Super invested in students and your  performance in his class! I learned a lot and miss this class!

i was facing some hardness attending some classes instead of asking me he just blame me about that even i gave him some Seak leaves he told me that it is UNREAL!!! 

maybe he is a good person but he doesn't care about the student.

Professor Curtis is my favorite professor of all time! He's super funny and caring. Cannot see our time during the speeches and cannot go under/over 10 seconds without docking points. Just practice the speech and have a notecard. Easy weekly quizzes based on readings. His class made me flourish as a speaker.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: My favorite professor I've had here by far. While yes you only get 3 absences, I enjoyed going to his class and it never was boring. His lectures were absolutely amazing and if you read the rubric and follow what it says, he's pretty lenient so an A is sure to follow. Usually one quiz a week but they're open note and online. Take him for CAS100!!

I was dreaded taking CAS100. Glad I took it with him. He made the speeches much less nerve-racking than they could have been. Cool guy too. Cares about his students.

If you show up to class (attendance is mandatory) and are decently prepared for your speeches, it's an easy A. Quizzes are online and easy.
He's strict and requires more work than expected for a mandatory 100 level class. His humor and energy isn't for everyone but he does care a lot and can offer a lot of help if asked.

One of my favorite professors I've had a Penn State, overall great guy. I actually enjoyed going to class. As long as you go to class and put in the work, it's an easy A. Highly recommend him for Cas100A

Great lecturer, you won't be bored in his classes. Has exercises and mini-speeches to help you improve your speaking. Very helpful. As long as you follow the rubric, you'll be on track in his class. Make sure to ask questions after classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Best CAS100 professor 100%. He has the perfect balance of professionalism while also knowing how to connect and relate to students. He makes the speeches relaxed because he's so real about just getting up there and presenting like you practiced. With all of the advice he gives you, if you prepare well for a speech, you will succeed. Such a cool guy

THE MAN!!!! If you have the chance to take Dr. Curtis for CAS100, DO IT! He is the definition of a players coach - someone that truly wants to see you grow and learn, but also someone that everyone wants to play for.
How can I take a professor seriously that worships Kanye and he himself is a narcissist. Come on Penn State. Do better! However the class itself is got it's perks
Again, shockingly bad vibes about this dude being my professor something is definitely off about, he only has good reviews because he commands the students to give them

This prof is so bad he actually makes no sense the way his course policies are laid out he makes sure to give you a hard time when you miss class time for something like THON but will not show up to the next class and wait to send an announcement. DO NOT take a course with this guy. HORRIBLE. His outfits are also not that great.

Dr. Curtis was AMAZING!!! Yes, this was not the easiest class but he makes it so enjoyable. While the attendance is mandatory, I would actually look forward to lectures. Gives specific, personalized feedback that makes it easy to improve. Put the work in on the speeches and you'll be totally fine. Cannot recommend him enough!!!!

Dr. Curtis is THE BEST PROFESSOR I have had at Penn State so far. The man is hilarious, inspirational, knowledgeable, and every quality you could think of. 
Attend class, work hard on the speeches, do the quizzes, and have fun in his class. It is a challenging class (like every other CAS class) but here he makes it a fun environment for learning.
I would take his class again and that's coming from someone who hates public speaking. He makes it fun, requires respect in the classroom, and makes it a comforting space.
Very fun and self aware professor. I really enjoyed taking his class
Truly an awesome teacher who wants his students to succeed. Gives very entertaining and interesting lectures. By far the best speech teacher you could get at Penn State, Dr. Curtis is the man.

Dr. Curtis is THE BEST professor! He wants everyone to succeed and always tries to make the lectures engaging with his humor. There are times were you are put on the spot in his class, but it's actually fun. He is a little tough on the rubrics and always seems to teach the approach well after it is assigned, but overall he is an awesome teacher!

Dr. Curtis was probably the best professor I've had throughout my time at Penn State. CAS100A was the class I hated the most at the beginning, but ended up being the most rewarding class I've taken. He truly cares about his students and it shows. Follow the personalized feedback he gives you but if you slack or skip class you will fail.
