I have never been motivated by math and Amine has made me like Maths, He is a great teacher, always willing to help. Go to office hours, they are really helpful.
Amine is an excellent math instructor. He is very easy to understand, and cares about his students learning the material. Highly recommended.

The best 141 professor I could have asked for.  Still hated the class because of the material and it's high level of difficulty, but Amine is extremely helpful both in class and office hours.  Attend office hours if you can, that's where I got most of my help.
Best math teacher I've ever had! He is seriously the teacher you are looking for!!
Take a class with him if you can- great teacher

Amazing teacher with a willingness to help. He even offered to help me next semester with a class he isn't even my professor for. 141 is extremely difficult but if you go to his class and do the additional homework he assigns, you will pass easily. I would only take 141 with him as the professor.

Great teacher! Makes everything clear and gives well-structured notes. However, the homework is extremely time consuming and the quizzes are usually pretty difficult. This class is overall really hard and Amine makes it easier, but it is certainly not an easy class. Best at communicating compared to other Math 141 teachers. Def recommend
if you are thinking about taking this class with him, you better have a very strong understanding about multidimentional vectors. hardest class ive ever taken in my life
He is legit.

He's a good teacher make's it really easy to understand. No textbook but you have to buy and use ALEKS which is an online text-type thing. It's A LOT of work but easy to do for the most part. Attendance is somewhat mandatory cause he gives in class work thats graded.

He's a cool teacher. Clear explanations and tries to answer every question the students ask. Gives extra time when not ready for quizzes and homeworks and the attendance is not mandatory, though then you won't know when the quizzes are unless you ask a classmate. If you have the choice, take him. He doesn't answer emails but that's okay.
Nice teacher, clear presentation on materials which makes the course much easier
Committed, will answer homework questions, will look over your quiz and send you back to your seat to try again if he sees an error, will answer reasonable questions during exam.

Professor was unresponsive when I tried to discuss my grade, including a requested Zoom meeting. I submitted make-up work before final grades, but several assignments were left ungraded. I was told work was late, which conflicts with my records. Keep proof of submissions.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Never again

Hardest grader ever for an English class that's just GenEd. Even when her rubric says have a small audience focus and you actually limit to just your city or school, she still says your topic/audience is too broad. Don't take her course if you care about your GPA or do pass/fail if possible. Whatever was left of my confidence in writing is gone
pretty hard grader 3 3-4 page essays 1 7-8 page essay

she was the toughest grader I have ever had in an English class. She thinks that her way of thinking is the only correct way.There are 4 main projects and 2 VERY long discussion posts a week. Each post I made was equal to about 2-3 page papers. I love to write, but this professor made this class unbearable.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson is a very helpful professor and she wants all of her students to succeed. Take her constructive criticism from your conferences seriously and ask questions. If you listen to what she has to offer there is no reason why you should not get at least a B+.
Professor is nice and always willing to assist students.
Can't recommend her enough. She is one of the best teachers I have ever had. She really makes an effort to get to know the class and goes out of her way to help students as much as she can.
This class is hard if you don't show up. But otherwise Dr. Anderson is a great teacher. She genuinely cares about your success and gives you all the help you need.
amazing professor. I highly recommend taking her class.

She is a very kind woman who truly wants to help all of her students.  Sometimes I was really confused on what she was asking us to do for each paper because she has difficulty explaining it at times.  This class is not easy and she does grade harder than other english teachers at PSU.  Good Luck

At first, Dr. Anderson comes off as a difficult teacher. However, all she expects is that you pay attention in class and do what the prompt tells you. Sometimes her lectures are vague, but if you ask her questions she clarifies it. She is more than willing to work with you and help you succeed. She is also very passionate about English.

At first, Dr. Anderson comes off as a very hard professor. She says she expects a lot from her students, and if you only do what is required and do not go above and beyond, you get a C. I was an A student in high school and got A's on all my papers. As long as you go to her office for clarification and actually try, it's not that bad.

At first, I thought she was a hard grader and that English would be a challenge for me. But after getting a B- and getting A's the rest of class, it made me realize that she taught me well. You need to use your textbooks for class and read outside of class, but when she assigns a reading as homework, I never did it.

Dr. Anderson's ENG class is a challenge.  You will write 6 papers through the semester.  DO NOT be discouraged when your first score is around a C (even if you're an "A" student).  Be patient and LEARN.  She comes off as rude, but she really is a great professor.  Trust what she's teaching you and GO TO OFFICE HOURS FOR EVERY ASSIGNMENT!
Very knowledgeable and gives good feedback on essays. Be prepared to read several novels and defend your opinions in writing. Would take again, but not an easy prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Do not take this class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--So many papers

reviews.comment: Lots of reading - but it is worth it. Anekso helps give great feedback on work, and his lectures are always interesting. I would recommend this course to anyone interested in law. The moot courts are scary at first but are enjoyable and fun to be a part of when prepared.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He was very passionate about the material but went about it in the wrong way. Gave a lot of the students bad impressions due to his lack of being politically correct and constantly using outdated terms.

i know this is kind of controversial but i would absolutely take anesko again. super easy class structure- you have to read the texts and then are given periodical pop quizzes (but most can be answered by using spark notes or are more opinion based). the final was challenging, but he is super generous with grading. funny guy too. super dry humor
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The general structure of his class was getting assigned a book, then writing an essay about it. If you are good at writing essays then the course can be easy, but the books assigned are quite long and complex. He is a very good writer and is intelligent about English. He is not good at facilitating discussions in his class and most are dead silent.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed Professor Anesko. He does not let you get away with only a shallow understanding of texts and goes into depth about important concepts of novels that are seldom discussed. If he sees that you care in his class, you will be good. He is clearly an expert in his field and talks about literature in extensive ways that make this clear.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dreadful. Doesn't use Canvas and doesn't tell you your course grade (even if you ask) until you receive it in LionPath at the end of the semester. Does not give good feedback, and whenever I asked how I could improve my writing, he would never give any tips and instead just continue talking about the plot of book we were writing about.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This man makes me cry. Was expected to read 500 page books in less than a week and then write a paper on them in like 2 days. He chooses novels that were written in the 1800s, and it is super hard to build a relationship with him even though he requires 1-on-1 meetings for essay review. Super boring and painful lectures, literally take anyone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Having Mr. Anesko was awful. He does not teach anything he is supposed to in English 15 and would give little to no time to finish a multi-page essay. We were expected to read 500 page long books within a week or two. He never responded to emails and was near impossible to reach out of class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: His main issue is his inability to relate with students and form connections. The class is VERY different from the rest of the English 15 classes and is extremely essay-heavy. He also uses the n-word often in relation to the required novels, which can be uncomfortable for some students. Would not recommend this class - lots of unnecessary work.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This professor is intelligent and caring. He expects a fair amount of reading (we had to read 4 novels in a semester), which some students will need to adjust to. However, if you can keep up with the work requirements, the class is rewarding, thought-provoking, and worth your time. You will get out exactly what you put into the experience.

This professor is one to avoid. I hope he retires soon to make room for a better professor.

Boring, unable to read the room, and incapable of updating his material to meet the needs and interests of a new generation. Out of class, he is inaccessible and even erratic.
One of the worst professors I have had to date. I came to this university intent on pursuing a degree in English but am now looking to other departments after taking courses with Anesko.

This professor really makes you work, and that is not for everybody. He makes you work, but the work is entirely worth it. Go to his office hours. He is brilliant, kind, and caring. I have the perspective of having taken him a short while ago and still remember some of his quips and perspectives. Wanna learn? Take him. He makes you smarter.

Not a terrible class but not great. Definitely lecture heavy and pretty boring, especially with everything being on zoom right now. He grades pretty reasonably but some not very understanding sometimes. I got into a car accident and he never replied to my email, then commented on my paper that it didnt meet the criteriasir, I had a head injury.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: One of the worst professors I've had. He was not clear about what he was looking for in a paper. He became visibly upset whenever I asked about the grading scheme and clarification about my paper. He's not very accessible outside of class, so be prepared to figure it out on your own. I would avoid this professor at all costs!
A really great guy, hes really passionate and knowledgeable about literature. Make sure you read, he grades on participation and pop quizzes. If you read, youll do fine.

The amount of reading he assigns is unreasonable (14 books, with roughly four classes spent on each one... low-key impossible). His lectures are extremely boring as well. I'm an English major and I like the content usually but I could never pay attention to him. I will say that he is always open to helping and it's easy to get an A on his papers.

He's a really good guy and is extremely knowledgable. His lectures can be a little dry, but he does encourage participation (he will tell you you're wrong), but by the end of the first few classes you figure out what he wants. Pop quizzes, easily graded, SparkNotes the whole course. His final was easy except for the author identification.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: just show up and do the quizzes. You have to do the readings, I didn't a few times and still got 80's so it worked out. I talked to him at office hours once and he said that he doesn't really care about his students so don't expect any help from him. The class was 1hr 15 mins, a waste of my time. The final is a joke and half the class failed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Nice guy, knows the material well. Very smart. It's pretty boring stuff if you aren't interested in it but its doable. Reading homework every day and class is only discussions and random quizzes based on the reading.. quizzes are open ended prompts and graded pretty easily if he can tell that you know what the story is about.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Anesko had a different approach than other ENGL30 professors. He gave a poem every week and would have students write 2-3 page papers on them. Prompts were rarely given. He spends the first two days of the week on background of poem/poet. He goes over a random student's paper at week's end. Takes attendance weekly.

Mr. Anesko doesn't deserve the low rating that he has. If you have any respect for the knowledge of the world, you'll like his class. It is not that bad. He knows what he is talking about and will make you see the world in a whole new way (especially attitudes towards poetry).

As most people have mentioned, the class isn't the most thrilling. It's very easy to find yourself daydreaming, and realize you missed the last ten minutes of his lecture. That being said, if you even spark notes half of the books, you'll get an A. The pop quizzes can be frustrating, but he grades them generously and is a generally very nice guy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: I couldn't go to office hours to get help on papers because the papers were assigned and due after the fact. His critiques typically weren't that helpful with improving papers and you have to cater to his opinion while assessing the topic. Also, he doesn't believe is giving A's.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: You're gonna read a lot. Like a novel a week. 8 open-ended pop quizzes throughout semester, so you gotta know the books. Discussion was thoughtful and he knows his stuff, but it's so so boring. So boring. It's just the way he is. Mandatory attendance, 8 quizzes, final author identification exam. Typical lit class. You'll learn, but you'll be bored.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: Sooooooooooooo Boring.  He takes a Women's study class and makes it painful.  Like we start counting the minutes until the end of class the second we walk in.  The books he choses aren't great, and all he does is boring lecturewith very little class discussions (usually because he says our opinions are wrong.)
I feel so bad because Mr. Anesko really knows what he's talking about and seems really passionate, but the class was just so boring for me.  I can't tell if it was him or the class.

Wow what a guy. He's an incredible human being regardless of the reviews on here. I learned so much from him. He appreciates genuine interest in his subject and his breadth of knowledge (on just about everything) is astounding. And his sense of humor is great, if not too witty for everyone to understand. One of the hardest classes I ever took tho.

This is a great professor. Everything is discussion based and he really makes you think. The text which were chosen were awesome! I never had a problem going to this because it was very engaging. Totally recommend!

Do NOT take this class. Sure he's nice and it's not hard but literally the WORST professor I've ever had. Knows nothing about teaching and is so boring! Rambles for 45 mins about history and then mumbles through the text. Not hard class but not worth the pain of his lectures.

Mr. Anesko is the most incredible teacher I've had at Penn State. His class is extremely interesting if you actually READ THE MATERIAL. He's so intelligent and insightful. I don't know what everyone else is talking about but I've never seen him put a student down or say his or her answer is stupid. I can't recommend his classes highly enough.
Great selection of novels barring a few, interesting lectures, and fairly easy to do well if you write well.

Terrible class. Anesko means well, but he is much more cut out for teaching grad students if he should be teaching at all. Even if you manage to figure out the question he is asking, he shoots down your answer--no one wants to participate. Went to him several times for clarity on assignments and ended up leaving his office even more confused.

Nice, knowledgeable guy, but terrible teacher.  Worst class I've taken.  He launches right into the lecture 2 minutes before class actually starts, reads straight from lecture notes, requires a massive final paper AND exam, and generally bores you to death.  Better to delay graduation than take this course.

Horrible teacher.  Knows material but knows nothing about teaching.  Hides behind the podium.  Never even says good morning to the class.  Asks a question, waits for an answer, hears silence then answers the question himself.  Reads directly off lecture notes.  Not engaging in any way.  Made me really sad.

This class is a total drag - most boring lecturer I have ever seen.  He takes attendance sporadically so it's hard to tell when you need to come to class.  Papers are graded very easily, and you don't actually have to do the reading or participate, but still - so boring, not worth it unless you are good at doing other work while he's talking.

Yes, his class is a bit boring.  Often his lectures are prepared and read, but his 'speech' on the last day summing up the class almost made me cry--it was beautiful.  He's a really nice guy and he's, if anything, too generous when grading papers.  Helped me out with an extension.  Incredibly smart. I would take him again.

I am dropping this class as we speak. I was very excited for this class.  I love 20th century American Lit. But Anesko knows how to make it incredibly boring. His grading was easy, but it was impossible for me to read the books knowing every answer I gave in class would be "wrong" and that he would suck out any joy I got by droning for 3 hours.

Best accounting professor I've had. I get the monotone review, but it's difficult to make accounting not monotone and it's clear she tries. She only lectures 50% of the time and the rest is review questions to prep for exams or homework. She literally tells you exactly what problems will be on the exams and some of them you can have a notes sheet.

I mean, yeah the class isnt that hard. She tells us what to expect on exams and the practice materials are really solid. The only issue is the lectures that are just read word for word. Not the worst thing in the world, if you flat out skip the lectures and use the practice material you can score an A pretty easily. Class is super exam heavy though
Genuinely goated. Literally tells you what to expect on the exam and you can actually understand what you're doing. Definitely the best accounting professor I've had
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Not sure why she is getting flack, the classes aren't the most engaging, but she makes it very clear what to expect on the exams. Not only that, she offers easy in class points and provides more than optimal resource to know almost exactly what is on your exam.

This class summarizes what I would believe to be a vacation in Hell. The lectures are ripped directly off of McGraw, and read in a monotone fashion. In-Class assignments are the most dull and torturous experiences imaginable. Save yourself, God knows I wish I had.

Dr. Anderson definitely can come off some type of way, but she's one of the most caring professors I've ever met. Her classes are tough, but if you actually put in effort and use the resources she provides, you'll do fine.

Britanny wasn't necessarily a bad teacher- but she was very detached. It seemed like she didn't care much, and she just wanted to say everything as quickly as possible rather than really explain the concepts. The homework is pretty intensive, and you get graded by a short 1-2 question quiz each week. Don't procrastinate and you'll probably do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Attendance was the only reason I went to class and pretty much all of my learning was outside of class. She takes her job too seriously but her class isn't too much work if you study for the quizzes.

She is a very lazy professor, and constantly takes shortcuts when possible, which isn't acceptable in a subject like chemistry. Shows no passion for what she does. More times than not, you're sitting in lecture solely for attendance, and then going back home to teach yourself the material. She is also very short and passive aggressive. Avoid.

Professor Anderson does not provide clear guidelines for each assignment, expecting students to research independently on how to complete elements like outlines or drafts for lab reports. This approach makes the class difficult but encourages self-directed learning. If you're comfortable with this method, her class might be a good fit for you!

She goes over elementary problems during lecture, but the exams will consist of advanced problems. I would recommend solving practice problems from college chemistry practice books as the problems you see on the exam will be very similar.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I had to take her although I didn't want to, based on the reviews here and on friends that previously took her, and they were saying an exaggerated truth. The problem, actually, was exams were misleading. The questions were not covered directly or were barely mentioned. Tho I tried hard and actually knew the material exams just destroyed me.

A lot of negative reviews however she was fine. She may seem cold but she really isn't she is just professional. I would say that studying is very important in this class but also if you're confused on any topic, utilize office hours and email, she responds fast. To do well in this class, you must pay attention during lectures and attend them.
Terrible professor who makes Chemistry even more boring than it already is. Okay lectures, tougher than average tests. Don't take labs with her. If you have an option, choose someone else.
Best chem professor on campus, she is awesome. Really good at explaining the concepts so that anyone can understand them. She wants you to learn and understand.
Not a good professor. She's passive aggressive and it's not flexible. Doesn't believe in emergency, can't reason with her.

Dr Anderson is an average teacher. She takes lots of short cuts in her teaching and puts minimal efforts towards the class. I dont see any passion for chemistry in her. In the lab she is very distracted, especially talking to the lab supervisor always. We had a lab accident this semester while they both were chatting; I would never take her again

She doesnt clearly state what she asks for on the lab reports. She puts hints on how to do it on the board along with complex examples to follow, but with new minds in class to the subject few know what to do and how to do the work. The labs are easy but she is a really tough grader so be careful. The hardest part is said lab reports.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr Anderson was one of my favorite profs, I probably ended up skipping one class out of three a week and still got a A- in the class. Shes very helpful out of class and the tests are just like the study guides but different numbers and a few extra questions, and the quiz in recitation you take every week, she goes over it exactly the week before.

Dr. Anderson is a great teacher. If you are struggling and need help she will make sure you understand the material. She cares about her students if you take time to put effort into the class. She gives examples during class time and during recitations she goes over the topics covered in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Anderson is a nice woman, but you really need to teach yourself outside of class. It seems like she moves on from one thing to the next in lecture and doesn't give you time to try practice problems yourself and just goes through them on her own. There is a quiz each class period that can be on anything and her exams are not like the practice.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I want to help my fellow Penn State colleagues, because we are paying stacks for this education. Do not buy the games, use wikipedia and go on youtube and look at the comments about a game, that's where it's at. It is an easy A as compared to the weed out courses, but you can find better.

While it is an easy A, trust me it's not worth the aggravation. Molly finds a way to infuriate me each day with another pointless discussion about something that really does not apply to video games. I really didn't think it was possible to make video games boring, and I was wrong.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: have fun getting assigned more than 3 things for each class..... she would give us super long readings that weren't at all important to the class
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: If given the option to rate her class as a 0, I absolutely would. I have more work in this class than I do for my major courses. Class is mandatory and it will negatively impact your grade if you don't attend. She also makes you purchase over $150 in games, only to discuss them in class for 5 minutes. Please take this class with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: If you are taking CMLIT191 with her, prepare to be bombarded with at least 3 assignments due each class. On top of this, there are 4 projects. This is a General Education course, covering GH with US. I have more work in this class than I do with all of my major-geared classes combined. If you want to take this class with her, please reconsider.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: You will have a paper due bi-weekly for the most part. There are always assignments due and journal entries to complete. Professor Appel is a young professor and is so kind and helpful. I really enjoyed having her as a professor. She gives great feedback on papers and the rest of her assignments are pretty easy. There is a final project.

She grades papers based on what she wishes you had done not what you actually did. There were also journal assignments (10 to be exact) that were more annoying than helpful. She is a grad student and still believes in the book and pennstatements, ugh.  She is not very clear in her explinations for papers, but she is willing to help at office hours.

Let's be fair here.  It's not Apfelbaum's fault that the course is so bad.  He actually does a good job.  The real issue is with the text and the tests.  The questions are irrelevant to anything related to a college class and are irrelevant.  For an INART class, the questions should be more direct and relevant.  But it's not the prof's fault.

This is the hardest class I've taken in college.  The exams are not about understanding the material but about trying not to be tricked with wording.  Also, there is no feedback as to why points are lost on writing assignments.  Overall, this class is taught as if it was part of your major instead of an elective.  Even if you like punk, don't do it

Not an easy A unless you're really into how hip-hop came about.  SO much reading every week.  Pretty crazy essay topics but not hard to do well on.  Honestly wouldn't recommend this class.  Joe was super nice (through email since this is an online course).  No hate fro Joe, just this course.
Worst class I've ever taken in my life. So much extraneous reading that goes towards nothing. Don't take this class; it's a colossal waste of time.

This was an awful class. Didn't think it would be too hard, turned out that it was my worst class. Chapters are very long and the questions on quizzes and exams are very specific. Don't think that you can just google all the answers. Ended up being my worst grade of the semester and I'm a decent student

Terrible class, definitely do not take. Course content was very boring and the online textbook is poorly written. Like absurdly poor. Apfelbaum himself is mediocre (not outright bad) but there's not really much he can help you with since there are no concepts to learn, only inane, repetitive, forgettable facts.

This is was the hardest online class ever. Tests and quizzes are very detailed and so specific that if you don't have amazing notes (that include everything) you won't pass. The worst questions are when he gives you one word in a question (like a name etc.) and you have to know whether one answer is correct, two of the above of all of the above.

I thought Inart 126 would be an easy A (its online and hip-hop) and while I got an A it was a lot of work. Papers had 65 average but do a unique topic and put some effort in and you'll be fine. Quizzes need to be done with someone else. Copy the text into a word document and search for it, only way to pass. Definitely take class with friend...

I loved Alyssa. She was super helpful with all assignments and is always willing to answer questions. There is a weekly quiz, but they are easy if you study and a lot of them ended up being open book anyway. She gives you good feedback on your articles and tells you exactly what needs to be fixed.

The course itself is annoying, but it's required for COMM majors. Appelman is hardly helpful, and made me feel like she doesn't have any interest in helping her students succeed. She is not understanding of personal situations.

It's horrible because it's a horrible class, but she did about as good a job teaching it as she could. The material you go over for the quiz is really direct, and the quizzes aren't too terrible if you don't rush through them. She makes a bad class as palatable as possible.
She made a tough environment as easy as she could. An online classroom can be tough, but it gets easy once you adjust. I recommend taking her.

She is a grad student with no idea what she's doing.  This is an online course that is overly complicated.  You would think it is easy but it certainly is not and, Alyssa does nothing to combat this.  She directs any questions or help you would need to the writing center.  Overall a completely useless teacher.
For one she's beautiful. That's always a plus when staring at someone for 16 weeks. Her class is wonderful all you have to do is open your mind and participate, an A+ will be at your fingertips.

Kikora is awesome! I've taken just about all of her classes and she is so passionate about her work it's ridiculous. As long as you show the slightest effort, you will do amazingly. It's as simple as that.

Very Passionate! She doesn't "embarrass" kids. She makes corrections to people out loud in front of the class. If your shy, you might not like this class. It's nothing personal, she just wants you to do your best. I wasn't the best dancer and she was very encouraging to me. As long as you give your all, you will be fine.
Great Instructor. She does not expect everyone to be the best, however she wants you to try your best. If you are dedicated and give 100% you will get a good grade. And attendance is a big thing!

Very good teacher.  She has a passion for dance and makes classes fun.  If you love to dance this class will be great for you.  She expects you to try your best and you'll get an A.  The dance are a lot of fun too.
No Comments

You will get a good grade as long as you go to class, but this teacher picks on kids in front of the whole class and is extremely demanding considering she teaches a 1-credit dance class.  She goes out of her way to embarass students.  I would never have taken this class if I knew what it would be like, and I really like to dance.
Amazing professor, he should come Nepal his country and makes lots of Human capital
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: He has slides and very clear notes for you to review. If you could be familiar with all the homework and practice problems, you well get high score in exams. lots of chance to earn bonus credits, generous curves, need some basic calculus..
Good teacher

all cared for grades, while he did not!! Knew everything but demanded lots from students in terms of their capabilities. Was extremely friendly and helpful outside the class. I liked the class and learned too. Ideas I learned helped me excel other classes.

reviews.comment: I enjoyed taking Dr. Bagyan's class. She is a very good lecturer and explains things well. Her exams aren't too difficult, and she lets you have a cheat sheet for them. She doesn't reply to emails very well, if at all, but she is a very good professor.
You have to study a little bit, but I thought the course materials were organized and easy to learn.

Get ready to hear "lets start the class". Speedruns through the lectures, does not post lectures notes online so if you miss class, you have to know a friend. Responds to email at her own pace, very strict with deadlines and marks you on the homework for every little mistake. Takes over a week to release quiz grades that are already graded.
Honestly refusing to post the notes is kind of silly. I'm still not coming to class anyways. Piss easy tests though. (418)

Refuses to post notes online. If you miss class, she says read the textbook and won't help you in any way. If someone asks a question in class, she says "does anyone want to answer that" and if nobody does, she says "you guys should review that then" then moves on without answering the question.

Loved her. You don't need to buy the textbook and class not mandatory. Her in class notes are better than reading the textbook and the practice problems in class are the best for practicing so I would say go to class.

Not a great professor, doesn't even answer emails. Doesn't post any lecture notes online so if you miss a class because you are sick it pretty much sets you up to fail. Just an absolute terrible class

Had a great time with this class as it was pretty straightforward with no surprises. Dr. Bagyan was a great professor who was always able to answer any questions. Make sure you attend class to complete the guided notes as they are not posted online. Exams are good and you can have a cheat sheet and calculator.

Only bad thing is a thick accent, but manageable.Textbook online with free practice problems but unnecessary. The lecture notes very comprehensive and you get to bring cheat sheets to exams which makes it pretty easy if you just put all the formulas on it. She tries to help students/get to ask questions. extra credit question on every lab and test.

Guided notes are given and covered in class but are not posted online so don't skip class. Weekly homework and short quizzes but the homework starts to get hard towards the end of the course. Midterms are in class which is pretty annoying because you only have 50 minutes. Tests are hard but she grades pretty leniently and there is extra credit.

I didn't like the code we used and how she assumed we knew certain things she never taught. Other than that, she was a good professor with lecture heavy classes. If you do all the homework you will pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is not a chatty professor. Lectures are straight-forward and she rarely stops for questions. Notes are posted but can only be filled in by attending lectures. Lots of homework and weekly lab does make it a lot sometimes but she is very accessible for office hours. Genuinely wants people to succeed in her class. Exams are easy but final is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I actually enjoyed her class. She has a few quirks with how she runs things that can be annoying, but she is actually a pretty good prof, I learned a lot. HW & labs are almost exactly like in-class examples, and so are exam questions. There are weekly labs and HWs, but if you complete it all, you'll be fine. I'd take another one of her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr. Bagyan overall was a great instructor for STAT 401. I suggest you show up to every lecture or if you do not make a friend in the class. Grades very easy, gives a lot of partial credit on the tests. HWs very easy and take 1-2 hours at maximum each week.

If you take this class, be prepared to work! The way her class is structured is every week there is Homework, Quiz, and sometimes a Lab. I would highly recommend downloading or printing out her lecture notes before the start of class! Her exams are also fairly easy, she allows you to bring cheat sheets to the tests which are very helpful.

She is very impatient and her notes are bizarre. She'll give questions in class only for time to run out and she won't even reveal the answer. Then she'll post the answers online with zero context or explanation. Do not take her and avoid her like the plague.
This woman did not post any annotated notes but only during class. Her notes are the most illegible writing I have seen in my life. She never curves the class when her exam averages are low.

Bagyan obviously knows the material, but moves through lectures quickly. If anything, both class and the textbook made the material more convoluted than it needed to be. If you cant avoid her class, the lesson notes posted to the department page will be your savior.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: No recording, notes posted online and less study material.

I got both A from STAT414/STAT415. 105/100 in both final exam. Get ready to take notes. Exams were not too bad with your cheat sheet. It is crucial to take notes from class. However, she did not reply my message for recommendation letter haha.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: You CAN learn stuff with her. She is strict, but gives detailed explanation and examples during lecture. She also answers questions after classes or during the office hours. Pay attention and take good notes. You are supposed to read textbook every week, but I skipped it. 1 homework with 8 or 9 problems and 1 quiz with 5 problems per week.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Prof Bagyan has made a relatively difficult class into a nightmare. Classes are not recorded and just give you bare basics of content while homework is difficult. Quizzes and exams require an advanced understanding of the concepts while providing a short time. One of the worst profs I've taken in my life. Do not recommend to anybody that likes life

Dr. Bagyan does not have very good lectures, all you do is practice one or two problems that you do not fully understand. Then you go into pointless breakout rooms where most people wont talk and the class is over before she gives solutions. Also the average on MT2 was an F and MT1 had a low D as the average. Try another prof at all costs!
Study ahead is the key to success in her class. The average of the second midterm is around 50 out of 100. Some may prefer her way of teaching, but obviously, most don't.

Personally, the concept gets more and more obscure. It gradually becomes necessary to read books if you really want to know what is going on. Her lecture is mediocre, which is reviewing the concepts and doing questions and breakout room. If you study ahead, that would be helpful. Still don't know if she will curve (probably not).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: She is very strict but potentially pursues perfection so that she requires students to learn her materials as carefully just as she did to us. No recorded lectures and no curve, but its another way to force us to study materials well. With her notes, homework and participation in her class, you can survive well in this course without the textbook.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: useless lecture and hard exams.
Try not to take any course with her.

Dr. Bagyan is definitely a difficult prof to have and the content itself is just extremely difficult to understand sometimes. Although she can be unreasonable sometimes, if you're confused and need help, go to office hours. She is much more helpful during office hours. Her homework and quizzes also are really good for testing your knowledge.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: The lectures were slightly helpful; the first 35-ish minutes are a review of content and rest were useless breakout rooms. She recorded lectures, but then took them away out of spite when attendance dropped right before Thanksgiving. Overall, the content isn't super difficult, but you're not doing yourself a favor by taking her section.

Probably the worst decision to took her class again. The course material wasn't hard but she made this course so hard. The time for quizzes was too strict this semester and I hate that some questions required unreasonable calculation provided the time given. Her lecture wasn't bad, but better to avoid choosing her if

I learned nothing. You just plug and chug. The quizzes and exams have trick questions and new problems, so even if you ace the (ungraded) homework, you can still fail easily. The subject really interested me coming in, but Bagyan can't teach it, and her class makes me hate statistics now.
2nd time taking her. Gets exponentially worst. Similar to the sequence of events in 2020.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Feedback need more than 3 days to get, too much homework
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: This is a cookbook class and one of the easiest 400-level math courses at PSU. As a math major, I was disappointed with how a lot of theory and proofs were omitted, but in turn, this made the remaining material trivial. Yes, she gives hefty homework, but I opine that it adequately prepares you for the exams. Exams are plug-and-chug, no trick Q's.
She teaches you to crawl and expects to you win a marathon. I'll regret taking this class with her.

unreasonable amount of questions for the exams. 11 questions in 50 minutes. These questions require multiple steps and sometimes multi-variable integration, which alone takes up a lot of time. That can be very frustrating because you'd end up doing badly not because of your lack of understanding, but the unreasonable time limit for the exam.

Dr Bagyan can be bored sometimes but she knows what she's talking about. This course was not meant to be easy at all, you need to work for it and I think her homework and quizzes really reinforced my concepts. In this class i feel like i actually learned something but if you want easy A then not the best choice
She's the best stat teacher ever! She's so patient and good at her work. Always hope to take her class again!

She can be very unreasonable. I understand professors have policies to follow but she has been extremely unaccommodating towards the needs of students when classes converted online. If you'd ask me, she went at a faster pace after classes converted online.

Dr. Bagyan is no doubt knowledgable in statistics, but she is terribly unaccommodating when it comes to her students. When the averages for exams and quizzes are F's, she will explain that it was the entire classes fault for not preparing well enough and refuse to curve. Do not take this class if you want to maintain a good GPA.

When classes converted online, she is the only professor I know who did not change the syllabus at all to accommodate to the tough environment during this tough time. She clearly stated the 1credit  3hours of study but her homework alone takes that amount of time. Avoid at all cost because you will be stuck stranded if something unexpected happens

The course material is difficult and she does not make it any easier. The exams excel the level of difficulty found in the textbook which means you need to have complete understanding of the material to get a passing grade. Class averages on a couple exams were below 70%. She seems nice and willing to help if you have a question.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This class is very difficult, but Dr. Bagyan is intelligent and good at teaching (also a bit intimidating). There are some extra credit opportunities, but the class is not curved. There is homework and a quiz each week and they are helpful for studying for the exams. Be prepared to work very hard in this class, but you will learn so much!!!
She is an amazing professor, but she is the most hardest stat professor in terms of her exams and assignments.
The class is not too bad if you familiar with conditional probability.

The course is not easy, but it's not her fault. Mandatory discussions are quite annoying, though. Anyway, she's a fair grader and gives partial credit. If you study, getting an A shouldn't be a problem, especially with the extra credit she offers.

The exams are super hard and they syllabus is immense. The class is already super hard, on top of that being taught by this prof. Please avoid taking her at all costs! Doesn't take hw late even if you had some serious problem going on
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Her lectures are pretty bland but they are better than reading the textbook. The exams make up the vast majority of the grade, and midterms are during class so you barely have time to finish. The homework is graded very harshly (blank answers lose more points than the question is worth) so make sure you start it early in the week.
She makes you work for it. She substitutes your lower midterm grade by the final grade if your final grade is higher than that exam. Tons of homework; usually took 6 hrs to solve on a weekly basis.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Bagyan is one of the best professors I've ever had at Penn State. Although many people seem to think she is a tough grader, this is not the case. Stat 414 and 416 are theory classes requiring you to have firm knowledge of the material. So don't take this class expecting an easy A! If you do all the work required, you will do very well in class.

Very hard online class with a lot of homework and exams that are difficult to finish in time. Exam questions are harder than HW, so you have to be really prepared. Fair grader, though, with partial credit. She was not prompt grading exams or answering questions, which is really frustrating - you will end up needing to figure things out yourself.

DO NOT TAKE ANY CLASS WITH HER EVEN WHEN YOUR LIFE DEPENDS ON IT ! She's the worst person to take any STAT elective with, her classes are boring, she's too picky about grading, and assumes we don't have any important class but hers. She's too harsh on midterms, especially on final. HW's and tests are inconsistent. WORST CLASS OF MY LIFE!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: This class isn't easy. Homeworks take about 5-6 hours per week if you want to understand. Understanding hw is the only way to do well. Exams take the full time given and are similar in difficulty to hard hw problems. Go to office hours. She helps! them. Test grading was fair, though, with reasonable partial credit given if you make a mistake.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This professor does not quiz/test on the material in the HW. You spend HOURS of HW each week, to no avail. Also, her exams are timed and she will do evil things like put double integration involving integration by parts TWICE on a timed test. She knows students struggle to finish within the time limit and she will not adjust her exams.
She is demanding and expects a lot from her students. She does know the materials well. Class can be boring sometimes and homework is not easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She always looks so mad.
This professor wants you to fail.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: I have to agree with some of the others on here. Do not take this instructor's course! She gives huge amounts of homework and then the quizzes have little to do with the all of the problems that you spend hours working on. Please find another instructor if you are taking STAT 414.

An online instructor's job is to answer questions and manage assignments/exams. She's fine at both - patient with questions, thorough answers, extra credit opportunities when exams skew low. Very reasonable exam grading and question difficulty, but she does make exams long to test fluency, so do problems beyond the homework assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Let me preface this by saying I got an A in the course so i'm not a disgruntled student. She takes herself way too seriously and doesn't provide any leeway. Took her class online and she was not helpful. Would really recommend taking another professor. Also, a lot of tedious homework that doesn't prepare you for the quizzes or exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: She expects a lot out of her students. There is a ton of homework... doesn't prepare you for the exams though. If you are having a hard time, don't expect any help. she just doesn't care. She does know the material however, so if you're someone that makes little to no contact with the professor and just need the grade, then she would be a good fit.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Good course, though the lectures tend to get boring.
great professor

Her accent is really strong, but she seems to have a very good understanding of the material. Her teaching style is pretty standard for a lecture based math class. I had this class at 8am, and that was really pretty hard to stay awake for. Also if no one answers her questions during class, she'll tack on extra homework, so stay sharp!

Sadly I must agree that a tutor is needed.  The instructor would disappear for weeks at a time and sometimes did not even answer a posted question.  Homework feedback consisted of a posted answer key, so if you didn't understand the problem in the first place you posted a question...which might not get answered until after the quiz.

Be prepared to spend hours on meaningless work that only gets a cursory glance. She makes it much harder than it needs to be. Buy the book and get a tutor because no help from her. Better yet - take someone else.

Teacher was very helpful and responsive until the last four weeks of class when she and the TA were nowhere to be found. Class and material is difficult but reasonable. Must keep up with work, be willing to work independently, and often complete extra homework problems to understand the material on quizzes.
Hard Class. This teacher could honestly care less whether you do well or not. Defintly suggest takign another prof.
She has a very good understanding of the material.  She has a strong accent but it does not make it hard to understand what she is saying.  Extremely helpful during office hours.

She is a great teacher, she is demanding but fair. She likes questions from students and gives clear explanations. She is very helpful in office hours. If you do the homework and go to class you'll be fine.

Dr. Ashley always made sure that we felt comfortable and supported in class. She tries to keep this class as light as it can be so you are not anxious to present. If you put in the work and follow directions on the assignments, you will succeed in this class.

Worst and most immature professor I've ever had. Complained about everything constantly and it was somehow always the class at fault. The quizzes were on bizarrely random facts from a random sentence, you needed to know word for word from a long chapter of reading. Overall it was fine, and easy enough, but worst class to sit through
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Although she is strict, she is a really good professor. Didn't like her at first but she is one of my favourites now. Gives amazing feedback and is always happy to help further. Quizzes are a bit annoying but not too bad. and gives extra credit just for going outside your room basically.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Dr. Ashley is the best professor I've ever had. She is very strict about her no-electronics policy, but once you learn to get over it and pay attention to her lectures, they are strong, powerful, and moving. I highly recommend taking it with her if you want to get something out of this required class.

Dr Ashley is nice and hilarious, but she goes by the syllabus, expecting us be prepared for pop quizzes and is a tough grader. Therefore, I am further stressed from the amount of zeros I have for the course. Plus, she has the grades display disabled.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Dr. Ashley was nice and her grading was reasonable.  It was an easy class as long as you do the work.

While Dr Ashley seems nice, her methods of grading and teaching are subpar. She grades quite harshly and prioritizes certain students over others. Many things are left to the last minute and speech weeks always clashed with my major's exams.
She was amazing
very poor communicator outside of class, lectures are lowkey disorienting as she speeds through material and her handwriting is very hard to read on the board
It feels like watching her do math is very scrambled. It's hard to follow each step and she moves way too fast. Her accent makes it hard to understand at first, but you get accustomed.
Very hard to understand her accent. So much homework, if you're not in class you will not pass.

Took CRIM 100 as a 7-week online course in the second half of last semester with her, it was great. Exams were in person in Pollock but honestly just know the Vocab for those and you should get at least a high B. Class was pretty quick and easy, she was great at communicating for an online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Class is a mix of exams (ONLY lecture content so not very hard), a paper (annoying but not graded harsh), discussion boards (also not graded harsh), and MindTap quizzes (annoying but the info is in the book). She's very nice and makes good study guides for the exams. I personally didn't like the MindTap/discussion board format of the class but eh.

She is AMAZING!!!! The test are so easy if you memorize the exams. All the quizzes can be found online, but you take A LOT of notes. I also got so sick during the semester and she was so kind and accommodating.

Took her 7 week Crim Class
Class is very manageable, her study guides for exams are godsend, do those and this class will be a breeze. 
Would recomend, great professor.
She is an amazing professor! Everything is super straight forward and the exams are really easy. Interesting class to take as well!
Goated professor. Take her if you can. She is very educated on the topics and teaches in a way that makes it understandable to us. She also does cool things like bring in cops, agents, etc.
She really cared about her students and answered any questions you had. The homework isn't hard and will take maybe two hours a week.

Dr. Yinger has been a great professor throughout the semester, and I plan to take her again in the spring. She makes the course pretty easy if you put in the work, her lectures are also pretty interesting. The exams are easy as the class usually has above a B average at the lowest. She's accommodating and understanding as long as you reach out.

She is a very nice lady and super understanding! There are 4 online exams and a final paper/project. Attendance is taken through top hat but is not a big part of your grade. Just note, if you are not interested in Criminal Justice than this class will bore you to no end...however, its a free "A"!

best professor I've had hands down. will work with you and will engage in class.
wish she could teach all-level crim
 would recommend 100%
ONE OF THE BEST PROFESSORS AND IF YOU WANT TO TAKE CRIM100, TAKE IT WITH HER

Dr Yinger is amazing. Her CRIM 100 class was extremely enjoyable and her examples from her career made the class even more easy to understand. The quizzes and homework assignments are easy to do and don't take long. Definitely take CRIM 100 with her!
Truly one of the best professors I've ever had. Her assignments are easy and she's very flexible if you need to turn in assignments past the deadline.

Professor is great! Attendance is taken but in syllabus not for a "grade". 
Lectures not mandatory, slides posted to canvas . Cengage + Packback are required which are, $60 to $90 each. Cengage is weekly 25 point quizzes which can be taken with the text book. Packbacks were due every Sunday. Homework/due dates are consistent!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Dr. Yinger is an amazing professor, by far one of my favorite ones I have had. Aside from her being incredibly nice and understanding, she knows her field very well. She is happy to answer any questions and her class was something I looked forward to attending. Please take her if you have the chance.

I had to take criminology for my major. It was her first year at university park after teaching at another campus and she did amazing! Her class was the only class I looked forward to. Understanding w/ due dates/kept class interesting. Attendance not mandatory, you always got out early, she barely gave hw. Overall I would take another class by her!

This was her first year at Penn State and I loved her. There are no exams but there is a final. Attendance isn't mandatory but it definitely helps if you go to class. All the assignments/quizzes are online and open note. As long as you do the work you'll get an A/B. She also has experience in criminal justice so I liked having her as a professor.

Please if you are seeing this FIND ANOTHER PROFESSOR like your life depends on it. This is by far one of the worst professors I have ever had. She constantly changes the assignment guidelines, and miss uses art vocabulary. This a 2D fundamental class, and our final is a 3D relief. She refused to acknowledge a relief is a sculpture.

Genuinely one of the worst art teachers, constantly changes her mind on what projects are about, when they are due, what medium they are, whether it's a group or solo project. Is constantly on a power trip and takes everything personally, even minor comments about her class. Is super particular about what the projects are like, her way or fail.

Genuinely the worst person who has ever tried to teach me art. Everything has to be done HER WAY and with HER IDEAS. Her favs would finish late and still get 100, but we wouldn't get 100 even if our work was done on time and genuinely better. The class was more about appeasing her than learning art.  The entire class hated her.

The class wasn't too difficult, but you have to do things HER way. She will take off points and not clearly explain why. She seems like a caring professor, but her methods were questionable. Also the amount of materials needed for this class was insane. Spent over $200. She is also very last minute and tends to switch deadlines around

As long as you put in effort outside of class you will probably be ok. She is not very clear with what she wants on most assignments and is very particular on what she looks for. Pay attention to almost everything she says in class because she changes things like requirements for assignments and sometimes due dates and will not update canvas.
Truly passionate about the curriculum and provides very thought provoking material to the students. I would highly recommend taking his courses!

PLSC 210N *Through the World Campus* is EASY, I've heard it's a tough class in person (in person has exams). As long as you write long discussion board posts (doesn't even have to be good) you get full credit, + if you actually try for your essays you'll get a high grade. Trust me, this is the easy online interdomain class you've been looking for.

I accidentally did the wrong asn- 3 hour movie & 5 page paper to realize by midnight that I actually did a future assignment, instead of turning in what was due. I wasnt harshly graded at all or given a zero, but I made sure to communicate. Hit ALL the objectives listed in the essay instructions, and STUDY HARD for tests-this class is worth it.

If you would like to learn the legal system through John Grisham's novels and movies, then this is the instructor for you. He has you watch movies with legal themes or ones that depict trials and essentially wants you to review them. It's a waste of time for anyone entering the legal field or criminal justice system.

Very easy class, just do the work on time. Class is online, so all quizzes (no exams) are open book, but they require understanding of every SCOTUS case which feels over-the-top. Can be a little difficult grader on essays, but if you're competent, then you'll get +90 on each one. Just make sure to do the discussions on time.

I don't know if Dr. Atkins would see this but he is an amazing professor. I had trouble submitting work on time due to work and obligations with the military, but nevertheless he was very understandable. Additionally, he allowed me to submit all work before the end date for final grades submission and I went from a very low F to a passing C!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Very nice professor, eager to help. 4 papers, 3 quizzes, and discussion posts. Quizzes are difficult, but doable as long as you read before you take them. The course is very reading intensive. Overall, great guy and you will learn a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Good professor expect for the fact that the quizzes were ridciuoulsy hard. I had 100's on everything and I was getting 70's on the quizzes.  He needs to give a study guide for the quizzes because they cover a lot of info. The quiz questions are very detailed and the time limit is also annoying. Really upset that I had 1 thing bringing my grade down
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: World Campus grad. Took 2 classes with Dr. Atkins. He uses multi-media; knows how to run an online class to keep it from becoming a boring grind; writes detailed instructions for the 4 papers he assigns; gives personalized feedback. Took 3 FT semesters at WC, Atkins was most competent professor I encountered. Must read the assigned work to pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Tons of reading and writing, but none of it is superfluous. You'll learn a lot. Professor knows what he's doing. If you don't read, you won't pass. If you read you'll do great. You can tell he's been doing this a long time, and even online there's no room for shortcuts in this class. Avoid if you're that type. Class is so worth it if you're not.

Recorded lectures are great. The text is essential and you WILL be reading, A LOT. I cannot stress that enough..... READING ASSIGNMENTS ARE PLENTIFUL. Professor gives excellent feedback on your work and as long as you make the changes he suggests, the class is easy. 4 or 5 papers, discussions on those weeks when there is no paper. Good class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: The feedback he gives on papers is usually very unclear. Vague instructions on assignments. Requires documentation to make up missed assignments. Would not recommend him unless you are a Political Science major or minor.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Atkins made this course relatively easy. You will read two books cover-to-cover but both are interesting enough to get through. There are four papers and three quizzes to complete but other than that most of the homework is discussion board posts. Quizzes are timed so be prepared on the material.

Took his 471 and 472 classes the same semester (they complemented each other nicely). Classes were paper-heavy but he grades them fairly easily. Topics were pretty interesting so they were actually fun to write. He's a very reasonable guy. He gave me an extension with no due date when I got ill. Also gave a generous curve at the end of the semester
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: The course model is typical; quizzes, discussion posts, short essays, midterm, and final exams. Much of the textbook reading is upfront and important for subsequent material. The course covers the evolution of rights in America. Dr. Atkins is extremely approachable and appears to care about student success.

You can pull through discussions and essays as Dr. Burton is very liberal with marking. But at least 5 hrs of dedicated study weekly is needed to crack quiz. No quizlet or book will help you unless you read the judgments. You cannot escape reading volumes to pull a A. Very very informative and exciting way of teaching. Movies, videos, discussion

Professor Atkins was respectful, caring and genuinely interested in the success of his students. There is A LOT of reading! (2 books, articles, court cases & MOVIES) He will provide you with links to what you need. Follow the paper guidelines! Touch on and describe each topic he suggests and you will get an A! Post discussions on time!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Straight forward stuff here, not difficult, just do the work. He's not interested in nuances or out of the box thinking, hit the objective points and move on. One downside is he doesn't give feedback on grades. Even with a few points off, I like to know how to improve, but then you feel like an idiot having to email to request notes.

Prof. Atkins is a good, accessible instructor. Clear in directions and fair in grading, thought PLSC 471 is more interesting than 472 (he teaches both). Substantial number of essays, easy quizzes if you do the reading, and a nicely-paced course. I did not like the textbook for this class, though - boring. Overall enjoyed the class + professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Very good lectures to outline and follow up with the readings. Very receptive to questions. Very pleasant disposition.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: He was very clear about what was required to succeed in his course. Atkins responded quickly to emails and graded assignments in a timely matter. I am taking him for as many PLSC courses as I possibly can.

Great instructor. The reading involved in this class is near overwhelming, but if you complete the work, you'll pass easily. He's succinct in his email replies, but gets to the point. Few quizzes, multiple papers, and no final exam. Incorporates movies and Grisham novels into his teaching. Con Law is super interesting, too.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: You will be reading at least five hours week. You will learn a lot. The reading is very important to passing the class. Dr. Atkins was very clear on what he expects of his students. As long as you do the work, which isn't that hard you will pass the class. I look forward to taking more of his classes in the future.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Atwill is a super chill guy
Interesting lectures most of the time Show up and you'll do fine

Hist10 is a good class. The lecture quizzes can get annoying but he makes sure you don't have any homework outside of class except for a book quiz which is easy if you read it (he gives a study guide). He's funny and tries to make lectures fun. Everything is TA graded though so I guess a lot depends on who you get but Dr. Atwill is cool and nice.

It is a CRIME he is not rated higher. He knows his classes are mostly gen eds and he in no way wants his to class to be one you have to worry about. He does super easy mini quizzes after his lectures so you need to show up to do them. Midterms and final are a breeze but his book quiz requires you to read. HE CARES ABOUT YOUR EDUCATION.

He is a genuine and kind professor that tries to make the lectures as interesting as he can and wants his students to succeed. Class is mandatory though because there are mini-quizzes at the end of each lecture. I would take this class again.

Professor Atwill is really amazing. He's well respected and always tries to make the lectures interesting. (some of them can be boring) The grading is very simple and clear. There aren't a lot of grades so your grade relies heavily on whether or not you show up but it's not a painful class to sit through.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I took this class as a freshman as a gen ed. Very interesting lectures, my grade received was due to my own faults and study habits. Looking back this is a very easy A, however, the only criticism I have is that Prof Atwill makes the tests strange because they are vocab and object heavy instead of concepts. Would take again.
TAs are annoying, This class is ridiculously hard. Not an easy ge. Have so many things read in the exam. Worst class in PSU.
Great prof great class. Totally knows you have other more important classes and makes his lectures interesting

Professor is nice. One of the female TA ruined the course. She is unfair about grading. My friend didn't do the extra credit, and he still got the extra point. Her participation point is grading from her feeling. She didn't provide that many questions to let u answer. It depends on she likes u or not. This class could be easy if u choose other TAs

I recently took History 188 with Dr. Atwill, and I would totally recommend it. The class is not a joke, but if you actually do the readings, participate in the discussions, and prepare for the exams, then you can get an A. Attendance was only mandatory on discussion and exam days, but there is a lot of information in the lectures, so its best to go

This class is amazing. I have 3.6 GPA and I like to suffer. I would LOVE to receive more C on this Awesome class. Come to every ducking class and you will start wonder what is life. Definitely retake this class. It is too inspirational!! Recommend to people who like to suffer. Just Do It!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Dr. Atwill's class is fantastic and a great introductory course to history. The lectures are entertaining and Dr. Atwill does a lot to make sure his students succeed (provides study guides, lecture outlines, etc.). Yes, you have to do the reading and come to class in order to learn/get an A, but isn't that the whole point of going to college?
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Definitely not an easy gen ed. You have to go to class and pay attention because there is a quiz after every class. You have to use a lot of information in the quiz to get a good grade too. His lectures are not clear and boring. There are also 3 map quizzes, 3 exams, and a book quiz. I dedicated a lot of time into the class especially for a gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The class is not an easy gen-ed. His lectures are very boring and long. He gives daily quizzes and it is pretty difficult to get 100s on them. He does give review guides for the exams but a lot of the material is not covered in class. He lectures off of an outline and usually doesn't go in order.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Gives a mini paragraph quiz at the end of class so attendance important. Website that has the notes pre-typed to just add in info from lecture. No homework but there are three simple map quizzes and three exams along with a book quiz. The book is short and easy to read. Easy enough exams, just mostly memorization of dates and vocabulary.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: David Atwill is the man. His lectures are interesting and the class is very easy to get an A in. He knows that we all have more important classes so there is never homework. We had to write one in class paper. There were three map quizzes and 3 midterms. He uploads study guides for all of them. Highly Reccommend

This class is a lot of memorization. Be prepared to memorize multiple dates and spend a lot of time studying. I also found the exam/quiz grading somewhat harsh for an elective. But Professor Atwill is an amazing professor and he keeps his lectures as fun and interesting as possible.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: You absolutely have to go to this class and pay attention; there are quizzes after every lecture. There are also 3 exams (hard especially for a gen ed class), 3 map quizzes, and a book quiz (that you must read). Definitely not a class you want to take for a gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He is a really good professor and he makes sure to emphasize things we are interested in. He is really funny and also does funny activities. His exams are super easy because he give really good review sessions the class before an exam also the quiz questions are never too difficult.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Amazing professor and TAs, all very helpful and easy to talk too throughout the year!

This class is an easy A as long as you show up to every class (it's a clicker class) and take diligent notes. There's 3 "midterm quizzes", 3 map quizzes, 1 book quiz (the only essay exam) and daily quizzes at the end of each class (where you just have to answer in a few sentences). The midterms are easy (mostly all matching style questions).

History 10 with David Atwill was honestly one of my favorite classes. He makes the lecture topics interesting and brings in tons of props to draw attention to the topic. You will take a daily quiz but if you listen to the material and write a few sentences you'll do fine. There is only one reading assignment. David Atwill is an amazing professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Hilarious--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great Professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: amazing lectures. easy class if you show up and do the mini quizzes. tests are NOT hard

This class is actually really easy. You have to show up and take notes and study and you'll pass. It's actually not that hard if you just pay attention and do your work. Professor is really funny and cool. Makes the class a fun time!

Great and caring professor, he wants you to succeed and gives you a lot of opportunities to do so. Only three midterms that are matching only, participation and small quizzes at the end of class. If you want a good grade, you'll get one.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Hilarious

reviews.comment: The TAs are kind of hard and gave certain grades for no reason explain but that was this semester. Professor Atwill was great, and very fair.
This class sucks, the TA's are annoying, so are the lectures. The tests are way too difficult, dont take this class bruh, its hard for no reason.
Easy course. Lectures are simple, have a small quiz at the end of each one.  He is funny and keeps the lectures light so you remain interested. I would highly recommend Professor Atwill!!

He is awesome. Easiest class ever. He tries to make lectures interesting by teaching uncommon stuff. He wants you to do well and makes the class as easy as possible. Take this class with him. Show up to class because there are quizzes everyday.

Much harder than his intro level courses. Just make sure to participate during discussion which is 40% of the grade. Papers are hard but everything in life isn't easy. Talk to him if you are having trouble. Other than that the final was 2 essays given a head of time. This class had a lot of dry reading but if you like Chinese history take it!
Class is extremely boring. The books are horrible. I wouldn't recommend taking this course or this teacher.
his lecture is really boring, lots of readings, but if you can read, you'll get an A

If you can read you can get an A- with little effort. Has 4 novels to read but he gives you the essay question and vocab that will be on the quiz a head of time. If you have questions he is more than helpful during office hours. Just make one or two comments per chapter unit on "discussion" days. EAST ASIAN STUDIES majors should take this class!
