Great teacher with clear lectures.  The books are interesting and the papers are not bad.  There is a final and a midterm, but he supplies you with the vocabulary and the essay questions in advance.  If you have any interest in China, this is a great class

Does well with the lectures but be forewarned: there is a LOT of reading to do. He has four papers on books of 300 pages length each. He also has several exams - none of which is at all easy. This class is only for those who have a serious interest in China and a solid background in its history.

has matching and essay tests. lectures can be boring but he tries to make them more interesting. he doesnt really use the text book much. but you do have to read 3 other books and take in depth quizes on them.

Essay tests.  They get easier as the semester goes on.  He lets you know what he wants to see in the essay.  Interesting topics.  He gave us the book for this semester, save some $$$$.  Good elective to take.

I always went to class, and the discussions too. Got 80% on pretty much everything. I then stopped going to lecture, and only went to discussion to sleep, and I got 97% on the second midterm. You can draw your own conclusions.

He wants his students to succeed, and his lectures are interesting. He gives a free text book, but its long and boring. No pictures or anything. Just text and text and text, like an TV manual. Yet he doesnt even force you to read it, so I guess its not that bad. Tests have review sheets and thats all you need really.

Subject is interesting, but the class is difficult for a 400 level history.  All assigned books need to be read and followed with a book review.  Books are usually longwinded (over 300 pages) and some are hard to write about.  Hard grader as well.  Expectations are unclear at times.  Although difficult, you will definitely learn in this class.
Dr. Atwill is not the most engaging speaker, but he wants his students to do well, does not assign textbooks (he thinks they're a scam), and his class is pretty easy.

Professor Atanga was sooo good! She made it very clear what her goal was teaching this class-- to help people learn, not to grade their assignments poorly. The class was pretty easy. TopHat quizzes based on class lectures and review sessions for the exams. Definitely recommend Barb for this course!
Actually the best prof I've ever had. Love her

She is a great professor. At first, she may seem strict, but she is easygoing. The reading for the textbook is simple, and the weekly quizzes are based on the text readings. Her assignments are easy, and she is always willing to give feedback. I strongly suggest her to anyone! Pay attention and you will get a simple A.
She is a very nice professor just shows up late to class a lot. She grades based on attendance, quizzes and a huge paper in APA format.

Barbara is a great person and very sweet! This class however is only 2 credits but more work than all of my 3 credit classes combined. There's a 10-page research paper in APA format, a quiz EVERY class, 2 exams and a final. The material is very dull but if you pay attention the exams are easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I love this Professor! This is my one of my first classes and she is my favorite so far. She is very caring and always willing to help. Go to class, read the textbook, and you will be fine. Make sure you use the resources she provides on APA.

She was a very nice professor. Gave us a lot of opportunities to do better and even dropped our lowest grades for a big project because she really cares about her students doing well. Definitely need to go to class for attendance and quiz credit. Easy class

Barbara is a really nice person! I love her style of teaching! She really cares about her students and makes sure they understand the material she is teaching. Her assignments are not too hard but also not too easy. As long as you participate in class, read the readings, and do everything that her assignments require you to do, you will do fine!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Sattar is truly excellent. Hers was one of the most well organized and consistently interesting courses I've ever had the pleasure of taking. Her assignments are consistently engaging and she also happens to be extremely flexible in terms of her students workloads. I would more than eagerly take another of her classes anytime.

Horrible professor. She acts as if the students world should revolve around her class and our other classes do not exist. She is not helpful, her essay prompts are confusing. She gave me an attitude when I told her I did not understand what exactly the prompt was asking. When I asked other students about the prompt they too were confused.

I personally liked Atia. I thought she was down to earth and reasonable. She even brought us cake once, who doesn't love cake! The class itself requires reading but it's a literature class what do you expect?

This man seriously has issues. He picks a group of students to befriend and treat like actual babies, and then finds another group to actually straight up bully and target and humiliate. If you're in the group he chooses to target, he will not give you actual criticism, but instead come for your character and belittle your work and you.

I don't like this guy. He likes to hear himself talk a lot and will give lectures on things mostly unrelated to the projects. He also is never clear and direct about grading criteria so he doesn't have to take accountability for points off. That said, the class isn't too hard, but it's fairly time-consuming.

Reggie was one of those kids in high school who had no friends so now thinks because a few of the teachers' pets make jokes with him he can be extremely rude and almost bully everyone else. The course isn't bad, but the projects take a bunch of time and if it isn't to his standards RIP your grade.
Class isn't too difficult, a lot of group projects, Reggie can be a bit rude but is overall a good caring guy.

Before I had Reggie, he had a reputation of being a tough grader and a moody guy. When he was my professor, that was not the case (beside the dad jokes) He is clam, gives great feedback, and doesnt give extra work (where other professors will). Talk to him about your design or anything else and you will come to like him as a professor and person.
He's a good professor, just be careful when he's in a bad mood.  He tends to hold grudges though so be careful the way you word things.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He will rip into your project even if it is really good. It might be a 3 credit class but he will give you the same amount as a 6 credit class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Reggie is a great guy. Jokes are so bad that they are somewhat comical. Very knowledgeable. Will give criticism, but it's well deserved. Not mean, but if you've never been scolded in your life and you're a softy, you will be offended. Wears different scarves for different moods. You can become good friends with him if you show effort and initiative

Loves to hear himself talk, not half as funny as he thinks he is. He'll give constructive criticism but he'll scorch you during presentations if you aren't 100% savvy with your designs. Not a very pleasant person to learn from
Expects you to make your life revolve around studio. Expect to stay up all night at least a few times working on projects. Likes to hear himself talk. Elbows.
He is a great professor, very knowledgeable and helpful. Someone you can always talk to about your design.
He is an incredible professor and loves what he does, and is great at teaching. Bald though.

Amazing guy. I don't click well with his teaching style (more stuff is said by him than written on slides) but other people do amazing in his class and I loved being in his class. He's extremely understanding as long as you are clear with him about what's going on. He has some great stories and he respects his students

Dr. Avery is one of the professors that really cares about what he teaches. He doesn't just spit information at you; he asks critical questions and his assignments make you use what you learn. I've learned by far the most in my major from him. You have to work to get what you learn, but he notices hard work and treats you with respect.

Amazing professor, one of the best I've ever had. He is hilarious and willing to help students out. As long as you pay attention in class, you're golden. His exams are more application based and he really wants you to understand the material. While attendance isn't mandatory, he makes going to class worth it. And Go to lab or you won't do well

Great guy, ok prof.  He's a funny guy and you can tell he has a lot going on in his head--for better or for worse.  The lectures are ok, the labs are solid.  Pay attention to comments he makes during lab, that's where you'll learn the most.

Dr. Avery is one of those rare professors who actually doesn't come to work to hate you or not give a crap about what he's teaching you. He takes attendance with clickers and missing a lot of classes won't benefit you, b/c he says things that you need to write down and aren't on the lecture slides. Don't last minute study for his exams either.

This is my favorite Penn State class.  Professor Avery is absolutely hilarious.  It doesn't hurt that I find the class material really interesting, but he also presents it really well.  We watch a lot of YouTube clips of different animal behaviors, and he makes the class more interactive with clicker questions.  Highly Reccomend.

So this teacher's at Cornell now, but I guess I'll post his rating here. He's a great lecturer when he actually lectures. He gave about 2 lectures for the whole semester then had other professors & guest lecturers for the rest. I was pretty surprised by this format, but still learned a bunch He's very helpful in OH & replies quickly to emails.

Not the easiest class ever, August is a very smart and helpful professor. His lectures can go a little fast, but he is very nice towards students and his style of presentation is clear. This is one of the only classes where I remember the things I learned a year after I took it. Definitely make use of the textbook.
Hard class, but he's so helpful if you go and talk to him. Make use of the podcasts and the figures in the book. He's easy to listen to in class because his voice is so soothing
Very intelligent professor and wants students to do well.  Have lots of reference and review material online.  Review sessions are helpful.

He's a great prof and has a really great accent. He may talk and drift off sometimes, but he's still understandable. I also think his exams are fair. He gives rewards for showing up for class AND even emails you personally to ask if you want to review anything from past exams. Overall, above my expectations.
attendance is mandatory, the professor is helpful but his class is hard. You are expected to know EVERYTHING and lectures are extremely fast.
difficult to understand, has accent.  Goes fast in lecture
No Comments
Hes an awesome awesome guy and very helpful.  the class was hard and he expects you to know everything.  but is more then willing to answer any questions and to clarify anything you dont understand.

I have nothing but great things to say about her. Clearly communicates the information, uses examples to aid in teaching, and responds to emails within 24 hours. Her homework's are tough, but in a good way. They force you to struggle with the material which ultimately helps cement the information. She makes you think, instead of just regurgitate it

Her accent is thick but nothing that an engineering student shouldn't already be used to.  Her lectures are pre-recorded.  She doesn't respond to email.  She appears to have no interest in teaching this course.
Very quiet and has a very thick accent. Expects you to learn most everything on your own.
Can't understand a word she says.  Typical nuclear engineering teacher
Wonderful teacher. Willing to help her students. Very rarely can be a little challenging to understand her, but her accent is not bad at all. Top notch prof.
awesome

He is a great professor.His classes are engaging and fun, so it is easier to learn hard concepts in his class. generally chem 110 is a difficult course but with him as professor its the easiest course you can take. exams are easy if you attend classes and recitations.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Great professor, but lectures get boring though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: 80% of this class came from 3 midterms(17% each) and 1 final (29%),I personally learned more during my recitation than from his lectures. If you dont watch the pre lecture videos on canvas prior to class you wont understand anything. He is a cool and chill guy and it shows that he cares and has a passion for chemistry. Overall hard subject cool guy
Good at clearly explaining complex concepts.

While I think Dr. Asbury makes lectures bearable, he tended to go on long irrelevant tangents. Also be prepared to spend hours on homework each week, and self teach yourself a lot of the topics. For Chem 110 in general I highly suggest getting the review packet for Chem 110, like I never watched the videos or read the textbook and I was chilling.

Attendance is mandatory to consider surviving. Get ready to do chem 6 days/week minimum from assignments that won't help you learn a thing. Overall nice guy and passionate about his job. Recitations are beyond painful. Tries to engage class with experiments.

Chem 110 is a notoriously hard class and it moves really fast, but Dr Asbury really does a good job simplifying hard topics. All content is easy to find on his Canvas too. I mainly used the videos for pre lecture material instead of reading the textbook. Definitely do not skip lecture because keeping up with this class is essential to pass.

He has good, thorough explanations of chemistry concepts that really resonated with me. The issue is that he glosses over some stuff. I do most of my learning through Dr. Bojan's videos that are posted in Canvas before each lecture, and then use the lecture itself to supplement that learning. There is a lot of homework. Asbury is a chill guy.

Chem 110 is a very, very difficult class at PSU. There is weekly homework with more or fewer than 15 problems, pre-lecture quizzes, weekly quizzes, 3 midterms, and a final. He is a very caring person, but it is a lot of work. There is top hat for attendance, I would not miss a lecture because the class moves very very fast.

Asbury is a great professor and very passionate about chemistry. He does a great job at explaining things, however he does occasionally speed through certain topics. As long as you pay attention for most of the class you will be fine. He also has many resources available for students to use that can help them prep and study for upcoming exams.
Chem 110 overall is a difficult course, however Dr. Asbury made the experience so much better. He answers emails quickly and would help with any problems behind the scene.

Dr Asbury is a great professor. Compared to other 110 professors, he has a very soothing voice. He's always willing to slow down and answer questions. He loves getting the class involved through experiments, practice questions, and the legendary talent show. It always felt like he actually wanted to be there, which can't be said about everyone.

I thought Asbury was great, and from what I've heard, he is the best you can get for CHEM 110, so you are lucky if you have him. For the class, grind the practice exams. There are three per exam, and they are very close to what you will see, just different numbers and elements and what not. Do the assigned work, pay attention, and you'll be fine.

Great professor; he made the lectures engaging and always answered questions. The class in general is very difficult and work heavy, but your assigned TA will grade all of your work. Overall very happy that I had him over less engaging professors
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Dr.Asbury was amazing. Very welcoming, opened the first lecture with his Piano Man parody, “Chemistry Man”. Chem110 it's self is awful, be ready to read everyday, but can be manageable. Dr.Asbury is one of the better chem110 professors.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Asbury's lectures are engaging and he seems to have a lot of fun with the demonstrations. He is always happy to help students and explains things well. This said, you won't be successful if you do not show up and apply yourself. Utilize the practice exams and resources like study groups, textbook, and videos!! Allow a few days to study for exams.

Just to preface: I am someone who doesn't just 'get it'. 

The professor is a nice 'play by the rules' person. However, my main issue is that he never finished his sentences when he was explaining quantum chemistry topics. It would just trail off and everyone would - at least, pretend - to understand. It would be like "xyz... as I explained prior".

In Chem 110, the professor doesn't actually matter all that much if you read the material. Your TA is more important in my opinion. That aside, I like Asbury's lectures and found them engaging and they helped me understand the material better. He is not very available outside of class time, but that is remedied by the TA office hours.

Asbury is definitely a good professor to take as far as chem goes. Chem is very difficult in itself but having a teacher like him makes it a bearable. I recommend taking notes on the videos for PLQs and making sure to use your time wisely in recitation which was super helpful. There's also extra credit at the end and the 75% or above rule is nice.

Asbury is overall a pretty solid professor. However, just be prepared to do a lot of individual studying on your own time. Lectures are helpful, but they are or refining information than they are for teaching content. Good demonstrations, clear that he has a passion for what he does. Make sure to do pre-lecture material & go to office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Asbury knows his stuff, but the lectures can get dry at times. If you stay engaged, go to class, and use resources like Unstuck ai alongside the textbook, you'll do well. Exams are tough, so utilize TA review sessions.

Asbury is a great prof to get, but this class is very hard. He was always very passionate and helpful during lectures, and explained things well. He also would answer any questions, even in the 300 person class. To pass this class, attend lectures, watch the PLQ VIDEOS, and do the practice exams that are provided.

Dr. Asbury seems really nice and has a passion for chemistry. However, if you do not understand chemistry, then this class will be extremely difficult for you. Even after perfect attendance, completing every assignment, and showing up to office hours, I struggled. The exams are what ruined my grade. The class averages were failing grades.

John asbury tries his best when lecturing and will answer any questions you have. But the course itself is really hard. When everyone agrees that Chem 110 is the worst, it should mean something. He is super sweet and wants to teach, but if you didn't understand the pre-lecture work you're kinda screwed. He is one of the better chem professors tho.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury was a decent professor. He answered emails rather quickly and always came to class with a positive attitude. However, Chem 110 is a very difficult course, which honestly needs a lot of effort put into it, especially if you have not taken AP or an IB Chem class before. The class has a lot of homework and quizzes, and tests weigh a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I was not happy with this class. I learned everything from the textbook because lectures were slow and not at all helpful. Dr. Asbury seems to like his job which I appreciate but when a class average on an exam is a 66% it can't just be the student's fault.

I took him my freshman year of college (fall 2021) and I obviously did not pass the class. I quickly learned that if you don't have an AP Chem level of knowledge, don't even try taking chemistry at Penn State. In fact on the first day he expected us to already know a lot about basic chemistry which was definitely a refresher for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Not responsive to email, even timely email that I have sent multiple times now. Should be there for your students, especially your Chem majors!  Good luck finding this faculty member if you need something.

Took this first semester, never took a real chemistry course due to covid and this was not the great introduction for it. You're expected to know concepts like the back of your hand when immediately thrown into the course. He was very boring and monotoned.

Dr. Asbury knows his stuff! But as times can get a bit boring. He does occasionally do some fun demos. Overall I learned a lot from him, but I wouldn't say it was fun. Participation in lectures is graded, and there is one small extra credit opportunity at the end of the year. GO TO THE LECTURE AND WATCH THE PLQ VIDEOS!!!

This course has a lot of homework, no matter who you have. I think that he was easy to talk to and would always answer in class questions. My grade was mainly affected by exams, so I would recommend going to the TA review sessions. He does not grade homework, the TA's do, so you will just have to hope you get a nice TA.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: Pretty cool dude who makes lectures not miserable at 9 AM. This class requires a good amount of self-teaching though, his lectures only help to clarify if you already know what you're talking about, otherwise, you're lost. Exams are also brutal if you're lost. If you get Dr. Asbury you're in for a safe bet, better than other chem profs out there.

Professor Asbury was very clear and his lectures were helpful. This class is tough no matter what professor you have, but Asbury is clear and takes time to explain the material. His lectures aren't very interesting, but you have to go to class and you will be fine.
good professor. Lots to interact with his students. He's always doing live demos and overall makes the class interesting.

Lecture slides are packed with information, made it hard to take notes. He cares about his students & wants them to succeed. If u can get by the workload & slides, u should be fine. Go to office hours though and study for exams!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Chem 110 sucks and I know few people who enjoyed it, but Asbury makes it tolerable. He makes the grading criteria very clear and gives a lot of resources for studying. Asbury's also pretty funny and his lectures are enjoyable. It's a hard class, but if you have a choice in professor choose Asbury.

I absolutely loved Dr. Asbury! He made chem actually enjoyable and was super super helpful. I didnt realize how good he was until my Chem 112 prof asked the class if she was going too fast and then basically said too bad, some people wont be able to follow, and then didnt explain anything further. Dr. A was always willing to help

An amazing professor and lecturer, especially for CHEM 110. Did great chemistry demonstrations that helped to connect topics, and was not afraid of fun. He posts his lecture slides on canvas and is always willing to help students learn. CHEM 110 sucks, but Asbury cultivates an interest for chemistry. 10/10 and would recommend over other profs!

Asbury isnt helpful, but The content itself isnt horrible and most of the lectures are done outside the classroom. Its nice because every week is the same so you get into a nice routine. Pre Lecture Quizes on Sunday, Tuesday and Thursday, Homework on Wednesday, Quiz on Thursday, Recitation on Thursday. The class itself was curved by about 6%.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Asbury is a really nice guy, but tends to go on tangents during lectures on topics that interest him. He explains hard concepts throughly and will always answers students question during lectures. The class itself is a lot of work, but its putting an effort in if you need to take chem 112.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: this professor clearly loves chemistry and tries to make it as interesting as possible for his students. he responds quickly to emails and is very willing to help students that request it. this class is very homework heavy, but if it wasn't, i wouldnt have passed the class.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chem 110 is very tough. Definitely spent the most of my time on this class. Prof Asbury is a decent choice. Really great guy, and loves to answer questions in class. His lectures are a little hard to follow and long, but you gotta go for clicker points. He doesn't use the chem110 study guide like other profs, which would have been really helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury does a great job of making the extremely difficult topic of quantum physics very accessible. His lectures do as good of a job of explaining it as I imagine is possible, and he answers questions really well. Reading the book is very helpful but not necessary. His exams are also very very similar to the practice except for the final.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Really mediocre professor for a pretty tough class. Overall Chem 110 is a difficult class and has a lot of work behind it and he doesn't really make it any easier. I emailed him a couple of times about my mental health during the semester and he ignored me every time which kinda put a bad impression on me :/ I heard others are better.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The most important thing is how are you going to study the test because they are so many ways that Asbury gives you to study. They are too many exercies, hw, quizz, practice quizz available that it can be hard to know what to study before exam. But in general asbury is so cool and wants to help you. I love this prof

Professor Asbury is really nice. He really cares about each student's work and loves answering any question you have during the class. TAs and LAs are helpful too. The only problem is that there are too much homework and quizzes. Also, exams take a large portion of your final grade, so you really need to study hard to get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury is such a nice professor. You can tell he is passionate about chemistry and is very receptive to questions (he never acted like anyone was asking a dumb question even if it was something he had just gone over). The class is extremely difficult, but that's just the course itself.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chem is always tough and I only passed because of a TA's study group. Asbury's class is a lot of work each week (3 pre-lecture quizzes, 1 longer quiz, 1 written HW from the textbook, and 1 recitation). If you put in the work yourself you'll be alright but you really have to understand the concepts.

Dr. Asbury has overall been a very good professor. He is willing to answer questions during lecture and will help students after class. The difficulty of his class has less to do with asbury himself but rather with the class in general. The class is one of penn states hardest weeder classes, and dr asbury tries to help students as much as possible.

Professor Asbury is so wholesome! He cares a lot about his students and takes the time to answer questions even after class is over. He has a lot of patience and tries his best even though we're over zoom. It's a little dry at times but if you pay attention and put in work you'll be fine. Grades are mainly based on exams which suck but it's ok.

Prof Asbury was definitely knowledgeable about the material. Overall decent lecturer with a few instances of not explaining the material well. Recitation sections are VERY HELPFUL towards nailing the material for homeworks and exams. Put the time and effort into reading the textbook and asking questions when you have them in recitation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: He does NOT create the Exams. People who do bad on exams and blame it on the prof are lazy. Average Prof but truly wants you to do well. Online HW and Quizzes that are helpful. If you do the bare minimum you'll get a C or fail. If you take advantage of what he gives you can get an A. I did 50/50 and got a B. Your work truly reflects your grade.

He is very passionate about the subject he teaches and really wants his students to do well. chem was a hard class that makes you work for it but asbury tries to make it understandable. There is a lot of reading and homework for the course but if you put in the time and effort you will do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury is a great professor to have for Chem 110. He provides you with lots of resources if you need help with the content, and he's a great guy to talk to as well. Just be ready to put in the work and ask questions, and Dr. Asbury will be willing to help you. Overall, Chem 110 with Dr. Asbury was my favorite class this past semester.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He is my dad, he is the Best Peter Asbury

Dr. Asbury really knows what hes talking about, and clearly wants everyone in his class to succeed. There are 3 exams and a final, and weekly online quizzes. Overall, hes a great guy and teaches the material very well.

Doctor Asbury is a wonderful professor. His lectures are super interesting. There are opportunities for extra credit, which is great. Overall, he cares about his students and goes above and beyond to prepare you for the exams.

I really can't judge his mediocre lectures because it's a huge lecture that a couple hundred people take, however, I will judge him for how he acts 1-on-1 when I went to his office hours. Asbury is extremely condescending if you're not doing perfectly in the class. So if you're not naturally good at chem, find someone else or get close with TA
Chem 110 is a pretty tough class in itself. If you put in the work, it will show. Exams are hard but not impossible.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury is an average professor. He knows what he's talking about and enjoys the material. However, he's not the greatest at teaching you the material. You'll do fine if you have him, but try to find a better prof.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class uses an online E-Book. There is a lot of pre-reading "required" but it really isn't 100% necessary. The only use for reading ahead of time is to get clicker points on the pre-week assessment. The easiest solution is to print out the readings/notes ahead of time and just use them during class. John is a goofball who is a decent teacher.
He gives amazing lectures and tests are pretty easy. TA and LA are pretty helpful. You have to do a lot of reading before class but it is worth it as it helps in your exams. Pretty funny guy as well.
Gave us so much work on the first week of school and it never got better.

John Asbury is the man. If you attend lecture and recitation, and do a little extra work outside class, things will be good for you. Chem110 might be the first big college class you have but don't be scared.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Pro: nice guy to talk to and able to help during office hours Con: when I took his class he didn't provide lecture notes, so we would just copy what he wrote on his paper, and he would kept using words like "ummm" to make the sentence smooth. But it wasted a ton of students. Overall: acceptable but not highly recommended.

This class was hard, no doubt. Asbury was a fine professor - he is extremely extremely smart and he tried to make the class as straightforward as possible. If you go to the homework sessions he will help you as much as you need. The practice exams and homeworks are similar to the real exams -- not really any surprises. Hard class but doable.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: He didn't tell us about a lot of the things that we needed to know for the tests. He made a lot of jokes but it kind of took out of class time.

I normally do well in school and I put in a crazy amount of time into this class but nothing worked. I would just attend lecture for the participation points but other than that it had no meaning. I thought it was me at first but attended a different profs lecture and understood more in the first 15 mins than I have in all his lectures combined.

Dr. Asbury is a awesome person but he connot teach chemistry effectively. Every day was the same thing he seems to look at the topics for the day/week then spit out information that in no way was organized. Homework is 10x harder then example problems. NOTHING will prepare you for the extremely hard tests.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury is a cool dude but isn't the best at explaining things. I found his train of thought a bit confusing. If you've taken AP Chem in high school, you'll be fine. If not, then I'd find another professor. Do the quizzes on Canvas to get 1% extra credit at the end. Shoutout to my awesome recitation TA Morgan for clearing all the confusion I had
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests? Not many--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: He doesn't explain anything. It's like he expects us to just know what he's talking about. He made me very frustrated.

Dr. Asbury is a great professor if you've done Chemistry or AP Chem in high school but weren't great at it. It's the perfect mix of blending in old info with new info, and he's a cool dude. Make sure to read the book and study.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He was an average chem lecturer, and I can't blame him because it is hard to lecture such a hard class with over 300 students. He covered all the material and sometimes it was hard to understand. Usually when I got personal help I was able to understand everything.

He's a funny guy but a bad teacher. You need to read the textbook before the lecture in order to understand, and even then it's hard to follow. He's not really good with office hours and tends to refer you to the TA or LA rather than help you himself. Tests are hard and even if you do well on the practice exams that doesn't mean you'll pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury was a pretty good professor for CHEM 110. He teaches all through notes and lecture in class, so basically you can't miss anything or you'll be lost. I also took CHEM 108 to go along with CHEM 110 and I realize now that I wouldn't have passed without it. Dr. Asbury is helpful for questions, but you have to study hard to well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Not a bad professor, especially considering he has to teach a room of 300 students rather difficult material. Can't complain about the homework, as that seems to be assigned by the department. If you have a question about the content, don't be afraid to ask him, he's friendly and will figure out where you're going wrong, and explain why it's wrong.

Dr. Asbury is friendly and kind of nerdy, but difficult to understand. If you didn't have a great chemistry teacher in high school or never had AP chemistry, you will have a hard time. He is available after class for about 10 min. If you want to schedule an appointment, he does it by email.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Dr. Asbury started out teaching well. About a quarter through the semester, I realized that the way he was teaching was very difficult understand and learn. He didn't have powerpoint slides, he wrote everything out on a Smart Board that showed up on the screen. He's kinda inconsistent in his teaching, lots of "um's" and pauses.
Loved him.

He just left too many subjects/ lessons too open ended when it came to solving the problem, and just expected we would get it right away. He tried too much to act like a cool funny guy to get our respect than teach. I also went to him for his office hours and he was not helpful at all. He just kinda of repeated everything I said and was rude.
Super clear lectures, if you listen you will know exactly what you need for the test. Took AP chem in high school and didn't get it but Asbury made it easy to understand.

Asbury knows his stuff, but a little too much. I know what the term "weed-out' really means now. If it wasn't for recitation, I would have been completely lost. You really have to work hard to stay on pace. Welcome to college.

As other people said, it is typical weed out class. I did not have sufficient chemistry background from high school, so I found this class especially and have to work really hard in oder to maintain Bs. I guess there is nothing left to say about this class. Just be prepared to do some college skill studying! Good luck!

Professor Asbury is a great teacher. His lectures are very clear, and is always willing to help you during office hours.  Very good at adding humor into his lectures. Beware of lots of helium and hydrogen balloons. Overall, great lecturer for this course b
He was fun. Did presentations in class

From what I've heard his tests are harder than the other CHEM 452 professor, but he is definitely the better teacher. He's also very helpful in office hours. Take him if you have an interest in learning quantum chemistry.

Dr. Asbury is the worst professor at Penn State. He is absolutely the most arrogant as well. It was terrible sitting through his lectures where all he did was say "um", mutter aimlessly, and bat his lips. Its almost comical to see him up front wasting your time until you realize its your grade that's going to suffer.
Tests are very tough.

Dr. Asbury is a relatively nice guy, but in a class of over 300 kids it was hard to learn from his lectures. The tests and homeworks are all standardized in Chem 110 so its not like he does anything special, good or bad.

Dr. Asbury is a very kind and humorous man, but he is an awful professor. His lectures were unclear and left most students leaving lecture not even completely sure of what they had just learned. His lectures consisted of a lot of awkward pauses, "uhm"s, later pointing, and explosions of objects to regain attention.

Not a great teacher. If you don't already know something about chemistry, you might get lost. He's not extremely helpful explaining things when you don't get something. I had to really study to keep up with the class and even used things like clutch prep to help me understand the more difficult concepts. I wouldn't recommend taking his class.
Dr. Asbury is VERY cut and dry and is quite monotone. He presents the material well but does not have much enthusiasm to keep you interested.

Honestly, I would suggest taking chem 110 with another professor.  I learned more from the book than I did in this class.  Also, I started sitting in on another professor's lecture and learned way more.  Other than that he seemed like a nice guy outside of class, I just didn't benefit from his teaching style.

Really great lecturer. Science Fridays were terrible, but other than that, he was really helpful and able to answer any questions asked of him. He's from America too, so it's not difficult to understand what he's saying like some of the other professors. YOU WANT THIS PROFESSOR!
Dr. Asbury is amazing. Covers a lot of material in class. His notes are very helpful.

He is a really quirky guy and a somewhat decent lecturer. He's a little obsessed with science Friday and explains pointless unrelated science facts on Fridays when he should be teaching the material. The overall course was pretty easy if you know what you're doing. The TAs are what make or break your grade so make sure you get a good one.

Dr. Asbury moves at a brisk pace through the course material, but will take the time to reiterate the concepts if even 1 student has an issue.  He is a fantastic lecturer, and is willing to take time out of his EXTREMELY hectic schedule to help any student who is having trouble with any course material.
Did not finish lectures often, and put many concepts/equations on the board but would not bother to explain them or would not explain them in an understandable language.

Definitely a great lecturer and professor. He will always be able to answer questions and explains things really well for those with a good background in chemistry. If you have AP credits or have taken the ap chem class, he is a great professor to have because he doesn't waste time explaining tiny details. If not, you might struggle a little more.

This class was a nightmare. Lectures are incomplete. You will spend at least 15 hours trying to get a good grade in the class, however, it's really tough. You need to read the book, do problems from the book, do problems assigned for recitation and quizzes. Asbury is a cool dude, but cannot teach. He spends more time popping balloons than lecturing

Asbury mumbles a lot so it's hard to hear him, and half of the time he doesn't finish his lecture notes. He couldn't do a practice problem the day of an exam. He had to ask a TA to help. I went to office hours, and once I told him my first 3 exam scores, he came across like I was was an annoyance, worth no more than a grain of sand.

Solid lecture teacher. He has notes that make sense and clearly describes things in class. He teaches a huge lecture so its hard for him to do better than he does. In general, he has the ability to make an 8am lecture somewhat enjoyable and he actually teaches you what you need to know. Solid Professor and I recommend getting him if you can.
Pretty Good. Pretty quick. Clear in clarifying doubts.

Dr. Asbury made a very difficult subject understandable. Make sure you go to class. You should do pretty well on the homework is you go to class. If you're not sure about a homework problem, Dr. Asbury is more than willing to guide you through it in office hours. Exams are tough, but your not taking a 400 level chem class for easy exams. Thumbs up

Dr. Asbury is a really great teacher. Quantum chemistry is not easy to learn let alone teach, and I think he did a great job. Very fair in testing exactly what he taught. If you went to lectures, did the homework, read the book and went to office hours it was not too hard to get an A. Extremely helpful, enthusiastic, and overall nice guy

This was the most miserable class I have ever taken at PSU. Asbury tries to explain the material at a level that makes sense to undergraduates, but ultimately fails. He scribbles equations on the board and fails to explain them. Homeworks are nearly impossible and way beyond an undergraduate level. Exams are extremely lengthy.

Asbury tries hard to be a decent teacher, but just comes up short.  Writing equations on the board and trying to explain them by using vocabulary way over most undergraduate's heads isn't the way to teach.  A little better in office hours, but not much.  Too many abbreviations/derivations/vague concepts and not enough visual learning.
Extremely helpful, and great at clarifying difficult concepts. Great teacher!

Really likes quantum chemistry and conveys that in lecture. Go to class because the book doesn't necessarily tell you everything he'll test you on. Very helpful during office hours. Homework was really difficult and exams were hard to finish in the time allotted. Good class overall.

He was a very strong lecturer, especially considering the subject matter (quantum chemistry).  The exams were fair , but a bit long for the time allotted.  They were typically based on the homework and lectures; however , he also assigned book problems that were ungraded.  Periodically, they would appear on the exams, as well.
He's easier to understand if you read before you come to class. He won't teach you everything you need to know but can clear things up sometimes.

Dr. Asbury is a great professor! If you just do the homework problems, attend recitation, and do the practice tests the class is easy! Definitely could get an A! I just slacked off a little bit and got a B and I'm no genius. He's extremely helpful and a wonderful professor. By all means try to get him as your lecturer! You won't regret it!

I thought he did a good job at instructing. He did go off on tangents sometimes, but I noticed that a lot of professors do that. Frankly, I hate chemistry, yet I pulled it together and still got a good grade. Chem 110 in general is set up poorly, but I think that Dr. Asbury did a fine job. Make an effort beyond attending lectures, & you'll be fine.

A nice guy who blows something up every class period which was good to keep me awake.  Could get boring at times, but hey it's chemistry.  He knows his stuff, and I feel that he prepared us well for the exams.
funny
Dr. Asbury is one of the best chemistry professors ive ever seen. This man is nice, funny and he loves to blow stuff up. What more could you ask for?

Dr. Asbury is a great guy, go to office hours so he gets to know you. He can explain an hour lecture in 5-10 mins at office hours. Only hard to pay attention because class is early. Reading the book helps a ton, got an A in this class...its not the teacher thats hard its the material. GO TO LION TUTORS CLASS. Worth the $30.

Dr. Asbury is a really nice guy.  But he doesn't always know what he's saying, or at least it seems like it.  I recommend using the book to help learn the material.  A plus for him though is that he likes to blow stuff up, so lectures are mildly entertaining.

I'm not exaggerating one bit when I say this guy is the worst professor I have ever had in my life. Trying to make sense of his lectures made me go insane. I finally quit going to his lecture and attended another professor's class which was the turning point for me. Otherwise, I would have really struggled in this class. Very unprepared, hard to un
He can not public speak. DO NOT take him as a prof for chem 110. The class isnt that bad if you go to class, read the book, and do all the homework.

I don't really think that he's confusing.  He does wander a bit, but if you pay attention the wanderings end up making sense w/ the material.  Very nice, and gets excited about chem. I thought he was a fine teacher, and learned a lot.

Nice guy, horrible public speaker.  I spent most of the time asleep in class but he does give useful examples that can help you with homework.  I suggest bringing a crossword or word search to class just to stay awake because otherwise it's near impossible.  On the plus side  there is many opportunities for help and the class is relatively easy.

Has potential to be a great teacher....very easy to get along with.  However, his lectures seem to be wandering and he really doesn't focus on things that will be on the test.  I ended up going to other chem classes (ahem...williams) to actually learn the material.  Probably did maybe 3 problems in class thus far. Its bearable, but not the best.
He is a great Teacher & is a very intelligent person.  I think he has a problem getting the class's attention all the time.  He is always willing to help-

Lectures are seriously pointless. He knows his stuff, but he def. can NOT teach it to anyone else. Tends to tell you something and move on without explaining what you need to know. Always puts examples that are the only thing helpful about lecture last and he always runs out of time for them. Don't take chem with him if you can avoid it.
good teacher learned a lot

this class sucks.  He is just like all of the chemistry department, they suck at teaching, and then they grade harshly, ruining many people's GPA.  The chemistry department seriously needs to reconsider how they grade, SOMETHING IS SERIOUSLY WRONG WHEN HALF THE CLASS EITHER DROPS OR FAILS THE CLASS!!!
He likes to show the overheads, tell you that you need to know the stuff that's on there, then moves on.  Lectures aren't much help, reading the book with that time is more helpful.

I disagree with those who say Asbury was a good lecturer.  For the 1st half of the semester (before I realized I was wasting my time)I went to every lecture and paid attention.  All I learned was that Asbury was a spectrocopist not a chemist and thats why he made so many mistakes during lecture.  He often lectures on completely irrelavent material.

he is a great teacher, if people would pay attention they would do better.  I was at every lecture and got an A, and a 95 on the final.  For those of you that say he is hard, the tests are made by the department not him.  He makes the subject fun.  COME TO CLASS.  COLLEGE IS HARD IN GENERAL.

Ignore those who are bitter because they did not do well in c12. Their grade is in no way tied to Dr. Asbury's ability to be a strong instructor in the classroom. I find Dr. Asbury to be an ok instructor, in an exceedingly difficult class. Dr. Asbury should not be faulted by the archaic tradition of c12 that causes many students to drop/fail.

I took this class as a buffer! lmao....I got the lowest grade in this one out of all my classes. He is a boring lecturer and doesnt explain concepts or give good examples. His monotone voice put me to sleep everytime I went to class and his notes were crap.
soo hard

Dr. Asbury was horrible! I breezed through ap chem with an A. I tested out of chem here, but took the course anyway, easy A right? WRONG! I will be lucky if I can pull off a C.  He talks in circles & confuses everyone. He's really smart, just can't lecture or teach. There was like 25 people in a 400 person lecture yesterday. DONT take this prof.

#1- he's not a chemist (he's a "spectropcopist" or some bs like that).  #2- he knows less about chemsitry than my dog.  His lectures are not only boring but also irrelavant.  I learned nothing from attending lecture.  I taught myself the course.  Chem 12 is hard enough, don't take it with Asbury.
acts like he's so smart but can't explain anything, leaves me more confused every time i go to lecture. massive tool who thinks he's funny.
Lectures are a waste of time.  The only reason i go is that he likes to blow stuff up and thats fun to watch.  Other than that lectures are a waste of time, just read the book.
He was the worst. He had complicated lectures notes and made even the most simplest things confusing.  I end up dropping this class.  Lectures were just time to sleep.
I lose knowledge by attending lectures

worst teacher ive had. i love chem and im decent at it but i dont like this prof at all. i went to a total of 5 lectures the whole semester and they were all the first 5 ones. i jus read the book and do the homeword and exams wit ease. i would rather read the book for 50 mins than sit in his lectures bc ill learn more.

Best professor i have had by far.  His lectures are fun, and he makes somewhat corny jokes.  It is very easy to come to hime and he tries his best to make the Chem lecture interesting.  If you can get him do it, really great.
very boring lectures
r u serious
fine teacher.  Humorous without telling any jokes.  very upbeat.  excellent explainations.
Very smart and gives great examples
Is he really a professor??

Austin Cramer is probably one of the best professors I've had so far. He truly cares about students and actually wants the best for them. In-class quizzes were very simple. Although he writes a lot, he likes to engage in conversation with his students and would help them understand if they actually ask. Very kind and sweet soul.

Cramer is pretty good. He's very laid back and nice. There are almost weekly quizzes that I will warn you about and his lectures are lengthy and can sometimes be explained simpler (I will admit the little history fun facts are neat). I would recommend him to anyone who already took calc, I'm not sure if he's the best for people new to calc 1!

He is a decent professor his lectures are good but he often over explains things to the point it would confused me. The class isn't all that difficult it is just very test heavy the homework assignments don't do much to boost your grade. He is definitely one of the better professor options for this course.

Math 140 was the first mathematics course of my college career, and I am genuinely grateful to have taken it with him. While he can be a bit reserved when lecturing in front of the class, he is exceptionally resourceful, patient, and supportive during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: THE GOAT, I did not go to most class, I missed quizzes, and some only homework yet I got an A. He is the nicest person I met at the uni so far.

I took calculus in high school and got an A, but now have a B- in the exact same course. Cramer severely overcomplicates lessons and tends to ramble about completely irrelevant topics based on his own interest in math. He's a nice person, but his teaching style sucks. And you can't read his notes AT ALL. Im warning you.

Austin is a grad student, and an amazingly caring teacher. He is extremely friendly in class and will help out a lot 1 on 1 as long as you are willing to ask. Textbook is mandatory, exams and quizzes are slightly easier than class material, and attendance is not taken. If you took AP Calc AB in HS, you will find this class pretty easy.

His lectures are pretty standard, you don't have to be there for every class if you're solid on Calc I things (he doesn't take attendance). He gives a heads up 4-6 days before the next quiz and exam (< also posted on canvas). He also informs students on resources they can use if his lectures aren't enough (office hours, LA session). :)

Overall pretty good professor but his notes are really illegible to read as he writes really fast and messy. Tests and quizzes are easier than what he lectures in class and he tends to overcomplicate things and add things in the notes that have no relevancy to the course. He does want students to succeed and gives extensions on things generously.

Overall he's a good professor, gives you lots of heads up for quizzes and tests, and tries his best to prepare you. But he's just not great at explaining simple calculus concepts. The simplest concepts seem impossible the way he explains them. My recommendation? Look up videos for the topic and do the homework. You'll be better off.

Gary Aurand is easily the worst professor I've ever had. He used chatgpt to help teach the class because he didn't know anything. He would assign homework despite never even attempting the problems himself, and then not help with the homework when asked in class. Not a tough grader at all though which is the only bonus.
Do not take

It is a little crazy how no one acknowledges that this professor seems checked out. He made some actionable comments when we first presented to him in 480, and we applied them, and we still did horrible. You wonder if he was just making comments because he had to or if he actually meant them. I know he wants to be nice, but his instruction is poor.

Students must know everything for all 4 experiments with no guidance. Your grade is based on several things, including CATME team ratings, 3 oral and 3 written reports, experimental plan presentations, excel prep, proper data collected from lab, etc. An "A" requires 93.00% despite the class difficulty. Gary also taught CHE470, still made it hard.

Terrible prof & takes it out on the students. If you had him for safety you haven't seen the real Gary. He has no idea what's going on but he will literally dig into you & be extremely demeaning when presenting your projects. He's also literally not qualified to be a professor, he has ZERO 1st author publications and took 10 years to get his PhD.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Graded by few things--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: He is the most miserable professor in the CH E department. He is a tenured teaching professor who cannot/does not want to teach. He grades based off of how he feels that day. He will conflict with his own feedback just so he can subtract points a second time. Genuinely doesn't care about the students or the class he teaches.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Gary is the worst professor in Chemical Engineering department. He has no adequate knowledge in the field and doesn't even know how to operate the most basic things on Aspen (required software for the course). He doesn't even know the requirements for the course most of the time. Without McFadden, students would be clueless in the course.
Clear and consise prof who gives good feedback and extensions if requested in advance. It's a lecture-based class, but everything can be found in Canvas for each assignment.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Textbook readings were a waste of time. Just focus on doing the discussions and adhering to the rubric guidelines for all written assignments and papers. I did not reach out to the professor much, only to review my papers if I had any questions. He was not available for most of the semester but it was ok overall.

Very useful class. Prof Ausherman is very helpful and makes his grading criteria clear, if you write down everything he says then you'll basically just be following a template to complete the assignments. He's always wiling to help in or out of class, and he's super reasonable. Attendance is taken every day with a paper passed around class.

Finished with a 94 but an A is a 95 and lost a third of a grade due to his attendance policy. It's clear cut in the syllabus and I was projected to end with an F because of missing 8 classes. He was understanding and cut me a break. His class is easy and gives you everything you need to know on the syllabus. Do not miss his class it will cost you.

Jim was a great professor! He made it very clear what he wanted from each assignment and made sure to answer any questions or help you needed on the assignments if you went to his office hours. He cared a lot about everyone's success in the class and moved a few assignment due dates around to make sure we could get them done. Highly recommend Jim!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very flexible and understanding. Always ready to help and give advice. From the beginning very clear on what is expected from the students and how are assignments graded. My favourite professor so far.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Writing assignments were very vague and the rubric seems non-existent. Takes forever to grade. I never knew what he wanted from us.

Jim's great! He really knows that his students are humans before students, meaning he's willing to accommodate mishaps that occur from time to time. I liked his lectures, they were pretty simple to follow. He can be a bit of a tough grader, but if you follow most of what he talks about in class and put some effort into your work, you'll be fine.

Learned a lot in this class. Jim is very nice and caring. Made the class interesting. Their was a total of 6 assignments which he gave a lot of time to do. Only complain would be that he takes forever to grade the assignments. He graded 4 out of 6 assignments during finals week. Recommend taking this class with him.

He does not grade in a timely manner. Just follow directions to the T and you will be fine. It is a lot of work discussion every week with 2 responses, a workshop and a project every week. I feel every class will consist of this but Ausherman is not an easy grader but not hard grader either.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--So many papers

reviews.comment: Jim is awesome! Definitely try to take ENG202 with him. His class isn't boring and he's really funny! Go to office hours or ask for help and he'll give you great tips in order to do well on the papers. Also, not an overwhelming amount of work (but this is a writing class so expect papers). Totally would take a class with him again!

Great teacher. Would go easy on students. If you can't submit an assignment before due date, just shoot him an email. He also cares about his families so when teaching schedules change, he would easily extend any due dates. However, he doesn't upload grades quickly, even in the end of semester. Not a tough grader unless you follow his instructions.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--SO MANY PAPERS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Many of the assignments were 'busy work' and didn't really teach me much. He is very strict with his grading scale- if you think you're going to get an easy A in this class, think again. His comments on your work don't provide much insight on how to improve and he is so slow on grading. Found out 60% of our grade in finals week - very disorganized.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Jim is a great professor and a cool guy. He is very helpful and would gladly help you prepare business papers even if you aren't in his class. He is understanding if you need an extension on a paper, but don't try to BS him. He is funny, but he is somewhat of a tough grader.

A previous commenter was spot on when he said his feedback doesn't give insight and that he is opinionated. I would add hyper critical. Tough grader and gives no latitude.  He provides no weekly class updates as he said he would. He always grades late. Very much do what I say, not what I do at least in this class.

A nice enough person and made class interesting. He is opinionated. Some of the grades he gives will leave you scratching your head. His comments on your work don't provide much insight on how to improve. If you're taking this class in the summer, try find someone else who will grade a little looser unless this is all you have to do for 6 weeks.
Best professor I ever had at penn state. He actually makes writing fun (I absolutely hate writing). His life stories are quite funny too, take him if you can!!!

I took English 202C with Jim years ago and thought he was pretty cool but never bothered to write a review until I realized today I was STILL using his strategies to write my PhD dissertation. Try to get him if you can! I actually learned things I still use!
Recommended. There is lots of writing, but tends to be more fun than the other 202C sections so it doesn't seem as bad. I've really enjoyed having him this semester.

Very friendly, supportive, and very clear and thorough in his requirements and explanations. Always eager to give help and comments during office hours. The lessons were truly interesting. He has high requirements, but if you plan on learning a lot, this is a class to take.
A very approachable and nice guy. Made an otherwise boring class quite droll and amusing. Take him if at all possible. You won't find another like him in the English department.
Jim is awesome, if you can get him for any class it's definitely worth it.  He's funny, laid back, flexible, and just overall a cool guy.  He makes the material interesting and worthwhile to learn.
Took a boring class and made it awesome, one of the best professors I've had at PSU.  Very clear and class is worth going to, because its entertaining.  I would highly recommend him.

Jim is a very good teacher. He's laid back, but still taught me a lot. He makes all the assignements understandable and is always available if you need to come in have him look at a paper. He's also really funny and made class worth coming to. Definitly try to get him as a teacher because he's really cool and can relate to all his students.

Great teacher, very laid back. Alot of classes we just talked about current events which had nothng to do with business writing, which i enjoyed. Class rarely went the full 1hr 15min, he also gave us plenty of days off to work on our assignments. Best class i had this semester by far!

this was definitely my favorite class. jim is an awesome teacher and grades fairly easily. we had alot of discussions on current topics in the news and such but that was fun too. sign up for one of jim's classes now and you won't regret it!

Great teacher, clear explanations of assignments, easy to meet deadlines, laid back personality plus he doesn't make you buy the book which saves money and he hands out detailed outlines of each individual assignment
Great professor, one of the best I had. Well spoken, easy to understand, no BS, very helpful.
This guy is the best. He grades pretty easy and is always availible for help if you need him. This was without a doubt the most enjoyable class i have taken in my 2 semesters at PSU

Great guy.  funny, relaxed, easy going and helpful.  he just seems to be a bit...too relaxed.  we didn't have to buy books, which saves money, but sometimes i wish i had something to refer to when doing these business letters and such.

He is a nice guy and he grades pretty reasonably.  As far as I can tell this was the only ENGL015 teacher who didn't assign any books to be read for his class.  You can't get an easier English 15 teacher.
Taught with passion and admiration toward chemistry, caring, and willing to take on any questions regarding the course.
really good
Very good TA and his way of explaining things helped me get good grades on tests.
The goat TA. Gets a little distracted but is overall great
He's actually a really funny TA and is surprisingly fantastic at teaching

Attendance was not manditory but definitely necessary to learn the material. Everything is on paper, and the class is lecture heavy. Prof Authier is nice and will switch to English if students are visibly confused. As long as you show up to class and take notes you should be fine, but the textbook also includes a lot of helpful information.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very knowledgeable professor but this class is very difficult. He doesn't use canvas at all or post grades, just gives you your graded exams back in class. This makes it hard to tell what your actual grade is. I wouldn't recommend taking FR 316 unless you have prior knowledge in linguistics. The material is really hard to follow.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class felt like a time warp to 1980 and not in a good way. No powerpoints, no use of Canvas, not even an overhead. Just writing paragraphs on the board over and over. This is fine unless you lose focus for even a second and suddenly you're lost and there's nothing to review. Only 3 exams so they're stressful. He's pretty friendly, has dad vibes.

Semantics was amazing and Authier made it so easy to understand, but you have to be in class or you will not understand. Good sense of humor, accessible outside of class, and very flexible. Only graded on a couple exams and a couple essays. No regular hw to hand in.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Prof Authier's lectures are amazing but you can't miss a day or you will be lost on that topic. That said, he is one of the best profs I've had, and he made it so easy to understand syntax. Would take him for every linguistics class if possible.

Professor Authier is super knowledgeable, but doesn't do a good job teaching students complex topics. His lectures are super unorganized and hard to follow as he just uses a whiteboard. You only have 2 exams and essays. Literally understood nothing. The course packet is in English and a good resource. Be prepared to teach yourself.

Prof. Authier was one of the nicest professors I ever had! His class is very lecture heavy, so to pass you MUST attend. The exams and quizzes are easy to understand as well, if you attend. This class made me interested in Linguistics as a whole, and is pretty easy on coursework! I recommend!

Prof Authier spends every class lecturing and there is almost no class participation. You just sit there and take notes while he talks. I was expecting there to be more opportunities for us to practice our French but I guess linguistics a different type of language class. He is really passionate about the subject and tries to make it interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: M. Authier is an awesome guy. He really wants you to learn the course concepts and will make sure to try and help you whenever you need it. Hard class due to the content itself, but he makes it as easy as he can. Three tests that are worth a lot and scattered quizzes throughout. Attendance isn't mandatory but you won't pass if you skip. Recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Probably the best professor I've ever had. Lectures are so interesting and very clear and specific. He includes so many examples so that you actually can understand the material. I've never taken linguistics and this has been the easiest class I've ever taken. So nice, so caring and passionate about the subject. Very reasonable.

Let's just say, it's hard to learn a complex discipline like linguistics in French. Dr. Authier does his best to explain everything clearly, but his lectures move quickly, and he continues with new material even when it's clear the class isn't following. Getting a good grade is doable, but you need to come to class and study for exams.

Incredibly passionate teacher. His life work is related to semantics so it was a pleasure learning from him. I was inspired by his knowledge on the subject which isn't my favorite, but was explained thoughtfully. Ask questions when confused. Appropriate toughness for a 400 level course.
The material in this class was really dry and very difficult at times, but the professor was always willing to clarify points and make sure we all understood.

FR316 is one of the hardest classes I've ever taken, but Authier is a great professor! He teaches in French but if the class is struggling he'll go into English until we understand. STUDY FOR HIS EXAMS AND GO TO THE REVIEW CLASSES. Attendance isn't mandatory but this isn't a class you want to miss. Overall a very helpful guy, highly recommend.

Although the material was difficult, he was always happy to help. I didn't pay as much attention in class as I should have but studied like crazy before the tests and did fairly well. I'd recommend taking a class with him if you can.
amazing professor, does reviews before the test that tell you pretty much everything you need to study for the tests

The class seemed like it would be impossible at first, but his notes are very clear and he knows the material very well.  As you attend class, and pay attention during exam reviews you should do fine.
Material will seem complicated during class but his reviews are extremely helpful when it comes to the exams.  Do not miss class the few days before the exam!
Very nice professor. Fairly easy class, as long as you attend.
Awesome!!! Take this class, you will learn a lot and have at the same time
cool and chill fun environment

Professor Autie is specific and communicative. The class consists of 4 papers with time lines and expectations clear. The only downside is the fact you cannot see your grade in Canvas throughout the semester, though that is the department's fault, not her's. She understands the stress and is always personable and accessible outside of class.

Professor Autie was great! She was extremely understanding and cares about her student's wellbeing. This class includes four papers and small lectures regarding the material. Attendance is mandatory, but the class is easygoing and not too stressful. She understands life as a college kid. I would 100% take her again!

Professor Autie is great. She's personable and specific. She gives clear directions, guidelines, and expectations. There are some readings but they're very short and minimal, she is very helpful with our 4 papers, and walks you through each step. If she taught other classes I would take them.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr.Audrey has obvious favorites. Her papers were easy but there was too many of them. It got really annoying because she wants things her way and only using her humor. Very weird hw assignments and prompts for essays.
Unbelievable hard grader. You could answer all her questions and still not get a perfect score.

Audrey was literally one of the best professors Ive ever had at PSU. She actually cares about helping you learn the material and how to write a well thought out research paper. She makes a really tough class worthwhile. She will actually give you constructive feedback rather than just leaving you to suffer like the rest of the English department
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Audrey is the best professor I have ever had the pleasure of learning from. Seriously, ever! I highly recommend going to her office hours as she will walk you through your papers and tell you exactly what she is looking for from you. This class was such a fun way to learn how to compose a research study!

Audrey is an eccentric, which makes for some very interesting discussions. The projects are difficult but doable and the general work is reasonable. She wants you to get a good grade, so go to her office hours with your rough drafts. She's very funny and the literature she chooses for analysis is diverse and engaging. You'll need and want to read.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Hilarious

reviews.comment: Best Teacher Ever!!!
THE SUBJECT IS DIFFICULT AND SOMEWHAT POORING BUT HE SUPPORT STUDENTS AND ALWAYS KIND WHEN COMMUNICATE WITH. FAIRIN GRADING AND HELPS YOUR EFFORTS TO IMPROVE YOUR GRADE

The quizzes are announced in advance and are really difficult. To do well on them is to actually do the assigned exercise problems (from which he selects the quiz question). Pro tip: the quiz problem he chooses tends to be from the end of the applicable problem set, so start at the back and work forward. Teaching is good, just class is hard.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Only saw him once a week, lectures were theory and not helpful at all. super boring. Half way thru I just stopped going and saw TA's the rest of the week. He was kind tho, I accidently missed my final and he let me retake it even tho i had a bad excuse. So he's nice and he might be better for other classes.

I had him for 211 and 212. He is not a great professor at all. Does not help his students and when you ask a question he interrupts you and doesn't answer the question. His grading is fair and there are quizzes every week.
Class material is boring and he doesn't make it any more interesting. Grading is very fair and straightforward. The quizzes and homework help a lot for the exams.
He is rude and always interrupts his students when they are asking a question. His lectures are very dull. It is an easy class as long as you look over the book. do not recommend him
Fantastic professor! The course itself is pretty difficult but his exams are all straight forward and his grading is extremely fair.

He is awesome. The class is terrible, but that's the subject's fault. He does a great job of explaining the material, and he cares about his students. Homework is graded and there are quizzes to help your grade-they are taken from the homework/example problems done in class. Exams were tough, but he did give a curve at the end of the semester.
The book for this class is horrible, too bad the homework is all from it. His exams were pretty straightforward though. Not a bad professor for a pretty hard class.

This class is ridiculous, and it's required. The prof is a real nice guy and will help you as much as he can. However, his teaching style isn't the best. He wrote his own "book" which was not comprehensible. It didn't cost us anything though. His HW is TOUGH and his exams are EVEN HARDER! He was easy on us though with grades, most people got A,A-

This class is ridiculous, and it's required. The prof is a really nice guy and will help you as much as he can. However, his teaching style isn't the best. He wrote his own "book" which was not comprehensible. It didn't cost us anything though. His HW is TOUGH and his exams are EVEN HARDER! He was easy on us though with grades, most people got A,A-

This was a quantum mechanics class, and it was bad. We didn't even have a book, he was writing his own. It wasn't really hard to get a decent grade, but it was impossible to understand any of the material. He just wrote equations non-stop for 50 minutes every class.
Clear explanations

I very smart person having a good technique of explanation to student. His is well organized and love to teach the subject. He brings the subject ideas in a sense that physics professors can not do. His target is to let his students to learn the subject more than other things.

Very knowledgable with material. Does a great job of explaining and will often make light of the difficulty/dullness of material. Takes a horrid class and makes it not so bad. I highly suggest going to his office hours and review sessions.

GOOD TEACHER. his lectures are clear and helpful to understanding the material. Homework can be hard but the TA's had sessions Sun-Thurs 7-10.  Exams are difficult but you are told what types of problems are on the test.  Still some questions you have no idea where to begin, but exams are graded very fair, as well as homework (effort usually).
