Austin is a very good guy and means well. He truly wants his students to exceed and to get good grades. Though at times, he can make things somewhat confusing, that is not very often and is always very responsive to questions you may have. He gives a lot of easy points and extra credit. Would definitely recommend him to my friends.

Austin is an awesome professor... definitely take his class if you have the option.  Easy 100% for class participation even if you don't always attend class.  SUPER ATTRACTIVE, SUPER SWEET, make sure you write down all of the examples he gives in class, and do the practice homework's.

I had 102 and 106 with him. After finishing 302, I can surmise that 102 did not set me up for 302. Whenever McLeod would say "you should've learned this in 102", it was a sure bet I wasn't taught it. In fact, I flipped through my 102 notes only to realize he never taught us DWL. I'm in 306 now and I'm scared. The plague has nothing on Boyle. AVOID!

I had a difficult time with Austin Boyle. I had always enjoyed Econ and found it fascinating, but after taking classes with him I am no longer interested in that field. I don't feel like his examples were that great and he didn't teach me all that much information.
Tests are tough so don't expect this course to be a piece of cake. It's not. Austin isn't that helpful either.

The first half of class, he is very easy and helpful, but as the material gets harder, so do the tests. I am an econ minor and I barely escaped with an A- but would try finding someone who is better at explaining.

If you have taken a statistics course before (state 200, or AP stat) this course will be a breeze. For those that haven't, you may want to consider taking another professor because Austin was quite confusing in his lectures and the people who hadn't taken a stat class before were completely lost.

Austin was a great teacher this semester. The lectures were long, but he offered engaging and occasionally funny examples to go along with the information. He also directs you to videos on his YouTube channel to revisit a tricky topic before an exam. He doesn't tolerate talking during class and worked to provide a good learning environment.

Austin is young and still learning the best way to lecture.  He has only been a professor for a few semesters.  Overall, the class is average.  Clickers are required for the class, but you only need 75% of the answers correct.  He gives homework, but like the clicker points, there will be more homework points available than needed.

I am happy to see that Austin is only teaching one Economics class next semester and not 106. I fell in love with Economics when Dirk Mateer taught my Econ 102 class in Fall 2012 and continued to enjoy knowledge provided by professor Goffe in 104. Now, I am unsure about my decision to major in Economics. I feel completely unprepared for Econ 306.

A good portion of my class would be very  disrespectful during the lecture.  I.E. talking, making noise, making jokes. He is not afraid to call them out in the middle of a lecture. It's pretty funny as long as he's not targeting you.

Professor Boyle is a great professor.  He really cares that his students understand the material and do well, and he's always looking for ways to improve his teaching.  He is always available during office hours.  His homework and tests are fair and the homework helps you learn the material.    It's not hard to get an A if you are willing to learn.
Hands down worst instructor in my three years here at PennState.

It is so easy to get a good grade in his class.  He gives plenty of opportunities for both clicker points and homework.  Go to class, fill out the course back, and study with the materials provided prior to exams and you'll do just fine.

I don't know why so many people are bashing Boyle on here. I had him this semester and got a 90% or above on all three tests simply by thoroughly completing the study guide and practice test he posted before each exam. It really was only about 3-5 hours of work for each exam, and it made the A easy to get. Homework and participation are easy points

The guy has good intentions but it simply comes down to this, he is a terrible teacher. Not a bad person; but just a horrid teacher. He is so confusing and bland it makes it nearly impossible to learn. I learned 99% of the class through the textbook. On top of all this, HIS TESTS ARE SO HARD. Save yourself some stress and take it with another prof

Honestly the clicker points and homeworkquizzes are an easy A. You only need like 60% of clicker points to get an 100 points and he gives out bonus. Same for homeworkquizzes 70%. The exams are pretty easy to get a B if you just look at the practice tests. They actual tests and practice are really similar. It's not hard to get an overall A.

I really enjoyed Econ 102 with Austin. I took it over the Summer and he was a very nice professor and I think he really wanted all of us to do well on the tests. His lectures definitely prepared us for the tests, and he gave us practice tests which were very similar to the tests we took. I  Definitely recommend him.
Lectures are in English, exams are in Chinese. I've never had an econ teacher who cared less  for their students. avoid if possible; if you're stuck with him, the textbook will be your best friend.

Austin Boyle lacks what it takes to be a good professor. Solicites students into giving him money; gives pointless examples and wastes time on useless examples. Also has a habit of getting his own questions wrong during lectures (which also does not help when you're struggling to understand the concepts yourself). His personality: cheeky, neurotic
Spent a lot of time of demonstrations that were unnecessary. Also a lot of things on his tests were not on the study guides. Do not recommend taking his class.

It takes an inexperienced breed to think he is a good professor. Clearly they have never taken more than 3 credits. Good professors don't waste class time with useless demonstrations, nor Poorly prepare students for exams, nor set em up to fail higher econs. No class "should" be easy but no class should have Austin teaching either. Avoid.

I was a little surprised by his initial rating I think its a little low. I thought he was a good professor. His lectures were always interesting and he makes class enjoyable. Economics is a boring subject to most people and he makes it at least worth attending his class everyday. His tests are tough so don't be stupid and study hard.

His lectures are interesting but sometimes don't help you understand his test questions. Clicker questions help out your grade and as long as you study for the tests you'll be okay. Not an easy A but a he is a really good professor.

He makes Econ interesting (which is sorta impossible) with hilarious examples. Nice guy and is not rude when answering questions, though his answers aren't helpful. When reviewing he will go into insane detail for a simple multiple choice question. My dad explained an entire 3 week lesson to me in 20 minutes over the phone. only reason I passed.

I took an Honors Economics class in high school which helped a lot, he flies by material doing one example and then moves on. I'm looking at a 92% in the class but thats because I worked my ass off outside of class. He made an intro to microeconomics class way harder than it had to be.
Not helpful at all. Whenever you ask him a question he never actually answers and he's rude about it. Request a different professor.

Knock knock! Who's there? Bad professor. Bad professor who? Bad professor Austin Boyle. Stay away. Condescending and boring. Class demonstrations don't help understand the material; they just waste time.

He makes the material harder than it needs to be. Usually he has a big class so it can become hard to pay attention. You will most likely have to learn the material yourself. Stay focused in the class and try not to play on your computer the whole time. His tests are really hard, you think you know the material until you take the test.
If you need proof of the failing education system in FL...here he is. Daily mistakes, and he is dismissive to his students. I Feel completely unprepared for 306.
Austin is a tough cookie test wise but he is extremely helpful. Examples used are hilarious. Besides that- he is super cute.. needs more flannel though.
Wait Austin's the best professor ever I don't know what you guys are talking about

Austin gives you all the tools you need to succeed, but won't do the work for you. The way any college class should be. Do the work, study for exams, and you will get an A. He tries his best to make the class interesting, which is pretty hard for Econ. He gave plenty of extra credit and even curved a small bit. But don't go in expecting an easy A.

This guy is a newer professor, so he's still learning how to teach.  That being said though, when I took him he constantly made mistakes in writing his own problems and showing how to solve his problems.  I'm taking the intermediate econ 306 now and i feel incredibly unprepared for it
Confusing and his exams are tough , final is impossible and doesn't curve a lot

Austin is great professor, and if you do the homework and review the exams you will be fine, it's not too hard. The clicker questions are boring however  because you may mess round if you get 2 questions wrong out of 3 in one question.

He's actually pretty interesting. Paying attention in class, getting the clicker questions right and submitting the assignments on time is crucial to getting an A. Also, read the book 2 days before the exam thoroughly once or twice and you should be good. The class in not overwhelming just redundant but fairly easy work.

I thought Prof. Boyle was awesome.  I have no clue why everyone seemed to hate him.  I came into econ 102 as a freshman with no exp. in economics.  Ny friends all complained about this class, but I thought it was easy.  20% of the grade is from clicker questions, and 15% is hw.  The tests can be difficult because you need to apply what he teaches.

I think Boyle really cares about his students he is just bad at teaching. I never paid attention to his lectures i just read the chapters from the book and usually got A's or B's on the exams. The material isn't hard you just have to put work in this class to get a good grade. The final is cumulative and tricky. If possible take another professor.

I thought Boyle was an interesting lecturer. If you go to class regularly, you'll do fine. His exams are a bit tricky, but some of the problems were right out of the practice exams and they're not impossible to prepare for.

Worst professor I've ever had. His exams are easy but his final is cumulative and impossible. He makes mistakes in class and on exams and has the worst attitude. Take class with a different professor if you can.
He's alright. The class is pretty easy to get a good grade in. Just show up and do the homework.

Clear in his presentations.  He's still young, but he is certainly improving.  The average grade listed here is B+.  That means his classes are definitely doable, and it's your own fault (not Austin's) if you don't get the grade you want.
Worst professor ever, take goldstein instead! Boyle teaches the wrong material

Grotesquely awful. I wrote Nittany Notes for this class, and his lectures still make little any sense to me. He makes mistakes all of the time, doesn't check his own work, and constantly distorts the order of the material. If I have to take Econ 306 with this guy, I think I'll cry.

As someone who had him for the whole year (102&106), I can definitively say, DO NOT TAKE 106 WITH HIM! In 102 you at least have a very useful book to work off of. In 106 he LITERALLY gives us the wrong formula every other class!! and We have to correct him (in class and his answer sheets)! btw, he's a lecturer, not a professor.

This guy is awesome. His teaching style is refreshing. Lot's of in-class examples, so if you learn by working through problems he is the best. He makes tough material easy. Very helpful during office hours. It seems a lot of people who give him a bad rep don't show up to class/pay attention... Hmmm... Honestly my favorite professor of all time.

Austin is definitely the worst of the ECON profs you could take this with. He has that new prof complex where he feels he needs to overcompensate his authority since he's young, and ends up just being a jerk. He is not helpful at all and will just belittle you in office hours. Take this class with anyone else.

DO NOT TAKE AUSTIN BOYLE AS A PROFESSOR. He is terrible at teaching his material, does not make class interesting, and thinks everything is the students' fault. If you ask questions he gets mad, if you don't he gets mad. His tests are unfairly difficult. If you MUST take him, be sure to get some extra help from tutors, nittany notes, ANYTHING.

As a new professor he had some kinks to work out but his lectures were always easy to follow.  Reading the book isn't mandatory but it definitely helped having some knowledge of the lecture before hand.  He always was extremely helpful in office hours.  Just be sure to not ask for a curve because then he definitely won't give one.

He was pretty cool. Everything he taught was self explanatory. Everyone complained at the end of the semester cause his tests were a little harder than the other professors teaching the course so watch out for that. Nothing he did was in anyway unfair though.

Seems like a really nice guy. Sorta reminds me of Michael Cera. Very little homework. Every class was a keynote though. Exams were really difficult too. For some reason, he likes to have three exams and a final instead of just two. Also, you never once use the book.

Econ isn't the easiest thing in the world but Dr. Boyle consolidates his material well; chapters will link seamlessly. PAY ATTENTION and ALWAYS print and bring the notes to class. Jot down any extra notes in class for an easy A. Tests are very fair and easy. He does not deserve the criticism people give him. His class is only for mature people.

You have to be willing to put the effort in. I read the chapters in the textbook and that helped me a lot for the tests. He also gives practice problems for his tests. First and second tests were easy. The third one was more difficult, but if you try, it is definitely possble. He's the hardest econ teacher but you can still get an A.
Follow the practice questions he posts and read the information at the end of each chapter in the book and you will get at least an A-

Though i got an A in the class I had to spend a lot of time reading the textbook and teaching myself. It was really hard to stay interested in his lectures and he wasn't that great at explaining the concepts. The homework assignments were also graded inconsistently by his TAs. Getting an A in this class is possible but hard.

Although I did enjoy Boyle's charisma, and interesting examples in class - I disagree that it is an easy A. As a not so great test taker, I found him extremely difficult. I could verbally explain everything in the course, but the multiple choice on tests absolutely killed me.

He isn't nearly as bad as everyone is making him out to be. He keeps class interesting and you can tell he cares about his students and getting better as a professor. Just show up, get the easy clicker points, pay attention and you will get a B.

You could tell that he knew his information but he was absolutely horrible at teaching. He read straight off the slides everyday during class and never tried to personally connect with the class. It was his first year teaching & you could definitely tell. If you want to get a good grade in this class take it with another professor.

Don't listen to all the mean comments. Boyle was very reasonable. Just read the book and go to class and you will be fine. His tests can be hard but he offered 4 extra credit opportunities and curved the class by 3 percent. He tries his best and is still getting the hang of teaching since it's his first year.

I was required to take this course as an engineering major, so right off the bat I was uninterested in economics and getting Austin Boyle as a teacher made it even worse. The tests were tough even with adequate preparation. I took my final exam on a lapboard in an auditorium with 1500 other kids, it was awful. Take it with someone else!

Great Professor. Not as easy as the other ones, but if you plan on minoring or majoring in Econ, this professor is extremely helpful and will get you to understand concepts very well (with the help of the textbook of course). Great course, great professor and a great challenge

Honestly this class was cake.  Professor Boyle was a great teacher and gave more than enough opportunities for extra credit and free points to boost your grades.  He taught larger classes this semester, but a lot of the students zoned out and did not bother to pay attention, but if you attend EVERY CLASS and PAY ATTENTION, you won't have a problem.

Boyle was okay--not great but not as bad as everyone says. His test questions are unclear, and he covers a lot of material, but he does fun demonstrations in class and gives a lot of extra credit opportunities. Attendance isn't mandatory but GO! You get a lot of points from clicker questions. If you can take another Econ teacher, you might want to.

Fantastic prof. I enjoyed all his lectures.  Austin makes things interesting, funny, and straightforward. Even if your in a large classroom, he's accessible if you need help or a TA for help. The students who complained are in for a very rude awakening; Austin is 100% devoted to teaching and if you pay attention, you'll agree with me.
Dr. Boyle was an awesome professor. If you go to class and go over all the slides before the tests you'll be fine. I don't think this class was very hard. I think he is a great teacher!

Dr. Boyle is Great! DO NOT listen to the upset kids that rate him so harshly just because he gives difficult exams. Austin is always helpful and genuinely cares about how his students do in class. Just attend class every day and PAY ATTENTION. You will be fine.

Austin is a great professor. He explains the things that you need to know, and he is always available by email or during office hours if you need help. He gave chances to grab extra points. You need to attend class to get clicker points. I got an A and I showed up to class for clicker points but mostly dozed off. The textbook helped a lot too.

Boyle was a great teacher and had very detailed explanations. Everyone that is complaining on here either did not go to class or did not read the book. I did not have the option to take econ in highschool and I got an A in his class. Just read the book and attend the lectures. Ignore all of the nasty comments!

Boyle was a great teacher. He tried making it fun and interesting which most teachers don't bother doing. He genuinely cared about our grades and if you're complaining about him, you probably know deep down that your grade is your fault and you could've studied harder. Most college classes are designed to teach yourself. Deal with it.

Boyle made the class a lot more difficult than it needed to be. Had I not taken AP Econ in high school, I would've probably done a lot worse. His lectures neglect to describe the graphs and a majority of the info needed on tests. If you have this class, don't expect to be taught, and be ready to teach yourself. Overall a hard class and bad prof

He's a alright guy, but his teaching is different. People are saying that these comments are from people who didn't work hard in the course which isn't true. I'm pretty sure majority did work hard because who wants to fail a class on purpose. If you like a professor who makes you really THINK, then he's for you, if not, find a different professor.

Probably one of the worst teachers I have ever had. He's a difficult teacher and all his lecture consists of are boring PowerPoints and extremely long examples that sometimes involve volunteers. Longest hour of my day. I recommend getting a different professor. Cumulative final and clicker questions based on correctness. Hard class. Low grade.

People are too hard on Boyle. He was a good teacher for being new to PSU. If you pay attention in class and study, it's an easy A. He tries hard to make sure students understand and does lots of interactive games. The homework is really easy, and the tests aren't too bad. Way nicer than other profs I've had.
He's like fine wine: he's going to need some time to mature and get better.

Not an Easy A, the tests were rather difficult even if prepared.  I'm not interested in Econ but it was as interesting as it could be, pretty interactive.  The professor did a good job and seemed to legitimately care.

So we all get it Boyle isn't the best professor. He has a fresh PhD and had to go back to teaching an intro level course. Although he's not so great at explaining, he tries very hard. He holds review sessions, plenty of office hours, and more than enough clickers and HW to improve your grade. Material isn't hard at all if you actually try.

Econ came easy to me in high school but Boyle makes everything more difficult and is not a good teacher. His classes were the only ones with a cumulative final (still not sure how that's allowed.) TAKE THIS CLASS WITH A DIFFERENT TEACHER.

I received an A- in this class, and I'll have to say, I was a better teacher than Mr. Boyle. He has the knowledge, however he has no idea how to convey it. Also, his clicker questions were based off correctness, unlike the other teachers. Also, he gave a cumulative final, unlike the other teachers. This would all be okay if he knew how to teach.
Compared to the other two econ professors Boyle's class is way to hard. He gives three test and a cumulative final. He uses long and useless examples in class that sometimes take the entire session.

He was not a bad teacher. Everyone complained that he was really hard and didn't teach at all but I disagree. The information was presented in a relatively clear way. He was very nice and if you visited his office hours he was very helpful and tried to get to know you. Overall, he was a good instructor and if you put in some effort you'll be fine.
Great Professor. Everyone that has rated him low was probably just looking for an easy A. Boyle was the most helpful professor I had this year, and I would definitely take his class again.

While this class challenging and at times frustrating, that's not entirely due to Austin. it's a difficult subject. if you go to office hours, he's a very nice guy who will help you in whatever way he can. It's difficult when he's teaching 600 students at once. People are too hard on him.

It's not that Boyle is impossible, it is just that the alternatives are way easier. Tests were worded weird and final was not bad, so I felt the class ended on an OK note. He could use some work, but we all have flaws. To me, the guys is OK. It's not the end of the world if you have Boyle, but you'll have to work harder for a lower grade.

Not quite as bad as everyone on here says. While he doesn't give curves attendance is 20% of the grade and he does give some extra credit. He posts the class powerpoints online and makes study guides for the tests, so he does try to help out. He can come off as rude in his emails. Probly not the best econ teacher at PSU but not terrible either.

Freshmen that took this class in Dr. Boyle's first year at the school seem to have a warped view of what to expect in college. Dr. Boyle was an exceptional professor in engagement and public speaking. The difficulty level of the class was a bit high, but certainly not a deal-breaker. Go to the lectures, read the darn textbook, and you'll be fine.
Great teacher. Interested in teaching the subject and helping students as much as possible.
The class itself sucks... don't take econ unless you want or have to. But Boyle was a great teacher. He was really into it and I loved listening to his lectures.

Worst teacher I have had at PSU. Insanely boring lectures and the tests are much harder than they need to be, while they also cover material that the other econ 102 teachers simply do not. Boyle is not friendly either. Do not take his class.

He's not THAT bad guys.  He could explain things in simpler terms to make comprehension easier.  The textbook was a real lifesaver right before exams as the author explains things in a simple way and has practice problems to better grasp the concepts.  Boyle's videos are a good change of pace though sometimes seemingly irrelevant to the topic.

I am reading so many comments which deride his teaching ability or choice on what material to cover for the final; Austin handled his first semester very well for handling over 1300 students.  It sad to see that his low ratings are coming from people who just don't have an interest in economics and wanted an easy Gen Ed.  He is a solid lecturer.

Boyle is an amazing professor. It annoys me that people complain about him because the other two Econ professors are "easier." He explains things very thoroughly and it is not difficult at all to get an A if you actually try and do not depend on Lion Tutors. Thought he was great!

I did well in this class but with absolutely no thanks to Boyle. It is not impossible to do well in this class but a lot harder than it should be for a gen ed typically taken by freshman. Clickers are worth a ridiculous amount of your grade and each test gets harder and harder, not to mention the final is cumulative (unlike any other econ class)

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS WITH AUSTIN BOYLE. Austin makes this class so complicated for absolutely no reason. Attending class is pointless because the examples he gives are so boring and difficult to understand. He also doesn't follow the same structure as the other econ102 classes.

This class was impossible. He isn't nice and he doesn't follow the same structure as the other economics professors. He is extremely difficult and going to class has been a waste of my time. I hate him and this class.

Austin obviously knows what he is talking about, but has no means of explaining it clearly to his students. I studied extremely hard for all the tests and received low scores. His test questions are all applied concepts, not what he taught us. Avoid this class at all costs.

Wow I can't believe he's rated so low. I guess everyone here must suck at econ, because I thought it was really easy. He's not the best at explaining stuff, but he's not that bad either. I give him some slack for managing a class of over 750 kids

ABSOLUTELY SO HARD. I am a senior taking this class and I study a lot and don't get anything more than a C on every exam. He does not take student's thoughts into consideration AT. ALL. Students complained of how hard it was and he didn't care. Doesn't explain things well, very boring lectures, doesn't answer emails, DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS W BOYLE

This class is nowhere near as        difficult as the reviews on here  make it out to be. Use Lion Tutors, the textbook, and the review questions Boyle posts online to study, and you will do fine. There are plenty of opportunities for points in this class so bombing a test meaning you can still get an A.
Not the best. Hard exams, LionTutors may help a little but please take another professor if you can. Save yourself
Not the best. Hard exams, LionTutors may help a little but please take another professor if you can!

Austin is not a bad teacher at all. He gives clear examples and uses feedback from students. Students are given essays and extra credit to boost their grades which is nice compared to just straight tests. The course material might be hard, but this is not at the fault of Austin. His powerpoint lecture notes are clear and prepare you for the tests.

What a joke of a professor. Heavy textbook use since listening to him isn't worth while. Got to go to class for cliker pts though. Take someone else. I'll probably get a B/B+, but no thanks to him. Youtube saved the semester.
No matter how hard I study I just don't do well on the exams and I attend all the classes :( Take someone else if possible.
it's ridiculous hard!!

This class is absolutely horrible. Boyle obviously knows what he is talking about, but he just can't explain it simply enough for students. This is an intro class and it does not feel like it. I take all the notes and study yet I do horribly on every exam
He can not teach and is rude.  Avoid this class at all costs
He does not care about his students.  His tests are 10000x harder than the work in class.  You need to be a genius to get an B-.

Austin Boyle is the worst teacher I have ever had. He is VERY rude and pompous. He reads off the slides, but really doesn't understand what he is teaching. If you go to office hours, he doesn't care if you are there.He has no interest in helping you. Do NOT take the class with him. Yes, you should be studying, but a teacher should be able to teach.

Take Dave Brown. Boyle gives 3 exams + a cumulative final. Brown gives 2 exams + a non-cumulative final. As far as I'm concerned, the hw is less for Brown as well. Additionally, Brown has experience teaching and is a lot better than Boyle.

Boyle is a very nice guy, he's new at Penn State and is trying his best this year but receiving a lot of complaints. If you go to class, complete ALL the homeworks and study for tests it's possible to get an A. There have been many times I didn't understand concepts he tried to explain, however with a little extra studying it's possible to succeed.

If you print out the lecture slides before class and just listen to what he says and write it down, this class will be easy for you. The people who have bad grades in this class try to copy the slides down on their own and miss important info. All it  requires to do well is studying the night before the exam. Many answers are from the powerpoints.

Confusing teacher but will probably improve (first year), but strongly suggest take another teacher as students in other two teachers course have it MUCH easier in terms of tests and grades and Boyle gave out a 3rd test (other teachers only two tests) on material not even apart of econ 102. If you take Boyle you will work harder for lower grade

Alright I'm pretty sure all the bad comments are from freshman business or comm majors. I'm a science major and this is also my easiest class. I attend class and do the homework's and barely study for tests and I have around an 80, its really not that bad. I heard the other professors are easier, but he's doing well for his first time teaching.
Don't take his class
Horrible teacher, not helpful at all. Aware that students to not understand material yet assigns homework and gives exams on it anyways. I would definitely not recommend taking Econ 102 with him.

Do not take him if you haven't taken an economics class before, he is horrible at explaining concepts. He focuses on the things that aren't even on the tests. He makes the multiple choice really hard, the questions are worded in confusing ways. He isn't much help outside of class, so prepare to teach everything to yourself. Easy homework though.

Austin is new at Penn State and doesn't have a clue about anything. His office hours aren't helpful because he just teaches things the exact same way and makes you feel stupid. He moves quickly and doesn't explain concepts well. TAKE A DIFFERENT PROFESSOR IF POSSIBLE.
Do yourselves a favor and take him after 2014.

Not a terribly difficult class if you take the time to study and pay attention during lecture. He could use some work on getting some of the concepts across, but overall not bad for his first year here.

He's a funny guy and a pretty good teacher. He likes doing demonstrations which makes class a lot more interesting. Attendance is pretty much mandatory though, so you have to go to class. The tests aren't that hard you just have to study. People get bad grades on the test because they don't study, so study for the the tests and you will be fine.

The powerpoints aren't very helpful and in lecture he moves through material so quickly you don't even have time to process it. He has very few office hours, and the TAs are COMPLETELY USELESS. Do not recommend. take someone else to make your life easier

Exams are way too hard for the introductory class level. Homework is graded inconsistently, Powerpoints are boring, fast paced, and difficult to understand. TA's are useless. Not to mention the ridiculous grading system based on "dollars", that makes it extremely difficult to know your grade. Stay away!

Not sure what all the complaints are. I'm an engineering major and this is the easiest class of my day. Prof is clear in his notes, funny guy, not much homework, exams are seriously easy if you do his study guide. He literally made the same questions and changed only the numbers. EASY EASY A+ IF YOU HAVE COMMON SENSE! Highly recommend this class.

His whole class is based on his power points and clicker questions. Don't do anyone's clicker questions for them because he walks around and checks. I wouldn't take this class if you had the choice. If you do go to lion tutors they help out alot.
Young guy who is funny as a person but bad as a teacher. His tests are confusing and answers are very alike. Take someone else if you can.

Honestly people, Austin is a good professor. His class isn't easy but it isn't hard either. Just read the chapters, pay attention in class, answer the clicker questions, and study before tests and there is no reason you shouldn't get an A.

One big thing about the class: you need clicker points. It is your saving grace. Exams are hard, Lion Tutors can't help you that much because he just started to teach at PSU. Nice guy overall, but when you go to his office hours he makes you feel like an idiot....so....try to get someone else, but not a bad guy. Work hard and you'll be okay.

Austin has a superiority complex about himself that you can sense almost every class. The power points are worded poorly and so are the clicker Q's. I have never had to use the textbook, mostly because he tells you it's worthless. Stay away at all costs.

Austin Boyle is hands down the worst professor I have ever had.  Whether it's his unorganized powerpoint presentations (which are all class, every class), confusing clicker questions, or wordy and tricky tests, no part of my experience has been good. Not to mention his grading is inconsistent to his rubrics.  If you can help it, DO NOT TAKE HIM!
he seems like a nice guy but the class is very hard. I went to Lion Tutors and studied in advance and yet I only got a 60 on the exam. If you have an option, don't take this class

Boyle is the worst teacher I've EVER had, and I've had some terrible teachers. He acts like hes taught forever, but hes way too young and doesn't teach anything He even told our class that it would look bad on him if everyone got an A. I study very hard and still fail the tests, he doesnt even know the answers to his own questions.

Austin is straight out of grad school and while may come off as a great guy outside of the classroom, he is a very poor professor. He does not pace the class correctly, over complicates basic concepts, and comes off very rude. I would not recommend you take this class with Austin. Geerling is a better choice.
This class is terrible. Take it with any other professor. Run away!! He goes to fast, doesn't clarify what he teaches, and the TA's are horrendous. Econ 102 shouldn't be this difficult.

This is a very hard class. Austin is new at teaching and I'm not sure if he is aware at how hard he is making the course. Clicker questions are difficult and graded. Homework is graded harshly. He moves very quickly in lecture. Pretty sure he doesn't give half credit on exam short answer questions. Hard to take notes during class.

Econ 102 is challenging, that would be the case with any teacher. The problems occur because he lectures for the entire class, he moves VERY quickly through the slides, and there is very little review (he is trying to add more review sessions before the tests.) He is a nice guy, and he is clearly trying. I hope his classes will get better soon.

Very boring. Powerpoint for full hour and 15 min. Very tough tests. First year teaching and doesn't really know how to transfer his knowledge to students. Give him time, but right now, don't take his class.

Such a bad teacher. I come to every class and have an extremely hard time understanding anything he says. I have a decent grade in the class, but i find myself learning everything on my own. Definitely do not take him if possible.

Apparently, you either like him or hate him. He posts the PowerPoints that he uses in class on Angel (incomplete so you kinda have to pay attention in class). He explains things fairly well, I think. He uses Clicker questions to check class participation. He has study guides for the exams so you actually know what you're supposed to study.

Rude and confusing. Posts incomplete lecture notes so you have no clue what you're trying to study for even if you attended class (which I always did). Probably going to have to drop because his class is not only incredibly difficult for no reason, but also severely boring. He's also the only professor I know of who uses the book.
Extremely difficult to understand, and rather rude when you try to email him or ask for help or simple answers. Would not recommend him to anyone.

Easy class if you show up to class each day and take notes.  I just review my notes a couple days before exams and only use the book when I'm confused on a topic.  With this seldom studying I got a 98 average on exams, however the class averages are around 75-80. Show up to class and review before exams and you'll be fine
His class is fair and he wants you to do well. Read the book and put the work in. You shouldn't need lion tutors in the first place.

Horrible teacher do not take this class with him. He goes way too fast and uses examples that are difficult to understand. This was his first year and you would expect that he would go easy to understand but he said this class is supposed to be hard. i went to lion tutors and understood it perfectly and then i didn't when i had to take the test.
Lectures are extrmely boring. He babbles on and makes nothing very clear. I studied his notes every day after class and still could not get above and 85%. Would not recommend him
Nice guy and relatively interesting.  He likes to use video clips, and his lecture is all powerpoint.  Its an easy class if you actually go and put in the work.  His tests can be a bit wordy.
Mildly interesting and pretty easy to understand.  There a times where he gets sidetracked but get off your phone and pay attention and you'll do just fine.

He's not the "best professor ever!". Give him a few more semesters and he'll have his teaching skills down. He knows his stuff but right now he's not good at communicating his knowledge to his students. The one "really bad" thing is that he can be condescending. There are better/more experienced econ professors but there are also worse ones.

Horrible professor. I asked him questions after class and his responses are extremely unclear. He gives clicker questions every day so attendance is mandatory, but those are confusing as well. He contradicts himself a lot and since he's newer there is no outside help besides Lion Tutors exam review once before every test.. DON'T TAKE HIS CLASS EVER
boring lectures. all powerpoint. very confusing

This was the hardest class I've ever taken. I highly advise against it. If this class isn't your main priority, you probably won't do very well. His exams all included 4 essays, except the final which had 8 essays. This doesn't include multiple choice, definitions, and fill in the blank questions. Do not take this class if you're mentally unwell.

Out of all the professors I've had so far, Dr. Dayrat is my favorite! He truly cares about his students and their success. He is always accessible outside of class and is willing to help.The lectures cover a lot of material, but attending office hours was very helpful. If you put in the work regularly, you'll be fine. Highly recommend this class!

AP Bio should be a Pre-Req since Dayrat expects his students to come with some understanding. Be ready to spend more time on bio than any peer not in 110H. You will spend long hours studying and memorize a lot of things beyond the science, like the history of it. He will push you far and you will learn a lot about work ethic. Take at your own risk.

Office hours are a non-negotiable must in this guys class. his honors course is easily one of the most difficult yet most interesting classes i have taken in my career. he is aware of the difficulty of this class and makes himself extremely accessible and genuinely wants you to succeed in and out of his class. genuinely cares about students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Dayrat has been my favorite teacher at Penn State so far. The content and lectures are dense with information, but if you regularly attend office hours, you will have no problem. Dr. Dayrat is very passionate about biology, and truly wants all of his students to succeed. It is a lot of work, but it is so worth it!

Take Dr. Dayrat! You might feel overwhelmed at first and that's completely normal, but he holds as much office hours as students want and will help you succeed if you're willing to put in the time outside of class. One of the most caring professors I've had, and he genuinely wants to see you succeed. Go to office hours and you'll be fine!

Dayrat really cares about the grades of his students and wants everyone to genuinely succeed. 110H was one of the most dense classes i have ever taken yet he made it insanely interesting. office hours are crucial.

LOVE Benoit. I actually took 484 and I adore the class. He will reward you if you make an effort to learn, regardless of ur grade. He expects greatness from his students, but it is very obtainable through effort and asking in OH. His compassionate, prepares you extremely well for exams, and tells you exactly what you need to know. TAKE HIM!

Dr. Dayrat is very passionate about what he teaches, so it is easy to listen to him lecture about it. Though you will have to put great amounts of effort into succeeding in his class, he gives you all the materials you need-- you only have to dedicate time. He has frequent office hours (almost every day), and wants all his students to succeed.

One of the nicest, most easily accessible professors. While his class is difficult, and requires you to go to office hours, he has an open door policy and will answer as many questions as you have. Grade is basically made of only exams (which are all short answer) but he gives you questions after every class that he only pulls exam questions from.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: History of Biology was an interesting class, however, it was poorly structured. There are 3 tests, the second and third are cumulative because he doesn't want you to "forget about the material". There's a final project that you choose to be either a final paper or presentation. Only take this class if you're really into the history of science.
Hard grader. Mean sometimes

I took CAS 100 online and Dr. Lori gave me 100's on ALL of my speeches. She does give readings to the online text book, you don't have to read, just skip ahead to the assignment, check out what terms it references, then search for those in the reading.

Professor Bedell is hands down the best professor I've had at Penn State. I was afraid of going to office hours at first, but she is so compassionate, and you can tell that she cares what's going on in her students' lives. That being said, there are a few assignments worth a lot of points, and if you're not on top of it your grade can drop quickly.

Professor Bedell was by far the most infuriating professors or person I have ever met. She picks favorites, so if you aren't one good luck. She pretends to care about issues but is nothing in the way of accommodation. That's the best way to describe her, fake. Whatever you do please don't take her if you care about your mental health or sanity.

Tough grader compared to other CAS137H professors. Going to *her* directly to make sure you're on the right track (outside of class) is really important- have assignment drafts done ahead of time to get good feedback. If she points something out and you fix it in submission, it's noticed. Had to spend a lot of time on this class but it's worth it!

Awesome teacher! She is not afraid to share her political beliefs, but she does not oppose it on her class. The assignments she gives are thoughtful and I learn a lot from them. Would recommend for everyone!

She can be a tough grader for written assignments, but she's fair with it. Lori is extremely easy to talk to and get along with. People say her office hours are extremely useful, but you can do fine without them. Get to know her, and you'll do fine figuring out how she grades. Very likeable and funny

Like other reviews, I encourage going to her office hours (esp for big projects) and taking her advice to heart when completing assignments. In addition to passion+RCL blogs, you also have a civic issue blog, so choose your issue wisely. She can be flexible w/ deadlines if you email her in advance + others in class express wanting an extension too

Good class atmo 10/10 Some of the readings seemed a bit long and redundant, but that might be more of a personal qualm. You're not really tested on them, though. Advice: There are 3 main units with major assignments in each. Talk to her about each one so she can give you advice on your work, and try to incorporate her advice into your project.

A harsh and biased grader; office hours is a must in the beginning of the semester so she knows you care, and she grades papers extremely harshly. Even if you miss one class, your participation grade will drop. One of the most stressful classes I had in the semester, but once you're on her good side, you're basically guaranteed a good grade.
Professor Bedell is a tough grader. She made a 101 course harder than a 300 level course. More assignments than 400 level courses. The average grade for our paper is around70 out of 100. AVOID!!!
Professor Bedell is by far the most immature person and professor I have ever met. She only grades you based on how much she likes you and is so unfair with her grading. Never take her classes.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lori Bedell is an amazing professor and in my opinion person. She really cares about her students and their work! She will push you out of your comfort zone but go to her office hours and ask for guidance. Its an honors class so its going to be hard but having a good relationship with her and trying your hardest will get you a good grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Overall, a nice class and a solid professor. Make sure to check your grammar on papers, space out the workload (which isn't that bad), and participate once in a while. Attend specifically her office hours, hopefully once per unit. When you choose a topic for a passion blog, make sure it's one you actually enjoy writing about and is broad enough.

Class was really interesting since she brought so many interesting guests on to talk about democracy. Lori was a really fun person to talk to and have as a professor! She was open to having a lot of different conversations, and tried to make the 2 hour class not so draining. Also uploaded textbook for us so that was great.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: I would never take her class ever again. I have had other professors in this field and have written extended research papers in the past. That being said, none of those professors compared to how harsh and subjective her grading was. I felt that most of my work was B quality or higher but I received a C at most for her assignments. DO NOT TAKE!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: One of the most difficult professors I have ever had. Impossible to please, expect emails every single day. Cant predict how you will do on assignments because it may be her grading it or it may be a TA. Overall ridiculous for a gen ed class and would not recommend taking, not worth the frustration.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Lecture heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Straight up mean and inconsiderate person. She puts on a fake attitude of caring and helpful, and refuses to help/grade accordingly for her students. The amount of effort Ive put into essays that she has graded as sub-par is insane, especially when I thought I did very well. Even the writing center and her TAs agree but she refuses to grade right
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Professor Bedell is a very kind women, but she is a VERY harsh grader!!! I worked for months on a paper and got an average grade because she thought it seemed rushed even though I considered it one of the best research papers Ive ever written. If you dont need the class, its not worth the stress in my opinion.

Dont take classes with her. Don't and don't. Just don't. WORST prof of your choice. She gives a lot of work and grades on how her personal preference for you not how you present your work. Never be reasonable, she always gives you some random nonsense reason to get off your points.

This class is awful. So many essays with little help from Bedell or the TAs. There is no help, even from office hours and one-on-one conversations in class with her. Beware your own opinion, because if it does not assimilate with her authoritarian left viewpoint, you will not get a good grade. I was excited for this class and left very disappointed
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--So many papers

reviews.comment: Dr. Bedell is one of the best professors I have met on Penn State's campus. She is very kind to her students and tries to make lectures exciting as well as interesting. My biggest advice for this class would be to use her office hours! Even if it is just to run an idea for one of the class projects by her, they are super useful!

She's nice in person and in class, but don't let that fool you. She will hound you for everything through her grading. For RCL, take any other professor, as they would be much more reasonable and caring (based on accounts from my friends).
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Lori is by far the best professor I've had at Penn State thus far. Though she does grade harshly, if you ask for help when you need it you'll be fine! I found that office hours really helped me run my ideas by her to make sure I was on track for the projects. I've learned so much from this class.

She is really nice but you have to earn every point in that class. The advice I would give you is talk to her about the assignment you are currently working on. She is very particular in what she wants to see so the safest way to earn a good grade is to ask her what she wants to see. Also, you can get away without the book. You talk about it twice.

Lori is one of those profs who make you feel passionate about learning. The textbook is used early in the semester and then forgotten about, and readings are not usually assigned. I had to put a lot of work into this class, but it paid off. Her office hours are helpful. Treat every major project like it's your life's work and you'll get an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Lori is passionate about this class. Her lectures are pretty good, but when it comes to grading, that's where she'll get you. She has no problem giving you a terrible grade and being non-transparent about it, even refusing to meet to discuss the grade and will never admit she is wrong. If you don't want to work unnecessarily hard take someone else
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Lori genuinely cares about her students and, as long as you show genuine interest and that you care about her class, is exceptionally patient, understanding, and helpful. She's a great person to have in your court and will help you find opportunities outside of the classroom if you take the time to get to know her and seek challenges.

She really cares about her classes, and it shows in her lectures. That being said, she grades really tough, so going to her office hours can help. You will have to write essays, give presentations, and create a long (7-10 minute) video for this class, but she gives you enough time to work on each.

I dreaded this class because oral presentations make me EXTREMELY nervous. However, Professor Bedell made this 8am class enjoyable! If you work hard and go to her office hours for extra help, it'll pay off. Her feedback is very good and she helps you come up with creative ideas for your assignments. Super caring and extremely thorough :)

Really great teacher and person! Super easy to talk to and gives really great advice IF you ask for it!! Take advantage of her office hours because I found them to be extremely helpful. Lectures are engaging and inspirational (even at 8 am). Participation is important and when it comes to the group project, for the love of God distribute the work.
She is really nice and very inspirational. I learned a lot form this class!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Lori comes across as very kind and calm, but beware: if you dare disagree with her, she has no problem arguing a nonsensical argument back at you and not making ANY logical points - and then pulling the superiority, seniority card.  She picks favorites super early in the year and is not at all transparent in her grading. bad.
reviews.rating_tags: SO MANY PAPERS--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: In CAS138T, Lori seems to grade based upon an "I like you" scale. Grading in English is always subjective, but there was definitely a difference in grading based upon her opinions of students.

Lori is two different people. In person, she is sweet and understanding. However, when you get your papers back, she always writes comments like, "you could do better" or "this isn't your best work." Your grades will not reflect the amount of effort you put into the class. I advise you to take a different professor. She also is a know-it-all.
One of the best classes I took here. Just make sure to always attend.

Bedell's lectures are great. She gives great examples that her students can connect and relate to. She's very passionate about the subject and knows what she is talking about. When giving feedback she often says one thing and then the grade you receive says another, but she's always there for help. She even let us rewrite one of our major papers.

She is an extremely tough grader and not lenient at all. She may seem like a very friendly and nice prof but do not get fooled! I can't agree more on the students who says that she has only one standard about whether it is a good speech or not, that is her own's. You will get a very bad grade if it is not something she wants even if you give effort

Professor Bedell is extremely nice and helpful. She makes a course that many math/science students dread engaging and fairly easy. That being said my only criticism would be with her feedback on papers. Many students in my class had positive rough draft feedback and then got bad grades when submitted. Luckily, she lets you rewrite one paper!

CAS 138T is like a less stressful and more interesting 137H. Lori definitely makes the class better. She tries to provide real world examples to the students. She is a really good professor, but it definitely took me a while to get into the groove of her grading. Sometimes, it is unclear exactly what is expected.

Very tough and unclear grader. She will encourage you and assure you your work is going well but then her grade will not reflect her previous comments. Her expectations are confusing and will leave even the best English student struggling

She's a pretty good professor. She's a very nice person and doesn't seem like she wants kids to do bad. But this is an Honors class and honestly there's quite a bit of work. She made it more interesting than inundating though. I'd recommend it especially if you need the Honors credit. But you can't just do nothing and get an A. I'd say to take it.

Lori Bedell -although not a PhD- takes the PhD attitude to a whole new level. She considers herself an expert and makes it known. Best advice I can give you, is to consult her opinion on everything. Because as you will find, her opinion is the only valid one. She considers herself an intellectual but acts like a child when confronted. Best of luck.
She is so nice and understanding. If you actually put some effort you will good a good grade.
She really made the class easy and fun rather than stressful and frightening. I liked attending her class, and the homework was easy. She is really helpful and flexible when it comes to grading.
I don't know how is she on fall and spring but on summer she's such a great teacher. She made the class enjoyable and it was one of the best classes that I have ever take at penn state.

Miss. Bedell is a wonderful instructor, but her incessant need to use controversial topics as examples of rhetoric; is an especially distracting way to teach the material. Her method of grading each assignment varies, and she often gives very vague reasons for points taken off, such as: "I don't like this", "I was expecting something different"

She is very political in her lectures, which would bother me way more if I was more to the right. She has a very my way or the highway attitude. Also, she is very vague on what she wants for projects and papers which hurt my grade.
Very sweet lady.

Lori is one of the Best CAS professors I have had at penn state. I didn't buy the book and didn't need to. Go to glass for the random participation exercises and the also the workshop class on fridays. If you follow her study guides, you cannot fail her tests. Two papers and two tests was not bad at all. Take her if you want to learn.

Lori is a great professor. If you attend class she notices and tries to help you out any way she can. People who dont show up or put the time into the class are the ones with the bad grades. Just show up, pay attention, and follow rubrics for the papers and you will be smooth sailing in her class. Dont listen to people who dont try in school.
She's an incredibly generous and kind person, yet her first year seminar class is not easy by any means. trust me on this one.
Not just an awesome teacher, but also an incredible person.  Do everything in your power to take CAS 100(H) with her.  Wait three years if you have to.  It's worth it.

Ok well I didn't get the grade that I wanted, and the minute response were annoying, but I think it's unfair to say that Lori WANTS her students to fail. Anyone who thinks this must not have paid too much attention in class, which probably resulted in a bad grade, which may also the negative review...

Lori Bedell may look and talk like a sweet lady... WRONG! She reads off her powerpoint slides that do not make sense so quickly you have no time to process. She is a ruthless grader with obscene fill in the blank exams. She is very unfair She wants her students to fail! Don't let it be YOU!  BLAH

Don't listen to the person who wrote the 4/25/10 review. This class wasn't THAT bad. If you're looking for an easy BS class, then maybe you shouldn't take it with her. Maybe you shouldn't even be in college. If you're looking for a class that challenges you and pushes you to do your best, take Lori. She actually teaches you.

worst professor at PSU-- talks down to students. i could do her job: she reads straight from power points which summarize the textbook. vague grading style; tests require you to remember power points word-for-word.getting an A, but could have saved a lot of suffering if i took this class with someone else. AVOID, there are far better CAS profs.

Depending on your fellow students, the class can be fun. As a professor she is alright. She is entertaining but her politics does seep through and if you have views on the far right, you may get annoyed at her sometimes. Otherwise, i took a CAS100 class that happened to be Honors and I did alright. So if you need a speech class she is alright.

She's a very nice woman.  She's also highly opinionated, and an extremely tough grader.  If she doesn't like you, she'll crucify you.  I got a grade much lower than the one I deserved, and she basically admitted it.  Don't take her.

Such a nice lady. She's not necessarily an easy teacher, but she is fair. Also, she really cares about her students and hopes that they do well. She is into politics, ethics, and the media so expect some discussion about current events. I would definitely recommend her class to anyone. She's just a nice woman.

Wonderful professor.  Definitely a tough grader but it's worth it.  This class is so much more than a speaking class.  It opened my eyes to a lot of ethical topics and to politics.  Making a point to see her in office hours really helps.  Take her section!

One of the best professors i've ever had.  She took a class I wasn't looking forward to at all and made it into a class where I looked forward to going.  She's a genuinely nice person as well.  Lectures are clear and you know what she expects.  You are a fool if you don't schedule her section!

I really loved this class. Don't listen to the reviews with grading. She grades fair and she asks for people do be different in their approach for speeches. The OLLE Assignments aren't hard at all. The final is open notes, which was ok. Just read the questions carefully on the exam. Speeches were fun. She is a great teacher.

Lori is a great teacher! Her office hours are great and she is always willing to help. Don't listen to others about the grading. She's a fair grader. She is super nice and always pleasant. Great teacher for CAS

A really nice woman.  She's not the easiest grader, but is fair and consistent.  The best thing about this class is that there's no busywork.  You also get a bunch of free points from journals and attending a forum discussion.  I would definitely recommend her as a cas teacher.
She's a hard teacher, don't let her outward niceness fool you. She's good though, but very VERY rough grader for speaches. Be wary and take someone else for an Easy A rather than the C+ I got.

Lori was one of the nicest teachers i've ever had. She made the class SO much fun. I really enjoyed going. She graded very fairly on speeches and made it possible to do well in the course. She was entertaining and very flexible with things. Lori ROCKED!!!!

One of the best teachers I have had at Penn State. She actually cares about and knows her students. The number of speeches is reasonable, and she gives constructive advice for all of them. Very organized, and always there to help.

A sincerely concerned instructor.  Make sure you get feed back and participate in class discussions and critiques.  Try to be different and stand out somehow in the class.  Otherwise, a great person and decent teacher.
Just an awesome teacher - such a nice and wonderful lady.  So much energy and love for her students, made you really feel welcomed in class. Would love to take again!

It really is hard to figure out what she wants from you on your speeches and projects.  I had things that I followed to the T and found out that I had done something wrong.  She'll tell you what you did worng, but check on what you need to do before you present anything.  GET FEEDBACK FROM HER!!
Lori is absolutely lovely. Sometimes her grading is a little confusing, but if you ask her about it, she'll be happy to explain.  I would LOVE to take a class from her again sometime.
Lori is wonderful. She is so nice and caring. I would take her for any class.

I thought I'd hate this class but it was really fun to go to.  It was one of the only classes I really tried not to miss.  You get a ton of info on the assignemtns so I don't think Lori was unclear.  I really like the political discussions.
I thought Lori was an awesome teacher.  I do agree that you need to go meet with her after class to see what she really wants for speeches, but overall great teacher.

Lori cares about her students, but is unclear in what she wants for your projects.  If you take her class, be sure to meet with her to get exact specifications, otherwise, expect poor grades and repeated dissappointment.
No Comments

She is a very nice woman who cares about the success of students. After the first exam I emailed her about the questions I got wrong and she immediately responded with a very long, detailed, and thoughtful message. Compared to Orgo 1 with Funk, this class has many more opportunities to keep your grade up. Definitely recommend her over anyone else.

Nice woman. She wants her students to do well. Class is heavily curved. I would say one thing is she holds off on posting keys for study materials until a day before the exam, which doesn't help. It would be more beneficial to have access to the keys.

Pros: Grades things very quickly by hand especially for how many people are in class, class is heavily curved, extra credit surveys, overall friendly and understanding 
Cons: Frequent mistakes in material (usually TA/LA stuff), all or nothing questions where you get a 0 even if 99% of structure is correct, unclear grading on exams

I think this class was structured fairly and the grading criteria was very clear. She was very willing to help and wanted her students to do well. The exams could be difficult , however they were very doable as long as you put in the effort.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I absolutely loved her. I don't know why she has so many bad reviews. I had her Spring 2025. She is a wonderful woman and a great teacher. She uses master's note packets and the class is curved a lot. If you put in the effort you will do fine.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The worst teacher I have ever had. Her notes/study material often have the wrong answers. She is an extremely harsh and inconsistent grader. There are 5 total homework assignments for the whole class so if you struggle on the exams (all open-ended) there is very little material to help you prepare or bring your grade up. DON'T TAKE EVER!!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I am a strong chem student(never received below an A- in any other chem). I have spent days leading up to exams completing practice exams and watching review sessions, yet get to the test to find the methods taught in class are now incorrect and we were supposed to know content never covered anywhere in class/recitation/homework.

There are no GSG sessions, no Learning Communities, and barely any practice problems. Homework is   timed. It is week 6 and there are no grades in. Her notes are incorrect. You can follow an exact mechanism from the notes and get it completely wrong on the exam, as did I. This class sets you up for failure.

Compared to CHEM 210, 212 with Elacqua felt significantly easier. Her lectures go over each concept methodically so you understand, but you will NEED to keep practicing after class ends. Form study groups regularly, and ask questions when possible. You will struggle if you don't put in the work, but you have plenty of resources.

Orgo in itself is hard, but this class makes it very hard to learn and pass. Elaqua is fine, I haven't seen any incorrect notes from her, only from TA's. There are VERY little study materials, most are posted about 3 to 1 days before exams. There are only 3 homework grades. This is a newer class format though, and every semester has differences.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Elacqua rarely gave extra practice other than the three homework assignments prior to the exam. She often made mistakes in class and did not correct herself which led to a lot of mistakes during exams. She also did not host office hours, so you were mainly reliant of the TA and the LAs for help outside of class
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was hard, but it is orgo 2 so that makes sense. Offered a bunch of extra credit (+5.5% to overall grade). Will do fine as long as you stay on top of the material and study a few hours. Elacqua had incorrect content in the notes, but if you got points off you could send them an email and get them back. The TA was an amazing resource.

She was actually horrible. You cannot trust anything that comes out of her mouth. Hint: every time she says something will not be on the exam it actually will be! Wish I knew that! She talks bad about Funk even though his class gets exam grades 10-15% higher than her class. She gives zero preparation for exams.

The course is hard by nature, but the difficulty in course material in no way explains how another professor, teaching the SAME material, has averages 20 to 30% higher. Elacqua is a nice person - but the grading is inconsistent and there were instances the notes SHE posted were incorrect and students were penalized for studying these notes.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Tough class, and even more difficult when there's no practice material. Very nice person, not a great professor as the exam averages were a 50%. Lots of extra credit because loads of failing grades though. Get ready to teach yourself a lot of the material & ask questions. Good luck is all I have to say.

She is a nice professor, but not good compared to other professors, as our exam average is ~20% lower than the other sections's. The graders for the homeworks do not seem well coordinated and she has taught us wrong material that she penalizes us for even though we learned this in lecture. Shout out to the TA Cordelia though, they are much better.

Teaches things wrong in lectures and will take off points on exams when we did it the way she taught us and grades inconsistently. Will say she doesn't want to trick us on exams but then puts questions on exams that we were never taught and labels the questions as being "never taught". Extra credit but that's only bc of the amazing TA Cordelia.
Nice woman, however the first exam average was a 53%.

Great lectures, respects student feedback, and answers all questions that are posed. Dr. Elacqua presents the information in a way in which recognizing patterns is emphasized over memorization. Dr. Elacqua is also passionate about the subject, and it shows in the lectures.

I took GEOSC 50 with him. He was okay, the readings were a lot. It was difficult to understand the content due to the fact it was only reading, no recorded lectures. Probably wouldn't take if you don't like lots of reading.

Reading discussions monday and quizzes friday. I think he took the critiques on this page to heart and the exams were open book, online. He was a fine professor, this was a simple gen-ed where he cared. Two projects too you should 100% get out of the way early. Says to buy a textbook, but most quizzes are common sense.

Awful class!!! 3 exams make up 60% of your grade. Lectures are completely useless as all he does is go over graphs that a 4th grader could interpret and does nothing to prepare you for exams. Read the textbook heavily, as he will pull the smallest details on exams, despite never being in lecture. He is also very rude if you have to contact him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: All he does is read read read. The quizzes (that are worth 40% of your grade) are so complex and don't talk about anything that you learned in class. THE AVERAGES ON ALL THE QUIZZES IS A 65... and he offers no curve or extra credit... that should tell you something. I took this class because I thought it was easy but it just brought my GPA down.
I'm not Betsy. She's fantastic!
Professor Campbell is kind to your face, but you have to do and complete everything in particularly her way only. Her LA's were helpful.

The TA's do all of the grading of assignments. Prof. Campbell is kind, however, most of the learning I did in this class was from reading the textbook, and not from her lectures. She was very strict about technology and we weren't even allowed to use laptops. Be prepared to have to participate every class. Exit tickets sometimes for attendance.

The TA's are the ones who do everything for the class and are super nice and helpful. The professor herself treats everyone like teenagers with her no tech policy and will legit yell out at you in front of everyone. The class is very easy with most assignments being simple but some of them especially the final project lack proper instructions.

basically the class is beyond easy and i passed with a 99 because the TAs do all of the grading and she does nothing but she is AWFUL at her job and forces u to speak in class, honestly i do recommend this course bc of how easy it is to get a good grade but she made it so hard to get up in the morning to attend and sit through
horrible person. i can tell she hasn't gotten done (if you know what i mean) in a while becauses shes so cranky in class.

She swears shes smarter than everyone in the room and acts that way but I guarantee you she is just compensating because she doesn't get any respect from her students. I feel bad for her really because her life must suck a lot if she is just talking about herself all the time and her experiences. I hope she never teaches a class again in her life.

Betsy was the most confusing professor I have ever had. She catcalls on people and has a no technology policy which is weird in the IST college. But going past that her lectures aren't very interesting and be prepared for random in class participation. IST 110 is the easiest class ever, TAKE IT just not with Campbell.

I wish I could give her a 0. Worst professor I have ever had, extremely rude and belittling/disrespectful to students. Treats everyone like an incompetent elementary school student. Cold calls the entire class, lots and lots of pointless busy work, but it's super easy. Thankful for the TAs at least, but I can't believe she is allowed to teach.

I was really trying to like Professor Campbell, but her classroom policies and final project made me write this review. First of all, her no-technology policy was fine with me until she started making such a big deal of it that it became more of a distraction than technology itself. The work is easy busy work. The final project is very ambiguous.

The TAs are very helpful when it comes to completing assignments and if you attend class you will be able to follow along fairly easily. 

However, Betsy is an absolute nightmare and I'm not sure how she is allowed to continue teaching here. She shows no interest in connecting with students. She will call you out and speak at you like you're dumb.
beware to be called on and speak during lectures

I want to emphasize first that IST110 is one of the easiest classes I have ever taken. In regards to her, she should not be allowed to teach college students. She treats the class like a bunch of middle schoolers and will literally yell at you if you have your phone or laptop out during class. She also left to Tunisia 2 weeks into class.

I took IST402. This course requires participation, or you risk losing upwards of 8% of your grade for one missed class. She's unresponsive to emails. I tried for a week to get in contact with no success. She's stubborn about attendance, regardless if you feel sick or are unable to come due to external conditions. There are no exceptions in her book

Easy coarse, terrible teaching style. The work is easy, but she treats her students like they are children. No phones (which I can respect), but she obsesses over this it becomes a big distraction. Be ready to participate, go to class. If you need to take this you will be fine. If she reduced the antics she would be a fine professor.

Dr. Campbell is not the professor to take if you want to enjoy learning about IST. All of the information covered in this class is very surface-level and not hard to grasp, yet you would think that she does not fully understand any of the topics that she is talking about.

One of the worst classes I have ever taken in my life. Had her for IST 402 which is about dancing with robots. First half the semester is her cold calling on 15+ page readings. She does not make this better as she forces you to dance in class and eventually a public performance dancing with a robot. Whole semester felt like a humiliation ritual.

Lectures are boring and are pointless. No phones or computers you will get called out for it. Attendance not mandatory but there are random exit tickets. She cold calls and makes snarky comments if you don't know the answers. The directions are unclear for most assignments. AVOID THIS PROFESSOR

Professor Campbell isn't terrible, the reviews seem to be by people that have been wronged by her. She is strict and doesn't allow phones or computers (when not being used for an assignment) to be out during class. She can be a little mean but it won't affect your grade. Take IST 110 for easy busywork and a high grade.

Please understand i cant use the language i want here, otherwise this post will be removed. Took her for IST402. Might be the worst professor i have ever taken. She doesn't help at all, tells you to put your phones away. Doesn't actually teach anything. She is the least understanding one i have so far. She ruined my entire sem and my mental health.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I gave her a one before, but I started skipping class, and it became 10x more enjoyable.

AI generates all the assignment details. There's a big final project but she hasn't talked about it and the Canvas pages about it are vague and aren't all in agreement with each other, so I don't actually know what we're supposed to do for it. Makes you turn on your camera/cold calls people in the ZOOM classes.

Honestly, she is a really bad teacher but she is also easy. The LA's in the class grades everything and they usually gives you all A's if you do the assignment. Honestly the LA's do more work than Betsy does. If you want to take a easy class take this class but she doesn't teach anything. There are no test, quizzes on Thursday's and exit tickets.

actually psychotic. cares more about yelling at students than the actual class. even the TAs hate her. awful professor and i don't feel like i've learned pretty much anything. my friends took the class to learn about IST and said they don't even know if they like it because she ruined the class. take any other prof at literally all costs
