Grade depends totally on TA. You never see Dr. Bischof even once. Chem lab is tedious and far too long. Usually takes anywhere from 2.75 to 4 hours. Lowlight of my week but it builds character.

I had her from Chem 111... not a big fan of her personally, but she did a great job running the gen chem labs. I have her again next semester because I'm in the chem majors section and she does a really good job helping students. If your a chem major then you should def take the major section.
You are never going to see her, Chem111 is entirely based on your TA. The one time I did have an issue though, she answered my email fairly quickly but didn't really help with the issue I was having.
you'll never really see her or be able to get ahold of her. Honestly doesn't really matter because it's all dependent on your TA.

You don't see her in class, and it is very hard to access her outside of class. You must work around her schedule, which speaks volumes when she is not much help if you do see her. Just a professor who doesn't care for the students but rather just getting the lab to run. This leaves the difficulty of the labs up to the TA. Hope you get a good TA!

For this course it's all about your TA. I unfortunately will be rating my TA because Professor Bischof is absolutely nowhere to be found ever. I attend every session and stay the full 4 hours. I ask for clarification and still am receiving poor grades with no feedback. I'm reporting my TA and recommend anyone in the same position follows. Good luck

All I can say is yikes. Clearly a lady who's here for a paycheck and not for the students. Last semester I found a lab structure that was poorly accommodating, disorganized, and unnecessarily work heavy. So sad that people have to experience her.

Incredibly disorganized. She is not accommodating at all, and she never even made an appearance once and I took both 111 and 113. The manual had typos and the instructions were very unclear. My TA was amazing but she seemed to get the short straw having to clean up Dr. Bischof's mistakes. She never foresaw student error, leaving the TA in the dark.

Gen chem labs are just so icky. It's exactly like 111 except there is a formal research report on bottled water halfway thru the course. I didn't see Angela once the entire semester, just my TA (who was great) and my section supervisor. This is not a difficult course but what was annoying is that we would cover topics here before we did in CHEM112.

Horrible professor and person alike. Non-accomodating nor understanding. You will not see her, and she will not know you in labs since she does not teach anything, but she has full control of your grades. Unfortunately, it's hard to avoid this lab if it's required, so all I say is good luck. Everyone else is more helpful.

You won't ever talk to Dr Bischof, the labs are run by TAs. This class doesn't feel like real chemistry, you just follow all the steps in the manual and then do 15 post lab q's that will take you the entire 4 hours. The grading is so subjective, if you get a harsh TA, this course can be rough. Go to office hours in Whitmore and always ask questions

Your grade is entirely dependent on your TA. Pre-labs and in-labs were annoying, and post-labs were painful. My TA for CHEM 111 was great and let us leave early if we finished experiments early. But for 113, my TA was super harsh and unapproachable - made us stay the whole 4 hours. The lab exam tanked the A that I worked so hard for.

Chem 111/113 lab is terrible. So much work for a 1 credit class, you'll be doing the post lab for hours after class, and its extremely difficult. If you get a good TA and lab partner you'll be ok. The lab exam is awful and will tank your grade as the average is always close to failing cause the lab makes 0 sense. Have fun!!!

reviews.comment: like a lot of other said you never actually meet professor bischof. this class was based only on your ta and your partner. i did not have a good ta or a good partner so i did not enjoy the class. i felt the class was disorganized and pointless at times. i had taken a lab prior to this one and was initially excited, but ended being very disappointed

This lab is all up to the TA's abilities to explain the experiments and help with questions. The pre-labs are a pain, the labs are long, and the post-labs are usually dreadful. If a student doesn't have any chemistry background, this lab will most likely be confusing. Go to office hours if you're confused about any questions on the post-lab work.

CHEM111 is entirely dependent on your TA. You will never see the professor unless you reach out. The 4 hour lab is definitely not fun, but it is not the end of the world. If you have half-decent partners, this course is tolerable, and TAs generally are okay, but just ask questions, be prepared to spend all 4 hours, and you will be fine.

REALLY depends on which TA you have. The labs are fine, post-labs are hard but good TAs help answer them when you are stuck. Pre-labs are annoying but fine. There is a Formal Report you have to do, but it isn't that bad if you put work into it and ask your TA for help. Dr B is very considerate of personal issues/emergencies that come up.

This lab is structured the same as Chem 111 with a couple of additional assignments, the same materials are needed as well. Labs are led by TAs and not the actual professor. My main complaint about the course is how dependent it is on the eTA you receive. Some TAs grade harder than others which can lead to unfair distributions.

You will never meet the actual professor, you are assigned a lab TA who will lead the lab and grade all assignments. Two books are needed for the class along with safety glasses. The lab is easy and attendance is mandatory and only one absence is allowed. The final is open note with your handwritten lab notebook so keep attentive notes.

Your performance in this lab will be determinate by the TA and your final exam. I was having a B+ on the class and they graded my final harshly and I dropped to a C+. Work on the lab assignments consistently because if you miss something you will be in the same situation as me.

This class was alright. Compared to other chemistry classes (which are fun), this class was more tedious than anything. It is disproportionately a lot of work for very little credit. Personally, I would not take it again, although I understand the vision and intention behind it. I believe CHEM113 may be similar to this class.
Your lab TA will determine your experience.

reviews.comment: I will not do the chem lab class again. I am so happy I am done mostly. Only 1 credit it is not worth for our effort and hard-working. TA is good but you still stay 4 hours for the class.

As many have already said, you will be lucky to even lay eyes on Dr. Bischof at all. Your experience in CHEM111 is 98% determined by your TA and 2% by your lab partner. ***It is completely luck of the draw.*** That being said, 111 was a slog and pretty tough, but if you diligently do your pre-labs, work carefully, and get a good TA, you'll be fine.

Chem 111 is entirely based on your TA. Never had any interactions with Bischof but I heard she was nice. Was the longest lab of my life but it's not too difficult to earn a good grade. The final in this class is pointless and I don't know why there is even one.

This class is graded by your TA and I barely escaped with an A because my TA was a harsh grader.I absolutely dreaded going to this class and my TA was no help at explaining things or helping answer post lab questions.Everything will depend on who your TA is so hopefully you get an easy grader and helpful one.  Also this class has way too much work.

Not too bad. Grading depends on your TA. Barely any extra credit. Pre-labs are annoying and repetitive but the class is manageable. The 4 hour lab is dreaded but it goes by fast as you are busy the whole time.

You will never see Dr. Bischof, but rather 1-2 TA's. Your grade mainly depends on how harsh your lab TA grades. Every lab comes with a pre-lab and post-lab assignment. Lab reports aren't hard, just a list of questions you have to answer. It is so much more work than a 1 credit class should be, but it was manageable and not terribly challenging.

I would have received an A in the course except for one thing: my TA tried to reach out to me to tell me my file was unable to be opened, but they did not release the comments in time. Due to this, I had to take a 30% deduction, which is what kept me under an A. Ridiculous to show A level of understanding but be denied for a stupid rule.

I never saw Angela Bischof during my lab because the only people you interact with are your assigned TA and your section supervisor. How enjoyable your lab is basically depends on your TA. Mine wasn't very helpful and graded VERY harshly. The post-labs were also often long and unnecessarily difficult. Way too much work/writing for a 1 credit class.

You don't interact with Bischof, mainly your TA or lab coordinator. I don't agree with these other reviews, yes lab is long but I could get everything done in one day, it is not that hard if you just focus and do the post lab in lab and read the intro in the manual. I do agree that it shouldn't be one credit, but I found it easy enough to succeed.

TA's lead the lab so you won't even see her. Pre-Lab assignments are due before class, they're easy but tedious. Post Lab Reports often take around 2 hours and are somewhat hard but TA's help with answers. Lab is 4 hours but if you finish the lab and report in class you can leave early. If you miss more than 2 classes you have to drop the course.

reviews.comment: u never see angela so its hard to rate her bc ur TA is the one doing all the teaching & grading. the course is hard if u have a harsh TA grader. if u have ryan o'neill, try to switch. i had him & he would take off points for every little thing even if i got the right answer. go to office hours, 1 of them gave me all the answers every time!!!

Labs are taught by TA's so you never actually see Bischof. The labs never actually took 4 hours, but some were tedious. If you do not understand chemistry, some of the pre and post lab questions will be difficult to answer.

labs are taught by TAs so you will almost never interact with this woman unless you have an issue like you were late to lab or late turning in an assignment. Dr. Bischof is very condescending, every interaction I've had with her has been stressful and left me feeling less of a person. You basically can't miss more than one lab, if you do, you have to fill out all sorts of forms and meet with her and jump through all these hoops to have a make-up lab in the same week.

The post-lab homework is due 24 hours from the end of lab. If you finish class at 5:30, it's due at 5:30 the next day, instead of at 11:59 like a normal person.

Although this class is only 1 credit, it has too much work to do. The prof is too strict about the notebook, you will lose points for silly reasons! There were pre-lab assignments and some of them were too hard because you have no idea what it's asking for or you haven't studied it before.

Never met her but I had a good TA. The content is not hard but the labs are tedious and the amount of work for a one-credit course is absolutely ridiculous. reviews.comment: Never met the professor as this is a lab. As such, your experience with this lab highly depends on your TA. My TA was amazing and I thoroughly enjoyed my time in this class. Concepts follow Chem110 well and as long you put in the time an A shouldn't be too hard to get.

The fact that Chem 111 is only a 1-credit course and not at least 3 credits baffles me. I've spent more time on work for this class that I have for multiple 3 credit classes. This class is a ridiculous amount of work for one credit. Shame on the chemistry department for making me spend twice the amount of time on one credit than I do for a 3 credit chem lecture. Dr. Bischof is such a nice lady and always willing to help during labs. The labs are graded harshly in my opinion, but I still succeeded with a high B. The labs are graded by the TA, however. I would definitely take the class again because of her personality.

Dr. Bischof is great. She always seems to be in a good mood and is always so willing to help you understand the concepts you are performing experiments on in lab. One of my favorite professors so far at psu.

reviews.comment: Chem 111 lab with Dr. Bischof and Professor Crowe was a great experience. They provide great explanations and are super caring for their students--they just want you to learn and get as much out of this experience as you possibly can.

reviews.comment: I've literally never seen this woman its all the TAs and the rubric they grade on is far too strict for a 1 credit class. Finished in 110 with an A by a landslide and just missed the mark for the A- in lab. Its online lab chill tf out. This class sucks!

Go to office hours for help on the lab reports. They are worth the bulk of your grade. Also, I had this online so I never met my instructor. Go to office hours and make friends in your lab

reviews.comment: Chem111 sucks online, but it is manageable. This class would be much better in-person since it is mostly hands-on. It is a class that keeps you busy despite it being only one credit. reviews.comment: I'm sure it is because of COVID-19, but I absolutely hated CHEM111 this semester. reviews.comment: Her lectures were good and she is clearly very passionate about chemistry. She required you to write out 3 things for each homework problem (which there were a lot of) that really bothered me. It felt like I was in elementary school again. She wanted you to write like what is given, what you want to find, and what outside information you need.

im not great at chem, but I did much better than I thought I would do bc she explained the material very well and always did the most she could to make sure you understood the material. if she taught other chem classes I would take her section.

Dr. B is a great professor for the first chem class in college. The questions on exams are based on homework and recitation sheets. Do not hesitate to go to office hours if some materials Dr. B did not cover her lectures. As long as you know how to solves those problems, this class should be an easy A for all of you.

Angela gives good lectures, is very nice and is accessible outside of class. Personally, I found the homework to be the most helpful thing when learning the content. Sometimes there is a lot, but it's always manageable and is worth the effort. Do the homework and sample exams and you'll be well off.

Honestly, I've never worked this hard for a class. Although thats not on the professor it's the course itself. She's fun, kind, and tries to simplify things as much as possible. She's always available during office hours, too. Her class reviews aren't very helpful though.

reviews.comment: She cares about her students and that they know all the information. It sounds like she is good for chem110 but DO NOT TAKE HER FOR CHEM113FC. it is a miserable ass 1 credit class and she takes it way too seriously. it was absolutely dreadful and so annoying. we all complained that she was too strict with grading for notebooks. just dont do it.

reviews.comment: Dr. Bischof is a fantastic, caring professor. She teaches pretty quickly sometimes but as long as you can follow along, you'll get a good grade in the class. reviews.comment: She gives amazing lectures. Her class almost always out performed all of the Chem110 sections. Definitely due to her great lectures.

reviews.comment: Angela Bischof was the best chemistry teacher I have ever had with no exaggeration. For a weed-out class, she taught the material extraordinarily well. As a first year engineering student, this class was unexpectedly my favorite. She presents material clearly and goes back if anyone needs the material to be restated.

She is such an amazing professor. You have to pay attention in class and actually show up. She is so nice and caring and really tries to make sure that you are doing your best. I found it best to print out the lecture slides before class and take notes on the actual paper than to write in a notebook. I would definitely recommend her.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: let's just say she was the best chem professor I have ever seen. extremely helpful, extremely kind, and really cares about her students. she develops amazing methods and ways to explain complicated concepts and make them much easier. would go through anything multiple times. definitely would recommend her.
She's really nice and her lectures are great. She also has nice hair. The colors are awesome.

Dr. Jayarao retired halfway through the semester and did not include any homework for us to do this semester because of this. It was purely lazy. 

Dr. B, who took over the class, was pretty cool and very open to criticism.

Dr. Jayarao definitely is knowledgable and gives great information, but his attitude is what brought down my view of the class for me. He is pretty arrogant and sometimes makes you feel silly for asking questions. He will not explain things a different way if you don't understand it his way, and may even get mad at you.

Dr. Jayarao was a pleasure to have as professor!! He was very knowledgeable about everything he covered and lectures were always engaging and interesting. The exams were a little tough but if you studied the provided powerpoints, they were very manageable. Would definitely take another class with him!!

Jayarao is my favorite professor at PSU so far! Take any class you can with him. He is super knowledgeable and made me love Public Health even more. Clearly loves what he does and I really enjoyed all of the real-world applications/
He is super accessible outside of class, between course content and advising questions. Could not recommend more!

Jayarao is really interested in the subject and passionate about helping students! He's great to talk to outside of class about things beyond just the course itself. The grading can be slightly strict but homework questions and exam questions are taken directly from the lectures so it's easy to study and do well.

Probably one of the best professors I've had at Penn State. Immunology is hard but she explains it well and wants you to learn and understand the material. Her exams are hard but she provides extra credit opportunities to get up to 20-25 points back for exams. Attendance is mandatory but they are a big grade booster if you attend class regularly.

She cared WAYYY too much about attendance in this class to the point she would get angry if someone up and left, so go to class because attendance is also worth a lot of points. Overall she was a good teacher for this class, no exams, small assignments and open note final.

She knows a lot, but shouldn't be teaching this course. She literally said she doesn't understand why we're struggling because immunology is easy, and gets so passive aggressive after exams when she sees how poorly we did or when she received constructive criticism on the MSEEQs. Her expectations are madly unrealistic for a 200-level intro course.

This is not taught like a 200-level course. You're expected to come in with a grad school-level understanding of immunology and be able to understand her talking at you at 4x speed; she says you can ask questions but gets frustrated when you do. There are easily 500-700 slides per exam and it's nearly impossible to even do well on the extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I recommend taking VBSC 130 with Dr. Katkere. Her PowerPoints are very interesting, and you learn a lot. Attendance is mandatory, so you have to attend class, listen to the lectures, and do the quizzes on time, and you will do well. I really enjoyed this course.

Dr. Katkere means business, no doubt, but don't let this keep you from asking for help. She is extremely caring and wants all her students to do well, as long as you put in the work and show that you're really trying. There's tons of extra credit, so take advantage of it.

Alot of my classmates were afraid to approach her for extra help because they thought she was mean,instead she was super caring and helpful when asked for help during office hrs.Theres a lot of information that will be covered but it only makes you better.None of her classes are blowoffs as there's many ways to improve your grade.She means business

I bet every student that's giving her bad reviews and is complaining fail to take responsibility of their grade and most likely didn't study. She's very clear on what will be on the exam and gives extra credit all the time. She just doesn't put up with 1st world laziness. VBSC 211 is hard, but she makes it obvious about what will be on the exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is passive-aggressive towards her students and can't handle constructive criticism. She brings up comments made on past SRTEs and defends herself, despite these comments being true. She accuses her students when grading, saying things like "not sure where you guys are getting this from," yet it's straight from the notes or textbook.

Dr. Katkere was slightly all over the place but clearly really cares for her students and wants them to do well. The lectures were very fast-paced and a LOT of info was included in the powerpoints, which did make it hard to study. Even so, the exams are doable and the presentation you have to give is very manageable.

Immunology is a hard subject, but Dr. Katkere offered an unholy amount of extra credit so I still pulled a A. The slides are very dense and I do wish she had more slides with less information on each. Tests were fair, but covered quite a bit of content. The only thing I didn't like was mandatory attendance that affected your grade.

Dr. Katkare was a good professor. The class was lecture heavy, and she talked really fast, because she tried to fit a lot of information in a small amount of time. Even with all those other things, she is very helpful, and if you need a help with your grade, or whatever it is, she will help. You can tell that she really cares for her students.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Katkere is an extremely caring and kind professor. Her lectures are overwhelming at first, but she shows you exactly how to study and gives you study guides and practice quizzes. Immunology is not easy, but she really wants you to succeed. There are quizzes that give you three tries and there are 3-4 exams. And extra credit!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: A lot of information covered, multiple chapters on each exam and slightly disorganized but overall a really good teacher. Exams will include very general questions so no matter how much you study the chapters, she doesn't exactly test on what the exam is supposed to be on. If you paid attention in MICRO 410, you should be fun. Presentation is easy

She is very nice and cares for students. The only grades in the course were 4 exams which cover a ton of information on each. The class is an intro course so get ready to memorize A LOT of info. She does her best to help give hints about test questions and gave extra credit on two of the exams. Def take her, she cares so much about students!

Lectures are long and become boring. She's very nice and willing to help if you go to office hours. A LOT of material is covered but she tries to narrow the material by telling you what to focus on for the exams. Exams are do-able though you must be willing to work pretty hard. She gives a lot of extra credit on exams and curves the class.
Will go out of her way to help you if you ask but hard to understand and expects too much from introductory course
Overload students with too much material. Consistently mentions "this will be covered more on later chapters". Could use some better organization and trimming in materials.
Tests were very unclear and grammatically incorrect, lots of double negatives and "more right" answers. Otherwise, powerpoints are clear and gives a good review powerpoint for her exams.

Dr. Bharti is honestly and one of the best professors for biology at PSU, and she is incredibly progressive when it comes to lecturing style and class structure. Is there a lot of reading outside of class? Yes. But that reading is relevant for the class and the exam, as well as being relevant to global health.

Dr. Bharti is the best professor I have ever had. She makes class interesting and makes it possible to succeed compared to others. Lecture notes aren't enough so get ready to read. Participation and extra credit heavy. Good level 400 bio course. Extremely interesting and highly recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Dr. Bharti seems to know the material extremely well and delivers it in a way that makes the classes interesting and dynamic. Attendance is key in passing, as the lectures are not posted and you rely heavily in the notes you take in class for studying. Opportunities for extra credit. Favorite class that semester and definitely recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Bharti is awesome! She's a great lecturer and has a ton of experience in the HumID field. Her study guides are very representative of what's on exams, and she offers a ton of extra credit. Make sure you go to class because lecture slides/notes are not posted. I feel like a more educated biologist AND citizen because of her class. Take it!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment:
The lecture notes are illegible. Not just hard to read, I mean literally incomprehensible.

The lectures are hard to follow, and the homework problems are obtuse. There is not specific textbook, and he does not make it clear which textbook is appropriate to use for each section.
I spent more time trying to recognize the professor's handwritten lecture notes than in comprehending the concepts.
He is very humble and accessible professor. His exam is hard but eventually you will learn something new. He is a theoretical guy, so you will learn something that is very useful to research.
Horrible

Seemed like an ok guy, but the worst teacher ever. He suggested about 8 books for the course, and randomly moved from one book to another when teaching. His notes were also really hard to follow, but the exams were harder than his notes. I felt he did not understand the material well himself. I will never again take a stats course thanks to him!!

Very understanding, probably the best lecturer I ever had. He is a really kind and nice guy. Unlike most math/ stats professors I had, he has a very good sense of humor. Humble, always accessible, and very passionate about what he teaches. He really cares about students.
Best Stats class I took at PSU

Honestly, on of the worst professors that I have ever had. The grading on exams is very strict with little room for any error. Speaking of exams, expect difficult, short exams with only three problems. Each of these problems have multiple parts that all rely on one another. Aren't confident on part b? You now lose all of the points for parts c-h.

If you are interested in the math behind the statistics, then this is a good class for a start. He provides simple intuition and understandable proof. There are some grading issues but the exams are not hard if you can follow in class.

He teaches the class ok and has good board writing. However his not reachable outside of class at all. Takes him two weeks to grade exam every time and two weeks to reply email. One of the exam grade was posted right after deadline of late drop(on purpose? not sure). I would say this class material has a lot of ambiguity and his a tough grader so..
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Tough grader

reviews.comment: He did not hand us back the midterm before the late drop deadline citing the reason that his TAs had an exam that Friday. Even tried to discredit the university saying the late drop deadline was useless. His lectures are good, but he skips a lot of stuff. Moreover, the homework and the exam are completely out of sync.

The good: nice guy, willing to help, really knows his stuff. The bad: took off for the last 2 weeks of the semester, but still responsible for a bunch of new material. Had sub for 1 week who barely taught. CHANGED GRADE SYSTEM FROM SYLLABUS at the end; dropped fewer homeworks than he said he would. Exams fair but inconsistent in difficulty.
Nice guy, cares about his students. Straight-forward class. Go to class, take notes, read the book, and you'll be fine.
Dr. Bharti is incredibly caring and kind. The class is extremely easy to get an A in. Group projects are rough.

terrible terrible terrible class+ teacher. only worth 3 credit and you have 6hr class each week. it's a basic class, but the professor make it terrible. she give way much work, and force you to have camera on. if you don't she mark you as absent. gives you repetitive work. literally learn nothing from the project, and it's annoying.

Before I came into this class, I wasn't really sure of pursuing an engineering major but after taking her class, it made me feel more confident in my engineering skills. The class is enjoyable and pretty fun. She's an easy grader but most of the time you have to figure out things on your own. But, she gives you feedback on your work.

Professor Bharti has zero idea what she is doing. If you ever ask her a question, she will likely pass it on to one of the MSA's to try to help you. Her lectures don't make any sense, and the class is so unorganized; we do different things every day, and then she makes new assignments and forgets about the old ones. She's so sweet though.

EDSGN is an easy class. As long as you show up and do the work, you should get an A. Dr. B makes the A very painful. She hardly explains any techniques required and expects you to perfect the skills in a matter of minutes even if you have not learned it yet. She often did not know the information herself and you would be safer just asking the MSAs.

Dr. Bharti's a really nice teacher. Went through remote learning with her, and she was a bit picky with grading imo. I always got a point or two taken off because of small mistakes, but in a sense, they were helpful I guess. She's a big energy and environment person, so take her if you are interested! I was and her projects were interesting to me.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: Smita is a very good choice for Edsgn100. She might seen all around the class sometimes, but the class is fun and not to heavy. There were only 3 quizzes and they were pretty light and easily. She gives extensions to assignments if you ask for them. And there are two major group assignments with hw's scattered through them both.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--GROUP PROJECTS

reviews.comment: By far my favorite professor I've had at Penn State! She's very interactive in the class and makes the two hour classes fly by! Definitely get to know her well and have a good relationship with her. It could help your grade, but more than anything, she's just a great person to know. The class itself is not too hard as long as you work in class.
She makes you work, she will take your phone away if you use it during class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr Bahrti is a good professor, always willing to help you. She is very light grading stuff. She assigns homework sometimes but its not too bad.
Great professor! Lives what she teaches! She has an accent, but you get used to it.

My favorite professor, I've ever had. TAKE THIS CLASS!!! She prefers being called "Caren." I think there was one exam, and she literally told us every question to expect. The exam was open-ended. Another big project we had was a debate (teams of 2-3). She understands that some people don't like public speaking, so she offers an essay option.

Caren is the best professor I have ever had. She cares for her students and wants you to do well. She inspires me to keep working towards my future goals. I genuinely enjoy her classes. She is clear about what she wants and doesn't assign busy work. If you have the opportunity to take any of her classes, do it. The best crim/soc/wmnst prof at PSU

Professor Bloom-Steidle is a solid professor for this Law and Society Class. I think she's makes a great prof for this intro law class as she is actually a lawyer outside of class. Only two exams in course! Know textbook bc Exam 1 is hard. Final Exam Easy & Easy Group project Weekly easy discussion boards and quizzes as long you read the book.
Caren is amazing. By far my favorite professor and the best experience I've had at college. If you can get in one of her classes TAKE IT.

Caren is awesome. Her open discussion format allows ideas to flow freely while educating you on a multitude of topics. She is the hybrid of a mother and a stand-up comedian. Caren is incredibly sweet and genuinely cares about her students. She is a true professor bringing real-life knowledge to the classroom. Mr. Bloom-Steidle is a lucky man.

I'e taken all of Caren's classes 453, 423, & 467. If you have the chance to take Caren absolutely do it..you won't regret it. She is extremely passionate about her subjects & is an inspiration. The bonus is her classes are easy! Show up, take a extremely easy quiz everyday, and write a few papers.

Caren is an amazing teacher who is inspiring and motivating. She cares about the subject and gets really fired up which makes paying attention in class so much easier. There were a couple assignments and reading quizzes but they were short and to the point. The activism project at the end was so much fun. Best class at Penn State hands down.

Unbelievably helpful, smart, interesting and funny.  Love going to class every day.  A touchy subject (sexual violence) but she teaches it in such a manner to make sure everyone is comfortable.  Great person to learn from after class, is full of fascinating information. TAKE THIS CLASS!

very intelligent, very influencialo teacher. the things you learn from caren will stay with you forever. she is very convicted with the material & her students enjoy learning from her. interesting material, useful discussions, essays, quizzes, attendance, participation for grade. so far my favorite PSU class.
Great class. couple papers that are pretty easy. Awesome discussions, loved the class overall.

Caren is a fantastic professor, she is such an amazing teacher and the class environment is great. Attendance is very important and a big part of your grade because most of the class is discussion based--I found all the class discussions engaging and interesting
I promise you this professor will change your life. Take her class

Caren is a great professor. Super nice, and tells great stories. Her classes are entirely discussion based and participation is graded. The grading is a bit harsh because her TA grades all the quizzes. It was easy otherwise. Highly recommend!!

Caren is nice, but she can give harsh feedback on assignments. You'll usually take 3 online reading quizzes a week. 2 mandatory exams throughout the semester and an optional final. All lectures are discussion based. There's one presentation and it's a group project. The course content is interesting but the harsh grading is hard to deal with.

Caren is a great professor for this class. She was a lawyer so she is able to apply real life examples to the material. There are reading quizzes due before every class and she notes every time that you participate in class discussion. As a CRIM major, I will absolutely be taking another one of her classes.

My favorite professor at Penn State, so caring and understanding. The class is discussion based so participation and attendance is important but it is so worth it, everything is so interesting and very eye opening. You won't regret taking her!

Takes forever to grade and will take points off for anything. If you talk to her in private before class she will then make it known to the class what it was about. No actual lecture or teaching, just constant discussion and random stories.
Caren cares about her students and makes the class enjoyable. It is a discussion-based class, so no notes are taken. She is really strict on attendance and participation, so make sure you go.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Caren is awesome. She cares about her students and wants everyone to do well. Class consisted of daily reading quizzes, 1 midterm, a group debate, and an (optional) final. She does grade participation pretty aggressively but fixes around at the end. Midterm was easy if you studied. Shes a lovely teacher and if I could take her again I would
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Professor does not have a set rubric for anything and will doc points on quizzes if not up to her standard. Is big on not going word for word but will ask for direct definitions in readings. Also does not work well with makeup work in class. Does not grade group work adequately. My group member did not show up and i got points taken away.
TERRIBLE. She is the toughest grader I've ever seen and I'm going to be a senior. She changes her mind at the last minute. The worst prof ever.

In my three years of attending PSU I've never had a more deplorable professor. She consistently takes off points for things not described in the syllabus and DOESN'T HAVE A RUBRIC. You don't know what this woman wants on her quizzes until the end of the semester when she finally grades them. Class would be great if she wasn't teaching. WORST PROF!!

Caren is awesome and makes every class entertaining. One of the few professors that remember everyone's names. Classes are discussion based and never boring. There are assigned readings and quizzes every week, but they are manageable. As long as you do the readings, show up to classes, pay attention and participate you'll get a good grade.

The whole class is a discussion, which I liked because I will participate and it wasn't at all boring, it was very engaging. You definitely have to participate though. She is caring, open to different opinions, and really loves to engage the class. You have a quiz based on readings for each class but they aren't difficult, just do the work.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Bloom-Steidle is a very nice professor. She gives very good feedback to help you become a better student. Her exams are open ended (3 total). There are weekly discussions and weekly quizzes, all open ended. She want's you to become a good critical thinker. I highly recommend taking the class, I definitely enjoyed it and learned a lot.

Professor Caren is a real gem, but her rubrics are unclear and she is a very tough grader. She loves her students and wants them to succeed while inspiring us with her stories and encouraging words. Lectures are informative and you will learn a lot in this class. You have to try your best because she does not have room for excuses, slow grader too.

Caren is the best professor I have ever had. It is 1 essay, service learning project, concept quiz, participation points, and reading quizzes. Her discussions are enlightening and I left this class feeling like I can make a difference in this world. I learned so much and cannot express how amazing this woman is.

Project heavy and thought-provoking class. Definitely do the readings and attend the lectures. She was very fair and set up the class schedule well. She did the whole virtual thing well, would like to take her classes in person.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Amazing professor, lots of reading, which no one is a fan of but she makes the reading worth the time, probably the best professor ive ever had at Penn state thus far in my third year, would recommend as long as you go to class
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Caren is literally the best professor I have ever had. I always looked forward to going to her class. She is so caring and funny. Classes are discussion based and actually interesting. There is a lot of reading, but it's worth it! If you have the option to take Caren do it!!
Love Caren! Classes are discussion based and so interesting! If you need to take a CRIM class, take a class with Prof. Bloom
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: Professor Bloom-Steidle is a solid professor for this Law and Society Class. I think she's makes a great prof for this intro law class as she is actually a lawyer outside of class. However, you must know her textbook and Exam 1 is pretty hard. Reason I got an B+ instead of an A. Weekly easy discussion boards and quizzes as long you read the book.

Caren is hands down the best professor I have ever had. She uses a discussion based lecture which makes the class fun and interesting. I have taken 3 classes with her and I have noticed that students really open up to her and the entire class during lectures. She is so inspiring and really makes you think about important issues in the world!

Caren is the best professor I have ever had in my Penn State career. You will not regret taking her classes. I've had her for 2 classes and wish I wasn't graduating so I can take her for more. This woman is an angel & her grading is clear and not difficult. You do have to read, but no textbook is required. She makes class fun & keeps it interesting

Caren is so a great professor, who definitely makes you forget that youre in class at times. She didnt have a required textbook, but sent pdfs throughout the semester. She was nonbias and made me feel comfortable to always speak in class. She uses her background as an attorney to correlate well with her lectures which kept me interested.
The best teacher I've ever had!!! Take this class asap even as an elective. The reading can be a lot sometimes but super interesting. Make sure you talk in class, she'll remember you that way.

Her grading makes no sense. All the discussions were graded very easy and with little to no feedback, also not graded very quickly. Come exam time, the exam is basically the discussions, but graded so much harder. The final exam was graded very easy, which was nice but very hard to get a read on her. She does not give you a lot of guidance, so read
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Caren is the best professor you'll have. Her exams are how all exams should be. If you know the stuff, you'll get a good grade. No memorization or all-nighters necessary. Her final basically asks you to reflect on what you learned and to tell her how you'll use it in the future. Participation does count, but you'll never want to miss a lecture.

Caren is literally the nicest cutest human I want to cry just looking at her. I could literally listen to her talk for hours and she will "mom" you so hard. Readings can be a bit much but it's always interesting so it doesn't feel like it. Always has really good stories and is absolutely hilarious without being offensive.

Pretty fair class. Read the lectures and assigned readings and you will do well on the quizzes, but also make sure you understand the theories in your words because this is what is expected on exams and quizzes. Do all the above and it will be an easy  A.

Took SOC467 online with her. Pretty typical, reading and quiz every week, with I think two tests. As long as you do the reading assignments you'll be in good shape. Also, there are group debates and she's good at individualizing your grade in case one of you members goes missing on you. Highly recommend her.

This is a discussion based class and she is very open minded. She plays devils advocate for both sides and it can get irritating because she does such a good job and she asks very difficult questions for us to discuss. I loved the people in my class and the discussions that we have had. Go to class, participate, and hand in your homework. simple

Caren was the best professor I have had so far in my 3 years of college. It's a discussion based course and the homework is easy. She really cares about her students and takes the time to make sure everyone is comfortable and feels like they are in a safe environment at all times. She's hilarious too.

Caren is an amazing teacher. This is the 1st class I've taken with her but scheduled her other 2 classes for next semester. She's hilarious and honestly does care about her students. You have to read a lot which can be time-consuming but needs to be done seeing as there's a quiz before every class. Take her and you won't regret it. Amazing person

Caren is such a great professor and an even better person. She really cares about the subject matter she teaches and has the experience as a Domestic Violence Attorney to back it up. I think every CRIM major should take a class with her; its a breath of fresh air. No exams, just really great class discussion.

Quiz everyday on the reading, not too specific you just need to prove that you read the book. Once the quiz is complete in the first 5 minutes of class, the class shifts to a discussion applying what you read to real life situations. Great class, essay exam that you must prepare for, and a debate at the end of the semester. Best teacher I have had!
Excellent professor, be prepared to read and participate in class discussions.

Caren truly cares about her students. She is so kind, understanding, and willing to work with you no matter your situation. The class is almost all discussion based, with a group project leading a discussion one day, 2-3 short answer essays, and reading quizzes each day. The material is interesting, and she really wants you to challenge your views.

Caren is an amazing woman, and easily my favorite professor at Penn State. She always talks about her experience as a domestic violence attorney and keeps you on the edge of your seat. The classes are also mainly discussion, which is what I enjoyed the most.

Very helpful. Class is an open discussion forum and less of a lecture. No exams. Essay assignments are pretty straightforward. Reading is a must. Only downside is pretty slow in grading and returning work, but you can see her for your grade if you need to.

Caren is awesome. Her open discussion format allows ideas to flow freely while educating you on a multitude of topics. She is the hybrid of a mother and a stand-up comedian. Caren is incredibly sweet and genuinely cares about her students. She is a true professor bringing real-life knowledge to the classroom. Mr. Bloom-Steidle is a lucky man.
GREAT CLASS, PAY ATTENTION AND READ AND YOU GET THE GRADE YOU DESERVE, SHE LOVES GROUP WORK

Caren cares more about her students than any other professor I have ever had. If you put in the effort-read, show up to class, and complete the assigned projects-there is no reason you can't get an A for CRIM 423. CRIM 453 and CRIM 467 are a little more difficult. I recommend all of her classes.
This class was a lot of fun

Caren is the best professor at PSU She is so willing to help her students whenever they have a problem and her office is always open for anyone that has a concern! The debates for the class makes it so interested and the conversations that the students engaged while on the class makes it more interesting. Her midterm is long but easy. She's awesome
Caren is a wonderful professor, who engages the students in her class and allows for the expression of diverse viewpoints.

Just had to add this. Caren is the most down to earth, caring, knowledgeable prof. Ever. She treats her students with so much respect, and better yet, she's hilarious. Don't doubt the little lady, she's a freakin boss!
Caren is awesome,she's genuinely excited to be there and hear what everyone has to contribute. You will get out of the class whatever you put into it.

Took Caren for two classes. Wonderful woman! She is very knowledgeable and keeps things interesting. She is truly there for her students and treats them like gold. Funny, kind and knows what she is talking about. Highly recommend!

Caren is an awesome teacher! Just about every class is debates, which keeps class interesting. Attendance is graded and there is easy quizzes at the beginning of every class just to be sure you read. No exams.
Provides an understanding of what she wants to see from the class.
Caren is definitely one of the best professors I've encountered so far!! Her smile and energy will entertain you and her knowledge will educate you!! She's the best!! Had her for 423 and 453

Caren is the cutest woman in the world.  she is so helpful and makes it easy to learn because she is interesting.  The class is so easy if you go.  a few quizzes, she drops the lowest, a midterm, one group debate, and a take home final.

I had Caren for several classes while at PSU.  I am in my final year of law school now and took many things I learned from her with me.  Just do the reading and participate a little and it's not a hard class and you might find it as interesting as me =)

Caren is an amazing teacher. She really cares about her students and will help out however she can. Although attendence is mandatory, the in-class discussions make attending class easy. The papers are easy as long as you follow the guidlines and the final is simple if you put effort into it. Great class, great teacher!

The textbook nearly killed me. It took hours to do the readings, and they were pretty boring. Start homework early! Caren's nice enough, and amusing. I really enjoyed the in-class debates and discussions. The class really wasn't too hard, though you need to write fast on the mid-term. Also took CRIM 453, which was even better than 467; take her!
Awesome class. Couple papers that were pretty easy. Interesting materials and great discussions. Loved the class.

alright Caren this is for you!  Greatest teacher I ever had at PSU.  Discussions are interesting and engaging and she makes you think and you learn a lot from her classes.  By the way she complained that no one rated her as hot on here so for all the knowledge she has given you people do her one back and give her a hot rating!!!
Excellent! Interesting! The best stories! Funny! Great! All around great woman and great woman role model!

Awesome professor....probably one of the best in the CLJ department.  Show up to class, do the readings and you'll be fine.  There are quizzes on the readings, a take home final, and an activism project.  I enjoy going to this class and can't wait for my 2nd class with Caren in the Spring

Anyone who wants to be an attorney must take this class. She was by far the nicest, most interesting and funniest prof I've had. The class is as easy as you make it for yourself. Read, go, and participate and you have an A. But if you can't even do that, then why are you even thinking of law school?

best prof ever at penn state! you learn so much and there are no tests! very easy paper grader and they do not take much time at allll... the discussions are amazing. this class is phenomenal everyone should def take it!!
Interesting teacher who is genuinely excited about the subject, if you come to class and participate you'll do well, not much work involved.  Cool class, will definitely take her again.
Class was all discussion based.  You have to read the book in order to do well ont he reading quizzes.
the BOOK hates men.  Great teacher, and great way of teaching, no notes, no tests, all discussion quizes and 2 papers. Recommended

Okay, this class is somewhat easy as most people are saying. Steidle In
amazing teacher~

Caren is the best.  She's funny and nice and definitely wants everyone to do well.  She's more than willing to help you with things... I definitely recommend getting involved in classroom discussions... you'll learn a lot from them. She does grade her exam pretty hard though. =(
Caren is awesome!
One of the few professors (might be the only one) who actually promotes learning. Compassionate, passionate, intelligent, caring, understanding, inspiring and so much more.
She was extremely understanding of a very sensitive subject, and had a very compassionate way of teaching not know the status of the students in the class.  Easy to approach.
I love Caren.  She is intellectual, caring, and amazing.

GREAT professor, very entertaining class. Really makes you think. Sometimes you leave thinking "wow." Not difficult, can be a lil tough when grading papers. Few quizzes once in awhile, as lon as you read you'll be fine :)
Love this "little lady" especially when she squeaks...she is the best!
Awesome teacher!
Awesome teacher! I learned more in her class than any other class I've taken. Discussions make you comprehend material so much better than lectures.

Only 4 assignments throughout the semester & all tests are open-note & online (out of class). Attendance is not mandatory, and he basically reads off the slides. The textbook is very long, but it is important to go through it.
