She will read her slides, ask for questions (not look around though so don't bother raising your hand), and move on. You're going to want a different prof is you want above a B in here.

Most people complain about her but also dont put much effort into the class. Shes super accessible outside of class and will give points back on exams if you go in to talk to her about them. While most people complain about her, I can tell she cares for her students and tries her best to make sure her students understand the material.

Patricia is one of the worst professors I have had at Penn State. She constantly seems frazzled and as if she doesn't understand the material well herself. She is very scattered in class and hard to understand because she mumbles and doesn't check to see if students understand. DO NOT take her

her voice is frustrating and lectures are borrrinngggg. there are so many test you can't catch a break and material builds on itself so if you dont know it your screwed. lion tutors saved me but its annoying that i had to pay to learn the information...

She posts the powerpoint online the day before the lecture, but blows through each slide, so come prepared. The labs, homework, and exams (7 of them, but no final) were all easy too, but she does not do a thorough job teaching the material, although you do learn and the labs help you actually apply the information. She's a very nice person though.

She has no idea how to teach. I took AP Stats in high school (thank god), and my heart aches for the people who haven't taken any stats. In my entire life I have never seen so many people in one lecture hall more confused and angry at a teacher at one time.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: poor course materials

Buchanan is a poor teacher but the material is not horrible, it just seems hard b/c she mumbles through slides with no explanations. The HW and labs are annoying and long but the exams aren't bad at all, especially if you go to Liontutors, gives you everything you need. 7 exams seems daunting but it's easier b/c theres only 1 chapter on each.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is a really nice lady, but if I am being honest, the class was extremely unorganized. The homework and labs are not parallel with the exams, which is very confusing. I spent so much time trying to figure out homework problems that never ended up on any exams. The exams are simpler than the homework but never explained which makes it hard.

It is nothing short of a tragedy that this class is required for my major because Pat Buchanan is nearly unbearable as a teacher. Not only does she slur her words and mumble, but she gives daily clicker quizzes, in which she gives you about 30 seconds to answer a question on material you've never seen and grades it on correctness. Avoid if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Pat may be one of the hardest professors I have had. There are 7 exams, including one 150 point cumulative exam. The lectures, labs, and home works are nothing like the exams. Textbook is not required, but it is the only way I was able to teach myself the material. Her lectures are boring, and she speaks fast & whines so it's hard to understand her

Pats pretty good. She has a lot of office hours and is very helpful during them. While lecture wasnt terribly exciting it was to the point and made sense. Mandatory due to clickers. As a science major this class was very easy. Get all the buffer points, study for exams, and youll do well. Pat gives a lot of extra material to prepare you for them.

Patricia although passionate about the subject lacked an understanding of students not understanding certain lectures or chapters. There is a gap between lectures and lab and the lab instructors do not know what is being taught and it is hard for students because there is a lack of connection sometimes. She is always open to giving extra help.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Very boring, mumbles, does not explain material well

Lectures arent very helpful, not helpful at all actually, mainly because quite literally every other word she says is the word again I guess she means well but honestly Im not paying this STEEP tuition to receive professors that are trying their best
Avoid if possible. The labs and homework are completely different from the exams. One plus though is there is no final.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Try your hardest to avoid Pat, but she's really not that bad. The most frustrating thing about the class is that the homeworks and labs are absolutely nothing like the 7 exams. The most important thing to know about this class is that LionTutors works miracles. LionTutors is strictly the reason I got an A- in this class.

Pat's lectures are not helpful at all. I only went for the clicker points. If you can, take this class with a group of friends so that you can all help each other out. It makes a HUGE difference. Exams can be difficult at times. Lab TAs were very helpful. Pat is not.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: None of the Stat teachers are great, but avoid if possible. Textbook and lab are where you learn if you're lucky.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: After hearing her cough into the microphone all semester I am glad it is almost over. She has 6 exams on each topic and a cumulative exam. If a person could talk too much during a lecture, it would be her, she rambles after every slide. There is a lot of homework

There are like 7 exams that make up 65% of your final grade, which I really disagree with. If you are a good test taker you have the upper hand. Lectures are boring and she doesn't explain concepts at all. Beware the 5th exam - it's hard. She also says the word "actually" over and over again, which can be a bit too much. She seems nice though.

Her class starts out very easy, yet as the semester drags on the classes get longer and longer and the material gets harder and harder. Towards the second half of the semester expect to be doing at least two to three hours of homework a week, not including studying. She also has started a new system of having an exam every two weeks.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: I know many say the STAT needs ourselves to learn more. But if it only depends on students, what does the professor stand here for? She may be a professional professor in STAT, but not in lecture.
Not a great professor, doesn't explain concepts very well. However, if you have prior knowledge of Statistics I would recommend her because she gives extra credit and her tests aren't too bad

Professor Buchanan lacks the ability to transfer information from herself to her students. It's evident that she has been teaching for many years and has a thorough understanding of statistics; however, this does not translate into effective teaching. She consistently gives extremely confusing lectures and even confuses herself pretty often. Avoid.
As long as you read the section before class, and complete all the assignments, this class is a breeze. Dr. Buchanan offers many office hours and works really hard for her students to succeed.
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: She is a kind woman and cares about her job, but she does not relay the information like a professor should. Her lectures are boring and she doesn't stop to answer questions if students don't understand. She's a good person, just not a good teacher

AWFUL Professor. Avoid her like the plague. The material itself is not hard; however, Buchanan cannot teach at an elementary level. Seemingly easy questions will have her confused and leave you without an answer. Lectures confused me more than taught me. Only go for the clicker points. My lab TA didnt speak much english. Awful. Pointless homework.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: The class is harder than it needs to be. Lectures are unclear, labs are confusing and often worded poorly, and WileyPlus made me extremely frustrated. Take advantage of GSG sessions because that's the only thing that helped me scrape by in this class. Read the textbook before lecture so you can have a basic idea of what she is talking about.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: This class feels so much harder than it needs to be. The lectures are a mess and she flies through them. She explains a topic in 5 mins then asks a question about it then moves to the next topic. Definitely suggest having a friend in the class to work through Hw and labs. Exams are somewhat difficult but theres 7 so there is space for mistakes.
*Cracks fingers* *types rapidly* She lacks the basic ability to transfer information. She stops lecturing for 20 second periods if there's two students talking in a room of 400 people.

There are 7 total exams, one cumulative (not during finals week), so prepare for tests every other week. Lab quizzes you do in pairs and almost always get 100%, she gives a few percentage points extra credit by literally taking a survey after your exam (so easy). Tests are nottt easy but they aren't awful because they're so close together.

Her lectures really don't make a lot of sense but definitely go and get as much extra credit as you can. Tests can be a little tricky, the lecture quizzes help a lot. I went to lion tutors for almost all of the exams I probably wouldn't have done well in the class if it weren't for Lion tutors

She's great. Her exams can be difficult but if you make an effort and study you shouldn't have a problem. Going to class is essential to understanding the concepts (And for the extra credit) even though getting to those 8ams can be difficult it will definitely be worth the grade.

As long as you go to class and pay attention (and fill in the power points for notes), you'll do fine. There are 6 exams, so if you do poorly on one of them you still have a chance for a decent grade. Exams are only 64% of the overall grade, which is awesome because I'm not a great test-taker. If you have to take Stat200, take this section.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: The concepts can be hard but theres so much extra credit and other grades besides the tests that its easy to get your grade up
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: attendance is not technically mandatory but it is required for clicker questions. She goes through the slides extremely fast. You rarely get to ask questions. the labs quizzes are decent because you can ask questions and homework is pretty easy but it's hard to learn material when you are not taught it to a certain extent.

If you have any prior knowledge of statistics, this class is a breeze. If not, it isn't that hard to get. As for Buchanan, her exams are pulled pretty much from her labs and homeworks. Downsides, she mutters when she speaks and almost expects you to know everything. But if you show up and do work, you'll get at least a B with all the extra credit.

This was my second time taking stat 200. I had a blended class, once a week where you had to do homework and lab by yourself. Taking with buchanan where you had to go to actual labs actually helped me a lot since there is T.A. She gives out lot of extra credit. Go through all the homework and labs for the exam and make sure you go to lectures.

The lectures were pretty much the entire course. If you don't go to lecture, you must be able to make sense of the textbook readings. Lab wasn't difficult, but the fact that the course was early in the morning was inconvenient. She always began Mondays with, "How was everyone's weekend? (silence)... That's nice. Moving on..." A great week starter.
Very boring and unclear. Really hard to follow

Pat's a really nice lady, but class is more of  hassle than it needs to be. The Angel page is unorganized and her instructions are hard to follow. Lectures are boring and not helpful, the ppts are useless if you don't go to class and fill them in. It's totally doable, but she makes it harder than it needs to be.

I had Pat my freshman year for Stat 200. She posted every powerpoint slide on angel and all you had to do was go to class and fill in the blanks. If you do that and go to lab, you can easily manage any grade between a B+ and an A. Each homework had two attempts. This was one of the easiest A's I received in college.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: simple to get all the easy points (everything besides exams)/ extra credit to boost your grade. make sure you show up to class because clickers. for labs ask the TA's for answers/work with partners. homeworks aren't difficult pretty time consuming but you get two tries so work with someone and ur fine. lots of extra credit.

Buchanan is a flat out awful professor. All she does is read off of her poorly worded powerpoints and yell into her microphone. She covers 45 slides in 50 minutes and doesn't clarify anything. Find another professor.

Highly unorganized and difficult to understand. Doesn't post the labs or notes until 7:30 the night before, making it impossible to work ahead-- who wants to do a lab at 8 pm the night before it's due? Especially if you work until 9 pm. Notes are vague and lessons are all over the book. Homework quizzes don't match the actual homework.
She goes so fast and you cannot understand half of what she is saying.  She is very bad at explaining points and moves all over the place in her powerpoint.  It is a lot of work for a class.

Her lectures are super boring but mandatory because of clicker questions. She kind of mumbles and expect to do a lot of work for an A. Make sure you go to lecture, do your work, and study. Gives a lot of extra credit.
Gives you the slides with parts missing.  I prefer writing my notes, so this wasn't great.  Class layout was great in terms of weights.  Uses iclicker which was great.

I didn't like Dr. Buchanan's teaching style at first, but it grew on me. She gives more extra credit than you would expect so take advantage of it and go to class! Don't be afraid to ask questions in lab, it'll help you get 10's on the quizzes. The lecture quizzes are helpful when studying for the exams. Get the easy points!

Pat was a great professor. She posts all of her slides to Angel, but you have to be in class to get the fill-in-the-blank parts. If you don't go to class, you won't do well in lab, which is a big part of your grade. She gives tons of extra credit. Overall, I thought this class was very fair, but you do have to work for your grade. Exams are fair.

Lectures can be boring, she goes by so fast and unclear. You have to do outside reading in the textbook (which is useless and confusing) I recommend going to Lion Tutors. There are clicker questions in class so attendance is somewhat mandatory.

The lab is very confusing if you don't attend lecture. Missing lecture cannot be made up by reading the textbook. Print the lecture slides before class and take notes, then review your notes before lab, or even start lab the night before. Also she can be hard to understand at times - slurs her words. MAKE SURE YOU COMPLETELY UNDERSTAND THE SYLLABUS

I don't know how I passed this class, to be honest. I shouldn't have. I could not bear to listen to her lectures, mostly because her voice is so awful. Labs were a huge pain, and homework quizzes weren't fun either. For both of these, you could do the assignment flawlessly and still get the answers wrong because she words them so strangely.

Not the best lecturer I've had but the class was extremely easy. Even without extra credit, I would have gotten an A. If you focus on the material and understand main topic, the class is a breeze. Just go to class, do the clicker questions, understand the big picture, and remember she gives the formulas on the exams.
She's the worst stat prof in Penn state

She's a really sweet person. She wants to see her students do well. The material starts out easy and gets slightly harder as the semester goes on. Theres PLENTY of extra credit available. Go to class and do the work and you should be fine. I also recommend going to office hours she's really helpful

You have to teach yourself in this class. Go to all the available help options and review your notes. Start doing this earlier because the material builds.  The end of the year was so much easier than the beginning of the year because of getting help and understanding the material early on.  If you go to her office hours she will help you.

Honestly, professor Pat is a pretty terrible teacher. I could not grasp anything she was saying in the lecture. However, the material is pretty easy if you learn it on your own and take the lecture quizzes she posts on angel. If you go to class, do the labs with partners, and put a decent amount of studying for the exams, its a pretty easy A

Overall, here's what you need to know, she DOES drop some labs & quizzes. She does NOT drop a test. She gives a load of extra credit, but you have to be in class to receive it. She's a bit all over the place with lectures but she does help when you attend OH. No, she doesn't give a cheat sheet. But if you try & seek help, you'll be fine!
Easy class ever
Hard to understand, unorganized notes. The TAs in lab didn't know the material to help. Clicker questions every lecture.  Examples weren't clear.

If you've taken stats in high school you'll be alright, but if not you'll be confused. She goes through lectures really quickly and doesn't see if her students have questions. Her voice is also pretty nasally. Labs are mandatory, but worth it because the TAs are very helpful. You only need the book for homework.

She was not helpful at all. I am not good at math and I took this class after my advisor said it would be easy. SHE WAS WRONG. homework and attendance is basically mandatory, if you don't show up you will fail, same with the homework. She also explains NOTHING. don't take her unless you have to.

I took this class with her after reading on here that she drops your lowest test grade. This may have been true in the past, but not anymore. She gives a lot of extra credit but you have to be in class on the right days to get it. At the end of the class I was .4 of a point from an A- and she wouldn't bump be up... Don't take this class with her.

She is the most boring professor. Her lectures are unclear and if you haven't taken Stat before you are sure to be confused. She has more work than any other professor (2 quizzes a week and a homework), 5 exams and attendance mandatory. She is really unhelpful and her voice is extremely annoying. Don't take this class if your life depended on it

This class is not the most interesting class and is not the easiest class by far, but if you put in the time and effort you can earn a fair grade.  She drops the 3 lowest lab grades and one lowest homework grade.  Offers a lot of extra credit and wants people to succeed.  However, her lectures are very boring and unclear.  Go to lion tutors.
She is knows her Statistics but she is really boring. Classes are mandatory because of clickrs, but the labs are more helpful. I'd take a professor who does not require mandatory attendance

Prof. Buchannan knows her statistics  but is an awful teacher. Her powerpoint slides have mostly examples and she doesn't come right out and tell you the definition of what you are learning about. I would definitely try getting a different professor for stat 200.

Labs and Homeworks, along with exams (obviously), account for most of your grade, but be warned. A decent percentage will hit your clickers too. Though, lecture is only necessary if you prefer 100 minutes of powerpoints versus 20 minutes of reading. Her exams reflect lecture quizzes too. The material isn't difficult, just requires some attention.

Must attend class for clicker points and the labs are annoying, but work with one another and it's actually not that bad. The beginning units are easy, gets harder along the way. A few extra credits and one dropped lab & homework to make up for anything you missed.

She is an awful professor. She knows her stats and is good at it, but she can't teach it at all. Instead of teaching concepts, she just uses fill in powerpoints that make no sense. She's helpful in office hours but its not worth it. There are also 5 exams plus other stuff, so it's a lot of work.

Pat is so nice! This was probably the easiest 4 credit math class I've ever taken. Go to lectures, take the notes, and you pretty much have all you need. She drops some grades so there's nothing to worry about. Having 5 exams sucks, though.

She's honestly one of the nicest teachers I've ever had. Coming from the 140/141 calc classes, it was such a relief taking a stat class. You never need a calculator for the exams so the material is basically watered down and spoon fed to you. Easiest 4 credit class out there. Buchanan also has TONS of extra credit!

not a bad teacher, though her use of the word "again" is pretty funny though annoying. Attendance doesn't matter though i'd recommend it. Hard to learn from her but the review sessions before tests overview everything pretty well and the tests are basically taken from homeworks and labs. though shes grades for corectness unlike ANY OTHER STAT TEACH

Not very good at all - she never taught concepts, she simply filled in the blanks of examples and moved on.  She doesn't take questions in class.  I had a difficult time understanding my foreign TA so I relied mostly on my LA to learn.  Not a hard class but only if you don't try to learn from her!

This woman is amazing!!! If you're like me and are terrible at math, go see her. She likes getting to know her students and is willing to help you if you genuinely want to do well. If I had the choice, I would take her again.
homeworks have NOTHING to do with the exams & take to long. The TA was hot & very helpful but the labs were hard.

First off, her voice could probably kill you if you listen to it for more than the 50 minute lectures. She drinks out of her water bottle every 5 minutes and you can hear it so loud through the microphone. She goes through 45 slides in 50 minutes and you always find yourself just copying notes and not learning anything. NEVER EVER. my god.

Easy A. Lectures are boring, but wise to attend because of lecture quizzes. Drops 1 of the first 2 tests. Tests aren't bad and only add up to 54% of the final grade. So an A is still possible if you do well on lecture quizzes, labs, and home work quizzes if you have like a B test average.
Probably one of the easiest classes I have ever taken.  Lots of drops and tests are very straight forward, I don't see how people struggled in this class.

TAKE THE SUMMER CLASS. Less material (not all topics are covered) but everything is faster. Final exam was optional. Buchanan was very consistent with her routine. During the summer, all you need to do is to get up to a certain amount of points. 600 points is a letter D. 920 points for a letter A. Very helpful with labs. Room changes were annoying.

She assigns lots of tedious work, but by the time you take the test you've seen 70% of the questions before.  You have to attend class because she assigns quizzes on the lecture.  You can drop the lowest few quizzes, homeworks and lab grades, which is great for your final grade.

Class was not too hard. You need to attend to get the lecture notes b/c you use them in the labs. The labs help you understand the concepts. As long as you pay attention, you should be fine. Many of the assignments are dropped, so if you miss one or two, it's all right.
The class was actually a joke. She drops so many things that it's really hard not to do well. She doesn't actually teach anything though, the TA's do most of that in lab.

If you go to class and do most of the work (a lot of it gets dropped which is nice) you will be fine. She gives a lot of resources to help you if you are having trouble.  Decent class if you have to take statistics.

Ridiculously easy. I don't see how it's even possible to do badly in this class since practically everything gets dropped. 3/4 exams count. 7/9 homeworks. 17/23 lab quizzes. 13/17 lecture quizzes. All easy. Plus plenty of extra credit.

You pretty much have to teach yourself, but there are so many quizzes and activities, and so many of them are dropped by the end that it ends up being a lot easier than you'd think. Exams are conceptual, not mathematical which is good if you're not too into math.

Hardly did anything in the class. You get to work with partners for labs so it's easy to get the correct answers.  The tests are easy if you invest at least a little time.  I suck at math and I got a 98 on the first exam.  There are tons of points so it's easy to get a good grade.

EASY CLASS...I basically slept through the lectures and got an A. Test are easy and most of the points come from labs. She is probable one of the top rated worse professor in the regards to teaching so you pretty much have to teach yourself. Dont expect for her to put stuff up on time, she is a sorry excuse for a professor at an elite school
She makes the class easy. Just make sure you do the labs and homework. An A or A- is pretty much guaranteed. And there's lots of extra credit.
If your looking for an easy professor to have statistics with, take it with her, she is really nice, and there are tons of little easy assignments that really boost your grade.
dont bother going to lecture, she is an idiot but do the work and you will do fine. take jenny shook if possible

Her lectures are very boring and tedious. She has quizzes after every lecture to make sure you attend and tedious lab activity quizzes after each lab. Her exams and quizzes ask questions regarding things we did not learn in class. You can know everything on the study guide and still get a bad grade.

This class was pretty easy.  However, most of her note outlines had typos or didn't make sense.  On quizzes and labs she words things so poorly that half the time when I asked the TA what the question was asking he didn't have an answer for me.  She does provide a lot of opportunities to get a decent grade.
40% of the class got an A last semester, not A-...an A.  Just memorize her powerpoints and you'll do fine.  She doesn't really trick you with any questions.  Projects are kind of annoying though

There are a lot of points in the class but she lets you drop the lowest grades which is nice. It's a good idea to go to labs and do the quizzes because exam questions are exactly like those. The only outside work you need to do is homework. Everything else you do in class or lab. Easy A-B
Just a tough class in general, but she teaches the material pretty well.  You will need to put some effort into the class.

She is definitely a nice lady; however, be prepared to be confused.  Labs are kinda easy (MAKE SURE YOU WORK WITH KIDS AROUND YOU).  Also, there are few homeworks, and few quizzes.  Her grading is designed to help you as she drops  a nice percentage of your work.  Nice lady, but be prepared to do your work outside the classroom

I took Stat 100 with Buchanan and it really helped me in taking it with her for 200. The class isn't really difficult, but for students who didn't take 100 with her, it can be a little challenging. Overall, nice lady who lets you drop your 2 worst quizzes, homework assignments, and 3 labs. Grading system is great.

This class was a lot less painful than i had anticipated, she made it very easy. However, i don't think i learned very much at all and the grade reflects the ease of the course rather than any knowledge.  Nice lady, not always altogether there and slightly strange, but nice

Easy, easy, easy. The grading system is kind of like how it was in highschool. You get so many points from labs and quizzes, that even if you bomb an exam (which you def. shouldn't) it barely even affects your grade. Plus, she's real nice. Take it!

Awful. Reading from powerpoints slides isn't the same as teaching, and it's impossible to  do well on the tests when the questions are grammatically confusing. Test question: Which one of these is untrue? option a: that the cause of the random action is a direct result of the consequence that comes after it. WHAT?! She is a nice lady, just boring.

The class is extremely boring to go to although all you have to do is fill in the slides posted on ANGEL.  She gives pop quizes which help your grade so you do have to go to class some of the time.  Quizes, labs, and exams arent that hard if you pay attention in class and study the notes because the questions come from the slides. Its not an easy A

Buchanan's class is VERY easy! Many of the questions on exams come straight from the notes. On top of exams, you are graded on labs, quizzes, and pop quizzes ,all of which are easy and only help to boost your grade! She let's you drop your two lowest pop quizzes, lowest indvidual quiz, lowest group quiz, and 2 lowest labs. Take this class!

Terrible.  You can't understand one word she says.  Her piercing voice doesn't speak in anything but a mumble and she flies through lecture.  Labs are easy and so are quizzes, but you won't enjoy listening to her talk.  Not a lot of out of class work required.

Easy class, i made the mistake of buying the textbook which you dont need it at all, horrible professor though, can't understand a word she is saying because she slurs and mumbles, she also never stops to answer questions or clarify, tends to speed through notes.  overall easy A if you go to class and pay attention.
really easy teacher...let's you know everything on the quizzes/test plus exams are out 111 points...just go to lab and u should do real well
Be prepared to teach yourself. Her lectures/slides/handouts are pretty bad and the textbook is even worse. There are better and easier Stat teachers out there.. dont waste your time.
Terrible teacher, very dismissive, tests/quizzes poorly worded

I believe those below who enjoyed her teaching for STAT 200, but in the 100 class she proved the dullest, least flexible professor I have ever had. She does nothing but read her own projector notes aloud during the lectures, and is virtually inaccessible outside of class. Moreover, her grammar is atrocious and she trusts TAs too much.

She  definetly knows her stuff but i had a hard time understanding her. she was helpful but i had better luck understanding other students than her.  if you have her i strongly reccomend organzing a student study group!
Very good teacher.  Knows her stuff.  She is also good at explaining the material.  All around good teacher. I would recomend her highly for stat
An all around great instuctor
The class was very organized and well run. Not the most approachable, but knows how to run a large lecture well. TAs, not so great, but passable
Probably the best prof. I'll had for a class of more than 300.  Pat obviously knows how to administer and teach a course.  Very nice person too...talk to her in labs.
She's alright.  Her TA's suck more than her.  She's always trying to help, but she's really unclear, so it's tough.  But she doesn't want to screw you over.  Just learn most of it on your own.

I have her class at 8:00 am so this response may be a little biased but I can hardly understand what she is saying sometimes. She seems a little scatter-brained but overall she seems O.K. She uses pretty interesting examples and you can tell she tries hard to have everyone understand. She's probably the best Stat prof. at University Park.

Her lecture were very boring; I found it hard to pay attention so I usually just waited until the day before the test to learn everything.  I studied with other people in the class and it took awhile, but eventually we understood the concepts... once you get them, the tests are ridiculously simple.  Dont like her teaching style, but a pretty easy A

She's very clear and explains EVERYTHING! But I'm lousy at stat and took it to satisfy the quantification req.  I did okay, B.  But I did understand a whole lot of it and I guess I got lucky on answering the questions I didn't know at random.

At first she seems like a miserable lady. NOT TRUE! she is very nice and very helpful. Go to her office hours and really show her that you are trying-she'll grade you on your progress. YOU HAVE TO DO THE WORK but in the end she'll reward you for the hard work.
Shes not a bad lady.  Honestly, from what Ive heard, there arent a lot of winners among STAT 200 teachers, so Pat will do.  It is a bit tricky though and depends a lot on how good the TAs are.
She doesnt teach at all. Class isnt that hard but all she does is read off the slides. The best class of the whole class is her sexy fanny pack.
i liked her tests. she takes things from homework and quizzes directly for the test.
Find another professor. Other sections get to use notes and stuff on tests. She doesnt help you at all!! She is boring and hard. Take another section.

The class is very easy, but the lectures go very quickly because she doesnt explain anything, and moreover, she doesn't care about whether anyone knows what she is talking about. she gives a lot of pop quizzes (easy) and there are a lot of easy lab quizzes. drops low grades, which is good.
Doesn't teach-- just gives us work to do. Her TA's do everything...

not a good speaker, but notes are very helpful. after you get used to the way she teaches you are fine. class is easy, a lot of the problems on tests are exact ones from notes and hw. im taking her again for 200

Knows the material but unable to teach it. Shes just not able to explain the concepts in lecture at all. Expect to learn everything on ur own from the book and get help from other students. Shes much better in office hours so try those if u need to.
This professor is not good. So not take this class with her. Her notes are incomplete even after going to lecture, they make no sense. Find another prof.
EXTREMELY SWEET!  may seem a little aloof at first, but if you need help she is ready to help you with everything/anything!  AWESOME

Not a terrible professor and class.  Powerpoints will make sense later when you look at the book, so you have to work on your own a lot to understand the material, but it's not impossible nor hard by any means.  Just make sure you stay on top of the homeworks, quizzes, etc, because they add up.

This woman can't write a sentence well, and it makes her powerpoints fairly tough to follow most of the time. The fact that my TA basically was of no help either didn't make me have a better view of the class either. If you can choose another Stat teacher for Stat 200, do it.

She is a nice person and a good teacher.  Her tests are simple if you study the notes and go to class.  So long as you attend lecture you'll find you will not need to study much outside of class.  She also has tons of office hours.

She is a very nice woman and willing to help you/clarify anytime you ask.  She knows what she is talking about and enjoys teaching.  People probably don't like the class because you actually do have to study and learn, but it's college, suck it up.
Dull lectures and you have to print out the notes.  You have to study or else.

The class seems difficult the way she teaches but once you take the first exam you will realize how simple this class really is. A little bit of studying is necessary before each exam. Lab Activities and Quiz's are simple too... I mean c'mon, you take them in groups.
Easy class if you take all the notes

This woman can't string together a coherent sentence to save her life, so don't count on learning squat from her powerpoints or notes. She can't really explain things too well, either. Read the book & don't bother going to class except for exams & labs.
She's nice but you have to pay attention, if you need help go to her and ask. Do well on the homework because it's helpful to bring your grade up.

This teacher is the worst, the material itself isn't that difficult if explained right but she rushes through so many of the lectures its impossible to follow. The TA's are kinda mean and ****y about help, overall the class isn't bad just take it with a different professor.

She's a really good teacher. Go to lectures, do labs with a partner and you'll do fine. By the ratings on other stat teachers, she's probably the best. The lectures may be confusing, but the labs are easy and help you understand.

TA's in this class are a joke, they make fun of us like we're in 5th grade.  Her lectures are more worthless than a Michael Bolton record.  There are 500billion stat professors at PSU.  Take someone other than Buchanan, it will be worth your while.

To her credit, I think she really does try and is very willing to give extra help. But I still found her class so boring, and she really didn't teach.She just basically read off her powerpoint slides. The labs got to be tedious though. But an easy math credit, so it might be worth bearing with it
Lectures are very boring, but the class is fairly easy. The quizzes and labs are very easy, but the exams are harder than you'd expect.

Very willing to help, just ask - she attended lab once/week as well. Explained concepts well, but you need to go to class.  Do the homework.  You have to take STAT 200 - So buckle down and realize it's work.  Then sign up for Buchanan.

She's a nice lady and helpful if you ask questions. The class is pretty boring though. She does give extra credit (which she considers partial credit that couldn't be given on exams), and if you study and pay attention, it's not too hard.
This class is so incredibly boring, I can hardly take it. If you've never taken stat before, good luck.

this class is so damn easy. you dont even have to go to lecture.. just walk in, pick up the handouts, then walk right back out. there are activites which are kinda hard but you get to work in groups, and quizzes which are simple. Take this!!
Don't take her.  She is a horrible professor.  She makes you study way too much information and she doesn't teach it well at all.

The professor is AMAZING!. She will go way out of her way just to help her students out when they struggle with this particular class. I liked her alot. If I had to take another Stat's class I would def. choose her to take it with. :)
No Comments

she is very willing to help you, but good luck if you never had a stat class before. the TAs made this class hard in my opinion they are impossible graders and their logic makes NO sense at all.  if i had different TAs i think i'd be fine. they ruined it.
Wonder how I'll do the second time around this fall...can't judge much since I appeared to be the only one who didn't understand anything.
The prof is not that great at explaining things, but the class is very easy.  Easy math credit-it's 4 credits but you only meet 3 times a week for 50 min!
It would be pretty helpful if you understand these equations. BME 313(last part) 401 409 413 423 ... are just repeating similiar transport problems.

exams are 75% of ur grade, he's nice but CANNOT teach, EXTREMELY disorganized (we had a week left before finals and we still hadn't taken midterm 2 because he kept pushing them back so he had to combine midterm 3 and the final), 50% of our grade was on the line during finals week
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Butler was a horrible professor.  He never actually taught us anything and just spent every class deriving stupid equations that we had to straight up memorize for exams.  Going to class is pointless and the he never prepared us well for the exams.  This was my least favorite BME class & professor so far - by far.

He knew a lot of things in this class but he did not write any important notes in class and show the hard-reading notes which he already wrote and  just talk about it, it makes people hard to follow. you can prepare exam for his exam review note even not come to class.
Confused class all the fall. Never take his class again.

Extremely disorganized, is not prepared for lectures, have to schedule office hours a week out from the date, exams not like the study guides. Very poor professor that obviously has no idea what's he's doing with this class. Makes mistakes on exams and homework and lectures frequently.
Worst professor in BME

I took this class when it was Dr. Butler's first time taking the course so keep that in mind. There was a fairly high variability in exam difficulty. I used to think lectures were boring and I wasn't learning anything, but this next semester made me realize how much I learned from this class. He's willing to go over HW problems in office hours.

Some exams were very easy and others I had no idea what concepts I was being tested. This was Butler's first time teaching the course, so hopefully he has the syllabus figured out if he teaches it in the future. Overall, the class was not awful just be very comfortable with the content on the practice exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Butler is a great guy. He knows what he's talking about and is always willing to help out students that come to him with questions. He truly cares about the subject material. Definitely recommend taking a class with him if you have the chance.
Peter Butler is the man.
This class is pretty useless. It's still in the design stages and it shows. Most of the work comes at the end of the semester, while there is little at the beginning of it.

Dr. Bueno is a pretty awesome guy, I recommend him if you want to learn SQL and be inspired to be a better person lol. He genuinely cares about all of his students and will always help if someone needs help.

Good:
inspirational messages every class
open to feedback (used to have a strict sick policy with no leanance but changed it)
tests are pretty easy if you know what youre doing


Bad:
zybooks (all have them)
his lectures arnt great for learning
cares deeply about attendance 
Can only use what is taught in class

Amazing professor, loved his motivational speeches at the start of his classes, TAs are really helpful too. If you put in the effort to show up to class and understand the material, you will do great.

Professor Bueno was very nice, but his grading and criteria had many flaws. LAs were very helpful; they were the only reason why I got an A-. If you did not use Bueno's methods, he would instantly flag you for AI. Tests were not difficult; the class was just a lot of busy work. He would always start each class off with an inspirational message.

Professor Bueno was very nice and often shared life lessons before class, but when it came to teaching Python… good luck. Strict attendance and had a frustrating AI policy, using anything not taught in class was flagged as cheating, even using prior programming knowledge. Take a different professor if this is your first coding class.

Dr. Bueno is an amazing professor, starts his lectures with motivation, but his good nature shouldn't be mistaken for lenience.
Bi-weekly chapter quizzes and programming quizzes
Weekly programming assignments (in/out of class)
Two lowest quiz grades are dropped
HARD final exam, I was at an A- but fell to C+ because of my underestimation.
Good Luck!

The class is definitely hard, but I had zero coding experience and got an A. There is lots of homework, but he is one of the most caring professors. He starts every class with a motivational speech and offers himself as a resource to his students. He has an accent but I had no issues understanding him. He's so kind and VERY caring toward students.

it is evident that dr bueno cares about his students. however, it is difficult to understand the material when he explains it because of his accent. that is the only reason why i wouldn't take another class with him. i relied on help from the LAs and did a lot of self study. i wouldnt recommend his class if you can't understand accents.

I learned a lot in this class. The class itself is set up pretty well, but I'm not sure this professor is the best to take the course. For beginners, this class can be hard, but not impossible with a lot of practice. If you must take him, work hard and practice a lot. The final exam is kind of tough, and it's worth 30% of your grade. Good luck!

Vesga is a good guy, the class itself is hard. It's set up focused on the textbook with short videos to explain the general concepts posted to Canvas AFTER textbook questions are due. The homework can be hard for new coders, as well as tests/other work. Textbook explains poorly, is expensive, and overall left me feeling more confused than confident
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I had Professor Bueno for IST 140 and IST 210; he teaches 210 much better. In his 210 class, he thoroughly covers the material and provides graded exercises. There are short quizzes every two weeks with study sessions beforehand. The TAs were very helpful, and I learned a lot. I recommend Bueno for IST 210, but not for IST 140.

Professor Bueno is kind, but his IST 140 teaching style is challenging. With no coding experience, I found the class difficult. He rushed through lectures, assigned 2-4 coding tasks weekly, biweekly quizzes, and expected students to learn from the textbook. His class suits those with coding experience. Newbies should get another professor.

His attendance policy is ridiculous. I had Covid, which kept me out of class for 6 days. His policy is that after you miss 5 days, every day drops your attendance grade 10%. I missed a couple classes after that due to other reasons, and he didn't make an exception for me. The attendance grade dropped my grade 10% at the end of the semester.

Had him for IST140. Course is the exact same as AP CS A. TopHat for attendance. ZyBooks is graded for participation before class out of 10. The multiple choice questions show the answers, the open ended answers can be found on Chegg. Bi-weekly quizzes (that are recorded so no cheating) with a weekly problem sets graded by TAs. Pretty easy overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Really amazing teacher. I had him for IST140 and IST210. He used Zybooks for assignments that are due before class but they weren't too difficult to do. He always starts class with a motivational speech which are very nice in my opinion. IST210 is one of my favorite classes Ive taken so far and the way he taught it made it so easy to understand.

One of the best professors I've ever had. Had him for my first semester at school. A fair and helpful professor who is willing to help all of his students outside the classroom if need be. There is a bit of homework but nothing too daunting. Just be sure to really study past projects, ZyBooks, and notes for difficult unit quizzes.

He was a great instructor, the class was not difficult. The way he has it organized makes it very hard to not get an A in it. Attendance is mandatory and don't try to leave a day or two early that will not fly for him. He threw in extra credit for showing up the day before spring break. He gives partial credit for attempts even on tests. Take him!

Jhon Bueno comes across as a very kind person, however he doesn't take into account different people's situations. (EX: traveling for spring break) Attendance is mandatory, so show up and do the work, and you should easily do well in the class. Personally, I didn't mind him but a lot of my friends did not like him at all. Easy class though.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Online Savvy

reviews.comment: Kind, compassionate professor who adds life lessons and motivation. Lots of group engineering projects. Canvas/due dates can be confusing since he tweaks projects—ask questions and clarify deliverables. If you attend, follow directions, and turn in what he wants, an A is very achievable. Don't skip class.

Best professor ever. This 8am class was 100% worth it. He genuinely cares that you learn and actually understand. He makes sure you learn the software and builds your critical thinking in really unique ways. Also cares about your wellbeing in and out of class. Attendance is mandatory- if you just show up, you'll be fine.

Can't recommend Dr. Butler highly enough. His class is a perfect example of how teaching should be done. He'll make sure you meet new people, step outside of your comfort zone, try new things, and learn a ton. His class is the place to be for EDSGN 100.

Don't have enough good things to say about him. Genuinely cares about you not only as a student but as a person. Project heavy. Attendance mandatory. Come to class and work on the projects. He will know, and you will get an A.

Fantastic edesgn teacher. Genuinely wants you to learn. Work consists mainly of group projects. He gives a lot of freedom how these are done. He knows if you were actually trying or not, and your grade will reflect that.  Regular absences will harm your grade significantly.
One of the best for ENGINEERING DESIGN

One of the Best Professor for E design I would really recommend taking a class with Dr.butler very easy to speak with and we Didn't have to take the practicum he told us to go to an event and he gave us the whole 15 percent , and also the class was very very fun. just do your work and you will get an A

Great guy. Explains Solidworks well and incorporates a lot of group work into the class, but should be expected with an engineering course like EDSGN 100. The class is very long in itself so you don't really get much homework outside of class, which is the nice thing about this class. The projects were very interesting for the class.

Dr. Butler was a great professor and a great guy. His feedback was always insightful and he was always helpful and available. The class is an easy grade but you get what you put into it, putting in a lot of effort can be very useful.

Dr. Butler is a very involved professor, and he makes a strong effort to get to know his students. He explains SolidWorks well, assignments are easy to follow. A lot of group work is involved, but it's an engineering class, what do you expect? Even so, the group projects are fun and easy, highly recommend his class.
Straight beast. Not only wants you to succeed in his class, but as a person/Engineer overall. Great guy, and amazing professor for it being his first year as a professor at Penn State.

Professor Butler just became a professor at PSU. Overall great guy, not only wants to see students succeed in his class, but as an Engineer overall. The projects you do are fun and are directly relevant to what you will do as an Engineer. Makes personal connections with his students and is very funny. Highly recommend.

He's the best, makes class so much fun. Despite his class being in an online format, he kept all his students engaged and was easily accessible. Dr. Butler also took the time to learn about every student and make a personal connection.

He has a unique style of grading, he mainly eyeballs your grade and takes into account exams, quizzes and attendance. I've never really been good at math but he encourages students to ask questions which was nice.

This is the kind of professor you either really love or really hate. He has a very unique personality and teaching style. My semester isn't over yet, but so far, as long as you know what you're doing, you'll get through the course fine. He does give off ADHD vibes, so expect random tangents and a general lack of structure.

Took him for 486 too. Great guy, wants you to succeed. No point in cheating, in his words, you have to sabotage yourself to fail. I was a terrible student and didn't do well on the tests (despite
My interest and want to do the course) and ended with a C. Seriously, if you want a no stress pass class, he's it.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He a a really caring professor who wants you to learn and an overall great guy who is great to talk to about anything (especially his jazz music). His call board management may be crazy but you get used to it and you can ask him anytime to clarify. Is also encourages us to ask because, like all of us, he makes mistakes.

Prof Bryne is such a kind professor. He does go on tangents sometimes you can still manage to find the meaning behind it if you pay attention. Attendance is mandatory but if you show up and write down the examples on the board, you will pass. He cares about his students and wants them to pass!! Currently taking him for a second time for 484

Not a bad person, actually really nice guy. But very unorganized & struggles with explaining concepts. Creates examples and quizzes off the cuff, which contribute to confusing lectures and bad understanding. 30+ years of experience in teaching is no  excuse for coming to class unprepared. Go to office hours if you want an A.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are hard to follow. You might find the class overwhelming, but if you show up and attempt the homework, you will end up with a good grade. He has a different grading system, so it's hard to predict your final grade, but he is caring, so hope he won't catch you off guard.

I have to agree that the professor's lectures can sometimes go a bit hay-wire with his whiteboard management. But he is a really nice guy with a clear cut grading policy and is very lenient with grading. Just showing an attempt at a problem and some basic knowledge despite getting it wrong will get you decent grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Caring--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you like goofy professors that grade easily, you'll like Byrne. If you like professors that are coherent and organized, you will find Byrne incredibly frustrating. Lectures and assignments were sporadic and vague. Class attendance was mandatory. We got bogged down in arbitrary notation rather than actually learning and applying concepts.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Mandatory attedance, but if you really try and get to know him while working for his class there is no way that you can get a grade that your not happy with.

Professor Byrne has by far been one of my favorite professors at Penn State yet. Although I am not the smartest student, his lectures were very helpful and his take-home quizzes really helped me to learn the material. He wants success for all of his students, but he requires that you put in the effort to do so. Lectures are mandatory.

His teaching style is very sporadic and he pretty much made his own ways to solve the problems so using youtube is useless. The solutions to the homework and quizzes are very hard to decipher. It is a plug and chug class, but he is very non traditional. He is okay not great but does care for your well being if that counts for anything.

None of the negative reviews are necessarily wrong but each chapter is essentially one type of plug and chug problem. All you have to do to pass is figure out the procedure. He just ends up on confusing tangents in the middle of explaining the steps.

At first, I really did not like his teaching & I agreed with most of the bad reviews on here. But once I reached out to him in office hours, he was fully willing to give 2nd (and even 3rd) chances. He can be annoying at times, but he really just wants you to learn the material & does not care about grades. Show up to class and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--Caring

reviews.comment: Really enjoyed this class and Prof Byrne is a very helpful guy. As long as you pay attention in class and ask questions and/or attend office hours for help you should pass. Has been very lenient with extensions on quizzes when students voice their opinion that they don't understand the topic yet and goes over very relevant examples during class.

This class is manageable if you pay attention in class. Exams are not hard but extremely long (3 hours) and require you to use Mathematica. He wrote the textbook but it's kinda confusing. He occasionally gets lost in the middle of solving a problem. The bright side is he is very helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Teaches well. He knows the material and can explain it well. Teaches for understanding and not just grades. Makes the lectures very practical (how to apply concepts in real life). Encourages going over and above the material and new methods of solving problems.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Eli does not prepare for class and is unclear. He gets lost in the middle of the problem he is doing in the board and do not finish it. He has been in psu for a very long time but is mediocre. The material itself is not supposed to be hard, but he is so mediocre the class becomes a struggle. Also, very odd grading style and assigned seats.
The professor is just horrible. Dont take.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr Byrne doesnt really prepare for lectures, but honestly the course is so easy he doesnt really need to. I think he is genuinely a caring person (although the first time I met him I thought we had very arrogant). Hes a nice guy, and I really appreciate him as a professor:)

Goes off on tangents too often and makes a big deal about us being in our 'assigned' seats. Tends to emphasize material that he's barely taught right before the exam. His exams are insanely long (2.5-3+ hours per exam on average) and a lot of the course is teaching yourself from his posted HW and textbook. Will call on people randomly. Prepare!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: The material of the course should be easy, but he always made mistakes during the class and in his notes (he let us use the notes as the textbook), so everybody is confused in his class. He is a good person, fun and humorous, but not a good teacher in my opinion.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Take this for my math major requirement. Really feel suffered because he kept making mistakes on class. Extremely bad on board notes, extremely ridiculous grading process. He doesn't have any nice personality that I enjoyed from other math professors. BTW he had taught this class for over 20 years, but he's still an AP now. Think about it why.

Garbage teacher. For the love of God do not take any class with him if you have the choice. Does not prepare for class, teaches about 25% of a problem and then spends the rest of class trying to make up problems that he also doesn't solve. One of the worst teachers I've ever encountered.

Preparing for course, I suppose, is the most fundamental thing to do as an educator, but he does not. In every lecture, he spends 20% of the time on coming up with an example, 20% of the time to do it, and 20% of the time on answering questions because nothing make sense. 40% of the course is past by watching him revising his miscalculation.

After years of studying at Penn State, I believe I gained the most valuable insights from Dr. Zhong. His genuine care for his students was evident. During the pandemic, he showed us strategies for coping with stress and hopelessness. Even today, I continue to apply his scientifically published tips to my daily life. Thank you, Dr. Z!

DRZ is the best, most understanding prof you may have at Penn State. Dr. Z is super smart, whose lectures are inspirational. Above all, he deeply cares about our mental health during the tough pandemic times. He cares about his students' learning. He is exemplary in delivering amazing lectures as an intelligent and caring prof.

I have taken 3 courses with Dr. Z and like him more each year. You'll miss a lot if you never take his courses at Bellisario College of Communications. Dr. is an inspirational professor who uses lots of real-world examples and case studies that apply the principles we were learning to the real world. I see comm major differently because of him.

I have 1 word for Dr. Z and his course - Journalism & Social Media Analytics - Amazing! The past year was difficult for all of us. Dr. Z took extra effort to make learning fun and inspirational. He deeply cares for his students and has a genuine passion for teaching/research. Dr. Z should be the Professor of the Year (2020-21) at Penn State.

Dr. Z is one of the best professors I've had at Penn State. The class was interesting as it focused on future developments for news media and the issues with current media. There were discussion posts every week, which included a lot of reading. There were also three big papers, but no tests. One of the most caring professors and recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: Dr. Zhong is a great professor and person. I am happy I took it with him because he is the most intelligent and caring professor I had at Penn State. This is the second time I took his course, all good experiences. I love PSU even better after meeting him.

Prof Zhong is so kind, really cares about his students, and is very understanding. Easy A if you do the readings and discussion posts. A couple group projects- he's a fair grader. I thought this class would be beyond boring but he makes it interesting and knows what he's talking about. I love him- definitely would recommend taking his classes

Dr. Zhong is very smart and knows what he's talking about. He is a GREAT professor and person with a passion for teaching, just from listening to one lecture you can learn so much about the current and future developments of news media, not just news media ethics. I love his class because Dr. Z is extremely experienced in his field.

Dr.Z is amazing. Great professor who really cares about his students and their success. I liked how we would learn about visual story-telling skills, esp. what works and doesn't, and then we would apply them to our four packages. I am glad I chose to attend his C465. Great expertise and personality. Love Dr.Z!
Bu is a very understanding professor, BUT he does grade pretty tough as it is a 400-level course.

You have many blog posts to complete, some which require you to attend guest speakers but, he cancels class to accommodate the time required. His lectures are somewhat boring but he is funny so it makes it tolerable. You need the textbook for the online tests because he uses a lot of info from the book but, the online tests are easy.

Dr.Z is a wonderful teacher, he makes you feel comfortable from the start. He helps you understand a very important skill -visual storytelling, which will help any career you like to pursue. I wish I could come to his classes earlier. He cares his students dearly. Above all, he knows so much about media tech.

Dr. Z is the Best professor I had at PSU. I gained a lot of confidence in myself after I took his class.  I wish I took his class earlier, not in my last year at PSU. I love the selfie I took with him.

Dr. Z is awesome! I love him inside and outside the classroom. I did not get A in his class (close enough) but I still love him. Attending his classes was a wonderful learning experience. Go to his COMM465 if you like to learn good skills. BTW, he cares his students and goes an extra mile to help you, plus a very fair grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Dr. Z is an amazing person and professor. He is overall just a kind and wonderful guy. He will go out of his way to help and accomadate you and he genuinely cares about your success in his class and in the real world. He went above and beyond to help me achieve the grade I did.

Great professor for TV reporting. He is fair and professional, and most importantly, he cares students. You will learn a lot from him if you put time and effort into it. You must contribute to teamwork, which is also fun part of the class.

Dr. Z is the best professor you dream to have at Penn State. You'll learn greatly from his expertise and rich industry experience no matter what level you are at. He cares you and helps you to achieve more. One example, he answered your email in minutes after it was sent to him after 1 a.m. After taking his class, I also learned a lot about myself.
Best teacher I've ever had in all my years of schooling. I considered changing my major just so I could take more classes with this handsome man.

Nice guy, and can be pretty funny once you get his sense of humor. The class is pretty easy although I found it kind of boring. You dont need to put as much of an effort as you might think either. Final project is easy. would rec.

Dr.Z is a really nice person and his lectures are considered fun since it is a nethical class after all. the final project is not that hard as long as you put effort and be patient with it. lots of extra credits to make up your grade, I spend less time on this class than my other classes and got an A, not a super easy A, but def not a hard one.
Dr. Zhong was very good.  Would definitely suggest taking him for COMM 409.  Easy to understand.  The Final Project was not easy so watch out if you have to do one.

Take Dr. Z's class if you seriously want to learn something, esp. critical thinking. This class is a life-change event for many but not for slackers. You will love every bit of Dr. Z's class as he really cares and has expertise in what he teaches. Also a very understanding and helpful professor. He answered your emails in two min.

This course seems easy at first with very few assignments other than short online journals and a group project that takes two days to prepare. The final project with rip your heart out. Its 10 pages long needing 8 sources and you get about 2 weeks to do it.  Nothing prior in the class prepares you for it. I'd avoid Bu Zhong's media ethics class.

BEWARE: People will tell you Dr. Z is the best for Media Ethics. Its true but class is not easy like people say. At first workload is super light, but final project is 12 pages needing 8 refs and you only get two weeks before finals to do it. In no way does he prepare you for this project.  Seriously, take another section of COMM 409.

Bu is a great professor, really invested in the topic and has a lot of valuable experience to share. You don't need the textbook which he told our class on the first day. He also allows you to bring a cheat sheet for every exam. As long as you go to class, do decent journals, and put some effort into the project you'll do fine. I loved his class!

He was truly a nice man. But the class was kind of confusing because what he wanted was unclear. It took me a while to figure out if you let him know ahead of time that you could miss many classes. The expectations for projects, quizzes and exams were not clear. It was frustrating, but the blogs we did for class were helpful for my internship.

Dr. B Zhong... is the coolest professor ever. His test are fairly simple and easy. He is a little hard to understand. But he does have powerpoints, so its not that bad. The class is a little boring, but what class about ethics is not. Just make sure to attend class, because he does take attendance. Don't buy the book.
So Bu Zhong was the most understanding prof I have ever had. I would take him..try to attend most classes...ditch the book it sucks. Use good cheat sheets and you have it made.

he was supposed to be a great producer at CNN back in the day. he knows a lot about the business, but not how to get you a great demo reel. i love him, i've had him twice and use him as a reference, i wouldnt take manion to save my life, so bu was the best choice ever!

Painfully boring. Everyone plays Sudoku/crossword in class. I thought I would find the subject interesting, but instead I find no motivation to come to class or do the work. English sometimes hard to understand, though usually not. Textbook not required, yet now he takes material from it for the exams? Just a life-draining experience all-around.

Honestly, his English isnt that bad at all, if you cant understand it that probably means youre a closet xenophobe. Anyway, he is pretty boring and the papers he makes you write are kind of demanding.

His class is great in every sense. Go to him if you like to learn. His teaching is well-organized, above all concise and easy to understand. Both his class notes and instructions for projects are clear, and easy to follow, and also posted on ANGEL. Extremely nice and helpful whenever I need it, including non-office hours. He replies email quickly.

Bu is VERY hard to understand because of his accent. His instructions for projects are VERY VERY unclear and disorganized. His class gets boring because you can't understand what he is saying. He is nice though, and understands if students need more time for projects etc. GO TO CLASS. dont need a book and there are no tests. lots of projects
A great instructor and always helpful.

Bu is awesome. He cares so much about his students and how well they are doing. I feel like he's an easy grader. Our TA is lousy, that's the only reason the quizzes might be hard once in awhile. But Bu will do anything to help his students out!! I definately recommend him if you're taking comm ethics.
A disorganized teacher. Class discussions have nothing to do with what's in the textbook but quizzes and exams come straight from the book. He does not explain what's in the book at all.

Kind of hard to understand him. Lot's and Lot's of work: many quizzes, papers, journal entries for this class.  He is a very nice teacher though, and always willing to help, but the workload is bit much. Quizzes are straight from the text book which he does not talk about in class. He gives extra credit.

Professor Byrd is very nice. The class is mostly graded on your four exams, and only a few HW assignments, and two papers. She is a fair grader. However, there is a lot of content and the exams can be quite tricky. You really will need to study.

Don't take this class if you are not interested in the field itself. I needed another class and thought this intro class would be easy. It feels like you are dropped into an advanced class rather than an intro. Tests can be very hard even after studying but she does a good job explaining in class. Homework is easy. Good teacher just hard work.
Dr. Byrd was inspirational. Her passion for speech pathology convinced me this is the field for me. The class wasn't easy, but all the work was clear and doable. She was always willing to help.
Professor is incredibly kind and is very passionate in the subject she teaches. Attendance is not mandatory, but TopHat questions are used as points for attendance.

Attendance is optional but gives TopHat questions that you're graded on for completion. Lecture slides are super long & you have to go to class to fill in missing parts of the notes. Exams are pretty tough so you definitely have to really study. Only gives 2 papers. Overall, really nice professor but class can drag a little!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I thought the observation class was very helpful and Professor Byrd was very accessible and ready to answer all my questions. I would definitely recommend this class.

Professor Byrd was very nice and she really wants her students to succeed, however her lectures are very boring and not interactive at all besides a few TOPHAT questions. The class was easy, and there are lots of opportunities for extra credit, but it was just a very boring class. Exams can be taken from home on ZOOM.
Interesting class but sometimes lectures would get pretty boring. Quizzes are taken online. Two papers are worth a lot of points and important.

Her classes weren't very interactive, they consisted of her just reading off the slides. Most of the time, test reviews didn't line up with the material that was actually on the exam. Overall, her class felt like a bore. The material was hard enough and she didn't put much effort into making it easier.

Honestly would not take this class again. I think I took this for an elective and I feel like I just learned a years worth of information. The homework is easy, but she is so specific on grading and every little detail has to be right or you get points off. Exams are hard because they are so question specific you HAVE to study. Ridiculous tbh

Professor Byrd has such a passion for CSD and is so inspiring. I would definitely take a million classes from her. She brings lots of her treatment experience to the classroom and has good jokes to supplement some of the drier parts of the lectures.

I love professor Bryd. Her tests are very straightforward; if you show up to class and take notes, you should do great. Though at times her lectures can be boring, she is a very nice and understanding person.

She is so passionate about her job, I thought she was a great teacher. She teaches by doing notes, and a lot of them so be prepared for that but she is clear and precise about what she is teaching. Her tests were not too bad if you studied and prepared for them! She is so sweet and understanding and I highly recommend her class.

Ms. Byrd is a great professor. She is very passionate about this class and it shows during her lectures. The 4 exams are very doable if you fill out the study guides and go over the power points. The 2 essays are also fine and I genuinely enjoyed turning what I learned into something creative. I would definitely take this class again!

She is so cute and passionate about CSD, clearly knows what she is talking about. Had to write a few papers and there were 4 exams (clear guidelines/study guides), goes over lots of content but she does a very good job teaching it (shows lots of videos to demonstrate what she is talking about). I really liked her and would take her class again.

Amanda has truly been one of the best professors I have had at Penn State. She is super friendly and eager to answer questions. It is obvious she knows a lot about the material and provides many resources (fill-in slides, videos of the material, study guide outlines for exams). She values your time and sticks to her syllabus' course schedule.

Professor Amanda Byrd gives incredibly boring lectures. All assignments are graded by the T.A's and are not always graded fairly. The class was an absolute pain to get through (this is coming from a future SLP). She puts blanks randomly on the slides so you cannot review slides after class unless you write out every random word she has a blank for.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: If you don't have a big interest in CSD, this class gets really dry and boring. However, Amanda is really sweet and it's clear how much she cares about her students and knows about CSD. The study guides are extremely helpful, I just filled them out extensively a few days before the exams and I did fine on all four.

Do not take if you have no interest in CSD, it will bore you to death and will make the exams harder. Exams are straightforward but cover ALOT of information. Study guides are long and covers more than what is on exam. Do not study last minute or you'll be overwhelmed. 2 Papers and 6 Hw are mostly easy.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Very easy class overall. For CSD146, she gave study guides for each exam and the final exam was basically just the 4th exam bc it wasn't cumulative. Basically just show up, fill in the powerpoint notes she gives u, use those to fill out the study guides she gives u, study 2 days prior to the exam, and you're fine. The 2 papers, extremely easy.

Lectures can get a little boring if you don't have interest in CSD. She's a good professor and gives examples. Attend lectures though because she does in class activities sometimes which helps. Exams are easy if you study and understand the material

Amanda is honestly the nicest woman I have ever met. Sometimes class got a little boring, but if you have interest in the material, I'd definitely recommend taking it with her. She makes concepts easy to understand and gives a study guide.

Amanda is nice but she's not the best teacher. Things arent explained super well and her grading criteria is not the clearest. Very quiet and monotone, lectures are boring. Go to class the first 3 weeks and get ur 25 clicker points then you never have to go back. Slides are put on canvas, they have blanks but you can google the answers

Amanda Byrd is a great professor! I can honestly say I enjoyed this class. Her exams are very straightforward - just study the study guides she puts out! Her homeworks are not hard to figure out, and she offers extra credit! You do have to attend class for clicker points, and she leaves some blanks on her PowerPoints.

She's a good teacher. Everything that you need to know for the exam is straightforward, no tricky questions. Study seriously for the tests and you'll do fine. There are homeworks and papers that'll bring up your grade. Attendance is kinda mandatory because she does clicker questions almost every day. She's nice and will help if you ask
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Professor Byrd really takes the time to be sure you learn the material. She is very smart and an expert clinician, and that experience makes it easy to see how the class will connect to therapy careers. I would definitely take another class with her.

The class was two exams and no final which was nice. The exams usually took around 2-3 hours and scheduled 7-10 which I wasn't a fan of. Professor Byrne is a great guy and really cares about his students learning and understanding the material. I wish he had better resources to learn from or old practice exams to study for exams.

Professor Byrne does this with "his own special method". I fell behind in the class and he isn't very understanding or helpful in this case. The material in the class isn't necessarily challenging, but because its "his own method" I can't go to youtube or anywhere to learn the materials. Not bad class, but I am just not a big fan of him

Professor Byrne is a top professor at Penn State. His lectures were engaging and thought-provoking. He created quality, non-mandatory homework assignments, quizzes, and his own (free) textbook. He holds plenty of office hours and wants to see every student succeed. Sometimes his humor or lectures were esoteric in nature, but ultimately he is a gem.
He cares about his students and his exams were not hard.
hard class, worth the effort!
He speaks well but not write well... I don't understand his emails...
