He cares a lot about attendance. His grading will seem pretty ambiguous but after all, he will give a reasonable grade to people who worked hard. He loves students who try their best and work hard. I personally loved his lecture, especially after the second midterm.

His grading system is broken into attendance, quizzes, and tests. Whatever category is the worst becomes 50% of your grade. His lectures are mandatory, dry, and he often gets sidetracked. No math professor at PSU talks in circles as much as Dr. Byrne. He will make tons of mistakes in class, and it's part of your participation grade to catch them.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Best professor I've ever had. Kinda irks me he isn't a 5. Not harsh in the slightest, has plenty of office hours, and will bend over backwards to help students. Only con I can think of is he makes attendance mandatory, but his lectures are both good and important enough that you should be going to them anyway. Gonna miss my lectures from Dr Byrne

Dr. Byrne is great! Really cares and works hard to make sure you understand the material. He is very relaxed with the grading, so it is hard to not pass this class. Plus, the material you learn is actually useful in the real world, so that's good!
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: This class is weird in the sense the material does take time and effort to master. He does almost the whole class on mathematica, because of which his grading is really lenient. He curves extensively but there's a lot of self study involved. It's painstaking but you're almost guaranteed at least a B if you just show up.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I took Chriss class in 2008. He was the most memorable professor at Penn State. He personally tutored me during his spare time when I needed help. Great guy!

Spends too much time making sure we're in our seats the first few weeks. Goes off on tangents too often. Tends to be a bit cocky and emphasizes material that he's barely taught right before the exam. A lot of it's teaching yourself from his posted HW solutions and his subpar textbook. Impossible to get below a C unless you never show up though.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Worst professor I ever seen in Penn State. He is knowledgeable but doesn't know how to teach at all.

In a field largely populated by poor teachers, Byrne stands out as more scatterbrained and disorganized than any other math professor I've had. He improvises the entire course, teaching one random thing, followed by the next, without every really drawing any clear connections. Worse yet, he holds different students to different standards. Useless.
This guy is a quack, i took his class and the class is very easy.  However, he wants everyone to learn and as a result i didnt learn anything...

Dr. Byrne is VERY smart and knows what he is talking about. Very willing to help; he wants everyone to do well and learn the material. Lectures get very detailed. If you pay attention and put in some effort, you will understand the material. Great sense of humor, great sax player, and a really nice guy in general.

Awful. Showed up 20 min late for his own tests. On the first day told us not to take notes because it would all be in the book. But guess what? He taught completely differently than the book did so the book was worthless for his tests. No notes on Angel. Rambles off on tangents so he's very hard to follow in lecture.

It was his first time teaching an IE class and I just wish for you guys that it would be his last time. I personally thought he wrote the good ratings on this site because I don't know how someone cna give him a overall rating better than 1. He never prepares for class. Always complains the class size is too big for his so-called "methods".
PRofessor Byrne is extremely helpful and knowledgeable in the field of game theory.  I would recommend Math 486 with Chris Byrne to anyone.

I think Dr. Byrne is one of the best and smartest professors I have seen at Penn State. He knows his material inside out and. He takes the time to make sure that you understand the material and goes at extra length to explain. I strongly suggest taking his class and you will do well as long as you attend,pay attention,and work hard.
Very strange guy.  Tries to change class times around a lot.  Tests aren't that hard; he really wants his students to do well.

He never prepares for class, so he makes everything up off the top of his head, so it all comes out in a weird order that doesn't make much sense.  The book used, he wrote, and well lets say the publishing company had to issue a book of corrections to it.  He talks on his phone in class.  Just very a unprofessional person, and it shows.

I liked his style.Byrne was very helpful in office hrs, and he knows a lot about the topic he teaches. It's nice to have a math professor who actually speaks English (no offense to other teachers..) and can relate the material to everyday occurrences. Sure, he had to reschedule or cancel class a few days, but having class at 8am, this was a relief!

I am a math ed student and took this class as an elective. He is typically 5-15 min late to class, and this semester has taken 5 vacation days. He works for the gov't and seemingly doesn't care about this class or students. Very hard to understand and everyone ive talked to in class feels similarly to me except compsci majors. Do not take his class

He is a really nice person! Very good in office hours! Has a lot of interest in the material, which makes the class more fun for the students. I would definitely recommend this class to others (have done so already!).

Very easy class-But u def. have to go to class. He doesn't miss alot of classes like everyone says. Besides how many of you have never missed a class!! Midterms were take home, & he gave practice ones that were exactly like the actual exams. The final was in class. Def. go to office hours if u need help. As long as you try you will do well.

The material is different than anything I've done before and Mathematica was new to me too.  He helped with any problems we had though, and explained things again if at first they were confusing.  Chris was lively and fun to learn from...definitely worth taking this class.

He admits that he has been working with this material for so many years that he forgets what is hard for new students.  The material is difficult and it is hard to explain to the whole class.  But, he was very very helpful if you make the effort.  Go to his office hours and he will answer all questions and make you understand as well as he can.
No Comments
He's a really likable guy and the class works well at the pace I'm accustomed to learning.

Misses class all the time for business. Kind of egotistical about how important he is. Teaches fast, tries to explain, but is not always clear. Not always clear about instructions for exams, which are all take home. No in class grading. But don't be fooled, go to class or you will miss alot!

easy class - all assignments are take home, exams are take home too. is hard to learn from, jumps around a bit, and often is late or shows up grungy and sweaty to class, kind of grossly distracting. makes a lot of business trips, so misses class often, an okay teacher.

Professor Byron is absolutely awesome. She made a really tough subject so easy to understand and digest. She is so understanding of students and is respectful of their time. Attendance wasn't mandatory as long as you let her know, and there were fun kahoots every week. The homeworks were long and tough, but they ended up being pretty fun.

I took ME 521 from Professor Byron several years ago.  It was one of the best classes I have taken at any level on any subject.  Dr. Byron consistently made herself available to everyone.  Her lectures were clear & well organized.  It was also apparent that she loves to teach. Take this class, but be ready to work hard and get over it.

This class is good if you want to have a basic understanding of fluid mechanics. If you have studied well in the undergraduate, probably one should not take this course because you won't learn anything extra. Professor's lecture notes and videos are well organized and she teaches very well. She is also really helpful during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Group projects--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Byron is great researcher but not an educationist. She expects you to know everything and says you should know this already from your undergrad courses, which is not helpful at all since not everyone remembers what they learned from undergrad. Her lecture notes are very disorganized, with all equations and little explanation.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Accessible outside class--Test heavy

reviews.comment: She is one of my favorite professors at Penn State. Her leadership and communication skills are amazing. This course is very difficult, but she does an excellent job -- expect to be prepared for heat transfer, etc.

I am so grateful for everything that Dr. Byron has taught me about science/engineering/research. She is a very kind person with a real passion for mentoring the next generation. She's always excited to teach people new things and you can literally see her eyes light up when she talks about fluid dynamics and her research. 10/10. She's amazing.

Like others have said, she is very smart and her passion for the subject is her best quality. The class is very difficult but you will learn a lot. Some of the homework questions are way too difficult. Go to her office hours for concepts, and the TA office hours to do the homework! She was very well respected and with the work you can get an A.

Byron is super passionate about what she teaches. However, she is far too intelligent to be teaching undergraduate fluids. Her homework is very challenging and her tests are just as difficult. She doesn't believe in giving equations, so you derive everything instead. You'll learn more than other kids in fluids, but you'll work significantly harder.

Professor Byron is extremely intelligent and passionate about fluid dynamics but she would be better off teaching grad courses. Her homeworks and exams are incredibly difficult and require new derivations of equations that you do not see in class.

Dr. Byron is a great professor. Though relatively new to teaching grad courses, she (in her own words), learned much of her teaching style from Dr. Cimbala. I won't have him until next semester, but the descriptions of his style on this site align with what I experienced with her. She is clearly very passionate and knowledgeable on fluid mechanics.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr Byron is a great professor. I learned a lot about fluid mechanics from her class, and office hours were pretty good too. Her lectures were exciting. There was a lot of homework and sometimes it was hard, but it was worth it. You won't regret taking her class unless you're lazy and expect everything to just be handed to you.

Homeworks are too hard. Tests are hard too. The gives pop questions to take attendance, and brings props to class / shows us videos of her research which is pretty cool. Overall I think she cares about the students, but it's a tough class.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: genuinely the most wholesome professor you might ever have at penn state. exams are easy, final paper is pretty straightforward, and discussions are always interesting. but also just like the nicest person you could possibly have as a professor

professor byun was one of the best professors I've ever had. he is willing to help and makes lectures fun by having students lead discussions so it makes all the content easier to understand. he grades heavily on attendance and participation. there's two exams and a final paper, all fairly straight forward, very hard to faik this class
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I took this class as an elective based and on the other reviews. Soo-Yong was funny and relaxed as a professor. Grades are based on attendance, participation, a midterm, a final, and a final paper. As long as you show up, join the discussion, and have a general understanding of the readings, the class is easy A. He does expect a lot of reading.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Soo-Yung is the BEST. He loves engaging everyone in discussion, and as long as you try, you'll get an A. He isn't focused on grades or tricking you, but more about having open discussions and all getting to know each other. Super chill class, really great time overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Byun is amazing! He is very knowledgable and has very good insights on topics of sociology. The class itself is truly fascinating and everyone should have to take it. The discussions are helpful and allow you to learn other perspectives. He assigns too much reading than can be expected but overall a fantastic teacher.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Caring

reviews.comment: What a wasteless use of space.  Terrible teacher.  Worst I've had at Penn State.  Tells jokes then gets angry when you don't laugh.  Hated every minute of his class.  Worst class in BBH.

Fun but HARD class unless you put in the time and effort. He knows his stuff, will take all the time he can to help you during office hours, and he's very down to earth. I was failing but I went to every single office hour for the entire semester and I passed. Get the book, sometimes it's hard to follow through in lecture!

Difficult class with emphasis on the textbook. Attendance is not mandatory and all answers for exams can be found in the book. Open ended and essay exams are tricky, but lots of room for partial credit. Professor is exciting and office hours are useful if you have questions.

Best professor I ever had. Never wanted to miss class, very interesting. His exams are straight forward w/ no trick questions & are straight from lecture & notes, which is why attendance is important. 4 HW assignemnts, & offers extra credit, very easy. Adds jokes & stories throughout class. Very nice guy, not out to get u. Take the class, easy A!!

I do not have any science backround so i thought the multiple choice exams were somewhat difficult.You have to read all of his slides and questions at the end of chapter to do well.  But the projects and extra credit opportunity bump your grade enormously.  Although u may think u r doing bad u will most likely end up with an A. Take the Class.

Not the best professor in the world. His exams rarely relate to the material and his lectures like to go off onto side tracks. His jokes are only mildly amusing at best. He does offer good extra credit opportunities, however, and the practicum make up for the usually cruddy exam grades. I would take this class with caution.
Pretty good. Many students stumble on the first test, but if you give his class a serious work ethic, you'll do well and learn a lot.

Easiest class ever, easy A, even if you don't go to a single class you'll end up with a B. When I did go to class it wasn't even bad, he has lots of funny stories about drugs and stuff, definetely take this class.
No Comments

This class was challenging but fun.  I discussed candidly many topics in class, and Dr. Jones helped me get a research position with one of his colleagues in Hershey.  All in all, one of my favorite professors at PSU.  A very cool guy.

This class was really easy, it's an easy A. Most of the informaation comes from the textbook. If it wasn't for him taking attendence it wouldn't have been worth going to class. He does add alot of his own funny stories though.
The Class is easy. His lectures not too great, but his office hours is a boon for you. Do your homeworks, quiizes are the same and an A is child's play

Byron is a really nice guy and cares about how you are doing in the class, however his monotone voice and unclear powerpoints doesn't help you learn the material. Although homework is somewhat mandatory, I highly recommend doing it, that is how I learned everything which helped me do well on the quizzes.

The class itself is easy. A very easy grader. Very helpful. He may appear not to know much, but he is good with his matter. You need to sit in front of the class to get better results as the back is very noisy, and he doesn't mind. His office hours, he can spend ours explaining till you get it right.. If you are in the EMS college, take 141G.

I took ANTH with this prof, I feel that she gets very politcal, and even though I agree with her, its really weird/ uncomfortable. I dont come to class to hear your political opinions... She grades very wrong, and talks WAY too much, pretty much everyone in this class feels this way. Shes nice but simultaneously rude and does unnecessary things.
Professor Warner was nice and kind enough definitely let personal bias bleed into her lessons for sure, wasn't very open to class discussion

Ridiculously hard grader for a 100-level course. She never gave rubrics for us to follow and then would drop us points for not following her instructions. There are only 8 graded assignments and I don't think anyone finished above a B+. Also a ton of reading each week. She would assign 200+ pages to be read every week.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Wanner has easily been the most helpful history professor I've taken a class with. There are weekly writing assignments part of the course criteria, but the topics are usually easy to write about. She truly cares about her students and it shows. Her grading is fair and works with you, not against you.
Really cares about her students and the material. There is a lot of reading but the history is not particularly hard to grasp. Take her if you can.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Caring

reviews.comment: Professor Wanner is a great human being and cares about her students. Do not take this class if you do not want to read or write extensively. If you do, take her class because it improves your writing and makes you think more cogently about interesting topics. 100/10
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She's a really nice person but I wouldn't take this class again. She seems to be forgetting that this is a 100 level course--she grades too hard and expects too much. While it's nice that she drops the lowest test grade, it's hard to get a high grade in the first place. I'm a straight A student and I only got a B+ in this class.

Prof. Wanner is the sweetest prof I have ever had. She truly wants the best for her students. Her exams are not the easiest, and there's a lot of reading. I wish there was a little more extra credit bc exams are weighted heavily. I can't even be mad at her for that though because she's an amazing professor and person overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Great teacher. Very helpful. Excepts a lot from her students, but is very helpful in helping students meet her expectations.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Dr. Wanner is really knowledgeable in what she teaches, and goes pretty in-depth during lectures.  She really cares that her students know the information, and incorporates plenty of extra credit opportunities that are worthwhile.  Lots of reading and a good number of papers to write.

She's very clear in her lectures, and if you do the readings. The readings aren't bad. They really enhance the lectures. This is NOT a good class to take if you do not want to attend class or not do the work. She notices who is there and who is not. She also notices who participates, and she recognizes your efforts. She makes it interesting!

i looked at past mc exams which were pretty easy. however, she made them essays sometime after the previous comment. honestly, i m super pissed. i kinda like this class and subject but the essay thing is annoying, time consuming and not "GPA friendly" especially u r taking this class for GEN ED and not a liberal art student.

I thought the material in class was really interesting and thought provoking. You really cover the span of communism, and she enjoys talking about her life experiences. I didn't really read any of the books. She made some of the most difficult multiple choice tests I have ever taken. Study the notes and you'll learn a lot.
Good class, good teacher who is pretty easy. Buy the Nittany Notes to go with the course, they help and basically remove the need to go to class.

Very intelligent and teaches in a way that makes the material understandable to people not familiar with the subject. It is easy to do go in her class if you really pay attention to what she says... and for a history class, she is not boring.
Great teacher, really nice lady.  Go to class becasue the tests are not really BS-able.  Pay attention to names, dates and major themes in the course.
Great teacher-Very engaging and intelligent.  Work load isn't bad if you are interested in Soviet Russia.

Her style is to do a lot of reading, and then have class discussions and lectures. She is very knowledgable on her topic, which makes the class really interesting. I would reccomend this class to anyone interested in it.
Difficult class. Notes aren't posted, you gotta take your own. But, she's a really nice prof that curves generously and wants each student to succeed

She is very nice but also kind of stern. Make sure you show up to class and if you have issues ask questions. Most of the assignments are self explanatory as long as you know the material. 1 group project at the end of the semester with 1 midterm.

4 problem sets and quizzes but she drops one quiz. Quizzes are pretty easy. 1 midterm, final, and presentation. She actually really likes the material which helps in lectures. She does not post anything on Canvas, not even grades, except problem sets. She gives back all the papers though. Can be frustrating but stick through and you'll be fine.

She is inexperienced as a teacher but she is incredibly well-rounded and is very aware of the subject matter due to her coming from the industry. She cares about the students' progress and grasp of the material. Though I struggled with a particular concept during my tenure in her classroom she made herself available to help me. Would take again!
She is not good fit for the PennState. I dont know how she get hired.

She can be very quiet and soft spoken in a big lecture hall, so hard to understand. She is a very sweet person and individually checks on students to see if they are understanding everything. Classes were typically long and boring, not engaging, and she doesn't have the best control of the class. She's nice but could be a better professor

YALL TRIPPIN. She is the sweetest professor. Her expectations are clear and she offers a lot of extra credit. Lectures can be boring but hello this is college. Also only two in-person exams and one was open note so
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: She is very moody. I want her to be a research professor instead of lecturer. But she is a good human being and yes all the young people can learn many things from her.

Her lectures are long and boring, and she constantly calls students out for small things, which is embarrassing. She's openly rude and inflexible with her strange grading system. Making each student stand up and be rated by classmates in a 40-person lecture was humiliating. I'd avoid this class at all costs.

Lectures are very hard to follow and hear overall. By attending class regularly and not studying, the exam was alright, so that's a plus. Takes 50% off of papers when they are 30 min- 1hr late. Take into account class participation and attendance heavily. would recommend another teacher but you should still be able to get a good grade if you attend

Do not take her class. Her lectures re impossible to follow and she is insane about attendance. Also, if a paper is 30 minutes late, she gives you a 50%. She is one of the worst professors I have had at Penn State and steer clear at all costs.

One of the worst HR teachers. Her tests are extremely difficult. Stay away from her at all costs. Even if you can take the class at a community college, that would be better. Also, if you are sick and can't attend class, you need a medical excuse for your absence. Otherwise, your grades will be lowered.

I took this class over the summer as a part of the LEAP program. The professors are the best: they're very caring and engaging. This is probably one of the easiest classes I'll take at Penn State, but also one of the most interesting. The "textbooks" are just two short books you'll read through the course of the semester, but it's very manageable.

One of my favorite classes has been science in literature (SC142N). I took it over summer 2025 and would highly recommend taking this course. Not only was the course engaging because of the material, but it was enjoyable because of the professors. Both of the Dr. Gs truly seemed like they loved the course, and wanted to be there.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Caring

reviews.comment: This course is one of my favorite classes I've taken here. It's partnered with her husband, and the class pairs very interesting science concepts with literature pieces. Both of the Dr. Gs made the class very entertaining and interactive, and were two of the best professors I've ever had. I would highly recommend this class and both professors.

I took Science in Literature over the summer of 2025, and it ended up being one of my favorite classes so far. It was both engaging and educational, which made it really enjoyable. I'd definitely recommend this teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I took Science in Literature over the summer, and it ended up being one of my favorite classes so far. It was both engaging and educational, which made it really enjoyable. I'd definitely recommend this teacher!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I was excited to take Prof. Gs class last sem because of her reviews. Big mistake. I did well in her class however she gave bad feedback so it was hard. her class is so so attendance and participation heavy and for a class so boring it's genuinely the worst. She has a bad attitude and thinks she is so much better than everyone. Run.

Fall24. I do not like the formatting of English courses, but Prof. Georgiou makes it much more bearable. She only assigns what she has to, and the essay requirements are clear. The slides give you everything you need, so most of the reading isn't necessary. Essays are graded based on the rubric. Responds to emails quickly and is very understanding.

Dr. G was an incredible professor and make English 15 fun and easy.There are three papers that you have to write in the course, first two are very easy and fun. The final one is a bit difficult but all English 15 students have to write it and she explains it well and makes it easy to write. She's an easy grader, just put in effort and go to class.

Ignore that one person who rated her bad, Dr. G is really amazing. Attendance is mandatory, but she gives you SOOOO much time in class to complete assignment. She is a super fair grader who gives amazing feedback, and overall just a kind professor who genuinely cares about you. Her dog is also super cute and she shows pictures of her :)
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I hate ENGL 15, but she is a great prof. Attendance is very important to your grade. Three essays, but she grades fairly and gives good feedback. Lots of busywork assignments but as long as you follow directions it is an easy A. Do not buy the textbook, needed it 1 time for an assignment, but I went to the library and checked it out for 2 hours
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: engl 15 is a class no one wants to take, but shes very nice and replies to emails super quick. required to buy the textbook, but i maybe used it once. her feedback on essays is super helpful, her grading is pretty fair, sometimes even a little too nice but i'll take it. make sure to go to class, it's a big part of your essay grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor G was a great teacher! English 15 in general is a stupid class, but she's so sweet and answers emails SO fast. Only thing is you HAVE to go to class. Attendance and class participation is part of your essay/infographic grade, so you should go. Homework is pretty easy and she gives you a lot of time to revise it.

I hate this class. So unnecessary and assigns stupid work for no reason. She always sounds out of breath and thinks she's so witty. WORK EVERY SINGLE CLASS. Gives B's and C's even though you meet the assignment criteria. You only get an A if your work is beyond exceptional. Ridiculous. RUN
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: She seems lost and says "um" a lot. It is very distracting and makes it very hard to listen. Also, assignments that I thought were easy and I thought I would get a good grade on, I did not. Exams are more writing heavy than multiple choice. There are no study guides at all so you are expected to know material that she struggles to teach anyway.

Dr. Cavigelli seems lost the majority of the time. She takes weeks to grade assignments, and she has a bit of an attitude, which made me not feel comfortable when asking questions in class. Overall, if you end up taking BBH-432, take it with someone else.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cavgelli is really nice and understanding, but she seems lost half of the time. She reads off the slide decks and skips multiple slides, saying we will come back to them, but never do. Exams are very specific, but if you study the slide decks, you will be fine.  Passionate about what she talks about, but doesn't ever finish her thoughts
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Good lecturer with solid slides, if you study the slides the tests aren't all that hard, lots of time to work on final project throughout, NOT very much homework

Not only are the tests extremely detailed so it is nearly impossible to get an A, but she literally just reads off of the powerpoints during lecture and doesn't actually teach you. Avoid her, her horrible teaching, and even worse grading system where you get no explanations as to what you did wrong AT ALL COSTS!!!!!!

I really enjoyed bbh 432. Not a lot of busy work or hw. She will usually send an email about what to expect on the exams. Exams are usually multiple choice and open ended. Group project worked on throughout the year. Lectures/PP contain everything you can expect to see on exam. Exams are usually straightforward.

AVOID AT ALL COSTS. Exams are open-ended (aka impossible). Doesn't care about your grade and doesn't give explanation/rubric of where grades are coming from. Final project is a group project where everyone gets the same grade so hopefully your group actually does their work or you're screwed.
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Group projects--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Dr. Cavigelli was an okay professor. She reads right from the slides, which aren't complete thoughts. She seems lost half the time when she's lecturing. There are 4 exams and a final group project. The exams were multiple choice and open ended, which kind of sucked because there's no reason all of the questions couldn't be multiple choice.

The class is based on writing your own research model and paper. I liked that and found Personality and Health interesting but sometimes the amount of writing (weekly) was hard to keep up with. The exams are easy to do well on though if you pay attention in class. She sometimes was a little disorganized but it also was her first time teaching it.

Sonia is a nice lady, however her exams consist of questions with many individual, detailed questions that need to be answer. The class is only 50 min long so it's difficult to answer all of the questions in that amount of time. On top of that, there are many writing assignments and readings for in class discussion. Overall, it's manageable.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Tests aren't too hard. Go to class and review the notes before the exam and you are golden. Textbook/readings is a waste of time and money. Pretty nice, a little boring. But easy A or B.

this class was a complete waste of time. she "teaches" in a very lackadaisical manner, nothing seems to relate to each other. we never knew what the hell to study for the tests, everything was ****ted and you'd get an A. she'd promise us study guides & then never delivered. she's a very nice person, just don't expect to learn anything.

Sonia was very contradictive of herself! She would say one thing   a slide then say the opposite on the next. Her tests are confusing and poorly written. She gives a lot of extra credit and there are other projects for a grade. You need the book for clarification because most of the time she doesn't know what she's talking about! She's very helpful

pretty easy class... i disagree on not needing the book, but i'm someone who needs that kind of backup.  it seemed like she didn't know about anything past the surface level.  any in-depth questions were rarely answered.  but whatever, easy enough.
No Comments
Very easy class. Tests ARE short answer/essay/multiple choice...and are very easy.  Make sure you take notes and the book is not necessary.
Very smart, great professor. Exams are very fair and his classes teach you so so much. This is the guy you want for your Markets class, Mehmet is the man!
Great professor.
Professor Canayaz is an absolutely amazing and sharp teacher. He cares about his students and really wants everyone to do well. He makes the class intuitive and helpful. Best FIN408 professor by far.

Professor Mehmet Canayaz is a very smart and intelligent professional. He cares about his students and is able to communicate fairly complex topics into terms anyone could understand. His class was structured around what the students needed/wanted and he had a welcoming and inclusive environment in his classroom.
If you work hard, you will succeed
Very rude. Dont bother coming to him for help, as you will be greated with hostility.

He is not helpful as a course coordinator in Stat200
His labs do not align with professor haubricks lectures and it's odd

This person either lacks an understanding of statistics or is out of touch with what students genuinely need. His primary focus seems to be enforcing tedious and excessive rules that hold little practical value instead of fostering a meaningful learning experience. Much time is spent on tasks unrelated to learning statistics. Avoid it at all cost!
Very mean in email, I have never had a teacher/professor be so rude and condescending to me. Has 0 respect for you at all. Deserves 0 respect.

If you have to take SC220, take it with him!! The STAT200 reviews drown out the amazing sc220 reviews. His approach to teaching SC220 is completely different than STAT200, so it's super easy. He's an amazing professor for that class as long as you show up and interact in class. He actually cares about his students!!

VERY rude when I emailed him asking a question basically said I'm too lazy to figure this out so good luck. He sends very condescending emails out accusing people of cheating when nobody cheats. BIGGEST EGO EVER. FIRE THIS GUY!

He is the worst Coordinator in PSU. He should be fired for not doing his job and degrading students. He only focuses on the documentation and doctor's notes even when It's not necessarily needed. Don't try to reason with him because it's not worth it. He will continuously repeat that he can't help students because he doesn't care.

Professor Shelton was the only reason I passed this course. He is extremely kind and has a sarcastic sense of humor. Anytime I needed assistance with the course material he was very helpful and provided a detailed step by step of how to solve the problem. If you take STAT 200, use Prof Shelton's help to your advantage. Do the assignments and study.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: The professor has helpful intentions and tries to help as much as possible. I was confused on a question during the final exam and he still tried to help as much as he could even though he was limited. The class overall isn't too bad, just attend and pay attention in lectures, ask questions, and do the necessary homework and you'll pass this class.

Super cool professor. Classes were just discussions of the weekly quizzes, and they were always pretty interesting. Never added any stress to my workload because the assignments were straightforward. I would definitely recommend if you need to take SC 220 to become an LA.
Very snobby in responses to emails.  Would frequently accuse students of lying.  Tests do not align with lectures.
Elementary class, with horrible tests. The wording is highly confusing.

never met a more ego-motivated prof at PSU. Beware of taking STAT 200 if you can bc he is the course lead & if you have any difficulties academically he does not give af about helping. Any convo you have w him he will belittle you even tho he doesn't even have his PhD & you will get nowhere when trying to work w him unsure how he isn't fired yet

The most difficult staff member I've ever dealt with at PSU. Not sure how he keeps a job. Lays off students' concerns, degrades students when they ask for help, is very negative. On top of this, he randomly accuses students of cheating on exams. This guy does not communicate well, and he deflects any/every issue students bring up. Should be fired!

Professor Shelton is a horrible professor. He degrades you and treats you like you're stupid if you email him for help. He's very unprofessional and if you have any choice do not take this class with him.

He accused me of sending my answers on an exam and I would get a 0. He said, "I don't mean to sound arrogant, but I've never been wrong about one of these." He saw me break down when he said something because I didnt do it. 12 hours later he sends email saying hes not going through with AI, with NO APOLOGY. He kept me on zoom for 30 mins, sobbing.

this man is the most unprofessional, hypocritical, condescending, and outright rude person i have ever encountered at PSU. in one of the recent email sent to the class, he decided to include a link to the eberly code of mutual respect and cooperation. i wonder if he realizes that code includes faculty since hes extremely good at breaking it!

He is the rudest and most unprofessional person I have encountered at PSU. He sends the most condescending and ridiculous emails to the class. He is completely unhelpful whenever there is a technology problem in a heavily technologically based class. The other staff in stat 200 were working hard to make the class better but his leadership was awful
Literally useless, rude, terrible professor.
If you need to take sc220 to become an LA I recommend him! Great class, easy, interesting.
absolutely horrible professor and disrespectful person all around. is rude to students and does not help you at all. avoid him at all costs
He is absolutely the worst teacher I have ever met. Terrible. Try your best to avoid him.
the absolute worst professor. no further comment needed.

(APLNG 491)
Professor Kinginger is very nice and caring, she's very knowledgeable about her field and willing to share and incite discussion. However, not great at updating Canvas with assignment information.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Gives good feedback--Respected

reviews.comment: If you have the opportunity to take a course with Celeste, I highly recommend it! She's kind, understanding, and very approachable. I really appreciated how she included group discussions for our projects and proposals. She always provided helpful feedback on our assignments, and her grading criteria is clear. It's hard to do poorly in her class!

This class is truly you get out of it what you put in. If you pay attention and participate in discussion, it is very interesting and worthwhile. You can give your all or the bare minimum. As long as you go your assignments, you will get a good grade. No quizzes or exams and a short final project.

this was my freshman seminar class. It was so so easy and it was just busy work. I enjoyed going to class but I really think that we did a lot of unnecessary papers and projects. She didn't really know what she was doing because it was her first seminar but I like her as a person and I liked the people in my class. It was an interesting experience.

Fun class. Learned a lot. Papers were a big shift, but not too bad. She's really nice and funny. On the first day, she did this group thing with us that just really pulled you into the class instantly. Very very helpful and cares a lot about everyone in the class. Mentions French a lot for things, but that's to be expected.
No Comments

She is one of the best teachers I have had a Penn State.  She is very knowledgeable and genuinely cares for each of her students.  She wants her students to have a better understanding of different tenses,etc.Be prepared to do work because you have to write 4 papers and do a final presentation, along with quizzes,hw. Celeste is the best!

worst french teacher I've ever had.  I can't stand the way she speaks and she treats us like we are completely ignorant.  I am not learning a thing and her class is making me hate the language in general, which is sad.
Hard to follow sometimes.  Didn't really learn much in class.

Multiple times I had emailed him about why I was getting points taken off and he never responded. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Unhelpful and condescending when asked questions. 

Most of the instructions given for group work is not clear at all, groups are required to have too many members, and final submissions are split in a way that makes no sense to fit the large group. You'll need to read everything carefully or you'll lose a lot of points. Does give a lot of feedback

The worst. Completely failed an assignment because of a short word count on a discussion reply. Your grade is 100% homework and he likes to knock of a couple of points from each criteria on the rubric. The only feedback I got was about word count and APA format (which I never studied and he never showed us). Avoid at all costs.

If you are taking this class online, don't. You learn nothing about business and all you do are business briefs that teach you nothing. He is one of the most unhelpful and least caring professors I have had. He does not care at all about anything but a due date. Awful professor. Do better as an educator

Beware of MBA Bernie Cesaraso. Nothing more than an east coast elitist that does not promote adequate core values to his students. He has the unhealthy of putting you down and also chooses to mistreat you.
Hard grader. Makes simple things more difficult. Trick questions on timed quizzes/tests. Avoid at all costs if you care about your GPA
Absolutley dreadful professor. Does not care about the students simply teaches to show authority over other people. Disgusting.
Carl Cotner embodies the kind of man I strive to be.
the goat. chill and talks about conspiracy theories. participate in class and you will like it.

The class material is somewhat boring and dated, so he does his best with it. Attendance is effectively mandatory because there's a graded assignment every lecture. Exams and quizzes are simple and he grades them generously. Honestly, the class itself just needs a rework.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Beware of pop quizzes--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Class isn't very difficult, but he's not a great teacher. Hard to access outside of class and lecture is filled with rambles. Assignments aren't hard (usually in groups), quizzes and exams have study guides. The slides on Canvas aren't helpful, so show up to class. Not a bad guy, but only good communication before and after class time.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Cotner is a great teacher. He's available by email and has 3 weekly office hours. The class, however, has an immense amount of info.

Cotner is a great professor. For 230 there is a textbook reading and related practice problems due each week which is very manageable. There are attendance worksheets graded for participation but he will let you make them up if you're out sick. He is very accommodating, and lenient with late work. I would definitely recommend taking him for IST 230

The class content was fine, but the exams were very challenging. The tests felt much harder than what we practiced, and the study guide didn't always match the exam style. Last spring he let them take exams online. Midterm average was 70. He said there would be questions he doesnt expect us to get. He made the final so much harder than it had to.

His lectures are boring and may wander off into unrelated topics that may be related but not needed to the particular class. Attendance is required and is graded randomly through submission of some worksheet that's small and not hard. Overall chill guy and a easy grader but his lectures are boring and get off subject.
I've taken both DS220 and DS300 with Professor Cotner, both have been great classes. Lectures are fairly interactive, and you get plenty of time in class to work on assignmnets. Nice guy aswell
Nice guy, class is very easy and relaxed. Could see him being tough in other courses, but for DS300 it's free if you just show up to class.
Professor Cotner's class was very laid back and easy. Only issue was assignments took forever to be graded.

Goes off on random tangets, knows what he is talking about but literally cannot teach one thing - I was not alone. Really needs to learn how to present and talk in a fashion that allows students to actually understand the words coming out of is mouth. He would just wing every class and kind of make up the daily material as he went about the lecture

Professor Cotner is an awesome professor! He is very caring and the assignments are very straightforward. He is willing to give student second chances on assignments for a better grade which is rare in the Graduate world. I enjoyed his class a lot and wish he taught my core courses.
Should have make this class optional, barely learn anything from the class and Carl has no idea what he is doing.

Professor Cotner goes off on a lot of tangents during lectures. He heavily relies on TAs and LAs for grading and any assignments, it would be best to ask them questions rather than him. Most assignments you can work in a group, the assignments were easy and I did learn from them but he is not helpful and it is barely talked about in class.

Easy class. However if you arent familiar with the database side of things, you'll need some help. The class is really a do it yourself class. The lectures are really just conversations about tangents related to the material. Theres a final project that's pretty easy. Quizzes and Exams are open-note and online.

Dr. Cotner is an amazing guy, his lectures were slow sometimes, but some of the topics were genuinely interesting to learn about. He is very passionate about data privacy and the importance of it. There was four group exercises that requires writing for assignments, he lets everyone make up any assignments and quizzes at the very end.

Professor is smart and cares, but it just doesn't work. The lectures have little to do with what you will be quizzed on and often end up going off on completely unrelated tangents. There is nearly ZERO communication on Canvas in every aspect you can think of (maybe 10-20 posts the entire semester, over half from TAs). Expect to teach yourself.

I didn't learn much. He does not follow his slide presentations and his lectures are hard to follow. He relies on videos in order to teach content. I could tell that he either created the assignments years ago or someone else created them because he struggles to answer clarifying questions. He relies on TA for everything. :(

This professor was incredibly unstructured and disorganized. He seemed to remember the lectures by reading the slides and then go off on random, confusing tangents.There were no due dates for any assignment or in-class quizzes, so you have to properly time manage yourself.There are probably around 300 questions to submit by the end of the semester.

Terrible professor, but nice guy. Did not teach anything all semester but would quiz and test you on them. There was no possible way to prepare for some of his quizzes and the class averages were super low.

Bruh, what? He has no clue what he is doing. On exams you could have the right answer, but it is not the answer he was looking for. He had wrong answers on the exam and so many people complained. The multiple choice questions were random data science questions that he wants you to google and answers are debatable. He had to give points back a lot.

This class is a joke. Students like him because he is an easy A. If you give effort, you're pretty much guaranteed above a B and in my case, I have always had As in his classes. It's not hard. We had a take home exam which was easy. He talks about covid-VERY PASSIONATE- and everything other then the class. If you want to learn anything, don't take.

I honestly don't even know where to begin. Saying he talks about nonsense the entire time doesn't do justice for what he is actually like. I did not learn anything, but you are almost guaranteed to get above a B as long as you put in some effort, so if you have a busy course load it's worth taking.

The ratings are harsh, he is the BEST professor I had at PSU. He is inspirational and talks about stuff in the real world, problems that are important for any student like Facebook and covid. I enjoyed taking this course. I wasn't BORED at all
He talks about everything, except Data Science. He hates Facebook. Gives grades easily.

He's a walking tangent. You never know what he'll rant about in class, in my experience: battleships, vaccines, human evolution, or the pitfalls of Aristotle's philosophy. He's liable to talk about practically anything other than Data Science concepts until the last 25 when he starts teaching. Labs, the main grade, are easy and often done in class.

The class was an absolute mess up until the last day. There was no constant syllabus or literally anything like that. Granted this was his first time teaching the course and he obviously did not have a lot to work with, so I do not totally blame Professor Cotner. Just for this specific course it was not ideal.

I liked professor Cotner as a person. As a teacher, it was a bit rough. He did not have a clear schedule on Canvas until the last minute. The tests would have been easier to take if the lectures were more structured. He does do a lot of last-minute grading. However it is an easy A if you show up to class and pay attention.

Do not do this. He was the most confusing professor I have ever taken. The Zybooks textbook taught me everything, and anything that wasn't included in the textbook was unintelligible. Coursework was so unorganized and negligent that he forced the class to take a final worth 35% of our grade because he didn't assign quizzes during the semester.

reviews.comment: Does not teach. Makes fun of covid and doesn't know a thing. I could have taught this class better (And I don't know anything about the topic. I still don't). Thanks for nothing Cotner. Avoid at all costs.
DO NOT TAKE

I want my tuition back.
Bruh. Just no. He does not teach and has to raise everyone's grade because everyone is failing. Have not learned a thing.

HORRIBLE. Where should I start?

Avoid, avoid, avoid.

He does leave everything to the last minute and if you work hard and get assignments done very carefully you can get a good grade as he boosts your grade. I wish he didn't leave everything to the last minute and still be a chill guy. He is a smart guy and helps you get a good grade if you argue with TA's but he should be more organized.

Try to avoid him if you want a professor who doesn't manipulate his students. He delays every assignment to the last week and has no understanding of this material. If you have no choice but to take him just be aware and never trust his words. The course is graded by TAs, Carl is just there to sit in his chair and check if the FBI is tracking him.

Save yourself and take this course with any other professor.  Lecture and textbook rarely match up.  He is extremely smart and knows what he is talking about but does not know how to properly convey what he is trying to teach.

Get ready to do stuff by your own. This is the first professor Ive seen that DOESNT TEACH! He makes fun of covid and doesnt believe that its real and yeah he would blame companies like Facebook every class because they track him. He is a JOKE shame on you PSU for letting this guy to teach.
I'm letting you know now don't do this. wait and take someone else

reviews.comment: Carl was clearly unprepared to teach this class and his lectures were all over the place. I didn't learn much but he did everything in his power to help the class get a good grade. He was super lenient and caring and I can't blame him for being unprepared because apparently the guy who was supposed to teach the course passed away over the summer.

I took DS200 with him. He is crazy. He spends most of the class period on political tangents about COVID that make everyone uncomfortable. 80% of the time has no idea what the material is and teaches it to himself while he tries to teach it to us. However, he does want everyone to pass so is very generous with curves and a lenient grader.

He had a surprise final that he told us about a few days before we took it and sent out the wrong review sheet. He then proceeded to send the right review sheet at 11:30 the night before the final. The TA's also do not know the information so they do not help you study. Lots of labs but tests are very hard and does not give any preparation time.
Nice professor

Nice guy, horrible Professor. He gets easily distracted and gets confused easily. He assigns quizzes randomly. Often can not answer his own questions and will forget what he asked. Easy class, but do not expect to learn ANYTHING. I will avoid him for future DS classes.

Had no clue what he was doing. And he is easily distracted. We played hangman a week before the midterm. That same class he says, Oh by the way, you have a quiz in two days and your midterm is next week. I didnt learn a thing in this class and very few people actually paid attention. Im sure he is a great math prof, but avoid for IST courses.
gave a pretty fair grade, and most of his content actually help me understand how things worked instead of getting lam-blasted with papers, mostly hands on material! 10/10 would recommend.
He's great, I would take him again

Great guy and great professor. Super helpful when you really need him and very funny. Most people giving bad ratings probably did very little to help themselves which is, you know, necessary in college.

Carl is a goof. He's a nice guy and means well, but he's not very good at explaining things and likes to digress on every explanation to stories about his kids or something. Assigns homework blindly that can occasionally take many hours to do. Tells us to look at other teachers online notes, which explain the course a lot better than he does.

Really nice guy. Terrible teacher. Spends a lot of his time telling us stories about his kids and asking us if we want to leave 20 minutes early. What he teaches, what is on the homework, and what is on the exams are on are 3 completely different things. He usually can't even answer questions asked of us on the quiz or homework.
MyMathLab sucks. End of story.
Carl is very good at explaining math and can answer any question you may have. His stories are hilarious as well.

The guy is cool, but he doesn't do much in class, leaving you to teach it to yourself basically.  He goes on tangents in class all the time and wastes half of it.  Very boring otherwise as well.  Homework is incredibly tedious and all online, which is set up by the course administrator.  because of that, he doesn't even know what problems there are
Homework was the most time consuming thing I've ever done and it didn't prepare you at all for the exam

Love the guy, but horrible teacher. I took calc my senior year and i still failed this class. he is such a sweet guy but so scattered brained and makes no sense. bring your old calc notes and study those. go to lion tutors.
Hilarious

The easiest class I had all semester. No notes, no test even. Just some small projects that involve technology. He talks about some hilarious and crazy stuff thats all interesting, but you may need a cup o coffee if ur tired u may find urself with ur eyes closed.

This class is pretty funny, Carl just speaks about random things and theres no tests or quizzes you don't even have to take notes. goods old Carl. He is a great guy. Great teachaer and he is hilarious. He wears shirts that somebody found in a cerial box. It's hilarious.

good teacher, native english speaker, funny, helpful, actualy wants to be there.

Professor Cesar is good and tries his best to help students navigate through the annoying class format. He is good at clarifying and does explain things in office hours. The course just sucks.

Just make sure to participate a lot(if you get it wrong he doesn't make you feel dumb) but there's a lot of opportunities to participate. MyLabs are annoying but that's for every Spanish class
