Math 140. She says that in her other sections, no one asks questions. That is not a good sign! Judging by the low exam average, it isn't because everyone knows that material. Try to find a professor who collects homework and gives a lot of quizzes, so  you have more opportunities to boost your grade.
She is a very good math teacher. She has an accent, but it is easy to get used to. She explains calculus by doing tons of examples, which I found helpful. I would recommend her.
Dr. Chopra is not a good teacher. The class is extremely boring and monotonous. No enthusiasm. Unwilling to give extra help if you don't understand. Avoid at all costs!
I had Neena for 2 semesters of Math.  She was great!!  She knows exactly what she is talking about and can back up where she is getting it from.  I highly recommend her!!
Great teacher.  She does not complicate anything and knows what to stress on for the tests.  HW is not due but quizes once a week.  They are not simple but really help for test.
She could be a little more thorough, but she is so nice that it doesnt matter.
I could not understand her at all.  I took calc in HS and she taught in a totally different way.  There was no help from her, everything I learned I either knew or did on my own.
Lessons are easy. So are her quizzes. Be prepared for a huge difference in exams and quizzes though.
It's math, if you get it it really doesn't matter who you have.  She knows what she's doing and is good at teaching it.  You can afford to miss a few classes a week as well.

Her english is actually quite good, and doesn't get in the way with her teaching at all. Slight accent; but really, I never had any problem understanding her at all. She has a fabulous teaching method; very clear. Weekly quizzes and drops the lowest 2 instead of hw like some other profs (but be sure to do the hw anyway if you want to do well.)
Very good teacher.  Soft voice and an accent, but you get used to it.  No problem with her quizzes or homework.

She may be a liitle difficult to understand, but you can understand after listening for a while. She is a really sweet woman, and after seeing some of the other professors in the math department with their barely able to comprehend accents, I'm thankful I got her.

Horrible teacher. doesnt speak English very well. doesnt teach either, terrible at explaining the material. dont take any of her classes you will be bored out of your mind and you'll have to teach the material to yourself. hated every minute of it

She's an amazing teacher...best teacher I have had so far.  She explains everything clearly, gives credit for homework and prepares you for exams very well.  She is always willing to help and always has a smile on her face.  If you have to take a math course, I suggest getting her as a prof.

This is one of the nicest profs I ever met.  She's always smiling and bringing cheer to the classroom.  While not the best English speaker grammatically, she talks slowly enough so that you can understand her.  She will never get angry at you, and she gives a ton of help.  Super prof in my book.
I had a good time in her class.  She was nice and really wanted us to do well.  Sitting in the front of the room is definately a good idea.

horrible, its a good thing i took calc in high school with a good teacher.  When i did go to her class,she made so many mistakes, ever fixed them,explained things wrong,and i spent more time correcting her,which is why i never went to class.still got an A.if you see her name look for another teacher
Never taking calculus before, i got a B in her class.  sit up front so you can hear her, and pay attention.  not the greatest explainer, but she will try her best at all times.  i recommend her.

Neena's a good person.  She doesn't always do the best job explaining everything, but she wants you to do well and will help you if you ask her the questions.  I was happy with her as a teacher because she is understanding and normally pretty interesting.

Neena Chopra cannot speak English.  She sucks at teaching, really.  Not helpful whatsoever.  Why can't we ever get an English speaking Math teacher at this campus?  She's not hot either.  Wait til you get to 141 and the teacher tells you that you should've already learned half this stuff in MATH 140
a very fun class.  she is cool about joking around, and often lets you out of class early.  she really cares about her students getting good grades, and will do a lot to help you succeed.

A decent prof, she really knows her stuff. Defines most concepts clearly. But definately sit in the front of the room, you will learn so much more since she is very soft spoken. Really wants her students to do well.
she sucks the big one. shrugs it off every time she forgets to cover certain material for upcoming tests. if you have this class on your roster, suicide is the only option.

She's a good teacher as long as you show up and keep up with the homework. College calculus is not for everyone, as you can see from the other ratings. She teaches best by example. If you need extra help, she's more than willing to spend time with you.

She's really nice and she's a great math tutor. She's inexpensive and she's really cool. She's saved my ass this semester. She's really smart and has like 3 or 4 math degrees. I do hear that she's not the best teacher tho.
Writes vague phrases and random examples on the board, does no actual teaching to students.  It's amazing that this woman is a Penn State professor.
even though she was quiet, she really knows her stuff and gave great examples.  She also was very helpful with the things you should know for the exams, and gave good instruction on new material.

She was very quiet. If you sit in the back of the class you wont hear a word. She knows calculus, but she doesn't know how to convey that knowledge to her students. She seems like a nice lady but it is easier not paying attention then to struggle to hear.

I have never had more trouble in math before. She was too quiet, but it didn't matter, because even if I could understand her, her teaching skills are somewhat lacking. Thank you to the University Learning Center tutors who taught me calculus.
This class is a 6 credit course so hardly anyone drops it, but this lady is truely retarded.  Cant understand her, my prior knowledge is the only thing that let me pass this class

She was soft spoken, did not give clear examples, and made it hard for students without a very good understanding of math. However she did grade very easy, but you essentially had to know everything prior to taking the class.
No Comments
She was not only a terrible teacher who hardly ever answered our questions but she is very unhelpful even for after class tutoring.

Will not respond to emails, homeworks are unnecessarily long, labs are not clear or concise, and overall just really hard to follow through. I feel like I was going to second hand resources 95% of the time to get the knowledge to pass this class. 4 midterms, 2 unnecessary oral exams, and nitpicky on feedback. One of the worst courses at Penn State.
The GOAT of the 211-214 series of physics.

I dislike physics, and this course reaffirmed that. There's a lot of weekly work—labs, quizzes, and readings. 4 multiple-choice midterms with no study guides, requiring you to review all material given. You have to teach yourself from the textbook and slides, with no lecture recordings. TAs grade everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Listen, as a class it kinda sucked cause there was only one section at 8AM, some homeworks had 20+ questions with h or k parts, but it was good practice. As a prof, I think Chad is as good as you can get. If you have a choice, choose him. His lectures were clear. The man never attended his office hours tho, he canceled them almost every week.

Decent professor. Use the OpenStax textbook for Expert TA homework problems. 4 midterms, test heavy. Lectures are just to reinforce your understanding of the topic, don't go in expecting to learn something completely new. Make sure you already know your stuff before lectures, so you can get extra credit from the TopHats.

Dr. Hanna was a nice person and he was always available after class to answer questions. The exam questions were slightly modified lecture, lab, recitation, and homework questions, so if you studied those things you would know what to expect for exams. The exams never seemed too difficult. Top Hat gives extra credit, so go to lecture.

I think Chad Hanna is a great lecturer. His lectures were very clear and easy to understand. However, I think the lack of lecture time (only two 50 minute classes a week) makes the class harder because much of the math elements must be figured out by doing the homework.

Worst professor at PSU literally skipped half of the semester not going to class. Study on my own 2 day before the exam and then pass the class. He is so useless that Penn State should demote him and make his salary lower cause he is so bad at teaching all he does is use a laser to point and talk about how nice he is yea how nice he us.
This was sadly my second time taking phys 212 but Dr. Hanna made it awesome. His lectures are easy to understand and if you put in the work you'll get a fine grade. Go to EVERY lecture.
He did not provide any exam practice and did not give students example to solve physics question. You can't learn anything by him. You only can do is learn by yourself.

Tophat is 3% extra credit. Interesting lectures but in my opinion exams seemed a bit rough although there was enough time given to complete all questions. Labs and recitations aren't too bad overall. Due to winter weather the admin announced that if we don't take the final exam the score will equal the midterm average. Barely passed the class

The lectures weren't super helpful for me personally. I learned more by reading the book and taking my own notes. The homework is very difficult and time consuming for the most part, but the exams weren't really that bad. Recitations and labs are easy points so make sure to go to them and put in the work.

Weekly HW is very complex and the easier questions are what appears on midterms. Lectures are deeply conceptual and impossible to follow along for me. Dr. Hanna knows what he's talking about but just explains in a very intellectual way that isn't for everyone. There is no practice exams or review sessions. You learn from doing HW, not lectures.

Very difficult class but relatively easy to get a good grade for how hard it is. Didn't learn anything at lectures, only went for the top hat extra credit. Learned everything through recitations/labs/looking through slides in my own time

Chad is a fantastic professor who is amazing at teaching. He knows how to keep a lecture interesting and understands his students really well. He is a funny professor. There are tophats in the lectures but they're just for extra credit. If you have to take PHYS212 I would recommend you pick Chad.

Chad Hanna is a great professor for 212. Physics is naturally going to be a bit of a challenge, but Chad makes it seem more manageable. Tophat is max 3% extra credit, so make sure to attend lectures. Exams use the same types of questions from homework and recitations.

Chad is a great professor. His lectures are entertaining and if you pay attention this course is honestly easy. There are tophats in the lectures but they're just for extra credit. If you have to take PHYS212 I would recommend you pick Chad

homeworks are really hard but only once a week. tests are weighted in a way that's way more favorable than 211. it's not that he was that great but the other choice was keim and i almost failed his 211 class. do the practice tests!! going to class isnt that helpful but that's the only way to get extra credit

Not a difficult class, most exams are curved, the final was difficult with the multitude of information but if you can understand all the last set of information you will do well. There is extra credit, and most of the mastering physics problems you can find online to help you understand the material and relate it to the equation sheet.

Lectures are useless. Seems like Chad doesnt care. Probably just at Penn State for research. Exams are horrible, no partial credit. This is the hardest class that Ive taken so far at Penn State and Chad Hanna didnt help at all. Physics is a mess at Penn State. The ultimate weed out course. Just managed to pass the class.

Top hat questions are extra credit, so do the lecture readings. Lectures don't help any more than just reading the book and doing the homework-- so go for the extra credit and specific equations. Labs aren't that bad. Recitations get horrible after exam 2. If you put in the work with homework and practice problems before exams, you should be fine.

Lectures are just not structured and he has a tendency to ramble. Its not really his fault because their isnt nearly enough lecture time to cover the complicated material. Your not going to see a big difference with any other teacher for 212 and hes at least a nice guy.

The honest answer is that Chad is literally too smart for me. He's extremely knowledgeable about the subject, but couldn't explain it simply enough for me to understand. I ended up stopping going to the lectures because they didn't help me. I ended up doing okay because the labs and recitations saved my grade. Really great guy though.

Man gives it his all, but somewhere down the line things fall apart. Lectures are fine, but the whole thing comes off as detached. Exams are worth a lot and can go South quickly. If you're gonna take him pray you get a good LA/TA because all it takes is a bad one to make things exponentially more difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: PHYS 212 is a very hard course by nature. Professor Hanna's lectures are detailed, and incredibly calculation heavy. You will need to spend a lot of time reading the book, reviewing lectures, and practicing problems to succeed. It is easy to get lost in the course, but there are ample resources to help you understand the material.
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Doesn't matter what professor you get. You only see them twice a week for 50 minutes each. Just like 211, they just read a list of formulas off of slides for the entire lecture and hope you absorb some of it. Lab and recitation are always poorly-made assignments and annoying to go to. Mostly the fault of the abysmal course coordinator.

A nice guy, but like others have mentioned, whatever professor you have for 212 doesn't really matter. Lectures were boring/unhelpful, and instead found reading/taking notes on the textbook & reviewing those notes and doing Mastering homework to be sufficient for exams (they changed exams to be basically Mastering questions with diff. numbers).

Dr. Hanna has a bad reputation on this website. Personally I think his lectures were engaging and informative. Physics 212 at its core is an unforgiving class so the class will not be "easy", but Dr. Hanna is very approachable should you have questions. I would take him as a professor again.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chad is a solid Physics teacher. Could be better and could be worse, but if you go to lecture and study the way he tells you to study, you will be fine. Also, don't be ashamed of rolling out of bed and heading straight to Osmond 119. Chad does the same

Uses clickers (massive class for 212 in fall). attendance isn't technically mandatory. He cracks some jokes in lecture, and overall isn't a bad teacher. Usually knows what trips students up, and will explain in detail. Great professor, and I highly recommend. This course also has a lab and recitation, which are easy 100s.

Chad Hanna is THE man to take for physics 212. He's actually a really funny and intelligent guy, and his LIGO research is extremely interesting. He made physics 212 easy and always prepared us for exams. With that being said, the class is still definitely a lot of work.

Overall, good. Although little content in lecture, he explain things well if you ask, and exam questions all comes from homework and lecture slide, meaning you can get an A as long as you attend class and do homework, figuring out the 'WHY'. You'll get good GPA by taking his course.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: PHYS212 was really weird this semester, so take this with a grain of salt. Hanna doesn't explain concepts very well and whispers in a classroom of 200 students. But somehow the exams were stupid easy because they were word for word from mastering physics. Hard to judge. I can't see this course being this simple in future semesters, beware.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Chad is the man. He is very knowledgeable and wants to help his students succeed. He also loves to tell knock-knock jokes.

The class was poorly ran but it was not his fault. Profoessor Hanna was knowledgeable and good at answering questions during lecture but the exams created by the department did not line up with his lectures well. Read the textbook and do the practice tests and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Tests and lectures are completely unrelated. Lecturepresentation��
DO NOT take physics 212 with this dodo looking of a man. He has the teaching abilities of a box turtle, this dodo's lectures and office hours are awful and all he does is complain about vectors.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: It honestly doesn't matter who you have for 212 because you have the same homework as everyone else, and you have access to both professor's lecture notes and office hours. READ THE BOOK. I only went to lectures for clicker pts. The tests are really hard, but they always curve so that the class average is a 70 (there was 11-pt curve on the final)
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Absolutely the worst professor from Penn State University by far. Spoke nothing of the material that would have been on the exam. I eventually had stopped going to lecture because I ended up getting more confused rather than learn something, along with most of the class. Our class had a 42% average on one of our exams.  Take someone else for ph212!
he was a bad teacher. I don't recommend

Very difficult class with Hanna, as he seems to believe everyone is a genius when it comes to physics and expects everyone to be extremely intelligent. Homeworks were incredibly long as he assigned the challenge problems at the end of each chapter on mastering physics and the exams were even worse. Avoid at all costs as this was a hard class.
If you can, do not take this class with Hanna.

Nice guy who really seems into what he's teaching. Not his fault that our second exam had a 40% average that resulted in a 30% curve as per the syllabus. Read the book before class and bring it with you to help with the reading quiz. Sometimes the questions aren't very fair to someone who doesn't have the book in front of them.

Well the course materials were hard so I didn't expect to enjoy the course so much. But this professor made it worse. He couldn't grab our attention at all. As the time pass, students began to stop coming to class. Do not take with this prof if you want to enjoy or major in Physics.

He saw the first exam was hard, made the second exam worse, and decided the best thing to do was to make a third exam which was harder than the first two. He thinks everyone is a physics/electrical engineering major, and doesn't understand that making the tests harder doesn't encourage more learning, it just makes the curve bigger. Worst class ever

She has a great personality, but my performance in this class was due to the learning I did outside of class. She derails often during the lecture which makes it confusing when you're trying to follow the content. Lastly, she accused me of using AI without proof & didn't ask for proof that I didn't use AI. This has never happened in any other class

Dr. Gulis is a very sweet person, but not a great professor. The class is very overwhelming, and the lectures are extremely repetitive after the first two-three chapters. She often accuses a lot of students of AI without any proof. You'll have to put a bit more effort than a regular class to do decent on the midterm, but offers extra credit.
Not a good professor. Got an A in the course and on the midterm and final, but I did not learn a single thing. Accuses every student of AI with zero evidence. Erratic and can be nonsensical at times.

I learned so much, and the support for the assignments was thoughtful and thorough. The lectures were fun and engaging, and the in-class hands-on activities really helped me learn with the professor's support. She was usually quick to respond to emails, and showed that she really wanted us to understand the material. I am so glad I took this class!

Probably the most caring professor I've had at Penn State. Always responsive via e-mail.

Class was fairly easy overall. Grading was very generous. If you show up to class and do the homework assignments you'll be in good shape. There was also the opportunity to get 10% extra credit by watching Interstellar and writing a short report on it.
BEST PROFESSOR EVER! She's very knowledgeable and I loved her enthusiasm and passion for the course!

THE MIDTERM IS NOT MULTIPLE CHOICE IGNORE WHEN SHE SAYS THAT. She's a very sweet lady and passionate about her field so I feel bad leaving this rating but do not take this for an easy A elective. Much harder than it needs to be. There are extra credit options, but the midterm is all open ended despite what she says in class.
One of the best Professors i have taken a class with.

Professor Cianci is amazing! She's super professional, kind, and always so stylish. Her lectures are clear and engaging, and she listens to every student's ideas. The class atmosphere is open and positive, and she makes even complex topics easy to understand. One of my favorite professors—100% recommend!

Professor Rebecca is by far one of the best professors in Penn State. She is understanding, very easy to get along with, charismatic, and down to earth. Her way of teaching is relaxed. I sort of struggle with social anxiety but since she is so welcoming I didn't feel nervous if I needed to ask a question.

Professor Cianci has a very immersive teaching style. She encourages participation and takes time to answer every query. She has a lot of patience and is a very calming yet exciting energy in class. I would love to take a class with her again! The work might seem extensive but just sit with for five minutes and you're good to go!

Professor Cianci was one of the best professors I've had. She not only is a professor, but an amazing source of help for advice and future career opportunities. I highly recommend going to class as she gives you insight for upcoming assignments. Papers are straight forward and the final group project you can pick your group!

Overall class had very little work, all you need to do is show up and fill out participation. Group project and paper worth 40% of grade but has clear outline and instructions. You get to pick your own group and a very easy grader. Only thing is not great at answering emails so you will need to speak to her in person.
Professor Cianci gave the class a wonderful experience with Case discussions and Guest speakers and was the most caring Professor I've ever had.

Rebecca is one of the best professors I've ever had. I've had her for two classes (LHR305 and LHR480) both of which I passed easily. She gives little to no homework, a few very easy 'papers' (max 750 words), and a group project for a 'final' (you can choose your group). Attendance is your grade, go to class and you will pass. Take her if possible!
Overall, it was a great class and professor! Do what is asked, and you should be more than fine! The materials and lectures were engaging, and she was a kind, knowledgeable person!
Great professor. Very easy to learn from and interesting class. Easy grader. Go to class and you will do fine.

Great in person professor. Makes lecture easy but be prepared to talk and engage as she will call on you. She is not the most accommodating and accessible outside of class, I needed accommodation and she ended up cutting communication with me and made success in this course very difficult as I was forced to navigate it solo. No class = No Pass.

I had her for 480 & 305 this semester and she is literally the sweetest and most easy going professor ive ever had. Her lectures arent boring or anything either the classes go by fast. Theres no homework or tests just do the participation and discussion questions its an easy a.

Professor Cianci is one of the best teachers I have ever had. Classes are based on weekly essay and attendance points. At the end of the semester there is a final group project and paper so the class has no exams in this class. Amazing teacher who genuinely cares and creates a dynamic of discussions in class so you aren't bored. Highly recommend!

Rebecca is great! Go to class bc there is a participation assignment every class. Mini papers throughout the semester and some discussion posts. She grades these really easily, and there are no tests. Show up to class you'll get an A no problem. She cancels class frequently. Final is a group project and pres but not bad at all! Take this class!

She cancels class all the time. So when it comes to writing the papers, it does get hard. There a three 7-page papers that you will have to write. Then there is a group project, and you only have a week and a half to do it. She is very nice and caring, so I do recommend her.
Easy class. Just do not skip a lot because attendance is 25%. Final group project is 40% of your grade, but she is not a tough grader, just follow the rubric.

I couldn't speak more highly of Prof Cianci. She is INCREDIBLE, as is this class. I loved it. I learned so so much about HR in the real world. It wasn't hard either. A few one-page essays and a discussion post here and there. The only big thing was the final project (40% of grade), but that was not bad at all as long as you actually try.

Amazing professor. She doesn't rely much on powerpoints but from her first hand experience in the field. Has daily participation attendance assignment but other projects are very easy and clear. You will get an A if you show up and do what is assigned. Group final presentation and no tests.

Rebecca is one of the best professors I've had. She gives great advice about the field of HR and is an all around joy to talk to. A lot of LHR professors don't have experience in the workforce but she provides great stories and relevant insight. 10/10 recommend

Awesome professor! You have a participation paper due after each class which can really help your grade and there is a few essays throughout the semester. She really cares about her students and is easy to talk to. Loved her!!

She is so nice and very laid back. I've been enjoying her class a lot and as long as you are paying attention you should be fine. The papers are not that bad, just make sure to follow the guidelines, read the text, and you'll be fine. It is discussion heavy but since it's about ethics and interesting.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Her lectures are really interesting, you won't be bored. Participation and attendance do matter but it's not hard to want to talk in class. She makes the class material fun. You do have quite a bit of work as far as online assignments but they are relatively easy to get done. She's awesome and has a good take on HR.
Very friendly professor, willing to help the students. Assignments are straightforward.
Great professor, all quizzes, h.w, and final exam online. Very concise and helpful videos on every lesson. Very helpful outside of class.

Professor Cimbala is absolutely awesome, his textbook is great as well as his YouTube channel which have all the material on it. Homework assignments are fair (sometimes easy and sometimes challenging), there are quizzes on almost every lecture (done online), and one final exam which it similar to the quizzes.

The class was fairly easy overall, with a few tougher topics that were manageable thanks to the lecture videos. Expect several quizzes each week plus homework. While the work is more tedious than difficult, the teaching style made the material easy to learn, and the professor's goofy, cringy humor kept it engaging.

Dr. Cimbala is easily one of my favorite professors that I've had at Penn State. He is accommodating and kind. 405 is so easy - all the lectures are posted online so you can work ahead, and the quizzes and HW are straightforward. He drops like the lowest 10 quizzes and 1 HW which makes it even easier. Final exam is just quiz questions. Easy!

Fun class. Definitely be prepared to write lots of matlab code or Excel, but it's not too hard.

I wish all professors were as organized and straightforward. If all educators were like Cimbala, higher education would be much more enjoyable.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: don't think just do the bes,t professor u will ever get

His course likely has the best structure of any class at PSU. Dr. Cimbala cares about his students, and it shows through his teaching. The youtube videos he posts are funny yet insightful, and his lectures help with making sure the concepts stick. Fluids isn't an easy subject, but this class was easy to score well in while still learning a ton.

he was AWESOME. So fair and such a sweet guy. Very week there are 4-6 quizzes in lectures and you get 4 tries on the and the average is the grade that goes in the grade book. My top advice is to put all your work into MATLAB because the final is online as EXACTLY like the quizzes. All there are no midterms which is awesome.
GOAT, what else can I say?

Fantastic professor. All of his lectures are online; he works example problems in class. But you can get through the course without them. Grades have a lot of cushion built in. Weekly lecture quizzes and HW all due the same night. Used to devote 1 night a week to crank them all out; stressful, but doable with a good study group.
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Too much work. Too many quizes and too many HW assignments that are way too lengthy.
1 of the best professors I've ever had, can really tell he cares student so much, and also puts lots of effort into teaching.

Dr. Cimbala is very knowledgeable and helpful in this class. The format of this class is well organized and rigid. The lectures are all posted online and there are no midterms. In lieu of this, short canvas quizzes make up the bulk of the grade, as well as homework. I would recommend taking him for ME 320.

Class is web with 4-5 lessons per week with a quiz for each lesson and 1 homework due every week, this format makes the subject easier.
The professor is very caring and has several office hours throughout the week.
Would definitely recommend

Class is setup very well to be able to get a solid grade and makes one of the hardest classes for ME majors easy. Everything is online with 4-6 lectures each week that are about 10 mins long. Each having a quiz. Quiz is 1 or 2 questions and you have 4 attempts and it averages out the score of the 4 attempts. Final exam was very easy.

I took ME405 indoor air quality this semester. The course was very straightforward and well organized. Because of COVID, the class was asynchronous which was great. 60% of the class was quizzes, one for each lecture. As long as you complete the assignments and put the work in, it is pretty easy to get an A. Cimbala is a 10/10 professor.

Professor Cimbala is a great teacher. I took his ME405 indoor air quality class and everything was very straightforward and methodical. 60% of the final grade was quizzes, which were due every MWF. These were 1 question each with a time limit of an hour, and were based off of the previous lecture. Not too difficult but a lot of gradual time put in

Professor Cimbala is an amazing teacher. He is caring and wants his students to succeed. Lectures are interesting, organized and easy to follow. Homework can be long and may take some time to complete but you can work in groups. Make sure you go over the HW solutions. Exams are fair, nothing out of the blue, you have seen it all in the lectures.

I took Air Pollution with Cimbala and he made what I originally thought was going to be a boring class into something interesting. Go to class, take notes, and go to office hours and youll have no problem doing well in this class. Also be sure to highlight what he tells you will be on the exams because I guarantee hes telling the truth.

I am a sophomore at PennState, so I have not gotten the chance to take many in-major classes yet. However, he has exceeded my expectations as an ME professor. His tests are fair, and he wants his students to succeed. I actually learned new, interesting stuff in this class and I would re-take if i could.

Cimbala taught a lot of higher level engineering classes when I took his ME433 Fundamentals of Air Pollution class. It was senior year, spring semester and all you wanted to do was barely show up while hungover half of the time. Expect a ton of hw and in class poll questions. The difficulty is a joke really but it was kind of a pain.

Fluids II is a hard class but this is definitely the guy you want teaching it. The lectures are well organized and easy to follow considering the topics are tough. You will learn a lot of practical knowledge in this class

Cimbala is one of the best in the ME department. His lectures and notes are very organized and easy to follow/understand. The homework can be pretty long and tough, but you get to work in groups and office hours can clear up anything you know how to do. Exams are cumulative, but if you review the lectures and homework beforehand you'll do well.
reviews.rating_tags: LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Great professor. Interesting class.

Dr. Cimbala is an all around great person. His lectures include many useful derivations left out of lower level fluids classes. He adds humor to the lectures and cares about every student in the class. The homeworks are a bit long sometimes but thoroughly teach you the material. Study everything starred in the notes, you will probably see it again!

Professor Cimbala is one of the great professors and his lectures are very interesting and help a lot to understand and do the homework. Show up and go to office hours and you will do fine. Also, exams are easy if you study the required materials and do your homework. Overall, great professor and interesting material.
Dr. Cimbala really has a gift for teaching. His explanations and analogies are very helpful. I have thoroughly enjoyed having him for a professor.

Dr.  John Cimbala is one of the best professors I have ever had. He has taught me more in the two semesters that I have had him than I thought possible. It took some work, but his teaching method and way of explaining things is really powerful at getting the point across.
Professor Cimbala is really good at teaching. Good lecture, always ready to answer your question inside and outside class. Homework help you learn a lot, while the exams are not tough.

He was a great professor and I enjoyed his class very much. Fluid Mechanics used to be a tough topic but he made it simple and clear. Lectures are easy to grasp, homeworks are fun to do. He asks candy questions too!

I had him for 345 and 320. His lectures are very thought out. The teaching structure is very great. He wants his students to do well. You will have no tests except for a final but you have to take quizzes in the pollock testing center every other week for all his classes. His notes and books help out a lot. He is a fair grader
He's a great. Extremely organized. Labs, quizzes, homeworks and everything are available to many students from previous semesters.
Best professor I've had at PSU so far.

This class is a lot of work, but anyone can get an A in it. Homeworks take a long time so make sure to work in a group. Cimbala's notes are awesome. He clearly lays out everything you need to know. Highly recommend this class because it's easy but you still learn a lot.
Great professor. His lectures are clear and his teaching style makes it easy to learn. You have to go to class because there's participation grades. Quizzes are straightforward if you study.

Genuinely the best professor I've had at Penn Stat. Cimbala is a good guy and his teaching style will actually help you learn the material easily and keep you interested. If you study the notes and the examples done in class, you will do well.

Cimbala is on of the best Professors at Penn State, he genuinely wants everyone to learn and do well. The pollock testing center isn't my favorite place but all the questions on the tests are things that he has said or gone over in class. I highly recommend Professor Cimbala and I wish I had the opportunity to take another one of his classes.

Pretty much agree with everything here. He is a great professor and genuinely appreciates student learning.  Homework  can be long so save things like the iterations on your computer.  The only bad thing was the tests in the pollock center which has sucky calculators.  Probably the best professor I had at Penn State.
Wish I was still ME to take more courses with cimbala. One of the best professors I have ever had.

One of the best professors I've had so far. Extremely knowledgeable and everything like notes and homeworks are already online. If you do the homework and review the most recent modules before the quizzes youll do fine. The quizzes are the most difficult part of the course if you dont study.
All around great professor. I still use his notes from 345 in higher level courses. I must say his lectures get quite dull and the quizzes can be tough but overall the course wasn't too bad.

Right up there as one of the best profs I've ever had. Explanations are super clear and he always provides relevance in real world applications. Reasonable work load and always provides an explanation wherever you lose points so you know where you went wrong.
Get a A in his class! The difficult part is quiz every two week in pollock  building. Forming a team to take quiz one by one is a good choice
One of the greatest professors I've had at penn state. He makes you interested intake topic at hand and I truly learned a lot.

Excellent professor. Homework and tests are straightforward from the notes. Professor Cimbala's notes are some of the best I have ever seen in college. I usually throw notes away, but I will be keeping his for a long time.

Kinda dull lectures, but going to class does help. Make sure you understand all the group homework and don't fall behind in the class and you should be fine. Cimbala knows his stuff and the class wasn't too hard, but make sure you study hard for the closed book tests!

Good guy. Makes a point to get to know you no personally. Best organized class I have ever taken, all notes, hw, labs are posted wayyy in advance. The class has a lot of material to cover.  The material itself is not hard there is just too much of it.

Simply the best professor in the ME department. I will take any class with him. Material is easy. The reason people complain homework is too much work is becasue they don't have a homework group. If you have a homework group to split the work, all you need to do is 1 or 2 problems per week.

Excellent professor. All material posted online, clearly outlined. Very systematic teaching process. Cimbala cares about the education of his students and is eager to answer student questions about relevant material. Very fair grader. Exams are predictable. I HIGHLY recommend doing all of the homework instead of breaking it up among group members.
Excellent teacher. You really will learn tons of interesting things in this course. Exams are rough, though.

Great professor!!! He really knows what he is talking about. All notes posted online as to easily review information and soak it in. You will learn a lot in this course and you will spend a great deal of time on homework but it's all worth it in the end. Would highly recommend Cimbala and would definitely take him again.

Cimbala is a typical role model professor. After going through his classes, you wonder how subjects can be taught easily. He can really make you understand fluid mechanics. Lecture notes posted online. They are very clear. Home works are lengthy yet do-able. My first preference professor and certainly one of the best prof at Penn State.

Clearly the best professor I have ever encountered in all my years as a student. His lectures are driven by his devotion to the word of the Lord, and in my book (as The Good Book) this puts him in the league of the Son of Man as a leader, a role model and guiding light, opposed to pseudo-scientific concepts like evolution, heliocentricity & choice.
Good teacher, gives some tough or time consuming assignments but you come away having learned the material well... unlike many other engineering professors.

Couple things to say here:  Cimbala really knows his stuff.  This makes him arrogant at times but, without a doubt, by the time you are done with this class, the material will be burned into your brain forever.  He constantly resurfaces old material and beats it into your head.  The exams aren't so great though, heavily weighted on the EE material.

Cimbala is a very fair professor. Weighs the homework heavily and gives you plenty of examples in class. Class is boring, but it's not his fault (the material just wasn't to my liking). Tests are all open notes and the notes are all online. Great teacher for ME 382.

Cimbala was a really good teacher for 382, given that it's a pretty boring subject. He gives you more than enough notes online to do just fine in the class without a great deal of effort (all the exams are open notes). He's a really good guy, really nice, and actually cares about his students and will go out of his way to help them.

Although tough, this guy makes everything relevant and weighs grades heavily on homework assignments. Do the work and you'll make it through and learn a lot. You can also miss classes because he posts his lectures online.
Very klowledgeable and helpful. Homework and tests are thorough. his lectures can be mundane tho.

Extremely Good professor take him if you can for this course.  He give a very practical view of very difficult subject.  I think his course lay out needs some improvement, but as an instructor he actually is very good at relating the material to real world applications.  Be prepared to work, but this is fluids, it is meant to be a hard course.
An extremely smart guy.  It's definitely a tough course and he didn't dumb it down at all.  Homework assignments are long but by the end of the course you'll know Fluids.
Wow was this guy boring. He grades hw, which is very time consuming and his exams are HARD, but if you're an engineer....you decided to put yourself through this.

5 for GER2, and I have to do it again for GER3. Great professor, but I dont like the tests in GER3 as much as I did in 2. Split into 2 days: 1 day is a conventional grammer/vocab/reading/listening. 2nd day is reading a prompt and responding with a written 8-10 sentence paragraph. I could go without that second day test, but minus that, great class.

Attendance is mandatory. Almost the entire lecture is spoken in German, which can be very confusing. She gives some extra credit opportunity which is nice. She is a really nice professor if you get to know her, just the exams and quizzes can be confusing.

Professor Civils clearly likes what she is doing, and is easy to understand. My only problem is that I haven't taken German for 2 years when I was put in this class. However, she made my reintroduction smooth, and now I only struggle when I forget to study. One problem is the class is mostly taught in German, but its not too difficult to understand

He does love his job and is so passionate about what he teaches, but the tests are literally so hard. I understand a lot of the concepts in class on a surface level and then you get to the test and it is all applying and having a lot deeper of an understanding of the material than he offers.

You can tell that he really loves his job and is interested in this stuff, but his exams are so incredibly hard. I'm not sure if he's just a bad online teacher, but this was horrible. Everyone I know from the class got an average of 50/100 on each exam. He usually curves them big time, which is the only thing that helped us pass.

Don't get the textbook. Everything you need is in class and online. True, his exams and home works are so hard that there's always a 15 point curve, but he's always willing to help. I'm no science major, but he really knows how to make the material accessible to everyone. I enjoyed the class. Just don't expect to do well the first four weeks.
His lecturers are incredibly interesting and well laid out so they are very easy to follow. The exams are pretty easy if you go to class and pay attention.

This class was great! He is an awesome professor, he has Fridays where he covers any questions (even ones for homework) His exams are a little hard but if you show up to class your fine and he curves all work so its easy. I recommend taking his classes!

I thought the class was good. I think I got around B- average for the tests and whatnot, and got an A overall. The weekly homeworks are 5 questions, think a lil bit on them. That's not much for college.. He talks fast sometimes, gets into it a bit much. But that makes it better. I didn't buy the book, and he said not to. How honest..I recommend it.

The tests and homeworks are truly difficult, but he curves so with a 75% average you can expect an A. I didn't even use the textbook, his power points and lecture notes are extensive and helpful. Lectures were sometimes boring, sometimes engaging, but that's true for most classes. I did learn a lot, and would definitely take another class with him.

Class is real hard and tests are tough. The curve saved me. People always complained about this class but I skipped half of the classes and got an A. Hard, but he curves like crazy. I got a 74 on the final. As long as you manage like 80s on every test you're guaranteed at least a B+ or A -.

Although the class is more difficult than a typical Gen-Ed, it is interesting enough to grasp the student's attention during the lecture.  The tests are challenging, but within reason of what he taught.  He provides plenty of information to work with including lectures and overviews  I got an A getting straight 85's on the midterms and final.

WAY TOO HARD FOR A GEN ED CLASS. He's really nice but the tests are impossible.They are curved, which helps, but it's not worth it.The lectures are interesting in the beginning, but once you see your grade, they just become annoying. I studied a lot for this class and managed a B.This class is designed to make you fail unless you're an astro major.

One of the worst teachers I have EVER had. The info we learn in class each day is WAY above that of a Gen Ed class. I took an earth/space class in HS, and he went far too in depth with the info for people that most likely have no knowledge of astro. There's 3 exams, one doesn't count, and they are all rediculously hard. DON'T TAKE THIS CLASS!!!
lectures are usually interesting and engaging.

His class is hard BUT he provides powerpts. for every class, there a text book, and on his website, he provides his own little essay version of what u learn in class that day which are not an outline of the powerpt. IF YOU ASK THE TAS FOR HELP ON HW, REVIEW NOTES, AND GO TO CLASS MOST OF THE TIME YOU GET AN A. HW is hard, but TA's are SO helpful.

If you are interested in astronomy, choose a different professor.  If you are interested in getting an easy A, choose a different professor.  This class is taught like a 400-level course, and tests are so difficult, he has to curve to make it look like we have learned something.  He makes you not want to go to class, which most people don't anyway.

When I signed up for this class I was really excited, but he does not teach Astro 001 like an entry level class. The class is very physics-concept based and he neglects our own solar system so he can talk about stars forever. HW is insanely difficult and his tests are impossible to ace, but there is a curve. I do NOT reccommend taking this class.
doesnt explain in depth, and goes off on tangents. the substitute was a better teacher

He's a really nice guy and can make you laugh, but the tests are RIDICULOUSLY hard, and the homework is extremely challenging. He has a crazy curve which helps, but I would highly suggest trying to find a different astro class
Definitely worth while to go to class.  Best way to get answers for homework is to read lecture notes on his website. He's very helpful if you go to office hours with questions.

Its a hard class.  Very hard HW and material.  But if you show some actual real effort and spend a little bit of time studying, you'll get an A.  You  just have to work harder than the person next to you and it's an easy A. His scoring curve is all relative

i thought astro was really confusing. he tries to explain the material in a simple way, but a lot of times the test questions are more complex than the explanations he gives in class. online homework was pretty difficult for me. he posts the lecture notes online, so you don't really have to go to class.

Very good professor.  Teaches difficult material extremely well by examples and antics that are both entertaining and informative.  Material covered in class is compelling and much more advanced than a HS course.  Definitely recommend Ciardullo.  Only negative is he's not very clear on what you should expect on exams, however, the material is easy.
He seems like a nice enough guy, but he doesn't teach well enough for a non-science minded person to grasp his ideas.  Very difficult to understand otherwise.

never went to class and still managed to get a B.  he posts his lectures and slides online nearly exactly the way he taught in class.  tests and homework are hard, but insane curve.  dont buy the book he tells u to use it as a door stopper or fire starter.

This guy is great but his tests are crazy hard.  But his curve is just as crazy as the tests.  If you get around the average you will get a B-.  the test averages are between 50 and 60.  Dont buy the book he tells you to use it as a door stop.

Very enthusiastic professor, makes most classes interesting and you learn a lot if you pay attention. Nice guy overall. Tests and homework were very hard for an introduction course though, but overall he is a good professor
Very enthusiastic and fun teacher. TESTS AND HOMEWORK VERY HARD. You should go to every lecture and keep up with the work. It's challenging but you learn and lot. He is a very cool teacher.
Interesting class, professor is very knowledgable, and is exciting about teaching.  However exams and homeworks are impossible.  If you need another science I suggest finding a different class.

This class is so freaking hard. I thought, 'astro 001, ooh easy stuff about stars and constellations'- THINK AGAIN! But he does have one heck of a curve in the class, my 70ish grades made a B+. But the hw and test questions were very hard and stressful. The curve saves everyone though...
hardest class ever. don't take this class unless you are willing to study 5 hours a night. the tests are impossible, and the homework is insane.

His class can be extremely hard. Tests and homework are a complete of really difficult and really easy questions. Make sure you go to class. he explains the concepts really well. Sometimes you do have to combine a couple concepts and ideas on your own. All in all the class really is not that bad.

Robin. Ciardullo. Is. The Man: friendly, funny, he knows what he's talking about, and he puts everything into easy terms so that even the most un-scientific student (like myself) can understand.  Tests and homework are designed to be hard, but if you get 70% or more correct, you're getting an A. Easy, fun, highly recommended.

Great teacher! The class is pretty hard, but the curve is huge, i got a 72 on the first test and still had an A. I'm definitely not a science person, and I still managed to get an A- just by studying sometimes and paying attention in class. He's really nice and enthusiastic. I would reccomend it if you need a GS and like Astronomy

Don't be fooled by the 1 in ASTRO and think its easy... I'd advise everyone not to take this class unless you area some sort of SCIENCE major!!! Sure, he is helpful with homeworks, BUT....his tests are INSAINE (in a not good way) and the observing project @ Davey Labs takes A LOT of time...+ the curve is so MESSED UP!! Find another Science ):
While he is a nice teacher, his tests are VERY hard. I am not a science person and I thought astronomy would be an easy class , but definitely not.

I absolutely loved this class. The material is  interesting and Robin does well at getting students to understand the lecture. His additional notes available online also help provide extra clarity to subjects incase you misunderstand something. The tests are not impossible, yet they do require thought. Put in some time and you'll have an A.

Robin was enthusiastic, and tries to explain the material as best he can. The tests are very hard, but they're curved (he says knowing about 70% of the material qualifies as an A). The class was confusing sometimes, but still really interesting.

Great prof, the material is interesting and you can tell that he enjoys what he's teaching.  The test averages are low, but if you pay attention in class getting an A is really easy.  Fascinating class and good prof to take it with :)

Excellent, excellent teacher. Really inspires you to   be interested and want to learn. Always answers questions and tries to make everything as clear as possible. I would definitely reccomend his class.
great teacher, really knows his stuff, tests are hard but if you study you'll be fine

great teacher.  explains things very very well.  however, many people got lost.  the secret for this class is pay strict attention to what he's saying, and ask questions.  he's very open when it comes to answering questions.

i thought this class was very hard. he does curve, but for a gen ed science class i thought it was more difficult than it should have been. only take if if you're really interested in astronomy & good in science.

Astro 1 is a HARD class... nonetheless, Robin's a decent guy and is always fair about curving tests. He's so smart that you'll occasionally get lost, but questions are always welcome, even in a class of 200.
This is one of those professors that you can tell is just a stand-up human being.  He made a very physics-ey subject 100% understandable to a liberal arts major, and he made it interesting too.
Easy class, easy A. Ciardullo does a lot of talking with his hands and dances around a bunch. Material isn't hard, but tests are incredibly difficult. No worries, 20-30 point curves.
Professor explained things very well. Interesting class. Very nice guy and easy to talk to!

The class is really cool and very interesting.  I really enjoy it.  There is so much to learn about space and how things, like our planet were made.  It gives a better understanding of what else is in space besides us (our planet) and what we can see from our yards.

a great guy/teacher but it was hard class. a lot of students failed every test; however, the curves always got us up to a 10 pt curve and sometimes even 2 letter grades!  .... not an easy a, but not impossible either....don't get stressed out if u r not doing good at first, u'll be fine in the end

Test avg. were generally low but there is always a nice (apx 10 pt.) curve.  I loved this class which made it very easy for me (didn't even take notes).  Still my only A in a college level course.  Robin is a great guy and goes over everything on the tests in class.  Course website is very helpful.
No Comments
hard class. nice prof. very helpful... although unclear at times. knows what he's talking about but sometimes can't explain it well. but you can tell he cares about teaching.

Great guy. Uses lots of examples that help you understand the material better. A bit unclear at times, and would sometimes make mention of a topic he had not already covered. Words of advice: NOT an easy A! Take only if you are interested in astronomy!

She is extremely nice, and as long as you do all the work and show up, you should be able to get a good grade. The grade is mainly built around essays and other writing, which she grades somewhat difficult, but if you do the other assignments like the peer review and drafts, you will be fine. The quizzes should be fine if you do the readings.
Genuinely cares and gives good feedback. So sweet and is willing to help with anything and everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Beware of pop quizzes

reviews.comment: Professor Franklin is such a nice lady. While lectures are pretty dry, she follows course material well. There are quizzes on textbook readings but she lets you know the class before. If you go to class (mandatory) and put in moderate effort, you will receive an A. She is so kind helps students out when they might be in a bad position. 10/10 prof!!

Nice guy, average professor. Had no idea how I was actually doing in the class bc only a few things ever got put in the gradebook and there's only five total. Struggled bc I hardly ever showed up to lecture but just make sure you understand what's going on especially with the equations and research articles. Textbook might help but I didn't use it
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super nice guy who makes lectures interesting, but he can't use technology to save his life which often took away from class time. He didn't post a single grade in Canvas, so my final grade in LionPath was a surprise. Exams in his half were a lot more challenging than in the ecology half, but overall, I'd take him again.

Claude is a good teacher, but I found his section to be boring. I felt underprepared for the first exam, but he was generous in grading and the questions were fair. Digging Deeper projects were really interesting and a great way to see the application of the material.

Claude was a great professor BUT DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS if it is COVID-mixed or remote! Both Ottar and Claude are great people but this class gave me so much anxiety because professors failed to keep us informed on grades. Final grades are technically due today and we still don't know how we did on the final exam. unecessarily stressful experience

Definitely a challenging course. Get ready to study a lot! Don't miss class because its 4.5 hours if you take it over the summer. The professor is really funny and overall a nice guy! But you are going to need to study your rear off because its a lot of information in a short amount of time and the tests are not easy.
Very nice professor and he tried to keep the class interesting. Class was very straightforward in what your are expected to know.  The lab section of this class is absolutely horrible though.

The evolution half of BIOL 220M with Dr. Depamphilis was fantastic. The lectures were filled with very interesting and relevant information. He always seemed very happy to help anyone that needed it. Class was engaging - it wasn't just a "sit, see, and memorize" deal.
I was never really interested in evolution, but Dr. dePamphilis made it less painful. He does expect you to think about questions and problems posed in class.

If this is your first math course at Penn State, I would highly recommend not taking it with Parsons. Gives homework daily, which takes at least 2 hours to complete. If you want to enjoy your first semester switch out of this class. She only cares about the students who have a really good understanding of calculus. Only plus is she creates the exam

math 141 is not an easy class, But Dr. Parons really made it much easier. Quick hint she is the coordinator for calc. And She made up the exam questions. I have attended her exam prep and IT IS REALLY useful, in the term that everything covered during review is on the EXAM. Plus, out of 50mins lecture, she would only use 20mins and it is enough.

She gives a lot of homework that is mandatory to do. However, she is good at teaching the material and she want to make sure you understand what she's teaching. She really wants her students to do well. She's also the course coordinator she she knows what goes on the tests...
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: She's extremely tough, but you will learn well under her. She filled in all my math holes and weaknesses. Homework is almost daily so be prepared to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Dr. Parsons is one of the best professors I've ever had. She cares about her students on a personal level. The class is difficult, but if you work hard it's extremely rewarding. I had never taken calculus before this course; she was always helpful when I had questions. Half the quizzes are dropped. I feel more than prepared for my next math course.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--Caring

reviews.comment: Be sure to study and learn on your own. She will go off on random stories in lectures and will go through the whole lecture within the last 20 minutes of class. Usually arrived 5 minutes late for class and made us stay after the 50 minutes scheduled. 35 long homework assignments over the 15 weeks. She was not the professor for me.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: She is one of the worst professors I've ever had. She spends more than half the class discussing non-relevant topics then crams the entire lecture into the final 10 minutes of class, oftentimes going 5 or more minutes over the scheduled end of class time. You're better off watching YouTube videos to learn calculus. CHANGE PROFESSORS AT ALL COST!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Worst teacher I have ever had in any class in my entire academic career. Pointless rants during class(that you essentially are paying for), unreasonable amount of homework, doesn't actually teach you material( more or less attempts to go through one problem per class expecting it to help you). The only pro : not foreign. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Wastes too much time talking about random things. Assigns way too much homework that takes 2-3 hours daily which is useful if you're willing to put the effort into it but a burden if you're not. Cares about her students and will help if you ask her. Does not teach many examples during class. Knows what she is teaching.

Dr. Parsons is the course coordinator for the university so she knows exactly what to prepare you on. She is hard on her students but want you to do well in her class. A lot of homeowrk but really makes you learn the material. Is willing to help and answer any questions you have. If you put in the work you will get the grade you deserve.

Basically, this is the best professor to take if you already have a complex understanding of calculus. The work is explained and proved using board covering complex algebra that is completely unnecessary. In addition there will be several 2 question quizzes that are nearly impossible, and homework almost every night.

Dr. Parsons is one of the best calc teachers you could have at PSU.  She expects a lot from her students but her daily homework really forces you to learn the material and this helps immensely on exams.  Homework is usually long, but effective and she only gives a few quizzes a semester.  Definitely take her if you want a solid calc foundation.

CJP is one of the smartest professors I've ever had. She knows math in and out and she is the course coord. so she knows exactly what to prepare you for on the exams. If you take the time to do the homework and review worksheets for the exams, you will do fine in her class. It's a tough course but she teaches well and is willing to help if you ask.
Hey, listen. It's a hard class. Take Parsons and you will be prepared for those exams. She assigns so much homework, it's hard not to know the material.

It's quite evident she care's about her students success in the long-run (ie getting a lucrative internship), however, it's not apparent she cares whether or not her students succeed in her class.  She likes to complicate things with large quantities of algebra, which then makes the amount of calculus she's actually testing on minimal.  STAY AWAYYY
Her orthodox offline methods of homework distribution and collection didn't match with my methods of studying.
worst teacher I've ever had. Run

While it is obvious that she knows the course material inside and out, her teaching methods are very hard to follow. She starts her classes with a discussion and usually only teaches for 23 of the class. I have found that if you need to see examples of the types of problems being done in class Professor Kazimierz Wiesak is excellent in Math 140.

terrible teacher, worst I've had in psu so far. Gives homework almost every class that are at least 2 hrs long usually more. Doesn't teach anything that is on the homework and if you get more than 50% wrong you get no credit for doing it. She tries to make everything way more complicated than it is. Terrible teacher, only have bad memories of her.

Dr. Parsons was not a good professor at all. If you went into office hours to ask questions she would tell you to read the book, wasn't helpful at all. Would ramble on about nothing in class, so you had to teach yourself everything. Overall my worst professor in my college experience so far.

I know that some people don't care for her teaching style. This is an engineering weed out course. She really knows the material and is always willing to help her students.  She is the 140/141 administrator and pretty much has final say on the exams. So she gears her homework to what you will encounter on the exams.  Do the homework, best advice.

One if the best math professors I've ever had. She gives a decent amount of homework but it really prepares you for the quizzes and exams. She really cares about her students and wants them to succeed. I definitely recommend her if you're going into engineering!

Horrible Professor. Nice lady and tries to make class interesting but when it comes down to her teaching methods, she is awful. Won't teach you the lesson til the last 10 minutes of class after rambling about random unnecessary topics. Homework takes roughly 2 hours on top of teaching yourself the lesson. Save yourself the trouble; don't take her.

She is not a good teacher. First half of the class, she will speak useless stuff and then will rush through the material in the second half. Doesn't give specific examples to explain new concepts. Homework is assigned almost everyday and it takes approximately 1-2 hours to do it.

If you don't have prior calculus experience don't take her. She doesn't start class with rambling about something stupid. Lectures are busted out in about 5 mins towards the end and no examples are used to help on the homework. Basically self taught course, i dropped the course. Although she is pretty nice at office hours, she treated me like a kid

Horrible professor. Great lady, but horrible at teaching. Common to not get started on an actual lesson until the last five minutes of class. You will be teaching yourself every lesson. Homework is daily which forces wasting 50 minutes in her pointless lectures. Worst time management I have ever seen in my life.

Dr. Parsons is by far one of the best professors I have ever had. She cares about her students and the material, while at the same time hosting a fun and interactive class. If you are going into engineering I highly recommend Dr. Parsons.

She will give you the best chance of getting As on the exams. Nightly homework is annoying but just go to the Davey lib. Ask for the solutions manual and you can pretty much just copy all the work out of that. Forces students to have good algebra and work nearly and clearly. I'd highly recommend her.
She spent all class talking about things that are not related to math. She gives too much homework that didn't help with the material. Avoid her if possible.
She spends 90% of class talking about everything but calculus. A sub par teacher that moves at a slow pace and chooses to disregard any proofs. Worst professor I've ever had.
Awesome teacher. Always helpful.
Awesome math teacher who really cares about her students.
One of the best math teachers i have ever had

Very demanding. Homework is assigned every night. Quizzes were ripped apart for style points. Always knew where to push students for extra help and cared about the students opinions on making the class better. Don't take 140E/141E unless you're looking for more work at to praise 70%

This teacher is the head of the Calc department, which helps at certain times. She is a very tough grader, and is sometimes hard to understand. However, she is a very good calc teacher and although her class is hard it's better than any of the other teachers. I would still recommend taking math with this teacher.

One of the best professors that you can get for calc, it is a tough class, but if you do the homework that is due every day, you should easily pass the class.it is a real advantage to be in her class if you want the A

Worst professor I have ever had, although she can be funny. If you have never taken a calc class before do NOT take her class. She expects you to get everything right the first time you try it. I worked so hard in this class and still had to drop it because there was no way I could pass it, even though I had gotten A's in every other honors/IB Math

Wow. What a class. Dr. Parsons is a great teacher, the material is just very hard. She does the teaching part, it's up to you to  do the learning. Do your homework and study...and maybe you'll get a B haha.

Great professor that explains everything very clearly.  Only 5 quizzes all semester, and two of them don't even count.  HW almost every night does suck, but its what is needed to learn sadly.  Our class had the highest avg on every exam, so I think that explains just about everything.

Dr. Parsons is one of the best professors around, if you have a question (even the stupid ones) she'll help you, theres hw most everyday but its really helpful if you want to learn the material (she never gives you any busy work) Before each class we would have discussion about anything for about 5 minuets to make the class more fun. be her student

I didn't mind the amount of homework given, but she rarely explained how to work the problems in class. In addition, she will not help you outside of office hours even if you have a class during them. She normally teaches the 140E classes, so if you aren't an engineering major I wouldn't take her, as she teaches as if you are an engineer.
took her class for both 140E and 141E and am thankful for every minute of it. her work is difficult yes, but she does what is necessary to make sure her students learn the material well.

Dr. P is by far one of the better math teachers I have ever had. The class is by no means easy. However, the grading system isn't constituted by her (although as a tenured "founding" member to the current math department she does have a lot of weight when it comes down to test making)

Parsons is incredibly intelligent and knows how to get the material across. Her classes are crystal clear and she always prepares her students fully for exams. The class by no means is easy, but i'm passing because of her.

she gives a lot of homework almost every day.most of the homework questions are useless. solving math problems every day for approximately 3 hours is not helpful at all because you will be angry, frustrated and exhausted. and one more thing half of the class time is spent over issues not related to the subject!!!! seriously
Good Prof makes herself available. Makes class as intersting as calc can be I suppose. you're gonna learn a lot just be ready to do homework... a lot of homework.

She gives about 2 hours of homework every night. This is extremely helpful. This is the only way you will do well in the course. Most of the class is spent on topics not related to the material at all. I was late to my class right after hers every day. Her office hours are at horrible times. I don't recommend taking Parsons.

Great prof if you actually want to learn.  Has near daily homework which is great for procrastinators.  Other math profs have all the weeks homework do once a week which ends up being done the day before.  She is very clear and helpful and will answer any question even if it isn't math related.  Great even if not going for Engineering.
One of the better math professors, but a difficult freshman course overall. Work outside of class will be required. She has an interresting sense of humor. I would take her again.
very intelligent Prof.

very nice lady. She assigns homework every night, but its good because then you actually learn the material. you have to go to class though. if you miss class you will have trouble understanding the info on your own.

Awesome teacher. Take her classes. She knows exactly what she's doing.  No other way to learn calculus. Homework every night: do it. If you don't, you fail. If you listen to what she says, you do well. period. She knows all. HighlyHighlyHighly recommend.

homework every night but you only need to attempt all the problems and get half right for full credit.  her review sessions are superb. she will challenge you so don't be a pussy. She takes a while to get used to but you'll love her once you do. I had her fall semester and scheduled her for spring too because i liked her so much
She gives homework everyday that is graded very harshly, and devotes a sugnificant portion of her class to other topics and doesn't know hoe to manage the time of the class.
she is good at getting students ready for tests because she knows the information inside and out and helps write the tests but her lectures assume you have a great background in math

CJP  is great! she knows how to properly challenge students while teaching the fundamentals of calculus- she does get off topic on occassion but that's not much of an issue. gives frequent homework, but this helps in the long run

worst math professor ever. plan on ATLEAST 2 hours of homework nightly. majority of homework are even problems graded for accuracy. Extremely condescending and arrogant. makes you feel like an idiot if you don't know calc as well as she does. exam problems are much much harder than quizzes and homework. ends class 5-10 minutes late each day
omg hard as anything
great professor all around. The subject material is very difficult but with daily homework collected and graded you learn a great deal. Take her if you can!

I had CJP all year, because she is awesome and I had to take her 2nd semester. Lots of work, but its better than failing the class with some other teacher.  Very helpful if you have any question, and gets to know you pretty well.  Lets Go Pens

CJP is one of the best math teachers I have ever had.  Many complain about the workload but our class' test means were consistently at least 15 pts. higher then other classes.  She knows her students on a personal level, and is always willing to help with any problems math or not.  I will definitely miss her as a teacher.

Dr. Parsons is one of the best math teachers I have ever had.  Her classes are enjoyable and she does a good job of explaining the topics.  Many people complain about the homework load but what can you expect, IT'S MATH CLASS!  The way you learn is by doing homework!  Also, I have NEVER found her to be arrogant or condecending.

C.J. is one of the nicest professors you will meet. Yet her class is incredibly hard. Coming into this class you must have a clear understanding of ALL algebra concepts. She is a wonderful lady but expect 2 hours of homework a night and you need a study buddy. Also the exams are very hard.I loved the prof.Even with a Calc in high school had to drop

Superb teacher. She really influences me to learn calculus. Her lectures are great and she really connected with my class (since we had her for 140 then 141E the next semester). She became like a friend to me and positively changed my life. I really miss having her for math class. Simply put, it's a lot of work, but CJ's awesome! And you'll learn.
She is very willing to help but she is intimidating at times.

Don't take this class.  If you like 3 hours of homework everynight on top of your current schedual then be my guest.  Oh and one more thing, you have 10 to 15 minutes of lecture while you are assigned 10 to 15 homework questions that make no sense. Hope for odd problems with the solutions manual and pray during exam time.
No Comments
Impatient and condenscending.  She is unclear, and has poor teach style compared to other calculus professors.

She's a horrible professor & is incredibly impatient.  She assigns her own hw problems which are mostly even & collects them & grades for accuracy, which is a problem b/c you can't check ur answers.  She should assign 'suggest hw problems' & use even problems as class examples.  Keep in mind, u only have so much time to go back & do sugg. hw. prob.

Dr. Parsons is the professor that you will only like once you no longer have her. I hated her class; she was ridiculous about homework format, she wasted a lot of class time, and she had boring lectures. But then when the exams came around, our class section outscored the mean by 5 or so points everytime. You will hate her but you will learn Calc.

Dr Parsons has to be the WORST math instructor I have ever seen in my life. spends so much time with stupid questions she only has time to lecture for 5 minutes. Dont bring questions to class or she'll just make you look like an idiot in front of class. She is very conceited and math can only be done her way. Good luck with this teacher, she sucks.

Worst teacher I ever had.I learned more about why state college has two walmarts then calc.The first 40 minutes will b spent on useless random talk about anything that you really want her to get sidetracked on.Then you get two basic examples before you struggle with 20 graded hw problems that take the concepts to a higher complexity level.Good Luck
