people talking about this class as being a waste of time are in the words of professor clemente, "dumbsh*ts." you'd be a fool not to take this class. There is more to college than text books and equations. Best class I will ever have & im only a freshman. no clue how i got into it by the way.

I didn't like this class at all. Nothing about the class seems to be about LHR - it's made of group projects weekly where you make the rest of the class do activities. Dr. Pearce is nice, but there's no grading criteria for the projects, and you don't get any grades until the end of the semester. I found the class to be really confusing overall.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super intelligent guy, don't be scared off by other reviews.The class is super easy if you go, pay attention, raise your hand, and have a good group to share work with. He doesn't use Canvas often, though, so you never know your grade, but he lets you know if you need to participate more. Take this class if you want to be intellectually challenged!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: The professor is a very intelligent and educated guy. The problem is I didnt like having a nine AM class discussion. If you wanna take it no problem, but be ready to read a lot and yap in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This class is very group work heavy, with groups leading their own seminar each week. Grades aren't clear until they're posted in LionPATH, and the professor is a tougher grader than expected. The course focuses on leadership, which wasn't fully what I anticipated going in.

Professor Pearce is a nice person but he loves to talk about himself and his work. All of the reading is actually his papers. The class content is jot hard to understand and very simple but its just tedious work. There are no quizzes just a few papers and very annoying group projects.

Both Craig as a person and this course are just so confusing. Like I can't even tell you how I got an A in here, I had no perception of how I was doing for the entire semester. He doesn't use canvas. All I know is your entire grade is based on how often you participate and how often you show up, there's no exams or anything. Only group projects.

Attendance is very important and the class is based on group projects. Craig is an awesome guy with lots of advice and stories to tell. The class might be harder than a typical seminar ,but you get the value of what your paying for.

Must show up to class. Every class is a group presentation. Moreso is busy than hard work. Projects: movie, short story, case study, free activity. Groups pick a different one per week and present. Final is a BEAST. So so so much work and effort. Effort and participation determine your grade. Big yapper. Loves to talk about himself. Wild stories.

Craig is definitely a yapper, I will say that, but I didn't mind it too much. He's been all over the country and likes to share. The class itself is easy as long as you participate in group discussions. I liked how the class was discussion based and there were no quizzes or tests to worry about. Big project at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class format sucks. You never use canvas, never get grades, can't really reach him. So many presentations. Material is eh. 2 big essays. Nice guy. Tough grader too and you never even know your grade anyways

Worst professor and overall person in general! Only cares about himself spends class time talking about himself and not course materials. Doesn't respond to questions or is consending when answering. Would give O if I could. Don't waste your time.

Worst professor I have ever had. His lectures made zero connection to the course content. Easy exams if you teach yourself all the material. Lost so many points for not participating enough in a half online half in person class.... ok? Kind guy but big waste of time to attend class when you have to teach yourself the material anyway.

If I could give this professor a zero I would. All he does is talk about himself during class time. It also took him a whole week once to answer my one email. He also dropped half of the classes final grades from an A to a B because we all didnt contribute bringing stuff into class for him to teach about. Dont take this professor.

I literally just showed up and sat there and was miserable. I thank the universe for allowing me to be online for that crap like it was insane how boring this class was. I mean it seems he has an interesting life but why only talk about his life and not the class material??! Im sorry, but Id have to agree that this was not my favorite class ever.

Dr. Pearce is by far the worst professor i have had at Penn State. His lectures are simply him telling stories about his past jobs. When students ask questions about course content via email or in class he doesnt answer or is condescending. Do the readings and it's an easy A but a waste of your time.

This class was definitely a little challenging, but I really enjoyed the lectures and discussions. He is really knowledgable and engages the class pretty well If you take notes and just study the cases he lays out for you the tests are very ace-able. If you participate in class and communicate with him, he will work with you and you will do well!
Great professor. Go to class and participate. Follow deadlines. Keeps it consistent.

I have never came across a professor like this until him. It seems like he dislikes our generation and acts as if we are clueless/below him. During lectures he makes snarky little remarks too. He is condescending, judgmental, and arrogant. He doesn't like to be called out either, only he can be right. It's unprofessional…

He is incredibly pretentious and constantly trying to guilt students with his lectures. A super lazy grader too. Grades hard, but gives about 2 sentences worth of feedback for an entire paper. If you skip class for any reason that isn't valid to him, he will make it tough on you. Stay away if you can.

Very pretentious and his tone is like he is talking at you not talking to help you understand. During my first week I attempted to switch out and even the advisor advised me that he's not the best and a very challenging guy. Overall don't recommend, don't know how he still has a job.

During lectures, it felt like he would prompt us with questions that would paint us as the clueless new generation, regardless of our answers.  I get it was him trying to make a point, but it often came across as arrogant. It seems like he makes a pretty quick character judgment, so try to be extra present in the first few weeks.

I agree with the previous reviews as well. He left rude comments frequently. He was not very encouraging, until the very end of the class. He grades pretty hard, if every answer is not exactly what he is looking for he takes off points. And this class was already hard because it has to do with law, so he was not very helpful.

I agree with the previous review that this class was disheartening. The professor graded hard, and his bedside manner left much to be desired. No communication for over a month, and for the 400-course level and topic, I would have thought (and appreciated) more teaching and contact. Also, less derogatory grading comments would have been a bonus.

I felt like the harder I tried, the more Professor Cramer hated me. It was disheartening because I really enjoyed the course material, but I found his feedback to be confusing, condescending, and at times entirely illogical. He once gave me 19/20 on a quiz without marking anything wrong or adding any comments. It's just been a frustrating course.

Ben is a fantastic professor.
He has a lot to say about the industry and his lectures are always interesting. 
If you are genuinely curious, this man has a lot to say. 
I loved all the classes I took with him which were multiple. I don't have the class list numbers with me.

Beware the syllabus! Show up for class! He'll either give you extra credit for being present, or deduct points for not. Especially around break times and special events. He gives lectures where you have to take good notes or you won't pass the tests. He has 3 current events papers and 4 tests. He assigns articles to read instead of a textbook.

Dr. Cramer was a nice professor and his lectures were interesting. However, he is a super unreasonable grader. He takes many points off if your answer wasn't what he was looking for then he provides minimal explanation to help you improve. If you don't show up to class, he will threaten to kick you out of exam reviews and specifically call on you
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Graded by few things--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Cramer is a good teacher and I did enjoy his class. But he is unforgiving, I missed a test due to my dad being in the hospital and he wouldn't let me retake it because I didn't give advanced notice. According to my advisor, this is a common thing with him. I don't want to discourage you but if you are a perfect student he will tear you apart.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Honestly, great professor. As long as you study you will get an A. He will call you out if you consistently don't come to class. He's very organized. He's strange, but you get used to it and it actually helps you learn.

At first, Cramer came off as kind of narcissistic and tough, but it only took me a couple more classes to realize he's actually just got an acute sense of humor about things. He's also extremely insightful into what he's teaching about to where I actually would leave class thinking about something he said. He's also very flexible and fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Inspirational--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had Cramer my freshman year, I'm a junior now and he is still one of my favorite professors. If you don't slack off in class and show up, he will take it easy on you, if you are a bad student he'll give you hell and for those who do try it's very funny. Don't skip class because he does give out in class extra credit on days everyone skips.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Cramer wants to see you do well. His classes aren't the most interesting by any means, but that is not necessarily his fault. Come to class everyday and participate in discussions and he will notice. He tends to make accommodations for students who are in constant communication with him, and are actually putting forth the effort to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring

reviews.comment: Not the most interesting class ever but very easy. I really enjoyed Ben Cramer, some people thought he was an ass but if you come to class and talk sometimes he will really respect you. Not a hard A

I really liked him. Though the class was going to be a snoozer but was pleasantly surprised at how interesting the material was. I think Cramer did a good job of structuring the class, providing background knowledge, and facilitating great discussions.

Talks softly. He is very pretentious and demeaning during his lectures. Has a napoleon complex despite being 6-5. He's straight forward with materials, but acts like he knows everything and we are worthless.
Very easy tests and papers are graded very lax. Dont need to attend class really but if you do the lecture is pretty interesting and always refers to current events. great class

Nice guy. The class is incredibly easy. The tests are straight off the power points, so you don't really need to go to class that often. He's pretty helpful, but a little boring. The papers are incredibly easy and he gives extra credit on occasion.
great class, he is a good teacher. very easy overall, go to class, and reading helps. papers are easy and he gives extra credit occasionally to those who attend and participate a lot.
Very easy just go to class. Exams are straight from power points. Pay attention and it's an easy A.

Go to lectures, do the homework and you will be fine! Dr. Cross gives you all the resources you could ever need and makes Ochem a breeze! I hated chemistry before this course and while I wouldn't say I love it now, it is definitely more manageable.

Dr. Cross was BY FAR the best professor I've had so far at Penn State. He genuinely made me enjoy orgo, coming from someone who hated gen chem. He gives engaging lectures, and he also records his lectures, which is very helpful when studying for exams. He really cares about his students succeeding and gives extra credit opportunities on most exams

content is just hard from midterm 3 till the final, midterm 1, 2 are easy but 3,4 and the final are just insane. He is a good professor, cares and does reviews a lot, gives about 1.5% extra credit if you do some stuff, not to mention the bonuses on each exam. do well before final as it is only worth 15% so you can do poorly and still get an A.
Dr. Cross makes organic chemistry manageable. Do not take Chem 202 or 203 with anyone else! The lab is very easy and never takes more than 2.5 hours.
Great Prof

He's nice and everything, I just personally struggled with his teaching. He zooms through everything in class and then expects you to remember it. Tests are like 80% of your grade, so the worksheets/homework don't help your grade at all. The worksheets are also like 5-7 pages long and only worth 1 point per worksheet, a little ridiculous.

He is a good professor. Lectures r entertaining. Review practice exams to prepare for exams!!! Ask for help when needed, and he will give it to you. Recitation is for help; hopefully, you get a good TA if you don't have a strong background in chemistry.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Cross really wants you to learn. If you go to class and actually pay attention you will be fine. It is mainly based off of lab, unlike 202. 45% of your grade comes from lab reports, so be sure to put a lot of effort into those. Exams were manageable and there was barely any HW. His practice exams are a direct reflection of the actual exams.

I loved having Dr. Cross. He is good at what he does. Exams are during class time and are simple. No exam during finals week. Labs were kinda boring. I wish that the LA problem sets could've been done at home every week as a commuter.

Dr. Cross sent emails out this semester complaining about all the work he has. Students don't pay the money they do for tuition to hear their teachers complain about their job. During lectures, he doesn't explain very clearly the process/what's happening he just writes everything out and expects everyone to know/understand.

Dr. Cross is one of the best professors I've ever had. Lectures are mainly based on what we are doing in lab. TopHat is used for attendance. The exams are extremely easy and are taken in class. There are LA problems sets due pretty much weekly. The only thing that sucks is having to spend time outside class doing NMR and IR in the instrument room.

I took chem 202 with Dr. Cross and I'm currently taking chem 203 with him as well, but I had to let people know to TAKE HIS CLASS! He is easily the best professor I have had so far at Penn State to date, making organic chemistry actually something I enjoy going to. He makes a hard class easy and it's such a funny guy. Whatever you do take his class

I literally went out of my way just to write this because I still think about how amazing he is to this day. I took chem 202 and 203 with him and he somehow made me LOVE organic chemistry and spectroscopy. Most perfect professor I have ever had, I genuinely wish I could take another course with him. Amazing teacher, cares about his students.
Very nice and made orgo easy. 3 exams total and no final finals week. Have to go to class though

Dr. Cross is so nice and understanding, he is very forgiving if you turn in a lab assignment late. His exams are EXACTLY like the exam review, he made orgo so much easier for me. Chem is not my strong suit and he made it so much easier to understand. I loved him so much

Dr. Cross is the best chemistry professor I have ever had - coming from someone who despises chemistry, he made orgo so doable. After years of chem classes, this is the first class where the material actually resonated with me and made sense; he is an amazing teacher. Very patient, understanding, and encouraging. I'm taking him again next semester!

Only need 50% of tophat points for participation. Lecture recordings are posted. Labs are super boring but the post-lab discussions are worth more than your exam grades. Exam reviews are VERY similar to the actual exam. Lots of easy points if you just look at your feedback for lab reports from previous weeks. Get ready for reaction mechanisms
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--So many papers--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He's not great, he's not bad. The exams are challenging, but manageable if you prepare correctly. All lectures are recorded which is great. He is VERY unorganized and his class was very delayed.

I personally think he might be the best professor I've had so far. He makes lectures very interesting and provides so many additional videos further explaining every concept covered. He really cares about his students and wants them to succeed, which is great for ochem. I was dreading this class and ended up loving it 100% recommend!

He was not a bad professor but not a great professor. He is funny and makes good jokes in class but he is unorganized and the exams for his class were so delayed. We had our third midterm the week before finals and he started the third midterm stuff right before Thanksgiving Break. He does provide plenty of concept problems and worksheets
reviews.rating_tags: Hilarious--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He was one of the only professors at Penn State who genuinely cared about the well-being of his students and wanted them to succeed. He is equipped in his knowledge of the field, and he does an amazing job at teaching. If you are going to take chemistry, please take it with Dr. Cross. Organic chemistry does not have to be scary !!

I don't know man. He's such a fun guy, but he has such a way of saying so many words but not actually saying anything at the same time. I find it hard to focus in his class. I feel like he repeats the easy concepts and flies through the hard ones. His class is super unorganized, not really a fan.

Dr. Cross is genuinely the best chemistry professor I have had in my entire academic career. He takes the relatively difficult concept of organic chemistry and makes it entirely bearable. Even as an avid chemistry hater, I actually found myself kind of enjoying the class. He's British and hilarious. What more could you ask for? If you can, TAKE HIM

Dr. Cross is an amazing professor! I've always struggled with chemistry, but he had entertaining lectures along with practice problems, additional lecture videos, and multiple attempts on homework. For the exams, he puts most of the practice problems on the actual exam, lol. As long as you use what he provides, you'll get a good grade.

The class itself was incredibly boring, and I'm glad I took it when we were still online, because I don't think I would have made it otherwise. Dr. Crosby is a nice guy, but his tone can be pretty monotonous, and can be harder to listen to for an entire class period.

I took the honors section Psych 100H. There wasn't much homework, and we didn't have to participate in studies. The tests were MCQ. In class, Dr. Crosby often had us talk with a neighbor about topic questions. I think that the honors section was easier and more fun than the regular Psych 100 section, so I highly recommend Psych 100H with Crosby!

guys please do NOT listen to the positive reviews on this professor he SUCKS. with all the love in my heart i think he is a good guy but diva this is not the career path for you. i have watched him randomly berate people in a huge lecture hall for having their phones out, he is so hard to follow in lectures but also if you don't go you will be lost
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Dr. Crosby gets a bad rep because he does not post lecture slides. You definitely will need to go to the lectures if you would like a high score in the course. He often has questions on the exams that you would only be able to know from going to the lectures. His exams are cumulative from the one prior.

Dr Crosby gave interesting lectures. There is very little homework, and your grade is mostly exams. He offers extra credit, which is pretty easy to get. He was generous with curving the exams. He definitely wants his students to succeed. You need to do some studying outside class to get a good grade, but it's not a hard class at all.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, Prof. Cosby is a nice person; however, the course has minimal activities to add towards the grade. It is very reliant on the exams and 5 homework. He does make sure that the class has plenty of opportunities to gain extra credits. The textbook is free and online, and participation in research for psychology is required (6 points minimum).

Professor is great and has good lectures. He has lecture outlines available to fill in while he lectures, which makes it very easy to review material. There is minimal homework and multiple extra credit opportunities. Must study before tests but they are not bad. Attendance isn't mandatory but if you don't go to class you will be confused.

He knows how to talk to a 600 lecture class very well. He keeps me engaged, and I reccomend sitting near the front as you get more engaged. His test are reasonable if you study. If you don't study you will fail, so you have to study. The material isn't difficult, it is more memorising. He gives extra credit and few easy hw assignments. I reccomend!
so interesting i learned so much! 10/10 recommend

Great lectures, people say the exams are hard but if you just review notes after the lecture and study the week leading up to the exam you will do great. There's multiple extra credit opportunities and only a few homework assignments. Use quizlet and the practice exams and you're good
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very nice experience overall tbh, only thing is he will keep you til the last second and get upset if you pack up early (which I do understand). Attendance not taken, however, I would recommend showing up, as he does not post slides or lecture notes (he does post a lecture outline to use to take notes!) Very accessible, textbook he uses is free!

Dr. Crosby is incredibly engaging and his class is fun. Be sure to study before exams because they are definitely difficult. 
He is pretty accessible for office hours and will explain whatever you need.
Knows how to talk to big classes and keeps people engaged - talks until the last minute of class
Professor does not clearly state his expectations and waits too long to give meaningful feedback. Would not take again.

I took Dr. Crosby's section of PSYCH490 on Sleep Psychology. I went into the class thinking it would be boring, but I ended up loving it. Dr. Crosby is super kind and understanding, and though he does take attendance, missing only 3 classes earns you extra credit. Would easily take another class with Dr. Crosby and recommend his Sleep Psych class.

I liked Dr. Crosby! His lectures aren't the most engaging ever, but the structure of his course is simple. 5 homework assignments that require little effort, 4 or 5 exams, and then SONA research credits. That's essentially your whole grade for the course, and I found the material to be super easy as someone who took AP psych in high school.

Prof Crosby was super nice and a good lecturer. He explains things in details and if you attend class and study 3 times a week for 15-20 min its impossible to get less than a -A. He gives study guides that have the same things he has in the exams. 4 exams and lots of extra credit. He doesn't post the lectures.

Brian's course and way of teaching is very engaging! Getting a good grade in this course doesn't require much but attending classes and getting all of the notes is crucial to performing well on exams. Don't be surprised if you skip class a lot and get bad grades on exams. Final exam was the easiest out of the 4 taken. Would recommend!

Class is entertaining but exams are difficult. The final was the easiest. I barely went to class & my grade was a C. He gives guided notes in class and doesn't post them on Canvas. But, overall, pretty fair and nice.

There is no attendance points but you have to go to class for the notes. Its honestly worth it though, he is such a good lecturer. He also posts study guides that have exactly what you need to know for exams. Got an 100 on one and really good grades on the others by just going to lecture and taking notes. Definitely gonna take him again for 270.

Prof. Crosby is nice. His lectures can be boring and he doesn't like when you're on your phone (and he makes that known). He offers 10 points of extra credit total. You have to go to class because he doesn't post the slides or anything. 4 cumulative exams including the final. You only are graded on 4 exams, 5 homeworks, and 10 points extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: If you have the option, do not take Brian. need to attend every lecture to get the bulk of exam material. overall super boring class and he gets moody also you have to actually try on the homework because both him and the TA's grade it strictly

He is a really nice guy. If you are interested in psychology and want to pay attention, he has good lectures. Use his outlines for your notes because they're pretty helpful and he follows them very closely. Exams are kind of hard, you have to make sure you are studying throughout the semester, but he makes this clear at the beginning of the class.

There is nothing you can do if you bomb the exams, there are only 4 or 5 homework assignments which do not do much to bring your grade up. His voice is very annoying and he keeps the temperature in the room at 100 degree and makes you fall asleep. At ALL COSTS DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Overall, Brian has been a decent professor throughout the semester. He gives good lecture outlines, but can be a little dry. The exams are pretty difficult unless you study multiple times a week and not just all at once, I learned that the hard way. It's not a bad class as long as you study the “right way” and attend most of his classes.

The class is decently entertaining and the professor is so nice. It's important to go to class, even though it's not mandatory, or you'll fall behind quickly. The exams are easy if you make flashcards (I used Quizlet) and study at least a week before. He makes expectations clear. Extra credit is offered lots but sign up for studies ASAP (online).

If you need to be told the same thing 10x to learn one vocabulary word he is a perfect teacher for you. He repeats the same things nonstop and goes on and on about how much he can't stand kids on their phones. Below average psych teacher and I ended up using my AP psych notes more than his notes. Take his class if you want to waste your time.

I did not like him as a professor because he was boring. His assignments weren't horrible, but there were just many of them. If you could get another professor for this class, do it. You will literally fall asleep in his lectures or not want to show up because of how boring he is. I do NOT recommend him.

Four big exams and that's really all that matters for your grade. You have to attend lecture and pay attention or you'll fall behind quick. Every test is remotely cumulative so don't wait to study old material. He is a nice guy but the lectures can feel a bit boring. Overall if you would rather have a few exams rather than quizzes pick him.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Never take this class as a GenEd. NEVER

He is a great professor, and I really enjoyed his class. However, it can be tough, especially if you've never taken a psychology class before. Good time management is important since the class is very test-focused, and doing well on exams is key due to its weight. Make sure to attend every class and take notes because he doesn't post the slides
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: loved the professor but super hard class. attendance isn't mandatory but you have to go to class in order to understand the material. professor does not record lectures. 4 multiple choices exams and 4 homework assignments. also have to participate in research studies and can go to extra studies for extra credit.

I would recommend taking with a different professor for PSYCH100, it would be the same course but a lot better. Only 4 exams and homework assignments. Exams are difficult, and not many opportunities to improve grades. No attendance taken, but slideshows are not posted; he does not include all content on the slideshow anyway. Would not recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof. Crosby is a nice guy. He gives "study guides" for exams but it's basically just a list of terms we need to memorize, which doesn't help a ton with application. Your grade is basically determined by 4 exams, and 5 homework assignments (which TAs grade, I have found them to be kind of tough graders). There are a few extra credit opportunities.

Relies on 4 homework, 3 exams, and final. Averages on all exams were around 75%, pretty hard and notes/lectures do not really help since it is all application. Would recommend taking someone else if possible, friends are in other Psych100 and have it so much easier.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!!!! Brian may seem like a good guy, but this class is nearly impossible. My friends in other PSYCH classes are passing with easy A's... but not this class. There are 4 exams and 4 HW assignments. You might as well not even study for the exams because it wont help. take another professor if you can!
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment:
Brian is a great guy, but it is VERY test heavy and there aren't enough opportunities for HW assignments or quizzes to even out your grade. 

Don't take this class if you aren't a good test taker.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: The class is literally all exams, and they are long and all situational based questions when we don't even practice applying information in class. I have never done so bad in a class. I do not recommend at all. There are not enough filler grades to even out exams.

Brian is an AMAZING professor. He's funny, personable, and a sweetheart whenever you see him. His lectures are never boring, his exams are very reasonable, and he offers students lots of extra credit. He also has interactive lessons where he sometimes invites students "onstage" for a demonstration or psych-related game.

Crosby was a great professor. Had really easy to follow lectures and provided good notes. You are graded by very few things (5 homework's and 4 Exams), so paying attention  lectures matters. He does also occasionally offer surprise extra credit during lectures, so showing up matters.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Amazing lectures --Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Great professor. Loved his lectures. Gave plenty of examples of concepts in class and always put in effort to make it interesting and engaging. There were a couple of written homework assignments that were an easy grade along with many extra credit opportunities. 4 exams throughout the semester including the final. Was given study guides for all.

Dr. Crosby was alright. Exams are like 90% of your grade. His lectures were long and there's a lot to remember, and no practice applying information (which is what you're expected to do on exams). This is a class where I can say I wish there was homework or quizzes. It's a lot of information. So much information that we skipped a lot of it.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Professor Crosby had amazing lectures! His tests are very straightforward if you go to class and look over the study guide. He only has a few homework assignments and they are simple!

Worst guy ever. Was told I had a learning disability after I failed the first test and was also no help to me. I did everything needed and still had a hard time passing. His tests are so much application so make sure you really know what everything is and like be ready to diagnose people. Hope to never be in the same building as this guy again.

He gives a lot of extra credit opportunities which is nice. You have to really study for the exams because there are so many terms to memorize per exam. He does curve though. I took this class as a gen ed-- I don't recommend doing that.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He does well going over topics in class but on exams he asks questions on exams about examples from class or specific details that weren't emphasized. Very few graded assignments so exams count really heavily towards your grade, but he curves them most of the time. Offers up to 10 points extra credit which really boosted my grade.

It was ok. He is clearly passionate about teaching and psychology, so that does help. The homework assignments are easy and kind of fun and boosts your grade a lot. But the tests are HARD and impacts your grade a lot, very specific scenarios that are confusing.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Exams are in person, in POLLOCK (not online, he changed that), so you HAVE to study. Each exam is also cumulative with 35 questions from the unit you are learning and 15 questions of ANY of the material from previous exams. Attendance isn't mandatory but he does extra credit in class on paper, so you cannot receive the points if you aren't there.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Prof Crosby is the best! He is super kind and caring, and you can tell that he really cares about psychology. His lectures are interesting and easy to understand. There are approx 5 assignments along with SONA research study credits you have to complete. The exams are easy if you study, and the study guides are very straightforward.

Do not take this professor because instead of taking examinations on the unit that we just learned, he does it on previous units, making it more difficult to study. You also do not get any quizzes, so your scores are based only on four homework assignments and exams and SONA.
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was an L, tests were very specific and situational.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: One of the nicest people you will ever meet. His lectures are enjoyable especially if you like psychology.

Brian is an amazing professor! His lectures aren't boring and you can tell he is experienced in the field. Content can be challenging but just STUDY!! that's it. There were like 3 assignments the entire semester and they weren't difficult at all. The exams can be rough so I recommend studying a couple weeks prior or even at the end of each week.

Crosby is amazing! I have recommended him to so many of my friends, and are looking to take more of his courses at penn state. He posts all of his lectures on canvas so if you have to miss a class it's no big deal. He gives lecture outlines, and a study guide with terms you need to know for exams. He is also so funny, and will have you laughing.

Professor Crosby is a nice guy overall. Some of his lectures could get monotone but every once in awhile he would say something that made the class laugh. Exams are difficult because of the wording of the questions but they're not impossible if you just study. You can tell he's passionate about his studies which is always nice in a prof.
Dont know how to feel about him. He comes across extremely nice in his lectures but meeting in private not as much.

Professor Crosby was a great professor. He was very good at explaining topics and gave many examples to help us understand better. All of his lectures are recorded so you can always look back if you missed something. Exams were a little difficult, it was more applying the concepts rather than what he was teaching.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Brians lectures were so engaging and it was hard to get bored. The material was very interesting and you can tell hes passionate. The tests are pretty tough so definitely study, but he provides a lot of extra credit if needed.

Crosby is a great teacher and knows what he is talking about, but the exams are far too difficult for an intro level class if you did not take Psych in high school. There is a lot of extra credit opportunities, and tests are slightly curved, but Crosby weirdly enjoys seeing his students' nervousness on test day.

Professor Crosby is a great lecturer. He provides lots of opportunities for extra credit and the homework assignments are relatively simple. If you took psych in high school, this is a good elective for your first semester.

Prof Crosby gives such dad energy in the best way possible. He is very caring and conscious of everyone's needs in the class. His lectures are interesting and he posts all lecture recordings at the end of the week if you missed one. He gives you the pdf of the textbook to read, I think most people can get by with just listening to the lectures tho

This is one of the best courses I've taken at PSU. I can't recommend Brian Crosby and this class enough. It's definitely a hard class, and you have to put in the work to do well, but if you're willing to put in the work it isn't hard to get an A. He's very understanding and straightforward in his expectations. And he offers in-class extra credit!!

Crosby is a good professor, not for 100 level class. Exams are so difficult and you have to know the terms like the back of your hand to get a decent grade. Exam questions worded very weird- almost grammatically incorrect. Little homework, so exams carry your grade. Nice guy and is always willing to help/accommodate you, but too hard for 100 level.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Please do not take his PSYCH 100! He started doing in-class closed-book exams now, and they are so difficult. Around 1/5 of the class failed the first exam, and the class average was only C-. The course is also extremely exams heavy (75%). His class is one of the hardest 100-level-class, and studying hard cannot guarantee you a good grade!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Crosby is very knowledgeable about abnormal behavior and gives plenty of examples to help his students with the material. I usually like to take my own notes, but his outlines are super helpful and to the point. He gave plenty of extra credit opportunities to help our grades. I would totally take any other psych class of his just based on this one!

Crosby's class is like a middle school class. Just make sure you go to class (or don't, all his lectures are recorded and posted online) and write down everything he says. Test questions are either the same or extremely similar to the situations he describes in class. There are a lot of opportunities for extra credit. Tests are online and open note

This class was pretty difficult for a 100 level. Exams were open-note but hard. The questions are worded very weirdly which makes them difficult. Also, I personally felt there was not enough time for the exams. He does offer extra credit but it barely adds any points to your overall grade.

Pretty easy general education class. I'm a business major and I didn't think it was too hard. Attendance was not mandatory and lectures were posted online. Exam questions have really weird wording but were open note.

I could not recommend Psych 100 with Crosby enough if you're looking for a GenEd. Crosby had interesting and  enjoyable lectures. His homework was always easy and simple like write 2 paragraphs on your sleep patterns or how you can reduce your stress. Exams are open note and online. This class is an easy A.

What a guy. He really knows his stuff and he knows how to teach it and make it enjoyable. I loved his class. He's a great guy with a good sense of humor that he uses to break up some of the material. His lectures are great. They are not boring to listen to because he's good at making connections and working in different forms of media. Also EC

Dr. Crosby is my favorite professor. He was so caring about his students. His lectures were really easy to understand and he made them memorable. His class was not too difficult, although his tests were difficult if you didn't study. He didn't give too much homework, and it was mostly just a grade booster. He was so understanding of us.
Lecture everyday, exam class averages were C's every time and we did not have enough time to take them.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I really liked this class. Homework was easy and Brian gives a lot of extra credit. Exams are tough, but take notes and you'll be fine. We were told to buy a textbook but I literally never used it, don't waste your money.
- Professor Crosby thought psych better than any other psych teacher I had so far. His lectures doesn't make you fall asleep, and he actually engages with us. he's also really funny.
One of my favorite professors at this school. He doesn't take attendance, but you need to take notes in class so it is kind of mandatory. All of the exams were online.
Love him. The tests are manageable but is a huge chunk of your grade. There are only a few homework assignments but extra credit is available often
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: If you don't take good notes during lectures, you won't get a good grade. You can tell Brian loves and cares for his students,. If you take good notes during the lectures, you don't need to use the textbook at all, at least for his online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Caring--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I really loved this course and how it was taught. The lecture slides and note outlines were super helpful when studying for exams. The homework assignments helped to reinforce ideas taught in class. He genuinely cares about his students. I really enjoyed this class; it might be my favorite class I've taken at Penn State-- Brian is awesome

Really cares about helping his students grow and succeed. As long as you pay attention and take notes the quizzes will not be hard and the homework is more than manageable. Also gives loads of EC oppurtunities. I raised my grade by 4% just by writing four-one page extra credit papers throughout the semester. If you dont slack you will get an A!

Dr. Crosby is OK. He is caring, but he is also a bit of a tough grader, especially for a 100 level class. The exams are hard, so make sure to study. His lectures were really interesting and fun though and got me interested in being a Psych major, so I would take him again.

Dr. Crosby is an ANGEL. Having a background in Psych helps, but he's a great lecturer and always makes sure his students understand the concepts. Quizzes were open-note, hws are super easy, and SO. MUCH. EXTRA CREDIT. Beware of the SONA participation though, if you forget, it'll be impossible to complete last-minute. Would HIGHLY recommend!

Dr. Crosby is an easy teacher. He gives guided notes and even a study guide for the final which is like unheard of in college. The quizzes are open note which is great because of the guided notes. There is so much extra credit it's crazy. The SONA research credits are super easy to get too. Just check daily and you'll get em done b4 September ends

I took AP psych in high school so this class was a breeze. I would recommend if you have had psych already, but it will be hard if you haven't. I only had to show up for lectures and take notes, and studied maybe 10 minutes for every quiz. I noticed that quiz scores were always low (Cs), so it might not be the easy gen ed youre looking for

Made you watch lecture material outside of class which was so annoying and very time consuming. Weekly quizzes on each topic were somewhat challenging. Textbook needed to get more info about lecture material and other things. Lectures just went over case studies and extra credit topics. Really nice guy but you do need to put work into this class.
This is an easy class. He is a good teacher but boring. Lots of extra credit.

I enjoyed Dr. Crosby's class, but found his lectures boring on Zoom. He has a quiz for every section, which are easy questions but students didn't perform very well. It makes the class hard because this is the majority of the grade. There are five homework assignments, one final and 10 extra credit opportunities. A boring class, but not horrible

Professor Crosby is so caring and funny. He loves telling relevant stories about his kids and was great with the examples he used to explain the material. The textbook is "required", but I did well without it because the notes cover everything you need for the quizzes. The homework is easy for getting points, and he offers tons of extra credit.

Crosby is a great prof! His class was very engaging for a 100-level intro course. It should be an easy A if you attend every day (but I did not). The material is straight from the textbook, so you should read and study from it for exams. He is funny and great at explaining and storytelling. I would have taken the course even if it wasn't required.

If you read the book or attend class you'll definitely pass the class. Everything on the tests he has specifically gone over in class so as long as you go you'll be all set, but attendance also isn't mandatory. If you learn better from reading the textbook you'd do fine in class too.

He is a great professor. Drops lowest two quiz grades and home works. All the assignments are easy from lectures and he makes sure you understand everything with examples. He has everything set up to make sure you pass the class with a good grade as long as you put in some work. Lots of extra credit too.

Very unfair grader. Tells you he wants specific data in research papers in APA format and when you put quotes in he marks you down full letter grades. Questions on exam are nothing like the practice tests he gives out and have nothing to do with what is in the lecture. Takes off points on everything because thats not they way hed do it.

I really enjoyed this class with Dr. Crosby. He gives really interesting lectures and the exams are not too bad as long as you read the questions carefully and come in prepared. I definitely recommend this class to people of any major, however there definitely may be easier options to complete a gen ed.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: He is fine; the lectures are kind of boring, but there are a bunch of quizlets online if you miss something. The exams are about 35 questions, but he gives you an 8-page study guide so it can be confusing. The best thing about this class is there are about ten possible extra credit points which help. He tries to be engaging but is soft-spoken.

Brian has great lectures and fully explains the material. He incorporates comedy into his and lectures in a way that makes the class more enjoyable. The syllabus said the book was required, but I did not get it. He does not take attendance, but he does not post the notes online. Overall a great professor and class!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Professor Crosby's Psych 100 class was by far my favorite class so far. Attendence is not mandatory, but the lectures are so interesting that I went almost all the time. He also gives fill in the blank notes that you just fill in during class. The exams are difficult, but personally I only did well on 2 and the final and still got an A-!

I loved having Professor Crosby this semester! Great lectures and lecture notes provided- I really enjoyed the class. I also got very sick in the middle of the semester and he was very understanding and accommodating :)

Going to class isn't mandatory however that is the only way you can get the notes, and every once in a while he will do random attendance checks and give you extra credit for being in class that day. He's a really great guy and I really enjoyed his class. The exams are more of applying the information learned, but you just have to apply yourself.
He's nice and entertaining guy and pretty fair about his exams but don't expect a cakewalk. Definitely easier classes to fulfill your gen-eds if that's why you chose this class.
Brian is a great professor. He really tries to give good examples to make sure topics are clear. He also gives online quizzes to boost grades and offers a decent amount of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Get ready for SONA studies to SLAP you in the butt. They are a pain in the butt. This course should be a 4 credit course bc you are required to do studies outside of class so you end up spending about 4 hours a week on Psych (including class). Professor is good, he's funny and uses a lot of videos. Lectures are interesting as well.

Professor Crosby is BY FAR the best professor that I've had at Penn State. If you don't take this class with him you'll regret it. His lectures are thorough and really entertaining. You can easily get an A on the exams and the hws if you go to class and study. He is always willing to help/meet with his students.

He is a great prof! He is funny and makes the content more interesting. You are given tons of opportunities for extra credit. If you show up, copy the notes (fill in the blank notes are available to you), and study the notes before the exam it'll be an easy A.

Took this online. Simple set up just a few discussion posts due every Sunday (no replies required). There are 2 exams and the final all quite easy. Don't waste your money buying the books just read the notes posted on Canvas.

A great guy overall. He basically gives you fill-in-the-blank notes, which are in the order of the lecture slides. You can't get the notes outside of class though, so you have to be there. The study guides are basically the exams. There are many chances for extra credit. Grade comes from participation in studies, quizzes, and exams.

I have taken two classes with Dr. Crosby (PSYCH 270 and 470) and absolutely loved both of them. He makes class interesting and doesn't give too much work. You can easily pass if you just apply yourself and study!

This class is pretty easy, and as long as you show up to class, take notes, and review the notes before the test, you should be okay. He always includes a test review and as long as you know all of the topics, it is pretty straightforward.
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: A very caring professor who gives great lectures full of examples and real-life connections so going to class is very helpful. Definitely, recommend taking this class with him.

Cool guy but going to class is essential to get the extra credit. Homework is a huge chunk of your grade and messing up on one test WILL cost you your grade because there are barely any grades. You also have to get the textbook because some exam questions come from the book and isn't taught in class.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: My favorite professor at Penn State so far. Really knows what he is talking about and takes pride in it . Has boring lectures if you are not interested in the subject. Would recommend.

Brian's class is fairly easy, as long as you go to class and fill in his lecture outlines. I never had to study too much for this class either because the information is pretty straightforward. This class should be an easy A.

I love Brian. He's a great professor and makes the class enjoyable. However, his exams are 35 qs and he gives a study guide with over 100 words each time. The questions are all application too so you really have to use the book, study HARD, and know your material extremely well. I am taking 6 classes, and this one is, to my surprise, my hardest.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: I LOVE Brian. Amazing professor! I already took Psych in high school, but he made it fun all over again! The material is easy, there's just a lot of it. He gives good extra credit and a lot of other points outside of exams. I would definitely recommend taking any class with him! He makes lectures understandable and fun!

Brian was absolutely great in my FYS class! He was always willing to answer questions and did a very good job with getting students involved in discussions. STUDY FOR THE MIDTERM (some people failed and it tanked their grade). Pay attention in class & it's very interesting content.
definitely recommend for an easy A
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: I worship the group Professor Crosby walks on. AMAZING man and really understanding professor. Class is super easy and he uses Office scenes frequently; just take good notes, but for the most part you wont need his textbook
reviews.rating_tags: GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Caring--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: He is the best psych professor at psu! His classes are pretty straightforward and exams are relatively easy if you pay attention in class. Attendance isn't mandatory but he gives examples of terms in class and those examples almost always show up on the exam. He offers a ton of extra credit as well!

Crosby is such a fun guy, his lectures are super interesting. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, I have never missed a class because I enjoy them so much. However, he tests you on concepts which aren't taught in the lecture. His exams can be difficult (I'm averaging a 78) but he offers lots of outside help, extra credit, and study groups.

Brian is a great professor. I highly recommend his class for anyone interested in psychology. He is very clear in what will be on tests and on other assignments. Also, he makes himself very accessible outside of class to help you out, even not during office hours.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Hes a bright and amazing professor. If you ever have any questions or confused on a topic he will help you out. Go to lecture and take notes, you will pass the class. It is a lot of memorization so dont think youll pass by just reading once or twice. You wilk need the textbook for homework assignments.

I honestly hated this class. I thought it was going to be interesting when i signed up for it but it's not. He teaches the most basic things in class then makes you read 120 pages for every exam. He puts questions on the exams that if you skim the readings you will do bad on the exams. I would not take this class again for any class with him.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Dr. Crosby is a nice guy, but has hard exams. I took psych 100 as an easy gen ed, but the class is difficult for someone who's never taken a psych or hdfs course before, like myself. Also, if you dont go to class & take good notes, the exams will be very hard. it was difficult to receive extra help in this course and the TA wasnt helpful at all.

One of those classes where you sit and take as many notes as possible from the powerpoint for each class. He gives lots of useful materials such as outlines for note taking, and study guides for each exam. Don't be discouraged by my grade in this class, I made stupid mistakes along the way. This is an easy A if you put in some time and effort.
one of the best professors ive ever had
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Dr. Crosby is a very nice guy, but this class is very difficult. He puts things on the exams that is not relevant to the overall topic. DO NOT trust his study guides and read the book. Im on a premed track taking bio and chem classes and this was my worst grade of the semester!
reviews.rating_tags: Clear grading criteria--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: If you would like to get an A, you better read textbook. Do not trust study guide, just study everything and read textbook, you will easily get an A. I took this class when I was senior, so I was not hard for me, but you are taking it when you are sophomore, you need to read textbooks and take detailed notes. If you do so, exams aren't hard at all
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Respected--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Crosby is a very outgoing professor. He really knows his stuff and even makes word (or pdf) documents that have what we need to fill out for notes, which is super helpful. The exams are okay, can be tricky if u don't pay attention or get the notes. Overall, I enjoyed the class.

If you don't come to class getting the notes can be very difficult. For the most part he is very straight forward. The final exam is worth 30% of your final grade and its cumulative. He's funny and very approachable. He gives out extra credit like candy so do it, it can really make a difference in your grade. Overall I would say he is pretty fair.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Skip class? You won't pass.--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Does not check attendance but occasionally offered in-class extra credit. 4 exams that aren't too hard, but there is always a few questions that were not covered in the notes. 10 online homework assignments that usually aren't too difficult. Lectures are very boring!

Dr. Crosby is a nice man and a good teacher. BEWARE, this class is not easy and is exam heavy. He puts questions on the exam that are very difficult and can only be found if you read the book very precisely. Doesn't give much extra credit but keeps the class fun. Material is interesting but would not take this class if you don't have to.
Dr. Crosby was my favorite professor for fall semester. I highly recommend taking him. Although lectures are not mandatory, they are very interesting and are worth your time.
Great guy! Would definitely take another class with him. He makes the lectures fun and is very clear about what will be on the exam and what won't.

Brian is my favorite psych professor thus far. He really makes you want to learn. His lectures aren't terrible and he offers some extra credit. Tests are a bit tough and you do need to study. need to go to class to get the information.

By far one of the most caring professors I've had at Penn State. You can tell he loves what he teaches and really wants his students to do well. He is also extremely helpful during office hours and will always offer his help. He gives a good amount of extra credit, too!
reviews.rating_tags: ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Awesome professor. The way he outlines the class makes it really manageable and not too hard. He gives guided notes on word which is awesome and his lectures are great and engaging. Exams are fair and not too hard, only 35 questions, 70 points. A lot of opportunity for extra credit. Missing class is fine, just don't get into the habit.
good lectures, super easy, gives note outlines and the power-points are super straight forward

Great prof! He posts lecture outlines that are great. You have to be in class to get the notes but if you do that and study the notes you'll get an A in the class. He really cares about his students, which is sweet.  10 online quizzes/hw  and extra credit available. Great guy

the lessons are very through. there are quizzes every two weeks on the material. there are a few discussions - as long as you participate you'll get 100%  and 2 group projects. no midterm or final. there is the option for extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Gives good feedback--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: I loved his class. He gives us notes guides to print out and bring to class and we just fill in the information during class. His kids are still small so he refers to them a lot so that's cute. His exams are easy to study for because he puts up easy to understand exam guides. I would definitely take his class again if I needed the credits.

Professor Crosby is great! He is a very helpful professor and is always looking to make sure students are understanding their material. Admittedly, having a background in psychology is helpful because the class is difficult. But, he does give substantial note packets and lots of opportunities for extra credit. A great choice for a gen ed credit!

I hated this course with Crosby. The material we learned was very different than the other Psych 100 courses. His tests are all application and can be confusing. The study guides he gives are pointless. They pretty much reiterate every single thing we did in class and dont give guidance to what will be on the exams.

Dr. Crosby is a great professor. He relates all of his topics to the real world to make sure they are understood in context. You are able to miss a few classes here and there but definitely don't make it a habit. He often shows The Office  videos so if you like The Office, you're in for a real treat. But seriously he's super nice and a great prof.

Brian is a great professor. You have to go to class in order to get the notes for the exam. Brian is very caring about his students. It was the beginning of the year and we lost a student in an accident. He cried while telling us and he gave us comfort. He didn't even know the kid very well because it's a large class. It just shows he cares.

Amazing professor that cares about the subject.  He makes his lectures interesting by using personal examples.  He assembles a note-taking outline of the chapter for all students.  He gives many opportunities for extra credit... Easy A.

Professor Crosby is one of my favorite professors at Penn State. His lectures are very interesting, and he uses great examples to explain each concept better. I never used the textbook. All test questions come from the notes and the lectures. You have to go to class in order to fully understand the material. Overall great professor

Very knowledgable professor and great at what he does. He makes the class interesting for the students while being very informative at the same time. He gives many chances for extra credit, which is really helpful for keeping your grade up. Overall, he is a great professor and I would take his class if you get the chance

DO NOT TAKE THIS PROFESSOR!! Only take this instructor if you can read minds! This professor expects you to know what his grading criteria is without telling you. The exams and essays are EXTREMELY DIFFICULT! Because he is such an unfair grader, you have to work really had to just pass the class. Take PSYCH 270 with a DIFFERENT PROFESSOR!!
He was funny, but the class itself was difficult.

He is an awesome professor.  Three tests plus final, four homeworks, and then three essays based on the same novel.  Tests are a walk in the park based off of only lecture notes.  Thought this was an easy A until the last essay happened.

The worst part was that his class was at 8 AM, but if you go to class then you'll do decent on the test. Take advantage of the extra credit. Can study for exams the night before. Probably the best option for PSYCH 100
Hard exams
really interesting, really great teacher. probably the best option for PSYCH 100

Dr. Crosby is really good at explaining things, smart guy, but doesn't answer questions very well and gives unsure answers that kind of avoid answering directly. Lectures were clear, exams weren't too hard, definitely a solid choice if you're taking Psych 100.

His class is awesome. If you want something pretty easy, then take his class. He gives out a lot of extra credit and gives an outline. I didn't really even need to use the textbook. The class is an easy on but you will still need to study. Sometimes it got boring but overall loved the class and him.

Good professor and easy class. Study exactly whats on the study guide and you will have an A. My very first class at Penn State and easier than high school. You dont have to go to all the classes as long as you study. I bought the textbook and always use it because im bad at paying attention and when i skip class I can teach myself at my own pace.
Great professor and passionate about material

I have this class at 8 AM and I actually don't mind getting up for it!  He's super nice, unexpectedly funny, and the class isn't too tough.  Plus, he posts AMAZING note outlines on Angel so you can fill them out quickly and still listen to the lecture.

Crosby is really passionate about his subject, but doesn't always present the information in the best way. There's so much information that it's hard to keep straight sometimes! Tests are a bit tough, but there are only 3 of them (in addition to 10 quizzes).

Dr. Crosby is a great professor, he has interesting lectures and provides different activities illustrating examples from the lectures. The exams are not easy but he provides good outlines and study guides. Great class that would definitely recommend

You definitely do not need to buy the textbook unless you plan on never going to class. The readings that are assigned are the exact same thing he goes over in class, but he includes more real life examples that are also usually on the tests (so just go to class). Lectures aren't bad and he's a nice guy. Doesn't take attendance.

My favorite professor at Penn State. Honestly so genuine and his examples are extremely helpful to understanding the information. His exams have a lot of material but the exams are no surprise, all of the notes from class. Definitely take for an easy, and interesting gen ed you will actually enjoy.

Good professor, knows his stuff. But exams are difficult. Have to know a lot of the same criteria for all different disorders. He's clear in his explanations, but it's just a lot of material that is very easily confused. But it's a very interesting class, just something to really apply yourself to.

Difficult written exams.  Had to know multiple disorders and all of the criteria and more in a short answer form. Had to read 200pg book and write 10pg paper amongst HWs and the massive amount of studying. Guidelines could be followed, but specific rubrics were given after assignments/exams were graded.
Easy- just make sure to memorize the outlines. I never used the textbook= all information that was tested was in the outlines. Just study the night before the test and you will be good

I did not use the textbook once- just study off the notes. You only need to come to class to do the occasional in class activities. If you just memorize the notes like two days before the test you will get an A
Best professor I've had. So nice, helps with anything and teaches the material to students in an interesting and manageable way. Amazing guy and the sweetest man. Take him!

Absolutely recommend taking psych 100 with Crosby. He puts chapter outlines online that go hand-in-hand with the textbook. Attendance is not mandatory but try not to skip every class because that's when he give out extra credit. Online quizzes, straight-forward exams, and ample opportunities to earn an A in this course,He can be funny sometimes too

Brian is a really great guy. He provides outlines for every chapter which you fill in during lecture, so you know exactly what he's looking for on the exams. No tricks. Clear and organized lectures and very approachable. Highly recommend

Lecture is not mandatory, but extra credit is sometimes given in-class. The lecture notes are given out online, and they follow the book to a tee. Don't buy the online notes. The book is a good replacement for lecture, but I found lecture to be really interesting. I would highly recommend taking Crosby and going to every class.

His class can be boring at times, but he provides you with really good notes. Make sure you go to lecture because he tests are based off of them. Also, you can earn a lot of extra credit points. Ultimately, he makes the class easy to understand and wants his students to do well.

Great teacher very engaging took him for child psychopathology. Uses fill in the blank power points. Sometimes gives extra credit so go to class!. Quizzes are based off of study guides which can be tricky but it was a great class .

I had a reasonably good experience with him in Psych 100. While he wasn't always the most inspiring lecturer, Dr. Crosby was very good at explaining the material and simplifying difficult-to-grasp concepts, in addition to having a thorough understanding of what he is talking about. As long as you display some effort, a decent grade can be attained.
Not a fan or psych, by Crosby made it interesting. He was always helpful to his students and gave plenty of opportunities for his students to get better grades.
Nice, calm, and explains everything. Very good teacher. Always answers any questions you may have and explains things very well. Good teacher to have!

Crosby is really great! He is so calm and easy to understand. He explains everything thoroughly and shows examples that make material easy to remember. He gives you guided notes and the material for exams is right off of them. Take Crosby for sure for any class! Great guy.

Professor Crosby always posts lecture outlines online prior to class, and follows them exactly, telling you what to put in each blank. He uses powerpoints that coincide with the book, which is really reader friendly. It is in your best interest to attend class so you can fill in the outlines. He keeps it interesting. Highly recommended!
Nice guy and keeps class interesting. Gives 15 "5 minute" papers in class and keeps the top ten. Tests could be somewhat challenging.

Great professor and you can definitely tell he knows his stuff because he explains everything in a lot of detail. He was VERY lenient with his grading scale since this is a hard class and exams were 85% of the final grade. I wish I had time to study for this class and go to his office hours because I definitely would've gotten a much better grade.

Cremer is a genuinely kind person, and he wants everyone to truly appreciate what he's teaching. He gets so into it, even though he might be a little dry. His lectures are mostly theoretical/derivations, so you'll NEED to do the problem sets and practice exams. Holds a lot of office hours. Really tough class but rewarding, and he's a great person.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Test heavy--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr Cremer was probably the best professor I've had at Penn State and taught my favorite class so far. He powered through a nosebleed during lecture like a boss. He was super engaging during lecture and especially in office hours, where he guided us through the problems instead of him just showing us. Seems like he has a genuine interest in thermo

He's good with what he explains however, he wasn't honest on what was on the final. He was a very tough grader. He told us to study the homework problems and the practice exams but then turned out to be not true. Try to avoid his class if you can since he is very tricky.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Favorite professor, so enthusiastic, makes you understand complex ideas you never thought you could. He is the best science professor I've had. Tons of math but it all clicks when he explains it. Had him for chem450. Awesome class.

Dr. Cremer is great. He's very enthusiastic and tries hard to make the material easy to understand. He's a little concept heavy; he wants you to really understand beyond solving for numbers. Read the book, go to lectures, do the hw! There is an unannounced quiz for each exam (drops one), but reading over notes is enough (not the exams though!)
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--BEWARE OF POP QUIZZES

reviews.comment: He really knows the material but lectures in such a boring pace. The class is hard, so it's imperative to pay attention, but it was so hard (at least for me) that I ended up falling asleep most of the time. I ended up going to another section with another professor.
Dr. Cremer was a great professor. His voice was kind of boring but he explained the material better than any other professor. Always had review lectures before exams that were really helpful.

Great lecturer, really understands the subject and has his lecture plans very well organized. Writes out most of his notes onto a projector so note taking is easy. It is a tough class so studying is absolutely necessary if you want a good grade

Cremer doesn't create the exams himself since this is a lecture hall. Cremer does his best to explain things, but he is more of a concept guy, not a "solve the problem" guy. He will explain the concepts, but won't do any math examples for you (the exams are mainly math). If you go to TA office hours, that should help you the most.

It's really not Dr. Cremer's fault that Chem 110 is awful, it is the course director, Mary Bojan's fault. The tests are difficult and meant to trick you, as are the weekly quizzes. The material isn't bad, and you can read OR go to class, choose one. Cremer's lectures are good if you don't understand what you read but he's a bit of a goof.

so the lecture and recitation section of chem 110 do not help at all for the exams or online quizzes(which suck as later on) that you have to take.  basically you teach yourself all the material through yahoo answers (this is true for all professors of chem 110) . The only way to do well on the exams is doing the given prac exams. effed in the a!

Although he is a good professor who is passionate, don't be fooled into thinking the exams are as straightforward.  You must delve deeper into the material than Cremer lectures in order to do well. I highly recommend as a Chem 110 professor.

I was a chem major (now physics) and thought this class was easy. Attendance of lecture is not mandatory except the recitation section. Because I learned these chem stuff before high school, the textbook is extremely useless for me. Exam was not difficult  if you know these concepts; I did perfect on one of the exams.

Cremer knows his stuff and is enthusiastic about teaching it. However, the tests are quite difficult (harder than many AP high school exam questions) and they try to trick you on most questions. Read in the book, do tons of practice problems, and go to review sessions and you should be ok.

Really great guy, keeps the class' attention. Explains things well, but you MUST keep up in the textbook and with homework and practice problems. Chem isn't easy, but he does a great job of breaking things down to make them easier to understand.

I didn't understand the structure of the class at the beginning, but later it made sense. The ability to resubmit essays is a huge help and she's easily available during her office hours which are very helpful.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: This professor is by far the most disorganized professor I have ever had. If this section was longer, I would write about how all she focuses are the negatives, and never highlights the good areas/improvements to be made. Only thing you'll hear from her is how you are not doing what she wants and to change it, but she won't tell you how or why!

The class is very structured and she genuinely wants students to succeed. If you are unhappy with the grade for an essay she gives the opportunity to fix the errors for a regrade. She starts every grade out with a C for the bare minimum and you increase the grade by going above. Participation definitely matters and a few questions go a long way.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: I did not have any problems with this professor in 202-C. Projects were pretty straightforward. She gave clear guidelines and let me revise my projects for a better grade. I found the job application project most helpful for resumes. Overall good experience.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: Professor Crowson was an amazing professor, I took her English 15 class during the summer and I personally thought she was great. Shes super nice and even offers essay revisions which I never expected. She has clear expectations for the essays, was a fair grader and always gave posotive  feedback. I would 100% recommend her as a professor!!
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Gives good feedback

reviews.comment: class was fun professor was cool.

Teaching assistant Crowson is unorganized and lacks professionalism. Yells, doesn't use textbook (even though we have to buy it), and misses schedule appointments with students. It's a mandatory class for my major but just know you can switch classes early in the semester and find a different teacher.

She is a great professor! You could even request to make changes to your essay if you aren't satisfied with your grade. Gives useful advice for changes when you ask too. Just do exactly what she says and you'll get an A.

She is horrible. She made us purchase an expensive textbook that we never used. If you ask her a question about a grade received, she will not tell you what you did wrong. She yells at students and does not let you use your phone in class. She says English 15 is the most important class you will take at Penn State... find another professor.

Professor Crowson is an amazing teacher. She's always willing to work with you regardless of how long it takes and loves getting the class involved in discussions. She's strict on grading (makes big fuss about word count) but is very transparent about what she looks for in our assignments, even giving us checklists to follow for each of our papers.
Professor Crowson is great! She can be a tough grader but always wants to help and will tell you exactly what to fix. Assignments are all easy if you pay attention and give minimal effort.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Participation matters--Graded by few things
