reviews.comment: Professor Crowson was an amazing professor! She was very clear about her guidelines and even allowed you to resubmit for full credit if you had small mistakes. Participation matters a lot as it's a small class but it's very easy to give your input. She gave us lots of room to choose for our 4 projects. Ask her for help and you'll be fine.

The class wasn't tough but, she is extremely disorganized. There is a good amount of homework. She doesn't explain topics and assignments well which becomes very frustrating. Following her lectures is difficult, she often loses her train of thought and she doesn't know how to teach it.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I loved Professor Crowson! She was so sweet and told you exactly what needed to be done. She is super friendly and keeps the classroom welcoming and super easy to talk to and ask questions. The workload is not bad at all and she tells you exactly what you need to do.

Really aren't sure what all the negatives reviews are referring to. All of them seem to indicate a problem with something that was either clearly discussed in class or outlined in the syllabus. Professor Crowson is a great teacher, is very easy to get a hold of, and will try her hardest to help you succeed. Show up to class and you will be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Professor Crowson is a great professor. She really likes to help her students and will always check in to make sure her student and their grade is ok. In addition, she is extremely kind and friendly and always willing to help. She wants her students to succeed and she made the English-15 understandable and manageable. Take English-15 with her.
No tests, but assignments have little communication and you figure it out on your own

Not a good instructor. Told me I needed to change my topic because it wasnt relevant to the course and then said that I used AI when I didnt. She missed two appointments and was not helpful when my family member was sick and I had to miss class.

Professor Crowson was a huge help to me. I struggled with some of the analyses parts of the course, but she was willing to meet with me and took her time to ensure that I was understanding how to do the assignments. I don't understand the other reviews because I never had a problem with her.

If you show up to class and pay attention, you will get a good grade. If you are not doing well, set up office-hour appointments. She will let you know how your work is and is very understanding of situations. Ask questions if you dont understand. She is super clear on what she is expecting and reiterates that on every new topic.

Professor Crowson is an amazing professor. She makes it clear from the beginning what she is expecting and tells us everything we need to do in order to get a good grade. She's understanding and the sweetest ever. Show up to class, pay attention, and participate. She never flakes on office hours!! If you have a choice, I 100% recommend her.

She was nice, but I got accused of using AI on a paper that I didn't use it on. She wasn't understanding when I tried to let her know that I didn't. I got As on everything but an F on that assignment so she tanked my grade from a straight A to a B. Very upsetting.

I have heard a lot of things about English 15 professors that made my peers dislike taking the class. Professor Crowson I am finding to be very enjoyable. Her lectures are easy to understand, she always makes time for students to recieve help and is a fair grader. She tells us exactly what she expects to see and reaches out to us often.

Dr. Craig is great! She clearly demonstrates the topics in a way that I, as a non-STEM major, can understand. She is very understanding when it comes to exam makeups. Loved her class so much I am taking her again for Bio 133.

Dr Craig is probably my favorite professor I've had in college. She does a really good job teaching exactly what is on the exams and uses real life examples to apply the concepts she is teaching, which makes the material more interesting. Always attend the lectures and complete the learning guides she provides before class.

Biology used to be my least favorite subject until I took her class. She prioritizes students understanding the material and does not fly through lectures. She is very funny and makes lectures fun to attend. I would recommend her over and over again!
Dr. Craig is amazing. Her lectures are entertaining and match the exams very well. She makes complex topics fun and easy to understand. She really does want her students to succeed.

I love Dr. Craig. Though BIO110 can be intimidating, she made this class much easier. She was helpful in preparing us for exams and made sure we understood every topic before we move on. Even though attendance isn't mandatory, GO TO CLASS. It makes everything SO MUCH easier. If you have the opportunity to take this course with her, do it.
great professor, and very knowledgeable. you just have to stay o ntop of this class and make sure to not fall behind. it is a very fairly graded class.
go to her office hours, make an impression
Makes the lectures fun and engaging as long as the students want to participate and answer the questions that are given.
I absolutely loved this professor. She made lectures interesting and fun.

Dr. Craig made biology so easy to understand. Make sure you attend lecture because she will tell you a lot of what you will see on the exam or hint at it. The learning guides were super helpful in preparing for exams as well.

The exams are not a reflection of lecture. I attended lecture everyday for the first 3 exams and would score in the 70s. When I stopped going I got As on both of the last 2 exams. Things are emphasized in class that won't be on the exam. Watch outside videos to grasp the concepts of the topic you are learning :)

Hands down, best professor I've had at Penn State. She is so caring and understanding and really wants her students to do well! Go to class and go to her office hours because it really does help and she is more than willing to! I would take a million other classes with her if I could. She also tells you exactly whats on the exam if you go to class.

Jenna Craig has been my favorite professor so far! Her lectures are very interesting, and she ensures everyone understands before moving on. She prepares you VERY well for exams by reviewing and creating study sheets in classes prior.

Great professor! This semester was her first time teaching biol133 and she was great. I'm not a science person but I was able to succeed because she made lectures interesting and engaging. Attendance isn't mandatory but strongly suggested because it really does help and sometimes she will randomly take attendance just to see who is showing up

AMAZING! This wasn't an option on here but I actually took her for BIO133. She really knows what shes talking about. Reviews for exams really well and will practically review straight from the exam questions. She explains things super in depth. I loved this class so much because of her. Never made me feel dumb and never had a complaint about her!

AMAZING Professor! If you go to class, you will do well in this class. She will stand in lecture with a copy of the exam in her hand and tell you all of the concepts you need to know. Definitely the best Bio 110 Professor. Super funny and easy to connect to. Very fair and helpful. Ta's were great also.

I honestly really struggled to understand bio but Dr. Craig helped SO much, she tells you exactly what you need to know on every exam. She was very helpful and nice during her office hours. so pls go to class and go to her office hours if you need help!!!!
Basically tells you what's on the exams, and the exams are questions you see on the learning guides, homework, and lecture prechecks. Very nice and funny prof too.

Honestly loved her lectures, she is very good at explaining the material simply but in depth. It you do the learning guides you WILL see those questions on the exams. I hope she teachers higher level bio class because I would definitely take her again. Lecture attendance isn't mandatory but GO! she gives helpful hints about exams.

She is so sweet and wants you to succeed. This is a tough course but she helps guide you to your success. There are review sessions that are pretty accurate to what the exam will look like. She is straight forward so if you attend lecture, listen, and study for the exams you will do well easily. Take her if you need to take bio 240W!!
i LOVED Dr. Craig. i would take her again in a heartbeat. super caring and gives lots of extra credit to make sure you receive a good grade
She was a really good teacher, you could tell that she cared about how well we were doing. On one of the exams, she gave everyone extra credit made my grade go up by 4 or 5 letter grade points.

Dr. Craig is the best professor I have ever taken. She is the most kind and empathetic person and has truly made an impact on my life. This professor is more than insightful/helpful and is eager to assist students in any way she can in and outside of the classroom. Words can't describe the extent of my appreciation for her, she is the absolute best

Amazing professor! Keeps the interest of students and has great learning activities. Overall the class is not hard and many grades are dropped (including one exam grade). Attendance is not mandatory, but exams will have material from class. Also, Dr.Craig has GREAT office hours!!!

8AM lectures are rough but she clearly cares about our success. All the course content, including lecture recordings, are posted online in case you oversleep one day. Lots of exams, but all the content is very simple. The class is very easy and you can easily get an A without attending class, if you wanted to.

Dr. Craig is the BEST professor I have every had. She made a huge impact on my life. I struggled in the beginning but once I talked to her she helped me learn ways to improve and believe in myself. Please go to class they are worth it. She cares for all of her students. Dr. Craig, if you are reading this, thank you for an amazing semester.

Dr. Craig is the professor to take for BIO 110!She is super helpful in class with making study guides for us (which other professors so not do). She also is great in office hours. I really think I had a huge advantage with exams just because I had her over other professors. She understands that we are humans and not robots. TAKE HER!!!

One of my favorite professors at Penn State! Shes very transparent on what the content is covering and provides zoom videos for thoso who cannot attend lecture. Overall, going to her office hours clearly tells how passionate and driven she is as a teacher and just an overall nice person. I highly recommend this class for a GENED!
She doesn't teach. It's all mainly pre-class work. This can be difficult when balancing between many classes, exams, and work.

Dr. Craig was easily one of my best professors so far, her lectures cover everything on the test. If you miss a couple of days she always has a review before the test along with study guides and worksheets that contain everything that will be on the test. The tests were very straight forward and a lot was just memorization. Go to class and ur good.

Her lectures were well written for the most part and the tests were what she prepares you for on the study guide. I loved the content of this class, however don't expect her to show you any grace when you genuinely are dealing with something outside of class and it interferes with your work.

She is very easy to understand. The workload isn't a lot but you do have to study a lot for the exams. There is also a little bit of extra credit that you can do for the course. I got a C in this class but I probably could've gotten a better grade myself which was sort of on me. She also has amazing study guides that help a lot for the exams.

Jenna Craig is an excellent, laidback, straightforward professor who cares about her students. Exams are very straightforward because she gives study guides with the same material. When exam scores are low, she will give extra credit. She is also lenient if you make one mistake and forget to submit one of the weekly quizzes. She has many resources.

Professor Craig was overall a great professor. She makes the exams very clear and straightforward forward and the lectures are interesting considering that it is an 8 am class. If you are taking BIOL 161 in the fall, I highly recommend taking her for this class. She also gives out study guides and study points a week before the exam.

She's a weird professor, every day she's in a different mood, and she likes to show it. This class was only given as a 8am lecture so I had to have an 8AM. If you're there on a day where no one is there, she'll let you in on things other people wouldn't know because they didn't show up, so go to class. Super easy bio, all freshman.

She was an amazing professor who clearly cared about her students succeeding. She would give extra credit when the test average was low and gave many hints for what would be on the test. The test were fairly easy if you went to lecture and paid attention. I would definitely take another class with her if I could.

My favorite professor ever!! She is caring, respectful, understanding, and on top of everything absolutely gorgeous! She was the only professor I genuinely liked and was excited to attend her lectures even though attendance wasn't mandatory. Loved her and wish I could take her class again!!!

i LOVE Dr. Craig. by far my fav professor. i have her 8am, and i have never missed class, even though she doesn't take attendance. she gives many extra credit options, and really cares about your grade. the homework load isn't bad, and the exams are easy bc on review days she tells you EXACTLY what you need to know

I love Dr. Craig so much! She is very interactive with her students. I have her at 8 am and she is always trying to make us talk and be lively at 8 am. She makes the class a lot better and takes the time to help draw strictures and diagrams that truly help when you study. She wants nothing, but for her students to succeed and it shows!

The best professor I have ever had! Even if you have to take an 8am with her, DO IT! She cares about each student and wants us to succeed. Go to her office hours so you can review what is in class. From someone who has no exposure to bio, I succeeded in her class and was very worried about it! TAKE HER CLASS!!!!

Dr. Craig is my favorite professor that I have had so far at PSU. Some of her exams can be tricky, but it is all taken directly from the class lectures and worksheets. There are many other assignments that can be used to maintain a good grade in the class aside from the exams. She is very down to earth and makes herself accessible outside of class.

Attendence is randomly taken throughout semester. Tophat is graded for participation as well. If you attend lecture, you will do fine on exams. Dr. Craig is my favorite professor at Penn State by far.

Dr. Craig is one of the nicest professors that I have had so far.  She genuinely cares about her students and wants them to succeed.  BIOL 110 has a lot of content, so it can be tricky.  However, she does an amazing job at making sure everything gets covered and will never move on if she feels like her students aren't getting it.

Very wonderful professor. He had a funny attitude and is always willing to answer questions. The work was very manageable just a few essays and his grading was very reasonable as well as his criteria.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Class was pretty easy but was pretty boring at times.  Shows a lot of movies.
Effective teaching method.  He expects you to learn, and rewards you for doing so.

You will not pass this class unless you are retaking it again or already took it in high school. The homework is just busy work and relates to nothing on the exams. I studied for hours, did all of the extra credit and homework to still fail the class. I fear reading off slides does'nt help anyone learn. For this hard of a class she SUCKS

Pretty easy class but you don't learn much. She emphasizes that the topics your learning don't matter for a grade but matter in real life (don't really matter for either). A respectable thing about her is she tells you exactly what is going to be on the exam and doesn't provide you too much busy work. Textbook is only required for hw not reading.
For this being an accounting course, she is probably one of your best options. The exams are hard but complete all of the other assignments to pass. Study and pay attention and you will be fine

Incredibly caring and will do anything to help you, but the classes tended to drone on. Lectures aren't the best but textbook auditing isn't the most exciting thing either. Tried to show real-life examples and cases which worked a bit better. Lots of homework that wasn't always connected to what we learned, but 60% of the grade was automatic 100s.
Difficult class but she really cares about her students succeeding. She does like to ramble about unnecessary things during class.

80% of the grade is exams, and there's weekly homework that takes at least an hour. Good extra credit opportunities, though, and she is super nice. Not the best lectures, but she is super energetic and helpful.
Great professor; willing to help you; flexible class and lab schedules
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: acctg is overall the hardest entrance to major course but def take prof curling for this class if available. energetic bubbly caring and gives us good advice and direction about the class and life. exams are very challenging but put in the time and effort you will make it. do extra credit as you go. friday labs are everything!!!!! love her

I found the class to be boring and a lot of work, but Professor Curling made it not as bad. Since their are lecture videos, the professor you having for Accounting 211 does not matter that much, but Curling is not a bad choice under any circumstance.

Professor Curling is amazing. Most complaints I see about her class are not applicable to her but more towards acc 211 in general. The class is going to be hard no matter who your professor is but she does a great job at making it as understandable and relating it to current events. The class is straightforward you just gotta put in the work

This is obviously a difficult class, but she genuinely is passionate and wants you to succeed. Getting a good grade is possible, but you have to put the time in. Definitely would recommend using practice sheets and sample exams to study.

i used to attend every lecture until i realized they weren't helping me because she was reading straight from the powerpoints on canvas and the book, so i learned everything through the online lectures. she is a super sweet person but i was not getting anything out of class. go to the ta labs. you have to put the work in to get the grade you want.

As a small honors class, she emphasized that she wanted to spend lots of time on our questions and interests. That worked great when you had a question, but not when someone else did and she spent 15 min on it. Have to use the textbook to learn the material, class doesn't do too much. She's nice and wants you to succeed, though. No tricks on exams.

She's a good ACCTG 211 teacher. The course is standardized so she doesn't have much freedom, but her lectures are helpful and interactive. I had her at 9:05 am, and she was always in a really good mood and high energy, which was nice to start the day. If you have her, you'll also have access to the recorded lectures by other 211 professors.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: She is a fun teacher that knows everything about accounting. She always motivates the class to try the hardest they can in life and Accounting 211. She offers a total of a 4% increase on your grade in simple extra credit homework. She is a great teacher and I recommend her.
Accounting can be difficult but Dr Curling did a great job. She cares so much about the success of her students. Ask for help and you will receive and suceed.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Caring--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Curling is a very passionate professor and explains the material well. there are tons of resources to help you succeed included exam reviews, TA labs, and practice exams. if you put in the time and effort you should do well. always do the extra credit because you get 4% added onto your grade for completing these and they help you understand better

The course itself is awful and boring, her teaching makes it worse, and the textbook is your best friend. Her practice exams are total and complete garbage because they look nothing like the exam. The homework is useless because it doesn't prepare you for the exam. Caring about this class is almost as hard as feeling confident in it.

Be prepared to learn absolutely nothing in lecture, because when the homework problems come, you will have nothing that will help you. The slides she makes and the book are not much help when it comes to the types of problems you are going to face in the homework. She tends to ramble a lot in class about things that don't even pertain to the course

Prof Curling is great. Her lectures are interesting and she seems like she really cares about her students. She is always available to answer any questions and wants to make sure you understand the material. Exams require thorough preparation but are not impossible. Recommend attending every class, especially exam review days, to best succeed.

Shelly is a nice, but this class lacked direction needed for students. In order to get a B you must put in a lot of work and study from the book problems for exams at least two weeks prior. Once again, Shelly is very approachable and goes to significant lengths for students to succeed. However, the content you are assessed on is unclear
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He barely teaches anything, every class he just rushes through his abstract PowerPoint slides.

worst experience ive ever had with a professor. he waited all semester to grade all of our assignments, so every student is sitting here one week after finals still without knowing their final grades. he doesnt respond to emails, either. speaking of the final, it was the worst test ive ever seen, and everyone bombed it because he doesnt teach. yay!

its so interesting how a required course for all comp eng majors, and arguably the hardest undergrad class for this major, is taught by someone that cant even teach properly. i havent learned a singular thing during this course. absolutely horrible experience.
Worst professor i've ever had. His lectures are unlearnable and the homeworks are 50x harder than anything you go over in class. why can't penn state just hire a good engineering professor for once?

Okay. He's ridiculously smart. But dude CANNOT teach a class. He speedruns through the notes, allowing zero time for comprehension, and forget about taking notes during class. You're better off learning from youtube. He also doesn't grade anything until the very end, pretty much leaving you in the dark on whether you're passing until it's too late.

Every class rush through lots of material, mostly just repeating what's on the slides. There aren't many examples; it's mostly about concepts. I did not learn much even after the whole semester, I still have to teach myself. The only good thing is easy grading. You still can still get a decent grade (B or B+), if you did really bad on the test.

Professor lacks the ability to teach meaningfully. 50 minutes of monotone slide reading on the most irrelevant details about signals and systems and is unable to answer any questions. It's pretty obvious that he uses a generous grading scale to make up for his lack of ability to teach this subject. Absolutely do not take him if you have a choice.

Just a meh professor. Hardly attended lecture because they were impossible to learn from. He just reads off his slides and teaches concepts very abstractly. Only way to learn is by doing homework, but you just have to figure out how to do it yourself. However, he is very lenient with grading. Homeworks are always 100%, and there's test corrections.
Awful...just awful, smart professor but unfortunately can't teach the subject.
Teaches with proofs that are extremely hard to follow. This makes simple concepts so much more confusing. Not sure why we choses to teach this way.
He is a good professor.

Like a lot of other reviews are saying for some of the other classes hes taught, he seldom uses examples, mainly just introducing the topics then showing some proofs for it and moving on. He's also a very slow grader. But he was also very lenient with with grading it was pretty much impossible to fail unless you did absolutely nothing.

Has a nice voice. 
Other than that, he is very hard to learn from. Struggled so hard in this class. Went to office hours but it didn't help much because he only speaks math.
Had about 7 HWs and 7 Canvas quizzes. They were both difficult and he didn't grade the HW.
Exams were extremely difficult. Had to rely on exam retakes and a stats phd friend.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: I hate to say it, but Professor Cullina is the worst professor at PSU. The professor rarely graded assignments. Avgs on exams ranged between 30-40%. The professor would regularly wait weeks to grade these despite small class. He allowed exam corrections but did not until finals week. Overall, this was the worst classes I have taken.

Reading the text book is much more easy than understanding what he talked in the class. Homework has no relationship with the class. It takes a lot of time to do it. But professor didn't even grade it. Practice exam cannot give any advice of the exam. The hints of the problem is never clear. Even the questions in the final has changed sveral times!

Absolutely awful class. Worst class I've ever taken. Gave 7 homeworks and didn't even grade them. Those homeworks were an absolute nightmare. He honestly doesn't know how to teach. He would never complete his sentences in class - This happens because. So the next topic is this. Didn't understand even a single thing after the first week. Avoid him!

I have never been so confused in my 4 years of school. Majority of the homework was stuff that we couldn't even find in our notes. We didn't get our first exam grades back until days after our second exam. He teaches all theory with basically no examples. He also rarely responded to emails asking for help. AVOID HIM IF YOU CAN!
reviews.rating_tags: Graded by few things--Test heavy--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Just a few weeks in and I'm thinking about dropping the course. In office hours his attempts to help students are generally more confusing than the questions he is trying to help with. So far it has almost been completely review from EE 350 which I did very well in and I feel like there is no way I'm going to do well on the first exam.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Here I sit, so weak and weary, Drowning in my tears so dreary. Our first exam will be next week, The topics covered, truly mystique. I simply cannot understand, how Daniel wound up in EE land. "But what", you ask, "is Daniel's tone?" I answer back, "A robotic drone." If you like numbers, don't take this class. Stay in 350, you'll probably pass.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: WORST TEACHER EVER. He exclusively teaches through proofs and he does not understand how to answer anything if it has a number in it. This guy loves his proofs and theory, but it is not the right way to teach. Also, he is not a chill dude either. He is very bland and lacks emotions or care. Pretty sure he was made in a lab somewhere in the desert.

Absolutely the worst teacher ever. It is meant to be a computational communications course, yet somehow we have never seen a number half way through the semester. Dude is a legit robot and has no idea how to teach. He is a glorified stat professor and miraculously the homework solutions make less sense than the homework itself. DO NOT TAKE HIM!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Teaches with very analytical explanations with little to no examples. The homeworks are only a couple of questions but you're expected to use material that he hasn't taught yet and the textbook is little to no help. This man seems to be just as confused as everyone else.

The man only teaches in theoretical terms with little to no examples. The book he selected also had no numerical examples so you couldn't even use that. Homework is only 4 or 5 questions but you will spend hours trying to figure out what it even is. By far the worst EE prof I've had.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment:
This class gets extremely complicated really fast w/ lots of equations and concepts you have to tie together. 

It requires a lot of focus & in-person lectures get confusing often, but he does record & post lectures & updated lecture notes (esp if he misses something), so use those constantly & focus on building skills (don't focus on being right).
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Wasn't my teacher but he posts his notes and lectures to the merged canvas page. Way easier to just watch those than even go to class/your actual section, and he will prepare you well for hw and exams. Seems super approachable and knows his stuff for upper level classes.

Honestly, for such a hard class, he made it a lot easier. His lectures are in depth and really helpful. He takes you step by step through multiple kinds of problems and gives you so many resources to do well on the exams. He also posts all of his lectures and notes from class which is amazing

This is a really hard class, but Joe is pretty good. He explains things really well in class and records and posts organized notes after. Homework is hard, but TAs are good at helping. Exams were really difficult and not rlly like practice exams. Apparently Gary Gray is better, but I though Joe was nice and funny. Lectures aren't horrible at all.

This class is super difficult no matter who you have. Prof C is very nice and smart, and knows how hard his course is. Homework is hard but all on Chegg. Exams are difficult but partial credit saves your grade. Write down what you know and try your best and he will help you out credit wise. Do all hw + attend review sessions and you'll be okay.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: He is not the best teacher for this class. Gary Gray is. Joe and others get their notes that they teach from Gary Gray who wrote the textbook and the best teacher. Joe rewrites what he is given, gives boring cutthroat lectures and is somewhat very critical of students, which can be humorous or quite condescending. Do the hw. Study-Go to Gray's
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: He is a pretty good teacher if you go to class and pay attention. No attendance and the homework solutions are easily available, so people tend to skip class and never catch up because they just copy down the HW problems and then they fail the tests. It is really not that bad, especially if you pay attention and/or don't cheat the HW. Nice guy.

literally, the worst EMCH teacher ever! I'm not calling him a bad teacher because he is not, but he is bad for teaching EMCH 212.  Let me summarize his lecture time distributed, 10 mins copying down the problem to the board, 5 mins setting up the equations(EMCH), 25 mins doing algebra(math), 10mins teaching emch. 15 mins of emch for 50 mins

"The universe doesn't care about you.  It's way bigger than you and you could never learn everything there is."  It was after this brilliant and poetically delivered insight that I realized how much of an influence this class on advanced dynamics would soon be on my life.  There was not a week in which less than 80% of my hours were spent on hw.

Dr. Cusumano is great. Besides being funny and extrovert he is super smart and really knows in depth what he is talking about. He is very clear and tries to make you understand the mathematics with perfect examples. His homework are pretty hard and time consuming but you learn a lot doing them. He is pretty slow correcting them also.
Cusumano is awesome. I loved going to class. He taught us the theory and then did examples like crazy. So helpful and I got a lot out of the class.
Dr. Cusumano rocks. If you have a chance to take him do it he's super clear and does a lot of helpful examples in class.
Really knows how to explain the material in a way that's easy to understand. If you pay attention to his examples, you'll be prepared for the exams. Highly recommended.
Dr. Cusumano really knows his stuff. May need to ask him to dumb things down for you at times, but he's pretty good.

If you have to take dynamics then take it with cusamano for sure. Hes a real nice guy and he always gives you a good idea of what will be on the tests. If you put effort into the class it definitely wont be as hard as people say

I liked Cusumano. He was very straight forward. Taught material and did problems. I found his lectures very clear. if you go to lecture you can do the homeworks, and if you can do the homework you can do the tests. my only complaint is the homework was worth too much of the overall grade

Lectures consist of him working problems from the book. His explanations are sub-par at best. You will have to learn a lot on your own for this course regardless of your prof, but if you like to ask questions in lecture, DO NOT PICK CUSUMANO. He HATES when you ask questions and will attempt to belittle you. Has clear handwriting on the board tho...

This class is extremely hard, and he makes it more difficult by not grading the homework?s because there is no motivation to do them. The quizzes are based on the hws, and the tests were ridiculous. Some people liked him, but I didn?t.

The class really doesn't deserve it's "extremely hard" rep.  In fact it's the same three methods taught in different reference frames.  Cusumano was a great prof, and I learned a lot from the maybe 3 quarters of classes I went to.  I recommend Cus greatly!

Great prof. Don't listen to the people who hate him... they probably just got a bad grade becuase the material is very difficult. However, I don't think anyone could have taught this subject better than Cusumano, he is the best.. and probably one of the best prof's I have had thus far at psu. Very helpful in office hours too.
He is there to help and does do alot of examples in class but that really doesn't make dynamics any easier.  He is sort of arogant and absolutely isn't going to round your grade or give you a break.

Competent Teacher.  Available after class.  No free ride, glad to say--you will get your money's worth.  As a person,though arrogant--more or less just another one of these genius-AH types.  I'm bored with 'em.  They act like 99% of the world isn't worth their precious time, but honestly they achieve little of deep value.

I thought his lectures were very clear, he works out examples very thoroughly. Maybe other people had more trouble with the class, but for me his explanations made the topics, which are incredibly difficult, seem very simple.
AWFUL!
subject material is very hard but he is very good at explaining/helping

Prof. Smith's class is interesting. He lectures for a few classes, and then you'll have an exam. The exam questions are exactly what he talks about in class plus some extra stuff from the assigned chapters so you'll need to take a lot of notes of both the lectures and the textbook. The textbooks are also affordable. Overall, not bad.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Do NOT take this course. For a level 1 gen ed course it ended up being my most challenging class and worst grade. Prof. Smith sits at the front of the room while drinking tea and talks for the entire class period. Lectures are so boring and you need to write down absolutely everything he says because the exam questions are so specific and difficult
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Professor Curtis Smith's class is well-structured and engaging, with his custom book providing clear guidance. Staying organized is essential, he helps with that. He uses analogies to simplify tough concepts and creates an inclusive environment. Follow the syllabus, attend class, and prepare for exams to succeed. It is all what you do.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Do not take take this class. You are only graded on 5 exams... that's it. His exam questions are so complex. His lecture he just sits at the front and talks the whole time. Exams are held in Pollock as well. Doesn't take attendance but if you miss a class then you miss like 15% of exam questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Be ready for quizzes every week and assignments that do not have clear due dates.

Took as an online class, each lecture he posts is upwards of an hour long and he talks incredibly slow. No final, but weekly quizzes that are 60 points and unnecessarily hard. Write down every single thing that comes out of his mouth because his questions are way too specific to lecture.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Interesting class and he teaches well but make sure you attend every class. I missed out on 2 classes before the Quiz 1 and got a C despite studying for it since the questions were insanely specific to his lectures. Make sure you note down every word that comes out of his mouth from the very start and you should easily manage anything above an A-
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: I wouldn't have taken this class if I had known what it would be like throughout the semester. At first, I was interested in learning about different religions of the world, but it's unbearable sitting through his lectures and studying for his exams. The exams are so detailed and class averages are never good. So happy this class is finally over.

Smith is definitely old-school, didn't use canvas or powerpoints for lectures, just sat there with a cup of tea and talked for an hour. BUT if you show up and take notes word-for-word, the class is super easy. You're graded only on 5 exams which are word-for-word from his lectures. Very simple topics and ideas. Easy A for me.
His lecture is boring and I would not take this class again. The materials are quit boring most of it talking about Buddhism.

Professor Smith is an amazing professor, and knows what he is talking about. He is old school with chalk writings, and lecture base classes. Was a good gen-ed to learn new things about religions. His lectures are important because that is what the tests are based off of. No homework assignments, just the tests, and readings.I definitely recommend!

There were weekly readings and tests that made up this class, along with a lecture video. I really enjoyed everything. I learned a lot, but it wasnt the easiest gened simply because of the dense readings.

Dr. Smith is old school/lecture heavy, but if you find religion even slightly interesting and you take decent notes, it's not much work beyond class. He'll have you spend about $20 in textbooks and the only grades he gives out are the 5 exams, one for each religion. Also, you can't skip a single class or you probably won't know 5-10 test questions.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: NOT AN EASY A. Dr. Smith is an oldschool professor; dense lectures, hard exams, and no opportunity for subjectivity in grading. He's intense but he has to be to fit so much information into one class. You will learn more than you expected to, as long as you come to class. If you don't, you won't pass. His chalkboard drawings are freaking rad.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--Tests are tough

reviews.comment: Only take if you have serious interest in religion, he knows his stuff but is insanely boring, dry and makes you want to fall asleep. You have to go to class, the tests are primarily class notes and examples he used in class. Tests are difficult and require a ton of studying notes as well as reading the book. NOT AN EASY GEN ED
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Professor Smith is great! In order to pass, you cannot skip lecture. Most of the exams are based on lecture with about 10 questions from the texts. As long as you attend lecture and study, it's totally an Easy A. Very interesting class as well. Religion is only studied, not practiced so you do not have to be religious to take it. Totally recommend!
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Great Professor.

interesting professor. Hes a nice guy and knows a lot about graphic design. Hes a great teacher and he'll tell you what to change on your project if you ask. Kind of strange sense of humor but overall a good teacher.
Easy class, do the work on time and take the quizzes when you're supposed to.  Easy 'A'.

Take this class if you already know what you're doing and it's a free A.  Even if you don't it should be easy.  Basically if you just actually try you'll do well, and it doesn't require a lot of effort.
Keith is a very good professor.  It is very easy to get an A if you read the online material and read the novel.  He is also very helpful
Very easy class just make sure you do all of the readings otherwise you will not do very good...Keith is a cool guy though
well it's been over 2 weeks since class ended and we still haven't gotten our grades. he does not respond to e-mails or really care. the class is easy, but he's not very helpful.
keith is the shizzy
I really liked Keith at first but my opinion has dramatically diminished.  He embarrasses his students in class and gives the most confusing comments to students.  Not helpful at all either.
He's a super nice guy. Its hard to get an A, but a B is pretty easy, and worse then a C is hard.

Keith is the man, doesnt have a care in the world. He's great to take if your taking another class with kristin or lanny, because the work load is not bad at all. Just give effort because he tends to be a hard but fair grader. Best quote: "I like it but I don't think its working." - Keith
Keith is a nice guy, tough grader, but fair.

He is an excellent teacher with genuine ability.  I think he is very talented and tries to envoke that in students. The person that complained about him is obviously a bitter no-talent and needs to change majors (and still fail miserably!)
He's the fly!!! He's the best!!! The most helpful prof at PSU!!! He ROCKS!
Very helpful.  The best graphic design prof. at PSU!!!
No Comments

Although he's clear in explanations, he's unprofessional and unhelpful.  He has often commented on how much he does not like a design, but does not offer suggestions to improve on it. He also lacks some knowledge in simple aspects of the subject area.
Very true. Only good design teacher in the department.  Helpful, professional, talented. A+
Funny, nice, helpful... but hard on grading. Only decent graphic arts prof @ PSU

One of the most unorganized and pointless classes I have taken at Penn State. She does not teach during class just goes off on tangents. Her tests are not at all what you cover in class, half the time I was just guessing based on stereotypes. Her exam breakdowns are inaccurate and she is extremely unhelpful if you reach out to her.
Worst nursing class I have taken. Exam questions were wordy and on material not covered in class. Lecture never goes the full class time but then exams are tough.
reviews.rating_tags: So many papers--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Very easy professor. All you need to do for this course is a weekly discussion post, a few tests (which she lets you use external resources for), a video presentation, and a final paper. She seemed like an easy grader and gave extra points for all the tests after grading them. Definitely a pleasant surprise after reading a lot of the other reviews.

Not only a terrible professor, a terrible person. No empathy for nurses working full time during a pandemic. Unprofessional manner when it comes to emails, tests have several spelling and grammar errors. Has rubrics, however, expects you to do things not listed on rubric. Extremely rude and disrespectful.

I took this class through World Campus, all online.  Professor Cutezo is very timely in responding and grading.  She gives a lot of assignments and a large community assessment project.  Be ready to work.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK

reviews.comment: Beth was interesting to say the least. In lecture she can be politically incorrect which is a little jarring in a major based on empathy. Her tests are all over the place so they're very difficult to study for. Always bring the workbook, even though the content is all over the place, she uses it all the time. Good luck, and get on her good side.

You would think senior year would be easy, laid back, and the staff be willing to help. Not the case! The exams contain random questions from material not covered and are in a poor format. Make sure you follow the rules and act professional because she isn't laid back when it comes to the handbook. She seems friendly at first but not there for you.

Beth is a stickler when it comes to the rules. Make sure you do not break any. She lives by the student handbook. She probably will mess up your schedule with clinical Makes community nursing almost unbearable. She is all over the place with lectures. She has failed seniors BEWARE. Take fall semester or take in Hershey with a different instructor.

Second semester senior year, things should be winding down- not the case with her exams.  She made them as hard as she could on purpose, just to trick us.  She did not cover many of the questions on exams in class, even though she tells us not to buy the textbook.  Don't get me wrong--clinical was fun! (Don't have to get up as early), just exams..

You would think that community is a joke right? Wait til you take her tests. Completely random, some questions are so ridiculous, that you think she'll give you points back, not the case. BE WARE her tests are much harder than they seem. STUDY EVERYTHING, especially the book, she lies when she says you don't even need it..

-really laid back teaching style...to the point you assume her exams will be just as chill. (They're not) Nice lady, but doesn't adequately cover material. Also, surprisingly politically incorrect esp. considering the subject matter.

Beth is Awesome. She has a Great personality and is one of the most laid back people I have met! She's always willing to help. She good at making things interesting too! One of the Best professors I've came across at PSU!

Best nursing teacher so far, so laid back, nice, and generally interesting. Very helpful and seems to never get stressed at all. She has all these traits and she's extremely knowledgeable about Nursing. LOVE her! After you take her you'll definitely be looking for any clinical or other classes she teaches. She's the best out there!!!

Beth is an amazing clinical teacher! She is so laid back and easy going. She has a great sense of humor and is always happy and loves what she does. I never feel uncomfortable talking to her or asking questions. She is the best clinical teacher I've had and has been my favorite teacher all through the Nursing Program.
Very easy class, just learning to golf.
Incredible guy and he makes it so that you learn a lot (coming from an absolute beginner golf) but also have a great time while getting an A if you put in basic effort. Highly recommend.

Absolute beast. Does a great job as a professor and would definitely recommend anyone to take this class. Been golfing for 3 years, but I still learned a lot from the class. Also great practice for anyone wanting to get better at putting/chipping.
Humorous and tolerant
Very nice
Great professor. So nice and the final exam is free-score. You can find answer for all question through the pervious quizs.

Garret is very knowledgable on the sport of golf and also happens to be super chill and very approachable. His class is meant only to help you get better at golf and not to stress you out academically or make your life harder. Regardless of your skill level, you stand to learn something from this class and will definitely enjoy it.

Garrett is a super chill and down to earth guy who happens to also be an expert golfer. His class is a lot of fun and also very helpful if you are a beginner (don't even need to have clubs). Even if you are experienced, this is still a refreshing class and you stand to learn something.

There wasn't a class where I didn't have fun. Nothing better than learning how to play golf by playing games and having a fun/chill teacher like Garret. He always gave students advice on how to get better and was always a positive.If you have the opportunity to take his class, take it. Everyone is should get an A if you come to class. He's the goat

Lots of writing with very limited involvement and late feedback. I can think of many ways to teach this material in a way that is more engaging and interactive - until then, I can't recommend taking this course online.

Truly one of the best professors at Penn State! So beyond caring and inspirational! She truly knows how to teach and keep her students engaged in class. So so happy I was able to take 202B with her. If you have the option to, pleaseee do!

I took 137H with Cynthia and loved her personality. It was definitely a little challenging as her instructions are a bit unclear but as long as you ask enough questions to her in person or zoom, you're set. There is a lot of writing and blog assignments but asking her questions and meeting with her will ensure you have enough support to get an A.

TAKE ENGL 137H and 138T with mazzant. Very little work is required as long as you show up to class and show some effort during class. There are only 5 assignments a semester that are confusing if you do not meet with her one on one. She is impossible to reach outside of class so be sure to ask any questions in class.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Group projects--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT let the bad reviews fool you; Cynthia is the BEST professor for 137/138. Her assignments can be tricky to understand, but she will help you if you ask (that is the trick). Show up, ask questions, and ask to schedule office hours for big projects. If you engage with her and pay attention in class, you'll do great. Participation = an A.

Probably one of the best professors I've had a Penn State. Awesome lady. Class was always fun and the assignments were fun and doable. She was very understanding and easy going. If you have the opportunity take her, take her!!!!!

She was kind but there was not much communication, she did grant me an extension when I asked though. There are a TON of peer reviews, as well as 5 major projects throughout the year. The whole class leads up to a grant proposal on the topic of your choosing. It's a lot of writing, but it is an English class. Also not the quickest grader.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--So many papers--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Cynthia is incredibly kind and understanding, yet somewhat disorganized. She would jump from topic to topic during lectures and grades things so slowly. She is very flexible with students and is seriously a sweetheart - but don't take this class with her unless you want to do an incredible amount of work for an English class. So much work!!

Cynthia is not a bad professor by any means... she just expects A LOT. She's very charismatic and personable which kept the 75 minutes upbeat. I can see why some people might give her a low rating since she asks so much for one class, but she was not a bad professor by any means! Take her if you think you can handle to work load.

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS (with Cynthia) IF YOU DON'T ABSOLUTELY HAVE TO. I wanted to drop out every time I walked into the class. Cynthia is a sweetheart but will make you question everything as soon as you leave those walls. Very unclear assignment descriptions. Expect things to change a LOT last minute. No one knows what's going on (TA INCLUDED).

Mazzant is a great person, but a not-so-good professor. Instructions are always confusing and she can be incredibly vague with answers. Please don't hope for clear expections on any assignment, more often than not I just winged my assignments because she never provided a grading scale, rubric, or guidance.

This class is the only one here at Penn State that I actually did well in. She is an amazing teacher that actually cares about her students. She is an easy grader, and everything she does in class will help you later with assignments.

Cynthia is the best. As long as you come to class and ask questions you will get an A. She is really accommodating and helpful with projects, and the projects are things you will be able to apply to your future career.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Group projects

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER CLASS IF YOU HAVE THE CHOICE. She is one of the most unhelpful profs I've had here. I like her as a person, but she doesn't have great organization skills and does not provide clear directions at all. My entire class struggles to understand anything she assigns us. I went out of my way to get another prof for sem2

Cynthia is super fun and a little chaotic to work with, but I liked it. This specific class is extremely writing heavy and you will need to attend class to do well. There is a textbook that we're supposed to read on our own time, but I haven't read any of it and am doing ok. If you go to class and participate she's lenient with due dates.

Cynthia does not explain a single assignment. You will be left in the dark for most of the semester. She hardly ever answers emails and when you ask for help or more specific directions she is not helpful at all. She also does not spread out the class and assignments very well compared to other 137h profs.

Do not take this class with Cynthia. While she can be a pleasant person, her teaching style is disorganized and cluttered making it very difficult to do well. She takes multiple days to respond to emails, provides very confusing feedback, and rarely provides clear directions on projects, if any direction is provided at all. Take any other teacher.

Mazzant is - at least for 202B - disorganized, unclear about grading criteria/expectations, and difficult to reach via email. There's a lot of random assignments which seem like pointless busy work - not conducive to learning. More of a facilitator than a teacher. Only reason she's tolerable is because she's not a hard grader. Lots of assignments!
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Group projects--So many papers

reviews.comment: Cynthia's a really interesting person and will constantly keep you captivated by sharing anecdotes throughout class. As a professor, she's a bit unorganized and all over the place, but ultimately, she will provide tangible, helpful feedback on projects and papers. Do the revisions for grade boosts and take assignments seriously.

Professor Mazzant was alright, just a bit confusing when discussing assignments. Before I got my first few assignments back, I had no clue if I bombed them or did well. Despite her vagueness, she wasn't a tough grader. She is kind and funny, but just really leaves you up to your own devices for about everything.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've had at PSU. Doesn't know how to teach and doesn't make the grading/ assignments clear at all. She gives pointless assignments that won't be graded later. The whole class did not like her as she never fully explained any of her spontaneous assignments. Easy grader though. Do not take her.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: She is literally the WORST professor I have ever had! She has No idea how to be person. She is not a teacher she was a drama major... why does she teach teachers.. NO ONE KNOWS!!! Never take her in your life, you will regret it tremendously. As a class we have reported her twice. Please for your own sanity do not that Cynthia Maria Mazzant!!!!!

This is the worst professor I have ever had at Penn State. She is literally horrible. I have no other words than never take her ever. You will regret 1 week in. She is an english teacher and refuses to give us rubrics or anything type of direction. She speaks over zoom and them expects us to write everything down when she talks so fast. THE WORST

Cynthia is well-versed in rhetoric and civics, and has a background and experiences which make her well-suited for the position. However, this is definitely the hardest of the honors English classes, and unnecessarily so. To succeed, you will have to redo most if not all material. Just take another teacher, and save yourself a lot of stress!
reviews.rating_tags: Accessible outside class--So many papers--Tough grader

reviews.comment: A lot of peer reviews, does not use a real textbook, assignments were unclear, and upon reaching out for help it was painfully obvious from the short and condescending answers, she is too busy to help. I have always done well in all my English and writing courses and I didn't have this much trouble in 400 and 500 level classes.
Not necessarily a difficult class but there is constantly assignments and work. Grading is not great, not super clear and takes just about the whole semester to grade anything.

I had her for my online class and she was a little unorganized. The assignments do not get graded within a week of submission, you won't know if you are passing until is three weeks pass the submission of your papers ... which is not good. Overall she is a good teacher and gives great feedback.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Get ready to read

reviews.comment: Cynthia is an awesome person, but just an okay professor due to the lack of clarity in her assignments and grading. She is extremely helpful when meeting outside of class, and she also offers quite a bit of extra credit (can boost final grade by just over 1%).

She talks a lot and expects you to remember everything. Her grading criteria is not clear and her schedule is not updated so you need to ask her about everything. However very understanding and flexible. I suggest you visit her office hours to get help and make sure you know someone else in the class to text when you need help outside of class.

Cynthia runs the hardest of the RCL classes, without a doubt. If you want an A you will have to WORK for it. But if you stick with it then you'll come out the other side a far better writer than you came in. She can seem intimidating in class but she's much more inviting and helpful if you see her during office hours.

RCL is not a fun class no matter who you take it with, however Cynthia always seemed to be giving the most work and making it the most confusing out of any of the other professors. She made it a much more stressful class than it needed to be and it was miserable. If you stick with her for second semester it's not as bad, she gets a little nicer.

She is very unclear as to how she wants your papers and homework done but to top it off she is an extremely hard grader! My average for any english I have ever taken is a 94-96%, with her I passed with a C barely. Very disappointed and wouldn't recommend her for this class or any online class.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Participation really does matter. If you actively engage and try your best it does NOT go unnoticed by her. I would love to have another class with her.

She can be confusing with what she wants you to do at times, but is EXTREMELY patient when you're asking her a billion questions for clarity. She is the kind of teacher you WANT to impress, and I respect her and am very fond of her! She grades tough only when she knows you didn't put your full effort in, and is an awesome teacher to have.

Professor Mazzant is a bit eccentric but a decent professor. Her grading criteria is a bit convoluted at times and it can be difficult to know exactly what she is looking for in a paper. Overall, its a fairly easy course if you go to class and participate in the group projects.

Assignments are often ambiguous and there's a lot of homework. Form a group me for the class and you'll figure it all out together. Makes you work hard to revise your work so try to do a good job your first time. She got a little more lenient in terms of grading towards the end of the semester when assignments were worth more points.

The biggest problem is the lack of instruction. She is irritated when you don't have what she wanted in your paper, but doesn't describe how the paper should be written until the day after it's due. You will have much more papers than other Engl202 professors, AVOID!
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--SO MANY PAPERS

reviews.comment: Online class. Pretty straight forward. DOES NOT RESPOND to emails. Most of my classmates and I traded several emails about our frustration. She did not respond to ANYONE! Doesn't give any feedback on drafts, only final papers. You have 3, 90 points, and then have lots of weekly assignments that she only gives 1 point for, and you need this points.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough Grader--Participation matters--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Definitely amazing lecturer, as long as you remain engaged in classes and do your work she really does not care that much about something else. Good chattering friend as well if you need one!
Good teacher, but may seem like she gives more work than all the other 137 profs. Make sure you actually do what she says.. (feedback-wise).

Prof. Mazzant is awesome. No exams, just 3 projects throughout the course, that you get to customize towards your own interests; its a writing course, and each of the projects is geared toward fiction, non-fiction, and poetry, but you get to write whatever you want within that genre. Weekly forums and workshops (EASY!) Very laid back course!! Fun!

Her class was very engaging, and she gives you almost complete independence while choosing your essay/project topics, while still giving great feedback. My only complaint is that she's not always completely clear with project expectations, but she's extremely helpful if you meet individually.

The most work I've had in any college course. I took honors English and wrote less. I'm not sure how other eng202a classes work but the bulk of the work is due tuesday, then some thursday, then some Sunday. With this class, you have to work at it every day. Takes as much time as all my other 4 classes combined. Can't find the time and regret taking

She's super confusing when she assigns something but its ok because everyone is confused and everyone somehow figures it out. Turned out she assigned so much more work for our class than any of the other sections but ended with a good grade. Also she seems to arbitrarily give out (usually good) grades so make a good impression.

Cynthia takes RCL very seriously in comparison to other teachers. However, if you  are willing to put in the work, you will come out of the class a better writer. Only real downside is that she is often ambiguous with her expectations for assignments.

Cynthia without a doubt takes RCL more seriously than every other professor. She assigns more work than anyone else, but in all honesty is probably the only professor that teaches the class correctly. I felt like I was actually learning and applying myself in her class. Always bring rough drafts for feedback from her and do EVERYTHING she says.

Course is unorganized and assignments are extremely ambiguous. She is a very subjective grader (wants you to do things her way only) but often lets you redo assignments for a better grade. She's a good person and as long as you show up to class, participate, and put some work in, you'll get an A. Ask for feedback on rough drafts to avoid the redo.
Cynthia is really funny and nice! As long as you do the work, and go to see her after class, you will get a good grade.

She can be extremely unclear of her expectations for assignments in class, but the key to success in this class is to meet with her outside of class prior to a due date and go over your paper with her (like how it's structured). I started off with a B-, and after doing this, ended up with an A-. She's also funny and personable, get to know her!

Wow, this was terrible. Cynthia was rude to students who didn't do things how SHE wanted them, taught us how to do assignments AFTER they were due, was completely disorganized about assignments, and required WAY too much work for a gen ed. I implore you not to take
She is the besttttt :))

Cynthia definitely made the most of a poorly-structured course. All the assignments were done in the community, so it felt like we were taking knowledge outside the classroom. She is always available for office hours or appointments if you need help. Put in effort, and you will be fine. Take Cynthia; she's the best RCL lecturer!!

Cynthia is quite a character. She is great because she lets you redo assignments to improve them and your grade. Take advantage of her office hours and show up to class most of the time and you will be fine. All she cares about is that you take the assignments seriously and put your best effort in.

she was really nice and personable but she was terrible at explaining her assignments and what she expected, also her class was a lot of video/film projects that took a lot of time to complete, that final blog was also annoying because the assignments were useless and also not clearly explained
Lacks clarity for assignment due dates but quickly adjusts to accomodate the students' needs.  Cynthia is my life.

Cynthia is an awesome teacher, and, if you like the subject she teaches, an awesome teacher. That being said, she does a really poor job explaining her assignments before your first crack at it, but she lets you try and try again until you put forth what you feel is a good finished product. If you want to be challenged and learn, take her class!

She is super nice! The work load was quite a lot but she gives you a lot of time to do the work. Go to her office hours! I did and I changed my grade from a B- to an A-!!!!! She let me redo some of my work to boost my grade! Participate in class too, you get points and ask for help, shows her that you're trying!
AWFULLLL !!! just dropped her class! so disorganized assigns things that day and due the next class. Shes horrible !

I do not understand why Cynthia has gotten bad comments... those students obviously did not use office hours.  She was SO helpful with all the papers we did. Hard class, but if you go and put time into it, you'll get a good grade. Made professional blog and taught for real life experiences.  Great Class! So glad I took it!

I wouldn't take this course. Unlike other professors, she requires her students to keep an online blog, which is very time consuming, and she crams all five writing assignments into the end of the course. Also, she doesn't grade you on assignments as you complete them, so you're not likely to have any idea what your grade will be until it's posted.

DO NOT TAKE. I'm not sure why she has such good ratings on this site because I had unbelievable amounts of work for this class. Most other english 15 teachers give five papers over the course of the semester but Cynthia gave 5 papers, around 30 blogs (posted online), along with a lot of other writings involving comic books. Do NOT take her class.

I am a straight A student and I really tried in this class, but still wound up with a B. Cynthia is a nice lady but does not tell you at all what is expected on projects. The material is mundane and irrelevant, and you spend more time wrestling with technology than learning. There are much better LA101 teachers, so avoid her if you can.

Cynthia is honestly an amazing teacher.  She, at times, could be very vague, but it was because she wanted us to actually come up with ideas on our own.  She was awesome at teaching, and she was a fair grader - not exactly easy, but definitely not hard.  Do your work, go to class, and you are pretty much gaurenteed at LEAST a B.

This was probably the best English class I've ever taken. Work is minimal, besides the required 5 papers, but she is a very easy grader. You study comic books, which is super easy and also fun. She cancels class and lets you out early a lot. Easy A.

awesome class. It is demanding, and a lot of work, but if you keep up with the class and show a genuine interest in the course material, you will be rewared in the end. only problem is that sometimes the assignments are very vague and can stack up if you dont keep on top of every one of them

Cynthia can be very nice and approachable. Unfortunately this is offset by the fact that she seems to have no idea what she wants from students' projects. She also tends to forget about assignments and then gives them at the last minute. Not a horrible teacher but a disorganized mess.

Cynthia is an awesome professor. She is  easily approachable, helpful, and enthusiastic about her job.  She's  one of the best English teachers I've ever had. Do your work, show interest, and you will do well. Definitely recommend her.

I LOVE this class. No tests. No final. No notes unless you want to take them. A lot of group discussion to get you interacting. There's a few 2 page papers, but she's a fairly easy grader as long as you support your point. No book to buy, just plays. I got all the plays from the library except for a few. Loves and knows a lot about her subject.

Cynthia is great at what she does and really helps you to improve your writing or explore a new style, very understanding as well. Participate in class and she'll like you. About 6 papers throughout the semester, not too hard but get started on your work early

Worst professor I've had at PSU. Completely unorganized. Assigns incomprehensible assignments, then changes what she wants to see on those assignments 3-4 days before they're due. Very unhelpful during office hours, won't give you advice on how to get a better grade with papers. Unfair grader. AVOID.

You can really tell Cynthia loves her subject. We were required to see 3 performances, and they were well worth it. Fairly easy grader, but still need to put work into it. Lots of group work that's actually interesting and you get to interact with the class as opposed to just sitting there for lecture. The plays we rare great too!

Very nice woman. Do the required work on time and you'll get an A. Not overly a lot of work. You will do a lot of reading about family dysfunction so be ready for it! Lots of group projects. Relates well to students. Laid back. If you want an easier class that's still interesting, this is the one to take.
Very nice, and very laid back. There is a balanced paper load, and she is a very fair grader. I'd definitely recommend taking her. I'm a chem major, but this was actually one of my favorite classes.

CYNTH! she is an amaaazing lady! we watched south park in class one day for no reason. she is soo helpful with your papers. if you're not satisfied with a grade, go see her during office hours. the class is super laid back. we never really did too much in class other than peer reviews and a few small presentations. it was silly and fun and amazing.

Don't take honors composition if you're not taking Cynthia. Her class was fun and a lot of work but I learned a lot. She was more than willing to help students and probably one the best english teachers I've ever had.

Two words: Awesome Professor! She was the most helpful teacher I have ever had, and her class showed how much hard work can pay off. She literally wants to help you, and its too bad that not ever professor is like her. All teachers should base their instruction off Cynthia. Take english 030 over 015 with her. You learn a lot more!
What an awesome teacher! I learned stuff in her class that I actually use in the real world. Very helpful and student-friendly. Wish I had more professors like her!

I got an A with barely any effort. I am an english major, but as long as you mean well and seem genuinely interested in writing, all you really need is an average aptitude for writing. She is really flexible with deadlines (which was handy for me, a self-proclaimed scatterbrain) and provides lots of opportunities to improve your grade, if needed.
A fun class. Do your work and it'll be an easy A.
great teacher, easygoing, flexible & fun. this class was interesting & was pretty hands-on for an english class.
Really great class
cynthia makes the class interesting... even the relentless **** of Peter Brooks... the assignments are relatively easy and to the point... loved this class... loved cynthia

The assignments are not stupid pointless crap like in Engl 15, but very practical ones that will most likely help you out in any major. Cynthia is very clear and concise and we only do what is necessary in this class. There is a lot of writing, but that is balanced out with many days off. We watched a couple films also. Take Cynthia if you need 202

Does let us out early, that's the only good thing about her; she expects way way too much out of her students and grades completely unfairly; treats senior english like we should all be pulitzer prize winners; it is a joke and honestly the worst class/teacher I have had in my college career.
she was great - very funny, made class enjoyable, and let us out early a lot.  She didn't keep us any longer than we had to be there.  Great class, great professor.
I took 268 primarily because Cynthia was teaching it.  She can make any material exciting and really understands how to relate to us as students.  Any class you can take from her is a must.

she was amazing. she gave us interesting work and if we finished class early- she let us go. she didnt have lecture just for the sake of having it. it always had purpose. i always did well in english classes and i still feel like i learned and improved my writing.
Cynthia loves her students, gives us food, laughs and makes a crappy english class fun...even if it is at 8 am. take her, she's great!
An amazing lady! So nice and makes the atmosphere fun. Got to leave early to go peer edit. I was really worried about this class but she made it great!
Great prof...funny person, she lets us out all the time
She has a great sense of humor and the class is always interesting. We get out of  class early a lot which is a nice perk. She's a fair grader and a genuinely nice person.

I had him for CMPEN 331 as a TA. Anytime he would post "helpful" announcements, they contained no information about what was intended to be helped. It feels like he's intentionally playing ignorant to get out of doing the work that the student's need from him.
Very interesting. Passionate about what he teaches. Dont fear this class, you dont quite get to everything in the syllabus. Exam grading is lovely.

Nice guy, lectures are alright. They're just discussions. The exams are pretty easy too, and he gets feedback from us on what should be better. He just never responds to emails and takes forever to grade. He said we'd have 4 projects, yet our 1st one is due a week before finals. Pretty disorganized, but for an easy grade who am I to complain.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Lectures are all over the place and hard to follow. Midterms take like forever to grade. Take this class if you already have a solid understanding of the material.

shes amazing. The class is so easy if you do the work. I would study an hour before the exam and do great on them. She gives a ton of extra credit and she really cares about her students. Would take this class again if I could

Cynthia is a nice woman, but she's difficult to learn from. Her teaching style is all over the place, and she never really provides much clarity. The TAs were very helpful, but they're the ones who ultimately got stuck explaining everything. She definitely understands all of the material and is very educated, but she's not the best teacher.

There are a lot of exams. Make sure you study the slides, the slides are all clear to understand so that you can ace the exams easily. There are many TAs that help us if we have questions. In-person class meeting is not mandatory because Dr. Simmons always recorded and you have the choice to attend either Zoom or in-person class.

She is nice and genuinely wants you to do well and pass the class! She is always ready to answer questions and help you. Even if you have a good grade in the class, you wont pass the class if you dont pass the libel exam at the end of the semester which seems unfair. But if you just listen in class and read the slides you will do good!

Cynthia is very kind and professional; she is willing to help you as much as possible! Don't be shy to reach out to her; she wants you to be successful. She also has a very high EQ, as she shows compassion and understanding. Love her.
Easiest class ever but most boring at the same time. TAs do all the work for her
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: This is a mandatory class so I know ya'll have to take this class especially if you are Communications major. But she's horrible. Like all the comments above, she is extremely disorganized and makes a lot of tiny mistakes that confuse these 300 students VERY OFTEN. I had 2 day heads up for exams and there was not a syllabus to follow.

We love Professor Simmons!!!! She is so passionate about what she teaches and she wants the best for all 300 students in her class. She's so understanding and explains things so thoroughly that it can come across as overkill, but you'll really appreciate it during exams (which are not hard if you take notes).

She is an amazing professor and I loved this class! It is actually super interesting, so I went to the lectures, but you definitely do not have to and can still get a decent grade if you put in effort outside of class. Do the practice exams and majority of the extra credit and you will probably get an A.
