Sooooo Much extra credit, its kind of hard to not do good in this class. The libel exam is extremely easy to pass so its no worries honestly. I would say to do majority of extra credit.
reviews.rating_tags: EXTRA CREDIT--Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: So much extra credit, I ended the course with a 101. Sometimes she would post a homework assignment only 24 hours in advanced but late work is accepted for full credit. I wasn't really interested in law but this was a required class that ended up being my easy A class.

Cindy is the best, always willing to help students when they're struggling. Very easy course, which includes easy in-class questions, reading logs and a moot court. Do the assignments, get full credit. Exams are also a breeze, even the libel exam (need to get a 60 to pass the course) which is overly hyped up. LOTS of extra credit! I loved COMM 403!

I thoroughly enjoyed professor Simmons. She comes off as very intimidating in the first week or so, and she makes the course sound impossible. BUT DONT LET THIS SCARE YOU OFF. Great lectures, she clearly states what will be on quizzes or exams, and does a lot of practice to prepare for exams. If you need to take this course I 100% recommend Simmons
she is a bad professor who does nothing her TAs do everything for her she just reads horrible PowerPoint slides. easy A but if you want to learn even a little its a bad class for that

Professor Simmons is very knowledgeable but extremely disorganized. Passing her class is easy since she cares more about effort than how correct your answers are. Gave in-class questions that were super easy. Just show up and listen, and you'll be fine.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great Prof. Lectures can be long, but they are interesting. Prof. Simmons has trouble hearing, so outside of class, communication is handled by TAs, but the TAs are solid. If you put forth a modest amount of effort and participation into this class, there is no reason not to pass. ! TEXT BOOKS - you can download for free!

I wish I could rate the TA's because they practically taught the class (they would get 5 stars). Cynthia herself isn't the best teacher. Although what she teaches is easily understood by her telling stories and explaining... it is still hard to grasp the information. The TA's send out review guides which help. Go do the work and go to class to pass

Her lectures go too fast for those who do not know how to type and write notes. They are sometimes a little confusing and she can be very disorganized as she didnt even give us enough time to present moot court. So we did all the prep with no satisfaction. The TAs carry her a bit. Shes nice and cool and is an easy A if you complete assignments.

SHE IS AWFUL!! Nice woman who means well but she didn't teach anything. the class was a disaster&extremely unorganized. she had her TAs do all her work so if you have good TAs you should be fine. You had 2 day heads up for exams and there was not a syllabus to follow. Class is overall easy if you can put up with a terribly boring&lazy prof.

The information can be difficult at times, but the class isn't. The study guides are pulled straight from the exams and paying attention to the lectures will help you greatly. She gives many extra credit ops (I am finishing with over a 100%) and overall the class was really easy. Only downside is Simmons talks and goes through slides FAST.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Group projects--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: Prof. Simmons is a tough professor, and she can be a little spacey at times. She's so extremely knowledgeable in her field, so her real-world examples are great. I'm applying to be a TA in the class because she was so great. Exams are tough, you have to pass the libel exam to pass the class. You'll do a mock moot court too, there's public speaking!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Test heavy

reviews.comment: I feel like Cindy gives good hugs. She has been very accommodating during COVID-19 and really wants the best for her students. She also has really helpful TAs that are always there if you need them. I would definitely recommend taking COMM 403 with her as you learn the material but also a lot of good advice for the real world.

If you're a journalism or PR major, this class is CRUCIAL. Yes, you have to pass the libel exam to pass, BUT if you read, do the practice exams and do outlines, you should be okay. Cindy's intimidating at first, but she really knows her stuff. The content gets interesting and she definitely wants you to succeed. The remote learning also helps.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: One of the most genuine professors I've had at Penn State and is really knowledgeable. There are four tests and several reading logs. She offers lots of extra credit too.
Cindy is one of the best professors I've ever had. She has experience in her field, passion for the course material, and a genuine desire to see her students succeed.

She doesn't grade assignments on accuracy, more on if you just tried. Showing up to class, and really just listening and answering clicker questions will get you an A. She as a teacher is very good at explaining all of her material and genuinely wants to make sure everyone does well.
reviews.rating_tags: Gives good feedback--Get ready to read--Participation matters

reviews.comment: You have to go to class because there are clicker questions almost every class, but other than that it was worthless. Simmons is a little inept. She doesn't email. Holds just one office hour a week. TAs do most of the work for the class. I didn't really learn much, but I got an A. She's not very good with Canvas either, grading took forever.

This class makes you work. But Simmons and the TAs definitely will help you out if you put in the effort. Go to class, there's tons of clicker points/quizzes. There is no time in the semester to slack even a little bit, and you also have to pass the libel exam (which isn't hard, but still requires you doing the work.)
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Skip class? You won't pass.--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: This was probably my favorite class at PSU and actually made me interested in attending law school. Prof Simmons knows what she's teaching and cares about her student's success. There are 3 exams, and the second one (Libel) you must pass in order to pass the class, but its not difficult because she gives you practice tests and you can use outlines.
Surprisingly, I had a lot of fun in this class.

Cindy is an ANGEL. Easiest class if you just do the assignments. She encourages working with classmates and splitting up the readings and work. Everything is so precise and she offers a lot of opportunities to get an A easily, like a practice exam before every test for extra credit. Just make sure you show up and do well on the clicker quizzes too!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Don't take this class if you don't have to!!! She is very broad and ambiguous with what she wants in the assignments. No matter your grade in the class when the third exam comes, if you fail that exam she will fail you. She also expects you to read 40+ pages before every class and complete an assignment on what you read. Very time consuming, class!
Don't take this class if you don't have to. She rush through all the work and then assign a test and you have to pass libel exam

Prof Simmons is FANTASTIC. She is funny, interesting, fair,& kind. She's also very intelligent,& it seemed like everyone liked her. Reading the bk& notes is important,but she goes over pretty much everything in class,& is cool,so definitely attend. There are quizzes. She also gives extra-credit,& attendance matters. Loved her, and enjoyed the class

Professor Simmons is truly an amazing professor. You WILL NOT pass the class if you do not pass the LIBEL EXAM, which is the second exam of the course. Simmons has an amazing attitude. Her lectures are extremely important to understand the material. HIGHLY recommend this class. It is not an easy A. You must read and attend class.

Favorite class I've taken so far at PSU. She's great and I loved the class so much I'm looking into going to law school. I'm not the typical case, but it is very easy to do well in this class. Do you work, go to class, and study for exams. Sounds simple. Cindy is great and loves teaching, so utilize her office hours if need-be. Highly recommend!!!

I honestly didn't enjoy the class AT FIRST. But it did eventually become my favorite class last semester. Even though her teaching is very unorthodox & sometimes takes a little while to grade(she had no TA btw -- with 120+ students) this class made me love the subject of Media Law. I would definitely suggest Criminology students to take this course

I took this as a fun elective since I had never taken a stats class before. This class was a little more intense than I initially expected it to be, but I feel that the professor presented the concepts very well. The class was also very organized and straightforward. I enjoyed it.

She's a very nice lady, but her lectures are VERY boring. She drags things out. She also doesn't explain concepts that well. But, not a terribly hard class. One cheat sheet for two midterms and two cheat sheets for the final. Not horrible.

Her dyslexia is her personality trait LOL. You don't need to go to class. Every exam you get a full cheatsheet front and back. She also makes good review slides too. Just do the homework for practice for the exam and you'll be fine. You have to do practice problems to do well. The final was literally multiple choice you should not fumble the easy A

her lectures are informative, but boring. the course is easy, but dont do my mistake and get confident after midterm 1. the course only gets harder and tougher. study and understand concepts dont just try to jam everything into the cheat sheet and call it a day as this screwed me over mid1 grade: 93 
mid2 grade:78
final; dunno but polly 70-80

i have no idea why her ratings are so low. she's very clear and direct as a professor. her 318 class is so well organized compared to most professors. she sets up clear expectations from the start, her exams are fair, she's a great lecturer. very easy to get an A in her class. don't listen to the negative reviews from this sem.
reviews.rating_tags: Amazing lectures --Clear grading criteria--Lots of homework

reviews.comment: the worst professor. does not have clear expectations. STAY AWAY!!
don't recommend

worst professor ever because her expectations is not clear. you can't say use hand calculations and then say you can't write hand-written. you can't say you say CI confidence interval this way and then continue saying that you need to be a different way. She is always looking to decrease points rather than help incourage the students
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Test heavy

reviews.comment: Go to class and do homework, and you should be fine. Lectures are good and tests are very fair.

Very clear in announcements and instructions, allows 1 cheat sheet front and back on midterms and 2 cheat sheets on final exam. Exams are very fair and are simple to do if cheat sheet is good. Averages on exams were very high because of this. She drops two homeworks and two quizzes and gave an extra credit quiz worth 2% extra of final grade.

Weekly Quizzes, Written HW, 2 Midterms and a final are what you need to expect. The exams are easier than HW. If you ever missed the lecture, just go through the class notes on your own. There are two materials that I think is important to strive an an A in this class : (1) examples on the notes (2) Go to her exam review lectures! (so effective.)

Dr LaJambe was a very organized lecturer and the in class examples she included in the lectures were very helpful. The weekly quizzes which were only multiple choice (in a math class) usually had a poor average. The tests were hard even with two pages of notes and those again, were mostly multiple choice. Overall average experience.

She's not a bad prof, but she is boring to listen to. Her exams are mostly multiple-choice, which means that getting one problem wrong can dock 5 points on your exam immediately, even though statistics should heavily grade work/thought process. Her quizzes can have 8pt questions out of 20 based on one inputted answer with no work evaluated.

The course materials are very heavy and fast. HW is due almost every week along with quizzes. Its very fast paced and sometimes it's really hard to learn. However, if you study and do all the assignments you will pass this course. Her exams are multiple choice so be prepared not to screw up.

She is not very helpful or accessible. However, if you don't get on her bad side she is relatively nice. Her exams aren't the worst in terms of content but they are primarily multiple choice and if you get one wrong then that's already 5-6 points off. Quizzes are similar. Keep up with the lectures and you should be fine.

She is a great professor and this is such an important class if you are aiming to become a data scientist or analyst in the future. She teaches the important distributions with great detailed notes. I still use her notes for my data science interview as they explain all the important concepts. Her exams are also not that hard.

Admittedly, she may not be the most interesting professor you've had. But she teaches this class well, and gets the content across. Through her course materials, I really learned the content pretty easily. The exams are predictable, and you will be prepared if you are doing the homework and quizzes weekly. I really wish she was teaching STAT319.

The teachers lectures were hard to sit through. She seemed illprepared with many mistakes both on lecture slides and on tests (to be fair she gave us points back on the test). When students ask questions she often replies with non-answers. The tests are almost entirely multiple choice. The lectures are like sitting through textbook reading sessions

I took PLSC 451. I wrote 7 essays for one semester, they're double spaced and 5 pages each. Her instructions are clear and concise. The papers were not hard but sometimes difficult to connect certain parts of the textbook to your essay that makes sense. She made the class easy to understand and fun! She is flexible and considerate.write a lot.
reviews.rating_tags: Participation matters--Clear grading criteria--So many papers

reviews.comment: I enjoyed this course and Prof. Lloyle. Lectures were actually interesting and she is passionate about the content. There were out of class readings to prepare for class discussions, but nothing crazy. The occassional projects and group work in class. Exams were fairly simple, short. If you need a humanities credit, take this course.

Dr. Loyle is an amazing professor, and this class was very interesting and had minimal homework. Definitely recommend if you need an interdomain gen ed. The exams were very easy, and we didn't have to write any essays aside from short paragraph assignments. She does call on people randomly, though, so pay attention and be ready to participate!

Professor Loyle was a good professor for a good choice of an interesting general education class. Three midterms (easy) with biweekly assignments (short). Fairly low effort for an A in a 3 credit course. Would recommend.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Participation matters--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Cynthia is really chill. I have to admit my participation was lacking due to this class being a 9am, but she truly is one of the most caring professors. Class comprised of quick weekly assignments talking about what you learned each week (you only have to do 8/12 to get 100) and then a midterm paper and a final paper or creative project!

DO NOT Take PHIL119 if you are looking for an easy A. Classes online are supposed to be fast and simple. Not this one. EVERY week Lessons that are 3X longer than my other classes. Test and then on top of that mandatory discussions & replies of at least 750to900 words each. Online school is supposed to be fast & easy that is the point. BEWARE.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lots of homework--So many papers

reviews.comment: Reading heavy. If you skim them you'll usually do just fine - wmnst isn't hard conceptually you just have to put some thought + effort into it. Not too bad. Discussion posts weekly. Enjoyable class overall. She cut a ton of assignments and extended deadlines / is understanding of situations. Very accessible for questions. Would recommend.

two papers. one page weekly response. cythia is frickn hysterical and super cool and chill. prob someone fun to smoke w lmao. this class literally just needs effort and youll get an A. rlly interesting material and learning about everything sex is a huge plus. ppl drop this class only when they wait till night of to write 6 page paper

cynthia changed my life. she deserves all the credit in the world. makes you think about life and people in so many amazing ways. i hope everyone gets the chance to be her student. she emulates such joy and passion about love and sex and has truly made me rlly sad to leave this section this semster. all u need to do is try and ull be fine

she is amazing. only take class if u dont mind writing two papers that u just need to put alittle effort into. met w her once for each paper and got high a on it. literally the best prof ive ever had and im truly sad this class is over. wld recommend this to everyone if i could. not a given A but thousand percent attainble w just a little effort
easy to get full credit if you focus enough

This professor is constantly contradictory on what she wants out of her students for her assignments. Often makes things extremely confusing & turns what could be a simple assignment into something that is incredibly confusing & a ton of work. When questioned, she acts as if she is smarter than everyone else because she has a PhD. Avoid her class.
The exams are not hard, but covered many chapters. Quite easy to get A. She gives extra credit to every exams, usually4-8 points. And provides other extra credit opportunities.

Dr. Adams is so sweet and always will stop to answer any questions that students have. Make sure you read through all of the PowerPoint slides and the textbook to make sure you're prepared for the exam. It's a lot of studying, but I really enjoyed the class. Sit up front to get a better understanding of what's going on since it's in a lecture hall.

Dr. Adams is a great choice for Nutr 251. My only complaint is her lectures are so detailed and the study guides are extremely basic. I never know what to study for exams. That being said, do the study guides, review lectures notes and read the book. She is nice and offers a lot of extra participation so going isn't always mandatory.
Dr Adams is a solid choice for Nutr 251. She is a kind and truly cares about this class. Her exams are not bad if you read the book and do the study guide.

She cares about her students, and loves her subject. I respect her for that, but she failed to cover all the exam materials and made us take an exam still having to study the materials we haven't learned about by ourselves. She often goes over class time, so I always had to run to my next class.

I took Math 140 with him last semester, he explained what is a relatively complex subject with ease. I don't think I've ever had a math class I enjoyed more than his, and I would reccomend him as a professor to anyone. He was also more than willing to stay after class to talk about his research, or explain concepts.

Best professor ever. Only reason I got a B was because I stopped going to class, but he explains everything clearly. If you go to class you can definitely get an A. His quizzes are very similar to the examples he does in class and are extremely easy. He always replies to emails, very willing to help during office hours, and super kind. Def take him

Professor Czuprynski is very knowledgeable about the topics. He is readily available for questions/help during his office hours. His exams became easier through the semester and he even assigned group projects. I would have liked it better if his study guides/review sheets were included as in-depth practice exams. He responds quickly to emails!

Good prof, nice lectures and helps during the office hours. Homework and projects are clearly worded. Projects had to be done in groups and include a presentation part, but I guess that's the way the course was set up before him.
reviews.rating_tags: Group projects--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Only take this class if you're actually interested in world religions. If you're looking for an easy A this is not it. The class is interesting, but the only things you do are go to lecture, read, and take exams. There are no assignments or discussions so there is very little class engagement, and you can feel it. Tests are super specific so study!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Although I learned a lot in this class and enjoyed the content, the structure of the class was not optimal. He lectures the entire time every class and the whole grade is just based off a few exams with very little assignments. The positive was there was very little homework, but I would not take this class unless you are interested in the subject.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: There's 1 quiz due every week that you have 25 mins to complete 25 questions (not enough time). There are about 2 hours of boring lectures every week that you have to watch to succeed on the quizzes, as well as a 20-page article about the topic. Overall, he is good at teaching; it's impossible to do well on the quizzes since you have to rush.

If you are looking for an easy A gen ed DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE! The entire class is based off 5 grades all of which are tests in pollock. If you do not attend every lecture and do not write down what he says word for word you will do poorly on his exams. I am a straight A student and because of how difficult this class was I got a C. Save yourself
reviews.rating_tags: Lecture heavy--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: He clearly knows his stuff and likes what he's doing. Take notes on just about every word he says, and DO NOT skip writing down the stories. Do the reading at least the night before the exam. I studied by rereading notes a few times and skimming highlights from the readings
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Test heavy--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: do not take this class. he's passionate about the subject but sits in a chair for 1.5 hours and just talks, no class slides or anything. your grade is based on tests, and the questions make no sense, he asks questions like "I mentioned this in class, why did I mention it?" attendance not taken but if you don't go you WILL fail the test.

Rating again because I disapprove of the hate he's receiving. Literally a great class, you learn a lot, explanations couldn't be simpler, makes you think and want to learn more. Very very interesting! Pay attention to every single thing he says though, even the stories you might think are just for fun, he does test on those too. Amazing professor!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Amazing lectures --Test heavy

reviews.comment: People who are complaining about this course clearly did not attend class. Yes, the class was all lecture and he talks the entire time and your grade was all exams. If you simply attend the lectures, take very efficient notes, and pay attention, you will do great on exams! His explanations are very clear, gives great examples and stories!

This class is incredibly hard. You have to write down every single word that comes out of his mouth during lectures. The only way to get close to an A is if you memorize all the lecture notes, the content from his reader, and read the textbook content twice. DO NOT take it if you're looking for an easy A.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Lecture heavy--Test heavy

reviews.comment: The lectures can be dry, but engaging with the material pays off. Quizzes are challenging, so take good notes and utilize resources like Unstuck AI for study prep. Overall, it's a demanding but rewarding course.

DO NOT take this class. It is extremely lecture heavy. Besides the textbook, there is no other resources to help understand material. The only grades consists of 5 exams. The material he lectures about in class is confusing and preparing for his exams (which are in Pollock btw) are near impossible because the questions he asks are so complicated.

Took the web version of this class. There was a lecture uploaded every week along with a quiz that you had to do. There was also a weekly reading but it was not very long. The quizzes were a little difficult, and you must take good notes from his lectures.

I really have very little to say about Prof. Smith. He is rather mundane personally but helpful and provides a very well structured course that certainly facilitates a learning of world religions. If you're looking for an easy A and not a professor to be chums with, he's it.

The class is easy if youre interested in the material. You have to attend EVERY lecture to take notes as well as do textbook readings in order to pass. There is only 5 tests, but some questions can get really specific, like one specific sentence in the book or class. But if you know the general vibe of the religion you can usually guess good
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: This is an online INTRO level course that is treated like a 400 level class. The lectures for each week are over 20 pages long (word doc). The quizzes each week aren't terrible, but he makes some of the questions so difficult that even doing the reading doesn't help. The final exam is so specific and hard for an INTRODUCTION course...

Do not take this professor if you don't have to. He is a very harsh grader and particular about parts of the class that don't matter and is really strict with formatting. If you don't write word for word what he's thinking you won't do well. I did take the online section. But, most of your grade is quizzes & if you read the material you can do well

His homework assignments are impossible to get an A on with his 400 word limit. Spent most of my time trying to shave off words just for him to tell me that I needed to provide more detail. Tests are really hard and you HAVE to read his chapters, which are treacherously boring and long. I had been looking forward to this class but it was miserable.
reviews.rating_tags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: Way too much effort for a 001 REQUIREMENT CLASS. Whole class is based on his "lectures" - poorly written text. The instructor grades very subjectively, the grading criteria is not clear for home works. Mandatory non-productive discussions with one question and no room to actually discuss things are graded very strict. Does NOT respond to email.

One of the best classes I've taken so far! Dr. Smith is a great and expressive lecturer, which really made me stay engaged. Attendance not taken, however lectures are not on slides or posted online, so in order to do well on exams, you got to go to class and write down what he says. Very independent class that held me accountable to get stuff done!

Loved every second of this class. His lectures are really something. I swear I got goosebumps multiple times. I would usually spend no more than 2 hours studying for each exam. His exams weren't difficult. You just need to have good note taking skills. Would definitely take again.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Easy A! The only grades for the course were five exams, no cumulative final. Exams were made up of multiple choice questions that were fairly easy. Exam material was based heavily on lecture and included some questions from both the required books, but they were not expensive. His lectures could be dry to some but honestly I liked how he talked.

Everything in lecture is fair game for the exam so be sure to write down everything he says. But other than that, his lectures are fantastic and he cancels class on the days of the exam. Final exam is also non-cumulative which is also a plus.
reviews.rating_tags: Respected--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: His lectures can be quite boring, however you can tell he is very passionate about the subject. If you are interested in world religions then you will enjoy the material. You definitely need to attend the lectures and read to do well because he makes very specific references, but if you do, it isn't hard to do well.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Never been a fan of 100% exam-based classes, but even after writing down every word he said and reading the textbook still resulted in me getting C's on the exams. Vaguely worded obscure references to metaphors he mentions once make up the same amount of the exams as actual book content that he doesn't mention at all. Only grades are the 5 exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--TEST HEAVY--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: Make sure that you go to every class as exams are directly from his lecture. His voice is monotone & boring, so it will be easy to fall asleep. His explanation is clear. However, you need to study hard for each exam. Memorize every single thing from his mouth and read textbook carefully. Don't expect an easy A. I think he curves a bit at the end.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY

reviews.comment: Worst professor I've ever had my entire college career and my chemistry professor had Glioblastoma. The only source of information is directly from the lecture which consists of him sitting in a chair, not moving, talking for an hour and fifteen minutes. If you want an A in the  class you better write down every word that comes out of his mouth.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was a very interesting class, but the exams were extremely difficult!! You need to memorize every word of the textbook and specifically what examples he gave in the lecture.  I got a B- and I do not think I have ever worked so hard for a B-.  Reading the textbook is extremely important.
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith's class is really lecture heavy, however, you have to do very minimal work outside of you allotted class time. There are 5 exams that combined total 446 points and that is all you are graded on. If you attend each class, take notes, and then study for a FEW hours  before an exam you will be in good shape. He is not as bad as everyone says
reviews.rating_tags: Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This was the worst class. I took it as  a GH expecting a manageable class, but this is impossible. His lectures are painfully boring and you have to write down his every word to even think about passing one of his tests. I read the book at least twice before each exam. I put the most effort into this class and this was my lowest grade.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--GRADED BY FEW THINGS

reviews.comment: Dr. Smith is great and is obviously really passionate about the class, but it is an extremely hard class to excel in. The grade is completely exam based and the exams are quite impossible. You have to practically memorize everything he says in lecture as well as in the textbook to even have a chance of passing the exams. Don't expect a GPA booster
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: This professor lacks any enthusiasm. Only 5 exam grades make up your final grade and the exams are really tough for a Gen Ed. Lectures are boring and exams are tricky. WOULD NOT RECOMMEND. I worked hard and barely made a B-.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: I really enjoyed this class.  If you go to lecture and do the readings, it is an easy A.  The class was very interesting despite the fact that his lecture can be a bit boring at times.

There is alot of reading for his class, and attendance is DEFINITELY mandatory, but I found that the minutes flew by. If you read the required readings, are an active listener in lecture, and find world religions intriguing then this is an easy B. Would love to retake this class!!!!!
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Skip class? You won't pass.--Inspirational

reviews.comment: DO NOT take this class unless you love Religions/History. Thought it would be an easy GH but it's the hardest class I'm taking right now and I'm barely getting by. There's only 5 tests and they are really hard with very specific questions. I really dread this class every day I have it.
reviews.rating_tags: TEST HEAVY--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--LECTURE HEAVY

reviews.comment: The problem with a course that is a gen-ed is that there are a lot of students. With this, of those who perform poorly, you always receive a disportionate amount of negativity than positive.  This course is not difficult. The average for my section was a 80. This is very standard. If you have any interest in religion, do not be afraid to take this.

He is dreadfully boring.  I couldn't stay awake so I stopped going.  I've heard the class is difficult with or without the text book so if you can, save your money.  The exams are not very easy and the questions are confusing at times.
Worst teacher i ve ever had, repeats every sentence he says minimum 4 times, he is really slow and has no idea what he is talking about. Repeats things so many times.

I was skeptical about this class before it based on these reviews, but it ended up being one of my favorites. Dr Smith was crystal clear and an excellent professor.  If you do the readings carefully, take good notes in class, and study for each test, then it is an easy A. Tests aren't impossible; they are really easy if you know your notes well.

I started off the semester thinking that Dr. Smith was crazy, but by the end of the class, I learned to appreciate the passion he has for what he's teaching. The lectures seem boring sometimes, but the readings can be really interesting... and trust me, you need to read if you want to pass the tests.
I found his lectures very interesting and they made a lot of sense. But the test are impossible and are setup to confuse you. You have to study a lot to get a decent grade.

Worst professor I have ever had in my entire life. Took this class as a gen ed thinking it would be really interesting. Yes, it was interesting. But the tests are the most difficult I have ever taken. You need you write down every word he says in class and read the book about 3 times through to pass the exams. DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS.

I took this class thinking it would be an easy gen ed, but I was VERY WRONG. This class was actually hard. DO NOT take it unless you love religion. The lectures are painful and the tests are very confusing and hard.  Curtis is helpful if you ask him, but no matter what you do the exams wont change.

This class is honestly horrible. The material is interesting, yet the readings are tedious and unenthusiastic. Mr. Smith sits at the front of the room and reads his notes for an hour and a half twice a week. The exams are impossibly hard, so make sure you take as many notes as possible & do ALL of the readings. It's a really tough class, beware.

well was looking for an easy gh. should have picked another class. his class is interesting at first, then the leactures seem to drag. a lot of reading his tests are mostly the book. so read and read theirs a lot of it.

This class was ridiculously difficult. I'm a regular A student but his exams are so nit picky that it makes it difficult to do well.  It's basically five multiple choice exams, but really all the answers could be correct for all of them.  Would not take again

I don't understand the down-voting on the people who criticise the course. Because I'm barely getting a B+ with all the effort I'm putting.  I'll be clear, if you want to know if A grade is possible, look at my checklist:  1. Interested in religions? 2. Ready for long intensive lectures? 3. Ready for reading?  Tip: use "Nittany Notes" notes

I read the reviews before choosing this class & i started to freak out a bit. But trust me guys, this class is really interesting and an A is definitely doable. Remember to write down everything he says in class (trust me on this) and while reading the book focus on the things he mentioned in class. I think in the end he rounded my score, too!

The exams are hard, but just make sure you go to all lectures and read the book. If you want a gen ed thats an enormously easy A, don't take this class. If you want an interesting gen ed that teaches you useful knowledge & still allows you to receive an A with a bit of work, take this class. Also, no papers so the only work is studying for 5 exams.

The class was incredibly interesting but lectures were a bit long.   Exams were very difficult. Not an easy A class. Exams were worded very difficult and you must go to every lecture and read the book. Basically know it inside out.

There are only 5 exams. Be prepared to take very good notes in class. Typing is recommanded. Buy his packet before the class. Book is cheap as well. He knows his stuff and sit in front of the room talking about religion in an objective manner. Sit in front so you won't fall asleep. Only take this class if you are interested in religion. Not Easy A

The WORST teacher I have ever had at Penn State. SITS in the front of the room and just READS his notes. The only grades are the five exams which are ridiculously worded and unnecessarily confusing. Not interested in helping students who are doing poorly. Went to every class and did every reading and still received a C.

I loved the class; very interesting and Dr. Smith is very clear and fair to each religion he discusses. However the exams are next to impossible. Even with good detailed notes and in depth reading of the assigned materials and textbook, the exams are very difficult and composed of random material. Be willing to put some work in if you're taking it!

DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. DO NOT. I was like you, reading his ratings online and saw a mix of good and bad so decided to take him. DO NOT. I am an A student and I got a B in his class even though I studied for hours prior to each exam. I knew the notes like the back of my hand yet still couldn't get a B+ on any exam because its ALL book memorization.

Nice guy, lectures are fairly interesting but the exams are ridiculous. Maybe 50% from the actual lecture, but rest is nitpicky questions from the textbook. 5 exams, but unless you memorize the textbook,it's tough to do well for an "easy" gen ed.

First of all, I never missed class took good notes and always studied hard.  However his exams are not just hard they are impossible. They are excessively detailed, and often contain the same answer twice, just phrased differently.  Questions also contain typos, or pour grammar making things even more difficult.  DO  NOT TAKE THIS CLASS!
He is a nice guy and knows his subject well. The tests are difficult because he asks random questions.

He is a very helpful guy, but the class is a lot of work for a gen ed. 5 exams-one every two weeks and a LOT of information on each one. Very interesting, but so much work. Look for an easier gen ed. Most GH classes are like this though...
Pretty easy A! He is a nice guy~

The lectures were so fun and interesting. The professor is really knowledgeable about materials he teaches, and his examples and analogies are so helpful to understand materials. But you should go to class every time and read the textbook very carefully before you take the tests. Only five exams, so simple and not a lot of work.
There was a lot of material and the exams were very difficult. On the bright side, no final exam. I wouldn't recommend this class if you have no prior experience in a religion class.

The lectures changed the way I look at different cultures, hence I liked the teacher, until the first midterm. His questions don't test your knowledge, they test your ability of memorization unnecessary details.

He's a very knowledgeable man. His class is interesting. Only 5 exams. It is easy if you read a text book and study notes from the lecture. I'm sure that people who complain about exam didn't read a book and didn't go to class at all. Videos are boring. I recommend you go to class and take some notes and read a textbook. It is not hard at all.
The easiest class ever! You don't have to show up, but just make sure you get the notes from someone else.
Very nice guy, but the exams are very difficult.

I officially want to change my major after this class. I wish Dr. Smith could teach every RLST class offered! Anyone that says anything otherwise got lazy or didn't possess enough interest to  simply pay attention or read a book.  There are 5 tests...go to class and read the book, that's it(easy A). Wonderful and extremely knowledgeable Professor!

I honestly don't understand why people on here are attempting to discredit Dr. Smith. He is a knowledgeable man who is a great lecturer and gives very fair tests. As long as you take good notes and read the book, you are pretty much guaranteed an A. The complaints on here are entirely unmerited.

This class was a great intro class to religion. 5 exams: Hinduism/Buddhism/Judaism/Christianity/Islam. Organized lectures, so easy to follow. Go to lectures, remember his examples and the points they made. Take good notes and review for ~two hrs before exam.  Read the textbook assignment. It is an easy A if you are interested and do these things.
Interesting class but exams are way too hard. theres 4 100pt exams and one 46 pt exam. highest i've ever gotten on an exam was an 80. DO NOT take this class if you're looking for an easy A.

Class was interesting, exams not too bad.  But - need to read the book to do well on exams.  Also lectures are all him talking, so need to show up and take notes to do well too.  That being said, one of the most boring professors I've ever had.  He definitely knows a lot, but I fell asleep almost every class...

if you need to fill your schedule with a GH or GA gen ed and this is the only class left, do not take it- just wait another semester until you can get a better gen ed that doesn't have to be late dropped because the tests are insane unless you study for several hours before but also have notes verbatim, word for word on what he said in class.

Professor Smith is very knowledgeable about all the material he lectures on. If you want to take this class make sure you can take specific notes and listen to his lecture because he goes fast. Also pay attention to the examples he uses in class and read the textbook because they will be on the test. Very good class and helpful if you ask for it.
The class average on the first exam was a 75- for an intro- level gen-ed class. enough said

This class is definitively harder than my other non-gen ed and gen ed classes. If you are taking this to satisfy a gen-ed and want an easy class do NOT pick this class. You must attend every single class (I missed one and it came back to hurt me) and read every single assigned reading if you want to get at least a B. The readings are long, dense,et

Classes are just him lecturing, but I found the material to be interesting. He is very knowledgable and is very helpful when students are confused. Grade is based of 5 multiple choice exams that are based of lectures, reading of the text book (very little reading required), and movies. I found the exam questions to be straight forward.

He's an absolutely amazing prof. If you take good notes in class and study from them before the exam you are guaranteed a good grade. He's very interesting...I've heard rumors from others saying that he used to even teach at Harvard.
Smith is my favorite prof at Penn State. His understanding and connections between history, philosophy, and psychology are brilliant.

I seriously don't believe some of these comments! People complain that he repeats things multiple times? I mean, *HINT HINT much? The concepts that are repeated are obviously going to be on the exam and he actually WANTS you to be aware of that or else he could simply move on and not care. Great person, extremely knowledgeable Prof-don't miss out!

This is NOT an easy Gen Ed. You are required to read a lot of material & you MUST attend lecture if you want to pass this class. You have to be extremely good at memorizing - the questions on his tests tend to be extremely obscure & often do not cover main topics. KNOW his analogies for the tests. I would not recommend this class.

Literally rambles on and on, repeating the same concept at least five times.  I studied my notes for the first exam and read the chapter and still failed the first exam.  Questions are about ridiculously obscure aspects of the chapter.  Class grade is only based on 5 exams.  Would not recommend!
HORRIBLE! I took this class for a gen ed and thought it would be an easy A considering it is an INTRO to religion class!!! tests are ridiculous and his lectures are pointless

He is an excellent teacher. Very  clear in his explanations. Reading the above comments, I was a little hesitant to take this class but I am very glad I am taking it with him. Reading the book wouldn't help at all if you don't attend the lectures. His lectures supplement the material in the book. I would urge you to take the course with him.
ABSOLUTELY SUPERB

The lectures can be boring at points but it's definitely and interesting course and he does a good job teaching it.  I finished with a B average because I didn't spend much time reading the text book but I could have easily ended with an A if i did.  Good professor overall.

Dr. Smith was ok when I had him Spring semester 2010.  Would urge you NOT to take him.  Tests are extremely difficult.  Material comes from text, mostly lecture notes and also movies.  Also can be boring in lecture.  I tried my best on each exam, got help and managed to pass.

Mr. Smith is a GREAT professor. He really enjoys what he does and attendance is a must because the exams come straight from it.... there are questions from the textbook so reading is crucial! At some times it can be a little boring, but he can be a pretty funny guy. Grade is based on 5 exams. No curves. If you read and go to class, you'll be fine.

This professor changed my outlook on almost everything concerning religion. In fact, i almost switched my major to RLST after taking this class!  Dr. Smith is an terrific teacher who not only knows the material, but is extremely appreciative of all differnt backgounds, beliefs, and cultures.  Although the book is required, it's certainly do-able!!!

Brilliant Prof!...loved every second of this class! Anyone who gave Dr.Smith a low rating are the ones who bombed the exams due to not reading the text carefully which is crucial. He will change make you think/question everything you've learned previously. I received a B on the first exam and A's on all the rest...certainly NOT an impossible class!

The most amazing Prof.I've had at PSU by far! He's extremely intelligent and his lectures are very interesting. Anyone who's complained about the tests are the people who are too lazy to read the book or fail to take adequate notes during lecture. Nothing more difficult than what is expected from any other PSU class. Don't miss out b/c of slackers!
The lectures and everything are very interesting but your whole grade is based on 5 exams. The exams are very difficult! I should have dropped this class after i got a 72 on the first test.

He's voice will put you in sleep. No extra credit, paper, attendance what so ever. Your grades are based on 5 exams only! If you fail one exam, drop it because it is pretty hard for gen ed class. Unless this is your major dont waste your time on this course. Even professor told me to drop this class

Doesn't waste your time with useless busy work or papers like most other gen eds.  Instead grades are based on 5 exams. This class is as easy or as hard as you make it.  Pay attention in the lectures, take good notes, READ THE BOOK.  Be sure to read the materials a second time before tests and you will be fine.
Dr. Smith's lectures are very interesting, however as many have said, his exams are extremely difficult. Don't take this if you're expecting an easy gen ed.

HARDEST CLASS EVER! DO NOT TAKE! Test are ridiculously hard! Lectures are interesting. BUT no matter how much I studied or thought I understand the concept I always managed to do very bad. READING THE TEXTBOOK IS CRUCIAL. ONLY 5 tests! no final no homework no attendance!

This is an interesting class, but the exams are brutal. I was enjoying being in this class but kept failing the exams after much studying and hard work. Dr. Smith is a good guy but the grading system is brutal as exams are all that count and they are miserably hard.

Uhm...an okay class. Lectures are interesting sometimes but the professor repeats every sentence three or four times. MUST READ TEXTBOOK. Tests are insanely hard and are based less on understanding the material and more on memorizing the text. I enjoy considering the professor's opinions though. It's college so..not bad.

He is a great teacher! Everything is explained in class, but you should NOT get Nittany Notes because you have to be there to understand the concepts.  Also, make sure you know his analogies for the test!  Review sessions are unnecessary.  Great professor!

This course really isn't that bad. The material is very interesting and Dr. Smith's lecturing style very good in terms of clarity. All you need to do to succeed in this course is take good lecture notes and do the readings. Nothing short of what is expected of any college class.

This class was ridiculously hard. His lectures are just him rambling on about the same five points over and over again that don't appear on the test except for his crazy analogies that make no sense. The test is about 85% of the book which is difficult to read because the author rights in such an ambiguous way. Stay away from this class. GPA KILLER
Great class, great teacher. Interesting lectures.  Textbook reading makes up about 40% of the test, so you have to do the reading and attend the lectures to succeed in this class.

Class was very hard, but very informative.  Everyone that gave the prof. a low grade was probably a person that failed to read for the first test and bombed it.  Reading is 40% of the tests so its important that you stay on top of it.  Def. a do-able class. I did the readings, took notes, and earned an A.  You will learn, question, and think a lot!

Make sure you go to every class, take good notes, do all of the readings, and study for the exams. I would suggest taking this class if you have an interest or a passion for any sort of religion.. otherwise you may not enjoy it. The class itself may require a bit more work, but Smith's lectures are worth it. My favorite class so far here at psu.

I thought this class was interesting just because I like learning about religions.  However, this prof is a little bit psycho- tests are really hard because they are testing to see if you read the book- but the way everything is worded is ridiculous. I pulled out a B, but i was sick of it by the end. Only good thing-no final
Prof. Smith is very knowledge and will explain everything in great detail. Very hard class though. Lots of reading and memorization. Not an easy Gen Ed.

Dr. Smith is a bias, and has a terrible teaching method. He clearly prefers Eastern Religion, and has openly criticized Chrisitanity. In addition Islam is a very little part of the course, a religion that is very misunderstood in this world and needs more attention. DO NOT TAKE THIS COURSE! Awful Prof., tests memorization not the actual religion.
Tests are ridiculous and have zero relevance to the material. professor is awful NEVER EVER TAKE THIS CLASS

This was the best class i have ever taken at penn state. Smith made religion so incredibly interesting and explained everything really well. if you go to class, write down everything he says in class, and read the book, you will do great.

Professor Smith is very nice & always willing to stay after class & help students out.  You have to make sure to read the book every night & don't wait til the last minute.  Study hard & you'll do fine.

This class was very difficult. I pulled out a B because I just got an 82. No curve at all even though tests are impossible. Professor isnt helpful at all. Knowing the basics will not get you a C. YOU MUST READ THE TEXTBOOK! I cant stress it enough. If you choose to take this class, take it seriously from day

This is possibly the hardest class I have ever taken at Penn State. His tests are impossible. You literally have to memorize about 70 pages of reading. He asks you the most obscure and ridiculous questions on the test. Take this class if you want to get a C or below.

You have to go the class. Reading the notes is not good enough because they will make almost no sense without listening to his explanations. He doesn't use angel; the class isn't even on it. 5 tests are the whole grade (no final which is the one nice thing). He is somewhat entertaining but uses a book and moves from the 60's. Pass on this class

Terrible, terrible class.  If you're considering taking this for your humanities credits, think again.  The tests are nearly impossible--he asks extremely specific questions on minutiae and exact words from his lecture.  You will not be able to stay awake during lecture.  Pick something else!

This man has no concern whether or not his students are learning the material. He asks questions about specific comments he makes in lectures and tries to mislead you by including the same answers in different wording. I spoke to him about his testing method and he yelled at me telling him I had no place questioning how he ran his class.

some of the lectures were awesome, & some of them put me to sleep. if you're going to miss a class GET THE NOTES! and be sure to be there for movie days. the TA=very helpful, go to review sessions. if you do the work there arent any tricks. study your notes especially the analogies he makes in class, & make sure you know whats in the book.

I would take this class if you like memorizing 50-70 pages of reading word for word.  Says that test questions are analyzing which is complete bs.    His tests are def not a good way to test you on what you learned. Memorizing notes will probably get you a D or F...a lot based on readings.

This is the WORST class ever! I am serious, do NOT take it.  Although I did find his lectures interesting, his tests are ridiculous.  He doesn't test on whether or not you understand the material, he tests you on whether or not you memorized 60 pages in the book, word for word.  Do NOT take this class.
This guy bored me day in and day out.He pretends to know everything. He is the worst prof. ever, please do not take his class.

I don't know why everyone is bugging out about Smith.  His lectures are easily understood and if you read everything the night before the test and study your notes you will be fine.  He gives some really good lectures and the book is actually pretty interesting.

If youre taking this for a gen ed, I would recommend dropping now. I took it because I was interested in it. I thought I learned a lot, but exams thought otherwise. The only grades come from multiple choice exams. I went to every class, took notes, and read everything assigned, and I got Cs and Ds on exams. I have a 3.9 gpa. The exams were just bad

Great class for fulfilling tons of Gen-ed's. Smith isn't that bad, his lectures are really boring, but managable for 50 mintues. The tests are hard and you have to read the book to pass the test. There is NO FINAL, the last exam is the shortest. You have to go to ALL CLASSES to take the notes and you must write eveything down to understand it.
His lectures were really interesting. Lots of readings from the textbook. Tests were hard. You have to put in a couple hours. No curve, no extra credit, no assignments. Just five tests.

If you are serious about studying religion do not take this class. Prof. Smith only cares about his interpretation of the material, there are no papers, and questions after class are usually met with a condesending and sometimes uninformed response. He is less than knowlegeable on some info and will not concede his factual innacuracies. STAY AWAY!!

Test material comes from textbook as well as lectures so attendance is important.  Tests have some tricky questions but in general aren't too challenging.  Great class organization and grading system.

an ok class if youre interested, smith can be a bit boring and repeats things alot but that helps if you tend to zone out. provides an indepth overview of the major religions without bias. going to class every time is a must because he doesnt use angel at all. tests are hard, but doable if you study, make sure to read! overall he's not a bad guy
Lectures as if uniterested in material.
Very easy class unless you don't know how to read.  I read once through everything the day of each test and did fine.  No papers and no final!  Great class.

This class is interesting and so is his lectures. However, the exams are primarily based on the textbook readings, of which, Smith doesn't lecture around. Definitions are not really the focus, but questions are based around analysis. READ!
lectures are interesting but exams are extremely hard.  his questions from the book are very very specific and requires a lot of attention to detail and memorization
test are very very very very hard.  The Class average is a 68 and he says he doesnt curve.
VERY GOOD TEACHER ... I REALLY ENJOYED HIS CLASS AND LEARNED MUCH MORE THAN I EVER THOUGHT I WOULD!
He is a great teacher !! makes you very interested in the subject and the lectures are very good.. you will get an A if you just attend every lecture and read everything. I really enjoyed this class.
the lecture is very interesting but the exams are impossible.

I really enjoyed his class, despite what anyone else on here says.  He made me even more interested in the world religions than I was before.  I felt his teaching could be bland at times, but he was still a knowledgeable teacher.  I really didn't have to study much and I ended up with a B+...  definitely take this course with Mr. Smith.

this class could have been great, except that smith taught it. The tests are way to hard and going to lectures and studying doesnt help. Good luck getting an A, or even a B in this class. Avoid his class at all costs. Curtis is just a poor example of what a professor should be.
Hardest gen ed available, you'd be exceptionally wise to avoid this man

NOT an easy A- but an extremely interesting class.  You MUST attend lecture and you MUST read the book- take this class if you're good at memorization or if you're interested in other religions. BTW NO CURVE

ridiculously hard exams, boring lectures, unhelpful if you ask for help. I attended every class, took good notes, did all the readings, took notes on all the readings and studied hours for each exam. I never got over a B on an exam. NOT an easy gen-ed by any stretch.
This was supposed to be an interesting, introductory course in religious studies. Unfortunately, it turned out to be one of my hardest classes and im an engineering major.
this class is interesting but the tests are impossible.  Don't take it unless you want to devote many hours of studying

This is probably the worst class I have ever taken at Penn State.  His tests are IMPOSSIBLE and have no relevance to his lecture.  He is extremely monotonous and the nittany notes do not even help.  It seemed like it would get easier as the class went on, but it never did.  DO NOT take this class simply for a Gen Ed.

Smith gives colorful, interesting lectures, but his exams are difficult. (Read: no curves and no tests dropped.) Still, he's an eye-opening and informative professor. I'd recommend him... just not for an easy A.

Professor Smith's exams were incredibly difficult, but I still enjoyed the class and learned a lot. You have to go to class to fully (as fully as is possible for this class) understand what everything means. It's an interesting gen ed, but if you're looking for an easy A, this class (at least with Smith) isn't it.

He clarified everything in lecture but the tests are testing superhuman feats in memorization. On the syllabus he says he's not on memorization, but that's not true. If you are in a heavy technical major and have no time for time spent memorization, better take it in the Summer. Interesting material, however

For as hard as exams are, I still enjoyed the class. Dr. Smith is very nice and I learned SO much, but I definitely worked hard for my B-. MUST read all assigned readings (100+ pages/exam) and go to every class. Write down all analogies and examples from lecture, sit in the front, READ! and bring some KY on exam day.

This guy's ridiculous!  His tests are unbelievable.  I took notes in class, I read the selected parts of the book twice.  What's my average?  C+.  The current class average is a 74 after 5 tests.  And when I went to ask him if there was anything I could do, what does he say?  'You're obviously not studying correctly'  This guy is a Grade A ****

Dr.Smith is very insightful and blatently knows a lot about all the religions he discuesses. if you read the book and take good class notes the test arn't a problem, but you HAVE to read the book. He loves analogies and is very awquard but pretty amuzing and you defently learn a lot from the class.

I found that Dr. Smith made all of the information very clear.  The tests were much easier than I thought they would be.  I really only study the night before/morning of and I average a 90%.  Basically, go to each class and take notes.  This professor is good, I would recommend it to anyone needing a humanities gen ed.

He's a good guy overall. The tests are rediculously hard and those in that faith probably counldn't do well. The questions on the exam have nothing to do with the notes so don't bother but def take notes on his examples and go to class. There is no homework just 5 exams. He's completely monotone. Avoid the class if you can. Def not an intro course.

Waaaaay too hard for a supposedly introductory course. His lectures are drier than two-week-old toast, you get little notes out of them, and the tests are just regurgitations of the textbook. If you have to take it, take it with someone else. Otherwise, definitely consider another gen ed in its place.

This guy was among the worst professors I've ever had at Penn State. Very egotistical...you'll grasp that within 5 minutes of his class. Will throw a bunch of questions on his exams that he never went over in class.
HE IS SOOOOO BORING!!!! HE HAS A MONOTONE AND THE GIRL NEXT TO ME IN CLASS DREW A PICTURE OF HIM WITH A STICK UP HIS BUTT!!!! MY ADVICE.... TAKE THE OTHER CLASS WITH THE OTHER TEACHER.

He's a nice guy, but a bit boring. He definitely repeats himself a lot. Pay attention in class, there aren't too many notes, but he'll say random things you should know for the tests. READ, READ, READ! There's no other homework in his class, so don't whine. Read or else you'll fail, that's all I can say.
Very interesting class, but the tests are way to hard. Don't bother taking the class unless you have time to memorize the book.

The class was very interesting. Dr. Smith, however, taught as though we were all 3rd graders. Perhaps this is necessary with a subject like this, but it made it very difficult on the tests. MAKE SURE YOU READ!!! But hey, it's the only work outside the class, so quit crying.

this class was waaay harder than it should have been.  curtis smith should not be a prof. - he was boring and unhelpful and repetitive.  test questions made no sense at times - you'll narrow it down to 2 answers and they both would essentially be the same.  terrible class, terrible teacher!

This class isn't easy but it is VERY interesting.  Smith repeats himself when he talks so if you can't stand that just don't bother signing up.  Doing good on a test means like an 80% and the readings, which are painfully long and boring, make up a lot of the test questions.  I liked it though.

worst religious studies professor in the world. he does not give a damn about his students.  he is unwilling to work with you too.  if you dont understand what he said, he will repeat it and move on.  if you want a good religous studies class, pick someone else.

This is one of the best professors I've had. He makes every topic clear, and if you have trouble with any concepts he will do everything to help you understand. Don't expect an easy intro class. An excellent teacher, but the exams are tough; he really makes you think. Make sure to read the material.

I really like the guy. If you have questions, ask him because he loves teaching and it really shows. He'll take as much extra time as he needs to help you out. The class is kind of difficult, but if you read the book, write down everything he says, and pay attention during the movie, you'll do fine.

I think Curtis is great, yeah you have to be interested in religion, but its not impossible.  He definately loves what he does and gets you interested, not an easy A but you come away having a better understand of the world around you... if you take it, get ready to "climb the mountain of moksha"
so hard. do not take unless u LOVE religiion. ugh i wish i could go back in time to erase this class from my transcript.
This class should not be 001

Difficult class, but he does a great job teaching it. It's a class like college should be- challenging, yet you learn so much. He's one of those profs you either love or hate, there's no middle ground. If you like the topic and don't mind a bit of extra studying, take the class, you won't regret it

This class was hard and he asked the most unfair ambiguous questions on the tests.. he asked about the readinds in great detail. If you really want to memorize all of the readings then take the class.
was unclear, made the class too in depth and not interesting for an entry level class

Worst teacher in the world!! Do not take him. His tests are impossible and he is not willing to help you or work with you. He repeats things way too many times and talks to the class like they are 5th graders!

He is an excellent teacher. This was one of the best classes that I have ever taken. The tests are somewhat challenging but I still got an A. It is not impossible. The people who are complaining are just lazy and did not work hard enough. This class is very interesting. Go to class, read, get an A.

This class is fascinating, but fairly difficult.  He gives an outline of every lecture, then follows it every class.  People who say bad things about him are just lazy and want to be handed grades like most classes at PSU.  Go to class, pay attention do the work, get a good grade.  SIMPLE.

everything from lecture is very understandable.  you must read the book at least twice jsut for a shot at a B tho.  asks the smallest, insignificant questions about the reading.  he claims to have office hours however he was never there when i went.  very interesting class but horrible teacher.

He's a good guy.... can be funny sometimes... he has a real interest in the subject he teaches, but his test are impossible.  They are so confusing and there IS NO CURVE AND NOOOOO BONUS POINTS.... what you get on the SIX exams... is unfortunately.... what you get...

He lectures to you like you're 5-yr olds and just when you think you know the material, he smacks you with an impossible exam! Despite it being '001' this is probably the hardest class i've ever taken. Its a great topic, shame he teaches it.
No Comments

Terrible class. I was very interested in the subject, but got nothing from the class. His tests are extremely unfair. I met with him after getting C's on the first few tests- no help at all. He doesn't even like people to ask questions in class.
He sucks.  Don't take this class.  The most boring class of my PSU career.

He makes u think, he makes u think, he makes u think.  He repeats everything at least twice. If u read the book at least twice, you will have chance to get a B like me.  A very interesting class though
He's a great lecturer, but his exams are hard. Take really good notes and you'll do well.
He's an excellent professor, but the tests are VERY specific.  You really have to know your stuff to do well.  I'd definitely recommend the class.

Extremely high-caliber professor.  Course is difficult, but it isn't busy work. He repeats everything twice. Don't miss a class, TAKE THOROUGH NOTES. Interest in religion will take you far. Take the class for the knowledge, not the grade.
Great teacher! The tests are very difficult but manageable if you go to class, take very good notes and read the chapter thoroughly.  You will learn a lot in this course.
very interesting material, but awful tests. You have six exams so you feel like you are studying for it all the time.  Last semester I received all A's except for this class.
Great class, learned a lot. Always interesting, the test are kinda hard though, read the book.
Very interesting class, but do NOT take it if you aren't interested in religion.  He know's his **** but tests are impossible!!  I am a senior and he gave me the 2nd C of my college career.
Amazing teacher, but his tests are incredibly difficult. This is a course to take only if you are a dedicated student. Missing a class is a death wish....
he's a very nice guy, knows his stuff, and is very willing to help..  but his tests are extremely hard.  i had to drop the class b/c i had a D avg after the first 9 weeks

The class was way too hard.  Whenever you go to take the test, there would be the most detailed questions asking about too specific of things for the length of time we had to prepare for the exams. My advice: take a different gen ed.

Probably the best class I've taken since I've been here. Go to every class, take good notes, and read to comprehend and you will do fine... Seriously amazing professor... changed my major to RL ST after this class... A+ for Smith.

I agree with the other - difficult class - go to every class, take great notes, and don't just read the book, but understand it.  Great teacher though.  An actually challenging class at Penn State.  Would take the class again.
No Comments
This class is interesting but hard in my oppinion. Take some damn good notes, buy the nittany notes, go to EVERY class, and finally read every word of the book. In other words, take another gen ed.
very interesting class, and you'll do well as long as you do the reading
good class, pay attention, interesting professor
read the book thoroughly and go to ALL classes, or you'll fail

She would show up late every single day. There are long readings due before every class and the discussions during class were pointless. I don't think I learned a singular this from this class

reviews.comment: Insane amounts of reading every week, don't even buy the textbook just make a vague comment during the lectures and you will get a good grade in the participation. Takes forever to get your grades back, I got mine the day they were due from assignments months earlier. Hardest part of this class is staying awake during the lectures.

She's a great professor, while a bit newer to teaching its clear she cares for all the students and wants you to succeed. The more you put into the class the better it will be and the more you will get out of it. Attendance is graded and participation matters. She gives great feedback on your essays and is very understanding if life gets in the way

She's soft spoken but very nice if you talk to her. Class participation is important but honestly if you give a vague relation to the texts you read, you'll be fine.  Me and my friends talked a LOT and got really good grades. Again, she is a great professor if you engage with her.

Must attend office hours. Provides insightful constructive feedback. Took this class last semester and enjoyed the interactive group discussions. Some assignments were a little tedious but gets the point across. GO TO CLASS. Attendance matters.

ngl she's actually fire IF you put in effort. like she'll legit help you level up your writing, but you gotta show up and try. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!! the ppl saying she's “hard” just wanted a free A. if you're not lazy, she's amazing.

I had Prof. David for intro English. She was fair and extremely helpful if you went to office hours. I'm not sure where the other reviews come from—I was able to succeed in the class once I started seeking her help individually. Very available professor.

Do not take this class with this professor. She was late to every single class by at least 10 minutes, however marked down your grade if you were late or absent. She took forever to grade previous assignments and would get you the grade back right before the next one was due with no helpful feedback. She also does a bad job explaining assignments.

Whatever you do, DO NOT take English 15 with this professor. She is constantly late to class, never grades assignments, has no idea what she is doing, and asked us to lie on our SEEQs for her promotion. How is it the last week of school and I still don't know wtf my grade is. She's still grading an essay we did a month ago, and spent the last two weeks doing NOTHING in class. DO NOT TAKE ENGLISH 15 WITH THIS PROFESSOR, SHE IS WAY TOO INEXPERIENCED

Very harsh grader compared to other english departments

Horrible professor. Not confident at all, unclear grading, classes don't keep people engaged, keeps talking about "department policy" while screwing over the class, and overall is just not a good teacher. reviews.comment: This teacher was extremely difficult. We had three assignments. The first assignment, an essay was not graded or returned until almost the end of the semester. I never received a grade for the second assignment also an essay. I do not recommend taking this professor.

She finalized the grades without grading many assignments, including an essay. She also took off points for assignments with no clear explanation. She seemed to have no clue about how to run the class.

This Professor had no idea what she was assigning and graded our assignments really hard. She also takes forever to grade assignments and I still have not received some essay grades and it has almost been a week since my final grade was posted. She also takes random points off of minor assignments and doesn't give an explanation why.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: I had her for 302 and 452! She is an amazing and caring professor. She doesn't use technology in class, so all notes are taken by hand on shell notes. I've found this to be super helpful and effective in learning the material. She is very enthusiastic, engaging, and makes the extra effort to get to know everyone's name in class!!

Dr. Rhubart is an amazing professor! She genuinely cares about her students, and the content in the class is very meaningful. There are weekly group discussions for points on the readings that are super easy, and two exams with a notecard included. As long as you pay attention and engage with the material, you will do great. I recommend!

I actually had her for BBH 452! 
Very caring and great lecturer. She takes times to learn students names and makes course content clear. Required textbook but reading aren't bad, its best to keep up but doing well in the group project and final matters most.

Dr. Rhubart was an amazing professor and I really enjoyed her class. There was a lot of reading to do every week but it was all pretty simple readings. The midterm and final weren't bad at all, pretty much all common sense. Reflections were annoying to do. She is very knowledgable and knows a lot, I highly recommend her.

Dr. Rhubart is honestly one of the most passionate BBH professors. She truly cares about her students and memorized everybody's name in a 70-person lecture. She does have a lot of class rules, but as long as you follow them and show up to class you'll have no problem succeeding. I was worried going into this class, but ended up loving it.

She honestly wasn't bad. Yea, the quizzes are annoying but if you already can understand that being marginalized = worse health outcomes, you can BS the quizzes. I barely read any of the material and still managed to get good grades on the quizzes. You also get a cheat sheet on both of the exams.
reviews.rating_tags: Get ready to read--Participation matters--Group projects

reviews.comment: Please take this class with anyone but Rhubart. Weekly reading quizzes are impossible (HOURS of readings), grading is harsh for "Your Choice Project", and only 2 exams. The exam questions are worded in the most confusing way possible, making it so difficult to do well on. No electronics are allowed. Only paper notes. Truly horrible professor.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Lecture heavy

reviews.comment: She does not allow you to have any laptop or technology to take notes on. Questions based on the readings (that take multiple hours per week) are so small and insignificant to lecture that it is almost impossible to get 100%. She is a tough grader. Class participation matters as well as attendance. I would not recommend any of her classes.

She has no regard for her students. She has you do over 3 hours worth of notes, readings, and videos for a weekly quiz that is timed 5 minutes for 5 questions. It heavily affects your grade and there are only 2 exams that help your grade. She does not care about her students. She will not help you if you are struggling.
reviews.rating_tags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: DO NOT TAKE HER! she has no care for any of her students and doesn't care if they do well or not. She is not considerate or accommodating and I extremely regret taking this class with her.
